servers.description: Production API server

get.description: List up to 1000 auth tokens (token values are not included). An account caller sees the account's tokens; an auth-token caller needs `resources.create_tokens` and sees only tokens created under it. A realm-scoped request lists only tokens usable in that realm. Check `truncated` before treating the list as complete.

public_key.description: Optional ED25519 public key (64 hex characters)

public_storage.description: Optional public JSON profile storage (max 64KB serialized)

ip_whitelist.description: Array of whitelisted IP addresses/CIDR ranges or "*" for all IPs

realm_ids.description: List of realm IDs this token is restricted to. Empty means no specific realm restrictions (unless allow_no_realm is false).

allow_no_realm.description: Only meaningful when realm_ids is EMPTY: set false to force an otherwise-unrestricted token onto a realm subdomain. A token with any realm_ids always requires a realm subdomain regardless of this flag.

permissions.title: TokenPermissions
permissions.description: Fine-grained permissions for this token. Any missing permission path defaults to false (deny).

delete.description: Can delete computers

kvm.description: Can enable /dev/kvm passthrough (run full VMs inside a computer). Rented/dedicated servers only.

env_values.description: Can read environment variable values. Without it the token still lists the key names (with computers.read) and may still set and delete variables (with computers.update), but every value in an environment-variable response comes back null with values_redacted: true. A "No change detected" answer to a set still tells an update-capable token that the value it sent equals the stored one. Not a secrets boundary: exec, file reads and logs can still reveal the environment.

delete.description: Can delete projects

purchase.description: Can buy, upgrade, pay for, cancel and toggle auto-renew of paid subserver subscriptions (spends the wallet)

bot_urls.description: Can manage External Bot URLs and their caller keys (create, settings, re-point, delete, panic, keys). Only for projects the account owns; project collaborators are refused.

support.description: Can open, read and reply to the account's support tickets (every ticket of the account). Refused to tokens limited to realms.

auth_token_public_profile.description: Can update the current auth token public_key and public_storage via self endpoint

create_tokens.description: Can mint/copy/manage child auth tokens within its own subtree (delegated token issuance). Children are clamped to a subset of this token; default-deny.

read_account.description: Can read the owning account's PII. On the profile endpoints (/api/v1/users/auth/me, GET/PUT /api/v1/users/{id} self) absent/false DEGRADES the response to identity fields (id, username, alias, public_key, timestamps). On the account-history surfaces (/api/v1/users/me/security-history, /api/v1/users/me/free-tier-status, and the notification inbox (GET /api/v1/notifications, GET /api/v1/notifications/summary), whose bodies carry security, billing and infrastructure events), absent/false is a hard 403, because a history has no meaningful reduced view.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token expires, or null if it never expires

is_enabled.description: Whether the token is currently active and can be used for authentication

vault_access.description: Whether this token can access user vault endpoints

event_access.description: Whether this token can access real-time event streams and event history endpoints

created_by_token_id.description: Lineage: id of the auth token that minted this one (delegated issuance). null = minted directly by the account.

delegation_depth.description: Delegation chain depth. 0 = root (account-minted); child = creator depth + 1.

last_used_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token was last used

last_used_ip.description: The last IP address that used this token

created_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token was created

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token was last updated

truncated.description: Present and true only when the list was too large to return in full, for an account caller or a token caller: the returned list is incomplete.

x-error-codes.title: Email not verified
x-error-codes.description: The password is correct but the account's email address is not verified yet. It is only returned after the password has been checked. On the login endpoint the response carries data.email, so the client can offer to resend the verification link. HTTP Basic authentication returns it on any operation, without the email.
x-error-codes.resolution: Complete email verification by clicking the link sent to your inbox, or call POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification to receive a new link, or complete a password reset, which also verifies the email.

example.message: Email not verified. Please check your inbox or request a new verification link.

x-error-codes.resolution: Generate a new code from your authenticator app and try again

data.description: Present on UPGRADE_REQUIRED: the retired names the request carried and their replacements.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid input
x-error-codes.description: A value passed the request schema but failed a check of this operation, for example two fields that must agree or a name that must exist. The message names the problem. The response's `error` is `Bad Request`; this code is not sent. A request that does not match the schema is answered with 422 `Validation Error` instead.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the value the message names, then send the request again.

example.message: public_key is required when public_storage is provided

x-error-codes.title: Unknown field
x-error-codes.description: The body names a permission key that does not exist, the singular `realm_id` (the field is `realm_ids`, an array), or any other field the request body does not declare (for example `expires_in`: the expiry field is `expires_at`). An unknown permission key set to exactly `false` is ignored rather than refused, and on create the `permissions` tree is not checked when a `permission_template` takes precedence over it
x-error-codes.resolution: Fix the spelling of each listed field or remove it; use realm_ids for realm restrictions and expires_at for an expiry

x-error-codes.title: 2FA verification required
x-error-codes.description: This operation requires 2FA verification because your account has 2FA enabled
x-error-codes.resolution: Provide an otp_code field with a valid TOTP code or backup code

x-error-codes.title: Invalid alias format
x-error-codes.description: The alias is blank (empty or only spaces). An alias with characters outside letters, numbers, spaces, underscores and hyphens, or one that is too long, is refused with 422 instead.
x-error-codes.resolution: Send an alias with at least one visible character, or omit it to get a generated one.

example.message: Alias must be a non-empty string

x-error-codes.title: Invalid IP address format
x-error-codes.description: A malformed address, CIDR range or wildcard is refused by the request schema with 422 `Validation Error`. This 400 covers an entry that passes the schema but is not a usable range, such as a CIDR range with host bits set (203.0.113.7/24 instead of 203.0.113.0/24). The response's `error` is `Bad Request`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Provide valid IPv4 addresses (e.g., "203.0.113.7") or CIDR ranges (e.g., "203.0.113.0/24"), or use "*" for all IPs

x-error-codes.title: IP whitelist too large
x-error-codes.description: ip_whitelist may hold at most 1000 entries, and its comma-separated string form at most 65536 characters
x-error-codes.resolution: Use fewer entries, for example by merging addresses into CIDR ranges

example.message: ip_whitelist must not contain more than 1000 entries

x-error-codes.title: Invalid expiration format
x-error-codes.description: A value that is not an ISO 8601 timestamp, a number, "today" or "tomorrow" is refused by the request schema with 422 `Validation Error`; null is accepted on copy and update only. This 400 covers a value the schema accepts but that is not a usable date. The response's `error` is `Bad Request`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a valid date format: ISO 8601 string, Unix timestamp (seconds/milliseconds), "today", "tomorrow", or null for non-expiring

example.message: Invalid expires_at date format. Use ISO 8601 format, Unix timestamp, "today", or "tomorrow".

x-error-codes.title: Public storage exceeds size limit
x-error-codes.description: public_storage must not exceed 65536 bytes as serialized UTF-8 JSON. The response's `error` is `Bad Request`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Reduce the size of the public storage payload and retry

x-error-codes.title: Expiration date in the past
x-error-codes.description: expires_at must be in the future. The response's `error` is `Bad Request`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Provide a future date for token expiration

example.message: expires_at must be in the future. The provided date is 3600 seconds in the past.

x-error-codes.title: Token alias already exists
x-error-codes.description: You already have an authentication token with this alias
x-error-codes.resolution: Choose a different unique alias for this token

example.message: Alias "<alias>" already exists for this user

x-error-codes.title: Request uses a retired name
x-error-codes.description: The request uses a name this API no longer accepts, or comes from a Hoody CLI too old for this API. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Send the name in data.renamed[].to, or update the Hoody CLI and SDK (npm i -g hoody-sdk).

example.message: This Hoody CLI is too old for the renamed API. Update: npm i -g hoody-sdk@1.0.1

data.description: Present on `TOKEN_CEILING_EXCEEDED`.

axis.description: Which limit of the parent token the request exceeds

paths.description: With `axis: permissions`, on an update made from a user session: every permission path the parent token lacks, for example `computers.create`

x-error-codes.title: Token ceiling exceeded
x-error-codes.description: The request would give a delegated token more than the token it was created from holds (or any token above that one): a permission, a realm, no-realm access, an IP range, vault or event access, a later expiry, or one more level of delegation. `data.axis` names which; for `permissions` on an update made from a user session, `data.paths` lists every permission path that exceeds. Nothing was created or changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Narrow the value named in data.axis so it stays within the parent token, widen the parent token first, or create the token from the account instead of from a token

example.message: Child token cannot hold permission 'computers.create' that its creator lacks

x-error-codes.resolution: Ask the resource owner to grant you access

schema.title: AuthTokenLimitReachedError
schema.description: The account or the creating token already has the maximum number of active tokens.

x-error-codes.title: Active token limit reached
x-error-codes.description: The account, or the token creating the new token, already has the maximum number of active authentication tokens. Expired tokens do not count; disabled tokens do.
x-error-codes.resolution: Delete tokens you no longer use (or let them expire), then try again

example.message: This account already has the maximum number of active API tokens (1000). Delete tokens you no longer use, then try again.

422.description: The request body failed schema validation, for example a `permission_template` that is not one of the listed templates.

schema.title: CreateAuthTokenValidationError
schema.description: The request body failed schema validation, for example a `permission_template` that is not one of the listed templates.

data.description: One entry per schema violation.

x-error-codes.title: Request validation failed
x-error-codes.description: The request body failed schema validation. The response's `error` is `Validation Error`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the fields named in the message and retry.

example.message: Validation failed: /permission_template must be equal to one of the allowed values

x-error-codes.title: 2FA verification locked
x-error-codes.description: Too many failed 2FA codes. 2FA checks are refused for up to 15 minutes; data.lockout_seconds says how long is left.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait data.lockout_seconds seconds, then try again with a current code.

example.message: Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.

x-error-codes.title: Rate limit exceeded
x-error-codes.description: Too many requests of this kind in a short time, counted per account, auth token or address. The request was not carried out. The body's `error` is `Too Many Requests`.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again. When there is no Retry-After header, the limit could not be checked: try again in a few seconds.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this endpoint. Please try again later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with a request-limit refusal when the allowance is used up.

alias.description: User-friendly alias for the token. If not provided, a random animal name will be generated (e.g., "clever-dolphin").

oneOf.description: ED25519 public key as 64-character hexadecimal string `null`: Clear the current public key

public_key.description: Optional ED25519 public key used for client identity derivation

oneOf.description: Arbitrary public JSON object (max 64KB serialized UTF-8) `null`: Clear public profile storage

public_storage.description: Public JSON object attached to the token public_key (at most 64 KB serialized), or null to clear it.

anyOf.description: IPv4 address or CIDR range
Wildcard (*) to allow all IPs
Comma-separated list of IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges
Wildcard (*) to allow all IPs

ip_whitelist.description: IP whitelist for this token. Accepts an array of IPv4 addresses/CIDR ranges, a comma-separated string, or "*" wildcard. When omitted, a token created from the account allows all IPs and a token created by another auth token inherits its parent's whitelist. At most 1000 entries, and at most 65536 characters as a string; larger values are refused with IP_WHITELIST_TOO_LARGE.

permission_template.description: Optional permission template to apply. If provided, it takes precedence over `permissions`; null is the same as leaving it out. Templates: full_access, external_customer, dev_team, finance_team, read_only.

permissions.title: TokenPermissions
permissions.description: Fine-grained permissions for this token. Inside a supplied permissions object, a missing path is denied. If neither permissions nor permission_template is sent, a token created from the account gets full access and a token created by another auth token inherits its parent's permissions.

realm_ids.description: List of realm IDs this token is restricted to: at most 500 for a token created from the account, and at most 100 for a token created by another auth token. A non-empty list restricts the token to these realm subdomains (an empty list restricts nothing unless allow_no_realm is false); a restricted token can still read its own details with GET /api/v1/auth/tokens/me on the base host.

allow_no_realm.description: Whether this token can be used without a realm scope (e.g. on base domain). Defaults to true for a token created from the account; a token created by another auth token inherits its parent's value. Set to false to create a strict sub-account token that ONLY works on specific realms. A token limited to realms (this false, or any realm_ids) cannot read account money data: wallet balances, transactions, invoices and payment methods are refused (403); it can still spend, without seeing balances.

vault_access.description: Whether this token can access user vault endpoints. Defaults to false for a token created from the account; a token created by another auth token inherits its parent's value.

event_access.description: Whether this token can access real-time event streams and event history endpoints. Defaults to true for a token created from the account; a token created by another auth token inherits its parent's value.

deny_reauthorization.description: Optional lock-down for scoped or script tokens. When true, the token gets no `resources.create_tokens` or `resources.vault` permission, `vault_access` is forced to false, and the token must expire (no permanent token), so it can never create child tokens or reach the vault. Rejected (400) if combined with an explicit `create_tokens`/`resources.vault`/`vault_access` grant. Defaults to false.

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the token should expire
Special keyword: "today" expires at midnight tonight, "tomorrow" expires in 24 hours
Unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds when the token should expire

expires_at.description: Token expiration: an ISO string, Unix timestamp, "today" or "tomorrow". If omitted, a token created from the account does not expire unless deny_reauthorization is true; a token created by another auth token always expires, and an omitted value gives it the latest expiry its parent may grant.

otp_code.description: TOTP code (6 digits) or backup code (10 alphanumeric). Required for a signed-in session (JWT) caller when the account has 2FA enabled and its token gate is on. Create, copy and add-realm need an unused code; remove-realm does not consume one.

env_values.description: Can read environment variable values. Without it the token still lists the key names (with computers.read) and may still set and delete variables (with computers.update), but every value in an environment-variable response comes back null with values_redacted: true. A "No change detected" answer to a set still tells an update-capable token that the value it sent equals the stored one. An unknown permission key set to exactly `false` is ignored rather than refused, and on create the `permissions` tree is not checked when a `permission_template` takes precedence over it

put.description: Create or update a key-value pair in your personal encrypted vault. Values can be any UTF-8 string (JSON, encrypted data, plain text). The API does NOT validate content - encryption is highly recommended for sensitive data. On an update, omitting `metadata` keeps the key's stored metadata, `metadata: null` clears it, and an object replaces it. PUT and PATCH behave the same. To save without overwriting a change made since you read the key, send its ETag in `If-Match` (or `If-None-Match: *` to create only): if the stored key no longer matches that ETag (or already exists), the answer is 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED and nothing is saved. Auth tokens need both vault_access: true and the resources.vault permission.

parameters.name: realm_id
parameters.description: Target a specific realm (24-char hex). When omitted and not on a realm subdomain, defaults to global scope (realm_id = ""). Case-insensitive: uppercase is normalized to lowercase.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Vault key name (alphanumeric, dots, underscores, hyphens)

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: Save only over the version you read: the ETag from an earlier GET or PUT of this key. If the key as stored now no longer matches it (value, metadata or millisecond timestamps), or no longer exists, the answer is 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED and nothing is saved. `*` matches any existing version.

parameters.name: if-none-match
parameters.description: Send `*` to create the key only if it does not exist yet. If it exists, the answer is 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED and nothing is saved.

patch.description: Create or update a key-value pair in your personal encrypted vault. Values can be any UTF-8 string (JSON, encrypted data, plain text). The API does NOT validate content - encryption is highly recommended for sensitive data. On an update, omitting `metadata` keeps the key's stored metadata, `metadata: null` clears it, and an object replaces it. PUT and PATCH behave the same. To save without overwriting a change made since you read the key, send its ETag in `If-Match` (or `If-None-Match: *` to create only): if the stored key no longer matches that ETag (or already exists), the answer is 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED and nothing is saved. Auth tokens need both vault_access: true and the resources.vault permission.

parameters.name: if-match

post.description: Authenticate with username (or email) and password. `data` takes one of three shapes. **LoginTokens**: a JWT access token (expires in 1 day) and refresh token (expires in 7 days); send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer {token}`. **LoginTwoFactorChallenge**: the account has 2FA, so no tokens are issued yet; `requires_2fa` is true and `temp_token` (valid 5 minutes) goes to POST /api/v1/users/auth/2fa/verify with the TOTP code. **LoginIntent**: with `response_mode: intent` and a `code_challenge` (hosted auth UI), an `auth_intent_token` and no session tokens; continue at POST /api/v1/auth/authorize. Every successful sign-in starts a session you can see and end under GET /api/v1/users/auth/sessions. An account can have up to 500 active sign-ins; at the limit, a new sign-in ends the one renewed longest ago (apps renew a sign-in regularly while they are in use). At most 300 new sign-ins can be started for one account per hour; beyond that this answers 429 `SESSION_CREATE_RATE_LIMITED` with a Retry-After header.

X-Hoody-Signature.description: ED25519 signature of response body. Format: t=<unix_ts>,kid=<keyId>,path=<urlPath>,sig=<128-hex>

data.title: LoginData
data.description: Exactly one of three shapes (see oneOf): LoginTokens when the session was issued, LoginTwoFactorChallenge when the account has 2FA, LoginIntent for the hosted-UI PKCE flow. The properties listed here accompany a shape as noted on each.

identity_claim.title: IdentityClaim
identity_claim.description: LoginTokens only. Hoody-signed identity credential for third-party verification. Verify with: nacl.sign.detached.verify(UTF8(payload_b64), hexToBytes(signature_hex), hoodyPublicKey) Fetch Hoody's public key at: GET /api/v1/meta/public-key Present to computer programs or third-party services to prove identity. May be omitted when identity signing is unavailable.

kid.description: Key ID. Re-fetch the public key if this does not match your cached key_id

payload_b64.description: base64url-encoded JSON payload containing: claim_type ("identity"), iss ("hoody-api"), sub (user_id), username, type (account type), iat, exp, kid

signature_hex.description: ED25519 detached signature over UTF-8 bytes of payload_b64 (128 hex chars = 64 bytes)

client_ip.description: LoginTokens only. IP address of the current request

recent_login_ips.description: LoginTokens only. List of recent unique login IP addresses (last 5)

auth_token_count.description: LoginTokens only. Number of active authentication tokens

user.title: User
user.description: LoginTokens and LoginIntent. The signed-in account.

public_key.description: ED25519 public key (64 hexadecimal characters)

metadata.description: Custom metadata object for storing additional user information

is_banned.description: Account ban status. Banned users cannot access the API.

email_verified.description: Whether the user has verified their email address

avatar_url.description: Avatar image URL from OAuth provider

signup_method.description: How the user signed up, for example email, github or google

free_tier_unlocked.description: Beta gate: whether this account may claim a free-tier server while an invite is required for free-tier access. Always true (or irrelevant) when no invite is required.

free_tier_unlocked_at.description: When the account was unlocked for free-tier claiming.

free_tier_unlock_source.description: How free-tier access was enabled for this account, for example invite_code. Null while it is not enabled.

onboarding.description: Per-account onboarding/UI milestones: key -> ISO timestamp (presence = done).

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 last modification timestamp

oneOf.title: LoginTokens
oneOf.description: The session was issued.

token.description: JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer {token}`.

refreshToken.description: Refresh token. Exchange it at POST /api/v1/users/auth/refresh for a new pair.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires

expires_in.description: Number of seconds until the access token expires

refresh_expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the refresh token expires

refresh_expires_in.description: Number of seconds until the refresh token expires

session_id.description: Id of the sign-in session this pair belongs to (not secret). Use it to recognise this session in GET /api/v1/users/auth/sessions or to end it with DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/sessions/{id}.

oneOf.title: LoginTwoFactorChallenge
oneOf.description: The account has two-factor authentication. No session exists yet: send temp_token with the TOTP code to POST /api/v1/users/auth/2fa/verify.

temp_token.description: Temporary partial JWT (valid 5 minutes). It is not a session token: send it to POST /api/v1/users/auth/2fa/verify.

method.description: The second factor to supply.

oneOf.title: LoginIntent
oneOf.description: response_mode 'intent' (hosted auth UI PKCE flow). Carries no session tokens.

auth_intent_token.description: Opaque single-use token (valid 60 seconds). Redeem it at POST /api/v1/auth/authorize with the same code_challenge, then POST /api/v1/auth/exchange.

post.description: Exchange a valid refresh token for a new access token and new refresh token. The refresh token must be sent TWICE: as the bearer credential (`Authorization: Bearer {refreshToken}`) AND as `refreshToken` in the JSON body. The server verifies the bearer and rejects the call with 401 unless the two are the same token, so sending the access token as the bearer (what an ordinary authenticated client does) always fails. Refresh tokens are single-use: every refresh returns a new refresh token and spends the one you sent, so save the new one. A spent refresh token is refused with 401. Presenting it again more than 30 seconds after it was spent also ends that sign-in (the account's other sign-ins stay), because it means a copy of the token is in someone else's hands. `SESSION_REVOKED` means the sign-in was ended (from one of your devices, by signing out everywhere, by a password or two-factor change, or as such a security measure): sign in again, and do not sign in again automatically. It is returned even for an expired refresh token whose sign-in was ended, so an app that was offline learns it; otherwise an expired one gets `TOKEN_EXPIRED`.

get.description: Retrieve the profile of the currently authenticated user. Works with JWT, auth token, or Basic authentication. When authenticated with an auth token, response includes `data.auth_token` introspection details (permissions and realm restrictions). This endpoint works even for banned users (read-only access). Note: when authenticated with an auth token that lacks the `resources.read_account` permission, the response is reduced to identity fields (id, username, alias, public_key, timestamps); email and other account PII are omitted.

public_key.description: ED25519 public key (64 hexadecimal characters)

metadata.description: Custom metadata object for storing additional user information

is_banned.description: Account ban status. Banned users cannot access the API.

email_verified.description: Whether the user has verified their email address

avatar_url.description: Avatar image URL from OAuth provider

signup_method.description: How the user signed up, for example email, github or google

free_tier_unlocked.description: Beta gate: whether this account may claim a free-tier server while an invite is required for free-tier access. Always true (or irrelevant) when no invite is required.

free_tier_unlocked_at.description: When the account was unlocked for free-tier claiming.

free_tier_unlock_source.description: How free-tier access was enabled for this account, for example invite_code. Null while it is not enabled.

onboarding.description: Per-account onboarding/UI milestones: key -> ISO timestamp (presence = done).

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 last modification timestamp

auth_token.title: CurrentAuthTokenIntrospection

public_key.description: Optional ED25519 public key (64 hex characters)

public_storage.description: Optional public JSON profile storage (max 64KB serialized)

ip_whitelist.description: Array of whitelisted IP addresses/CIDR ranges or "*" for all IPs

realm_ids.description: List of realm IDs this token is restricted to. Empty means no specific realm restrictions (unless allow_no_realm is false).

allow_no_realm.description: Only meaningful when realm_ids is EMPTY: set false to force an otherwise-unrestricted token onto a realm subdomain. A token with any realm_ids always requires a realm subdomain regardless of this flag.

permissions.title: TokenPermissions
permissions.description: Fine-grained permissions for this token. Any missing permission path defaults to false (deny).

delete.description: Can delete computers

kvm.description: Can enable /dev/kvm passthrough (run full VMs inside a computer). Rented/dedicated servers only.

env_values.description: Can read environment variable values. Without it the token still lists the key names (with computers.read) and may still set and delete variables (with computers.update), but every value in an environment-variable response comes back null with values_redacted: true. A "No change detected" answer to a set still tells an update-capable token that the value it sent equals the stored one. Not a secrets boundary: exec, file reads and logs can still reveal the environment.

delete.description: Can delete projects

purchase.description: Can buy, upgrade, pay for, cancel and toggle auto-renew of paid subserver subscriptions (spends the wallet)

bot_urls.description: Can manage External Bot URLs and their caller keys (create, settings, re-point, delete, panic, keys). Only for projects the account owns; project collaborators are refused.

support.description: Can open, read and reply to the account's support tickets (every ticket of the account). Refused to tokens limited to realms.

auth_token_public_profile.description: Can update the current auth token public_key and public_storage via self endpoint

create_tokens.description: Can mint/copy/manage child auth tokens within its own subtree (delegated token issuance). Children are clamped to a subset of this token; default-deny.

read_account.description: Can read the owning account's PII. On the profile endpoints (/api/v1/users/auth/me, GET/PUT /api/v1/users/{id} self) absent/false DEGRADES the response to identity fields (id, username, alias, public_key, timestamps). On the account-history surfaces (/api/v1/users/me/security-history, /api/v1/users/me/free-tier-status, and the notification inbox (GET /api/v1/notifications, GET /api/v1/notifications/summary), whose bodies carry security, billing and infrastructure events), absent/false is a hard 403, because a history has no meaningful reduced view.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token expires, or null if it never expires

is_enabled.description: Whether the token is currently active and can be used for authentication

vault_access.description: Whether this token can access user vault endpoints

event_access.description: Whether this token can access real-time event streams and event history endpoints

created_by_token_id.description: Lineage: id of the auth token that minted this one (delegated issuance). null = minted directly by the account.

delegation_depth.description: Delegation chain depth. 0 = root (account-minted); child = creator depth + 1.

last_used_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token was last used

last_used_ip.description: The last IP address that used this token

created_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token was created

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 date when the token was last updated

has_realm_restrictions.description: Whether the token is restricted to specific realms or requires realm scope

requires_realm_scope.description: Whether the token must be used on a realm-scoped URL

allowed_realm_ids.description: Realm IDs this token is allowed to operate in (empty means no explicit allowlist)

allow_no_realm.description: Only meaningful when realm_ids is empty; a token with realm_ids always requires a realm subdomain

active_realm_id.description: The realm resolved from the request host, or null when the request has no realm scope (for example on the base API host).

max_delegation_depth.description: The deepest delegation_depth a token may have on this server (a token made from a user session is 0). A token whose children would be deeper cannot create tokens (403).

auth_token.description: Present only when the request is authenticated with an auth token.

pending_pool_invitations.description: Number of pending pool invitations for the user.

pending_email.description: An email address change waiting for confirmation from the new address (null when none). Shown the same whether or not that address already has an account.

pending_email_expires_at.description: When the confirm link of the pending email change stops working (null when none).

email_change_undo_until.description: Until when the previous address can undo the last email change (null when none). No other email change starts and no free server is claimed before then.

limits.description: Account limits. Present on the full account view only (not for an auth token without resources.read_account, nor for one limited to realms: the count covers every realm of the account).

paid_subservers.description: Paid subservers: `max` you may hold, `used` counted toward it.

support_reply_email.description: Whether a "Support reply" email is sent when support answers one of your tickets. The email and the in-app notice always read "You have a new reply in a support ticket. Sign in to read it." and name no ticket, subject or text. The effective value: true unless you turned it off. Change it with PUT/PATCH /api/v1/users/{id} from a signed-in session (JWT only: auth tokens, HTTP Basic and impersonation are refused).

support_reply_email_stored.description: Whether you stored a choice for support_reply_email; false means the default (on) applies.

has_password.description: Whether a password is set on this account. False means no password is set on this account: it sets one with the reset link (POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with the account address), and until then every operation that asks for the account password (password change, email change, the 2FA operations that take a password) answers 400 PASSWORD_NOT_SET. Left out for an auth token without account read access, and when the read fails.

env_values.description: Can read environment variable values. Without it the token still lists the key names (with computers.read) and may still set and delete variables (with computers.update), but every value in an environment-variable response comes back null with values_redacted: true. A "No change detected" answer to a set still tells an update-capable token that the value it sent equals the stored one. Not a secrets boundary: exec, file reads and logs can still reveal the environment.

purchase.description: Can buy, upgrade, pay for, cancel and toggle auto-renew of paid subserver subscriptions (spends the wallet)

bot_urls.description: Can manage External Bot URLs and their caller keys (create, settings, re-point, delete, panic, keys). Only for projects the account owns; project collaborators are refused.

support.description: Can open, read and reply to the account's support tickets (every ticket of the account). Refused to tokens limited to realms.

On the account-history surfaces (/api/v1/users/me/security-history, /api/v1/users/me/free-tier-status, and the notification inbox (GET /api/v1/notifications, GET /api/v1/notifications/summary), whose bodies carry security, billing and infrastructure events), absent/false is a hard 403, because a history has no meaningful reduced view.

email_change_undo_until.description: Until when the previous address can undo the last email change (null when none). No other email change starts and no free server is claimed before then.

support_reply_email.description: Whether a "Support reply" email is sent when support answers one of your tickets. The email and the in-app notice always read "You have a new reply in a support ticket. Sign in to read it." and name no ticket, subject or text. The effective value: true unless you turned it off. Change it with PUT/PATCH /api/v1/users/{id} from a signed-in session (JWT only: auth tokens, HTTP Basic and impersonation are refused).

support_reply_email_stored.description: Whether you stored a choice for support_reply_email; false means the default (on) applies.

has_password.description: Whether a password is set on this account. False means no password is set on this account: it sets one with the reset link (POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with the account address), and until then every operation that asks for the account password (password change, email change, the 2FA operations that take a password) answers 400 PASSWORD_NOT_SET. post.description: Signs the account out on EVERY device, not only this client. Called with a session JWT, it revokes every access and refresh JWT issued to the account before this moment: other browsers, the CLI, other apps and this client all have to sign in again. Long-lived auth tokens (`hdy_…`) are not affected; revoke those with DELETE /api/v1/auth/tokens/{id}. Called with an auth token or HTTP Basic credentials, nothing is revoked and only the audit entry is written. A client should also drop its own stored access token, refresh token and credentials, or its automatic re-login signs it straight back in. To end one session, or every session but this one, use DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/sessions/{id} or POST /api/v1/users/auth/sessions/revoke-others. Creates an audit log entry. Works even for banned users.

get.description: Every place your account is signed in (browsers, the CLI, apps, device-code sign-ins), with when each started and was last confirmed, from which address and country, which client, and which one is this one. `state=active` (default) lists open sessions, this one first, then newest first. `state=ended` lists sessions that ended in the last 180 days (platform policy; older ones are deleted), newest ending first, with why and from which of your sessions. Pages of `limit` (default 50, at most 100); pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. `client`, `client_name` and `user_agent` are reported by the client and unverified; `method`, addresses and times are recorded by the server. An account can have up to 500 active sign-ins. At the limit, a new sign-in ends the one renewed longest ago (apps renew a sign-in regularly while they are in use). At most 300 new sign-ins can be started for one account per hour. Every ended sign-in shows when and why it ended. Ending a session signs that browser, CLI or app out at once. It does not delete the auth tokens (`hdy_…`) created while signed in with it: each session lists the ones it created; delete each under /api/v1/auth/tokens/{id}, which also ends the tokens they created in turn. Identity claims already issued stay valid until they expire (claims issued at sign-in last up to 30 days by default; re-issued ones at most 24 hours). An app that keeps your password and signs in again by itself stays out only if it stops when told its sign-in was ended (`SESSION_REVOKED`); changing the password ends every sign-in. Only your own sign-in can call this: auth tokens, HTTP Basic and impersonation are refused. Works for a banned account.

post.summary: Issue a fresh audience-bound identity claim
post.description: Mint a fresh, audience-bound identity claim for the authenticated caller without a re-login. Requires a first-party signed-in session (JWT); API auth tokens and HTTP Basic are refused. The claim proves "Hoody authenticated this user" to the audience named in the request; third parties verify it offline against GET /api/v1/meta/public-key. Claim lifetime is clamped to [60s, min(server ceiling (default 24h), remaining JWT lifetime)], default 1 hour.

identity_claim.title: IdentityClaim
identity_claim.description: Hoody-signed identity credential for third-party verification. Verify with: nacl.sign.detached.verify(UTF8(payload_b64), hexToBytes(signature_hex), hoodyPublicKey) Fetch Hoody's public key at: GET /api/v1/meta/public-key Re-issued claims are audience-bound: verifiers MUST check payload.aud against their own identifier.

get.description: Returns your own account security history (sign-ins and, on request, rejected attempts and other security events: logout, 2FA changes, OTP outcomes) with IP address, resolved country, source channel and timestamp, newest first. **History covers the last 180 days, which is platform policy and the same for every account; older logins are purged automatically and cannot be recovered.** Login records cannot be edited or deleted by the account holder: the trail is append-only so it stays trustworthy as evidence. Pass `include_failed=true` to also see REJECTED sign-in attempts. A burst of them, or any from a country you have not visited, is the clearest sign someone else is trying to get in. Failures are only recorded when a credential was presented against a REAL account (an attempt on an unknown address is never recorded, so this cannot be used to test whether an account exists), and are capped at 200 per account per hour: beyond that, further attempts in the same hour are not listed. Pass `include_security=true` for other account-security events: logout, 2FA enable/disable, OTP verification outcomes and backup-code use. `country` is filled in shortly after the event is recorded. It is `null` when the location of the address is not known, or when the lookup has not completed. Treat null as **unavailable**, never as a location. Note also that a null does not necessarily become non-null later: an event that is not resolved soon after it is recorded may keep a null country permanently. Auth tokens need resources.read_account. It cannot be read through an impersonated session.

parameters.description: Page number

parameters.description: Results per page

parameters.name: include_failed
parameters.description: Also return REJECTED sign-in attempts against this account. Opt-in: mixing them in by default would make failed attempts look like your own sessions.

parameters.name: include_security
parameters.description: Also return other account-security events already recorded for you: logout, 2FA enabled/disabled, OTP verification outcomes, backup-code regeneration.

outcome.description: Coarse read of `event`: `failed` means a credential or code was rejected.

country.description: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2, or null if not resolved

post.description: Start changing the email address of your account. Needs the current password, and a two-factor code whenever two-factor authentication is on. The new address gets a confirm link (valid 24 hours); the current address gets a notice. Until the link is confirmed nothing changes. After the change, the previous address gets an undo link valid for 7 days; during those days no other email change starts and the previous address stays reserved for this account. Changing the password, signing out everywhere or changing two-factor settings cancels a pending change. The answer is the same whether or not the new address already has an account; an address that does gets a mail saying so instead of a link. Only your own sign-in can call this: auth tokens, HTTP Basic, impersonation and realm-scoped requests are refused. Accounts without a password, with an unverified address, and staff accounts cannot use it.

post.description: Redeem a single-use invite code to unlock free-tier server claiming during the beta, and try to provision a free server. When none is available the answer is still 200, with server null and claim_blocked_reason pool_empty: the account stays unlocked and POST /api/v1/users/me/retry-setup claims one later. Idempotent if already unlocked. No-op (no code consumed) when the beta gate is disabled. Refused with 403 FREE_TIER_MAILBOX_ALREADY_USED, before the code is redeemed, when another account with this mailbox already received a free server. Requires a first-party signed-in session (JWT); API auth tokens and HTTP Basic are refused.

server.description: The claimed free-tier server, or null if not yet claimed.

project.description: The default project (id and alias), or null.

get.description: Returns whether the beta gate is enabled, whether this account is unlocked, whether it already owns a free server, and (advisory, point-in-time) why a claim is currently blocked. Never attempts a claim. Auth-token callers must hold the `resources.read_account` permission (account-level status); tokens without it receive 403. JWT/owner callers are unaffected.

gate_enabled.description: Whether the beta access gate is currently enabled.

unlocked.description: Whether this account is unlocked for free-tier claiming.

has_free_server.description: Whether this account already owns a free-tier server.

can_claim.description: Whether a claim would currently succeed.

claim_blocked_reason.description: Why a claim is blocked (advisory snapshot): already_claimed → mailbox_already_used / email_change_window → hold_review → hold_waiting → invite_required → pool_empty → none. mailbox_already_used = another account with this mailbox (the same address or a spelling the provider delivers to the same inbox) already received a free server; it applies whether or not the beta gate is on. email_change_window = the account email was changed recently; a claim waits until that change can no longer be undone (7 days). hold_review / hold_waiting = the free server is held (see hold): waiting for a review, or for the hold to end.

signup_code_failed.description: True only while invite_required AND the invite code from the signup link definitively failed to redeem (already used, disabled, expired, or unknown). A valid code can still be entered manually.

hold.title: FreeTierHold
hold.description: When the free server of this account becomes available. null when there is nothing to wait for.

kind.description: timed: available at the time given by release_at. review: availability is decided by a review.

release_at.description: When a timed hold ends; null until the email address is verified, and for a review hold.

next_action.description: wait: the hold has not ended yet. claim: claim the free server now (POST /users/me/retry-setup). review_pending: waiting for a review. use_invite: the review was declined; an invite code still releases the hold.

denied_reason.description: Why the review was declined, as written by the Hoody team.

delete.description: Permanently delete a project with its permissions and aliases. A project that still holds computers is refused with 422 PROJECT_HAS_COMPUTERS and nothing is changed: delete its computers first, or pass delete_computers=true to delete the project together with all its computers. Once the delete succeeds the project is gone, and deleting it again returns 404. Removing its computers from their servers continues in the background and is retried if it fails. You must be the owner or have "delete" permission. Your default project cannot be deleted: 403 with `error: "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS"` and message `Cannot delete your default workspace`. WARNING: This action cannot be undone.

parameters.description: Project ID to delete

202.description: A project with many computers is deleted in bounded steps. The deletion is decided and the project refuses new computers; the rest continues in the background. Repeating the DELETE resumes it (409 PROJECT_DELETION_IN_PROGRESS while another run holds it); a GET of the project answers 404 once it is done.

data.description: With PROJECT_HAS_COMPUTERS: the counts below. With REQUEST_SCHEMA_INVALID: one entry per schema violation.

anyOf.description: How many computers the project still holds, so a client can offer the next step without reading the message.

computers.description: Computers the project still holds. All of them block the delete.

expired.description: How many of them are on a server that has ended. These are left out of the computer list unless include_expired=true, and can still be deleted.

deleting.description: How many of them are already being deleted. When this equals computers, try again in a few minutes.

Computers that do not show in the computer list (data.hidden) can be removed by support.

get.summary: Get all computers for a project
get.description: Get all computers for a project with pagination, filtering, and sorting. A project member (a collaborator at any permission level) reads a reduced view: identity, status, server and summary flags only. It never carries the SSH public key, the comment, volumes, environment fields, runtime information, proxy domains or proxy permission documents; runtime and include_proxy_domains are ignored for a member and include_proxy_permissions answers 403.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: Include live runtime information. Accepts "true", "false", or a URL-encoded JSON string like `{"displays":true}`. An empty JSON object `{}` fetches all info. Runtime information may be up to 2 seconds old.

parameters.name: include_proxy_domains
parameters.description: Include proxy domains (aliases) for each computer. When true, adds a proxy_domains array to each computer object.

parameters.name: include_proxy_permissions
parameters.description: Include the full proxy-permissions documents (computer-level proxy_permissions and parent-project-level project_proxy_permissions) for each computer. Returns proxy authentication group configuration including credentials. Request only when explicitly needed. Auth tokens additionally require the resources.proxy_aliases permission.

parameters.name: include_expired
parameters.description: Include computers that have expired due to server termination. By default, expired computers are excluded from results.

parameters.name: include_deleting
parameters.description: Include computers currently being deleted. By default, deleting computers are excluded from results.

project_alias.description: Project alias as a helper field

datacenter.description: Present for a dedicated server. Absent when the computer runs on a subserver (paid or free).

paid_subserver.description: True for a paid subserver (a paid slice of a shared host); false for free slices, rentals and dedicated servers.

shared_compute.description: True for free-tier slices: cpu_cores/ram_gb are null because the slice has no per-slice CPU/RAM quota.

expires_at.description: Current rental end (ISO 8601) for dedicated (non-free) servers; null for free-tier servers or when no rental is active.

kvm_supported.description: Whether this server can give a computer /dev/kvm (run ordinary hardware-accelerated VMs). null = not known yet, or the last check is older than 1 hour. KVM is only on rented bare-metal servers, never on free or paid subservers. This says nothing about whether you may enable it right now: the computer must be stopped, and your permissions and account state still apply.

kvm_nested.description: Whether VMs you run here may themselves run hardware-accelerated VMs (nested virtualization). Off by default; enabled per server by Hoody on request. The VM also needs the host CPU virtualization features passed to it (for example QEMU `-cpu host`). false whenever kvm_supported is false; null = unknown.

kvm_checked_at.description: When Hoody last checked this server's KVM support (ISO 8601). A value with kvm_supported null means that check is too old to trust. null = never checked, or not applicable (subservers, expired or past rentals).

ssh_hostname.description: SSH connection hostname (computed from project, computer, and server)

env_sync.description: Environment-variable apply state: pending = your latest environment variables have not yet been confirmed inside the computer (they are applied automatically); last_error names why the last apply failed (ENV_DEST_UNSUPPORTED, ENV_BLOCK_MALFORMED, ENV_HOST_CONFIG_TOO_LARGE, ENV_LEGACY_OVERFLOW, ENV_UNREPRESENTABLE, ENV_APPLY_FAILED) or null.

exhausted.description: True when the computer's environment has reached its change limit, so further environment changes are refused (409 ENV_REVISION_EXHAUSTED). Contact support to reset it.

hoody_kit.description: Whether hoody_kit toolkit is installed in the computer

dev_kit.description: Whether dev_kit development tools are enabled

kvm.description: Whether /dev/kvm passthrough (run full VMs inside the computer) is enabled. Rented / dedicated (bare-metal) servers only; never free tier.

autostart.description: Whether the computer starts automatically on host boot

is_default.description: True if this is the user's auto-provisioned default computer. Exactly one computer per user has this flag after signup.

failure_reason.description: Why this computer failed, when its status is failed and its creation or copy failed; otherwise null. code: CREATE_NOT_STARTED (the host could not accept the creation, so nothing was created on it: delete the computer and create it again), CREATE_FAILED (the creation failed on its host) or COPY_FAILED (the copy failed on its host).

environment_vars.description: Always {} in this response: read the variables with GET /api/v1/computers/{id}/env.

ssh_key_fingerprint.description: OpenSSH-format fingerprint (SHA256:...) of the installed public key - the same string `ssh-keygen -lf` prints and code hosting sites display. Null when no key is installed.

ssh_key_installed_at.description: When the currently installed key was set or last replaced. Null when no key is installed, or briefly while a just-made key change is still settling.

server_expired.description: Whether this computer has expired (its server ended or was reinstalled). Listed only with include_expired=true.

server_expired_at.description: When the computer was marked as expired

realm_ids.description: Realm IDs this computer belongs to

pid.description: Process id of the display's viewer service. Null when it could not be read; absent when state is parked or x-live.

state.description: live: running, can be viewed and driven. x-live: started, but its viewer service is not running, so it cannot be viewed or captured. parked: set up by a terminal session and not started yet; it starts on first use.

proxy_domains.description: Proxy domains (aliases) for this computer (only included if include_proxy_domains=true)

url.description: Pre-built proxy alias URL

has_proxy_permissions.description: True when a non-default proxy-permissions configuration is stored for this computer or its project (auth groups, program rules, default-deny policy, proxy disabled, or hooks). Configuration-present signal: it does not by itself mean traffic is currently restricted; read the full document(s) via include_proxy_permissions=true to evaluate enforcement. Null when the API could not check (proxy_permissions_scope is then unknown): treat it as not known, never as false.

proxy_permissions_scope.description: Where the non-default proxy-permissions configuration lives: computer-level document, parent-project-level document, both, or none. unknown when the API could not check during this read; has_proxy_permissions is then null. unknown says nothing about the rules: treat it as not known, never as none.

proxy_permissions_computer_state.description: This computer's own stored proxy-permissions document, never its content: missing when none is stored (it follows only its project), default when one is stored that changes nothing (for example an open document allowing anyone), applied when one is stored that adds rules, invalid when the stored one cannot be read (it applies nothing). A document version can stay above 0 after a delete: read this field, not the version, to tell whether a document is stored. unknown when the API could not check during this read: treat it as not known.

has_proxy_domains.description: True when at least one proxy alias (custom domain) targets this computer. Counts aliases regardless of who created them, including disabled aliases and expired aliases that have not been deleted (an expired alias is kept until it is deleted). Under a realm subdomain only aliases belonging to that realm are counted (the realm_id query param filters computers, not this field). Note: the proxy_domains array from include_proxy_domains=true lists only the requesting user's aliases, so this can be true while proxy_domains is empty.

proxy_domains_count.description: Number of proxy aliases targeting this computer. Same scoping rules as has_proxy_domains.

proxy_permissions.title: ProxyPermissionsDoc

project.description: Project ID this document belongs to

groups.description: Authentication groups configuration (jwt/password/ip/token or OR-arrays). Contains credentials. A document can hold at most 256 groups and 1 MiB; one already over either limit can be edited and reduced but not grown.

permissions.description: Per-group program access rules (defines WHICH instances are ALLOWED)

default.description: Default access policy for requests matching no group. A project document has allow or deny. A computer document has allow or deny when it overrides the project, or inherit when the project default applies (allow when the project has no rules).

enable_proxy.description: Whether the reverse proxy is enabled for this entity. Always present on a project document (true unless it was switched off). On a computer document it is present only when the computer sets it; when absent, the project value applies (true when the project does not set it either).

hooks.description: Per-service proxy hook arrays (computer-level documents only)

schema_version.description: Document format version; absent for documents saved in the older format

file_version.description: Monotonic write counter. 0 = no stored document yet OR a document saved before versioning existed; either way use If-Match: file:v0 for the first save. Use in If-Match as file:v<N> when PUTting.

etag.description: Precomputed If-Match precondition value for PUT round-trips (file:v<file_version>)

post.description: Create a new computer for a project. A create can take several minutes. Send an Idempotency-Key header to make it safe to retry: a retry with the same key and body gets the first request's answer, with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header, instead of creating a second computer or failing on the name: 201 with the computer as it is now when the create succeeded, its error when it failed after making a computer (data.computer_id names that computer), 409 COMPUTER_CREATE_INTERRUPTED when it stopped before finishing, and 404 when the computer has since been deleted. While the first request is still running a retry waits up to 20 seconds, then answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After. A key is kept for 24 hours and belongs to the user who sent it. A create that fails with nothing created frees its key.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Makes the create safe to retry. 1 to 128 printable characters, for example a UUID; use a new key for each new computer. A retry with the same key and the same body gets the first answer; the same key with a different body is refused with 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

Nothing was changed. `data.used` is omitted for a token limited to realms (it counts every realm of the account).
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a realm the account already has, remove a realm from every project and computer that carries it, or move to a higher limit: accounts that have held a paid server or rented a bare-metal server get more realms. x-error-codes.resolution: Sign in again, or refresh the session.

x-error-codes.title: Parent auth token no longer valid
x-error-codes.description: The auth token was created by another auth token, and that token (or one above it) has been revoked, disabled or has expired, so this one no longer authenticates
x-error-codes.resolution: Create a new auth token from a valid one, or sign in again

x-error-codes.title: Invalid credentials
x-error-codes.description: The provided username/email or password is incorrect
x-error-codes.resolution: Verify your credentials and try again, or use the password reset feature

x-error-codes.title: Email not verified
x-error-codes.description: The password is correct but the account's email address is not verified yet. It is only returned after the password has been checked. On the login endpoint the response carries data.email, so the client can offer to resend the verification link. HTTP Basic authentication returns it on any operation, without the email.
x-error-codes.resolution: Complete email verification by clicking the link sent to your inbox, or call POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification to receive a new link, or complete a password reset, which also verifies the email.

example.message: Email not verified. Please check your inbox or request a new verification link.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid OTP code
x-error-codes.description: The provided 2FA code is incorrect or has expired
x-error-codes.resolution: Generate a new code from your authenticator app and try again

x-error-codes.description: You do not have the required permissions to perform this action
x-error-codes.resolution: Ask the resource owner to grant you access

x-error-codes.title: Account banned

x-error-codes.resolution: Contact support for information about your account status
