x-error-codes.resolution: Verify the resource ID and ensure it exists

409.description: Default Response

data.description: COMPUTER_NAME_IN_USE: field is "name"; computer_id and status name the computer holding the name when you can see it (status is creating, without computer_id, while it is still being set up). COMPUTER_CREATE_INTERRUPTED: computer_id and status name the computer the interrupted create made, when you can see it.

x-error-codes.title: Computer name already in use
x-error-codes.description: A computer with this name already exists in the project. data.computer_id names it and data.status gives its status when you can see it; data.status is creating while it is still being set up.
x-error-codes.resolution: If it is the computer you meant to create, use it. Otherwise choose a different name.

example.message: Computer name already in use within the project

x-error-codes.title: SSH public key already in use
x-error-codes.description: SSH public keys must be unique per computer. A single public key cannot be assigned to multiple computers.
x-error-codes.resolution: Generate a new SSH key pair for this computer, or remove the key from the other computer before reusing it.

example.message: SSH public key already in use

x-error-codes.title: No free computer name found
x-error-codes.description: No name was given, and every generated name tried was already used in the project. Nothing was created.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry, or give the computer a name.

example.message: Unable to generate unique computer name after multiple attempts

x-error-codes.title: Target server is being deleted
x-error-codes.description: The server the computer would be placed on is being deleted. Nothing was created.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry once the deletion has finished, or choose another server.

example.message: The target server is being deleted. Retry once the deletion has finished.

x-error-codes.title: Storage share being removed
x-error-codes.description: A storage share of this project is being removed and is recording which computers use it. Until that finishes (seconds to a few minutes), no computer can join or leave the project, and a computer the removal names cannot move.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry in a few seconds.

example.message: A storage share of this project is being removed, so no computer can join or leave the project right now. Retry in a few seconds.

x-error-codes.title: Target server no longer available
x-error-codes.description: The server the computer was placed on went away before the computer was set up. The computer was not created.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry the create.

example.message: The target server is no longer available; the computer was not created.

x-error-codes.title: KVM could not be set up
x-error-codes.description: KVM could not be set up for the new computer, so the computer was not created.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry the create, or create the computer without KVM.

example.message: KVM could not be set up for the new computer; the computer was not created.

x-error-codes.title: KVM not available on this server
x-error-codes.description: KVM needs dedicated hardware that supports it, and this server does not provide it. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a server with dedicated hardware, or contact support.

example.message: This server does not provide KVM to computers. KVM is only available on dedicated hardware. No changes were made.

x-error-codes.title: Server does not support KVM yet
x-error-codes.description: The server must be upgraded before KVM can be enabled on it. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the server has been upgraded, or contact support.

example.message: This server does not support KVM yet, so KVM cannot be enabled until it is upgraded. No changes were made.

x-error-codes.title: Another KVM change is running
x-error-codes.description: Another KVM change is in progress on this server. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry shortly.

example.message: Another KVM change is in progress on this server. Retry shortly.

x-error-codes.title: Server busy
x-error-codes.description: Another change is running on this server, so this request was refused. A refused create or copy changed nothing; a refused server delete leaves the server closed to new paid sales.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry shortly. A create or copy can also choose another server.

example.message: Another change is running on the target server. Retry the create shortly, or choose another server.

x-error-codes.title: Subserver has another owner
x-error-codes.description: A subserver has exactly one owner, and every computer on it must belong to that owner. The computer would belong to someone else, or the subserver still holds another user's computers. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Place the computer on a server its owner may use, or move or delete the other user's computers first.

example.message: This subserver belongs to another user; a subserver holds only its owner's computers.

x-error-codes.title: Request still in progress
x-error-codes.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the Retry-After delay with the same key and body to get its result.

example.message: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed. Retry after a few seconds with the same key to get its result.

x-error-codes.title: Computer create interrupted
x-error-codes.description: Creating the computer was interrupted before it finished. data.computer_id names the computer it made.
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the status of data.computer_id and delete it if you do not want it. Create again with a new Idempotency-Key.

example.message: Creating this computer was interrupted before it finished. data.computer_id is the computer it made; check its status, and delete it if you do not want it.

422.description: Default Response

x-error-codes.title: Idempotency-Key reused
x-error-codes.description: This Idempotency-Key was already used for a request with a different body, project or realm.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a new key for a new computer. Reuse a key only to retry the same request.

example.message: This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request. Use a new key for a new computer.

429.description: Too Many Requests: a request limit of this operation is used up

x-error-codes.title: Rate limit exceeded
x-error-codes.description: Too many requests of this kind in a short time, counted per account, auth token or address. The request was not carried out. The body's `error` is `Too Many Requests`.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again. When there is no Retry-After header, the limit could not be checked: try again in a few seconds.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this endpoint. Please try again later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with a request-limit refusal when the allowance is used up.

data.description: On an Idempotency-Key retry of a create that failed after making a computer: computer_id and status name that computer, when you can see it.

x-error-codes.title: Computer creation could not be started
x-error-codes.description: The create request could not be sent to the server, so nothing was created. Its name, SSH key and quota slot are free again.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry the request. If it keeps failing, try another server or contact support.

example.message: Computer creation could not be started on its host

503.description: The server could not be reached before anything was sent. Nothing was created; retry after the Retry-After header.

schema.title: ServiceUnavailableError
schema.description: The server could not be reached before anything was sent. Nothing was created; retry after the Retry-After header.

x-error-codes.title: Computer server temporarily unavailable
x-error-codes.description: The server for this computer could not be reached for a moment, so the create or copy request was never sent and nothing was created. Its name, SSH key and quota slot are free again.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.

example.message: The server for this computer could not be reached right now. Nothing was created. Retry shortly.

name.description: Name for the computer. Must be 3-100 characters, alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores. Omit or use "rand" to generate a random name.

color.description: HEX color for the computer (e.g., #FF0000 or FF0000). If not provided, a random color will be generated. The # prefix will be added automatically if missing, and the color will be converted to uppercase.

computer_image.description: Computer image to use. If null or not provided, will use the default configured image. Shorthand is resolved automatically: a bare distribution name or a hyphenated version ("debian", "debian-13") becomes the canonical base image ("debian/13"), as do the "debian:13" and "debian 13" forms.

ai.description: Whether AI features are enabled (default: true)

environment_vars.description: The computer's initial environment variables. Keys must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` and be at most 128 characters long.

ssh_public_key.description: SSH public key for computer access. SSH public keys must be unique per computer (one computer per key). If not provided, will inherit from project defaults.

comment.description: Optional comment for the computer (max 16000 characters)

hoody_kit.description: Enable all Hoody Kit features: extra package sources, a package download cache, basic and developer packages, extra shells, the Hoody daemon, sudo setup, snapd removal, web view, desktop, a default user, a web terminal, and VM tooling (about 185 MiB; running VMs additionally needs the separate kvm grant).

dev_kit.description: Enable dev_kit development tools in the computer. Defaults to true when hoody_kit is true, false when hoody_kit is false (unless explicitly set). Cannot be updated after creation.

kvm.description: Enable /dev/kvm passthrough (run full VMs inside the computer) at creation. Available on rented / dedicated (bare-metal) servers ONLY (never free tier), and rejected (403) on a free server. Defaults to false. Can also be toggled later via PUT /api/v1/computers/{id}/kvm on a stopped computer.

dev_kvm.description: Accepted alias of `kvm` on input (`kvm` wins if both are sent and they must agree).

autostart.description: Whether the computer should start automatically on host boot (default: true)

ramdisk.description: Whether to mount a ramdisk at /ramdisk in the computer (default: true). The ramdisk KEEPS data when you stop/start/reboot the computer, but LOSES data if the physical host server reboots. Can store up to 50% of total host memory. Ideal for security (data automatically wiped on server seizure), temporary files, or extremely fast I/O at no cost.

realm_ids.description: Realm IDs to assign this computer to. If creating from a realm subdomain (a 24-character hex realm id, e.g., https://0123456789abcdef01234567.api.hoody.com), the subdomain realm is automatically included and merged with any explicitly provided realm_ids. Note: Computers can have different realm membership than their parent project.

get.description: Get all computers across all projects for the current user with pagination, filtering, and sorting. This endpoint provides a global view of all computers without being scoped to a specific project.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination - starts from 1

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of computers to return per page - maximum 100 items

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Field to sort computers by

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort direction - ascending or descending

parameters.name: realm_id
parameters.description: Filter by realm ID. Only returns computers that belong to this realm. Alternative to using realm subdomain in URL.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: Include live runtime information. Accepts "true", "false", or a URL-encoded JSON string like `{"displays":true}`. An empty JSON object `{}` fetches all info. Runtime information may be up to 2 seconds old.

parameters.name: include_proxy_domains
parameters.description: Include proxy domains (aliases) for each computer. When true, adds a proxy_domains array to each computer object.

parameters.name: include_proxy_permissions
parameters.description: Include the full proxy-permissions documents (computer-level proxy_permissions and parent-project-level project_proxy_permissions) for each computer. Returns proxy authentication group configuration including credentials. Request only when explicitly needed. Auth tokens additionally require the resources.proxy_aliases permission.

parameters.name: include_expired
parameters.description: Include computers that have expired due to server termination. By default, expired computers are excluded from results.

parameters.name: include_deleting
parameters.description: Include computers currently being deleted. By default, deleting computers are excluded from results.

project_alias.description: Project alias as a helper field

datacenter.description: Present for a dedicated server. Absent when the computer runs on a subserver (paid or free).

paid_subserver.description: True for a paid subserver (a paid slice of a shared host); false for free slices, rentals and dedicated servers.

shared_compute.description: True for free-tier slices: cpu_cores/ram_gb are null because the slice has no per-slice CPU/RAM quota.

expires_at.description: Current rental end (ISO 8601) for dedicated (non-free) servers; null for free-tier servers or when no rental is active.

kvm_supported.description: Whether this server can give a computer /dev/kvm (run ordinary hardware-accelerated VMs). null = not known yet, or the last check is older than 1 hour. KVM is only on rented bare-metal servers, never on free or paid subservers. This says nothing about whether you may enable it right now: the computer must be stopped, and your permissions and account state still apply.

kvm_nested.description: Whether VMs you run here may themselves run hardware-accelerated VMs (nested virtualization). Off by default; enabled per server by Hoody on request. The VM also needs the host CPU virtualization features passed to it (for example QEMU `-cpu host`). false whenever kvm_supported is false; null = unknown.

kvm_checked_at.description: When Hoody last checked this server's KVM support (ISO 8601). A value with kvm_supported null means that check is too old to trust. null = never checked, or not applicable (subservers, expired or past rentals).

ssh_hostname.description: SSH connection hostname (computed from project, computer, and server)

env_sync.description: Environment-variable apply state: pending = your latest environment variables have not yet been confirmed inside the computer (they are applied automatically); last_error names why the last apply failed (ENV_DEST_UNSUPPORTED, ENV_BLOCK_MALFORMED, ENV_HOST_CONFIG_TOO_LARGE, ENV_LEGACY_OVERFLOW, ENV_UNREPRESENTABLE, ENV_APPLY_FAILED) or null.

exhausted.description: True when the computer's environment has reached its change limit, so further environment changes are refused (409 ENV_REVISION_EXHAUSTED). Contact support to reset it.

hoody_kit.description: Whether hoody_kit toolkit is installed in the computer

dev_kit.description: Whether dev_kit development tools are enabled

kvm.description: Whether /dev/kvm passthrough (hardware virtualization for running full VMs inside the computer) is enabled. Rented / dedicated (bare-metal) servers only; never free tier.

autostart.description: Whether the computer starts automatically on host boot

ramdisk_scope.description: Sharing scope for /ramdisk. `computer` (default) mounts only private storage. `project` additionally mounts /ramdisk/project, shared with your other computers in this project ON THE SAME SERVER (a RAM disk cannot span servers). Refused when the project has other members.

ramdisk.description: Whether to mount a ramdisk at /ramdisk. Backed by a shared per-server memory pool (512 MiB by default, never more than 50% of the server memory) shared with your other computers on that server. Data survives computer restarts but is LOST on a host reboot. Counts against memory, not disk.

is_default.description: True if this is the user's auto-provisioned default computer. Exactly one computer per user has this flag after signup.

failure_reason.description: Why this computer failed, when its status is failed and its creation or copy failed; otherwise null. code: CREATE_NOT_STARTED (the host could not accept the creation, so nothing was created on it: delete the computer and create it again), CREATE_FAILED (the creation failed on its host) or COPY_FAILED (the copy failed on its host).

environment_vars.description: Always {} in this response: read the variables with GET /api/v1/computers/{id}/env.

ssh_key_fingerprint.description: OpenSSH-format fingerprint (SHA256:...) of the installed public key - the same string `ssh-keygen -lf` prints and code hosting sites display. Null when no key is installed.

ssh_key_installed_at.description: When the currently installed key was set or last replaced. Null when no key is installed, or briefly while a just-made key change is still settling.

server_expired.description: Whether this computer has expired (its server ended or was reinstalled)

server_expired_at.description: When the computer was marked as expired

realm_ids.description: Realm IDs this computer belongs to

pid.description: Process id of the display's viewer service. Null when it could not be read; absent when state is parked or x-live.

state.description: live: running, can be viewed and driven. x-live: started, but its viewer service is not running, so it cannot be viewed or captured. parked: set up by a terminal session and not started yet; it starts on first use.

proxy_domains.description: Proxy domains (aliases) for this computer (only included if include_proxy_domains=true)

url.description: Pre-built proxy alias URL

has_proxy_permissions.description: True when a non-default proxy-permissions configuration is stored for this computer or its project (auth groups, program rules, default-deny policy, proxy disabled, or hooks). Configuration-present signal: it does not by itself mean traffic is currently restricted; read the full document(s) via include_proxy_permissions=true to evaluate enforcement. Null when the API could not check (proxy_permissions_scope is then unknown): treat it as not known, never as false.

proxy_permissions_scope.description: Where the non-default proxy-permissions configuration lives: computer-level document, parent-project-level document, both, or none. unknown when the API could not check during this read; has_proxy_permissions is then null. unknown says nothing about the rules: treat it as not known, never as none.

proxy_permissions_computer_state.description: This computer's own stored proxy-permissions document, never its content: missing when none is stored (it follows only its project), default when one is stored that changes nothing (for example an open document allowing anyone), applied when one is stored that adds rules, invalid when the stored one cannot be read (it applies nothing). A document version can stay above 0 after a delete: read this field, not the version, to tell whether a document is stored. unknown when the API could not check during this read: treat it as not known.

has_proxy_domains.description: True when at least one proxy alias (custom domain) targets this computer. Counts aliases regardless of who created them, including disabled aliases and expired aliases that have not been deleted (an expired alias is kept until it is deleted). Under a realm subdomain only aliases belonging to that realm are counted (the realm_id query param filters computers, not this field). Note: the proxy_domains array from include_proxy_domains=true lists only the requesting user's aliases, so this can be true while proxy_domains is empty.

proxy_domains_count.description: Number of proxy aliases targeting this computer. Same scoping rules as has_proxy_domains.

project.description: Project ID this document belongs to

groups.description: Authentication groups configuration (jwt/password/ip/token or OR-arrays). Contains credentials. A document can hold at most 256 groups and 1 MiB; one already over either limit can be edited and reduced but not grown.

permissions.description: Per-group program access rules (defines WHICH instances are ALLOWED)

default.description: Default access policy for requests matching no group. A project document has allow or deny. A computer document has allow or deny when it overrides the project, or inherit when the project default applies (allow when the project has no rules).

enable_proxy.description: Whether the reverse proxy is enabled for this entity. Always present on a project document (true unless it was switched off). On a computer document it is present only when the computer sets it; when absent, the project value applies (true when the project does not set it either).

hooks.description: Per-service proxy hook arrays (computer-level documents only)

schema_version.description: Document format version; absent for documents saved in the older format

file_version.description: Monotonic write counter. 0 = no stored document yet OR a document saved before versioning existed; either way use If-Match: file:v0 for the first save. Use in If-Match as file:v<N> when PUTting.

etag.description: Precomputed If-Match precondition value for PUT round-trips (file:v<file_version>)

proxy_permissions.description: Computer-level proxy-permissions document (only included when include_proxy_permissions=true; default document with file_version 0 when none is stored). Contains auth-group credentials.

get.description: Get a computer by ID. A project member (a collaborator at any permission level) reads a reduced view: identity, status, server and summary flags only. It never carries the SSH public key, the comment, volumes, environment fields, runtime information, proxy domains or proxy permission documents; runtime and include_proxy_domains are ignored for a member and include_proxy_permissions answers 403. A member gets no ETag.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: Include live runtime information. Accepts "true", "false", or a URL-encoded JSON string like `{"displays":true}`. An empty JSON object `{}` fetches all info. Runtime information may be up to 2 seconds old.

parameters.name: include_proxy_domains
parameters.description: Include proxy domains (aliases) for this computer. When true, adds a proxy_domains array to the computer object.

parameters.name: include_proxy_permissions
parameters.description: Include the full proxy-permissions documents (computer-level proxy_permissions and parent-project-level project_proxy_permissions) for each computer. Returns proxy authentication group configuration including credentials. Request only when explicitly needed. Auth tokens additionally require the resources.proxy_aliases permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the computer to retrieve

ETag.description: Strong ETag of the computer's editable settings (name, color, ai, autostart, ramdisk, ramdisk_scope, environment_vars, ssh_public_key, comment, realm_ids). It changes whenever one of them changes, and not when only the status does or when realm_ids only change order. It names the settings' content, so settings changed back to exactly what you read give that tag again. Send it in If-Match on PUT /computers/{id} to save only over the settings you read. Answered to the project owner and admins, never to a project member.

datacenter.description: Present for a dedicated server. Absent when the computer runs on a subserver (paid or free).

kvm_supported.description: Whether this server can give a computer /dev/kvm (run ordinary hardware-accelerated VMs). null = not known yet, or the last check is older than 1 hour. dev_kit.description: Whether dev_kit development tools are enabled

name.description: Human-readable name for the computer - must be unique within the project

color.description: HEX color for the computer (e.g., #FF0000 or FF0000). If omitted, the current color is preserved. The # prefix will be added automatically if missing, and the color will be converted to uppercase.

ai.description: Whether AI features are enabled. If omitted, the current value is preserved.

autostart.description: Whether the computer starts automatically on host boot. If omitted, the current value is preserved.

ramdisk_scope.description: Sharing scope for /ramdisk. `computer` mounts only private storage. `project` is temporarily unavailable and is refused with 400; `/ramdisk` stays private to each computer.

ramdisk.description: Whether to mount a ramdisk at /ramdisk. If omitted, the current value is preserved. Backed by a shared per-server memory pool (512 MiB by default, never more than 50% of the server memory) shared with your other computers on that server. Data survives computer restarts but is LOST on a host reboot, which is why it suits secrets and scratch data that must not persist to disk. It is RAM, so it counts against memory rather than disk.

environment_vars.description: The computer's whole set of environment variables. When sent, it replaces the stored set: a variable you leave out is removed, and {} removes them all. If omitted, the current variables are preserved. A computer response always shows {} here, so do not send back the value you read. To add or change variables and keep the rest use PUT /computers/{id}/env; to remove one use DELETE /computers/{id}/env/{key}. Keys must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` and be at most 128 characters long.

ssh_public_key.description: SSH public key for direct SSH access to this computer. Keys are globally unique - one computer per key; re-sending the same key for the same computer is a no-op (and completes an earlier change that did not finish). Set to null to REMOVE the key: direct SSH stops accepting it within about a minute, an already-open session is closed shortly after, and the key becomes installable again afterwards. An empty or whitespace-only string is rejected with 400 (send null to remove). Requires a token with the ssh-keys resource permission to set or replace; removal needs only computer update permission.

comment.description: Optional comment for the computer (max 16000 characters). Set to null to clear existing comment.

realm_ids.description: Update realm membership for this computer. Computers can have different realm membership than their parent project. A signed-in session (JWT) or an auth token without realm restrictions can modify realm_ids; realm-restricted tokens cannot change realm membership.

delete.description: Delete a computer. When this call answers, the computer's service URLs (files, terminal, `http-<port>` and the rest) already answer `404` with error code `MAPPING_NOT_FOUND`, unless the call could not confirm that with the computer's server (for example when the server cannot be reached); then they stop answering when the background removal runs. A `GET` of the computer can answer `404` before its URLs do, usually by under a second; when its server is slow or cannot be reached, until the background removal runs. The computer and its data are removed from its server in the background. Your default computer cannot be deleted (403) unless its server has expired.

post.description: Creates a copy of an existing computer. The copy operation runs asynchronously and the new computer will start automatically upon successful completion. If the copy fails, the new computer's status becomes `failed` (it cannot be started); delete it and retry the copy.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the source computer to copy

schema.title: ComputerCopied
schema.description: Computer copy initiated successfully

project_alias.description: Project alias as a helper field

ssh_hostname.description: SSH connection hostname (computed from project, computer, and server)

hoody_kit.description: Whether hoody_kit toolkit is installed in the computer

dev_kit.description: Whether dev_kit development tools are enabled

kvm.description: Whether /dev/kvm passthrough (hardware virtualization for running full VMs inside the computer) is enabled. Rented / dedicated (bare-metal) servers only; never free tier.

autostart.description: Whether the computer starts automatically on host boot

ramdisk_scope.description: Sharing scope for /ramdisk. `computer` (default) mounts only private storage. `project` additionally mounts /ramdisk/project, shared with your other computers in this project ON THE SAME SERVER (a RAM disk cannot span servers). Refused when the project has other members.

ramdisk.description: Whether to mount a ramdisk at /ramdisk. Backed by a shared per-server memory pool (512 MiB by default, never more than 50% of the server memory) shared with your other computers on that server. Data survives computer restarts but is LOST on a host reboot. Counts against memory, not disk.

is_default.description: True if this is the user's auto-provisioned default computer. Exactly one computer per user has this flag after signup.

ssh_key_fingerprint.description: OpenSSH-format fingerprint (SHA256:...) of the installed public key - the same string `ssh-keygen -lf` prints and code hosting sites display. Null when no key is installed.

ssh_key_installed_at.description: When the currently installed key was set or last replaced. Null when no key is installed, or briefly while a just-made key change is still settling.

kvm_note.description: Present when a copy-time `kvm:true` has an outcome to report. For example, KVM could not be enabled during the copy, so the copy was created with KVM off (enable it later via PUT /api/v1/computers/{id}/kvm on the stopped copy). Absent when `kvm:true` was not requested or KVM was enabled.

copy_firewall_rules.description: Whether firewall rules will be copied from source to target

copy_network_rules.description: Whether network rules/settings will be copied from source to target

post.description:
Issues a signed, portable computer authorization claim.

The returned `computer_claim` is an ED25519-signed credential that proves:
- Who the user is (sub, type)
- Which computer they are authorized for (computerId, projectId)
- Which grant asked for it: `token_id` and `scope` (the auth token's granted permission
  paths, e.g. `computers.read`) for an auth-token caller; both `null` for a login session
- When Hoody issued the authorization (iat, exp)

An auth token needs both `computers.read` and `computers.actions.exec` (403 otherwise),
because a program that accepts the claim may treat it as full access to the computer, shell included.

A computer in status `failed`, `deleting` or `deleted` cannot be authorized (409).
A computer still being set up returns 409. An expired computer also returns 409 for non-admin callers.
A quarantined computer, or one whose owner no longer has access to its server, returns 403 for non-admin callers.

Computer programs can verify this claim **offline** using Hoody's public key
at `GET /api/v1/meta/public-key`. No API round-trip is needed during verification.

A project collaborator needs edit permission. Claims are short-lived (15 minutes by default)
because an issued claim cannot be revoked: `expires_in` gives the exact lifetime in seconds.
Clients should re-call this endpoint to refresh before expiry; the refresh is refused once
the caller has lost access.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Computer ID (24-char hex)

X-Hoody-Signature.description: ED25519 signature of response body. Format: t=<unix_ts>,kid=<keyId>,path=<urlPath>,sig=<128-hex>

computer_claim.description: The signed computer authorization claim bundle.

kid.description: Key ID used to sign this claim. Look up this key from GET /api/v1/meta/public-key.

payload_b64.description: base64url-encoded JSON payload of the computer claim: claim_type, iss, sub, computerId, projectId, type, token_id, scope, iat, exp, kid.

signature_hex.description: ED25519 signature as 128 lowercase hex characters.

computer_id.description: The authorized computer ID (echo of path :id).

project_id.description: The project that owns this computer.

type.description: Network configuration type - proxy type or block for traffic blocking

proxy.description: Proxy server URL (required for non-block types; for `block`, omit it: a non-empty proxy URL is rejected), e.g. "socks5://proxy.example.com:1080". Credentials may be embedded as userinfo ("socks5://host:port") to set/replace them; omitting userinfo on an UNCHANGED endpoint preserves the stored credentials (write-only secret). The response never echoes userinfo back (see `credentials_configured`). The URL names a public host name or IPv4 address and a port from 80 to 65535; IPv6 and local, private or reserved destinations are refused with 400. A user name and password embedded in the URL may contain only letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `:`.

country.description: Optional descriptive label, at most 100 characters (a longer one is refused with 400). It is stored and returned as given; it does not select or change the proxy location.

city.description: Optional descriptive label, at most 100 characters (a longer one is refused with 400). It is stored and returned as given; it does not select or change the proxy location.

region.description: Optional descriptive label, at most 100 characters (a longer one is refused with 400). It is stored and returned as given; it does not select or change the proxy location.

comment.description: Optional comment describing the network configuration (max 1000 characters)

dns_servers.description: Custom DNS servers are not applied: any value sent (at most 4 entries) is accepted and stored as ["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8"].

post.description: Add a new ingress (inbound) firewall rule to a computer. Use this endpoint to control which traffic can reach your computer. All rules default to `state: "enabled"` if not specified. The Hoody kits (terminal, files and others) are reached over TCP on fixed ports inside the computer (by default 4, 5, 44-46, 48, 50, 55, 59-62, 74-78, 3971, 3998, 3999, 23333); a `drop` or `reject` rule covering one of them blocks the kits for traffic it matches, so the response then carries a `FIREWALL_RULE_COVERS_KIT_PORTS` entry in `warnings`. The rule is added either way. `destination_port` is required when `protocol` is `tcp` or `udp` and not allowed with `icmp4`; without it the request is refused with 400 `INVALID_RULE_DEFINITION`. How rules are evaluated: `drop` and `reject` rules are applied before `allow` rules, whatever order they were added in, and traffic no rule matches is allowed. So an `allow` rule never overrides a matching `drop` or `reject`, however specific it is (an `allow` for one host plus a `drop` for every address drops that host too), and since unmatched traffic is already allowed, `allow` rules alone restrict nothing and cannot build an allowlist. To permit only some addresses, add `drop` or `reject` rules that cover everything else (the complement ranges); `source` and `destination` take at most 512 characters per rule, so a long list is split across several rules.

The rule was still added.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid Firewall Rule
x-error-codes.description: The firewall rule definition is invalid: a field required by the protocol is missing (destination_port for TCP/UDP), a field is not allowed with the protocol (ports with icmp4, icmp_type with tcp/udp), or a value is malformed (a port outside 1-65535, a range whose first port is not lower, an address that is not IPv4 or IPv4 CIDR). `data.field` names the field. The rule was not added or changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the field named in data.field. Ports are 1-65535, ranges are written low-high, addresses are comma-separated IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges.

post.description: Add a new egress (outbound) firewall rule to a computer. Use this endpoint to control which traffic your computer can send. All rules default to `state: "enabled"` if not specified. `destination_port` is required when `protocol` is `tcp` or `udp` and not allowed with `icmp4`; without it the request is refused with 400 `INVALID_RULE_DEFINITION`. How rules are evaluated: `drop` and `reject` rules are applied before `allow` rules, whatever order they were added in, and traffic no rule matches is allowed. So an `allow` rule never overrides a matching `drop` or `reject`, however specific it is (an `allow` for one host plus a `drop` for every address drops that host too), and since unmatched traffic is already allowed, `allow` rules alone restrict nothing and cannot build an allowlist. To permit only some addresses, add `drop` or `reject` rules that cover everything else (the complement ranges); `source` and `destination` take at most 512 characters per rule, so a long list is split across several rules.

delete.description: Remove one or more egress (outbound) firewall rules. Provide filters to match specific rules, or use `all: true` to remove all egress rules. A body with no filter and no `all: true` is refused with 422 `FIREWALL_FILTER_REQUIRED`, and a body carrying a filter name this direction does not have is refused with 400 `FIREWALL_UNKNOWN_FILTER`; an omitted `state` matches rules in either state. Removal filters do not require `destination_port` when `protocol` is TCP or UDP. Not equivalent to reset - this only deletes rules and keeps the firewall active.

x-error-codes.title: Unrecognised Firewall Filter
x-error-codes.description: A remove request carried a filter this direction does not have: a misspelled name, or a field that belongs to the other direction (`destination` on ingress, `source` on egress). An unrecognised filter would be ignored, which combined with `all: true` would remove every rule in the direction. `data.unknown_filters` lists the names. Nothing was removed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct or drop the names listed in data.unknown_filters and send the request again.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid Firewall Rule
x-error-codes.description: A filter value is malformed: a port outside 1-65535, a range whose first port is not lower, ports with a protocol other than tcp or udp, or an address that is not IPv4 or IPv4 CIDR. `data.field` names the field. Nothing was removed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the field named in data.field. Ports are 1-65535, ranges are written low-high, addresses are comma-separated IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges.

put.description: Merge environment variables into the computer. Existing keys are updated, new keys are added. Keys not present in the body are left unchanged (merge semantics). Keys starting with HOODY_ are reserved and will be rejected. Propagation: vars are written to `/etc/environment` inside the computer (visible to PAM/SSH on next login) AND applied to the computer runtime environment (visible to new exec/console sessions). Already-running processes do not pick up the change until they re-exec. The response returns the whole map; for an auth token without computers.features.env_values its values are null (values_redacted: true).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Computer ID

message.description: "Environment variables updated successfully", or "No changes detected" when every value was already set.

environment_vars.description: Current environment variables (key-value pairs). Every key is listed. Each value is null when values_redacted is true.

values_redacted.description: true when this caller may not read environment variable values: an auth token without the computers.features.env_values permission. The keys are still listed, each with a null value. Always false for a logged-in session.

synced.description: Whether the change was applied AND verified inside the computer during this request. false if no changes detected or the apply is still pending (see env_sync; a pending change is applied automatically shortly after).

env_sync.description: Whether the latest environment change has been applied to this computer yet.

data.description: Sent with ENV_BLOCK_TOO_LARGE and ENV_UNREPRESENTABLE only: the size of the environment the change would leave, and the keys to fix.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid Environment Variable Key
x-error-codes.description: The environment variable key is invalid. Keys must start with a letter or underscore, contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, and must not start with HOODY_ or LD_ in any letter case (hoody_x and ld_x are refused too). A key that fits this pattern is still refused when it is a system key (for example PATH, HOME, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS or a proxy variable). The message names the rule and the key.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a key that matches [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*, does not start with HOODY_ or LD_ in any letter case, and is not a system key.

example.message: Environment variable key is forbidden (system-reserved): PATH

x-error-codes.title: Reserved Environment Variable Prefix
x-error-codes.description: Environment variable keys starting with HOODY_, in any letter case, are reserved for system use and cannot be set or deleted.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a different key name that does not start with HOODY_.

example.message: Environment variable keys starting with HOODY_ are reserved: HOODY_TOKEN

x-error-codes.title: Invalid Environment Variable Value
x-error-codes.description: The value cannot be stored as written: it contains a newline, a carriage return, a NUL byte or "#", is not well-formed Unicode, or is longer than 4096 bytes. When several values are set at once, the message ends with the key of the refused value. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Remove the characters the message names, or shorten the value.

example.message: Environment variable values cannot contain "#" (/etc/environment treats it as a comment, even inside quotes). (key: GREETING)

x-error-codes.title: Environment Too Large
x-error-codes.description: The environment the change would leave on the computer is larger than the computer can hold. `data` gives the sizes (`rendered_bytes`, `json_bytes`, `cap_bytes`), the number of variables (`entries`) and the keys with the largest values (`offending_keys`). Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Delete or shorten some variables, starting with the keys in `data.offending_keys`, then retry.

example.message: Environment block too large: 5012 rendered bytes / 4950 JSON bytes (cap 4608).

x-error-codes.title: Environment Cannot Be Applied
x-error-codes.description: The environment the change would leave on the computer holds a variable that cannot be applied (for example a stored value with a character values may not contain), or more than 256 variables. `data.offending_keys` names the variables that cannot be applied; `data` also gives `entries`, `json_bytes`, `rendered_bytes` and `cap_bytes`. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Delete or correct the variables in `data.offending_keys`, or remove variables until at most 256 remain, then retry.

example.message: Environment contains values that cannot be represented: CALLBACK_URL

schema.description: Keys must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` and be at most 128 characters long.

patch.description: Merge environment variables into the computer. Existing keys are updated, new keys are added. Keys not present in the body are left unchanged (merge semantics). Keys starting with HOODY_ are reserved and will be rejected. Propagation: vars are written to `/etc/environment` inside the computer (visible to PAM/SSH on next login) AND applied to the computer runtime environment (visible to new exec/console sessions). Already-running processes do not pick up the change until they re-exec. The response returns the whole map; for an auth token without computers.features.env_values its values are null (values_redacted: true).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Computer ID

message.description: "Environment variables updated successfully", or "No changes detected" when every value was already set.

environment_vars.description: Current environment variables (key-value pairs). Every key is listed. Each value is null when values_redacted is true.

values_redacted.description: true when this caller may not read environment variable values: an auth token without the computers.features.env_values permission. The keys are still listed, each with a null value. Always false for a logged-in session.

synced.description: Whether the change was applied AND verified inside the computer during this request. false if no changes detected or the apply is still pending (see env_sync; a pending change is applied automatically shortly after).

env_sync.description: Whether the latest environment change has been applied to this computer yet.

data.description: Sent with ENV_BLOCK_TOO_LARGE and ENV_UNREPRESENTABLE only: the size of the environment the change would leave, and the keys to fix.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid Environment Variable Key
x-error-codes.description: The environment variable key is invalid. Keys must start with a letter or underscore, contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, and must not start with HOODY_ or LD_ in any letter case (hoody_x and ld_x are refused too). A key that fits this pattern is still refused when it is a system key (for example PATH, HOME, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS or a proxy variable). The message names the rule and the key.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a key that matches [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*, does not start with HOODY_ or LD_ in any letter case, and is not a system key.

example.message: Environment variable key is forbidden (system-reserved): PATH

x-error-codes.title: Reserved Environment Variable Prefix
x-error-codes.description: Environment variable keys starting with HOODY_, in any letter case, are reserved for system use and cannot be set or deleted.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a different key name that does not start with HOODY_.

x-error-codes.resolution: Remove the characters the message names, or shorten the value.

x-error-codes.title: Environment Too Large

Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Delete or shorten some variables, starting with the keys in `data.offending_keys`, then retry.

x-error-codes.title: Environment Cannot Be Applied

get.summary: Get proxied-usage documents for a computer
get.description: Per-month proxied request counts and response bytes for one computer. The owner of the computer's project or an administrator can read this usage. A non-administrator with a shared project permission gets 403. Counts COMPLETED, ROUTED, non-excluded HTTP responses only, not forward-proxy/CONNECT egress, direct SSH, raw computer egress, or WebSocket sessions until they close. Reports live computers only; see excludes_deleted_computers. TOTALS sum the documents actually returned: they are NOT comprehensive whenever coverage_complete is false (some usage could not be read, or a month is no longer available), and they always exclude deleted computers. totals.exact is false if a sum exceeded exact integer range. Older months are kept only if they were read before they expired, so a month never queried in time may be gone permanently. A month withdrawn by an ownership change stops being served.

get.summary: Get proxied-usage documents for every computer in a project
get.description: Same measurement as the per-computer route, for every computer in the project. The project owner or an administrator can read this usage. A non-administrator with a shared project permission gets 403. Expired and suspended computers ARE included. TOTALS sum the documents actually returned: they are NOT comprehensive whenever coverage_complete is false (some usage could not be read, or a month is no longer available), and they always exclude deleted computers. totals.exact is false if a sum exceeded exact integer range. Older months are kept only if they were read before they expired, so a month never queried in time may be gone permanently. A month withdrawn by an ownership change stops being served.

get.summary: List notifications for the authenticated user
get.description: Paginated list of the notifications visible to the authenticated user (global notifications plus those targeted to them), newest first. Results are PAGINATED: page 1 is not the complete set; follow pagination.next_cursor (or increment page) to read the rest. Notification bodies carry account-security, billing and infrastructure events, so auth-token callers must hold the `resources.read_account` permission; tokens without it, and tokens restricted to realms, receive 403. JWT/owner callers are unaffected.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (offset paging). Ignored when `before` is supplied.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (max 100).

parameters.name: unread_only
parameters.description: Return only notifications the user has not read. Mutually exclusive with read_only.

parameters.name: read_only
parameters.description: Return only notifications the user HAS read (the archive half of the inbox). `pagination.total` counts the same filtered set, so it can drive page numbers directly. Mutually exclusive with unread_only (sending both is a 400, not an empty page).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Keyset cursor from a previous response's pagination.next_cursor ("<created_at>,<id>"). Prefer this over `page` for an inbox: offset paging duplicates or skips rows when a new notification arrives mid-read.

project.description: Project ID (must match path :id)

type.description: Authentication type. Required: a group without one is refused with 422.

secret.description: For type jwt. Key used to verify token signatures. HS256: a shared secret of at least 32 characters that is not a PEM key and does not contain secret, password, 123456, test, dev or default in any letter case. RS256: a PEM SPKI RSA public key of 2048 to 8192 bits with a public exponent of at most 65537. ES256: a PEM SPKI P-256 public key. A new or changed key that breaks these rules is refused with 422.

algorithm.description: Algorithm (HS256/RS256/ES256 for JWT, sha256 for password)

sources.description: For jwt, required: a non-empty array of header:<name> or cookie:<name> entries, such as ["header:Authorization", "cookie:__Host-jwt"]. For hoody-identity, optional: each entry must be header:X-Hoody-Identity-<name>.

claims.description: Required JWT claims to validate (values must be string, number, or boolean)

password.description: Password plaintext or SHA256 hex (for type: password)

salt.description: Salt for password hashing (for type: password)

range.description: IPv4 CIDR range like "10.0.0.0/8" (for type: ip)

cookie.description: Cookie name (for type: token). Must not contain U+FFFD.

param.description: Query param name (for type: token). Must not contain U+FFFD.

value.description: Token value to match (for type: token)

audience.description: REQUIRED for type: hoody-identity. The exact audience the identity claim aud must equal.

allow_types.description: Account types allowed (for type: hoody-identity). Omit to allow every signed-in Hoody account.

users.description: Optional user-id allowlist, 24-hex each (for type: hoody-identity)

max_age_seconds.description: Freshness gate on claim iat (for type: hoody-identity)

expose_type.description: Also inject X-Hoody-Identity-Type (for type: hoody-identity; default false)

header_authoritative.description: When true and any configured header source is present in the request (any value, even empty), only header sources decide membership. When false or omitted, any configured source with a valid token counts (for type: jwt).

groups.description: Authentication groups. Key is group name (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,50}$), value is group config.

anyOf.description: ACCESS RULE: true = allow all instances/ports, false = deny all
ACCESS RULE: Allow only this specific port/index number (e.g., 22 means "only port 22 is allowed")
ACCESS RULE: Allow only these specific port/index numbers (e.g., [80, 443] means "only ports 80 and 443 are allowed")
ACCESS RULE: Allow port/index range (e.g., "8000-8100" means "ports 8000 through 8100 are allowed")
ACCESS RULE: Wildcard "*" = allow all instances (same as true)

additionalProperties.description: Program-level access control rules. Key is the canonical program name (terminal, files, exec, etc.); a short alias such as t or f is refused with 422 naming the canonical name. Value defines WHICH instances/ports are ALLOWED, NOT which exist. For `http` and `https`, name the ports: a bare true, false or "*" is refused with 422, and one cell may open at most 16384 ports. `logs` takes a boolean only, like files, services, notifications and exec.

permissions.description: Per-group program permissions. Key is group name, value is map of program→access-rule. These are ACCESS CONTROL rules defining WHAT IS ALLOWED, not inventory of what exists.

default.description: Default access policy when no rules match (defaults to "deny" if omitted)

enable_proxy.description: Enable or disable the proxy. Defaults to true.

hooks.description: Not accepted: hooks are computer-level only. A project document that carries this field is refused with 422; set hooks on each computer instead.

project.description: Project ID (must match path :id)

type.description: Authentication type. Required: a group without one is refused with 422.

secret.description: For type jwt. Key used to verify token signatures. HS256: a shared secret of at least 32 characters that is not a PEM key and does not contain secret, password, 123456, test, dev or default in any letter case. RS256: a PEM SPKI RSA public key of 2048 to 8192 bits with a public exponent of at most 65537. ES256: a PEM SPKI P-256 public key. A new or changed key that breaks these rules is refused with 422.

algorithm.description: Algorithm (HS256/RS256/ES256 for JWT, sha256 for password)

sources.description: For jwt, required: a non-empty array of header:<name> or cookie:<name> entries, such as ["header:Authorization", "cookie:__Host-jwt"]. For hoody-identity, optional: each entry must be header:X-Hoody-Identity-<name>.

claims.description: Required JWT claims to validate (values must be string, number, or boolean)

password.description: Password plaintext or SHA256 hex (for type: password)

salt.description: Salt for password hashing (for type: password)

range.description: IPv4 CIDR range like "10.0.0.0/8" (for type: ip)

cookie.description: Cookie name (for type: token). Must not contain U+FFFD.

param.description: Query param name (for type: token). Must not contain U+FFFD.

value.description: Token value to match (for type: token)

audience.description: REQUIRED for type: hoody-identity. The exact audience the identity claim aud must equal.

allow_types.description: Account types allowed (for type: hoody-identity). Omit to allow every signed-in Hoody account.

users.description: Optional user-id allowlist, 24-hex each (for type: hoody-identity)

max_age_seconds.description: Freshness gate on claim iat (for type: hoody-identity)

expose_type.description: Also inject X-Hoody-Identity-Type (for type: hoody-identity; default false)

header_authoritative.description: When true and any configured header source is present in the request (any value, even empty), only header sources decide membership. When false or omitted, any configured source with a valid token counts (for type: jwt).

groups.description: Authentication groups. Key is group name (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,50}$), value is group config.

anyOf.description: ACCESS RULE: true = allow all instances/ports, false = deny all
ACCESS RULE: Allow only this specific port/index number (e.g., 22 means "only port 22 is allowed")
ACCESS RULE: Allow only these specific port/index numbers (e.g., [80, 443] means "only ports 80 and 443 are allowed")
ACCESS RULE: Allow port/index range (e.g., "8000-8100" means "ports 8000 through 8100 are allowed")
ACCESS RULE: Wildcard "*" = allow all instances (same as true)

additionalProperties.description: Program-level access control rules. Key is the canonical program name (terminal, files, exec, etc.); a short alias such as t or f is refused with 422 naming the canonical name. delete.description: Remove all proxy access control configuration from a project. Publication can remain pending or fail. propagation.state "applied" means publication completed; it does not confirm proxy enforcement. patch.description: Enable or disable the proxy for a project. Disabling is a kill-switch, not a bypass: while enable_proxy is false, new requests that reach the proxy permission layer are denied with 403, evaluated before authentication groups, permission rules and the default policy, so no configured rule can re-open access while it is off. Computers keep running; only proxy reachability is cut. The project value applies to every computer that does not set enable_proxy itself; a computer document that sets enable_proxy true or false overrides it. A full-document replacement that omits computer enable_proxy leaves it unset. Granular updates preserve fields they do not change. Computers saved before this behaviour usually carry an explicit true and stay on while the project is off; send enable_proxy null to the computer-level endpoint to make such a computer follow the project again, or false to disable it.

project.description: Project ID owning this computer

type.description: Authentication type. Required: a group without one is refused with 422.

secret.description: For type jwt. Key used to verify token signatures. HS256: a shared secret of at least 32 characters that is not a PEM key and does not contain secret, password, 123456, test, dev or default in any letter case. RS256: a PEM SPKI RSA public key of 2048 to 8192 bits with a public exponent of at most 65537. ES256: a PEM SPKI P-256 public key. A new or changed key that breaks these rules is refused with 422.

sources.description: For jwt, required: a non-empty array of header:<name> or cookie:<name> entries, such as ["header:Authorization", "cookie:__Host-jwt"]. For hoody-identity, optional: each entry must be header:X-Hoody-Identity-<name>.

claims.description: Required JWT claims to validate (values must be string, number, or boolean)

password.description: Password plaintext or SHA256 hex (for type: password)

cookie.description: Cookie name (for type: token). Must not contain U+FFFD.

param.description: Query param name (for type: token). Must not contain U+FFFD.

value.description: Token value to match (for type: token)

audience.description: REQUIRED for type: hoody-identity. The exact audience the identity claim aud must equal.

allow_types.description: Account types allowed (for type: hoody-identity). Omit to allow every signed-in Hoody account.

users.description: Optional user-id allowlist, 24-hex each (for type: hoody-identity)

additionalProperties.description: Program-level access control rules. secret.description: Key used to verify token signatures. HS256: a shared secret of at least 32 characters that is not a PEM key and does not contain secret, password, 123456, test, dev or default in any letter case. RS256: a PEM SPKI RSA public key of 2048 to 8192 bits with a public exponent of at most 65537. ES256: a PEM SPKI P-256 public key. A new or changed key that breaks these rules is refused with 422.

algorithm.description: JWT algorithm to use for signature verification. HS256 uses symmetric keys, RS256/ES256 use asymmetric keys.

sources.description: Where to look for JWT tokens in incoming requests. Format: "header:Name" or "cookie:Name" ("param:Name" is no longer accepted). By default a valid token in any listed source counts (see header_authoritative). Name cookie sources with the __Host- prefix.

items.description: Token source location. Examples: "header:Authorization", "cookie:__Host-jwt"

claims.description: Optional JWT claims that must be present and match exactly. Values must be string, number, or boolean.

header_authoritative.description: When true and any configured header source is present in the request (any value, even empty), only header sources decide membership. When false or omitted, any configured source with a valid token counts.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with a request-limit refusal when the allowance is used up.

secret.description: Key used to verify token signatures. HS256: a shared secret of at least 32 characters that is not a PEM key and does not contain secret, password, 123456, test, dev or default in any letter case. RS256: a PEM SPKI RSA public key of 2048 to 8192 bits with a public exponent of at most 65537. ES256: a PEM SPKI P-256 public key. A new or changed key that breaks these rules is refused with 422.

algorithm.description: JWT algorithm to use for signature verification. HS256 uses symmetric keys, RS256/ES256 use asymmetric keys.

sources.description: Where to look for JWT tokens in incoming requests. Format: "header:Name" or "cookie:Name" ("param:Name" is no longer accepted). By default a valid token in any listed source counts (see header_authoritative). Name cookie sources with the __Host- prefix.

items.description: Token source location. Examples: "header:Authorization", "cookie:__Host-jwt"

claims.description: Optional JWT claims that must be present and match exactly. Values must be string, number, or boolean.

header_authoritative.description: When true and any configured header source is present in the request (any value, even empty), only header sources decide membership. When false or omitted, any configured source with a valid token counts.

project.description: Project ID this document belongs to

groups.description: Authentication groups configuration (jwt/password/ip/token or OR-arrays). Contains credentials. A document can hold at most 256 groups and 1 MiB; one already over either limit can be edited and reduced but not grown.

permissions.description: Per-group program access rules (defines WHICH instances are ALLOWED)

default.description: Default access policy for requests matching no group. A project document has allow or deny. A computer document has allow or deny when it overrides the project, or inherit when the project default applies (allow when the project has no rules).

enable_proxy.description: Whether the reverse proxy is enabled for this entity. Always present on a project document (true unless it was switched off). On a computer document it is present only when the computer sets it; when absent, the project value applies (true when the project does not set it either).

file_version.description: Monotonic write counter. 0 = no stored document yet OR a document saved before versioning existed; either way use If-Match: file:v0 for the first save. Use in If-Match as file:v<N> when PUTting.

etag.description: Precomputed If-Match precondition value for PUT round-trips (file:v<file_version>)

propagation.description: Publication status of this setting. `applied` means publication completed; it does not confirm that the proxy already enforces it. Changes can take several seconds or longer to take effect.

committed.description: false for reads and true for successful write requests.

complete.description: True when publication finished for every current target; it does not confirm proxy enforcement.

retained_count.description: Earlier publication targets kept outside the current target set.

project.description: Project ID this document belongs to

groups.description: Authentication groups configuration (jwt/password/ip/token or OR-arrays). Contains credentials. A document can hold at most 256 groups and 1 MiB; one already over either limit can be edited and reduced but not grown.

permissions.description: Per-group program access rules (defines WHICH instances are ALLOWED)

default.description: Default access policy for requests matching no group. A project document has allow or deny. A computer document has allow or deny when it overrides the project, or inherit when the project default applies (allow when the project has no rules).

enable_proxy.description: Whether the reverse proxy is enabled for this entity. Always present on a project document (true unless it was switched off). On a computer document it is present only when the computer sets it; when absent, the project value applies (true when the project does not set it either).

hooks.description: Per-service proxy hook arrays (computer-level documents only)

schema_version.description: Document format version; absent for documents saved in the older format

file_version.description: Monotonic write counter. 0 = no stored document yet OR a document saved before versioning existed; either way use If-Match: file:v0 for the first save. Use in If-Match as file:v<N> when PUTting.

etag.description: Precomputed If-Match precondition value for PUT round-trips (file:v<file_version>)

propagation.description: Publication status of this setting. `applied` means publication completed; it does not confirm that the proxy already enforces it. Changes can take several seconds or longer to take effect.

committed.description: false for reads and true for successful write requests.

complete.description: True when publication finished for every current target; it does not confirm proxy enforcement.

action.description: The latest recorded action: `upsert` or `delete`; `unknown` if no action is recorded. The field may be absent if status is unavailable.

retained_count.description: Earlier publication targets kept outside the current target set.

401.description: Unauthorized: no credentials, or credentials that are invalid or expired

x-error-codes.title: Authentication token missing
x-error-codes.description: The request carries no Authorization header, or the header holds no token
x-error-codes.resolution: Send an Authorization header as "Bearer <token>" with a sign-in token or an auth token

x-error-codes.title: Invalid authentication token
x-error-codes.description: The provided authentication token is malformed or invalid
x-error-codes.resolution: Obtain a new token by logging in again or using a valid auth token

x-error-codes.title: Authentication token expired
x-error-codes.description: The sign-in token (JWT) has expired. An expired auth token is refused with INVALID_TOKEN instead.
x-error-codes.resolution: Sign in again, or refresh the session.

x-error-codes.title: Parent auth token no longer valid
x-error-codes.description: The auth token was created by another auth token, and that token (or one above it) has been revoked, disabled or has expired, so this one no longer authenticates
x-error-codes.resolution: Create a new auth token from a valid one, or sign in again

x-error-codes.title: Invalid credentials
x-error-codes.description: The provided username/email or password is incorrect
x-error-codes.resolution: Verify your credentials and try again, or use the password reset feature

x-error-codes.title: Email not verified
x-error-codes.description: The password is correct but the account's email address is not verified yet. It is only returned after the password has been checked. On the login endpoint the response carries data.email, so the client can offer to resend the verification link. HTTP Basic authentication returns it on any operation, without the email.
x-error-codes.resolution: Complete email verification by clicking the link sent to your inbox, or call POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification to receive a new link, or complete a password reset, which also verifies the email.

example.message: Email not verified. Please check your inbox or request a new verification link.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid OTP code
x-error-codes.description: The provided 2FA code is incorrect or has expired
x-error-codes.resolution: Generate a new code from your authenticator app and try again

403.description: Forbidden: the credentials do not allow this operation

x-error-codes.title: Insufficient permissions
x-error-codes.description: You do not have the required permissions to perform this action
x-error-codes.resolution: Ask the resource owner to grant you access

x-error-codes.title: Account banned
x-error-codes.description: Your account has been banned and cannot access this resource
x-error-codes.resolution: Contact support for information about your account status

data.description: Additional error details, when the refusal has any.

x-error-codes.title: Computer not found
x-error-codes.description: The computer does not exist, or the caller is a project collaborator outside the computer's server pool. The message names the computer ID. Other permission refusals are 403. The response's `error` is `Not Found`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the ID or name. List the resource first if unsure.

x-error-codes.title: Project not found
x-error-codes.description: The project (of the computer, for a computer route) does not exist. The message names the project ID. The response's `error` is `Not Found`; this code is not sent.
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the ID or name. List the resource first if unsure.

data.description: Sent when the version is stale: `current_version` (the stored file_version) and `client_sent` (the If-Match value read). Absent when the header is malformed.

x-error-codes.title: Version precondition failed
x-error-codes.description: Nothing was written. Either If-Match is not a strong validator of the form file:v<N> (message "If-Match must be a strong validator of the form file:v<N> (weak W/"..." forms rejected)", no `data`), or the document changed since the version it names (message "etag_mismatch", or "File version mismatch" when the whole document is deleted, with `data.current_version` and `data.client_sent`).
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the document again, re-apply your change to what you read, and retry with its etag in If-Match.

422.description: The body does not match the request schema, or the range is not a valid IPv4 CIDR range.

schema.description: The body does not match the request schema, or the range is not a valid IPv4 CIDR range.

data.description: The failing checks, when there are any: one entry per problem, each with a path and a message.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid group or access value
x-error-codes.description: The body does not match the request schema, or the range is not a valid IPv4 CIDR range.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the value named in the message and send the request again.

example.message: Invalid proxy permissions: range must be valid IPv4 CIDR like 10.0.0.0/8

data.description: Additional error details, when the refusal has any.

x-error-codes.title: If-Match required
x-error-codes.description: The write must name the document version it was built from in an If-Match header (file:v<N>, the etag of the last read). Nothing was written.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the document, then resend the write with If-Match set to its etag.

example.message: If-Match header is required. Read the current file_version with GET first.

429.description: Too Many Requests: a request limit of this operation is used up

x-error-codes.title: Rate limit exceeded
x-error-codes.description: Too many requests of this kind in a short time, counted per account, auth token or address. The request was not carried out. The body's `error` is `Too Many Requests`.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this endpoint. Please try again later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with a request-limit refusal when the allowance is used up.

range.description: IPv4 CIDR range specifying allowed IP addresses. Format: "IP/mask" where mask is 0-32. Examples: "192.168.1.0/24" (subnet), "10.0.0.0/8" (class A), "203.0.113.5/32" (single IP).

post.description: Create a custom domain alias for a computer to mask its real Project ID and Computer ID in shared links. Instead of sharing https://{projectId}-{computerId}.{server_name}.computers.hoody.com/, you can share https://{alias}.{server_name}.computers.hoody.com/. You can provide a custom alias (3-61 chars) or let the system auto-generate a 48-character hex string for maximum obscurity.

computer_id.description: Target computer ID

program.description: Program or protocol the alias targets

target_path.description: Landing path served for root requests, with its own query. With allow_path_override true, requests carrying their own path are forwarded as-sent (never a prefix); with false, it is the only path served.

allow_path_override.description: When false, only the root, or target_path itself, is served, as target_path; other paths 404, and target_path's own parameters cannot be overridden. When true, a request that carries its own path is forwarded as sent.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiration date

enabled.description: Whether the alias is active

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 last modification timestamp

server_id.description: ID of the server resource you own. For computers on a subserver, this is the subserver ID; for computers on a physical host, this is the physical server ID.

server_name.description: Routable hostname label for URL construction. Always the physical (parent) server name, even for subserver computers.

computer_id.description: Computer ID that this alias points to. You must own this computer.

alias.description: Custom alias name (a-z, 0-9, hyphens only, 3-61 chars, cannot start/end with hyphen) OR null/false for auto-generated 48-char hex. Two independent uniqueness rules apply, either of which answers 409 ALIAS_IN_USE: the name must be free on the computer's physical server (across every tenant hosted there), AND your own account may hold a given name only once across all servers. A different account can reuse your name on a different server; you cannot. Reserved and rejected: the exact label "computers" (an infrastructure label of the computer proxy domain), and anything equal to a reserved service name (such as "egress") or starting with that name followed by "-" (such as "egress-"). Distinct labels such as "computers-my-app" and "egressmyapp" are allowed. A name another account released in the last 90 days on the same physical server, or from a computer that was deleted, is also refused with 409 ALIAS_IN_USE.

program.description: Which computer service the alias targets: a built-in Hoody program ("terminal", "files", "code", "browser", "display", …) or a transport protocol ("http", "https", "ssh"). To point an alias at an HTTP server you run yourself inside the computer (a process started via the daemon, a dev server, anything listening on a TCP port) use program "http" (or "https" for a TLS backend) and give the port via the "port" field (e.g. program "http" + port 3000 forwards to http://<computer>:3000). A port is required for "http"/"https": without one the request is refused (400 PORT_REQUIRED). The combined "http-3000" form and the "index"-as-port form also work; when more than one is supplied the order of authority is port > the port embedded in "http-<port>" > index, so a leftover/default index can never override a real port. Must be a known Hoody program name (or one of its aliases) or protocol.

port.description: Target port for the "http"/"https" protocol: the port your server listens on inside the computer (e.g. program "http" + port 3000 → http://<computer>:3000). Preferred, unambiguous way to point an alias at a raw HTTP/HTTPS server; takes precedence over "index" and over any port embedded in the program string ("http-3000"). Ignored for built-in Hoody programs, which have fixed kit ports.

index.description: Instance index, or target port for the "http"/"https" protocol. For a built-in Hoody program it selects which running instance to route to (e.g. terminal 2) and defaults to 1. For "http"/"https" it is the port your server listens on inside the computer and has no default: give it here, in "port" or as "http-<port>", or the request is refused (400 PORT_REQUIRED), but prefer the dedicated "port" field; if "port" or a port embedded in the program ("http-3000") is also supplied, that wins over this index (so an accidental index of 1 will not route you to port 1).

target_path.description: Landing path served when https://{alias}.../ is requested with no path (a root request); a query written in it is sent too. With allow_path_override true, a request that carries its own path is forwarded as-sent, resolved from the computer root, and this value is never used as a prefix. With allow_path_override false, it is the only path the alias serves. Auto-prefixed with / if missing.

allow_path_override.description: When false, the alias serves only the root, or target_path itself: once the proxy permissions allow the request, a request to either lands on target_path and any other path is refused (404). A parameter written in target_path always keeps its value, the visitor's other parameters are passed on, and the method, request body and WebSocket upgrade are forwarded as sent. When true (the default), a root request lands on target_path with its query plus the visitor's parameters, and a request that carries its own path is forwarded as sent. Either way anyone who has the link can open the alias: use proxy permissions to restrict who may.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO 8601 expiration date in the future, or null for none; a date that is not in the future is refused with 400. The alias is disabled automatically after this date.

enabled.description: Whether the alias is initially enabled (defaults to true)

post.summary: Point a Bot URL at another computer
post.description: Moves the URL to a Bot in another computer you own (for example after copying the computer). Same label and keys. The destination server's limit is checked when the move adds the URL to that server (from another server, or a detached URL); a move between computers on the same server keeps the URL's place there while it holds one. A detached URL is attached again, and its state is then derived from its other facts (an owner switch that is off or a suspension still applies). Needs `otp_code` when your account requires 2FA for API keys: the URL's keys then reach the new Bot. Owner only: the project owner (or an administrator); project members are refused. Auth tokens need resources.bot_urls.
