post.description: Opens a ticket with its first message. Use it for one distinct problem (a bug, a billing or account question); add to an existing ticket with POST /api/v1/support/tickets/{id}/messages instead of opening a second one about the same thing. Cost: one ticket against `open`, `tickets_day`, `tickets_30d` and `retained`, and one message against `messages_day` (GET /api/v1/support/limits shows them). Subject: one line, up to 200 characters. Body: up to 4,000 characters and 200 lines. Send `client_key` to make a retry safe. The same subject, category and message within 60 seconds of a ticket that is not closed is refused (409 SUPPORT_DUPLICATE, naming the saved ticket) and spends no ticket or message limit. Support never asks for passwords, one-time codes or keys: never put them in a ticket. Then poll GET /api/v1/support/tickets/changes for the reply. A reached account limit answers 409 SUPPORT_QUOTA_REACHED with `data: {limit, tier, retry_after_s}`: `limit` is open, tickets_day, tickets_30d, messages_day or retained, `tier` is free, paid or banned, and `retry_after_s` (when present) is how long until the limit frees itself. Read GET /api/v1/support/limits first instead of probing. A refused text answers 400 SUPPORT_TEXT_INVALID with `data: {field, rule, at, index}`: `field` is subject or body, `at` is `input` (as sent) or `cleaned` (after cleaning), `index` is the character offset, and the text is never repeated. Rules: lone_surrogate, nul, escape, c0_control, c1_control (control characters); bidi_control, invisible_char, tag_char (characters that hide or reorder text); private_use, noncharacter; combining_flood (too many marks on one character); multiline (a line break in the subject); empty (nothing visible); too_long, too_many_lines, line_too_long (size). Harmless noise is cleaned instead of refused (line endings, zero-width characters, trailing spaces, Unicode normalisation) and listed in `cleaned`. Your own account only, on the base API host: HTTP Basic, impersonation and realm-scoped requests are refused, and auth tokens need resources.support and must not be limited to realms. Staff, admin and platform accounts cannot use support tickets.

get.description: The way to wait for a reply. Tickets that changed since `since`, oldest change first, each once in its newest state. Polling flow: (1) call it once without `since`: it returns no rows, only the current position in `next_since`; (2) every 60 seconds, call it with the last `next_since`; (3) for each returned ticket whose `unread` is true, read it with GET /api/v1/support/tickets/{id} (that also marks it read); (4) when `has_more` is true, call again at once. `next_since` is opaque and belongs to your account: store it as it is, never build or edit it, and never reuse another account's. When nothing of yours changed you get the same value back. A 422 INVALID_CURSOR means the position is no longer accepted: start again without `since`. Cost: one read against the per-account read limit (600 a minute by default); no ticket or message limit. Your own account only, on the base API host: HTTP Basic, impersonation and realm-scoped requests are refused, and auth tokens need resources.support and must not be limited to realms. Staff, admin and platform accounts cannot use support tickets.

post.description: Adds your message to one of your tickets: answer support, or add details about the same problem. A reply to a ticket closed less than 30 days ago reopens it; an older or terminal ticket answers 409 SUPPORT_TICKET_EXPIRED or SUPPORT_TICKET_FULL (open a new one). Up to 50 of your messages per ticket (409 SUPPORT_TICKET_LIMIT). Cost: one message against `messages_day`; a reopen also counts against `open`. Send `client_key` to make a retry safe. Repeating your own latest message on a ticket that is not closed, within 60 seconds, is refused (409 SUPPORT_DUPLICATE, naming the saved message) and spends no message limit. Never include passwords, one-time codes or keys. A reached account limit answers 409 SUPPORT_QUOTA_REACHED with `data: {limit, tier, retry_after_s}`: for a reply `limit` is messages_day, or open when the reply reopens a closed ticket; `tier` is free, paid or banned, and `retry_after_s` (when present) is how long until the limit frees itself. Read GET /api/v1/support/limits first instead of probing. A refused text answers 400 SUPPORT_TEXT_INVALID with `data: {field, rule, at, index}`: `field` is subject or body, `at` is `input` (as sent) or `cleaned` (after cleaning), `index` is the character offset, and the text is never repeated. Rules: lone_surrogate, nul, escape, c0_control, c1_control (control characters); bidi_control, invisible_char, tag_char (characters that hide or reorder text); private_use, noncharacter; combining_flood (too many marks on one character); multiline (a line break in the subject); empty (nothing visible); too_long, too_many_lines, line_too_long (size). Harmless noise is cleaned instead of refused (line endings, zero-width characters, trailing spaces, Unicode normalisation) and listed in `cleaned`. Your own account only, on the base API host: HTTP Basic, impersonation and realm-scoped requests are refused, and auth tokens need resources.support and must not be limited to realms. Staff, admin and platform accounts cannot use support tickets.

get.description: Get the shares targeting this computer (direct shares and project-level shares): what storage this computer is configured to receive. Only enabled shares are listed; disabled, expired and self-shares are left out. An active direct share takes priority over a project share of the same path; a failed one gives way to it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Computer ID

items.title: IncomingStorageShare

source_computer_id.description: Computer ID that owns the source directory

source_path.description:
Absolute path in the source computer. The source computer controls WHAT to share (this path), NOT WHERE it appears in targets: Hoody sets that once, at create, and returns it as mount_path. Users cannot choose a mount location.

At most 1000 characters. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 / - _ . ( ). The path is normalized (repeated slashes collapse). Refused: `.` or `..` segments, any name containing `..`, null bytes, the root (/), /hoody, and paths at or below /proc, /sys, /dev, /boot, /run, /var/run, /hoody/shares and /hoody/containers. Returns the normalized canonical path.

Examples of ALLOWED paths:
  ✅ /home/user/data - User home directories
  ✅ /opt/application/files - Application software
  ✅ /var/lib/app/shared - Application state data
  ✅ /data/team-files - Custom data paths

Examples of BLOCKED paths:
  ❌ /proc/* - Kernel interfaces, process memory
  ❌ /sys/* - Hardware interfaces, kernel parameters
  ❌ /dev/* - Device files, raw disk/memory access
  ❌ /boot/* - Boot files, kernel images
  ❌ /run/* - Runtime secrets, sockets
  ❌ ../etc - Path traversal attempts
  ❌ /proc/../etc - Bypass attempts via normalization

mount_path.description: Where the share appears inside each receiving computer: /hoody/shares/<name>-<suffix>, where <name> is the last folder of source_path and <suffix> is 8 to 16 hex digits. Set once when the share is created and never changed; it cannot be set or edited.

target_project_id.description: Target project ID for project-wide share (auto-mounts on ALL computers in project). Mutually exclusive with target_computer_id.

target_type.description: Share target type: "computer" for 1:1 share, "project" for project-wide (all computers)

mode.description: Mount mode: "readonly" (read-only access) or "readwrite" (full read-write access)

enabled.description: Creator-controlled: Whether the share is enabled (default: true). Disabled shares are kept but are not mounted.

status.description: Share status: "active" (set up and working), "failed" (could not be set up or mounted; see status_message)

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) when share expires and is auto-deleted. Null = never expires.

created_by.description: User ID who created the share

created_at.description: ISO 8601 date when share was created

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 date when share was last updated

items.description:
Incoming shares (receiver view) exclude creator's organizational fields (alias, label, description) and the expiry-notification flag (expiry_notified).
          
DEDUPLICATION: When same source_path from same source_computer appears in both direct and project shares, the direct share takes priority while its status is active. A direct share whose status is failed gives way to the project share, which is the one mounted.

FILTERING: Automatically excludes self-shares and expired shares.

patch.description: Enable or disable mounting of an incoming share. Allows target computer owner to accept/reject incoming shares. Both creator's enabled flag and receiver's mount flag must be true for the share to be mounted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target computer ID (receiver computer)

parameters.name: shareId
parameters.description: Share ID to toggle

source_computer_id.description: Computer ID that owns the source directory

mount_path.description: Where the share appears inside each receiving computer: /hoody/shares/<name>-<suffix>, where <name> is the last folder of source_path and <suffix> is 8 to 16 hex digits. Set once when the share is created and never changed; it cannot be set or edited.

source_path.description:
Absolute path in the source computer. The source computer controls WHAT to share (this path), NOT WHERE it appears in targets: Hoody sets that once, at create, and returns it as mount_path. Users cannot choose a mount location.

At most 1000 characters. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 / - _ . ( ). The path is normalized (repeated slashes collapse). Refused: `.` or `..` segments, any name containing `..`, null bytes, the root (/), /hoody, and paths at or below /proc, /sys, /dev, /boot, /run, /var/run, /hoody/shares and /hoody/containers. Returns the normalized canonical path.

Examples of ALLOWED paths:
  ✅ /home/user/data - User home directories
  ✅ /opt/application/files - Application software
  ✅ /var/lib/app/shared - Application state data
  ✅ /data/team-files - Custom data paths

Examples of BLOCKED paths:
  ❌ /proc/* - Kernel interfaces, process memory
  ❌ /sys/* - Hardware interfaces, kernel parameters
  ❌ /dev/* - Device files, raw disk/memory access
  ❌ /boot/* - Boot files, kernel images
  ❌ /run/* - Runtime secrets, sockets
  ❌ ../etc - Path traversal attempts
  ❌ /proc/../etc - Bypass attempts via normalization

get.summary: Get Hoody API Signing Public Key
get.description:
Returns the ED25519 public key(s) used by Hoody to sign API responses
(X-Hoody-Signature header; empty and streamed responses carry no signature), identity claims issued at login, and computer
authorization claims.

**Third-party verification flow:**
1. Fetch this endpoint once (cache for 24h+)
2. Locate the key by `kid` from the `keys[]` array
3. For response signatures: parse `X-Hoody-Signature: t=<ts>,kid=<id>,m=<method>,s=<status>,path=<url>,sig=<hex>`
   and verify sig against the newline-joined tuple `${t}\n${method}\n${status}\n${path}\n${responseBody}`
4. For identity/computer claims: verify `claim.signature_hex` against `claim.payload_b64` bytes
5. If `kid` in a signature/claim does not match any cached key, re-fetch this endpoint.

No authentication required. This endpoint is intentionally public.

X-Hoody-Signature.description: ED25519 signature of the response. Format: t=<unix_ts>,kid=<keyId>,m=<method>,s=<status>,path=<urlPath>,sig=<128-hex>; signed data is the newline-joined t/method/status/path/body tuple

keys.description: JWKS-style array of active signing keys. Currently one key; supports multiple during rotation.

kid.description: Key identifier. Treat it as an opaque string and pick the key whose kid matches when verifying.

public_key_hex.description: 32-byte ED25519 public key as 64 lowercase hex characters.

public_key_b64url.description: Same key as base64url (URL-safe, no padding).

active_kid.description: The kid of the currently active signing key. New signatures will use this key.

signing_format.description: Reference documentation for the signing formats.

response_header.description: Format of the X-Hoody-Signature response header.

response_signed_data.description: Data that is signed for response headers: the newline-joined tuple of timestamp, method, status, path, and body.

identity_claim_signed_data.description: Data that is signed for identity claims (same format as computer claims).
identity_claim_signed_data.example: base64url(JSON.stringify(claim_payload)) — the b64url string itself (UTF-8 bytes)

computer_claim_signed_data.description: Data that is signed for computer claims (same format as identity claims).

replay_tolerance_seconds.description: Recommended maximum age (|now - t|) in seconds for response signature freshness checks.

503.description: Response signing is not available right now.

schema.description: Response signing is not available right now.

get.description:
Returns counters for the public Hoody social channels: GitHub stars,
Telegram members, Discord members (total + currently online), X followers,
and LinkedIn followers.

Counters may lag behind their source channels. When a channel cannot be read,
its last known value is kept.

A field is `null` when no value is known for it yet, or when the counter is
not being shown. A field that had a number can become `null` later, so
handle `null` on every call.

No authentication required.

github.description: GitHub repository star count. Null when no value is known yet.

telegram.description: Telegram channel/group member count. Null when no value is known yet.

get.description:
A small, flat key/value map that Hoody publishes for its website and for anything else that
needs current public platform facts.

**Flat by contract.** Every value is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean or null). There are
no nested objects and no arrays, and keys cannot contain dots, so the shape of the response is
always one level deep.

Keys with a default value are always present, and further keys may appear at any time. A
value can change at any time but a key with a default value never disappears.

Served with `Cache-Control: no-store` so a change is visible immediately. Fetch it
once per page and share the result rather than per component.

No authentication required. Every value here is public.

data.description: Additional error details

x-error-codes.title: Plan not available
x-error-codes.description: The plan version is retired, hidden or unknown, so it cannot be bought or upgraded to. Nothing was charged. `data.plan_id` names the plan that was asked for.
x-error-codes.resolution: Pick a plan from GET /api/v1/subserver-plans.

x-error-codes.title: Plan change is not an upgrade
x-error-codes.description: A plan change must keep or raise every resource. `data.lower_fields` lists the resources the target plan would lower (`ai_allowance` for its Free AI allowance). Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: To go smaller, buy a smaller subserver, move your data, then cancel the bigger one.

example.message: A plan change must keep or raise every resource. To go smaller, buy a smaller subserver.

x-error-codes.title: Billing period has ended
x-error-codes.description: The subscription is paid only up to `data.paid_through`, which has passed, so an upgrade has nothing left to prorate. Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Renew or pay the subscription first, then upgrade.

example.message: This billing period has ended. Renew first, then upgrade.

x-error-codes.title: Nothing to pay
x-error-codes.description: The subscription is in a state where a payment has no effect (`data.state`), or it is closed. Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the subscription. A held subscription can be paid until its deletion starts. A deleted one cannot. An active one renews by itself.

example.message: This subscription has nothing to pay right now.

x-error-codes.title: Subserver is being wiped
x-error-codes.description: The subserver is being permanently deleted; the subscription can no longer be paid for. Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: None. Contact support.

example.message: This subserver's unpaid hold has ended and it is being permanently deleted. It can no longer be paid for. Nothing was charged.

x-error-codes.title: No host has room
x-error-codes.description: No host open for paid subservers has room for this plan, or the host of this subserver has no room for the upgrade. Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Try again later or pick a smaller plan.

example.message: No host has room for this subserver right now. Nothing was charged; try again later or pick a smaller plan.

x-error-codes.title: Host unavailable
x-error-codes.description: The host of this subserver is not ready, so it cannot be changed or resumed now. Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Try again later.

example.message: The host of this subserver is not available right now. Nothing was charged; try again later.

x-error-codes.title: Paid subserver limit reached
x-error-codes.description: The account already has as many paid subservers as its limit allows. `data.max` is the limit and `data.used` the paid subservers counted toward it. Nothing was charged. `data.used` is omitted for a token limited to realms (it counts every realm of the account).
x-error-codes.resolution: Contact support to raise the limit. GET /api/v1/users/me shows the limit and the count under limits.paid_subservers (full account view only).

x-error-codes.title: Subserver is not active
x-error-codes.description: The computer is on a paid subserver whose subscription is not active (on hold, being delivered, or being deleted) or has a change in progress, so computers on it cannot be created, started, stopped, changed, copied, shared or deleted. `data.reason` is `not_active`, `operation_in_flight` or `no_subscription`. Nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry once the subserver is active again (renew a held subscription, or wait for the change to finish).

example.message: This subserver is not active: its subscription is on hold, being delivered, or a change to it is in progress. Try again once it is active.

x-error-codes.title: Idempotency key reused for a different purchase
x-error-codes.description: The supplied idempotency_key was already used for a reservation with different terms: a different offer, duration, pool or confirmed total. Returning the original would silently give the caller something other than what this request asked for, so it fails instead.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a fresh idempotency_key for a genuinely new purchase.

example.message: That idempotency key was used for a different reservation.

x-error-codes.title: The total must be confirmed before money moves
x-error-codes.description: The request would debit an account and carried no max_charge_cents, so there was nothing to bind the quoted price to the charged one. Nothing was charged. This applies to every paid purchase, including servers with no one-time setup fee. The fee is a separate thing, and its absence never meant the total did not need confirming.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the current total, show it to the customer, and retry with max_charge_cents set to the value they confirmed. Never auto-retry with the total from this error: that defeats the confirmation it exists to obtain.

example.message: Please confirm the total before proceeding.

resources.description: Resources of this plan version. Units match the server fields of the same name.

x-error-codes.resolution: Try again later or pick a smaller plan.

x-error-codes.resolution: Use a fresh idempotency_key for a genuinely new purchase.

example.message: That idempotency key was used for a different reservation.

x-error-codes.title: The total must be confirmed before money moves
x-error-codes.description: The request would debit an account and carried no max_charge_cents, so there was nothing to bind the quoted price to the charged one. Nothing was charged. x-error-codes.resolution: Read the current total, show it to the customer, and retry with max_charge_cents set to the value they confirmed. Never auto-retry with the total from this error: that defeats the confirmation it exists to obtain.

example.message: Please confirm the total before proceeding.

x-error-codes.description: The live total (rental price plus any one-time setup fee) is higher than the max_charge_cents ceiling supplied with the request, so nothing was charged.

x-error-codes.title: A subserver stays in its region
x-error-codes.description: An upgrade named a region other than the one the subserver is in. A subserver never changes region. Nothing was charged. The response `data.region` is the region it is in.
x-error-codes.resolution: Leave region out of the upgrade, or buy a new subserver in the other region.

x-error-codes.title: Rate limit exceeded
x-error-codes.description: Too many requests of this kind in a short time, counted per account, auth token or address. The request was not carried out. The body's `error` is `Too Many Requests`.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again. When there is no Retry-After header, the limit could not be checked: try again in a few seconds.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this endpoint. Please try again later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with a request-limit refusal when the allowance is used up.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-generated. Replaying it with the same request returns the original operation, charged once. A refusal for a business reason (for example the region is full or a limit is reached) is remembered under the key and answered the same way every time: use a new key to try again. If an answer says the result is not known yet, retry with the SAME key, never a new one. The same key with a different request is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH`.

max_charge_cents.description: Ceiling on the debit, from the quote. Required whenever the charge is above 0.

state.description: provisioning, active, past_due, held, wiping (being permanently deleted), host_wiped (deleted; older records only), delivery_failed, change_stuck or terminated (closed, or permanently deleted after an unpaid hold).

region.description: Region code, lower case. Pass it as `region` to quote or buy in this region.

auto_renew.description: true renews the subscription from the wallet at the end of each paid period; false lets it stop when the current period ends. Only the account owner (signed in personally) or an auth token can turn it on.

post.description: Turns auto-renew off. The subserver keeps running until paid_through, then goes on hold. No refund.

state.description: provisioning, active, past_due, held, wiping (being permanently deleted), host_wiped (deleted; older records only), delivery_failed, change_stuck or terminated (closed, or permanently deleted after an unpaid hold).

server_id.description: The subserver. Null when a purchase starts; it can be set while state is still provisioning, so wait for state active before you use the subserver. Null again after a failed delivery and after close.

server_name.description: The subserver's own name. Null when server_id is null.

region.description: Region code, lower case. Pass it as `region` to quote or buy in this region.

Where the subserver is: set from the purchase on, also while it is still provisioning. Null after a failed delivery or a close, and when the place has no region code. A subserver never changes region.

anchor_day.description: Day of the month each period renews on.

auto_renew.description: true: the wallet is charged at the end of each paid period to renew it. false: the subserver stops when the current period ends.

active_operation_id.description: The operation in progress, if any.

plan.description: The plan version this subscription is on (plan_id), even if that version is no longer sold. Text follows locale / Accept-Language, English fallback, like GET /api/v1/meta/subserver-plans.

price_cents_per_month.description: Wallet cents charged at each renewal.

hold_days.description: Days an unpaid subserver is held before it is permanently deleted.

resources.description: Resources of this plan version. Units match the server fields of the same name.

ai_multiplier.description: Free AI allowance as a multiple of the Free plan: 1 is the Free level. Free chat token and web search limits that this plan does not set to its own value are multiplied by it. Every other free AI limit, voice included, is set separately and need not rise by this factor.

max_proxy_aliases.description: Proxy aliases (custom computer URLs) allowed on a subserver on this plan.

max_bot_urls.description: Bot URLs allowed on a subserver on this plan.

ai_tier.description: Hoody AI tier of a subserver on this plan; some AI models may be limited to tiers.

post.summary: Transfer from general balance to AI credits
post.description: One-way transfer from general balance to AI credit balance. Provide amount as a strict string (USD, up to 2 decimals). An auth token limited to realms may transfer; its receipts and replays carry no balances.

gross_transferred.description: Gross amount debited from general balance

net_ai_credit.description: Net amount credited to AI balance after fee

general_balance.description: General balance after the transfer. Omitted when the caller is an auth token without `financial.wallet.read` or one limited to realms.

ai_balance.description: AI credit balance after the transfer. Omitted when the caller is an auth token without `financial.wallet.read` or one limited to realms.

limit_sync_pending.description: Present and true only when the transfer completed but the new AI credit may take a moment to become usable. A caller that may read balances gets it re-applied on its next balance read; any other caller re-applies it by sending the same request again with the same idempotency_key (or, without a key, it re-applies on the account's next balance view). Any balances above are already updated.

replayed.description: Present and true only on an idempotent replay of a prior transfer with the same idempotency_key; omitted on a fresh transfer. NO funds were moved on a replay; the balances shown are the current post-transfer values.

400.description: Refused, nothing was moved. INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: the general balance is lower than the amount. Without a code (`error` is "Bad Request"): the amount is 0 ("amount must be greater than 0"), has more than 15 digits before the decimal point ("amount is too large"), or leaves no AI credit after the fee ("amount is too small: after the transfer fee no AI credit would be added"). A body that does not match the schema is refused with 422.

amount.description: USD amount as a string with up to 2 decimals, e.g., "10.00". No exponent, no negatives. The transfer fee is rounded up to a whole cent, so every transfer with a fee pays at least 0.01; an amount so small that no AI credit would be left after the fee is refused (400).

idempotency_key.description: Optional caller idempotency key. Retrying with the SAME key AND same amount returns the original receipt without moving funds again; the same key with a different amount is rejected (409 TRANSFER_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED). Always send one: it makes a double-click or retry-after-timeout safe, and a caller that cannot read balances re-applies a pending spending-limit update by sending the same request again with the same key.

expected_fee_bps.description: The platform fee in basis points that the user was shown and confirmed (the current fee is `ai_credit_fee_bps` of GET /api/v1/wallet/payment-availability). Required while a fee applies: without it the transfer is refused (409 TRANSFER_FEE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED). A value that is not the current fee is refused (409 TRANSFER_FEE_CHANGED), so the user confirms again. Both refusals carry the current fee in `data.current_fee_bps`. It may be left out while the fee is 0. Not checked on an idempotent replay: the same idempotency_key and amount return the original receipt even if the fee changed since.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Optional JSON object of field filters, e.g. `{"status":"completed"}` or `{"amount":{"gte":10}}`. A plain value matches exactly; an object applies operators `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `like` (case-insensitive substring; `%` and `_` in the value are wildcards) and `in` (array, at most 100 values). Fields: `transaction_type`, `status`, `amount`, `currency`, `reason`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Any other field or operator, a value that is not a string, number, boolean or null, or a `filter` that is not a JSON object is rejected with 400.

x-error-codes.title: Rate limit exceeded
x-error-codes.description: Too many requests of this kind in a short time, counted per account, auth token or address. The request was not carried out. The body's `error` is `Too Many Requests`.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again. When there is no Retry-After header, the limit could not be checked: try again in a few seconds.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this endpoint. Please try again later.

x-error-codes.title: Daily payment limit reached
x-error-codes.description: With this amount, the payments started with this payment method in the last 24 hours (failed, expired and cancelled ones excepted) would exceed the daily limit. data.spent_24h_usd is what already counts. No Retry-After header is sent. Nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Try again later, or pay a smaller amount that stays within data.daily_limit_usd.

get.description: Get list of available servers for rental

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Filter by country code (e.g., US, DE)

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Filter by region (e.g., us-east, eu-central)

parameters.name: max_price_per_day
parameters.description: Maximum price per day in USD

parameters.name: available_durations
parameters.description: A server matches when it supports at least one of these rental durations (days).

parameters.name: min_cpu_cores
parameters.description: Minimum CPU cores

parameters.name: min_cpu_score
parameters.description: Minimum CPU benchmark score

parameters.name: cpu_score_type
parameters.description: CPU benchmark type for score filtering

parameters.name: min_ram_gb
parameters.description: Minimum RAM in GB

parameters.name: ram_types
parameters.description: Filter by RAM types

parameters.name: min_total_storage_gb
parameters.description: Minimum total storage in GB

parameters.name: disk_types
parameters.description: Filter servers with these disk types

parameters.name: min_bandwidth_mbps
parameters.description: Minimum network bandwidth in Mbps

parameters.name: min_traffic_tb
parameters.description: Minimum monthly traffic allowance in TB

parameters.name: unlimited_traffic_only
parameters.description: Show only servers with unlimited traffic

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by server category

parameters.name: featured_only
parameters.description: Show only featured servers

parameters.name: discounted_only
parameters.description: Only listings with a sale running now.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Language for the sale label (e.g. de, pt-BR). Wins over Accept-Language; unknown or invalid values fall back to English.

discount.description: The listing's sale, or null when none is running. It cuts the FIRST payment only: the prices shown are what a purchase is charged now, and renewals (extensions) cost the list price. A rental bought at a discount always needs max_charge_cents on its extensions.

percent_off.description: Percent taken off each tier price (rounded down to the cent, never below 1 cent).

label.description: Short display text for the sale, in the requested language when one is set, else English. Plain text: render it as text, never as HTML.

label_locale.description: The locale the label was served from (per the fallback requested → base language → en).

ends_at.description: When the sale ends. After it, the list price applies.

prices.description: Map of duration days to the price a purchase is charged now, in dollars (discounted while a sale runs; see `discount`). E.g. { "1": "10.00", "7": "50.00", "30": "150.00" }

setup_fee.description: DEFAULT one-time setup fee in dollars, charged once when a rental starts and never on extension. An individual duration can override this (including waiving it to zero), so for some tiers this is NOT what is charged. Use price_tiers[days].total_first_payment for the real first payment. "0.00" here means no default fee, not necessarily no fee.

setup_fee_cents.description: The same DEFAULT fee in integer cents. Per-duration overrides are already resolved into price_tiers[days].total_first_payment; this field is not.

price.description: Tier price a purchase is charged now (discounted while a sale runs).

list_price.description: The undiscounted tier price, present only while a sale cuts this tier. Renewals cost this price.

total_first_payment.description: Price for this duration PLUS the one-time setup fee: what the customer actually pays on the first payment. Renewals cost the list price only (`list_price` when present, else `price`).

price_tiers.description: Canonical per-duration representation with price and hold days

x-error-codes.resolution: The exact figures are in this error's data: show the customer data.setup_fee_cents as a one-time charge and data.total_cents as what they will pay now, then retry with max_charge_cents set to data.total_cents. Do not compute the total yourself.

x-error-codes.title: The total must be confirmed before money moves
x-error-codes.description: The request would debit an account and carried no max_charge_cents, so there was nothing to bind the quoted price to the charged one. Nothing was charged. x-error-codes.resolution: Read the current total, show it to the customer, and retry with max_charge_cents set to the value they confirmed. Never auto-retry with the total from this error: that defeats the confirmation it exists to obtain.

rental_days.description: Number of days to rent (must match server pricing durations, max 3650)

max_charge_cents.description: Ceiling on the TOTAL debit (rental price + one-time setup fee), in integer cents. REQUIRED for every paid rental. Omitting it returns 409 CHARGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, or 409 SETUP_FEE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED when the server also carries a one-time fee. It is NOT optional for fee-less servers: the fee is a separate charge, and its absence never meant the total did not need confirming. Only a total of zero needs no ceiling. If the live total exceeds this ceiling the request is rejected with 409 CHARGE_EXCEEDS_MAX and nothing is charged; re-read the server and confirm the new total. A ceiling (not an exact match) so a price DROP still succeeds. Read it from pricing.price_tiers[rental_days].total_first_payment, a dollar string, converted to cents ("95.00" is 9500).

total_paid_cents.description: amount_cents + setup_fee_cents: the rental total to date. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

renewal_pricing_frozen.description: The renewal tiers this rental is guaranteed, frozen at purchase: a map of days to integer cents. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

is_free_tier.description: True for your free-tier subserver entry. It is not a paid rental and does not expire; its rental_end is a far-future placeholder, not a real end date.

network_limit_mbps.description: Only on your current free-tier server: its network cap in Mbit/s, the same in each direction (download and upload). It is the per-server cap when one is set, else the free tier default. Null when no cap is applied to this server, or when the cap cannot be read. Absent on every other row.

computer_capacity.description: Occupied computer slots vs this server's effective limit ("X / Y computers"). Present ONLY for free-tier servers currently held by the caller, when signed in directly (JWT session). Absent for dedicated/bare-metal servers (no limit applies), for auth-token, HTTP Basic or realm-scoped requests (not disclosed), and for past rentals. `used` counts capacity slots exactly as the SERVER_COMPUTER_LIMIT error does: computers still being created or copied occupy a slot; failed, deleted or deleting computers do not, so it can differ from the number of computers you see listed. `max` may be 0 when new computer creation is paused on this server. Some creates do not change the count and can still succeed at used == max. The pair corresponds to the error envelope's current_count/limit.

datacenter.description: Present for a whole machine (a bare-metal rental). Absent for a subserver (paid or free).

kvm_supported.description: Whether this server can give a computer /dev/kvm (run ordinary hardware-accelerated VMs). null = not known yet, or the last check is older than 1 hour. KVM is only on rented bare-metal servers, never on free or paid subservers. This says nothing about whether you may enable it right now: the computer must be stopped, and your permissions and account state still apply.

kvm_nested.description: Whether VMs you run here may themselves run hardware-accelerated VMs (nested virtualization). Off by default; enabled per server by Hoody on request. The VM also needs the host CPU virtualization features passed to it (for example QEMU `-cpu host`). false whenever kvm_supported is false; null = unknown.

kvm_checked_at.description: When Hoody last checked this server's KVM support (ISO 8601). A value with kvm_supported null means that check is too old to trust. null = never checked, or not applicable (subservers, expired or past rentals).

x-error-codes.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again. When there is no Retry-After header, the limit could not be checked: try again in a few seconds.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this endpoint. Please try again later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with a request-limit refusal when the allowance is used up.

expected_rental_end.description: The rental's CURRENT rental_end, exactly as the API returned it. The extension is applied only if it still matches, so a retried request (a lost response, a double click) is refused with 409 EXTENSION_ALREADY_APPLIED instead of charging and extending a second time. Re-read the rental before retrying; never resend blindly.

additional_days.description: Additional days, 1 to 3650; the duration must be priced by the rental's frozen renewal tiers or the server's current pricing.

max_charge_cents.description: The total you confirmed, in whole cents. The extension is refused if it would cost more. For a positive charge this is REQUIRED when the rental has no frozen renewal price (409 CHARGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED): without a quoted ceiling nothing bounds what the current server tiers can charge. It is also REQUIRED for a positive charge when the rental's first payment was cut by a listing discount: renewals cost the list price, never the sale price. A zero charge needs no ceiling. Otherwise optional while the rental still carries frozen tiers, which are themselves a ceiling the customer accepted at purchase.

get.description: Alias for GET /api/v1/rentals. Returns all rented servers for the authenticated user.

setup_fee_cents.description: FROZEN one-time setup fee actually charged when this rental started, in integer cents. 0 when none applied. Never the current server pricing value. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

total_paid_cents.description: amount_cents + setup_fee_cents: the rental total to date. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

renewal_pricing_frozen.description: The renewal tiers this rental is guaranteed, frozen at purchase: a map of days to integer cents. A CEILING, not a fixed price: a later price CUT is passed on, a rise is not. Null when the rental has no guaranteed renewal tiers, in which case the current server tiers apply. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

is_free_tier.description: True for your free-tier subserver entry. It is not a paid rental and does not expire; its rental_end is a far-future placeholder, not a real end date.

network_limit_mbps.description: Only on your current free-tier server: its network cap in Mbit/s, the same in each direction (download and upload). It is the per-server cap when one is set, else the free tier default. Null when no cap is applied to this server, or when the cap cannot be read. Absent on every other row.

computer_capacity.description: Occupied computer slots vs this server's effective limit ("X / Y computers"). Present ONLY for free-tier servers currently held by the caller, when signed in directly (JWT session). Absent for dedicated/bare-metal servers (no limit applies), for auth-token, HTTP Basic or realm-scoped requests (not disclosed), and for past rentals. `used` counts capacity slots exactly as the SERVER_COMPUTER_LIMIT error does: computers still being created or copied occupy a slot; failed, deleted or deleting computers do not, so it can differ from the number of computers you see listed. `max` may be 0 when new computer creation is paused on this server. Some creates do not change the count and can still succeed at used == max. The pair corresponds to the error envelope's current_count/limit.

datacenter.description: Present for a whole machine (a bare-metal rental). Absent for a subserver (paid or free).

kvm_supported.description: Whether this server can give a computer /dev/kvm (run ordinary hardware-accelerated VMs). null = not known yet, or the last check is older than 1 hour. KVM is only on rented bare-metal servers, never on free or paid subservers. This says nothing about whether you may enable it right now: the computer must be stopped, and your permissions and account state still apply.

kvm_nested.description: Whether VMs you run here may themselves run hardware-accelerated VMs (nested virtualization). Off by default; enabled per server by Hoody on request. The VM also needs the host CPU virtualization features passed to it (for example QEMU `-cpu host`). false whenever kvm_supported is false; null = unknown.

kvm_checked_at.description: When Hoody last checked this server's KVM support (ISO 8601). A value with kvm_supported null means that check is too old to trust. null = never checked, or not applicable (subservers, expired or past rentals).

post.summary: Sign up with email and password
post.description: Requests account creation with email and password. A successful response asks the person to check their email and does not reveal whether the address already has an account. The account is not active until the email is verified. Answers 403 SIGNUP_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED while sign-ups are paused by the daily limit of new accounts, 403 SIGNUP_DISABLED while registration is switched off, and 503 SIGNUP_STATE_UNAVAILABLE (retry) when that state cannot be checked; existing accounts can still sign in. A person may have to complete a short check in a browser first: the answer is then 403 CHALLENGE_REQUIRED with data.challenge (verification_url, match_code, token, secret). Show the link and the code, then repeat the same request with challenge: {token, secret} every `interval` seconds: 403 CHALLENGE_PENDING until the check is done, the normal success once it is, a new CHALLENGE_REQUIRED if that check failed, 403 CHALLENGE_INVALID when it expired (start again without challenge), 503 CHALLENGE_BUSY (wait Retry-After seconds).

post.description: Undo the two-factor enrollment named in a "two-factor authentication was turned on" alert, with the token from its link (valid 7 days). Two-factor authentication is turned off and the account is secured: every sign-in ends, all auth tokens and Bot keys are deleted or revoked, GitHub and Google sign-in links are removed, and the password is cleared (set a new one with a reset link). If the account email was changed away from the address the alert went to, and that change can still be undone, it is undone too and that address comes back. The link works only while the account still has that enrollment: after two-factor was turned off or set up again it answers `TWO_FACTOR_UNDO_STALE` and changes nothing. A link used before answers `secured` and changes nothing. No sign-in needed.

x-error-codes.title: Idempotency key reused for a different purchase
x-error-codes.description: The supplied idempotency_key was already used for a reservation with different terms: a different offer, duration, pool or confirmed total. Returning the original would silently give the caller something other than what this request asked for, so it fails instead.
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a fresh idempotency_key for a genuinely new purchase.

example.message: That idempotency key was used for a different reservation.

x-error-codes.title: One-time setup fee must be confirmed
x-error-codes.description: This machine carries a one-time setup fee, charged once when the rental starts and never on an extension. The request omitted max_charge_cents, so the total was never confirmed and nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: The exact figures are in this error's data: show the customer data.setup_fee_cents as a one-time charge and data.total_cents as what they will pay now, then retry with max_charge_cents set to data.total_cents. Do not compute the total yourself.

example.message: This machine has a one-time setup fee. Please confirm the total before proceeding.

x-error-codes.title: The total must be confirmed before money moves
x-error-codes.description: The request would debit an account and carried no max_charge_cents, so there was nothing to bind the quoted price to the charged one. Nothing was charged. This applies to every paid purchase, including servers with no one-time setup fee. The fee is a separate thing, and its absence never meant the total did not need confirming.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the current total, show it to the customer, and retry with max_charge_cents set to the value they confirmed. Never auto-retry with the total from this error: that defeats the confirmation it exists to obtain.

example.message: Please confirm the total before proceeding.

x-error-codes.title: Price changed since the quote
x-error-codes.description: The live total (rental price plus any one-time setup fee) is higher than the max_charge_cents ceiling supplied with the request, so nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Re-read the listing (GET /api/v1/servers/available for an in-stock server, where the total is pricing.price_tiers[rental_days].total_first_payment, or GET /api/v1/offers for an offer), show the user the new total, and retry with an updated max_charge_cents once they confirm. Do NOT auto-retry with the returned actual value: that would defeat the confirmation.

example.message: The price changed. Please review the current total and confirm again.

get.description:
Creates a new browser instance or returns metadata for an existing one.
This is the primary endpoint for explicitly creating browser instances.

**Key capabilities**:
- Create isolated browser instances with custom configurations
- Retrieve metadata for existing instances
- Configure browser emulation (user agent, viewport, geolocation)
- Set locale and timezone for accurate geolocation

**Instance identification**: an instance is the `browser_host` + `browser_port` pair. Inside a Hoody computer the `browser-{N}` service hostname selects it (the proxy fills both from `N`); `browser_id` is NOT a selector. Calling `/start` on a running instance returns its current metadata. Supplied options are validated first; valid ones are then ignored, except that the backend they resolve to must match the running one: the backend follows `stealth` (true when omitted) and `browser` (`firefox` never uses stealth), and a mismatch is rejected with `409 INSTANCE_BACKEND_MISMATCH`. So a `/start` without `stealth` on an instance started with `stealth=false` is rejected too.

**Size limits**: the options of one instance are capped at 96 KiB (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR` above that). Options travel in the query string here, and the whole request head (request line with query string, plus all headers) may be at most 16 KiB (16,384 bytes): a larger request is refused with a bare `431` (no JSON body, no CORS headers) before the 96 KiB check. `/start` and `/restart` accept only GET; an option set that does not fit in the query is passed in the JSON body of a `POST /browse`, `POST /eval` or `POST /cookies` that starts the instance.

The response includes the `webSocketDebuggerUrl` field which provides the Chrome DevTools
WebSocket endpoint for remote debugging (when available with `useRemoteDebuggingPort: true`).

parameters.name: browser_id
parameters.description: Selects the instance: SDK and CLI clients send the request to the `browser-<N>` service host. A value that conflicts with the host's instance is refused with 400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT. On `/history` it also filters. Against a bare server it selects nothing; address instances there with `browser_host` + `browser_port`.

parameters.name: chromiumVersion
parameters.description:
Chromium/Chrome version selection for the instance.
This option applies only when `browser=chromium`.

Supported formats:
- Full version: `136.0.7103.113`
- Major version: `136` (mapped to a known stable patch for the current OS)
- Channel tag: `stable`, `beta`, `dev`, `canary`

Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `chromiumVersion`. A full version that no download source has is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too, answered once the download is refused. A major version with no known build is treated as if omitted.

Omitted, the server uses the Chrome major of a `userAgent` you pass, and otherwise the Chrome build supplied with the computer: the stable build from its last successful update, so it starts without a download. It may lag the newest stable, and `browserFullVersion` in the metadata reports the version that started. If the computer has no supplied build, the server resolves the current `stable` build. Pass `stable` (or a version) to resolve it when the instance starts; a build the computer does not have is downloaded on first use.

The request **blocks** until the requested browser build is available on the server.

parameters.name: fingerprintId
parameters.description:
Base fingerprint profile id.
The server uses the `context` and `launch` defaults of the configured fingerprint profile with this id,
then applies any request overrides over them (top-level options and `userProfile` values both win over the profile). An unknown id starts with an empty profile.
The id is 1-64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`; any other value is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

parameters.name: useRemoteDebuggingPort
parameters.description:
If `true`, the instance will launch Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port` and will populate
`webSocketDebuggerUrl` in metadata responses.

parameters.name: remoteDebuggingPort
parameters.description: Ignored. The kit always assigns the DevTools port itself (a caller-supplied value is never honoured, for isolation); read the assigned URLs from `/devtools-url` or the instance metadata. Kept only so older clients do not fail validation.

parameters.name: remoteDebuggingAddress
parameters.description: Interface address the DevTools port binds to. Connect through the URLs `/devtools-url` returns.

parameters.name: extensions
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of absolute extension directory paths to load.
Extensions are Chromium only (`browser=chromium`, the default; with Firefox the start fails) and require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode); they launch a persistent profile.

parameters.name: extensionsDir
parameters.description:
Directory containing extension subfolders to load (each subfolder is treated as an extension).
Extensions are Chromium only (`browser=chromium`, the default; with Firefox the start fails) and require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode); they launch a persistent profile.

parameters.name: extensionsStoreIds
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of Chrome Web Store extension IDs to download and load.
Requires `showBrowser=true` and works only with `browser=chromium`. Each ID is 32 letters from `a` to `p`; anything else, or an ID the store does not offer, is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
Downloads of the same extension are serialized across instances; an instance that waits more than 5 minutes for another instance's download fails with a "try again later" error.

parameters.name: proxyServer
parameters.description:
Proxy server for browser traffic. Supports `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://`, or `socks5h://`.
Example: `socks5://127.0.0.1:9050`

parameters.name: proxyUsername
parameters.description: Proxy username (if required). Only with an `http://` or `https://` `proxyServer`: the browser cannot authenticate to a SOCKS proxy, so `proxyUsername` or `proxyPassword` with a `socks4://` or `socks5://` proxy (and `socks5h://` under Firefox) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

parameters.name: proxyPassword
parameters.description: Proxy password (if required)

parameters.name: proxyBypass
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of hosts that should bypass the proxy

parameters.name: enableQuic
parameters.description: Enable QUIC/HTTP3 transport. Defaults to `false` (QUIC blocked). Use `enableQuic=true` to re-enable QUIC.

parameters.name: enableDnsOverHttps
parameters.description: Enable DNS-over-HTTPS for browser DNS resolution. Defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: dnsOverHttpsUrl
parameters.description: DoH resolver URL (HTTPS only). Defaults to Cloudflare: `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query`.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description:
X display number or identifier for headful mode. Required when `showBrowser=true`
and no `DISPLAY` environment variable is set on the server.

parameters.name: showBrowser
parameters.description: Whether to run the browser headful (visible). Defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: sessionName
parameters.description: Custom session name for identifying this browser instance

parameters.name: timezoneId
parameters.description: IANA timezone identifier for browser geolocation

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: BCP 47 language tag for browser locale

parameters.name: userAgent
parameters.description: User agent string to apply to the browser context.
parameters.example: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

parameters.name: viewport
noViewport
parameters.description: Set to `true` to disable fixed-viewport emulation (alias for `viewport=null`). The page then resizes with the browser window instead of being pinned to an emulated resolution. Cannot be combined with a fixed `viewport` object.

parameters.name: geolocation
launchArguments
parameters.description: Additional Chromium/Firefox command-line arguments. Pass the query key repeatedly (`launchArguments=--a&launchArguments=--b`) or a single JSON array string (`launchArguments=["--a","--b"]`); every value is kept. Entries must be strings (400 otherwise). On Chromium, every entry must be a switch (`--name` or `--name=value`) that does not open a page: a positional URL or path and `--app` are refused, because a startup page loads before the browser's local-file block is in place. A kit started with local-file access enabled accepts them.

parameters.name: browser
parameters.description: Browser engine to use (`chromium` or `firefox`). The raw HTTP query also accepts `chrome` as an alias of `chromium`; the SDK and the CLI accept only `chromium` and `firefox`. Fixed for the life of the instance.

parameters.name: firefoxVersion
parameters.description:
Firefox version label (informational only). Playwright-managed Firefox builds are used by default.
If omitted, a Playwright Firefox build is downloaded on demand. A value that is not a label (letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`, at most 64 characters) is ignored.

parameters.name: firefoxExecutablePath
parameters.description: Absolute path to a custom Firefox executable (overrides download)

parameters.name: showDevtools
parameters.description: Whether to open DevTools on launch (Chromium only)

parameters.name: userProfile
parameters.description: Optional user profile object (JSON string): `locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgentString`, `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport`. Precedence for each field: the top-level request option (`locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgent`, `geolocation`, `viewport`) > `userProfile` > the fingerprint profile (`fingerprintId`, `default` when omitted) > the engine default. A value set here always replaces the fingerprint profile's value. `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport` must be objects and get the same checks as the top-level `geolocation` and `viewport`; a bad value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the field. An empty value (`null`, `false`, `0`, `""`) is treated as not set.

parameters.name: stealth
parameters.description:
Launch Chromium in stealth mode using Patchright (anti-detection patches).
Only applies to `browser=chromium`. Ignored for Firefox.
Defaults to `true`. Bare `?stealth` is treated as `true`.

parameters.name: iframe
parameters.description: The bare `/` URL serves the instance status page. Open `/?view=display` for the full-page display; if no display address can be resolved, the status page is returned.

parameters.name: iframe_url
parameters.description: Explicit URL for the display iframe. If not provided, the URL is auto-detected from the Host header subdomain pattern.

parameters.name: maximize_new_windows
parameters.description:
Control the `maximize_new_windows` flag stamped onto generated display URLs (iframe pages, status pages, `iframe_url` metadata). The flag is always explicit (`true` or `false`); when true the hoody-display client opens new top-level app windows maximized.
Enabled by default; set to `false` to keep the display client's centered default-size placement (the explicit `false` also overrides a display-side `default-settings.txt` enable).
Explicit `iframe_url` values are never modified.

400.description: A request parameter failed validation. `code` is always `VALIDATION_ERROR` (there is no per-parameter code), and the message names the offending parameter and constraint. This includes a parameter found invalid only while the instance starts (for example an unparseable `display`, a malformed `chromiumVersion`, or `extensions` without `showBrowser=true` or with a directory that does not exist): no instance is left running and the start is not retried. No `details` object is attached on this route. `INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT`: the request came through a `browser-{N}` service hostname, which serves browser `N` only, and a `port`, `browser_id` or `host` in its query, or a `browser_port`, `port`, `display`, `browser_id`, `browser_host` or `host` in its JSON body, names a different instance. On that hostname the platform sets `browser_port` and `display` in the query itself, replacing any value sent, and keeps a `browser_host` the query carries. `details.field` names the parameter. Nothing was run. Call that instance's own hostname, or leave the parameter out.

x-error-codes.title: Validation Error
x-error-codes.description: One or more request parameters failed validation. The message names the parameter (for example "browser_port must be an integer" or "Invalid browser_host format").
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the message: it names the parameter and the constraint that failed

x-error-codes.title: Instance Selector Conflict
x-error-codes.description: The request came through a browser-{N} hostname and names a different instance
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the other instance's own browser-{N} hostname, or leave the parameter out

409.description: `INSTANCE_BACKEND_MISMATCH`: the existing instance uses a different stealth backend. Or `PORT_IN_USE`: the instance's `browser_port` on `browser_host` is already bound by another process. The request is valid but the port is taken right now: the message names the host and port, nothing was started, and the start is not retried. Pick another `browser_port`, or stop the process holding it.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Backend Mismatch
x-error-codes.description: The existing instance was launched with a different stealth mode/backend
x-error-codes.resolution: Stop the running instance first, then start again with the new stealth mode

x-error-codes.title: Port In Use
x-error-codes.description: The instance's browser_port is already bound by another process
x-error-codes.resolution: Pick another browser_port, or stop the process holding it

example.error: Instance backend mismatch: running with stealth=true (patchright), requested stealth=false (playwright). Switching stealth mode requires a different backend. Stop this instance first via /stop?browser_host=0.0.0.0&browser_port=9223, then call /start again.

431.description: The request head (request line with query string, plus all headers) is over 16 KiB (16,384 bytes). Refused by the HTTP layer before routing: the status line only, with no JSON body and no CORS headers, so a browser page sees a network error. Pass large option sets in the JSON body of a `POST /browse`, `POST /eval` or `POST /cookies` that starts the instance.

500.description: Instance creation failed. `code` is one of exactly four values: `INSTANCE_START_TIMEOUT`: the instance did not finish starting within `--worker-timeout`; plausibly retryable. `BROWSER_LAUNCH_ERROR`: the browser process itself failed to launch. `CHILD_PROCESS_ERROR`: the instance failed to initialize for another reason. `INTERNAL_ERROR`: anything unexpected. Messages are server-authored: an exception name is never published as a `code`, and engine text is never published as a message, so no other code can appear here. A failure caused by a parameter you sent is never a 500: it is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the parameter. No `details` object is attached on this route.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Start Timeout
x-error-codes.description: The instance did not finish starting within `--worker-timeout` (default 600000 ms)
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if it persists, raise --worker-timeout or check the computer's load

x-error-codes.title: Browser Launch Failed
x-error-codes.description: The browser process itself failed to launch
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry with a chromiumVersion the deployment provides: a full version, a major version, or a channel tag such as stable

x-error-codes.title: Instance Initialization Failed
x-error-codes.description: The instance failed to initialize for a reason other than the browser launch
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the server log; the published message is server-authored and deliberately opaque

x-error-codes.title: Internal Error
x-error-codes.description: An unexpected failure the server declines to classify further
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the server log for the requestId

startTimeout.summary: The instance did not finish starting in time

value.error: Child process timeout exceeded

launchFailed.summary: The browser process failed to launch

value.error: Browser launch failed
Browser instance initialization failed

502.description: `INSTANCE_QUARANTINED`: a previous instance at this `browser_host`/`browser_port` was stopped but has not been seen to exit, so the address is held until it exits. No new instance is created and none is returned; the address is not create-eligible until then. Retry, or pick a different `browser_port`.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Quarantined
x-error-codes.description: A prior instance at this address has not been confirmed exited
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after a few seconds, or start on a different browser_port

example.error: Instance is temporarily unavailable (prior process exit unconfirmed)

503.description: `INSTALL_IN_PROGRESS`: this call had to start a browser instance, and another process was still installing the Chrome or Firefox build, or a Chrome Web Store extension, that the instance needs when the wait limit (about 5 minutes) ran out. No instance was started. Retry after the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header. The message names what was being installed: Chrome with its version, Firefox, or the extension id. A failure to take the install lock for any other reason is not this error: it is a `500` initialization failure. `DISPLAY_UNAVAILABLE`: this call had to start a headful instance (`showBrowser=true`, the default) and no display accepts connections: the display server is not installed (answered at once), the display was stopped while the terminal session that started it stays open (answered at once; delete that terminal session to bring the display back), or the display did not come up within about 45 seconds. The message says which. No instance was started, and the start is not retried. Start the instance with `showBrowser=false` (headless), or retry once the display runs.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying

x-error-codes.title: Install In Progress
x-error-codes.description: Another process is installing a browser build or extension this instance needs
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the Retry-After delay; the install finishes in the background

x-error-codes.title: Display Unavailable
x-error-codes.description: A headful instance needs a display, and none accepts connections
x-error-codes.resolution: Start the instance with showBrowser=false (headless), retry once the display runs, or delete the terminal session whose display was stopped

example.error: Timed out waiting for another process to finish installing Chrome 136.0.7103.113; try again later

504.description: `TIMEOUT`: the instance launch took longer than the server's request timeout (`--request-timeout`, default 600000 ms). Answered by the server, with `details.phase` `launch` and `details.outcome` `unknown`: the launch is not cancelled and the instance may still come up. Check with `/metadata?start=false` (404 until it is running) instead of retrying at once.

x-error-codes.title: Timeout
x-error-codes.description: The instance launch outlasted the request timeout; its outcome is unknown
x-error-codes.resolution: Poll /metadata with start=false until it answers 200, or raise --request-timeout
