get.description:
Stops and recreates a browser instance. The rebuild inherits the options the instance was created with (engine, headless mode, locale, viewport, proxy, …); any parameter passed on this request overrides the inherited value, except the engine: a request that would switch between Patchright and Playwright answers `409 INSTANCE_BACKEND_MISMATCH` and changes nothing. Firefox always runs on Playwright, so `browser=firefox` is accepted only for an instance created with `stealth=false` (or already Firefox); a default (stealth) instance is refused, even with `stealth=false` added. To move a default instance to Firefox, `/stop` it and call `/start?browser=firefox`. Browser state (cookies, tabs, console/network buffers) is reset.
Accepts the same parameters as `/start`.

parameters.name: browser_id
parameters.description: Selects the instance: SDK and CLI clients send the request to the `browser-<N>` service host. A value that conflicts with the host's instance is refused with 400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT. On `/history` it also filters. Against a bare server it selects nothing; address instances there with `browser_host` + `browser_port`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Controls instance creation behavior.
- Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation.
- When auto-start is disabled globally: set to `true` to create an instance.

Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

parameters.name: chromiumVersion
parameters.description:
Chromium/Chrome version selection for the instance.
This option applies only when `browser=chromium`.

Supported formats:
- Full version: `136.0.7103.113`
- Major version: `136` (mapped to a known stable patch for the current OS)
- Channel tag: `stable`, `beta`, `dev`, `canary`

Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `chromiumVersion`. A full version that no download source has is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too, answered once the download is refused. A major version with no known build is treated as if omitted.

Omitted, the server uses the Chrome major of a `userAgent` you pass, and otherwise the Chrome build supplied with the computer: the stable build from its last successful update, so it starts without a download. It may lag the newest stable, and `browserFullVersion` in the metadata reports the version that started. If the computer has no supplied build, the server resolves the current `stable` build. Pass `stable` (or a version) to resolve it when the instance starts; a build the computer does not have is downloaded on first use.

The request **blocks** until the requested browser build is available on the server.

parameters.name: fingerprintId
parameters.description:
Base fingerprint profile id.
The server uses the `context` and `launch` defaults of the configured fingerprint profile with this id,
then applies any request overrides over them (top-level options and `userProfile` values both win over the profile). An unknown id starts with an empty profile.
The id is 1-64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`; any other value is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

parameters.name: useRemoteDebuggingPort
parameters.description:
If `true`, the instance will launch Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port` and will populate
`webSocketDebuggerUrl` in metadata responses. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: remoteDebuggingPort
parameters.description: Ignored. The kit always assigns the DevTools port itself (a caller-supplied value is never honoured, for isolation); read the assigned URLs from `/devtools-url` or the instance metadata. Kept only so older clients do not fail validation.

parameters.name: remoteDebuggingAddress
parameters.description: Interface address the DevTools port binds to. Connect through the URLs `/devtools-url` returns.

parameters.name: extensions
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of absolute extension directory paths to load.
Extensions are Chromium only (`browser=chromium`, the default; with Firefox the start fails) and require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode); they launch a persistent profile.

parameters.name: extensionsDir
parameters.description:
Directory containing extension subfolders to load (each subfolder is treated as an extension).
Extensions are Chromium only (`browser=chromium`, the default; with Firefox the start fails) and require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode); they launch a persistent profile.

parameters.name: extensionsStoreIds
parameters.description:
Chrome Web Store extension IDs to download and load (Chromium only).
Requires `showBrowser=true` and works only with `browser=chromium`. Each ID is 32 letters from `a` to `p`; anything else, or an ID the store does not offer, is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
Downloads of the same extension are serialized across instances; an instance that waits more than 5 minutes for another instance's download fails with a "try again later" error.

parameters.name: proxyServer
parameters.description: Proxy server URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h)

parameters.name: proxyUsername
parameters.description: Proxy username (if required). Only with an `http://` or `https://` `proxyServer`: the browser cannot authenticate to a SOCKS proxy, so `proxyUsername` or `proxyPassword` with a `socks4://` or `socks5://` proxy (and `socks5h://` under Firefox) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

parameters.name: proxyPassword
parameters.description: Proxy password (if required)

parameters.name: proxyBypass
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of hosts that should bypass the proxy

parameters.name: enableQuic
parameters.description: Enable QUIC/HTTP3 transport (`false` blocks QUIC). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: enableDnsOverHttps
parameters.description: Enable DNS-over-HTTPS for browser DNS resolution. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: dnsOverHttpsUrl
parameters.description: DoH resolver URL (HTTPS only). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description:
X display number or identifier for headful mode. Required when `showBrowser=true`
and no `DISPLAY` environment variable is set on the server.

parameters.name: showBrowser
parameters.description: Whether to run the browser headful (visible). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: sessionName
parameters.description: Custom session name for identifying this browser instance

parameters.name: timezoneId
parameters.description: IANA timezone identifier for browser geolocation

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: BCP 47 language tag for browser locale

parameters.name: userAgent
parameters.description: User agent string to apply to the browser context.
parameters.example: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

parameters.name: viewport
noViewport
parameters.description: Set to `true` to disable fixed-viewport emulation (alias for `viewport=null`). The page then resizes with the browser window instead of being pinned to an emulated resolution. Cannot be combined with a fixed `viewport` object. On a restart, `false` turns off a `noViewport=true` the instance was started with, and the default viewport comes back. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: geolocation
launchArguments
parameters.description: Additional Chromium/Firefox command-line arguments. Pass the query key repeatedly (`launchArguments=--a&launchArguments=--b`) or a single JSON array string (`launchArguments=["--a","--b"]`); every value is kept. Entries must be strings (400 otherwise). On Chromium, every entry must be a switch (`--name` or `--name=value`) that does not open a page: a positional URL or path and `--app` are refused, because a startup page loads before the browser's local-file block is in place. A kit started with local-file access enabled accepts them.

parameters.name: browser
parameters.description: Browser engine (`chromium` or `firefox`). The raw HTTP query also accepts `chrome` as an alias of `chromium`; the SDK and the CLI accept only `chromium` and `firefox`. Fixed for the life of the instance: when omitted, the instance keeps its engine.

parameters.name: firefoxVersion
parameters.description:
Firefox version label (informational only). Playwright-managed Firefox builds are used by default.
If omitted, a Playwright Firefox build is downloaded on demand. A value that is not a label (letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`, at most 64 characters) is ignored.

parameters.name: firefoxExecutablePath
parameters.description: Absolute path to a custom Firefox executable (overrides download)

parameters.name: showDevtools
parameters.description: Whether to open DevTools on launch (Chromium only). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: userProfile
parameters.description: Optional user profile object (JSON string): `locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgentString`, `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport`. Precedence for each field: the top-level request option (`locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgent`, `geolocation`, `viewport`) > `userProfile` > the fingerprint profile (`fingerprintId`, `default` when omitted) > the engine default. A value set here always replaces the fingerprint profile's value. `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport` must be objects and get the same checks as the top-level `geolocation` and `viewport`; a bad value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the field. An empty value (`null`, `false`, `0`, `""`) is treated as not set.

parameters.name: stealth
parameters.description:
Launch Chromium in stealth mode using Patchright (anti-detection patches).
Only applies to `browser=chromium`. Ignored for Firefox.
When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. Bare `?stealth` is treated as `true`.

parameters.name: iframe
parameters.description: The bare `/` URL serves the instance status page. Open `/?view=display` for the full-page display; if no display address can be resolved, the status page is returned. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

parameters.name: iframe_url
parameters.description: Explicit URL for the display iframe.

parameters.name: maximize_new_windows
parameters.description:
Control the `maximize_new_windows` flag stamped onto the generated display URL (always explicit `true`/`false`); when true the hoody-display client opens new top-level app windows maximized.
When omitted, the instance keeps its setting.

400.description: VALIDATION_ERROR: a request parameter failed validation; the message names it. This includes a parameter found invalid only while the new instance starts (for example an unparseable `display` or `extensions` without `showBrowser=true`): no instance is left running and the start is not retried. `INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT`: the request came through a `browser-{N}` service hostname, which serves browser `N` only, and a `port`, `browser_id` or `host` in its query, or a `browser_port`, `port`, `display`, `browser_id`, `browser_host` or `host` in its JSON body, names a different instance. On that hostname the platform sets `browser_port` and `display` in the query itself, replacing any value sent, and keeps a `browser_host` the query carries. `details.field` names the parameter. Nothing was run. Call that instance's own hostname, or leave the parameter out.

x-error-codes.title: Validation Error
x-error-codes.description: One or more request parameters failed validation
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the error details for the specific parameter and constraint that failed

x-error-codes.title: Instance Selector Conflict
x-error-codes.description: The request came through a browser-{N} hostname and names a different instance
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the other instance's own browser-{N} hostname, or leave the parameter out

example.error: extensions, extensionsDir and extensionsStoreIds require showBrowser=true (headful mode)

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: no instance runs at this address and this request may not create one: `start=false`, or auto-start is turned off in the server's configuration and `start=true` was not sent. Nothing is created.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Not Found
x-error-codes.description: No browser instance runs at this address, and start=false (or disabled auto-start) forbids creating one
x-error-codes.resolution: Create the instance with /start, or omit start (or send start=true) to let /restart create it

example.error: Instance not found: no browser instance at this address, and this request may not create one (start=false, or auto-start is disabled without start=true)

409.description: `INSTANCE_BACKEND_MISMATCH`: the restart would switch the instance's stealth backend (Patchright to Playwright or back), which includes `browser=firefox` on a default instance. The instance keeps running unchanged. Or `PORT_IN_USE`: the instance's `browser_port` on `browser_host` is already bound by another process. The request is valid but the port is taken right now: the message names the host and port, nothing was started, and the start is not retried. Pick another `browser_port`, or stop the process holding it.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Backend Mismatch
x-error-codes.description: The existing instance was launched with a different stealth mode/backend
x-error-codes.resolution: Stop the running instance first, then start again with the new stealth mode

x-error-codes.title: Port In Use
x-error-codes.description: The instance's browser_port is already bound by another process
x-error-codes.resolution: Pick another browser_port, or stop the process holding it

example.error: Instance backend mismatch: running with stealth=true (patchright), requested stealth=false (playwright). Switching stealth mode requires a different backend. Stop this instance first via /stop?browser_host=0.0.0.0&browser_port=9223, then call /start again.

431.description: The request head (request line with query string, plus all headers) is over 16 KiB (16,384 bytes). Refused by the HTTP layer before routing: the status line only, with no JSON body and no CORS headers, so a browser page sees a network error. Pass large option sets in the JSON body of a `POST /browse`, `POST /eval` or `POST /cookies` that starts the instance.

500.description: The restart failed for a reason other than a parameter you sent (those are `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`): `INSTANCE_START_TIMEOUT` (the new instance did not start within `--worker-timeout`; plausibly retryable), `BROWSER_LAUNCH_ERROR` (the browser process failed to launch), `CHILD_PROCESS_ERROR` (the instance failed to initialize) or `INTERNAL_ERROR` (anything unexpected). Messages are server-authored. The old instance is gone either way.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Start Timeout
x-error-codes.description: The instance did not finish starting within `--worker-timeout` (default 600000 ms)
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if it persists, raise --worker-timeout or check the computer's load

x-error-codes.title: Browser Launch Failed
x-error-codes.description: The browser process itself failed to launch
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry with a chromiumVersion the deployment provides: a full version, a major version, or a channel tag such as stable

x-error-codes.title: Instance Initialization Failed
x-error-codes.description: The instance failed to initialize for a reason other than the browser launch
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the server log; the published message is server-authored and deliberately opaque

x-error-codes.title: Internal Error
x-error-codes.description: An unexpected failure the server declines to classify further
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the server log for the requestId

502.description: `INSTANCE_QUARANTINED`: the address is held until a prior instance there is confirmed to have exited, so no replacement was started and the old instance is gone. Raised either because the address was already quarantined when the restart arrived, or because this restart's own stop could not confirm that the old instance had exited. Retry, or start on a different `browser_port`.

x-error-codes.title: Instance Quarantined
x-error-codes.description: A prior instance at this address has not been confirmed exited
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after a few seconds, or start on a different browser_port

example.error: Instance is temporarily unavailable (prior process exit unconfirmed)

503.description: `INSTALL_IN_PROGRESS`: this call had to start a browser instance, and another process was still installing the Chrome or Firefox build, or a Chrome Web Store extension, that the instance needs when the wait limit (about 5 minutes) ran out. No instance was started. Retry after the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header. The message names what was being installed: Chrome with its version, Firefox, or the extension id. A failure to take the install lock for any other reason is not this error: it is a `500` initialization failure. `DISPLAY_UNAVAILABLE`: this call had to start a headful instance (`showBrowser=true`, the default) and no display accepts connections: the display server is not installed (answered at once), the display was stopped while the terminal session that started it stays open (answered at once; delete that terminal session to bring the display back), or the display did not come up within about 45 seconds. The message says which. No instance was started, and the start is not retried. Start the instance with `showBrowser=false` (headless), or retry once the display runs.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying

x-error-codes.title: Install In Progress
x-error-codes.description: Another process is installing a browser build or extension this instance needs
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the Retry-After delay; the install finishes in the background

x-error-codes.title: Display Unavailable
x-error-codes.description: A headful instance needs a display, and none accepts connections
x-error-codes.resolution: Start the instance with showBrowser=false (headless), retry once the display runs, or delete the terminal session whose display was stopped

example.error: Timed out waiting for another process to finish installing Chrome 136.0.7103.113; try again later

504.description: `TIMEOUT`: the restart (stopping the old instance and launching the new one) took longer than the server's request timeout (`--request-timeout`, default 600000 ms). Answered by the server, with `details.phase` `launch` and `details.outcome` `unknown`: the launch is not cancelled and the instance may still come up. Check with `/metadata?start=false` (404 until it is running) instead of retrying at once.

x-error-codes.title: Timeout
x-error-codes.description: The instance launch outlasted the request timeout; its outcome is unknown
x-error-codes.resolution: Poll /metadata with start=false until it answers 200, or raise --request-timeout

example.error: The browser instance did not finish starting within the request timeout; it may still come up (check /metadata with start=false)

servers.description: The computer's browser kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-9999).

get.description:
Navigates to a URL and/or captures a screenshot of a browser tab.

**Navigation + Screenshot workflow**:
- If `url` is provided: Navigate to URL → Wait for page load → Capture screenshot
- If `url` is omitted: Capture screenshot of current page state

**Key features**:
- Smart tab management with `onlyIfNotExists` to avoid duplicate tabs
- Multiple output formats: PNG, JPEG, or Base64-encoded
- Full page capture with `fullPage=true`
- Quality control for JPEG compression
- One element with `selector`, or one area with `clip`
- Elements covered with `mask` (for private data) or left out with `hide` (for cookie banners and ads)
- `scale=css` for one image pixel per CSS pixel

**Common use cases**: Visual regression testing, website monitoring, content verification

parameters.name: browser_id
parameters.description: Selects the instance: SDK and CLI clients send the request to the `browser-<N>` service host. A value that conflicts with the host's instance is refused with 400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT. On `/history` it also filters. Against a bare server it selects nothing; address instances there with `browser_host` + `browser_port`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Controls instance creation behavior.
- Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation.
- When auto-start is disabled globally: set to `true` to create an instance.

Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to navigate to. Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`), on GET and on POST alike: a request naming two destinations is answered rather than silently resolved to one of them. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `url` is governed by the body schema. Only an absolute `http`, `https` or `data` URL, `about:blank`, or (on Chromium engines only) a `chrome:` URL is accepted. Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an http, https or data URL, about:blank, or a chrome URL on Chromium; file and other local schemes are refused`), and a value that is not an absolute URL (such as `/etc/hostname`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an absolute URL, like https://example.com/`). Every other `about:` page is refused (Firefox's `about:reader?url=file:…` loads a local file), and `chrome:` is refused on Firefox, where it is the browser's own privileged UI. A value that is not a string is `url must be a string`. The `url` is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On `/screenshot` and `/pdf` a supplied but empty `url=` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too (omit `url` to capture the current tab). The browser itself blocks local files as well (see "Local files" in the API overview).

parameters.name: tabId
parameters.description: The ID of an open tab, from `/tabs`; tab ids start at 1. Omitted: all tabs for `/console` and `/network`; a new tab for `/browse`, unless `onlyIfNotExists=true` finds a tab already showing the URL; the active tab for other tab operations. Supplied: exactly that tab. An unknown id returns `404 TAB_NOT_FOUND` (with `details.openTabs`) and a malformed id `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; the request never falls back to another tab. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`tabId must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output format: `png` (default) and `jpeg` answer the image bytes; `base64` answers JSON with the PNG bytes base64-encoded. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `format`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`format must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Image quality for JPEG format (0-100); not used for `png` or `base64`. A value that is not an integer from 0 to 100 is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `quality`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`quality must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: fullPage
parameters.description: Capture the entire scrollable page. `true` or `false`; any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `fullPage`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`fullPage must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Capture only the first element matching this CSS selector, at its own size; the page is scrolled to bring it into view. One CSS selector, at most 4096 characters (a selector list such as `.a, .b` is one). `>>` chaining, braces, comments, Playwright's own pseudo-classes (`:visible`, `:has-text()`, `:text()` and the like, also escaped; the same text inside a quoted value or an escaped name is fine), an empty value (`selector=`; omit the key instead), and a selector that the page's CSS parser or the engine's selector parser does not accept are each a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `selector`. No match is `404 ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND`, and a match that is not visible (hidden, or with no size) or that `hide` covers (itself or anything it is rendered inside: an ancestor, a slot, a shadow host) is `422 ELEMENT_NOT_VISIBLE`, both at once rather than after the capture timeout. Cannot be combined with `clip` or `fullPage=true` (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`selector must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: clip
parameters.description: Capture one area: `x,y,width,height` in CSS pixels from the page's top-left corner, for example `0,0,800,600`. `x` and `y` from 0 to 1000000, `width` and `height` above 0 and at most 16384; an empty `clip=` is refused too. With `fullPage=true` the area is measured on the whole page, otherwise on the viewport, and it is cut to what is there; an area entirely outside is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `clip`, and so is a malformed value. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`clip must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Paint over every element matching this CSS selector with an opaque box in `maskColor`: in the top page and its open shadow roots, not inside iframes. A selector list such as `.cookie-banner, .ad` covers several. This is the option for keeping private data out of an image. A selector that matches nothing covers nothing and the capture still succeeds, so check it against the page first (for example with /snapshot) when the cover matters. One CSS selector, at most 4096 characters (a selector list such as `.a, .b` is one). `>>` chaining, braces, comments, Playwright's own pseudo-classes (`:visible`, `:has-text()`, `:text()` and the like, also escaped; the same text inside a quoted value or an escaped name is fine), an empty value (`mask=`; omit the key instead), and a selector that the page's CSS parser or the engine's selector parser does not accept are each a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `mask`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`mask must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: maskColor
parameters.description: The colour of the `mask` boxes, as an opaque hex colour: `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` (a colour with alpha, which would let the covered content show through, is refused). Default `#FF00FF` (pink). Any other value, an empty one, or `maskColor` without `mask`, is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `maskColor`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`maskColor must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: hide
parameters.description: Leave out every element matching this CSS selector: a style rule (`visibility: hidden; opacity: 0`, both `!important`) is added to the page, every iframe and every open shadow root for the capture only and removed after it, so matches keep their space and are not painted, children included (except a child that sets `visibility: visible` inside a `display: contents` match, which has no box of its own to fade). It is a style rule, not a cover: a declaration the page itself marks `!important` in an element's `style` attribute wins over it, and a selector that matches nothing hides nothing while the capture still succeeds. To keep private data out of an image, use `mask`. One CSS selector, at most 4096 characters (a selector list such as `.a, .b` is one). `>>` chaining, braces, comments, Playwright's own pseudo-classes (`:visible`, `:has-text()`, `:text()` and the like, also escaped; the same text inside a quoted value or an escaped name is fine), an empty value (`hide=`; omit the key instead), and a selector that the page's CSS parser or the engine's selector parser does not accept are each a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `hide`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`hide must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: `device` (default, also when `scale` is empty): one image pixel per device pixel, so a page with `devicePixelRatio` 2 gives an image twice its CSS size. `css`: one image pixel per CSS pixel. Any other non-empty value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `scale`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`scale must not be repeated`).

data.description: Base64-encoded image data

400.description: Validation error. An empty `url=` or a `url` outside the allowed set (`http`, `https` and `data` URLs, `about:blank`, `chrome:` URLs on Chromium), or one that is not an absolute URL, is `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `details.field` `url`; it is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On a call that has to start the instance, it is also the answer for a launch parameter found invalid only while the instance starts (for example `display`, `chromiumVersion`, a `firefoxExecutablePath` that does not exist, an `extensionsStoreIds` ID the Chrome Web Store does not offer, or `extensions` / `extensionsDir` / `extensionsStoreIds` without `showBrowser=true` or with a directory that does not exist or is not a directory): the message names the parameter, no instance is left running, and the start is not retried. `INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT`: the request came through a `browser-{N}` service hostname, which serves browser `N` only, and a `port`, `browser_id` or `host` in its query, or a `browser_port`, `port`, `display`, `browser_id`, `browser_host` or `host` in its JSON body, names a different instance. On that hostname the platform sets `browser_port` and `display` in the query itself, replacing any value sent, and keeps a `browser_host` the query carries. `details.field` names the parameter. Nothing was run. Call that instance's own hostname, or leave the parameter out.

x-error-codes.title: Validation Error
x-error-codes.description: One or more request parameters failed validation
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the error details for the specific parameter and constraint that failed

x-error-codes.title: Instance Selector Conflict
x-error-codes.description: The request came through a browser-{N} hostname and names a different instance
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the other instance's own browser-{N} hostname, or leave the parameter out

404.description: TAB_NOT_FOUND: a `tabId` was supplied but no such tab is open (`details.openTabs` lists the open ids); ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND: no element matches `selector` (`details.field` `selector`); or NOT_FOUND: no tab at all / no instance and auto-start disabled

x-error-codes.title: Not Found
x-error-codes.description: No browser instance runs at this address (or, on a tab route, the instance has no tab at all)
x-error-codes.resolution: Check browser_host/browser_port, or create the instance with /start

x-error-codes.title: Tab Not Found
x-error-codes.description: A tabId was supplied but no such tab is open; details.openTabs lists the open ids
x-error-codes.resolution: Pass a tab ID from /tabs, or omit tabId for the active tab

x-error-codes.title: Element Not Found

get.description: Opens a new tab (or uses an existing one) and navigates to a URL

parameters.name: browser_id
parameters.description: Selects the instance: SDK and CLI clients send the request to the `browser-<N>` service host. A value that conflicts with the host's instance is refused with 400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT. On `/history` it also filters. Against a bare server it selects nothing; address instances there with `browser_host` + `browser_port`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Controls instance creation behavior.
- Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation.
- When auto-start is disabled globally: set to `true` to create an instance.

Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to navigate to. Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`), on GET and on POST alike: a request naming two destinations is answered rather than silently resolved to one of them. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `url` is governed by the body schema. Only an absolute `http`, `https` or `data` URL, `about:blank`, or (on Chromium engines only) a `chrome:` URL is accepted. Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an http, https or data URL, about:blank, or a chrome URL on Chromium; file and other local schemes are refused`), and a value that is not an absolute URL (such as `/etc/hostname`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an absolute URL, like https://example.com/`). Every other `about:` page is refused (Firefox's `about:reader?url=file:…` loads a local file), and `chrome:` is refused on Firefox, where it is the browser's own privileged UI. A value that is not a string is `url must be a string`. The `url` is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On `/screenshot` and `/pdf` a supplied but empty `url=` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too (omit `url` to capture the current tab). The browser itself blocks local files as well (see "Local files" in the API overview).

parameters.name: tabId
parameters.description: The ID of an open tab, from `/tabs`; tab ids start at 1. Omitted: all tabs for `/console` and `/network`; a new tab for `/browse`, unless `onlyIfNotExists=true` finds a tab already showing the URL; the active tab for other tab operations. Supplied: exactly that tab. An unknown id returns `404 TAB_NOT_FOUND` (with `details.openTabs`) and a malformed id `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; the request never falls back to another tab. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`tabId must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.

parameters.name: waitUntil
parameters.description: Navigation readiness to wait for. networkidle is deliberately not offered. Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`waitUntil must not be repeated`), on GET and on POST alike: two copies could disagree about when the navigation is done and only the last would be read. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `waitUntil` is governed by the body schema, not by this.

parameters.name: timeoutMs
parameters.description: Budget for viewport settling + navigation. Omitted: the navigation itself may take up to 30000 ms (the server bounds the request with `--request-timeout`). Present: the whole budget, and the server bounds the request by timeoutMs + 5 s. Either way a navigation that runs out of time is a `504 TIMEOUT` (phase navigation). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`timeoutMs must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name does not suppress that: it is governed by the body schema instead. A body that is not a JSON object at all, or that fails the operation's own validation, is rejected first, with its own message and the same status and code.

parameters.name: instanceGeneration
parameters.description: From /metadata; mismatch → 409 INSTANCE_CHANGED (also when no instance exists, and no instance is spawned). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`instanceGeneration must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Make the tab active (focused) after navigation. Strict boolean: spell it `true` or `false` and nothing else. `1`, `0`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `TRUE`, and a present-but-empty `?active=` are each rejected with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`details.field` names the parameter) before any tab is created or reused. A supplied value is never coerced and never silently falls back to the default. ONLY omitting the parameter takes the default. Repeating the key is not an error on this parameter: the instance reads the last occurrence. That leniency is specific to the `/browse` booleans. The server rejects a repeated QUERY key named `url`, `waitUntil`, `script`, `scriptBase64`, `tabId`, `instanceGeneration`, `maxChars`, `includeValues` or `timeoutMs` with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Those name a destination, a program or a bound, where two disagreeing copies must not resolve silently to one. That rule inspects the query string and nothing else: a JSON body property sharing one of those names, array-valued or not, is governed by the operation's body schema instead.

parameters.name: onlyIfNotExists
parameters.description: Reuse an existing tab whose URL already equals the target instead of opening a new one. The reused tab is still navigated (this is tab reuse, not a navigation dedup). Same strict boolean rule as `active`: only `true` or `false`; anything else is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, never coerced.

parameters.name: ignoreGetParameters
parameters.description: Ignore query parameters when checking for existing URL. Same strict boolean rule as `active`: only `true` or `false`; anything else is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, never coerced.

400.description: Validation error - a required parameter is missing or a value is invalid. A missing `url` is `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Missing required parameter: url"; there is no separate code for it. A `url` outside the allowed set (`http`, `https` and `data` URLs, `about:blank`, `chrome:` URLs on Chromium), or one that is not an absolute URL, is `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `details.field` `url`; it is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On a call that has to start the instance, it is also the answer for a launch parameter found invalid only while the instance starts (for example `display`, `chromiumVersion`, a `firefoxExecutablePath` that does not exist, an `extensionsStoreIds` ID the Chrome Web Store does not offer, or `extensions` / `extensionsDir` / `extensionsStoreIds` without `showBrowser=true` or with a directory that does not exist or is not a directory): the message names the parameter, no instance is left running, and the start is not retried. `INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT`: the request came through a `browser-{N}` service hostname, which serves browser `N` only, and a `port`, `browser_id` or `host` in its query, or a `browser_port`, `port`, `display`, `browser_id`, `browser_host` or `host` in its JSON body, names a different instance. On that hostname the platform sets `browser_port` and `display` in the query itself, replacing any value sent, and keeps a `browser_host` the query carries. `details.field` names the parameter. Nothing was run. Call that instance's own hostname, or leave the parameter out.

get.description:
Returns the Chrome DevTools WebSocket URL and HTTP discovery URL for the specified
browser instance. The HTTP URL (`/json/version`) can be used to resolve the WebSocket
endpoint automatically.

**Hoody CDP relay**: In computer deployments these URLs are normally minted on the `cdp-{N}`
hostname (e.g. `https://{projectId}-{computerId}-cdp-{N}.{server}.computers.hoody.com`),
paired 1:1 with the `browser-{N}` instance that owns the debugging session. The relay is
reached HTTP-first: connect with `chromium.connectOverCDP("https://{projectId}-{computerId}-cdp-{N}.{server}.computers.hoody.com/")`, which
fetches `/json/version` to resolve the live WebSocket endpoint before upgrading, and
cold-starts instance `N` on demand if it isn't already running. Only the read-only
discovery endpoints (`/json/version`, `/json/list`, `/json`) and DevTools WebSocket
sessions (`/devtools/browser/<id>`, `/devtools/page/<id>`) are relayed. Mutation endpoints
(`/json/new`, `/json/close`, `/json/activate`) are not exposed.

**Availability**: These URLs are populated when the instance is launched with
`useRemoteDebuggingPort=true` and `browser=chromium`. Otherwise it will be `null`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Controls instance creation behavior.
- Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation.
- When auto-start is disabled globally: set to `true` to create an instance.

Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

get.summary: Accessibility snapshot of a tab with element refs
get.description: Returns Playwright's AI-mode ARIA snapshot (YAML text) of the tab's top document including same-process iframes, with `[ref=…]` element references, plus a `snapshotId`. Refs are valid only while this snapshot is the tab's latest and no MAIN-FRAME navigation has happened (a cross-document commit or a pushState in the top document; a child frame navigating does not invalidate them): use them as `{ref, snapshotId}` targets in /action and /wait. Never creates an instance. Takes the per-tab mutation gate (409 TAB_BUSY while an /action or /browse is in flight). Semantic and CSS targets address the top document only; use a ref to act inside an iframe. Refs are opaque tokens: a prefix like `f2` is Playwright's frame-sequence namespace and says nothing about iframes. Pass refs back verbatim. Entered form values are REDACTED by default (`<value hidden>`); set `includeValues=true` to get them. `url` never carries `user:password@` credentials. LINK TARGETS are filtered too, and a `/url` attribute is one of exactly three things: the page's own bytes unchanged; the bytes before its first `?` or `#` followed by `***`, when something in the reference matches the secret-parameter policy; or the whole value replaced by `***`, when nothing about it can be published safely (a credential in the authority, a reference that does not parse, an encoding that cannot be resolved). A `***` is a REDACTION MARKER and never part of a target: do not follow or request one, and read a truncated target as a page reference whose parameters are unavailable.

parameters.name: includeValues
parameters.description: Include the CONTENTS of form controls in the snapshot. Off by default: the accessibility tree serialises `input.value`, so a snapshot taken after the agent typed a password, card number or token would hand those back on every subsequent loop iteration. With the default, the value of a non-empty textbox, searchbox, spinbutton, slider or editable combobox (an input with a `<datalist>`, or `role=combobox`) renders as `<value hidden>`, whatever its label contains; only a native `<select>` keeps its option names, when it holds nothing but `<option>`, `<optgroup>` and `<hr>` elements and none of them uses `aria-owns` or `aria-labelledby` or is editable (every other node in it keeps its role and ref but not its name or text), and the content of every other combobox, ARIA autocomplete popups and customizable selects with rich option content included, is hidden whole (an empty one renders with no value at all, so the caller can still tell them apart). Content inside an editable region (a `contenteditable` element, or a whole page in `designMode`) is hidden too: the region keeps its role and ref, its contents become `<value hidden>`, and its name is shown only when it is authored (`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at non-editable content); text the snapshot folds from an editor into an enclosing element is hidden there too. If the page cannot be asked in time, the text and computed names on such a page are hidden and the refs are kept. Set to `true` only when the values are known not to be sensitive. Omitted or empty uses the default (false); any other value than `true` or `false` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, and repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`includeValues must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: browser_id

parameters.name: tabId

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Controls instance creation behavior.
- Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation.

Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

400.description: VALIDATION_ERROR: `tabId` is malformed (not a non-negative integer), or the instance address is missing or malformed (`browser_host`, `browser_port`). The message names the parameter. On a call that has to start the instance, it is also the answer for a launch parameter found invalid only while the instance starts (for example `display`, `chromiumVersion`, a `firefoxExecutablePath` that does not exist, an `extensionsStoreIds` ID the Chrome Web Store does not offer, or `extensions` / `extensionsDir` / `extensionsStoreIds` without `showBrowser=true` or with a directory that does not exist or is not a directory): the message names the parameter, no instance is left running, and the start is not retried. `INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT`: the request came through a `browser-{N}` service hostname, which serves browser `N` only, and a `port`, `browser_id` or `host` in its query, or a `browser_port`, `port`, `display`, `browser_id`, `browser_host` or `host` in its JSON body, names a different instance. get.description:
Returns the page in a tab as clean Markdown, for language models and people, with its metadata. Reads the active tab, or `tabId`; with `url`, navigates that tab there first (waiting for `load`, at most 30 seconds) and reads the result.

**Conversion**: the page's current HTML (the main frame only: iframe content and shadow DOM are not included) is read once and converted with [Defuddle](https://github.com/kepano/defuddle) and its default settings. With `onlyMainContent=true` (the default) Defuddle extracts the main content, as a reader view does: navigation, headers, footers, sidebars and comments are left out. With `onlyMainContent=false` the whole `<body>` is kept, after the same cleanup. The Markdown follows Defuddle's conventions (for example tables with merged cells stay HTML tables, MathML becomes LaTeX, a YouTube or X embed becomes `![](url)`). Nothing is fetched from the network during the conversion.

**Links and images**: every link and image target is published the way `/snapshot` publishes link targets. Relative references are resolved against the page (and its `<base>`); a target carrying a secret-named query parameter (a `token`, `code`, `sig` and the like) keeps its path and loses its query and fragment (`https://example.org/cb?***`); a target with credentials in it is removed. Inline `data:` images become their alt text. CSS and SVG attributes that can carry a URL (`style`, `url(...)` presentation attributes, SVG references other than a plain element id such as `#icon`) and `title` tooltips are removed. Visible text is never changed. Use `/html` for the page's raw HTML with the original URLs.

**Size**: conversion cost grows with the number of elements and their nesting, so a page is refused with `422 PAGE_TOO_LARGE` when its HTML is longer than 4 MiB (4194304 characters), has more than 25000 elements, nests elements more than 256 deep, resolves its link and image references to more than 16777216 characters, or has tables that would pad out to more than 500000 cells (`details` names the limit). A long article such as a large Wikipedia page fits; such a page takes several seconds to convert. Other tabs of the same instance keep answering while a page converts and its link and image targets are published: both run off the instance's main thread. An instance converts two pages at a time; further calls wait their turn. A conversion that runs longer than 60 seconds, publishing the link and image targets included, is stopped (`504 TIMEOUT`, `details.phase` `conversion`). `maxChars` cuts the Markdown body at a line boundary.

**Timeout**: the call can include starting the browser instance, so clients wait up to 740 000 ms by default. Deployments started with a longer `--worker-timeout` or `--request-timeout` should pass `timeoutMs` accordingly. When the client stops waiting, a `url` is still navigated to on the server, but the conversion is skipped or stopped.

parameters.name: includeImages
parameters.description: `false` removes images from the Markdown (embeds such as YouTube videos stay). `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `includeImages`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`includeImages must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: includeLinks
parameters.description: `true` adds `links`: every `http`/`https` link on the page, resolved, without fragments, published like the Markdown's links, sorted and deduplicated, at most 10 000. `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `includeLinks`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`includeLinks must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: frontmatter
parameters.description: `true` puts a YAML frontmatter block (`title`, `author`, `site`, `published`, `language`, `description`, `source`; empty keys left out) on top of the Markdown. The block is not counted against `maxChars`. `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `frontmatter`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`frontmatter must not be repeated`).

parameters.name: maxChars
parameters.description: Longest Markdown body returned, in characters. A longer one is cut at the last line break within the limit when there is one after the first character, otherwise at the limit without splitting a surrogate pair; `truncated` is then true. Any value outside 1 to 2000000 is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `maxChars`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`maxChars must not be repeated`).

get.description: Returns buffered browser console messages (console.log, console.error, page errors) from every tab, including tabs the page or a CDP client opened, from their first load on. Keeps the last 500 entries. Object arguments are recorded with their content (on Firefox a preview of at most 2000 characters each, read through the browser's debugger so that recording runs none of the page's code: no getter, toJSON, toString or valueOf, no Proxy trap and no built-in the page replaced; it lists an object's own enumerable properties, a getter reads as `undefined` and is never called, a Proxy shows as `[Proxy]`, and maps, sets, typed arrays (except `BigInt64Array`, `BigUint64Array` and `Float16Array`, which Firefox reports as plain objects), dates, errors and functions show by type only; a tab's previews are built one argument at a time, at most 16 wait and later ones keep the placeholder, and after an object holding a BigInt, a BigInt64Array or BigUint64Array included, the rest of that document's lines keep theirs). Full capture needs the standard engine: on a stealth instance (`stealth=true`, the default) only messages the browser reports itself are recorded (failed resource loads, Content Security Policy violations), never the page's `console.*` calls, uncaught errors or unhandled rejections, and the answer carries `capture: "partial"` with a `reason`; start the instance with `stealth=false` to record everything.

parameters.name: since

get.description:
Returns paginated browsing history entries with optional filters. History is stored persistently. History is recorded for all navigations including API-triggered and manual browsing.

**Scope**: through a `browser-{N}` service hostname the history is browser `N`'s only: `browser_id` defaults to `N`, and any other value is refused with `400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT`. Against a bare server, omitting `browser_id` returns every instance's history.

**Page-driven changes**: every page load is an entry of its own, whoever started it (a link, a form, a script redirect, back/forward to another document); a tab that loads more than 10 pages within any one second (a redirect loop) has the excess not recorded. A page's own URL changes that load no new document (History API updates, hash changes) are written at most once a second: of those inside one second only the newest is kept, so a URL the page passed through in under a second may not appear. Such changes less than 1 second apart within one site (for a `data:` page, one document), with no change to another site in between, are kept as one entry that shows the newest URL and title and keeps the time of the first change, so such an entry can take up to a second to show its final URL. A merged entry takes changes for at most 60 seconds; the next change starts a new entry. Stored `url` and `requestedUrl` are cut to 8192 characters.

delete.description:
Stops one instance and ends everything running in it: open editors,
integrated terminals, tasks and the extension host. Its data
directory (settings, installed extensions, workspace state) is kept,
so the next `GET /api/v1/code` for the same instance starts it again
from there.

This operation never starts an instance. Asking to stop an instance
that is not running answers `404` with the code `unknown-instance`,
and nothing is spawned to answer it.

An instance that is still starting counts as running and its startup
is cancelled. A request that was waiting on that startup is answered
`503`, unless the startup had already finished, in which case it
received a page for the instance this request then stopped. A
restart (`restart=true`) in progress counts the same way, including
while its old child is still exiting: this request answers `200`, the
replacement is not started, and the restart request is answered `503`.

The answer is `200` only once the instance's process has been seen to
exit, or at once when its start is cancelled before a process existed. If it cannot be confirmed to have exited even after being
killed, the answer is `500` and the instance keeps its place in the
deployment's instance limit; send the request again to retry. Until
that process has exited, `GET /api/v1/code` for the same instance
starts nothing and answers `503`.

## Which instance

Inside a Hoody computer the `code-{N}` hostname selects the
instance, as for `GET /api/v1/code`: the edge proxy sets `id` to `N`
and overrides any value sent. To stop instance 5, send this request
to the `code-5` service URL. `id` is required, and read with the same
strict rules as on `GET /api/v1/code`.

## Instances also stop on their own

An instance whose editor has had no open connection for the
deployment's idle timeout is stopped as if by this operation. The
timeout is three hours unless the operator set another or turned it
off. Three hours is also how long the editor keeps a disconnected
session's terminals and extension host for a reconnect, so with the
default settings nothing a user could still have reconnected to is
ended by it.

Only the editor's own report of inactivity stops an instance this way,
asked twice, and any request for the instance that reaches this
service while it decides, or in the two minutes before, keeps it
running. An editor whose report
cannot be trusted (it does not prove it is the process this service
started, or reports no usable time of last activity) is never stopped
automatically.

On a `code-{N}` service URL the edge proxy sets it from the
hostname and overrides any value sent, so a caller there neither
needs to send it nor can change it. It is required: there is no
default instance to stop, so a request without it is answered
`400`.

Read exactly as strictly as the selector on `GET /api/v1/code`: an
unsigned decimal integer, under the literal name `id` only, never
given more than once, and at most `65535 - basePort`.

post.summary: Stage a VS Code extension from a URL
post.description:
Downloads a `.vsix` from a URL and stages it for installation.

## Staging is not installation

The editor installs staged extensions **only while an instance is
starting**. A successful response means the file is in place and the
next start of an instance will attempt to install it, not that any
running editor now has it. The response says so in `appliesAt` and
`requiresRestartToApply`, and `GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` is the
only place installation can be confirmed.

## Scope

Staging is shared across instances: the directory written here is the
one every instance reads at startup, so an extension staged through one
instance is installed by all of them. `stageScope` reports this.

## Replacement

One version of an extension is kept at a time, identified by publisher
and name from the archive's own manifest rather than by filename.
Staging a newer version replaces the older one. A downgrade is refused
unless `allowDowngrade` is set, and the response names what was
replaced.

## Staging while an instance is starting

An instance installs staged extensions as it starts. A stage that lands
during that window can be installed inconsistently: the instance may
record one version's details and hold another version's contents. It is
not a partial or corrupt file, and both versions are ones this service
accepted; it is the wrong pairing.

`GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` shows the mismatch, and restarting
the instance installs whatever is staged at that point. Stage before
starting an instance, rather than during, if this matters to you.

## Where the file may come from

The URL is fetched under the service's outbound policy: `http` and
`https` only, no credentials in the URL, and no address inside the
computer or on a private network, checked again on every redirect.
A refused destination answers `403`. Repeating the request will not
change that answer by itself: nothing in the request, and no setting,
widens the policy. It is not a statement about the future, though. What
a hostname resolves to, and where a redirect points, are both chosen
elsewhere and can change, so a URL refused today can be accepted
tomorrow and the reverse.

A far-side failure answers `502` and may be worth retrying. A redirect
that leads somewhere this service will not follow is a `502` as well,
including one to a scheme other than http or https or to a URL carrying
credentials: the URL you supplied was usable, and a remote party chose
the hop that was not.

Required: a request without an `id` has named no instance and is
rejected rather than defaulted to a first one. The value is an
unsigned decimal integer, under the literal name `id` only, never
given more than once, and at most `65535 - basePort`.

## Where it comes from

On a `code-N` service URL the platform's edge proxy sets it from the
hostname, so a caller behind the edge neither sends it nor can
override it, and the generated clients leave it out of the query for
exactly that reason. It is required because there is no discovery
branch here to fall back to: a request without an `id` has named no
instance and is answered `400`.

get.summary: Staged extensions, and what the instance appears to have installed
get.description:
Reports two different things and keeps them apart.

`desired` is what has been staged for installation. `observed` is what
this instance appears to have installed. They disagree between a stage
and the next restart, which is normal and is the point of reporting
both.

A section that could not be read is reported as `unavailable` rather
than as an empty list: "no extensions" and "could not look" are
different answers and only one of them is a problem. `partial` is true
when either section is in that state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Which instance this request is about.

Required: a request without an `id` has named no instance and is
rejected rather than defaulted to a first one. The value is an
unsigned decimal integer, under the literal name `id` only, never
given more than once, and at most `65535 - basePort`.

## Where it comes from

On a `code-N` service URL the platform's edge proxy sets it from the
hostname, so a caller behind the edge neither sends it nor can
override it, and the generated clients leave it out of the query for
exactly that reason. It is required because there is no discovery
branch here to fall back to: a request without an `id` has named no
instance and is answered `400`.

get.summary: Execute cURL requests over a WebSocket channel
get.description:
Establish a persistent WebSocket connection for multiplexed, validated CurlRequest execution.

This endpoint is separate from `/api/v1/curl/ws`, which only streams async job lifecycle events.

The channel is buffered, except for these streaming cases. When SSE is enabled, body-bearing `2xx` upstream responses with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` stream their events as they arrive if their bodies are unencoded or decoded by the service. With `binary=true`, other body-bearing `2xx` responses also stream, as binary BODY frames, unless their `Content-Length` is 16 KiB or less. Every other response is fully received before its body chunks are sent, and so is every response when the service runs with `--no-sse`. Query parameters configure per-connection limits such as `max_concurrent`, `max_queue`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_request_bytes`, `chunk_bytes`, `stream_timeout_secs`, and `idle_timeout_secs`.

parameters.description: Maximum queued streams waiting for a per-connection execution slot

delete.summary: Cancel a pending or running job, or delete a finished one
delete.description:
Without `purge`: cancel a job that is pending or running. Once cancelled, the job cannot be restarted. Cancelling is idempotent: a job that already finished is left as it is and the call still succeeds.

With `purge=true`: permanently delete a finished job (completed, failed or cancelled). This removes its stored record, response body included, and every download it saved with `save=true`. A job that is still pending or running is refused with 409 `JOB_NOT_FINISHED`: cancel it first, then purge once `GET /api/v1/curl/jobs/{id}` reports it cancelled. A purged job returns 404 `JOB_NOT_FOUND` afterwards.

Finished job records are also deleted automatically after the server's retention period (`--job-retention-hours`, default 7 days); saved downloads are only removed by a purge or the storage API.

post.summary: Execute HTTP request with full cURL capabilities
post.description:
Execute an HTTP request using libcurl with comprehensive configuration options. Supports both synchronous (immediate response) and asynchronous (background job) execution modes. Includes advanced features like retry logic, cookie sessions, and automatic response storage.

A body (`data`, `json` or `form`) with no `method` is sent as `POST`, like curl's `-d`/`--json`; an explicit `method` is always used as given.

**Execution Modes:**
- `sync` (default): waits for the request to finish and returns its response. A body-bearing `2xx` upstream response with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` streams its events as they arrive instead, unless the service runs with `--no-sse` or the event stream stays compressed
- `async`: Returns job ID immediately, executes in background

**Response Modes:**
- `transparent` (default): returns the upstream status and body with hop-by-hop headers removed. When the service decompresses the body, `Content-Encoding` is removed and `Content-Length` adjusted
- `json`: wraps a buffered response in JSON with timing metrics and metadata. An event stream that streams (see `sync`) is sent as the stream even when `json` is requested

**Example Use Cases:**
- API integration with automatic retry
- Large file downloads with progress tracking
- Multi-step authentication flows with session cookies

Recurring requests are created with `POST /api/v1/curl/schedule`; this endpoint runs the request once.

post.description:
Create a new cron-based schedule that executes an HTTP request repeatedly at specified intervals. Schedules are persistent and survive server restarts. Send `enabled: false` to create the schedule disabled; it does not fire until it is enabled with `PATCH /api/v1/curl/schedule/{id}` or `PATCH /api/v1/curl/schedule/{id}/toggle`.

**Cron Expression Format:** 6 fields - `second minute hour day month weekday`
- `0 * * * * *` - Every minute
- `0 0 * * * *` - Every hour
- `0 0 9 * * MON-FRI` - Weekdays at 9 AM
- `0 0 0 * * *` - Daily at midnight
- `0 0 12 1 * *` - Monthly on 1st at noon

**Common Use Cases:**
- Periodic API data collection
- Regular health checks/monitoring
- Scheduled report generation
- Automated backups or synchronization

patch.summary: Update a schedule's cron expression, request or enabled state
patch.description: Change an existing schedule in place: its id, `created_at` and `last_run` are kept. Send any of `cron`, `request` and `enabled`; absent fields keep their current value, and a `request` replaces the whole stored request. Validation is the same as `POST /api/v1/curl/schedule`: the request must pass the same checks, and an enabled schedule needs an expression with a future occurrence. The change applies from the next occurrence; an occurrence already running finishes with the old request. Returns the updated schedule, credentials redacted as in `GET /api/v1/curl/schedule/{id}`. A credential sent back exactly as `GET /api/v1/curl/schedule/{id}` showed it (`[REDACTED]`, or the redacted URL, `json` or `data` body) keeps its stored value, so a schedule can be read, edited and written back. This holds only while the request URL keeps the same scheme, host and port: when changing the destination, send the credentials again or remove them, otherwise the update is refused with 400. Changing only the path or query on the same scheme, host and port keeps them: whoever may update the schedule can already aim its stored credentials at any endpoint of that service.

get.description:
Retrieve a list of all active cookie sessions, sorted by last used time. Sessions enable stateful HTTP interactions by preserving cookies across multiple requests, essential for authentication flows and stateful APIs.

**Session Lifecycle:**
1. Created automatically on first use with session_id
2. Cookies updated after each request
3. By default an idle session can be removed after 30 days. Reusing an expired session ID starts an empty cookie jar. The retention period is configurable (`--session-idle-retention-hours`, default 720); setting it to 0 disables idle-session expiry.

**Common Patterns:**
- Login flow: POST login → save cookies → subsequent requests use session
- API authentication: cookies set by `Set-Cookie` are stored in the session. Send bearer tokens yourself on each request
- Multi-step workflows: Each step uses same session

parameters.name: job_id

schema.description: SSE frames. The first frame is `retry: 5000`. Each event frame is `event: <name>` and `data: <JSON>`; `jobstarted`, `jobcompleted` and `lagged` frames also carry `id:`, the lifecycle `seq` to resume from (`Last-Event-ID` or `since`; a `lagged` frame's `id:` is the `seq` just before the first event still kept); the JSON carries the event name again as `type`: `jobstarted` is `{type, job_id, name?, seq}`, `jobprogress` is `{type, job_id, progress}` (`progress` from 0 to 1), `jobcompleted` is `{type, job_id, status, seq}`, `error` is `{type, message}`, and `lagged` is `{missed, code, min_seq, max_seq, incarnation}` with no `type`. Idle periods get `:` comment heartbeats. The stream does not end on its own.

get.description: Retrieves a complete list of all configured daemon programs with their full configuration details. Supports multiple filters that can be combined: hoody_kit, lazy_load, enabled, boot. Optionally include runtime status for each program.

parameters.name: hoody_kit
parameters.description: Filter by hoody_kit status. Use "true" for Hoody Kit programs only, "false" for user (non-kit) programs only.

parameters.name: lazy_load
parameters.description: Filter by the lazy_load field. Use "true" for lazy-loaded programs only (started on-demand), "false" for programs whose lazy_load is false. This does not tell whether a program auto-starts: filter on `boot` for that.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Filter by enabled status. Use "true" for enabled programs only, "false" for disabled programs only.

parameters.name: boot
parameters.description: Filter by boot status. Use "true" for programs that auto-start on system boot, "false" for manual-start programs.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter by exact program name (e.g. "hoody-agent"). Lazy mode: the proxy resolves the agent BY NAME because it is a standard program with no port_range (the port filter cannot match it) and program ids are positional. Invalid names return 400.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Filter programs by single port number. Returns only programs whose port_range includes this specific port. Example: ?port=8042 returns programs with ranges containing 8042.

parameters.name: port_from
parameters.description: Filter by port range start (must be used with port_to). Returns programs whose port ranges overlap with the specified range. Uses overlap logic: program.start <= port_to AND program.end >= port_from.

parameters.name: port_to
parameters.description: Filter by port range end (must be used with port_from). Returns programs whose port ranges overlap with the specified range. Multiple programs may be returned if their ranges overlap.

parameters.name: include_status
parameters.description: Include runtime status for each program. When true, adds a "status" field to each program showing current running state, instances, and process details.

parameters.name: include_stats
parameters.description: Include resource stats (CPU, memory, process tree) for each running program. Turns status on only when `include_status` is omitted: an explicit `include_status=false` suppresses both status and stats. Where the stats land depends on the program: a standard program gets a top-level `stats`; a port-range program gets one `stats` per running instance, on `status.instances[]`, never at the top level. Each carries pid, started_at, cpu_percent, memory_rss_bytes, process_count and a per-process breakdown.

200.description: Successfully retrieved list of all programs

400.description: A query parameter was unknown or present but unparseable. An unknown parameter (a misspelt filter such as `nmae`) is answered with `code` `INVALID_QUERY` and a message that names it and lists the accepted parameters. An unparseable value (include_status, include_stats, port, port_from, port_to) is rejected too. Neither is silently ignored: a dropped value does not mean "no opinion", it widens the operation to its default. An invalid `port` would return every instance instead of the one named, and an invalid or misspelt filter would return the full list.

value.error: Unknown query parameter 'nmae': accepted parameters are hoody_kit, lazy_load, enabled, boot, name, port, port_from, port_to, include_status, include_stats

post.description:
Creates a new daemon program from a JSON request body. The program is validated and saved. Its definition is installed at once only when it is enabled and has `boot`, `lazy_load`, a `port_range` or an effective `sandbox`; an enabled `boot: true` program is therefore applied during this call and can start at once. An ordinary program is registered when it is first started. A sandboxed program whose definition cannot be applied is a 400 AFTER it was persisted (the error says so). So is an ordinary program whose definition the process manager refuses or cannot confirm it can load, or that could not be written (`saved but NOT applied`). Any other apply failure of an ordinary program is only logged, so a 200 does not prove the definition was installed or that anything started.

For custom programs only (your own code/scripts), not system services.

**Correct examples:** `node app.js`, `python my_script.py`, `ruby custom_server.rb`, `./my-binary`
**Wrong examples:** `apache2`, `nginx`, `postgresql`, `mysql`. Use `systemctl` for these.

**Sandbox.** An optional `sandbox` block confines the program (see `SandboxConfig`). The body is parsed by the handler itself, so a body that is not JSON, a field of the wrong type, an unknown key inside a typed sub-object such as `sandbox`, or a repeated top-level key is a 400 carrying the `{success: false, error: "invalid program body: ..."}` envelope (a repeated key answers `duplicate field "<key>": a repeated key leaves it ambiguous which value applies`). Only a body over the 1 MiB limit is refused with a 413 carrying the same envelope. Unknown TOP-LEVEL keys are ignored, not rejected, with one exception: a key that is a near-miss of `sandbox` (`sandbx`, `sand_box`, `Sandbox`) is a 400, because dropping it silently would run the program UNCONFINED behind a 200. Every controller rejection (that one, a `writable` path overlapping a protected root, a listening set that overlaps another program's ports, `user: root`, `terminal_id`) is a 400 carrying the usual `{success: false, error: ...}` envelope, and nothing is persisted. A block that restricts nothing is stored as absent.

post.description:
Updates an existing program. The path id identifies it; an `id` in the body is ignored. A top-level field that is omitted or `null` keeps its stored value (except `sandbox`, `port_range` and `terminal_id`, where `null` removes the field; removing `port_range` also removes `port_param`, and removing `terminal_id` also removes `terminal_shell` and `terminal_interactive`, unless the request sends them), and the create defaults do NOT apply (changing `user` alone does not recompute `directory`). Three fields are replaced as a unit rather than merged: `environment` replaces the whole map (`{}` clears it), `port_range` needs both `start` and `end`, and a `webhooks` object must carry `enabled` and `urls`, which replace the stored ones while omitted `events`, `timeout` and `retry` keep theirs and supplied `headers` replace the header map. A partial `port_range` or `webhooks` object is a 400 naming the missing field (`missing field `end``). `webhooks: null` does not clear stored webhooks. Unknown top-level keys are ignored, except a near-miss of `sandbox`, which is a 400.

**When it takes effect.** An edit that leaves the program disabled removes its installed definition at once; a removal that fails is a 400 after the edit was saved. An edit to an enabled program with a current or former `boot`, `lazy_load`, a `port_range`, or a current or former effective sandbox is applied before the call returns and can restart the running instance, so changing `boot` alone can restart the running process; an apply failure is a 400 after saving when a sandbox is or was involved, or when the process manager refuses the definition or cannot confirm it can load it, or the definition could not be written (`saved but NOT applied`); any other ordinary apply failure is only logged and still returns 200. Any other enabled program keeps its running definition until its next start.

**Sandbox.** `sandbox` is three-state: absent leaves the current block unchanged, `null` clears it, and an object replaces it as a unit (no field-level merge). A policy rejection is a 400 with the usual `{success: false, error: ...}` envelope and changes nothing; a body that cannot be parsed is a 400 carrying the same envelope (`invalid program body: ...`); only a body over 1 MiB is refused with a 413 carrying the same envelope. An apply that fails AFTER the edit was persisted is also a 400, and the program stays persisted; a persistence or firewall failure is a 500. An accepted change replaces the loaded definition, because the policy revision is part of its definition: the instance running under the old policy stops, and `boot` and `lazy_load` decide whether a new one starts. An edit that normalizes to the same policy may skip the reload. When the change narrows or moves the listening set, the previous revision's ingress rules stay installed until every instance running under them is confirmed stopped; the call returns once the change has been applied; a firewall drain continues in the background and its response body is unchanged, carrying no firewall field. Drain state is visible only through `GET /programs/{id}/sandbox`, which reports `firewall: "draining"` until the old revision is gone.
