get.description:
Counters and gauges in the Prometheus text exposition format 0.0.4, for a scraper or a quick `curl`. Unauthenticated, like health. As on every route, a request that does not come through the program's URL is refused with 403 by the Source IP Guard: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only. Families are named `hoody_pipe_*` and carry only fixed labels, never a pipe name or a client IP:

- `hoody_pipe_build_info{version}` (gauge, always 1) and `hoody_pipe_start_time_seconds` (gauge)
- `hoody_pipe_pipes_active{state="waiting|streaming"}` (gauge): pipes waiting for a counterpart and pipes streaming (each capped at 1000)
- `hoody_pipe_spectators_active` (gauge): open `?progress` streams
- `hoody_pipe_transfers_total{result="completed|failed"}` (counter): transfers that started streaming, one per transfer whatever `n` is
- `hoody_pipe_transferred_bytes_total` (counter): bytes read from senders, counted once (not per receiver), including the part of a transfer that later failed
- `hoody_pipe_hashed_bytes_total` (counter): bytes hashed for `?sha256`
- `hoody_pipe_rejections_total{reason}` (counter): `pending_cap` and `spectator_cap` (one per refused request), `active_cap` (one per refused pipe), `wait_timeout` (one per sender or receiver whose `wait` passed), `idle_timeout` (one per transfer ended by the 5-minute idle limit), `ws_cap` (one per refused `?ws` request), `live_cap` (one per refused live request), `sender_key` (one per POST or PUT refused because the name is held and its sender key is missing or wrong)
- `hoody_pipe_ws_pairs_active{state="waiting|paired"}` (gauge) and `hoody_pipe_ws_relayed_bytes_total` (counter): `?ws` pairs and the message payload bytes they relayed, both directions
- `hoody_pipe_live_viewer_joins_total` (counter) and `hoody_pipe_live_viewers_cut_total{reason="overflow|stall"}` (counter): live viewers counted at their first byte, and those cut off for falling behind (`overflow`) or for taking nothing for 60 s (`stall`)

Only reachable at `/api/v1/pipe/metrics`. A bare `/metrics` returns 404 with the body `[ERROR] '/metrics' is not a valid path. Use '/api/v1/pipe/metrics'.\n`, so a scraper pointed at the root fails at once instead of waiting as a receiver. Both are matched like health (case-insensitive, one trailing `/` or `.` allowed). `HEAD` returns the headers only; `OPTIONS` returns 204 like health; other methods return 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`. Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

text/plain.example:
# HELP hoody_pipe_transfers_total Transfers that started streaming, by how they ended.
# TYPE hoody_pipe_transfers_total counter
hoody_pipe_transfers_total{result="completed"} 12
hoody_pipe_transfers_total{result="failed"} 1

- **HTTP method not supported**: Metrics accepts GET, HEAD and OPTIONS only. Example: `[ERROR] Method POST is not allowed.` What to do: use GET.

get.description:
Receive data from the specified pipe path. The response blocks until a sender connects and starts streaming. Once established, the response body contains the sender's data with original headers forwarded.

**Lifecycle:**
1. Receiver GETs a path → request blocks
2. When a sender POSTs/PUTs to the same path with matching `n`, the pipe establishes
3. Response starts streaming with the sender's data
4. Response completes when sender finishes uploading

**Headers forwarded from sender:**
- `Content-Type`: sender's content type (dangerous types rewritten to text/plain; foreign params dropped except a safe charset)
- `Content-Length`: only when the sender provided a valid `^\d{1,19}$` value AND the body is non-multipart (multipart parts use chunked encoding)
- `Content-Disposition`: if provided (e.g. `attachment; filename="report.pdf"`); a sender-supplied `inline` is upgraded to `attachment` unless the effective Content-Type is on the inline-safe allowlist (image/audio/video/text/plain/application/pdf, excluding image/svg+xml)
- `X-Piping`: custom metadata from sender
- `X-Hoody-Pipe`: custom metadata from sender

Forwarded headers are CRLF-sanitized (Content-Disposition, X-Piping, X-Hoody-Pipe) to prevent header injection.

**Download control:** Receivers can override Content-Disposition behavior using query parameters:
- `?download`: force `attachment` disposition (triggers browser download)
- `?download=false`: suppress Content-Disposition entirely (always display inline)
- `?filename=custom.txt`: set a custom download filename (implies `?download`)
- These work per-receiver: with `n=2`, one receiver can download while the other displays inline

**Multi-receiver:** When `n > 1`, all receivers get identical copies via lockstep fan-out: each chunk is written to every receiver before the next chunk is read from the sender. Memory is bounded to roughly one chunk per receiver, with no per-receiver queuing. Consequence: the slowest receiver paces the entire transfer. Its backpressure applies to the sender and, transitively, to all other receivers. Fast receivers never run ahead of the slowest one.

**Connection ordering:** Receiver can connect before sender: the server holds the connection until sender arrives (up to this receiver's `wait`, default 5 minutes).

**Security headers on a receiver data response** (not on the HTML pages or `?status`):
- `X-Robots-Tag: none`: prevents indexing
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`
- CORS headers reflecting the receiver's Origin

A live viewer gets `X-Hoody-Pipe-Live: 1` and `Cache-Control: no-store` instead of `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`.

Also accessible without prefix (e.g. `GET /myfile`).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
Pipe path name to receive from. It must match the path used by the sender.

Reserved paths (`/help`, `/noscript`, etc.) return their own content on GET instead of acting as pipe receivers.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description:
Expected number of receivers. Must match the sender's `n` value exactly: a mismatch returns 400.

When `n > 1`, the pipe waits for all `n` receivers and the sender before streaming.

With `video`, `share` or `receive` (browser pages), `n` is the receiver or viewer count the page uses; there an invalid value becomes 1 and a value above 256 becomes 256.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description:
Control whether the response triggers a browser download.

- `?download` (bare), `?download=true`, `?download=yes`, `?download=1`: force `Content-Disposition: attachment` (triggers download). Uses sender's filename if available, otherwise pipe path basename. A `live` viewer never gets the pipe path as a filename: without a sender or `filename` value its disposition is a bare `attachment`.
- `?download=false`, `?download=no`, `?download=0`: suppress `Content-Disposition` entirely, even if sender set one (forces inline display).
- Absent: the sender's Content-Disposition is passed through after sanitising. Multipart `form-data` dispositions are auto-converted to `attachment`, and an `inline` disposition is converted to `attachment` unless the content type is an image (not SVG), audio, video, `text/plain` or `application/pdf`.

Works per-receiver: with `n=2`, one receiver can have `?download` and the other can display inline.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description:
Set a custom download filename. Implies `?download`: the response will have `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<value>"`, unless `?download` is also given as `false`, `no` or `0`, which sends no `Content-Disposition` at all.

**Priority:** `?filename` overrides any filename from the sender's Content-Disposition header.

**Sanitization:** Null bytes, CRLF, path separators (`/`, `\`), leading dots, and control characters are stripped. Truncated to 255 characters. Non-ASCII filenames use RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''...` encoding.

A `?filename` that sanitizes to empty falls back to the sender's filename (from its Content-Disposition), then to the pipe path's last segment (sanitized); only when neither gives a usable name is the header a bare `attachment`. A live viewer gets neither fallback: the live stream carries no sender filename and no path, so it gets a bare `attachment`.

With `receive` (browser page), the sanitized value pre-fills the page's "Save as" field and names the download.

parameters.name: video
parameters.description:
Return an HTML page with an embedded MSE (MediaSource Extensions) video player instead of raw pipe data. The player page fetches the raw stream internally, so no pipe receiver slot is consumed by the page itself. The page does not contain the pipe name: the player fetches its own page URL (with `live`, `n` and `wait` as the page uses them), so a link that shows only its own URL keeps the name to itself and still plays.

**Browser detection:** Only serves the HTML player when the client sends `Accept: text/html` (i.e. a browser) and no `X-Pipe-Stream: 1` header. Non-browser clients (VLC, mpv, curl, ffplay) with `?video` fall through to normal pipe receiver behavior and get the raw stream, ensuring automatic compatibility with media players. The player's own fetch sends `X-Pipe-Stream: 1` and gets the stream the same way.

**Auto-detection:** The player detects the container/codec from the stream's first bytes:
- WebM (VP8/VP9/AV1 + Opus/Vorbis), or audio-only WebM (Opus/Vorbis)
- MP4/fMP4 (H.264/H.265/VP09/AV01 + AAC)
- MPEG-TS is recognized, but most browsers cannot play it: the player then says so. Play MPEG-TS in a media player (VLC, mpv, ffplay) from the same URL.

**UI features:**
- Click to unmute (autoplay requires muted)
- Right-click to pause/resume
- Status overlay: "Waiting for stream…", "Connected", "Stream ended"; for audio-only streams a lasting "Audio — click to unmute" / "Playing audio"
- Plays each stream to its end, including a short file that arrives all at once, and keeps waiting on the path: the next stream sent there replaces it at once, even if the earlier one has not finished playing
- With `?n=N`, the N players may be tabs of one browser
- Without `live`, never skips content: a stream that fell behind stays behind, and the player reads at most 45 s ahead of playback. With `?video&live`, a player that falls behind jumps to the live edge
- Playback that stops for 1.5 s with media buffered ahead moves on to that media
- A valid `wait` on the player URL is used by each of its receives (how long it waits for a sender); an invalid one is ignored and the default applies

**Values:** `?video` (bare), `?video=true`, `?video=yes`, `?video=1` → show player. `?video=false`, `?video=no`, `?video=0` → normal pipe receiver.

**Security:** CSP with nonces (`script-src`, `style-src`), `connect-src 'self'`, `media-src blob:`, `default-src 'none'`.

parameters.name: progress
parameters.description:
Return real-time transfer progress as a Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream or HTML dashboard. Does NOT consume a pipe receiver slot: spectators are completely independent of the transfer.

**Accept header routing:**
- `Accept: text/event-stream` → SSE stream (EventSource, curl)
- `Accept: text/html` → HTML dashboard page (browser)
- `Accept: */*` or missing → SSE stream (default to data, not markup)

**SSE event types:**
- `state`: state snapshots: `idle`, `waiting` or `streaming` while a transfer runs. The end arrives as a `done` event (its `state` is `complete` or `failed`), sent only to spectators connected when the transfer ends. A spectator that connects after the end gets no event and no final state: its request is answered `204 No Content` (see **After a transfer**)
- `progress`: during streaming (throttled 250ms): bytesTransferred, speed, ETA, receivers
- `done`: terminal event with final stats (bytesTransferred, duration, avgSpeed, `reason` when failed, `sha256` (the digest with `?sha256` on a complete transfer, else null) and `transferId`)
- On a live stream (`live`), every `state` and `progress` event (the first ones a spectator gets on connecting included) also carries `live: true` and `totalReceivers: null`; `activeReceivers` is the viewers watching now, and a viewer joining or leaving sends a `progress` event (within the 250 ms throttle). `totalBytes` and `eta` are null.

**State machine:** `idle` (no pipe) → `waiting` (sender/receivers connecting) → `streaming` (data flowing) → `complete` or `failed`

**DoS protections:** Max 50 spectators per path. A `?progress` stream stays open for at most 30 minutes (EventSource reconnects after it closes). When 500 names have an open `?progress` stream or a waiting or running transfer, a subscription to another name gets 429 (names already counted stay allowed); a finished transfer with no open progress stream does not count.

**After a transfer:** after a transfer on the path finishes, the SSE request is answered `204 No Content` for up to 30 s, until the path is used again (no stream, so EventSource does not reconnect); the HTML dashboard then shows "Transfer already finished". The dashboard's elapsed time follows the `elapsed` field of `progress` events, so it counts from the transfer start.

**Values:** `?progress` (bare), `?progress=true`, `?progress=yes`, `?progress=1` → show progress. `?progress=false`, `?progress=no`, `?progress=0` → normal pipe receiver.

**Security:** HTML dashboard uses CSP with nonces. Pipe path HTML-escaped. SSE includes `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for Nginx compatibility.

parameters.name: receive
parameters.description:
Return the receive page instead of raw pipe data. The page itself takes no receiver slot.

**Browser detection:** like `video`, only a client whose `Accept` header includes `text/html` gets the page. Other clients with `?receive` fall through to the normal receiver and get the data.

**What the page does:** it shows the pipe name and whether a sender is waiting (from the `?progress` stream). On **Receive**, or by itself with `autostart=1`, the browser's download manager receives `/{path}?download` (plus `n` and `filename`), so the data streams to disk at any size without passing through the page. Progress and the result are in the browser's downloads list: the page cannot see the download and never reports it as finished. It fails with the server's error text, for example `Timed out waiting for sender.` when no sender comes within 5 minutes (or the `wait` given), or a receiver-count mismatch; **Receive again** retries. What is happening on the path for all its senders and receivers (no sender yet, a sender waiting for receivers, a transfer running) is shown as information only, under a "Status for this name" label; while it cannot be read the page says `Status unavailable, retrying…`. **Cancel** frees the receiver slot while the receive waits; a download that has already started continues in the browser's downloads. Without JavaScript it shows a plain download link.

**Page parameters:** `n` (receiver count, editable on the page), `filename` (download name), `autostart`, and the receiver's own `wait` and `sha256`, forwarded to its download (and to the no-JavaScript link). An invalid `wait` is dropped there. The page shows no checksum: compare one with `?status&transfer=<id>` from a client that reads the `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id` header.

**Values:** `?receive` (bare), `?receive=true`, `?receive=yes`, `?receive=1` → page. `?receive=false`, `?receive=no`, `?receive=0` → normal pipe receiver.

**Precedence:** with several page parameters a browser gets `video`, then `progress`, then `share`, then `receive`. With `video` on, the other page parameters are ignored for every client: a browser gets the player, and the player's own request (`X-Pipe-Stream: 1`) or any other client gets the data, so a link showing only a `video` URL never reaches a page that shows the name.

**Security:** CSP with nonces, `connect-src 'self'`, `frame-src 'self'`, no external resources, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Values from the URL are only rendered as escaped text. The page uses no cookies or browser storage.

bare.summary: Bare param (receive page in a browser)

parameters.name: share
parameters.description:
Return the share page: stream the screen (a screen, window or tab, optionally with its audio), a camera with microphone, or the microphone alone, live to the viewers of `/{path}?video`. The page itself takes no receiver slot.

**Browser detection:** like `video`, only a client whose `Accept` header includes `text/html` gets the page. Other clients with `?share` fall through to the normal receiver.

**What the page does:** Start asks the browser for the capture (the user picks the screen, window or tab in the browser's own picker), records it as WebM (a non-live video share falls back to MP4 in a browser that cannot record WebM) and sends it to the path as one streaming upload. The page shows a link for viewers (`?video`, with `n` when it is above 1; copy button and QR code), viewers connected, streaming state and elapsed time. Stop, or ending the share from the browser's own controls, finishes the stream; Start again on the same path reconnects the viewers. A share nobody joins ends after the server's 5-minute wait (not with Live, which starts at once). A browser that cannot stream an upload gets a clear "not supported" message.

**Live:** with the Live box ticked (`live=1` on the page URL) the upload is a `live` broadcast (`POST /{path}?live`): it starts at once, viewers join and leave at any time through `?video&live=1` (each from the next keyframe; the page asks the recorder for one every 2 s), `n` is ignored, and the page shows the viewers watching now from `?progress`. Live needs a WebM recording; a browser that cannot record WebM gets a "not supported" message.

**Page parameters:** `source`, `audio`, `surface`, `quality`, `fps`, `live`, `n` (viewers). They only pre-fill the controls: capture always starts with the user's click on Start.

**Values:** `?share` (bare), `?share=true`, `?share=yes`, `?share=1` → page. `?share=false`, `?share=no`, `?share=0` → normal pipe receiver.

**Security:** CSP with nonces, `connect-src 'self'`, no external resources, `Cache-Control: no-store`. The page uses no cookies or browser storage.

bare.summary: Bare param (share page in a browser)

parameters.name: autostart
parameters.description: Receive page (`receive`) only: `1`, `true`, `yes` or bare starts the receive without a click once the page has loaded. Any other value, or none, waits for the user's click. Ignored on every other request.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Share page (`share`) only. Pre-selects the source. `screen` (default) is a screen, window or tab; `camera` is a camera with microphone; `audio` is the microphone alone. Invalid → `screen`.

parameters.name: audio
parameters.description: Share page (`share`) only. `1`, `true`, `yes` or bare pre-checks "include audio" for a screen share (tab or system audio, where the browser offers it). Default off.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: Share page (`share`) only. Which kind of surface the browser's picker offers first. `monitor` (a whole screen), `window` or `browser` (a tab). The user still makes the choice. Default no hint.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Share page (`share`) only. Capture size and bit rate. `low` (about 480p), `medium` (about 720p, default) or `high` (about 1080p). Invalid → `medium`.

parameters.name: fps
parameters.description: Share page (`share`) only. Frames per second for screen and camera, 1-60. Invalid → 30.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Return one JSON snapshot of the name (`PipeStatus`) instead of receiving. It takes no receiver slot, is answered at once and is never held open; poll it from scripts and agents that cannot hold a `?progress` stream. Checked before every other parameter (`progress`, `share`, `receive`, `n`, `wait`, and the modes `live`, `ws` and `live` with `ws`), for browsers too. With `video` on it is not answered: a link that shows only a `video` URL passes other keys through, and the snapshot carries the sender's own transfer id. Without `video`, `HEAD` with `?status` returns the headers only. A POST/PUT with `?status` ignores it and is a sender as usual (a live sender with `live`).

- `state`: `idle` (nobody on the name; an unused name is idle, not 404), `waiting`, `streaming`, `complete`, `failed`
- `kind`: `null` when idle, `"pipe"` for a transfer, `"ws"` for a WebSocket pair (`ws`), `"live"` for a live stream (`live`)
- `peers`: with `"ws"`, the peers connected now (0-2); `null` for a transfer
- `transferId`: set from when the transfer starts streaming, or from the sender's arrival when it chose its own (`transfer` on the sender); the same value receivers get in `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`
- `hasSender`, `activeReceivers`, `totalReceivers`, `bytesTransferred`, `totalBytes`, `speed` (bytes/s), `eta` (s), `elapsed` (s): the `?progress` fields; `speed` is the average since streaming started, and in `complete`/`failed` `elapsed` and `speed` are frozen at the end
- `reason`: why it failed (`Timed out`, `Idle timeout`, `Sender disconnected`, ...), else `null`
- `sha256`: the digest in `complete` when `?sha256` was on, else `null`

A finished transfer stays visible for 30 s (at most the 1000 most recent ones), then the name reads `idle`; a new sender or receiver on the name starts a fresh `waiting`. Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Values:** `?status` (bare), `true`, `yes`, `1` → snapshot; `false`, `no`, `0` → normal receiver.

parameters.name: transfer
parameters.description:
With `status`: answer for one transfer, by the id a receiver got in `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id` or the id a sender chose with its own `transfer`, even after the name was reused or its 30 s linger ended. A `?sha256` transfer, and every transfer with a sender-chosen id, leaves a receipt (state, reason, digest, bytes) kept 10 minutes (at most 1000; the oldest go first), so a receiver verifies its bytes after it has read them all: `complete` with the same `sha256` means the bytes match. A sender-chosen id answers from the sender's arrival on (`waiting`). An id that is neither the name's current transfer nor a kept receipt for this name is 404.

A `transfer` on a `ws` upgrade is 400 (with `status`, the snapshot is answered before `ws` is looked at).

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: How long this receiver waits for the sender (and the other receivers of an `n` transfer), in seconds, counted from its own arrival: an integer from 1 to 3600 (default 300). When it passes it gets 408 `Timed out waiting for sender.` (no sender connected) or `Timed out waiting for receivers.` (the sender is there, fewer than `n` receivers are), and a waiting sender sees `[INFO] A receiver disconnected.` and keeps waiting. Anything else (`abc`, `1.5`, `0`, `3601`, or a bare `?wait`) is a 400 and nothing is registered.

parameters.name: ws
parameters.description:
WebSocket relay: open a duplex message connection on the name instead of receiving. Send `GET /{path}?ws` with a WebSocket upgrade (`Upgrade: websocket`; a plain GET is 426). Two peers on the same name are paired 1:1: every message one sends reaches the other with its type (text or binary) and boundaries kept. The first peer is accepted at once (101) and its messages are held until the second arrives (at most 4096 messages / 2 MiB); it waits `wait` seconds (default 300), then is closed with 4408 `Timed out waiting for peer.`. A third peer is 409. Behind HTTP/2 a browser opens the socket over HTTP/1.1 (no extended CONNECT is needed).

A name holds one kind of session: a name with an HTTP transfer (sender or receivers) refuses `?ws` with 409, and a name with a WebSocket pair refuses senders and receivers with 409. `?status` reports a pair as `kind: "ws"` with `peers` 0-2; `?progress` sees its state and byte counts.

**Subprotocol:** the first peer's `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` choice (its first offered token, echoed back) is latched for the pair; the second peer must offer that token, or offer none when the first offered none (else 409).

**Limits:** messages up to 1 MiB (a bigger one closes its sender's connection with 1009, and the other peer is closed with 1009 `Message too big.`). Each direction buffers at most 2 MiB for a slow reader; past that the pair is closed with 1013. Idle peers are pinged; one that does not answer within about 120 s is dropped.

**Close codes:** a peer's close is forwarded to the other: 1000-1003, 1007-1014 and 3000-4999 as sent; 1005 (no code) as 1000; anything else (1006, a dropped connection) as 1001 `Peer disconnected.`. The relay's own: 1013 `Relay buffer full: no peer yet.` / `Relay buffer full: the reader is too slow.` / `Relay dropped a message.`, 4408 `Timed out waiting for peer.`, 1011 `Internal error.`, 1001 `Server shutting down.`.

Not with `n` (400). `live` with `ws` is 400 before any other check except `status` without `video`, with or without an upgrade. `wait` applies as for receivers.

**Values:** `?ws` (bare), `true`, `yes`, `1` → WebSocket relay; `false`, `no`, `0` → normal receiver.

**Upgrade response:** an accepted peer gets `101 Switching Protocols`; the first peer gets it at once, before the second arrives.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description:
Watch a live stream (a sender with `?live`): join at any time, leave and rejoin at will. With no live sender yet, the viewer waits like a receiver (`wait`, default 300 s, then 408 `Timed out waiting for sender.`). The body is a **suffix** of the stream: no `Content-Length`, `X-Hoody-Pipe-Live: 1`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, no `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`. A WebM stream starts with its header, sent as soon as it is known so the response begins without waiting for a keyframe, then a Cluster that begins with a video keyframe (any Cluster for audio-only); other bodies start at the next chunk. A live viewer gets none of the sender's own metadata: no `X-Piping` or `X-Hoody-Pipe`, and of its `Content-Disposition` only the type, and only `inline`, `attachment` or `form-data` (as `attachment`), never a filename.

**Slow viewers:** a viewer that falls 2 MiB behind skips whole Clusters (WebM) until it has caught up to 512 KiB, resuming at a keyframe Cluster. One more than 8 MiB or 4096 pieces behind, one that takes nothing for 60 s, or the most-behind one when the server's live memory budget is full, is cut: its body ends without the chunked terminator. The others are never slowed.

**Ending:** after the sender's clean end a viewer takes what it was already sent (up to 60 s), then its body ends normally; if the sender fails, every viewer is cut. A viewer's response counts against the limits until it disconnects, or until 35 s after its body ended cleanly (6 s after it was cut).

**Plain GET:** a GET without `live` on a name whose live stream is running joins it the same way (a suffix, marked `X-Hoody-Pipe-Live: 1`). While `?live` viewers wait for a sender, a plain GET or `live=0` is 409. `?video&live` serves the player for a live stream; on `?share` (a browser), `live=1` pre-ticks the page's Live box.

Not with `n` above 1, `sha256` or `ws` (400). At most 256 viewers per stream and 4096 live viewer responses in all (429).

**Values:** `?live` (bare), `true`, `yes`, `1` → watch live; `false`, `no`, `0` → an ordinary receiver (409 on a live name).

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description:
Ask the server to hash the transfer (a receiver can switch it on alone). Read `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`, hash the bytes as you receive them, then compare with `?status&transfer=<id>` (see `transfer`). The digest cannot come in-band: response headers go out before the body, and HTTP trailers are not sent.

**Values:** `?sha256` (bare), `true`, `yes`, `1` → on; `false`, `no`, `0` → off.

200.description:
Streamed data from sender, or, with `status`, a `PipeStatus` JSON snapshot, or, with `progress`, `video`, `share` or `receive` and an `Accept` header that includes `text/html` (a browser), the progress dashboard, the video player, the share page or the receive page as `text/html`. Content type of streamed data matches what the sender sent (dangerous types rewritten to text/plain; foreign params dropped except a safe charset).

Forwarded headers (when present on the sender side and not stripped/capped): Content-Type, Content-Length (only when the sender sent a valid `^\d{1,19}$` value AND the body is non-multipart), Content-Disposition, X-Piping, X-Hoody-Pipe.

Always set on receiver response: `X-Robots-Tag: none`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`. CORS headers reflect the receiver's request Origin.

A live viewer (`live`, or a plain GET on a running live stream) gets `X-Hoody-Pipe-Live: 1` and `Cache-Control: no-store` instead of `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`, and never `Content-Length`.

X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id.description: This transfer's id, for `?status&transfer=<id>`, either a generated UUID or the id the sender chose with `transfer`. On receiver data responses only (not on live viewers).

X-Hoody-Pipe-Live.description: `1` on a live viewer's response: the body is a suffix of a live stream

X-Robots-Tag.description: Always `none`, which discourages indexing of pipe payload

Access-Control-Expose-Headers.description: `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`, plus `X-Piping, X-Hoody-Pipe` when the sender provided either custom header; live viewers: `X-Hoody-Pipe-Live` only

204.description: With `progress` on an SSE request (`Accept` names `text/event-stream`, or does not name `text/html`), when the last transfer on the name finished (`complete` or `failed`) less than 30 s ago and the name has not been used again. The response has no body and sends no event, not even the final state, so EventSource does not reconnect. Read the result with `?status`, or with `?status&transfer=<id>` for a kept receipt. A browser asking for the progress dashboard gets the page (200) instead, and the page shows "Transfer already finished".

400.description:
Bad request: invalid parameters, active transfer, slots full, or n mismatch. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Service Worker request blocked**: Requests with `Service-Worker: script` header are rejected to prevent service worker registration via pipe paths. Example: `[ERROR] Service Worker requests are not allowed.` What to do: do not register service workers via pipe paths.
- **Path contains forbidden characters**: The path has an encoded control character (`%00`-`%1F` or `%7F`), an encoded slash or backslash (`%2F`, `%5C`), or a percent-escape that does not decode (such as `%zz`). Example: `[ERROR] Path contains forbidden characters.` What to do: use a name without those characters.
- **Path has an active transfer**: A transfer is already streaming on this path: no new receivers can join. Example: `[ERROR] This name is already in use by an active transfer.` What to do: wait for the transfer to complete, or use a different path.
- **All receiver slots taken**: All `n` receiver slots for this path are occupied. Example: `[ERROR] All 2 receiver slot(s) for this name are already taken.` What to do: wait for a receiver to disconnect, or use a different path.
- **Invalid receiver count**: `n` must be a decimal integer from 1 to 256. A value that is not a plain decimal number (such as `-1`, `1.5` or `2x`) gets `[ERROR] Invalid receiver count — "n" must be a positive integer.`; `0` gets `[ERROR] Receiver count must be at least 1 (got 0).`; a value above 256 gets, for example, `[ERROR] Receiver count too high (max 256, got 300).` What to do: set `n` between 1 and 256.
- **Receiver count mismatch**: This receiver's `n` doesn't match existing sender/receivers on this path. Example: `[ERROR] Receiver count mismatch — expected 2 but got 1.` What to do: use the same `n` value as the sender.
- **Invalid wait**: `wait` is not a decimal integer (or is empty). Example: `[ERROR] Invalid wait — "wait" must be an integer number of seconds (1-3600).` What to do: set `wait` to whole seconds between 1 and 3600.
- **Wait out of range**: `wait` is below 1 or above 3600 seconds. Example: `[ERROR] Wait out of range (1-3600 seconds, got 0).` What to do: set `wait` between 1 and 3600.
- **Invalid transfer id**: With `status`, `transfer` is not a transfer id (16-64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`). Example: `[ERROR] Invalid transfer id.` What to do: pass the value of the `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id` response header.
- **n with live**: `n` other than 1 on a live join (`live`, or a plain GET on a running live stream). Example: `[ERROR] "n" cannot be combined with "live".` What to do: drop `n`.
- **sha256 with live**: A live viewer gets a suffix; there is no digest to verify. Example: `[ERROR] "sha256" cannot be combined with "live".` What to do: drop `sha256`.
- **transfer with ws**: A WebSocket pair has no transfer id. Example: `[ERROR] "transfer" is not supported with ?ws.` What to do: drop `transfer`.
- **n with ws**: A WebSocket pair has exactly two peers; `n` is refused. Example: `[ERROR] "n" is not supported with ?ws (a WebSocket pair has exactly two peers).` What to do: drop `n`; use one name per pair.
- **live with ws**: `live` and `ws` cannot be combined. Example: `[ERROR] "live" cannot be combined with "ws".` What to do: use one of them.
- **Invalid subprotocol offer**: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` is not a comma-separated list of tokens. Example: `[ERROR] Invalid Sec-WebSocket-Protocol token.` What to do: offer RFC 7230 tokens only.
- **Invalid WebSocket handshake**: The upgrade request was refused by the WebSocket layer (for example a missing or bad `Sec-WebSocket-Key`). Example: `[ERROR] Invalid WebSocket handshake.` What to do: use a WebSocket client library.

404.description:
With `status&transfer=<id>`, the id is neither the name's current transfer nor a kept receipt for this name. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Unknown or expired transfer**: Receipts are kept for `?sha256` transfers and transfers with a sender-chosen id only, 10 minutes, at most 1000. Example: `[ERROR] Unknown or expired transfer.` What to do: look the transfer up sooner, or treat the digest as unavailable (not as a mismatch).

text/plain.example: [ERROR] Unknown or expired transfer.

405.description:
Method not allowed. The body is a plain-text message:

- **HTTP method not supported**: Pipe paths accept GET, POST, PUT, OPTIONS, and HEAD with `?status` (not beside `?video`). `Allow` lists HEAD only when `status` is on and `video` is not. Example: `[ERROR] Method DELETE is not allowed. Use GET, POST, or PUT.` What to do: use GET to receive data.

408.description:
Timeout: the transfer did not start within this receiver's `wait` (default 5 minutes), counted from its own arrival. The plain-text body names the missing side:

- **Timed out waiting for sender**: Waited `wait` seconds (default 300) and no sender was connected. Example: `[ERROR] Timed out waiting for sender.` What to do: retry, and make sure sender and receiver connect within the wait.
- **Timed out waiting for receivers**: Waited `wait` seconds (default 300); the sender is connected, but fewer than `n` receivers are. The sender keeps its own wait. Example: `[ERROR] Timed out waiting for receivers.` What to do: retry, and make sure all `n` receivers connect within the wait.

text/plain.example: [ERROR] Timed out waiting for sender.

409.description:
The name holds another kind of session, or (with `ws`) its WebSocket pair is full or uses another subprotocol. The body is a plain-text message:

- **WebSocket pair full**: Two peers are already on the name. Example: `[ERROR] This name already has two WebSocket peers.` What to do: use another name, or wait for the pair to close.
- **Name in use by an HTTP transfer**: `ws` on a name with a waiting or streaming sender or receiver. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by an HTTP transfer.` What to do: use another name, or wait until `?status` reads `idle`.
- **Name in use by a WebSocket pair**: A sender or receiver on a name with a WebSocket pair. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a WebSocket pair.` What to do: use another name, or wait until the pair closes.
- **Subprotocol does not match the peer's**: The first peer latched a subprotocol (or none); this peer did not offer it (or offered one). Example: `[ERROR] The peer on this name uses subprotocol 'chat.v1'; offer it in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol.` What to do: offer the same subprotocol as the first peer, or none when it offered none.
- **Name in use by a live stream**: `live=0`, or a plain GET while `?live` viewers wait for a sender. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a live stream. Add ?live to watch.` What to do: add `?live`.
- **Name in use by an ordinary transfer**: `live` on a name with a waiting or streaming ordinary sender or receiver. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a normal transfer.` What to do: use another name, or wait until `?status` reads `idle`.

text/plain.example: [ERROR] This name already has two WebSocket peers.

414.description:
Path too long. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Path exceeds length limit**: Path exceeds 1024 characters. Example: `[ERROR] Path too long (max 1024 characters).` What to do: use a shorter path.

426.description:
`ws` on a request that is not a WebSocket upgrade. The body is a plain-text message:

- **WebSocket upgrade required**: `?ws` needs `Connection: Upgrade` and `Upgrade: websocket`. Example: `[ERROR] ?ws needs a WebSocket upgrade (Upgrade: websocket).` What to do: open the URL with a WebSocket client (ws:// or wss://).

429.description:
Too many transfers. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Pending transfer limit reached**: Server has 1000 pending transfers. Example: `[ERROR] Too many pending transfers. Try again later.` What to do: wait and retry.
- **Active transfer limit reached**: Server has 1000 active transfers: pipe established but cannot stream. Example: `[ERROR] Server at maximum active transfer capacity. Try again later.` What to do: wait for transfers to finish, then retry.
- **WebSocket pair limit reached**: Server has 500 WebSocket pairs (waiting or paired); joining an existing pair is still allowed. Example: `[ERROR] Too many WebSocket pairs. Try again later.` What to do: wait and retry.
- **Live stream full**: The live stream has 256 viewers (waiting, watching, ended cleanly in the last 35 s, or cut in the last 6 s). Example: `[ERROR] This live stream is full (256 viewers).` What to do: retry later.
- **Live viewer limit reached**: Server has 4096 live viewer responses (waiting, watching, ended cleanly in the last 35 s, or cut in the last 6 s). Example: `[ERROR] Too many live viewers. Try again later.` What to do: wait and retry.
- **Progress spectators full**: 50 `?progress` streams are open on this path. Example: `[ERROR] Too many spectators on this path. Try again later.` What to do: retry later.
- **Spectator groups full**: 500 names have open `?progress` streams or a waiting or running transfer, and this name is not one of them. Example: `[ERROR] Too many spectator groups. Try again later.` What to do: retry later.

501.description:
The server is shutting down. The body is a plain-text message:

- **WebSocket relay not enabled**: A `?ws` request arrived while the server was shutting down. Example: `[ERROR] WebSocket relay is not enabled on this server.` What to do: retry after the server restarts.

503.description:
The server is shutting down; a `?live` viewer still waiting for a sender is answered at once. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Server shutting down**: A `?live` viewer waiting for a sender when the server stops. Example: `[ERROR] Server shutting down.` What to do: retry after the restart.

next_steps.reason: A sender must POST/PUT to the same path for data to flow

prerequisites.reason: Check server health and capacity

post.description:
Send data to the specified pipe path. The sender's request body is streamed directly to receiver(s) when they connect, with no server-side storage.

**Lifecycle:**
1. Sender POSTs to a path → gets back a streaming response with `[INFO]` status messages
2. Server waits for `n` receivers to connect (default: 1)
3. Once all receivers connect, data streams from sender to all receivers simultaneously
4. Sender receives `[INFO] Upload complete.` then `[INFO] Transfer complete.`

**Status messages** (streamed to sender as text/plain):
```
[INFO] Waiting for 1 receiver(s) to connect...
[INFO] Streaming to 1 receiver(s)...
[INFO] Upload complete.
[INFO] Transfer complete.
```

**Multipart uploads:** When Content-Type matches `multipart/form-data` (case-insensitive), the server extracts the first *file* part (non-file form fields are drained and skipped) and streams its contents. The part's Content-Type and Content-Disposition are forwarded to receivers. The transfer ends when that part ends: anything after it in the body is ignored, and the server stops reading the body once the transfer finishes. A body cut off or dropped before the chosen part ends fails the transfer: the sender gets `[ERROR] Transfer failed`, receivers still waiting get 500, and a receiver already streaming sees its body end with an error. **Content-Length is NOT forwarded for multipart inputs** (the response uses chunked transfer encoding): the part's declared byte count is unreliable as a receiver-side length and forwarding it re-introduces response-smuggling/desync risks. If the body has no file part, the first form field named `input_text` (the noscript page's text mode, capped at 1 MiB) is sent instead, as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`; a file part anywhere in the body always wins over it. A multipart body with neither, or whose `input_text` exceeds 1 MiB with no file part, is rejected with a `[ERROR] Transfer failed` status and receivers receive 500. Slow-loris bound: parsing aborts if no part arrives within 30 s, and the upload times out if the body stops making progress for 5 minutes.

**Custom headers:** Set `X-Hoody-Pipe` or `X-Piping` request headers to forward arbitrary metadata to receivers. Each header is capped at 8 KiB (over-cap headers are dropped) and CRLF/control chars are stripped. The receiver response carries `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Piping, X-Hoody-Pipe` only when at least one was supplied.

**Content-Type safety:** Dangerous MIME types that execute scripts in browsers (text/html, image/svg+xml, application/javascript, the full WHATWG JS-essence list, XHTML/XML) are rewritten to `text/plain`. Parameters are stripped except for a single safe charset (`utf-8`/`us-ascii`/`iso-8859-1`). Embedded CR/LF and control chars are dropped.

**Connection ordering:** Either sender or receiver(s) can connect first: the server holds the early party until counterparts arrive.

**Limits:**
- Path length: max 1024 characters
- Receiver count (`n`): 1–256
- Pending transfers: max 1000 server-wide
- Active transfers: max 1000 server-wide
- Waiting for receivers: `wait` seconds (default 300, at most 3600)

Also accessible without prefix (e.g. `POST /myfile`).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
Unique pipe path name. Must not be a reserved path (`/`, `/help`, `/noscript`, `/favicon.ico`, `/robots.txt`). POST/PUT to a reserved path return 400; any other method except GET/HEAD/OPTIONS returns 405 with `[ERROR] Method <verb> is not allowed.\n` and `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`.

Examples: `myfile`, `transfer123`, `secret.png`, `logs/today`

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of receivers to wait for before starting the transfer. All receivers get identical copies of the data (fan-out). Must be a positive integer, max 256.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
How long this sender waits for its `n` receivers, in seconds, counted from its own arrival: an integer from 1 to 3600 (default 300). When it passes, the status stream ends with `[ERROR] Timed out waiting for receivers.` Receivers already waiting keep their own `wait`, so another sender may still come for them. Anything else (`abc`, `1.5`, `0`, `3601`, or a bare `?wait`) is a 400 and nothing is registered, so a script is never given a shorter wait than it asked for.

**Through the Hoody edge:** a sender whose large body is still waiting is cut after about 30 minutes; receivers and small senders can wait the full hour. For long waits with large files, let the receiver wait (`?wait=3600`) and start the sender once `?status` shows it.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description:
Compute the SHA-256 of the bytes forwarded to receivers (for multipart, of the file part or `input_text`, which is what receivers get). On a complete transfer the status stream gets `[INFO] SHA-256: <64 hex>` between `[INFO] Upload complete.` and `[INFO] Transfer complete.`, and the digest is in the `?progress` `done` event and in `?status`. A failed transfer has no digest. Any receiver can switch hashing on as well. Hashing adds processing overhead per byte, so it is opt-in.

**Values:** `?sha256` (bare), `true`, `yes`, `1` → on; `false`, `no`, `0` → off.

parameters.name: transfer
parameters.description:
This transfer's own id instead of a generated one: 16-64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. A sender cannot read response headers while it uploads, so it picks the id up front to follow its own transfer with `?status&transfer=<id>`. The id is the `transferId` in `?status` from the sender's arrival (also while it waits), the `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id` receivers get, and the `done` event's `transferId`. A transfer with its own id leaves a receipt for every outcome, kept 10 minutes: `complete`, or `failed` with its `reason`, also when it ended before streaming (`Timed out waiting for receivers`, `Sender disconnected`, `Server at capacity`).

Any other value is 400. An id still held by a waiting, running or finished transfer on any name, or by a kept receipt, is 409. Not with `ws` (400). On a `live` sender it is the live stream's `transferId` in `?status` from the start, and its receipt (`"kind": "live"`, `complete` or `failed`) once it ends; live viewers get no `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description:
Live broadcast: start streaming at once, even with no viewers, and let any number of viewers join and leave at any time (`GET /{path}?live`; up to 256 at once). Nothing waits for a receiver and nothing is stored: bytes sent while nobody watches are dropped. Viewers are never in lockstep: one that falls behind skips ahead (WebM: whole Clusters, resuming at a keyframe Cluster) or is cut, and never slows the sender or the others.

**WebM bodies** (starting with the EBML magic, e.g. MediaRecorder or `ffmpeg -f webm`) get keyframe joins: a viewer receives the stream header, then the stream from the next Cluster that starts with a video keyframe (any Cluster for audio-only). Join delay is the keyframe interval. **Any other body** (logs, text, other containers) is sent to a viewer from the next chunk on.

**Status lines** (at most four): `[INFO] Live: streaming. Viewers can join at any time.`, then `[INFO] Live stream ended (peak N viewers).` on a clean end, or the idle-timeout / failure `[ERROR]` lines. Viewer counts are on `?progress` and `?status` (`kind: "live"`).

**Ending:** a clean end lets each viewer take what it was already sent (up to 60 s), then its body ends normally. A sender that disconnects, fails or idles 5 minutes cuts every viewer (their bodies end without the chunked terminator, which clients report as an error). The name is free for reuse as soon as the sender ends, unless the sender held it with `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key`.

Not with `n` above 1, `sha256`, `ws` or a multipart body (400). A name with waiting or streaming ordinary transfers, or a WebSocket pair, is 409. At most 100 live streams and 4096 viewer responses at once (429). `wait` is validated but a live sender never waits.

**Values:** `?live` (bare), `true`, `yes`, `1` → live; `false`, `no`, `0` → an ordinary sender.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key
parameters.description:
With `live`: a secret that holds the name for this sender. The first live sender that sends one holds the name while it streams and for 1 hour after its stream ends; in that time every POST or PUT on the name, live or not, must send the same key (403 otherwise), and `?ws` on the name is 409. Viewers never need it. Send it on every restart of the stream; a name held by nobody takes a new key. The hold starts with that first keyed sender, so start the stream before sharing its viewer link. Only a hash of the key is kept, in memory.

16-128 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -` (400 otherwise); without `live` on a name nobody holds, 400. At most 1000 names are held at once (429 for a new key past that; nothing is released early).

200.description:
Sender connected. Response body streams `[INFO]`/`[ERROR]` status messages in real-time.

**Success sequence:**
```
[INFO] Waiting for 1 receiver(s) to connect...
[INFO] Streaming to 1 receiver(s)...
[INFO] Upload complete.
[INFO] Transfer complete.
```

**Receiver disconnected:**
```
[INFO] A receiver disconnected.
[INFO] All receivers disconnected before transfer completed.
```

**With `?sha256`:**
```
[INFO] Upload complete.
[INFO] SHA-256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
[INFO] Transfer complete.
```

**Error:**
```
[ERROR] Timed out waiting for receivers.
[ERROR] Server at maximum active transfer capacity. Try again later.
[ERROR] Transfer aborted — idle timeout exceeded.
[ERROR] Transfer failed — sender encountered an error.
```

When an ordinary transfer is ready to start and 1000 transfers are already streaming, its sender still gets `200` and its status stream ends with the capacity line; its receivers get `429`. A `live` sender gets `429` `[ERROR] Too many live streams. Try again later.` instead.

text/plain.example:
[INFO] Waiting for 1 receiver(s) to connect...
[INFO] Streaming to 1 receiver(s)...
[INFO] Upload complete.
[INFO] Transfer complete.

400.description:
Bad request: invalid parameters, reserved path, duplicate sender, or receiver count mismatch. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Invalid sender key**: `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key` is not 16-128 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. Example: `[ERROR] Invalid sender key — 16-128 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -.` What to do: send a random 16-128 character key from that alphabet.
- **Sender key without live**: `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key` on a sender without `live`, on a name nobody holds. Example: `[ERROR] A sender key needs "live".` What to do: add `?live`, or drop the header.
- **Path is reserved**: The requested path is a system-reserved path (/, /help, /noscript, etc.). Example: `[ERROR] '/help' is a reserved path. Use a custom path like '/myfile' or '/transfer123'.` What to do: choose a different path that is not reserved.
- **Path contains forbidden characters**: The path has an encoded control character (`%00`-`%1F` or `%7F`), an encoded slash or backslash (`%2F`, `%5C`), or a percent-escape that does not decode (such as `%zz`). Example: `[ERROR] Path contains forbidden characters.` What to do: use a name without those characters.
- **Path already has a sender**: Another sender is already connected to this path waiting for receivers. Example: `[ERROR] This name already has a sender connected.` What to do: use a different path, or wait for the existing transfer to complete.
- **Path has an active transfer**: The path is currently in use by a streaming transfer. Example: `[ERROR] This name is already in use by an active transfer.` What to do: wait for the current transfer to finish, or use a different path.
- **Invalid receiver count**: The `n` query parameter must be a decimal integer from 1 to 256. A value that is not a plain decimal number (such as `-1`, `1.5` or `2x`) gets `[ERROR] Invalid receiver count — "n" must be a positive integer.`; `0` gets `[ERROR] Receiver count must be at least 1 (got 0).`; a value above 256 gets, for example, `[ERROR] Receiver count too high (max 256, got 300).` What to do: set `n` to a positive integer between 1 and 256.
- **Receiver count mismatch**: Sender's `n` doesn't match existing receivers' `n` on this path. Example: `[ERROR] Receiver count mismatch — expected 2 but got 1.` What to do: use the same `n` value as the receivers.
- **Content-Range not supported**: Content-Range headers are not supported for streaming transfers. Example: `[ERROR] Content-Range headers are not supported.` What to do: send the complete file without range headers.
- **Invalid wait**: `wait` is not a decimal integer (or is empty). Example: `[ERROR] Invalid wait — "wait" must be an integer number of seconds (1-3600).` What to do: set `wait` to whole seconds between 1 and 3600.
- **Wait out of range**: `wait` is below 1 or above 3600 seconds. Example: `[ERROR] Wait out of range (1-3600 seconds, got 7200).` What to do: set `wait` between 1 and 3600.
- **n with live**: A live stream has no fixed receiver count; `n` other than 1 is refused (on senders and on every live join). Example: `[ERROR] "n" cannot be combined with "live".` What to do: drop `n`.
- **sha256 with live**: Viewers get a suffix of the stream, so there is no single digest to verify. Example: `[ERROR] "sha256" cannot be combined with "live".` What to do: drop `sha256`, or send an ordinary transfer.
- **Invalid transfer id**: `transfer` is not 16-64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. Example: `[ERROR] Invalid "transfer" — 16-64 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -.` What to do: pick an id of 16-64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`.
- **live with ws**: `live` and `ws` are different modes (a GET with `status` gets the status instead). Example: `[ERROR] "live" cannot be combined with "ws".` What to do: use one of them.
- **Multipart with live**: A live body is streamed as sent; multipart form uploads are not supported. Example: `[ERROR] "live" does not support multipart/form-data.` What to do: send the raw bytes (e.g. `curl -T -`).

403.description:
The name is held by a live sender key and the request did not send it. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Name held by a sender key**: A POST or PUT (live or not) on a name a live sender holds with `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key`, without that key or with another one. The hold lasts while it streams and 1 hour after. Example: `[ERROR] This name is held by a live sender. Send its sender key.` What to do: send the key the name's live sender used, or use another name.

405.description:
Method not allowed. A POST gets it only on `/api/v1/pipe/health` and `/api/v1/pipe/metrics`, which accept GET, HEAD and OPTIONS. The response carries `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Method not allowed on health or metrics**: A POST to `/api/v1/pipe/health` or `/api/v1/pipe/metrics`. Example: `[ERROR] Method POST is not allowed.` What to do: use GET.

text/plain.example: [ERROR] Method POST is not allowed.

409.description:
The name holds another kind of session (a WebSocket pair, a live stream, or, for a live sender, an ordinary transfer), or the `transfer` id is in use. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Name in use by a WebSocket pair**: A sender on a name with a WebSocket pair. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a WebSocket pair.` What to do: use another name, or wait until the pair closes.
- **Name in use by a live stream**: An ordinary sender (or `live=0`) on a name with an active live stream or `?live` viewers waiting. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a live stream.` What to do: use another name, or send with `?live`.
- **Name in use by an ordinary transfer**: A live sender on a name with a waiting or streaming ordinary sender or receiver. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a normal transfer.` What to do: use another name, or wait until `?status` reads `idle`.
- **Transfer id in use**: `transfer` is held by a waiting, running or finished transfer (any name) or by a kept receipt. Example: `[ERROR] Transfer id already in use.` What to do: pick a new id for each transfer.

414.description:
Path too long: exceeds 1024 characters. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Path exceeds length limit**: The pipe path exceeds the maximum length of 1024 characters. Example: `[ERROR] Path too long (max 1024 characters).` What to do: use a shorter path name.

text/plain.example: [ERROR] Path too long (max 1024 characters).

429.description:
Too many transfers: server at capacity. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Too many held names**: A live sender with a new `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key` while 1000 names are held. Example: `[ERROR] Too many names held by sender keys. Try again later.` What to do: retry later, or send without a key.
- **Pending transfer limit reached**: Server has 1000 pending transfers (waiting for a sender or receivers). New ones are refused until a pending transfer starts, or all of its participants have timed out or left. Example: `[ERROR] Too many pending transfers. Try again later.` What to do: wait a moment, then retry.
- **Live stream limit reached**: Server has 100 live streams (or 1000 active transfers in all). Example: `[ERROR] Too many live streams. Try again later.` What to do: wait and retry.

text/plain.example: [ERROR] Too many pending transfers. Try again later.

requestBody.description:
Data to stream to receiver(s). Any content type is accepted.

- **Binary files:** Use `application/octet-stream` or the file's actual MIME type
- **Text:** Use `text/plain`
- **Multipart:** Use `multipart/form-data` for browser uploads. Only the first file part is streamed; leading non-file form fields are drained and skipped
- **No body:** An empty POST is valid: receivers get an empty response

put.description:
Identical to POST: send data to the specified pipe path. PUT is provided as an alias because `curl -T file URL` uses PUT, making it natural for file transfers.

**curl usage:**
```bash
# Send a file (uses PUT)
curl -T myfile https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/pipe/mypath

# Send stdin
echo 'hello' | curl -T - https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/pipe/mypath

# Send a directory as tar.gz
tar czf - ./mydir | curl -T - https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/pipe/mydir.tar.gz
```

All parameters, request body handling, status messages, and errors are identical to POST.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Unique pipe path name (same rules as POST, so no reserved paths and at most 1024 chars)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of receivers to wait for (must match receivers' `n`, max 256)

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds this sender waits for its receivers, 1–3600 (default 300). Same rules as POST.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description: Compute the SHA-256 of the forwarded bytes. Same rules as POST.

parameters.name: transfer
parameters.description: This transfer's own id (16-64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`). Same rules as POST.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: Live broadcast (any number of viewers join and leave at any time). Same rules as POST.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key
parameters.description: With `live`, a secret that holds the name for this sender. Same rules as POST.

200.description:
Sender connected, streaming status messages (identical to POST). The stream can end with one of these error lines:

```
[ERROR] Timed out waiting for receivers.
[ERROR] Server at maximum active transfer capacity. Try again later.
[ERROR] Transfer aborted — idle timeout exceeded.
[ERROR] Transfer failed — sender encountered an error.
```

When an ordinary transfer is ready to start and 1000 transfers are already streaming, its sender still gets `200` and its status stream ends with the capacity line; its receivers get `429`. A `live` sender gets `429` `[ERROR] Too many live streams. Try again later.` instead.

text/plain.example:
[INFO] Waiting for 1 receiver(s) to connect...
[INFO] Streaming to 1 receiver(s)...
[INFO] Upload complete.
[INFO] Transfer complete.

400.description:
Bad request (same cases as POST). The body is a plain-text message:

- **Invalid sender key**: `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key` is not 16-128 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. Example: `[ERROR] Invalid sender key — 16-128 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -.` What to do: send a random 16-128 character key from that alphabet.
- **Sender key without live**: `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key` on a sender without `live`, on a name nobody holds. Example: `[ERROR] A sender key needs "live".` What to do: add `?live`, or drop the header.
- **Path is reserved**: The requested path is a system-reserved path. Example: `[ERROR] '/help' is a reserved path. Use a custom path like '/myfile' or '/transfer123'.` What to do: choose a different path.
- **Path contains forbidden characters**: The path has an encoded control character (`%00`-`%1F` or `%7F`), an encoded slash or backslash (`%2F`, `%5C`), or a percent-escape that does not decode (such as `%zz`). Example: `[ERROR] Path contains forbidden characters.` What to do: use a name without those characters.
- **Path already has a sender**: Another sender is already connected. Example: `[ERROR] This name already has a sender connected.` What to do: use a different path or wait.
- **Path has an active transfer**: The path is currently in use by a streaming transfer. Example: `[ERROR] This name is already in use by an active transfer.` What to do: wait for the current transfer to finish, or use a different path.
- **Invalid receiver count**: `n` must be a decimal integer from 1 to 256. A value that is not a plain decimal number (such as `-1`, `1.5` or `2x`) gets `[ERROR] Invalid receiver count — "n" must be a positive integer.`; `0` gets `[ERROR] Receiver count must be at least 1 (got 0).`; a value above 256 gets, for example, `[ERROR] Receiver count too high (max 256, got 300).` What to do: set `n` to a positive integer between 1 and 256.
- **Receiver count mismatch**: Sender's `n` doesn't match existing receivers' `n` on this path. Example: `[ERROR] Receiver count mismatch — expected 2 but got 1.` What to do: use the same `n` value as the receivers.
- **Content-Range not supported**: Content-Range headers are not supported. Example: `[ERROR] Content-Range headers are not supported.` What to do: send the complete file.
- **Invalid wait**: `wait` is not a decimal integer (or is empty). Example: `[ERROR] Invalid wait — "wait" must be an integer number of seconds (1-3600).` What to do: set `wait` to whole seconds between 1 and 3600.
- **Wait out of range**: `wait` is below 1 or above 3600 seconds. Example: `[ERROR] Wait out of range (1-3600 seconds, got 7200).` What to do: set `wait` between 1 and 3600.
- **n with live**: A live stream has no fixed receiver count; `n` other than 1 is refused (on senders and on every live join). Example: `[ERROR] "n" cannot be combined with "live".` What to do: drop `n`.
- **sha256 with live**: Viewers get a suffix of the stream, so there is no single digest to verify. Example: `[ERROR] "sha256" cannot be combined with "live".` What to do: drop `sha256`, or send an ordinary transfer.
- **Invalid transfer id**: `transfer` is not 16-64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. Example: `[ERROR] Invalid "transfer" — 16-64 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -.` What to do: pick an id of 16-64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`.
- **live with ws**: `live` and `ws` are different modes (a GET with `status` gets the status instead). Example: `[ERROR] "live" cannot be combined with "ws".` What to do: use one of them.
- **Multipart with live**: Multipart form uploads are not supported with `live`. Example: `[ERROR] "live" does not support multipart/form-data.` What to do: send the raw bytes.

403.description:
The name is held by a live sender key and the request did not send it. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Name held by a sender key**: A POST or PUT (live or not) on a name a live sender holds with `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key`, without that key or with another one. The hold lasts while it streams and 1 hour after. Example: `[ERROR] This name is held by a live sender. Send its sender key.` What to do: send the key the name's live sender used, or use another name.

405.description:
Method not allowed. A PUT gets it only on `/api/v1/pipe/health` and `/api/v1/pipe/metrics`, which accept GET, HEAD and OPTIONS. The response carries `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Method not allowed on health or metrics**: A PUT to `/api/v1/pipe/health` or `/api/v1/pipe/metrics`. Example: `[ERROR] Method PUT is not allowed.` What to do: use GET.

text/plain.example: [ERROR] Method PUT is not allowed.

409.description:
The name holds another kind of session (a WebSocket pair, a live stream, or, for a live sender, an ordinary transfer), or the `transfer` id is in use. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Name in use by a WebSocket pair**: A sender on a name with a WebSocket pair. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a WebSocket pair.` What to do: use another name, or wait until the pair closes.
- **Name in use by a live stream**: An ordinary sender (or `live=0`) on a name with an active live stream or `?live` viewers waiting. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a live stream.` What to do: use another name, or send with `?live`.
- **Name in use by an ordinary transfer**: A live sender on a name with a waiting or streaming ordinary sender or receiver. Example: `[ERROR] This name is in use by a normal transfer.` What to do: use another name, or wait until `?status` reads `idle`.
- **Transfer id in use**: `transfer` is held by a waiting, running or finished transfer (any name) or by a kept receipt. Example: `[ERROR] Transfer id already in use.` What to do: pick a new id for each transfer.

414.description:
Path too long. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Path exceeds length limit**: Path exceeds 1024 characters. Example: `[ERROR] Path too long (max 1024 characters).` What to do: use a shorter path.

429.description:
Too many transfers. The body is a plain-text message:

- **Too many held names**: A live sender with a new `X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key` while 1000 names are held. Example: `[ERROR] Too many names held by sender keys. Try again later.` What to do: retry later, or send without a key.
- **Pending transfer limit reached**: Server has 1000 pending transfers. Example: `[ERROR] Too many pending transfers. Try again later.` What to do: wait and retry.
- **Live stream limit reached**: Server has 100 live streams (or 1000 active transfers in all). Example: `[ERROR] Too many live streams. Try again later.` What to do: wait and retry.

options.description:
Handles CORS preflight requests for cross-origin browser access. Returns permissive CORS headers reflecting the request Origin.

**Headers returned:**
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`: reflects Origin (or `*` if none/null)
- `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`: `GET, POST, PUT, OPTIONS`, or `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, OPTIONS` when the URL has `?status` (on a pipe data path only without `?video`; a reserved page lists HEAD with `?status` whether or not `?video` is on). HEAD is otherwise supported same-origin on reserved paths only
- `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`: `Content-Type, Content-Disposition, Authorization, X-Piping, X-Hoody-Pipe, X-Hoody-Pipe-Sender-Key`
- `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`: `true` (when Origin present and not "null")
- `Access-Control-Max-Age`: `86400` (24 hours)
- `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network`: `true` (when requested)

The `"null"` origin string is rejected: it defaults to `*`, which blocks credentialed requests from sandboxed iframes.

**Scope:** this preflight (`200`) answers every valid pipe path, and the reserved pages share it. `OPTIONS /api/v1/pipe/health` is answered separately with `204`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type` and no `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network`. A path that fails routing checks gets that error instead of a preflight: name over 1024 characters → 414, forbidden characters → 400, bare `/health` or `/metrics` → 404; `OPTIONS /api/v1/pipe/metrics` → 204 like health.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Any valid pipe path (reserved pages included). They all get the same preflight. Health has its own 204 preflight (see above).

200.description: CORS preflight response with permissive headers

head.description: `HEAD /{path}?status` returns the headers of the `?status` snapshot with no body: a cheap liveness probe. HEAD without `?status`, or with `?video` on, on a pipe path is 405.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Pipe path name

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Must be on (`?status`, `true`, `yes`, `1`)

parameters.name: transfer
parameters.description: Answer for one transfer, by the id a receiver got in `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id` or the id a sender chose with its own `transfer`, even after the name was reused or its 30 s linger ended. The answer has no body, so the status tells the result: 200 when the id is the name's current transfer or a kept receipt for this name, 404 when it is neither, 400 when it is not a transfer id. Receipts are kept as for `GET /{path}?status&transfer=<id>`, which also returns the snapshot.

200.description: Headers of the `?status` snapshot (`Content-Type: application/json`, `Cache-Control: no-store`), no body

400.description: `transfer` is not a transfer id (16-64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`), or the path contains forbidden characters (an encoded control character, `%2F`, `%5C`, or a percent-escape that does not decode). No body. What to do: pass the value of the `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id` response header, and use a plain name.

404.description: With `transfer`, the id is neither the name's current transfer nor a kept receipt for this name. No body. Receipts are kept only for `?sha256` transfers and transfers with a sender-chosen id, for 10 minutes, at most 1000. What to do: look the transfer up sooner, or treat the digest as unavailable (not as a mismatch).

405.description: HEAD without `?status`, or with `?video` on. No body. HEAD is supported on pipe paths only with `?status` and without `?video`. What to do: add `?status`, or use GET.

get.description: Returns the identity this request resolved to: userId, username, role and notebookId. `role` is always the role stored for that username in that notebook, never the one the request carries: a later call with another `role` value (query parameter or Bearer token) does not change it, and it is `none` when the notebook has no such user. The identity comes from an `Authorization: Bearer` token (base64url JSON of {userId, notebookId, username, role}), else from the `username` and `role` query parameters (defaults `user` / `owner`). Query identities are auto-provisioned in the default notebook on first use, with the role of that first call; a user first seen with role none is not a member. This identity does not establish notebook membership: a notebook route answers 403 unless the username is a member of that notebook with a role other than none, and acts with the role the username has in that notebook. Membership comes from creating a notebook (the creator) or adding a user to it; sharing a page with an existing member does not grant it.

Every connection, including a reconnect after a drop, needs a fresh id from socket-init: a used id is closed with 1008. The socket carries the identity the socket-init call was made with. get.description: Streams a ZIP archive of the whole notebook, or of one section, folder, page (with its sub-pages) or database (`nodeId`), as Markdown (default) or HTML. Pages and records become documents, databases become CSV files (UTF-8 with BOM), and attachments are included byte for byte unless `attachments=false`. Each archive has an `index` file at its top listing what it holds and what it leaves out. Only what the caller can read is exported, checked again for every entry while the archive is written; channels and messages are never exported. Links between exported items are relative; an item outside the export is shown as "… not in this export". `dryRun=true` runs the same checks and limits and answers 204 without a body, or the error the download would get. Exports are bounded (items, sizes, nesting, time): over a limit the answer is 422 `export_too_large`. At most two exports run at once and one per member: another call gets 429 `export_busy` with `Retry-After`.

post.description: TUS 1.0.0 resumable upload of the bytes of a file node (type file, status pending) created first through the node-creation endpoint; only the user who created the node may upload. Flow: POST to the upload URL with Upload-Length, then PATCH with Upload-Offset starting at 0 until the offset reaches Upload-Length; after an interruption HEAD returns the offset to resume from. The final chunk marks the file ready. This call creates the upload; send no body. A create that already holds every byte (Upload-Length 0) finishes the upload at once: 200 {uploadId}, with the Location of the (complete) upload.

parameters.name: Tus-Resumable
parameters.description: TUS protocol version. Every TUS request must send `1.0.0`: a missing header is refused with 412, any other value with 400.

parameters.name: Upload-Length
parameters.description: Total size of the file in bytes. Must equal the file node's `size` (set when the node was created), which must not exceed the notebook's maximum file size. Upload-Defer-Length is not supported.

parameters.name: Upload-Metadata
parameters.description: Optional TUS metadata: comma-separated `key base64(value)` pairs.

200.description: Upload created and already complete (Upload-Length 0, or a creation-with-upload body that carried every byte): the file is ready and there is nothing more to send. Location names the upload, as on 201; a HEAD there reports it complete.

Location.description: URL of the upload: this path, with the caller's `username` and `role` query parameters when it sent them.

201.description: Upload created. The body is empty. Send the chunks to the Location URL (this same path).

Location.description: URL of the upload: this path, with the caller's `username` and `role` query parameters when it sent them.

patch.summary: Upload a chunk to a TUS upload
patch.description: TUS 1.0.0 resumable upload of the bytes of a file node (type file, status pending) created first through the node-creation endpoint; only the user who created the node may upload. Flow: POST to the upload URL with Upload-Length, then PATCH with Upload-Offset starting at 0 until the offset reaches Upload-Length; after an interruption HEAD returns the offset to resume from. The final chunk marks the file ready. This call appends one chunk at Upload-Offset; Content-Type must be application/offset+octet-stream. Chunks for one upload are taken one at a time: a chunk sent while another is being written gets 409 once that one moves the offset.

post.description: Creates a new node (section, page, channel, message, database, or record) in the notebook. Every type except `section` needs a `parentId`: pass the id of the node it goes under, such as the notebook's Home section for a page, folder, database or channel. A `section` can only sit at the root, so it takes no `parentId`; without `attributes.collaborators` the caller becomes its admin. A request that breaks this answers `400` with code `parent_required` or `section_must_be_root`; `403` means the caller's role does not allow the creation.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional idempotency key (max 256 chars), such as a random UUID per node. Reusing the same key with an identical request body replays the original response instead of creating a second node; reusing it with a different body returns 409.

get.description: Retrieves document content for a node. Supports block filtering via blockIds and line range queries.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Optional (RFC 9110): ETags of copies the caller already holds, or `*`. When the document is still at one of them the JSON output answers 304 with no body. Ignored by the Markdown and HTML outputs.

Repeating a request that succeeded with the same key, path and body returns the stored response without recording the open again. The same key with a different method, path or body returns 409. A request that failed stores nothing, so repeating it runs it again. A repeat sent while the first request is still running waits for it, up to 60 seconds, and is then handled the same way; if the first is still running then, the answer is 409. A longer key is refused with 409.

parameters.description: Optional idempotency key, at most 256 characters, such as a random UUID per request. Keys are kept per notebook and user. get.description: WebSocket upgrade endpoint for the multiplexed tunnel session. This is not a request/response call: a plain HTTP GET cannot use it. The client MUST send a WebSocket upgrade offering subprotocol `hoody-tunnel.v2` and/or `hoody-tunnel.v1` (the server selects the first one it supports, in the client's order), then send exactly one binary frame as its first message within the HELLO timeout (default 5 s): either HELLO (frame type 0x01) to open a session, answered by HELLO_OK (0x02), or, on `hoody-tunnel.v2` only, JOIN (0x09) carrying a single-use ticket from HELLO_OK to attach a secondary socket to an existing session, answered by JOIN_OK (0x0A) or JOIN_ERR (0x0B, followed by close 1000). Every message after the upgrade is a binary hoody-tunnel frame; the SDK protocol helpers build and read them. Handshake failures: a text frame, a first message that is not exactly one HELLO/JOIN frame (or whose payload exceeds 4096 bytes), a missing first frame at the timeout, JOIN on v1, the pre-auth cap being full, or malformed JOIN JSON close the socket with no close code; a full session cap (`--max-sessions`) gets GOAWAY(RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, "tunnel session limit (N) reached; ...") then close 1013 with the reason "tunnel session limit (N) reached"; a HELLO the handshake rejects gets GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR) then close 1002; an exhausted file-descriptor budget or a concurrent handshake for the same session closes with 1013; resuming an expired session closes with 1008. After the handshake, a text frame is a protocol error: on the primary socket the server sends GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR, "text frames not allowed") and then drops the socket with no close code; on a JOIN-attached secondary it ends the whole session, with the GOAWAY sent on the primary. Ending a session: a GOAWAY from the client, or a WebSocket close frame with no code or code 1000, on the primary socket ends it for good, and its ports are released as soon as the kit reads it; a primary that drops without a close frame, or closes with any other code (e.g. 4000), keeps its bindings for the takeover grace (`--takeover-grace`, default 60 s) so a HELLO with `resume.sessionId` can reclaim them. The kit takes no credential of its own: access control is the edge proxy's. SDK: use the protocol helpers (`TunnelSession`, `exposeTunnel`, `pullTunnel`), not a generated HTTP method.

parameters.description: Required. Comma-separated subprotocols to offer, in preference order: `hoody-tunnel.v2`, `hoody-tunnel.v1`, or `hoody-tunnel.v2, hoody-tunnel.v1`.
parameters.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol

101.description: Switching Protocols. WebSocket upgrade accepted; the selected subprotocol is echoed in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. Send HELLO next to open a session, or, on `hoody-tunnel.v2`, JOIN to attach a secondary socket.

400.description: No supported subprotocol offered. The body is plain text naming the supported subprotocols.

post.description: Pushes the deadline of the upstream lease `lease_id` out by the lease's `ttl`, counted from now, and persists it. When the renewals stop (the client was killed, lost its network or went to sleep), the service disables the upstream at the deadline, exactly as `DELETE /api/v1/egress/upstream` does, so a dead exit cannot leave the computer refusing every proxied request.
