get.summary: Resolve an application and return exact shell command
get.description:
Resolve and select an application using query parameters, then return the exact shell command to run.
Supports all selector fields plus pick mode and output control.
When the effective pick (from the request or the selected profile) is unset or ask, it returns an HTML page listing the matching applications instead: with format=html, or with no format and an Accept header that includes text/html with a quality above 0. format=json always answers JSON. The UI construction catalog lists the parameters embed URLs accept.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Primary name query

parameters.name: os
parameters.description: Target OS filter

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Source kind filter (repeatable)

parameters.name: source_id
parameters.description: Search only the configured sources with these source ids (repeatable; GET /api/v1/run/sources lists them). Intersects with source, the profile and the policy; it never enables a source. An id that is not configured gives 400 INVALID_SELECTOR; a named source that is disabled or filtered out adds a SOURCE_NOT_SEARCHED warning

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: App kind filter

parameters.name: arch
parameters.description: Target CPU architecture filter

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Free-form selector tags (repeatable). Accepted and passed through to sources and recipe templates; they do not filter or rank candidates

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Named profile for default preferences

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Release channel hint. Accepted but not applied yet: no source filters or ranks on it, and setting it adds a SELECTOR_HINT_IGNORED warning

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Exact version or provider-defined version constraint

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: Provider-specific variant hint. Accepted but not applied yet: no source filters or ranks on it, and setting it adds a SELECTOR_HINT_IGNORED warning

parameters.name: publisher
parameters.description: Keep only candidates by this publisher, compared case-insensitively: a Docker Hub namespace or publisher (library or docker for official images), a GHCR owner, an npm scope (with or without @) or publisher, a PyPI author, a GitHub owner of an AppImage. A candidate whose source reports no publisher (nix, pkgx, system) is kept with a provider note saying it was not checked

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository hint such as owner/name

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: Release hint such as a tag name

parameters.name: asset
parameters.description: Desired asset name or pattern

parameters.name: pick
parameters.description: Candidate selection mode (ask, first, index, id)

parameters.name: pick_index
parameters.description: Candidate index (required when pick=index)

parameters.name: candidate_id
parameters.description: Specific candidate ID (required when pick=id)

parameters.name: set_id
parameters.description: Bind pick to a specific candidate set

parameters.name: terminal_id
parameters.description: Terminal session ID (default 1)

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: X11 DISPLAY number

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Origin identifier for observability propagation

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: If true, force command-only response (hoody-run never executes)

parameters.name: print_curl
parameters.description: Generate curl command (hoody-run)

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output format (json or html)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max candidates (default 25, clamped to 1-100)

parameters.name: enrich
parameters.description: Fill candidate details more completely with extra requests per candidate (Docker Hub repository and tags, the npm packument, PyPI download stats, GitHub repository metadata); at most 10 candidates per source, inside the source timeout. Default false: a plain search makes none of these requests. Accepts true, false, 1 or 0

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Launch argument for the selected app (repeatable, in order; at most 64, each at most 4096 bytes). Appended as separate words to the selected command; a source-authored shell command answers 400 ARGS_UNSUPPORTED

parameters.name: pass_env
parameters.description: Env name an OCI command passes into the container as --env NAME, without a value (repeatable, at most 32)

parameters.name: launch_tag
parameters.description: Tag of one launch, 16 lowercase hex characters; an OCI command gets -it --name hoody-run-<tag> --label hoody.run.tag=<tag>

parameters.name: launch_env
parameters.description: inline (default) exports env values in shell_command; separate writes no value into any command and returns them in launch_env

get.description:
Search and filter through the stored request/response and event logs.

**What is stored, and for how long.** Every request to the computer's services is logged, including your app's visitors; reads of the logs are not. By default a computer keeps at most 50,000 entries, 100 MB, and 7 days of logs; the oldest entries go first. By default, only a request that declares a `Content-Length` of 64 KB or less can have its body stored, and a response body is stored up to its first 64 KB (images, audio, video, fonts and `application/octet-stream` are not stored). Bodies are returned only with `includeRequestBody` / `includeResponseBody`. A request to your app is stored without its query string and without its headers, and `Authorization`, `Cookie` and API-key header values are never stored.

**Redaction.** Before a body is stored, the value of every field whose name marks a secret becomes `[REDACTED]`, in JSON, form and multipart bodies and in query strings inside them: passwords and passphrases, tokens, secrets, API and private keys, cookies, sessions and credentials; PINs, passcodes, one-time and MFA codes (`otp`, `totp`, `mfa_code`); card numbers and card security codes (`card_number`, `cvv`, `cvc`), IBANs and social security numbers (`ssn`); and an OAuth `code` sent beside `state`, `redirect_uri`, `code_verifier`, `grant_type` or `client_id`. Some values are redacted under any field name, in every kind of body: a Hoody token (`hdy_…`) and the user and password in a URL (`https://host`) wherever they appear; a Bearer token (a string that starts with `Bearer `) or a JWT sent as a whole JSON string value or inside double quotes; and the value in a JSON string that starts with a `password=…` or `token=…` assignment. get.description:
Opens a persistent SSE connection streaming new log entries.

**Framing**: each live log entry is one frame with a numeric `id:` line:
```
id: 12345
data: <LogEntry JSON>

```

Not every frame has an `id:`. A fresh connection (no `Last-Event-ID`) first receives one id-less `data:` frame holding a JSON array of recent matching entries, when any exist; with none, its first frame is a live entry with its `id:`. The `gap` event below has no `id:` either, and heartbeats are comments. Keep the last `id` you received; a frame without one does not change it.

The `id:` line numbers frames for `Last-Event-ID` and is not the entry's row id. Each entry's own `id` field is its row id, the cursor GET /_logs takes as `afterId`.

An entry whose frame would exceed 256 KiB is sent as a stub that keeps its `id` and carries `truncated: true` and `originalFrameBytes`.

**Reconnect resume**: clients MAY send `Last-Event-ID: <id>` on reconnect, with the `id` of the last frame they received. The server then replays the buffered frames newer than that id that match the stream's filters, instead of the initial batch.

The replay buffer holds at most the 2,000 most recent frames and at most 8 MiB of them, whichever limit is reached first; entries can leave the buffer sooner. The server can also end a stream once it has sent a per-connection byte budget; reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` continues from where it stopped.

**Named events**:
- `event: gap`: sent first on a resume when frames your stream could match were dropped from the buffer after your `Last-Event-ID` (or the buffer does not reach back that far); those entries are not replayed. It has no `id:`. Its data is `{"after": "<your Last-Event-ID>", "resumedFrom": "<id of the next frame kept for your stream>"}`. Read what you missed from `GET /_logs` (match on `traceId` and `tsMs`), then carry on with the frames that follow.
- `event: purged`: carries an `id:` and `data: {}`. It stands in for a buffered entry whose logs were deleted, so your cursor still moves past it.
- `event: scope-destroyed`: computer destroyed; stream closes immediately after. Clients should exit cleanly.
- `event: reset`: the stream is being reset and closes right after. Discard the last `id` you saw and reconnect without `Last-Event-ID`.

**Server restart**: a restart ends every open stream without an event and the replay buffer starts empty, so reconnecting with an id from before the restart gets a `gap` event followed by new frames.

A `: keepalive\n\n` comment heartbeat every 5 s keeps the connection alive. The server also sends one `: open\n\n` comment as soon as the stream is set up, after any initial batch, replay or `gap` event, so a stream with nothing to deliver yet still starts at once. Both are SSE comments, not frames: ignore them.

patch.description:
Changes a VM's mutable fields: `memory_mib`, `vcpus`, `disk_gib`, `display`, `cdroms`, `autostart`, `disk_bps`, `disk_iops`, `share_quota_bytes`, `stop_grace_seconds` and `ports`. The VM must have no running process and no operation in progress, otherwise the call is refused with 409 `BadState` or `OperationInProgress`. This normally means Stopped; a Failed VM whose launch left no process is also accepted. Changes take effect at the next start.

Omitted fields are left unchanged. `display: null` makes the VM headless, `cdroms: []` ejects every disc and `ports: []` removes every port forward; `ports: null` is an error. `disk_gib` only grows the disk and must be sent alone, in a request with no other field.

These fields are fixed for the life of the VM and cannot be changed: `firmware` (with `secure_boot`), `machine_type`, `tpm`, `cpu`, `agent`, `audio`, `console`, `console_input`, `share`, `bus`, `display_adapter` and `name`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

200.description: The VM's configuration after the change, with any warnings.

400.description: `NameInvalid`: the name in the path is invalid. `SpecInvalid`: an empty body, an invalid value, `disk_gib` combined with another field, a missing disk, or a `disk_gib` smaller than the current size. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

409.description: `BadState`: the VM is not stopped. `OperationInProgress`: another operation on this VM is in progress; retry later. `Orphaned`: the service cannot manage the VM, and the guest may still be running. Either the VM's run cannot be verified (the recorded process is gone, does not match its record, or the record cannot be read), or the service has blocked the VM (after a restart it found more than one run that may still be live, or a delete stopped before it could tell whether the VM was removed); the error message says which. For a run that cannot be verified, check the process yourself, then call `POST /vms/{name}/force-adopt` to resume managing it or `POST /vms/{name}/force-mark-dead` to record it as dead (accepted only when the VM's disk is not locked by a running process). For a blocked VM both are refused: resolve the condition the message names, then restart hoody-vm, which settles the VM's state as it starts. `PortForwardConflict`: a host port in `ports` is already declared by another VM, running or not. `DisplayRangeExhausted`: `display` is `"auto"` and no number in the automatic range is free. `DisplayInUse`: `display` is a number something other than this VM is already using; choose another number, or `"auto"`.

503.description: `DisplayUnavailable`: the service could not check whether the display number is in use, so nothing was changed: for `"auto"`, none was picked. Retry, or for `"auto"` give an explicit number.

507.description: `InsufficientSpace`: there is not enough free space to grow the disk to the requested size.

get.summary: Open a VM's screen in the browser
get.description:
Redirects (302) to the browser address of the VM's display: the computer's `display-N` URL for the number in `spec.display`, on the same server and domain as this request. With `format=json` it answers 200 with the VM's name, its display number and that address instead.

The address is built from the hostname this request arrived on, each time, and is never stored: call this route through the computer's `vm` URL. Through any other hostname, and for display `0`, which has no browser address, there is no address: the redirect is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid` and the JSON answer omits `url` but still carries `display`.

The address opens the computer's display service, which applies its own access rules: being allowed to call this route does not grant access to the display, and the address carries no credentials. This route starts nothing. The page shows the VM while the VM is running; starting the VM starts its display if nothing is running on it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `json` answers 200 with `{name, display, url}` instead of redirecting. Absent: redirect. Any other value is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`.

200.description: With `format=json`: the VM's display number and its browser address.

302.description: Redirect to the VM's display. The address is in `Location`.

400.description: `SpecInvalid`: `format` has a value other than `json` or the query has another key; or, for the redirect, the request did not arrive through the computer's `vm` URL or the VM's display is `0`, so there is no address to redirect to.

Either the VM's run cannot be verified (the recorded process is gone, does not match its record, or the record cannot be read), or the service has blocked the VM (after a restart it found more than one run that may still be live, or a delete stopped before it could tell whether the VM was removed); the error message says which. For a blocked VM both are refused: resolve the condition the message names, then restart hoody-vm, which settles the VM's state as it starts.

put.summary: Change the disc in a running VM's CD-ROM slot
put.description: Put a disc into one CD-ROM slot of a running or paused VM, as if swapping the disc in its drive: QEMU's `blockdev-change-medium`, opened as a raw read-only image. Whatever was in the slot is replaced. `source` is checked exactly as one entry of `cdroms` in `PATCH /vms/{name}` is. The VM's `cdroms` records the new disc before QEMU opens it; if QEMU refuses, the slot is put back. Only a slot that held a disc when the VM started has a drive in this run, so filling a slot that was empty at start is refused until the next start; set it with `PATCH /vms/{name}` while the VM is stopped. To change a stopped VM's discs, use `PATCH /vms/{name}`. The call returns once QEMU has answered, at most 10 seconds (the monitor command deadline).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: The CD-ROM slot, counted from 0 in the order of the VM's `cdroms`. Slot 0 is the one the VM boots from.

200.description: QEMU opened the disc in the slot; `spec.cdroms` names it.

400.description: NameInvalid: the VM name does not match the naming rule. SpecInvalid: the body is not valid JSON or has an unknown field, the slot is not a number or is past the VM's last slot, or `source` is not an absolute path to a regular file that may be attached. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

404.description: NotFound: no VM has this name

409.description: BadState: the VM is not running or paused, its monitor is not answering, QEMU refused the command (its message is included: a tray the guest has locked, a file QEMU cannot open, or a slot that was empty when the VM started and so has no drive until the next start), or the service is shutting down; the slot is unchanged. OperationInProgress: another operation on this VM has not finished, including another CD-ROM change, or the slot changed while this call ran; poll `GET /vms/{name}` and retry. Orphaned: the service cannot manage the VM, and the guest may still be running. Either the VM's run cannot be verified (the recorded process is gone, does not match its record, or the record cannot be read), or the service has blocked the VM (after a restart it found more than one run that may still be live, or a delete stopped before it could tell whether the VM was removed); the error message says which. For a run that cannot be verified, check the process yourself, then call `POST /vms/{name}/force-adopt` to resume managing it or `POST /vms/{name}/force-mark-dead` to record it as dead (accepted only when the VM's disk is not locked by a running process). For a blocked VM both are refused: resolve the condition the message names, then restart hoody-vm, which settles the VM's state as it starts.

500.description: MonitorCommandIndeterminate: the command was sent and QEMU did not answer in time, or the monitor closed first, so the VM did not confirm it. The slot `GET /vms/{name}` shows is not proof either way: after an insert it already shows the new disc, and after an eject it still shows the old one. Check the disc inside the running VM before retrying, and do not retry automatically. StorageFailed: the VM's record could not be read or written.

post.description:
Prepare a snapshot for download as one portable artifact containing its disk, UEFI varstore, vTPM state and manifest, identified by a single sha256. Empty regions of the disk are skipped, so the artifact is usually much smaller than the disk. The response gives the size, `part_size`, number of `parts` and `sha256`; download the parts with `GET /vms/{name}/snapshots/{label}/export/parts/{part}`, then import the artifact elsewhere with `POST /imports/{sha256}`.

Idempotent: calling again returns the same export. No copy is made on disk. While this call is running, the snapshot and the VM cannot be deleted. Preparing an export hashes the whole disk, which can take a while for large disks. Release the export with `DELETE /vms/{name}/snapshots/{label}/export` when the download is complete.

get.summary: Download one part of a snapshot export
get.description: Return part n of a prepared export as raw bytes. Part n starts at byte `n * part_size`; every part except the last is exactly `part_size` bytes. Parts can be fetched in any order and fetched again, so an interrupted download resumes from any part. Join the parts in order and check the result against the export's `sha256`. At most a few part downloads run at once; extra requests are refused with 409 `BadState` and can be retried shortly. A download whose client stops reading for 30 seconds, or that takes longer than 30 minutes, is cut off (the connection is closed before the body is complete); request the same part again.

parameters.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Zero-based part index. The part starts at byte offset `part * part_size`.

200.description: The bytes of part n. The last part may be shorter than `part_size`.

400.description: NameInvalid: the VM name or the label does not match the naming rule. SpecInvalid: the part index is past the last part or is not a non-negative integer. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

409.description: BadState: the VM was deleted and recreated under the same name since the export was prepared, too many part downloads are running at once (retry shortly), or the VM's create failed. OperationInProgress: the VM is still being created; retry shortly. Orphaned: the service cannot manage the VM, and the guest may still be running. Either the VM's run cannot be verified (the recorded process is gone, does not match its record, or the record cannot be read), or the service has blocked the VM (after a restart it found more than one run that may still be live, or a delete stopped before it could tell whether the VM was removed); the error message says which. For a run that cannot be verified, check the process yourself, then call `POST /vms/{name}/force-adopt` to resume managing it or `POST /vms/{name}/force-mark-dead` to record it as dead (accepted only when the VM's disk is not locked by a running process). For a blocked VM both are refused: resolve the condition the message names, then restart hoody-vm, which settles the VM's state as it starts.

post.summary: Begin or resume an installer image upload
post.description:
Declare an upload of an installer image under its sha256 and total size. If the image is already published, the answer is `phase: ready` and no upload is needed. If an earlier upload was interrupted, the answer gives `next_part` to resume from. Safe to repeat: it never truncates an upload in progress.

On a resume, sending a different `bytes` replaces the declared total if it is at least the bytes already stored, and the resume point is recomputed from it; this is how a mis-declared upload is corrected.

200.description: Upload declared, resumed, or already complete; read `phase`.

400.description: NameInvalid: sha256 is not 64 lowercase hex characters. SpecInvalid: `bytes` is zero, or on a resume is below the bytes already stored. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

409.description: OperationInProgress: another call is working on this digest; retry shortly.

507.description: InsufficientSpace: the declared size does not fit (on a resume, the remainder does not fit).

next_steps.reason: Send the parts, starting at `next_part` from the response

put.summary: Upload one part of an installer image
put.description:
Append one part of the image. Parts are sent in order: part n is accepted only when exactly n*part_size bytes are stored. Every part except the last must be exactly `part_size` bytes. A replayed part is refused rather than applied twice, so retrying a request whose response you did not see is safe.

When the stored `bytes` reach the declared total, call `POST /isos/{sha256}/finalize`. If an upload is interrupted mid-part, `bytes` is reported at the last part boundary and `next_part` names the part to send again. After any failure, read `GET /isos/{sha256}` to find where to resume.

parameters.description: Zero-based part index. Part n covers bytes [n*part_size, (n+1)*part_size).

404.description: NotFound: no upload is in progress for this digest; call `POST /isos/{sha256}` first.

409.description: BadState: this is not the part the stored length calls for; read `next_part` and send that. post.summary: Download an installer image from a URL
post.description:
Start fetching an installer image from a URL into the image store. Answers 202 with a download job and transfers in the background; poll `GET /isos/downloads/{id}`. The image is published only after the transfer completes and every byte has been hashed.

With `sha256`: the bytes must hash to it, and a mismatch publishes nothing. If that digest is already in the store, the call answers 409 `AlreadyExists` without fetching; check `GET /isos` first if you want to treat that as success.

Without `sha256`: the bytes are published under the digest they hash to, and the job reports `verification: "tofu"` (trust on first use) because nothing checked that they are the vendor's bytes. This is visible only on the job: `GET /isos` keeps no record of how an entry was verified, so a `ready` image means content-addressed, not vendor-authenticated.

Joining: if you supply a `sha256` that another download is already fetching, the call returns that job instead of starting a second one. Its `url` is the URL the first caller supplied, which may not be yours, and a delete from either caller cancels it for both. Without `sha256`, two requests for the same URL are two independent downloads.

Allowed targets: public internet hosts over `http` or `https`. At submission, a URL is refused with 400 if its host is a private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade-NAT, reserved or multicast IPv4 address, an IPv6 literal, a bracketed or percent-encoded host, a numeric host in anything but canonical dotted-quad form, or if it carries credentials (`user@host`). A host name is resolved when the job runs; if any address it resolves to is not public, or it has only IPv6 addresses, the job ends `failed` (IPv6 addresses are ignored). Up to five redirects (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) are followed, and each hop is checked on the same terms before it is contacted. Any other non-2xx final status fails the job.

`osinfo-db` publishes no checksums, so a URL from `GET /osinfo` is normally a trust-on-first-use download; supply the vendor's published SHA256 if you need verification.

202.description: Download accepted. The body is the job to poll.

400.description: SpecInvalid: the url is not http or https, is longer than 2048 bytes, contains a byte outside printable ASCII, carries credentials, has a bracketed, percent-encoded or non-canonical numeric host, or names an address that is not publicly routable (private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, reserved or multicast). `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

409.description: AlreadyExists: an image with that `sha256` is already in the store. OperationInProgress: too many downloads are running, or the retention limit is reached and no finished download can be removed to make room (every retained one is still running or verifying, or the files of a finished one could not be removed; such a download stays listed until you delete it). At the retention limit the oldest removable finished download (`ready`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`) is removed automatically to make room. Wait for a running download to finish, or delete a finished one, then retry.

503.description: DownloadFailed: this host has no program available to fetch URLs, so no download can start until an operator installs one. Retrying is safe but will not succeed. Failures at the remote end (DNS, TLS, an HTTP status, a timeout) are not reported here: they happen after the 202 and appear in the job's `error` field.

delete.summary: Cancel or remove an image download
delete.description:
Cancel a running download, or remove the record of a finished one. Cancellation is asynchronous: 204 means the request was accepted, not that the transfer has stopped. The transfer is stopped at its next check (every 250 ms), its partial bytes are removed, and only then does the job read `cancelled`, so an immediate GET can still report `running`. Poll until the state is terminal if you need to know it is done.

The image published by a `ready` job is not removed; use `DELETE /isos/{sha256}` for that.

A job in `verifying` cannot be cancelled and answers 409 `BadState`: its bytes have arrived and are being hashed, and it will publish. Poll until it is `ready` or `failed`, then delete. A finished job whose files could not be removed also answers 409 `BadState` and stays listed.

204.description: Cancellation accepted, or the finished job removed.

400.description: NameInvalid: the id is not 32 lowercase hex characters. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

404.description: NotFound: no download job has this id.

409.description: BadState: the download is being verified, or its files could not be removed; `error.message` says which. Wait until it is `ready` or `failed`, or fix the storage problem, then delete again.

get.description:
List operating systems and the installer images published for them, with the URL each image can be fetched from. Use it to choose an image before downloading or uploading one; `GET /isos` lists the images already in the store. 

Rows come from the host's `osinfo-db` package. By default only `x86_64` media is listed, because it is the only architecture this service can boot. Pass `arch=all` for every architecture, or name one to filter by it. 

To use a `url`, either pass it to `POST /isos/downloads` (the service fetches it, hashes it and publishes it under the computed sha256) or fetch it yourself and upload it with `POST /isos/{sha256}`. `osinfo-db` publishes no checksums, so a download started from this catalogue without an expected digest reports `verification: "tofu"` (trust on first use). 

`available: false` means the host has no usable database and `entries` is empty; `status` says whether to install (`absent`) or repair (`damaged`) `osinfo-db`. The database is a package and lags new releases: an image newer than the installed `osinfo-db` is missing here, and once uploaded `GET /isos` lists it by its own volume label without a resolved name. 

URLs are the vendors' own and are not re-checked, so some may be dead. This happens mostly for end-of-life releases the vendor has removed from its mirror, and for URLs pinned to a point release that has since moved to an archive path (Debian, for example). Treat a failed fetch as a normal outcome: a dead URL fails the transfer and publishes nothing.

parameters.name: arch
parameters.description: Architecture to list. Defaults to `x86_64`. `all` lists every architecture, including media this host cannot boot.

post.summary: Begin or resume a snapshot artifact upload
post.description:
Declare an upload of a snapshot artifact under its sha256 and total size. If the artifact is already published, the answer is `phase: ready` and no upload is needed. If an earlier upload was interrupted, the answer gives `next_part` to resume from. Safe to repeat: it never truncates an upload in progress.

On a resume, sending a different `bytes` replaces the declared total if it is at least the bytes already stored, and the resume point is recomputed from it; this is how a mis-declared upload is corrected.

Plan for twice the artifact's size: the artifact and the VM rebuilt from it exist at the same time.

409.description: OperationInProgress: another call is working on this digest; retry shortly.

507.description: InsufficientSpace: the declared size does not fit (on a resume, the remainder does not fit).

put.summary: Upload one part of a snapshot artifact
put.description:
Append one part of the artifact. Parts are sent in order: part n is accepted only when exactly n*part_size bytes are stored. Every part except the last must be exactly `part_size` bytes. A replayed part is refused rather than applied twice, so retrying a request whose response you did not see is safe.

When the stored `bytes` reach the declared total, call `POST /imports/{sha256}/finalize`. If an upload is interrupted mid-part, `bytes` is reported at the last part boundary and `next_part` names the part to send again. After any failure, read `GET /imports/{sha256}` to find where to resume.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Zero-based part index. Part n covers bytes [n*part_size, (n+1)*part_size).

200.description: Part stored. The body gives the stored `bytes` and the `next_part`.

400.description: NameInvalid: sha256 is not 64 lowercase hex characters. SpecInvalid: the part is empty or larger than `part_size`, or the part index is not a non-negative integer. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

404.description: NotFound: no upload is in progress for this digest; call `POST /imports/{sha256}` first.

408.description: RequestBodyStalled: the request body stopped arriving for 30 seconds, or the part took longer than 30 minutes. Nothing was stored; send the same part again.

409.description: BadState: this is not the part the stored length calls for; read `next_part` and send that. BadState also means too many parts are being received at once; this part was not started, so send the same part again. AlreadyExists: the artifact is already published. OperationInProgress: another call is working on this digest; retry shortly.

507.description: InsufficientSpace: not enough storage for this part.

post.description: Hash every uploaded byte and publish the artifact if the result matches its sha256. Only a published artifact can be used to create a VM. Takes a few seconds per gigabyte. parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

204.description: All bytes were sent to the guest's serial port. This does not confirm the guest read them; read the console to see the effect.

400.description: NameInvalid: the VM name is not valid. SpecInvalid: the body is empty or larger than 4096 bytes. `SpecInvalid`: this operation takes no query parameters, and a request carrying any is refused.

404.description: NotFound: no VM has this name

408.description: RequestBodyStalled: the request body stopped arriving for 30 seconds, or took longer than 30 seconds in total. Nothing was written; send it again

409.description: BadState: the VM was created without `console` or without `console_input`. OperationInProgress: another console write to this VM is still in progress, or the VM is still being created; retry after it finishes. Orphaned: the service cannot manage the VM, and the guest may still be running. Either the VM's run cannot be verified (the recorded process is gone, does not match its record, or the record cannot be read), or the service has blocked the VM (after a restart it found more than one run that may still be live, or a delete stopped before it could tell whether the VM was removed); the error message says which. For a run that cannot be verified, check the process yourself, then call `POST /vms/{name}/force-adopt` to resume managing it or `POST /vms/{name}/force-mark-dead` to record it as dead (accepted only when the VM's disk is not locked by a running process). For a blocked VM both are refused: resolve the condition the message names, then restart hoody-vm, which settles the VM's state as it starts.

500.description: ConsoleDeliveryIndeterminate: the write failed partway and some of the bytes may have reached the guest. Read the console before resending, or the guest may receive the input twice. StorageFailed: the VM's stored configuration could not be read. Nothing was written, so the request is safe to resend once storage recovers

503.description: ConsoleUnavailable: the connection to the guest's serial console is not established right now (not yet connected, or already closed for this run). Nothing was written; the request is safe to resend

schema.description: The bytes to send to the guest's serial input: at least 1 and at most 4096. The body is sent exactly as given and the `Content-Type` header is ignored, so a JSON body is typed as its literal text. Nothing is added: end a command with its own newline (`\n`), and send control characters as themselves (0x03 for Ctrl-C, 0x04 for Ctrl-D).

see_also.reason: Read the console to see what the guest did with the input. This is the only way to confirm a write had an effect

get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream of one VM's changes, an alternative to polling `GET /vms/{name}`. Changes are pushed as they happen rather than sampled, so a state that lasts only an instant is still sent unless the filter or the buffer described below drops it.

The server subscribes to the VM's events first, then reads the VM and sends that state as the first frame, a `state` event, whatever `?events=` says. Because the subscription comes first, a change made while the snapshot is read is not missed, though the filter and the buffer below still apply to it. After the snapshot, `?events=` decides which kinds are sent; `deleted` and `resync` cannot be excluded. The server skips a change the snapshot already reflects (a non-zero `seq` not above the snapshot's `seq`). Events with `seq: 0` are not checked against the snapshot: process every one you receive. Events wait in a bounded buffer. If this client reads too slowly and the oldest are dropped, the server reads the VM again and sends `resync` with the number lost and the current state, or with `error` if the state cannot be read; if the VM turns out to be gone, it sends a final `deleted` with `lost` instead. `deleted` ends the stream. Frames carry no `id:` and nothing is replayed: to reconnect, open a new stream, whose snapshot gives the current state.

`monitor-stalled` is easy to miss: it carries `{run, stalled}` and is sent when QEMU stops responding to control commands and again when it recovers. The VM stays `Running` throughout, so no `state` event marks either change. While `stalled` is true, pause and resume are refused; `GET /vms/{name}` shows the same fact as `monitor_stalled`.

The stream follows the VM its snapshot described, identified by `vm_id`, not by name. If the VM is deleted and a new VM is created with the same name, the new VM's events are not sent here; a `resync` that finds the name held by a different VM ends the stream with a `deleted` for the original one.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Comma-separated event kinds to receive: state, progress, sidecar, qmp-error, snapshot, share-quota, monitor-stalled. Omit the parameter to receive all of them; an empty value (`events=` with no kinds) is refused with 400, as is an unknown kind. `deleted` and `resync` are sent whatever this parameter says, and cannot be named here. The opening `state` snapshot is sent regardless; the filter applies to the events after it.

200.description: The event stream (`text/event-stream`). A comment is sent every 15 seconds to keep the connection open

400.description: NameInvalid: the VM name is not valid. SpecInvalid: `events` names an unknown kind, or the query string has a parameter this operation does not accept

404.description: NotFound: no VM has this name

409.description: BadState: too many event streams are open on this service (128, shared by both event operations); close one or poll instead. OperationInProgress: the VM has just been created and is not ready yet; retry shortly. A VM whose create is still running or has failed is not refused: the stream opens with a `state` frame whose state is `Creating` or `Failed`. Orphaned: the service cannot manage the VM, and the guest may still be running. Either the VM's run cannot be verified (the recorded process is gone, does not match its record, or the record cannot be read), or the service has blocked the VM (after a restart it found more than one run that may still be live, or a delete stopped before it could tell whether the VM was removed); the error message says which. For a run that cannot be verified, check the process yourself, then call `POST /vms/{name}/force-adopt` to resume managing it or `POST /vms/{name}/force-mark-dead` to record it as dead (accepted only when the VM's disk is not locked by a running process). For a blocked VM both are refused: resolve the condition the message names, then restart hoody-vm, which settles the VM's state as it starts.

oneOf.name: share-quota
oneOf.title: Shared folder quota
oneOf.description: The VM's `share.over_quota` state changed; the quota is `share_quota_bytes`. `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota.

over.description: The new `over_quota` state: `true` on going over, `false` on coming back (a complete measurement at or below `quota - quota / 16`, rounded down) or on removal of the quota.

bytes.description: Size of the measurement the decision was made on, in bytes (allocated blocks); a lower bound when `partial` is true. When the quota is removed while no measurement is available, `bytes` is `0` with `partial: true`: no measurement is behind the event.

quota_bytes.description: The quota the crossing was judged against; null when the quota was removed.

partial.description: `bytes` is a lower bound: the measurement stopped early, or no measurement was available (then `bytes` is `0`).

get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream of changes to every VM on one connection, including VMs created after it opens, so a create can be watched from before it is requested. It never answers 404, and opens normally (and stays quiet) when there are no VMs.

Every event carries `name` and `vm_id` except `resync`, which is about the connection rather than a VM: detect it by `scope` or by the absence of `name`, never by a particular name (`all`, for example, is a valid VM name).

oneOf.name: share-quota
oneOf.title: Shared folder quota
oneOf.description: The VM's `share.over_quota` state changed; the quota is `share_quota_bytes`. `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota.

get.description:
Metrics in the Prometheus text format. Also served at `/metrics` without the API prefix, for scrapers that expect a fixed path.

The 26 metric families: process_uptime_seconds, process_resident_memory_bytes, hoody_vm_vms_by_state, hoody_vm_starts_total, hoody_vm_stops_total, hoody_vm_failures_total, hoody_vm_qmp_errors_total, hoody_vm_monitor_stalls_total, hoody_vm_autostart_failures_total, hoody_vm_share_sample_failures_total, hoody_vm_share_quota_refusals_total, hoody_vm_sidecar_restarts_total, hoody_vm_adoptions_total, hoody_vm_permits_held, hoody_vm_permits_orphaned, hoody_vm_permits_leaked, hoody_vm_unidentified_runs, hoody_vm_unidentified_run_bytes, hoody_vm_admitted_guest_ram_bytes, hoody_vm_admitted_permit_bytes, hoody_vm_reflink_fallbacks_total, hoody_vm_share_bytes, hoody_vm_share_sample_partial, hoody_vm_share_quota_bytes, hoody_vm_share_over_quota, http_requests_total.

`hoody_vm_vms_by_state{state}` always carries a series for each of the eight VM states, and `hoody_vm_sidecar_restarts_total{kind,degraded}` one for each of the three helper processes, even when the value is zero. The four `hoody_vm_share_*` families are always declared, but a VM appears in them only once its shared folder has been measured, so a missing series means not yet measured, not zero. `hoody_vm_share_quota_bytes` and `hoody_vm_share_over_quota` also include only VMs that have a shared-folder quota.

`http_requests_total` is labelled by `method`, `path` (the matched route template, such as `/api/v1/vm/vms/:name`, or `unmatched`) and `status`, for example `http_requests_total{method="GET",path="/api/v1/vm/health",status="200"} 245`.

get.description: Reports the BYOA delegated-session backend availability (claude): enabled flag, on-PATH status, trust posture. A fixed status object, NOT a paginated collection. SCOPE: the report is resolved through the layered settings the delegated session would use, so X-Hoody-Config-Dir (override) and X-Hoody-Cwd (project layer) are folded. For REMOTE BYOA, a bound X-Hoody-Computer switches the report to ON-COMPUTER detection/login probing. The realm selects that realm's settings for the report and scopes the on-computer probe; omitted, the realm a session created without a realm runs in: on an agent pinned to one realm that realm; otherwise, under a login limited to realms, its first realm, and else the active realm. The per-agent secret value WRITE is PUT /api/v1/agent/acp/agents/{agent}/secrets/{key}. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

x-error-codes.description: The daemon's own administrator check refused the request. Access to the HTTP API is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy, but the daemon keeps a separate administrator check: when the daemon was started with its own administrator token, it refuses these operations, because an HTTP request cannot supply that token. In the standard HTTP deployment the daemon has no such token, the check allows the request, and this code is not returned.
x-error-codes.resolution: Run the daemon in the standard HTTP deployment (--auth-token-path, no separate administrator token) so its check allows HTTP requests, or perform the operation from the agent's terminal interface inside the computer.

post.summary: Copy Claude Code's login to another computer, as previewed.
post.description: Applies a credential import preview: reads the source again and writes the file onto the target, readable by its owner only, through a staging file put in place in one step, so a failed copy leaves an existing login as it was. The token is used up by the call. When the source or the target no longer matches the preview, it is refused 409 preview_stale and nothing is written. An existing (or unchecked) target is replaced only with overwrite true, else 409 target_exists. A target the preview showed as absent is written only if nothing has appeared there since; if something has, it is left as it is (502 transfer_failed). A target path that is a directory is never written into. A lost answer from the last step is 503 outcome_unknown: the login may or may not have been replaced. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. Both computers must be in the request's realm. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

mode.description: file copies one file; dir copies the eligible files below a directory. kind.description: host: the computer this agent runs on. computer: the computer named by computer.

computer.description: The source computer's id; required with kind computer.

source.description: Where the files are read from. kind host reads them on the computer this agent runs on (the default when source is omitted); kind computer reads them on another computer of the same realm, named by computer.

target_computer.description: The id of the computer the files are written to. It must be another computer than the one this agent runs on.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Copy Claude Code files to another computer, as previewed.
post.description: Applies a file sync preview: plans it again and copies each file onto the target through a staging file put in place in one step. The token is used up by the call. When the file list, a file's contents or which targets exist differs from the preview, it is refused 409 preview_stale and nothing is written. A file the preview showed as present or unknown on the target is replaced only when overwrite lists its path; otherwise it is left as it is and reported in skipped. A file the preview showed as absent is put in place only if nothing has appeared there since; if something has, it is left as it is and the copy stops there (502 transfer_failed). A target path that is a directory is never written into. A path in overwrite that the preview did not plan, or planned as absent, is 400 bad_request (details.reason overwrite_not_planned) and nothing is written. Files are copied in path order; a failure stops there (502 transfer_failed, or 503 outcome_unknown when the failed file may be in place), with details.written listing the files already written. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. Both computers must be in the request's realm. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

put.summary: Set a BYOA backend's default model and effort.
put.description: Sets the default model (and reasoning effort) a BYOA ACP backend runs on. These are the values the daemon passes to the backend at connect; a delegated session started without an explicit model inherits them. An empty value clears the pin and returns the backend to its own default. The model is a Claude alias (opus, sonnet, haiku) or Claude model id, with or without the anthropic/ or claude-code/ prefix, and is stored as Claude Code takes it; another model is refused 422 model_unavailable (details.reason not_claude), an effort Claude Code does not take is refused 400 bad_request (details.field effort), and nothing is stored. 404 unknown_agent for anything that is not a known BYOA backend (claude). Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Omitted, the settings of the realm a session created without a realm runs in are written: on an agent pinned to one realm that realm; otherwise, under a login limited to realms, its first realm, and else the active realm.

put.summary: Store an ACP per-agent secret value.
put.description: Stores (or clears) one per-backend env VALUE for a BYOA ACP agent in a dedicated owner-only secrets file inside the computer. The agent settings hold only the env KEY NAMES; the VALUE lives ONLY in that secrets file. An empty value DELETES (unsets) the reference. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. SECURITY: the value is NEVER returned: the reply confirms only (agent, key, stored|cleared). 404 unknown_agent for an agent that is not a known BYOA backend (claude). Per-agent environment values are used only when Claude Code runs on this agent's own computer. A session bound to another computer uses Claude Code's credentials there, not that computer's agent secret store. Any effective per-agent environment values on the driving agent (secret or non-secret) cause a remote launch to be refused, even if the target is already authenticated. Clear all such values on the driving agent before using remote sessions; clearing a credential can prevent local sessions from authenticating. POST /sessions may return 201 before this launch check; the refusal is reported on the first turn with delegated_launch_failed.

get.summary: List the files that shape the agents.
get.description: Lists the files that shape the agents' behavior in the requesting cwd/config_dir scope, each with its absolute path on the agent's machine, so a client can open it in an external editor such as the files kit's `?edit` page. Rows, in order: the chat agent definitions (the configured default chat agent first, marked chief), the skills (SKILL.md), the instruction files (CLAUDE.md per layer and the project's AGENTS.md) and the workflow prompt files (prompts/**/*.md). Shadowed definitions are left out, every file listed exists except a shipped default agent with no file yet (see editable), and only absolute paths are returned (without X-Hoody-Cwd there is no project layer). editable is false, with a reason, for a shipped default agent the realm has no file for yet (path is where a save through PUT /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source would create it) and for a built-in hoody-* skill (reserved), which the agent rewrites at every start: write your own skill and name it in an agent's `skills:` list instead. An edit made on disk applies at the agent's next turn (applies: next_turn), with no restart and no new session: agent definitions are re-read when their file changes, skills are watched, and instruction and prompt files are read on every turn. An external editor writes the file directly: it takes no revision, so a save overwrites a concurrent change made through PUT /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source, PUT /api/v1/agent/skills/source or the agent's own tools (last writer wins). settings.json is not listed. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of agent definitions, sorted by name, without the definition files whose stem is not a valid agent name (see name); each element is the daemon's agent info with the properties below.

name.description: The agent's name: its definition file's stem, the value a session's agent and every agents/{name} route take. Unique in the list. A definition file whose stem is not a valid agent name (lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or digit) is left out of this list. A new name is capped at 128 characters; an agent named before the cap may be longer and is still listed.

frontmatter_name.description: The frontmatter name, present only when it differs from name.

description.description: The agent's description. Omitted when empty.

path.description: The definition file. Empty for a shipped default the realm has no file for.

provenance.description: Where the definition comes from: the user layer, the project's .hoody layer, an unmodified copy of the shipped default, the embedded shipped default (no file), or product-owned for the bot agent, which always runs the shipped definition and whose model alone can be pinned.

shadows_lower.description: True when this file overrides a same-named file in a lower layer. Omitted when false.

model.description: The agent's model. Omitted when it inherits the session model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort from the frontmatter. Omitted when unset.

max_turns.description: Turn cap from the frontmatter. Omitted when unset.

tools.description: The tools list. Omitted when absent, which means every tool unless strict_tools. An empty array is `tools: none`: the agent has no tools at all.

strict_tools.description: The agent gets exactly its tools list. Omitted when false.

mcp_tools.description: The MCP tools the agent gets, each server/tool or server/*; an empty array means none. Omitted when the frontmatter has no mcp_tools key.

skills.description: The skills the agent gets; an empty array means none. Omitted when the frontmatter has no skills key: then the chat agent gets every enabled skill and a spawned agent none.

compaction_max_tokens.description: Prompt tokens at which the agent's automatic compaction starts, as the chat agent, when that is lower than the box's threshold. Omitted when unset.

unknown_tools.description: Entries of tools that are not built-in tools (advisory). Omitted when none.

unknown_skills.description: Entries of skills that name no installed skill in this scope (advisory). Omitted when none.

missing_vs_default.description: Tools the shipped default of the same name has and this file lacks (advisory). Omitted when none.

name_mismatch.description: The frontmatter name differs from the file stem. Omitted when false.

duplicate_name.description: Another listed file has the same frontmatter name. Omitted when false.

is_configured_default.description: The configured default chat agent for this scope. Omitted when false.

shipped_default.description: Hoody ships an agent of this name, whatever file defines it now: such an agent can be reset to the shipped definition, and it cannot be renamed, nor deleted except as a scoped realm's own copy (a shared project-layer copy is not the realm's own) that is not the configured default (is_configured_default). Omitted when false.

spawn_advertised.description: Whether spawn_agent's menu lists the agent; a hidden agent is still spawnable by name. Always present.

prompt_preview.description: The system prompt's first six non-empty lines. Omitted when the prompt is empty.

prompt.description: The full system prompt. Omitted when empty.

realm.description: The agent definition's realm: "global" for one not tied to a realm, else its 24-hex realm id. Pass it as X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) to reach it by id.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages (the full count, not the page size).

limit.description: Items per page (present only when limit>0).

requestBody.description: Chat-agent definition.

model.description: A provider/model spec or a fusion/<slug> composite.

tools.description: Built-in tool names the agent gets.

effort.description: Reasoning level. xhigh is refused when the agent's model does not take it; omit for the model's default.

max_steps_per_turn.description: The most model requests one chat turn of this agent may make. A turn that reaches it stops with error_code max_steps, and the next message continues. It applies to the agent's own chat turns, a Claude Code session's included, and not to it as a helper or workflow step. A Claude Code session needs Claude Code 2.1.306 or later to stop there; on an older one a turn of this agent is refused with error_code step_limit_unavailable before it starts. Omit for no limit.

labels.description: Grouping labels; no commas or newlines.

strict_tools.description: true gives the agent exactly its tools list.

mcp_tools.description: MCP tools the agent gets: server/tool, server/* or mcp__server__tool; an empty array means none.

skills.description: Skill names the agent gets; an empty array means none. Left out: every enabled skill as the chat agent, none as a spawned agent.

prompt_blocks.description: Block name to boolean; false drops that optional system-prompt block.

ask_timeout.description: How long an approval or question this agent raises as a helper waits on a session with helper_gates on. A duration such as "10m" or a whole number of seconds, more than zero and at most 24h. Default: 15 minutes.

thinking.description: Turn reasoning on or off.

response_format.description: Ask for a JSON object reply.

compaction.description: same_prefix: a compaction resends the session's own system prompt, tools and transcript so it reuses the prompt cache. Fusion models use the default compaction, and so does a compaction that recovers from an overflowed request or whose own request overflows. Omit for the default compaction.

compaction_max_tokens.description: Prompt tokens at which the agent's automatic compaction starts, as the chat agent, when that is lower than the box's threshold. Keeps a long conversation's prompt small, so a provider cache miss stays fast. Omit to use the threshold alone.

frontmatter.description: Optional frontmatter keys: description, model, tools, effort, max_turns, max_steps_per_turn, labels, strict_tools, mcp_tools, skills, prompt_blocks, ask_timeout, thinking, temperature, response_format, compaction, compaction_max_tokens. Any other key is rejected. strict_tools is a boolean: true gives the agent EXACTLY its tools list (no skill or workflow tool is added, no MCP tool unless mcp_tools names it, and a call to any other tool is refused), and with no tools list it gets only ask_question_to_user, todo_read, todo_write, task_output, list_tasks and bash_job_wait. mcp_tools is an array of the MCP tools the agent gets, each `server/tool`, `server/*` (every tool of that server) or `mcp__server__tool`: when present the agent is given exactly the matching MCP tools, strict or not, and an empty array means none; when absent a non-strict agent gets every MCP tool and a strict one none. skills is an array of skill names: when present the agent gets exactly those of them that are installed and enabled, and an empty array means none; when absent the chat agent gets every enabled skill and a spawned agent none. prompt_blocks is an object of block name to boolean: false drops that optional system-prompt block when this agent runs, as the chat agent or as a helper or workflow step, and never turns on a block the box settings turned off (names: contract, transcripts, frequent_files, hook_context, memory, project_instructions, agent_instructions, team_rules, skills, workflows, verbosity, hoody_platform, hoody_exec, fleet_notice, environment). ask_timeout is how long each approval or question this agent raises as a helper on a helper_gates session waits before it is denied: a duration string such as "10m" or a number of seconds, more than zero and at most 24h; the default is 15 minutes. thinking (enabled or disabled), temperature (a number from 0 to 2) and response_format (json_object) are model settings sent on every turn the agent runs, as the chat agent (a session's model_settings win per field), a helper or a workflow step; one the model cannot take is left out of the request and logged, not an error. thinking enabled takes its level from effort on models that take a level; thinking disabled together with an effort is rejected. compaction (same_prefix) makes a compaction resend the session's own system prompt, tools and transcript so it reuses the prompt cache (fusion models use the default compaction); omit it for the default compaction. compaction_max_tokens (a whole number of at least 8192) starts this agent's automatic compaction, as the chat agent, once the prompt reaches that many tokens when that is lower than the box's threshold, so a long conversation's prompt stays small and a cache miss stays fast.

delete.description: Deletes a custom chat agent. The answer is 200 with {output, is_error}; when the agent cannot be deleted, is_error is true and output says why. The agents that ship with Hoody and the default chat agent cannot be deleted: edit them with PUT /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source or restore them with POST /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/reset-to-shipped. In a realm that has its own copy of a shipped agent, deleting that copy brings the shipped agent back. The bot agent is shipped too, and only its model can be chosen: deleting a realm's own copy removes that realm's model choice; anywhere else, clear the model with PATCH /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/model and an empty model, or with POST /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/reset-to-shipped. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. An agent that does not exist is 404 not_found "agent not found", and so is a realm this login does not serve. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

requestBody.description: New agent source (the {name} comes from the path).

content.description: The full markdown source (frontmatter + system prompt). Frontmatter is read as one `key: value` per line: a `tools:` line must be a comma-separated list on that same line, because a YAML block list underneath it parses to NOTHING and the agent is then granted every tool (only the benign special tools when `strict_tools` is on), the opposite of the restriction it looks like. The turn cap is spelled `max_turns`; a `turns` line is ignored.

expected_revision.description: Optional: the `revision` GET /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source returned. A save whose source changed since is refused 409 revision_conflict (details.current_revision) and writes nothing. Omit to save unconditionally. The revision is bound to the realm this request resolves to: on a gateway without a realm pin, a revision read while another realm was active is refused 409 revision_conflict (details.current_revision is this realm's), never written into the other realm.

model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
description: Web-focused research agent.
tools: web_search, read_file
max_turns: 12
---

requestBody.description: New tool allow-list (the {name} comes from the path).

tools.description: Tool names allowed for the agent; an empty list removes the line (= all tools, or only the benign specials for a strict_tools agent).

none.description: Optional: true, with an empty tools list, writes `tools: none`, so the agent has no tools at all. With a non-empty list it is refused 400 bad_request and nothing is written. Omitted or false: tools as above.

^(?:computer|computer_id|config_dir|cwd|.description: A scope member (computer, computer_id, config_dir, cwd or realm) is not refused as an unknown field, and its value is ignored: a request's scope comes from its scope headers and parameters, never from the body.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Toggle a single tool for an agent.
post.description: Toggles one tool on/off in an agent's frontmatter tools line. Each call flips the tool's current state; there is no way to request a specific state. The bot agent is product-owned: this is refused for it with 400 bad_request; only its model can be pinned (PATCH /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/model). An agent that does not exist is 404 not_found "agent not found", and so is a realm this login does not serve. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.description: The tool.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Speaks `input` with a speech model and answers the whole audio. A capability the model lacks (a format, instructions, a speed) is 400 before any paid call. Each call takes one of the client IP's completion slots. The call is billed to the realm it acts in. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Omitted, an agent pinned to one realm uses that realm and any other agent its active realm. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: pcm: 16-bit little-endian samples, no header.

X-Hoody-Audio-Format.description: The audio format: wav, mp3 or pcm (16-bit little-endian, no header).

X-Hoody-Audio-Rate.description: The sample rate in Hz. For mp3 it is present only when the model declares a rate.

X-Hoody-Audio-Op.description: The id of the speech operation, as in the session usage rows.

post.summary: Turn text into speech, streamed over SSE.
post.description: The same request as POST /api/v1/agent/audio/speech, answered as Server-Sent Events while the audio is made: speech.audio.delta frames (pcm or mp3), then speech.audio.done. Only for models that stream speech. Nothing is written before the first frame: a failure before it is an ordinary JSON error with its status; after it, an error frame. A `: ping` comment is sent every 25 s. Every call is billed: do not replay a stream automatically. Each open stream holds one of the client IP's stream slots. The call is billed to the realm it acts in. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Omitted, an agent pinned to one realm uses that realm and any other agent its active realm. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

200.description: SSE stream of the audio: speech.audio.delta frames, then speech.audio.done. A `: ping` comment line is sent every 25 s and carries no data.

post.summary: Turn speech into text, streamed over SSE.
post.description: The same request as POST /api/v1/agent/audio/transcriptions for wav and mp3, answered as Server-Sent Events: transcript.text.delta frames as the model hears more, then transcript.text.done with the whole transcript. Only for a model whose GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models row has partials true (another model is 400 bad_request before any paid call); response_format is json. Nothing is written before the first frame: a failure before it is an ordinary JSON error with its status; after it, an error frame. A `: ping` comment is sent every 25 s. Every call is billed: do not replay a stream automatically. Each open stream holds one of the client IP's stream slots. The call is billed to the realm it acts in. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Omitted, an agent pinned to one realm uses that realm and any other agent its active realm. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.description: Lists the voices a text-to-speech model offers; ?model= names one model, omitted lists the voices of every available one except the Hoody AI relay models, whose voices are listed only when ?model= names one. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= may name a realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); the listing is the same in every realm and is not billed. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported; on an agent that is not pinned, a named realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. Omitted, an agent pinned to one realm uses that realm, and any other agent its active realm, refused with 409 realm_blocked while that selection is blocked. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found.
