servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Lists the realm's Bots, sorted by id. The default Bot, chief, is created on first use, so the list is never empty. With ?realm=all it lists the Bots of every realm this login serves, global included, sorted by realm and then id; each row carries its realm and address. Under ?realm=all, chief is not created in a realm that has no Bots yet. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of Bots. A Bot another agent process on this machine serves is a locked row (owned_elsewhere: true) carrying only its id, realm and address.

id.description: The Bot's id, unique in its realm and fixed at creation; the {id} of the Bot routes.

uid.description: The Bot's globally unique id, fixed at creation. Use it to tell Bots apart across realms.

realm.description: The realm the Bot lives in, fixed at creation: global, or a realm id.

address.description: How the Bot is named in its own messages and logs: bot:<realm>/<id>.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph; empty when not set. The Bot is told its name and role before its next message.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. Empty when none.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session. Empty until the first message is posted. The Bot runtime posts to it: send your messages with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id this view shows while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. A question on this session whose frame_request kind starts with bot. is one of the Bot's own tool calls: the Bot runtime answers it, so do not answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer.

model.description: The model chosen for the Bot's session; empty means the bot agent's own model. A change takes effect when the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset).

session_model.description: The model the Bot's current session runs, as that session reported it. It differs from model after a change of model until the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Absent while the Bot has no session or its session has not reported a model yet.

guardrails.description: Limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens.

allowed_computers.description: Computers the Bot may open delegates on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents the Bot may open delegates with. Empty means any.

yolo.description: When true, every delegate runs with YOLO mode on: its tool approvals are granted without asking.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: How the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs answer a message whose reply starts delegates. false: the answer waits up to wait_seconds for each delegate the reply started to show its first step (it asks for an approval or an answer, reports, closes, or its first tool call finishes without asking), so an approval asked right away comes in the same answer. true: the answer comes at once, for apps that keep listening on their own; what the delegates ask or report later comes with the answer to the next message (and with the MCP updates tool and the Bot's stream). A reply that starts no delegate never waits, and the Bot's own routes are not affected. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, an answer waits for the delegates its reply started when async is false, a whole number from 1 to 60; 15 until changed. The answer still never waits past its own time limit. Kept but unused while async is true.

mcp_hints.description: Whether the results of the Bot's MCP tools ask, ask_audio, answer and status end with one line saying how many new messages and approvals wait for the caller, and the MCP instructions tell the app to call updates when they do. status reports the counts (pending) either way. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. null when routing is off and names no workers.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed. Empty when not set.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it. Empty when not set.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

stt_model.description: The speech-to-text model of the Bot's spoken messages (a model with the stt capability). Empty: the agent's default.

language.description: The language spoken: a language code such as en, or auto. Speech output always accepts auto. Speech input is checked only when the model lists languages; then it must be one of them (auto only if listed).

speed.description: The speaking speed of tts_model, within the model's range. Omitted: the model's normal speed.

stt_prompt.description: Words the speech-to-text model should expect, such as names. Only for an stt_model that takes a prompt.

speak_wakes.description: Read aloud the Bot's replies to delegate reports, not only its replies to your spoken messages. Default false.

speak_gates.description: Announce approvals and questions waiting on you in a voice conversation. Default true.

tts_chars.description: Characters read aloud per day; 0 turns speech output off.

stt_seconds.description: Seconds of speech transcribed per day; 0 turns spoken messages off.

limits.description: The Bot's own daily speech limits, per UTC day. Each is at most the realm's limit; omitted: the default (200000 characters, 14400 seconds).

speech.description: The Bot's speech settings: the models, voice and language its spoken messages and replies use. null when none are set. An unknown model, one without the needed capability, or one the model catalogue marks unavailable is refused 422 model_unavailable naming the field; a missing key or relay is not checked here (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether the speech settings are ready). A voice, language, speed, prompt or limit the models cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

session_id.description: The delegate session.

state.description: pending: its session has not confirmed the change yet; it is sent again until it does. refused: its approval policy does not allow YOLO mode, so it keeps asking for approvals; it is not sent again until yolo changes.

reason.description: Why the last attempt did not apply, when one failed.

yolo_unapplied.description: Open delegates whose YOLO mode does not match yolo yet. Empty when every open delegate runs as yolo says.

kind.description: api: created through this API. system: created by the agent itself (the default Bot, or a Bot made before creators were recorded).

id.description: Who within the kind, when known.

created_by.description: Who created the Bot. A record only: it grants nothing.

revision.description: The revision of the Bot's settings: it goes up by one on every PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} and PUT /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/guardrails, and never on the Bot's own work. Send it back as expect_revision on those two routes so a change made since you read the Bot is not overwritten; send uid as expect_uid on them and on delete, reset, forget and purge so a Bot created again under the same id is not the one changed.

used.description: Dispatches and delegate messages the Bot made on its own since your last message.

max.description: How many it may make on its own between two of your messages.

per_delegate_max.description: How many of them may go to one delegate.

waiting_for_you.description: true once the Bot reached a limit: it does nothing more on its own until you post a message.

autonomy.description: The Bot's follow-ups without you. Work that reacts to your message is not counted; each message you post starts the count again.

used.description: Realtime user items the Bot has seen; null when they could not be read.

max.description: How many it may see; realtime_max_items, 1048576 until changed.

realtime_items.description: The Realtime user items the Bot has recorded. An item id is recorded once and never forgotten, so a client replaying its history never sends an old item to the Bot again. At max a new item is refused and its connection closed until the owner raises realtime_max_items.

open_delegates.description: Delegate sessions the Bot has open.

queued.description: Messages and delegate events waiting to be posted to the Bot.

turn_running.description: true while the Bot works on a turn: the Bot accepted a post (a message or delegate events) and the turn has not ended. false when the Bot is idle, including while a post waits or was refused.

turn_id.description: The Bot's running turn on its session, present only while turn_running is true. To stop that turn and no later one, send it to POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session.

gate_id.description: The gate's answerable id. Correlate on this string: [gate] log rows name it and the answer routes take it. The number called gate_id inside an answer's `resolved` object and in the session's gate_resolved events is a different id.

type.description: confirm: an approval. question: a question to answer.

summary.description: What it asks, in one line.

generation.description: The gate's generation; echo it with gate_id when answering.

pending_gate.description: A gate parked on the Bot's own session, waiting for you: a rule asked to check in before one of the Bot's dispatches. Answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer for a question) on the Bot's session, echoing gate_id. The Bot never answers it itself. A message sent to the Bot while it waits declines it, telling the Bot a new message was sent, and is posted when the Bot's turn ends; delegate events stay queued until that turn ends. null when none.

kind.description: The platform.

state.description: The connection, as GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels/{cid} reports it.

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known (the same values as the channel's own state_reason). Absent when none.

paired_count.description: How many people are paired with it.

requested_chats.description: How many of its chats ask to be approved (state requested).

code.description: What the note is about.

field.description: The setting it is about.

reason.description: Why, when the code has reasons.

notes.description: The notes of the account's last credential check, as the channel's effective.notes carries them (for example telegram_privacy_on); [] when none.

channels.description: The Bot's chat channels, in short; [] when none. GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels has the rest. Credentials are never shown.

oneOf.title: BotLockedRow
oneOf.description: A Bot another agent process on this machine serves: nothing of it is read here. Its routes answer 409 bot_owned_elsewhere until this agent takes it over.

realm.description: The Bot's realm: global or a 24-hex realm id.

owned_elsewhere.description: Always true on a locked row.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages (the full count, not the page size).

limit.description: Items per page (present only when limit>0).

suspended_count.description: How many Bots of the listed realm (of every realm this login serves, with ?realm=all) are suspended and so not listed. POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume brings them back. A Bot is suspended when the account this agent is signed in with signs out, changes, or no longer serves the Bot's realm: it stops working, is not listed, and its routes answer 404 not_found as for an unknown id. It resumes on its own when the same account serves its realm again.

items.name: Chief
items.role: Keeps the web app's releases moving.

post.description: Creates a Bot: a long-lived assistant that works by opening delegate sessions on computers and agents, following them, and telling you what they did. Its own session is opened when the first message is posted. guardrails are limits on the work, not instructions to the Bot: they apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens. The Bot receives them before its next message, and each delegate receives them at the top of its first prompt as limits set by the owner of the work. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The new Bot.

example.name: Chief
example.role: Keeps the web app's releases moving.

id.description: The Bot's id, unique in its realm and fixed at creation; the {id} of the Bot routes.

uid.description: The Bot's globally unique id, fixed at creation. Use it to tell Bots apart across realms.

realm.description: The realm the Bot lives in, fixed at creation: global, or a realm id.

address.description: How the Bot is named in its own messages and logs: bot:<realm>/<id>.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph; empty when not set. The Bot is told its name and role before its next message.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. Empty when none.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session. Empty until the first message is posted. The Bot runtime posts to it: send your messages with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id this view shows while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. A question on this session whose frame_request kind starts with bot. is one of the Bot's own tool calls: the Bot runtime answers it, so do not answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer.

model.description: The model chosen for the Bot's session; empty means the bot agent's own model. A change takes effect when the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset).

session_model.description: The model the Bot's current session runs, as that session reported it. It differs from model after a change of model until the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Absent while the Bot has no session or its session has not reported a model yet.

guardrails.description: Limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens.

allowed_computers.description: Computers the Bot may open delegates on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents the Bot may open delegates with. Empty means any.

yolo.description: When true, every delegate runs with YOLO mode on: its tool approvals are granted without asking.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: How the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs answer a message whose reply starts delegates. false: the answer waits up to wait_seconds for each delegate the reply started to show its first step (it asks for an approval or an answer, reports, closes, or its first tool call finishes without asking), so an approval asked right away comes in the same answer. true: the answer comes at once, for apps that keep listening on their own; what the delegates ask or report later comes with the answer to the next message (and with the MCP updates tool and the Bot's stream). A reply that starts no delegate never waits, and the Bot's own routes are not affected. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, an answer waits for the delegates its reply started when async is false, a whole number from 1 to 60; 15 until changed. The answer still never waits past its own time limit. Kept but unused while async is true.

mcp_hints.description: Whether the results of the Bot's MCP tools ask, ask_audio, answer and status end with one line saying how many new messages and approvals wait for the caller, and the MCP instructions tell the app to call updates when they do. status reports the counts (pending) either way. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. null when routing is off and names no workers.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed. Empty when not set.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it. Empty when not set.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

stt_model.description: The speech-to-text model of the Bot's spoken messages (a model with the stt capability). Empty: the agent's default.

language.description: The language spoken: a language code such as en, or auto. Speech output always accepts auto. Speech input is checked only when the model lists languages; then it must be one of them (auto only if listed).

speed.description: The speaking speed of tts_model, within the model's range. Omitted: the model's normal speed.

stt_prompt.description: Words the speech-to-text model should expect, such as names. Only for an stt_model that takes a prompt.

speak_wakes.description: Read aloud the Bot's replies to delegate reports, not only its replies to your spoken messages. Default false.

speak_gates.description: Announce approvals and questions waiting on you in a voice conversation. Default true.

tts_chars.description: Characters read aloud per day; 0 turns speech output off.

stt_seconds.description: Seconds of speech transcribed per day; 0 turns spoken messages off.

limits.description: The Bot's own daily speech limits, per UTC day. Each is at most the realm's limit; omitted: the default (200000 characters, 14400 seconds).

speech.description: The Bot's speech settings: the models, voice and language its spoken messages and replies use. null when none are set. An unknown model, one without the needed capability, or one the model catalogue marks unavailable is refused 422 model_unavailable naming the field; a missing key or relay is not checked here (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether the speech settings are ready). A voice, language, speed, prompt or limit the models cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

session_id.description: The delegate session.

state.description: pending: its session has not confirmed the change yet; it is sent again until it does. refused: its approval policy does not allow YOLO mode, so it keeps asking for approvals; it is not sent again until yolo changes.

reason.description: Why the last attempt did not apply, when one failed.

yolo_unapplied.description: Open delegates whose YOLO mode does not match yolo yet. Empty when every open delegate runs as yolo says.

kind.description: api: created through this API. system: created by the agent itself (the default Bot, or a Bot made before creators were recorded).

id.description: Who within the kind, when known.

created_by.description: Who created the Bot. A record only: it grants nothing.

revision.description: The revision of the Bot's settings: it goes up by one on every PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} and PUT /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/guardrails, and never on the Bot's own work. Send it back as expect_revision on those two routes so a change made since you read the Bot is not overwritten; send uid as expect_uid on them and on delete, reset, forget and purge so a Bot created again under the same id is not the one changed.

used.description: Dispatches and delegate messages the Bot made on its own since your last message.

max.description: How many it may make on its own between two of your messages.

per_delegate_max.description: How many of them may go to one delegate.

waiting_for_you.description: true once the Bot reached a limit: it does nothing more on its own until you post a message.

autonomy.description: The Bot's follow-ups without you. Work that reacts to your message is not counted; each message you post starts the count again.

used.description: Realtime user items the Bot has seen; null when they could not be read.

max.description: How many it may see; realtime_max_items, 1048576 until changed.

realtime_items.description: The Realtime user items the Bot has recorded. An item id is recorded once and never forgotten, so a client replaying its history never sends an old item to the Bot again. At max a new item is refused and its connection closed until the owner raises realtime_max_items.

open_delegates.description: Delegate sessions the Bot has open.

queued.description: Messages and delegate events waiting to be posted to the Bot.

turn_running.description: true while the Bot works on a turn: the Bot accepted a post (a message or delegate events) and the turn has not ended. false when the Bot is idle, including while a post waits or was refused.

turn_id.description: The Bot's running turn on its session, present only while turn_running is true. To stop that turn and no later one, send it to POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session.

gate_id.description: The gate's answerable id. Correlate on this string: [gate] log rows name it and the answer routes take it. The number called gate_id inside an answer's `resolved` object and in the session's gate_resolved events is a different id.

type.description: confirm: an approval. question: a question to answer.

summary.description: What it asks, in one line.

generation.description: The gate's generation; echo it with gate_id when answering.

pending_gate.description: A gate parked on the Bot's own session, waiting for you: a rule asked to check in before one of the Bot's dispatches. Answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer for a question) on the Bot's session, echoing gate_id. The Bot never answers it itself. A message sent to the Bot while it waits declines it, telling the Bot a new message was sent, and is posted when the Bot's turn ends; delegate events stay queued until that turn ends. null when none.

kind.description: The platform.

state.description: The connection, as GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels/{cid} reports it.

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known (the same values as the channel's own state_reason). Absent when none.

paired_count.description: How many people are paired with it.

requested_chats.description: How many of its chats ask to be approved (state requested).

code.description: What the note is about.

field.description: The setting it is about.

reason.description: Why, when the code has reasons.

notes.description: The notes of the account's last credential check, as the channel's effective.notes carries them (for example telegram_privacy_on); [] when none.

channels.description: The Bot's chat channels, in short; [] when none. GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels has the rest. Credentials are never shown.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. The Bot's name, role, instructions, guardrails and dispatch limits together must fit in 16 KiB; a write that would go past that is refused 400 bad_request with details.field naming a field.

model.description: The model the Bot's session runs. Omit it for the bot agent's own model. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable.

guardrails.description: Limits that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens. The Bot's name, role, instructions, guardrails and dispatch limits together must fit in 16 KiB; a write that would go past that is refused 400 bad_request with details.field naming a field.

allowed_computers.description: Computers delegates may run on. Empty or omitted means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents delegates may run. Empty or omitted means any.

yolo.description: Run every delegate with YOLO mode on (approvals granted without asking). Default false.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked. Default strict.

async.description: true: answers on the OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs come at once; false: one waits up to wait_seconds for delegates its reply started. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: 1 to 60; default 15. A wrong type, null or out-of-range value here, in async or in mcp_hints is refused 400 bad_request (details.field).

mcp_hints.description: MCP results end with a count of new messages and approvals. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. Omitted: off.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

stt_model.description: The speech-to-text model of the Bot's spoken messages (a model with the stt capability). Empty: the agent's default.

language.description: The language spoken: a language code such as en, or auto. Speech output always accepts auto. Speech input is checked only when the model lists languages; then it must be one of them (auto only if listed).

speed.description: The speaking speed of tts_model, within the model's range. Omitted: the model's normal speed.

stt_prompt.description: Words the speech-to-text model should expect, such as names. Only for an stt_model that takes a prompt.

speak_wakes.description: Read aloud the Bot's replies to delegate reports, not only its replies to your spoken messages. Default false.

speak_gates.description: Announce approvals and questions waiting on you in a voice conversation. Default true.

tts_chars.description: Characters read aloud per day; 0 turns speech output off.

stt_seconds.description: Seconds of speech transcribed per day; 0 turns spoken messages off.

limits.description: The Bot's own daily speech limits, per UTC day. Each is at most the realm's limit; omitted: the default (200000 characters, 14400 seconds).

speech.description: Speech settings for spoken messages and spoken replies. Omitted: none. An unknown model, one without the needed capability, or one the model catalogue marks unavailable is refused 422 model_unavailable naming the field; a missing key or relay is not checked here (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether the speech settings are ready). A voice, language, speed, prompt or limit the models cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

^(?:computer|computer_id|config_dir|cwd|.description: A scope member (computer, computer_id, config_dir, cwd or realm) is not refused as an unknown field, and its value is ignored: a request's scope comes from its scope headers and parameters, never from the body.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Resumes the suspended Bots of the realm, or of every realm this login serves with ?realm=all. A Bot is suspended when the account this agent is signed in with signs out, changes, or no longer serves the Bot's realm: it stops working, is not listed, and its routes answer 404 not_found as for an unknown id. It resumes on its own when the same account serves its realm again. A Bot resumed here runs under the account signed in now. A Bot suspended after the agent accepted the call (for the first time, or again after another call resumed it) stays suspended and is not listed: the later suspension wins, and a new call resumes it. Calling it again answers an empty list once none is suspended. A 503 means a Bot could not be resumed right now and stays suspended: retry in a moment. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all. A realm this login does not serve answers 404 not_found, unless ?realm=all skips it. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: The realm whose Bots to resume: "global" (Bots not tied to a realm), a 24-hex realm id, or "all" for every realm this login serves, global included. Also accepted as the X-Hoody-Realm header, except "all". Omitted, the agent's current realm.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The Bots this call resumed.

realm.description: Its realm: "global" or a realm id.

resumed.description: Each Bot this call resumed, in realm and id order; empty when it resumed none: none was suspended, each was suspended after the agent accepted the call, or a Bot was being suspended or resumed at that moment (call again).

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Returns one Bot. chief is created on first use. The Bot's live progress is on its own session: follow session_id with GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream for its reply text and thinking as they are generated, its tool calls and the end of each turn (event.agent_done). GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream carries only the finished log rows. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id shown here while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/delegates/{sid}/stop stops one of its delegates, not the Bot. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The Bot.

example.name: Chief
example.role: Keeps the web app's releases moving.

id.description: The Bot's id, unique in its realm and fixed at creation; the {id} of the Bot routes.

uid.description: The Bot's globally unique id, fixed at creation. Use it to tell Bots apart across realms.

realm.description: The realm the Bot lives in, fixed at creation: global, or a realm id.

address.description: How the Bot is named in its own messages and logs: bot:<realm>/<id>.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph; empty when not set. The Bot is told its name and role before its next message.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. Empty when none.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session. Empty until the first message is posted. The Bot runtime posts to it: send your messages with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id this view shows while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. A question on this session whose frame_request kind starts with bot. is one of the Bot's own tool calls: the Bot runtime answers it, so do not answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer.

model.description: The model chosen for the Bot's session; empty means the bot agent's own model. A change takes effect when the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset).

session_model.description: The model the Bot's current session runs, as that session reported it. It differs from model after a change of model until the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Absent while the Bot has no session or its session has not reported a model yet.

guardrails.description: Limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens.

allowed_computers.description: Computers the Bot may open delegates on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents the Bot may open delegates with. Empty means any.

yolo.description: When true, every delegate runs with YOLO mode on: its tool approvals are granted without asking.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: How the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs answer a message whose reply starts delegates. false: the answer waits up to wait_seconds for each delegate the reply started to show its first step (it asks for an approval or an answer, reports, closes, or its first tool call finishes without asking), so an approval asked right away comes in the same answer. true: the answer comes at once, for apps that keep listening on their own; what the delegates ask or report later comes with the answer to the next message (and with the MCP updates tool and the Bot's stream). A reply that starts no delegate never waits, and the Bot's own routes are not affected. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, an answer waits for the delegates its reply started when async is false, a whole number from 1 to 60; 15 until changed. The answer still never waits past its own time limit. Kept but unused while async is true.

mcp_hints.description: Whether the results of the Bot's MCP tools ask, ask_audio, answer and status end with one line saying how many new messages and approvals wait for the caller, and the MCP instructions tell the app to call updates when they do. status reports the counts (pending) either way. Default true.

used.description: Dispatches and delegate messages the Bot made on its own since your last message.

max.description: How many it may make on its own between two of your messages.

per_delegate_max.description: How many of them may go to one delegate.

waiting_for_you.description: true once the Bot reached a limit: it does nothing more on its own until you post a message.

autonomy.description: The Bot's follow-ups without you. Work that reacts to your message is not counted; each message you post starts the count again.

used.description: Realtime user items the Bot has seen; null when they could not be read.

max.description: How many it may see; realtime_max_items, 1048576 until changed.

realtime_items.description: The Realtime user items the Bot has recorded. An item id is recorded once and never forgotten, so a client replaying its history never sends an old item to the Bot again. At max a new item is refused and its connection closed until the owner raises realtime_max_items.

open_delegates.description: Delegate sessions the Bot has open.

queued.description: Messages and delegate events waiting to be posted to the Bot.

turn_running.description: true while the Bot works on a turn: the Bot accepted a post (a message or delegate events) and the turn has not ended. false when the Bot is idle, including while a post waits or was refused.

turn_id.description: The Bot's running turn on its session, present only while turn_running is true. To stop that turn and no later one, send it to POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel.

type.description: confirm: an approval. question: a question to answer.

summary.description: What it asks, in one line.

generation.description: The gate's generation; echo it with gate_id when answering.

pending_gate.description: A gate parked on the Bot's own session, waiting for you: a rule asked to check in before one of the Bot's dispatches. Answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer for a question) on the Bot's session, echoing gate_id. The Bot never answers it itself. A message sent to the Bot while it waits declines it, telling the Bot a new message was sent, and is posted when the Bot's turn ends; delegate events stay queued until that turn ends. null when none.

patch.description: Changes the fields the body names. name, role and instructions are announced to the Bot before its next message. id, uid, realm, created, created_at and created_by never change: a body that names one is refused 400 field_immutable and nothing changes. yolo applies at once to every open delegate. allowed_computers, allowed_agents, routing and the worker settings apply to the next delegate the Bot opens. guardrail_check applies to the Bot's next dispatch or delegate message. async and wait_seconds apply to the next answer of the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs, and mcp_hints to the next request to its MCP URL, with no reset. model applies to the Bot's next session: the running session keeps its model until POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset starts a new one. Guardrails are changed with PUT /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/guardrails. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: expect_uid
parameters.description: The uid of the Bot you read. When the id now names another Bot (the one you read was deleted and a new one created under the id), the request is refused 412 bot_changed and nothing changes. A Bot that is gone answers 404 not_found, as without it, and a request carrying it never creates chief. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: expect_revision
parameters.description: The revision of the Bot you read. When the Bot's settings or guardrails were written since, the request is refused 412 revision_mismatch and nothing changes. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The Bot after the change.

example.name: Chief
example.role: Keeps the web app's releases moving.

id.description: The Bot's id, unique in its realm and fixed at creation; the {id} of the Bot routes.

uid.description: The Bot's globally unique id, fixed at creation. Use it to tell Bots apart across realms.

realm.description: The realm the Bot lives in, fixed at creation: global, or a realm id.

address.description: How the Bot is named in its own messages and logs: bot:<realm>/<id>.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph; empty when not set. The Bot is told its name and role before its next message.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. Empty when none.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session. Empty until the first message is posted. The Bot runtime posts to it: send your messages with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id this view shows while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. A question on this session whose frame_request kind starts with bot. is one of the Bot's own tool calls: the Bot runtime answers it, so do not answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer.

model.description: The model chosen for the Bot's session; empty means the bot agent's own model. A change takes effect when the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset).

session_model.description: The model the Bot's current session runs, as that session reported it. It differs from model after a change of model until the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Absent while the Bot has no session or its session has not reported a model yet.

guardrails.description: Limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens.

allowed_computers.description: Computers the Bot may open delegates on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents the Bot may open delegates with. Empty means any.

yolo.description: When true, every delegate runs with YOLO mode on: its tool approvals are granted without asking.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: How the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs answer a message whose reply starts delegates. false: the answer waits up to wait_seconds for each delegate the reply started to show its first step (it asks for an approval or an answer, reports, closes, or its first tool call finishes without asking), so an approval asked right away comes in the same answer. true: the answer comes at once, for apps that keep listening on their own; what the delegates ask or report later comes with the answer to the next message (and with the MCP updates tool and the Bot's stream). A reply that starts no delegate never waits, and the Bot's own routes are not affected. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, an answer waits for the delegates its reply started when async is false, a whole number from 1 to 60; 15 until changed. The answer still never waits past its own time limit. Kept but unused while async is true.

mcp_hints.description: Whether the results of the Bot's MCP tools ask, ask_audio, answer and status end with one line saying how many new messages and approvals wait for the caller, and the MCP instructions tell the app to call updates when they do. status reports the counts (pending) either way. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. null when routing is off and names no workers.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed. Empty when not set.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it. Empty when not set.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

stt_model.description: The speech-to-text model of the Bot's spoken messages (a model with the stt capability). Empty: the agent's default.

language.description: The language spoken: a language code such as en, or auto. Speech output always accepts auto. Speech input is checked only when the model lists languages; then it must be one of them (auto only if listed).

speed.description: The speaking speed of tts_model, within the model's range. Omitted: the model's normal speed.

stt_prompt.description: Words the speech-to-text model should expect, such as names. Only for an stt_model that takes a prompt.

speak_wakes.description: Read aloud the Bot's replies to delegate reports, not only its replies to your spoken messages. Default false.

speak_gates.description: Announce approvals and questions waiting on you in a voice conversation. Default true.

tts_chars.description: Characters read aloud per day; 0 turns speech output off.

stt_seconds.description: Seconds of speech transcribed per day; 0 turns spoken messages off.

limits.description: The Bot's own daily speech limits, per UTC day. Each is at most the realm's limit; omitted: the default (200000 characters, 14400 seconds).

speech.description: The Bot's speech settings: the models, voice and language its spoken messages and replies use. null when none are set. An unknown model, one without the needed capability, or one the model catalogue marks unavailable is refused 422 model_unavailable naming the field; a missing key or relay is not checked here (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether the speech settings are ready). A voice, language, speed, prompt or limit the models cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

requestBody.description: The fields to change; omitted fields are kept. id, uid, realm, created, created_at and created_by are fixed at creation: naming one is refused 400 field_immutable.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph. Empty clears it.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. "" clears them. The Bot's name, role, instructions, guardrails and dispatch limits together must fit in 16 KiB; a write that would go past that is refused 400 bad_request with details.field naming a field.

model.description: The model of the Bot's next session, started by POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset; the running session keeps its model. Empty for the bot agent's own model. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable and nothing changes.

allowed_computers.description: Computers delegates may run on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents delegates may run. Empty means any.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: true: answers on the OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs come at once; false: one waits up to wait_seconds for delegates its reply started. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: 1 to 60; default 15. A wrong type, null or out-of-range value here, in async or in mcp_hints is refused 400 bad_request (details.field).

mcp_hints.description: MCP results end with a count of new messages and approvals. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. The object replaces the Bot's routing whole; it applies to the Bot's next dispatch and is announced to the Bot before its next message.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it.

realtime_max_items.description: How many Realtime user items the Bot may record, from the larger of 1 and the number already recorded (realtime_items.used) to 16777216; 1048576 until changed. A lower value, null or anything but a whole number is refused 400 bad_request with details.field realtime_max_items, and nothing changes. A new value applies to the next item.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

stt_model.description: The speech-to-text model of the Bot's spoken messages (a model with the stt capability). Empty: the agent's default.

language.description: The language spoken: a language code such as en, or auto. Speech output always accepts auto. Speech input is checked only when the model lists languages; then it must be one of them (auto only if listed).

speed.description: The speaking speed of tts_model, within the model's range. Omitted: the model's normal speed.

stt_prompt.description: Words the speech-to-text model should expect, such as names. Only for an stt_model that takes a prompt.

speak_wakes.description: Read aloud the Bot's replies to delegate reports, not only its replies to your spoken messages. Default false.

speak_gates.description: Announce approvals and questions waiting on you in a voice conversation. Default true.

tts_chars.description: Characters read aloud per day; 0 turns speech output off.

stt_seconds.description: Seconds of speech transcribed per day; 0 turns spoken messages off.

limits.description: The Bot's own daily speech limits, per UTC day. Each is at most the realm's limit; omitted: the default (200000 characters, 14400 seconds).

speech.description: Speech settings. The object replaces the Bot's speech settings whole; null removes them. A refused value changes nothing. An unknown model, one without the needed capability, or one the model catalogue marks unavailable is refused 422 model_unavailable naming the field; a missing key or relay is not checked here (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether the speech settings are ready). A voice, language, speed, prompt or limit the models cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

^(?:computer|computer_id|config_dir|cwd).description: A scope member (computer, computer_id, config_dir or cwd) is not refused as an unknown field, and its value is ignored: a request's scope comes from its scope headers and parameters, never from the body.

delete.description: Deletes the Bot and its log and archive. First, best effort and for at most a few seconds: every open delegate that is working or waiting on an approval is stopped, an approval the stop did not reach is declined, and auto-approve is turned off on the delegates the Bot turned it on for. Its session and its delegates are not closed: they stay listed under GET /api/v1/agent/sessions, and they end like any idle session. A person can continue a delegate directly; the Bot's own session has no responder any more, so fork it to continue its transcript. Deleting chief removes it; the next use creates a new one. A Bot that is being stopped (for example while the agent shuts down) answers 503 service_unavailable with a Retry-After header: send the delete again after that many seconds. A delete sent again after one that went through answers 404 not_found. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: expect_uid
parameters.description: The uid of the Bot you read. When the id now names another Bot (the one you read was deleted and a new one created under the id), the request is refused 412 bot_changed and nothing changes. A Bot that is gone answers 404 not_found, as without it, and a request carrying it never creates chief. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.
