schema.description: A page of rows.

items.text: [report] 9a1be4c07d2f4c11 "Run the tests" (self, default) completed: The tests pass.

seq.description: The row's position in the Bot's log; increases by one per row and survives forget.

role.description: user: a posted message. bot: the Bot's reply to one turn, written when the turn ends; a turn with no reply text writes none. event: a delegate event the Bot is told about ([report], [gate], [gone] or [stop] line), or a [gate] line naming the Bot's own session, which waits for you (pending_gate on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}). system: a note from the runtime.

text.description: The row's text.

session_id.description: The session the row is about: the Bot's own for a reply, the delegate's for an event.

turn_id.description: On a reply: the Bot turn it ends.

message_id.description: On a user row: the id the message was accepted under.

message_ids.description: On a reply, and on a [limit], [provider] or [error] system row about a turn: the message_ids of the messages the turn answered, in the order they were accepted. A turn no message started (a delegate event) has none.

kind.description: user: you. bot: the Bot (id is its uid). delegate: one of its delegates (id is the session). system: the runtime.

id.description: Who within the kind, when there is more than one.

from.description: Who wrote the row. Absent on rows written before it was recorded.

trigger.description: Why the turn the row belongs to ran: human (your message), wake (a delegate's event) or clear (forget). Absent when not known.

via.description: The door the message came through, never set by the client: tui (the terminal app), openai, anthropic or mcp (the compat doors), voice or twilio, or telegram, slack or discord (a message from a chat channel of the Bot). Absent for POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages.

sender.description: On a user row that came through another door than POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages: that door.

schema_version.description: The row's format version. Absent on rows written before versions were recorded.

kind.description: On a runtime row (an event or system row, and a [stop] row written in your name): what it is, from its leading tag ([report] is report, [not sent] is not_sent); note for an event or system row without a tag. Absent on posted messages and replies, and on rows written before it was recorded: read the leading tag of those.

fail_kind.description: On the [provider] or [error] row of a failed Bot turn: the cause. content_filter and refusal are the provider stopping the reply ([provider]); no_credentials, auth and unconfigured mean the Bot could not use its model provider; quota_wait and rate_limit mean the provider asked to wait; model means the provider does not accept the Bot's model; spend_cap means the Bot's session reached a spend cap or its spend settings file is not valid; other is a cause without a name of its own. Absent on rows written before it was recorded.

delegate_title.description: On a row about one of the Bot's delegates: the title the Bot gave it, as it was when the row was written. Absent when it had none, and on rows written before it was recorded.

origin.description: The door the audio came through: rest (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages/audio), mcp, ws (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice), realtime or twilio.

duration_ms.description: The audio's length in milliseconds; 0 when the door does not report it.

lang.description: The language the speech was transcribed as, when known.

conn.description: On a voice-connection message: the connection that sent it, as that connection's session frame names it.

utt.description: On a voice-connection message: the connection's utterance it was assembled from; with conn it names the spoken send.

voice.description: On a user row of a spoken message: how it came. Absent on typed messages (a voice connection's typed text included) and on rows written before it was recorded.

items.description: The page of archived rows after since, oldest first.

next_since.description: The seq of the last row returned (since when none): pass it as since to read on.

has_more.description: true when rows after next_since were already written: read on with since=next_since. With before or tail: true when older rows exist; read them with before.

before.description: With before or tail: the seq of the oldest row returned (the before asked for when none). Pass it as before to read the older page. next_since is then the seq right before the one asked for: follow on from there with since or GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream.

post.summary: Stop the Bot's running turn, and only that turn.
post.description: Stops the Bot's own turn named by turn_id: the turn_id GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} shows while turn_running is true. The turn stops if it is still running; a turn that already ended is not touched, and neither is any later turn, so a Stop that arrives late never stops newer work. The Bot's delegates keep running: stop one with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/delegates/{sid}/stop. matched is true when turn_id was the Bot's running turn when the request arrived, and false when it was not (the turn already ended, or the Bot was idle): then nothing was stopped. A 200 means the stop was sent to the Bot's session; the Bot view shows turn_running false once the turn has ended. A 503 means it is not known whether the stop reached the session: send it again, which never stops another turn. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

patch.description: Changes the settings every channel of the Bot inherits. Unknown names are 400; a refused value is 422 setting_invalid and nothing is applied. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. 503 service_unavailable means the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now: send the request again, after Retry-After when it is set. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of channels.

kind.description: The chat app.

state.description: The connection: connecting, connected, awaiting_owner (no owner paired yet: send the enrolment code to the bot in a direct message), degraded (reconnecting or rate limited), standby (another channel runs this bot account), conflict, auth_failed (the credentials were refused; replace them), paused (state_reason says why), realm_unserved (the Bot's realm is not served here), stopping, stopped (the Bot is being deleted).

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known. Absent when none. One of: identity_in_use (standby: another channel runs this bot account); other_poller (conflict: another program reads this Telegram bot's updates); webhook_set (conflict: the Telegram bot account has a webhook set, so the channel cannot read its updates; update it with enabled true and delete_webhook true to remove it); stop_stuck (stopping: the channel did not stop in time); payload_too_large (a message to or from the chat app was too large); credentials_missing (the stored credentials cannot be read); unauthorized (auth_failed: the chat app refused the credentials); missing_scope (auth_failed: the Slack token lacks a scope the channel needs); missing_intent (auth_failed: Discord refused the intents); mismatched_app (auth_failed: the two Slack tokens belong to different apps); unreachable (the chat app cannot be reached); app_unverified (auth_failed: the Slack app could not be verified); missing_access (the chat app refused access to a chat: the app was removed from it or may not post there); guild_unavailable (a Discord server is unavailable on Discord's side); message_content_missing (degraded: Discord refused the message content intent); binding_changed (auth_failed: the credentials now name another bot account); rate_limited (degraded: the chat app is rate limiting the bot); storage_failing (degraded: the agent cannot save the channel's state); gateway_refused (degraded: Discord closed the connection with a code a reconnect cannot fix); lock_unavailable (the agent cannot lock the chat app: file locks fail, or a Discord chat app is missing its IDs); lock_lost (the lock was lost while the chat app was running); channel_disabled (paused: the channel is turned off); bot_paused (paused: the Bot's channels are paused); not_running (paused: the channel is on, but no channel runtime is running for the Bot).

post.summary: Connect a Bot to a chat app.
post.description: Checks the credentials with the chat app and stores them; a channel created on, while the Bot's channels are not paused, also takes the bot account for this channel. A channel created off, or while the Bot's channels are paused, is only checked: the bot account is not taken and nothing runs it until it is turned on and the channels run. The credentials are never returned. With dm_policy owner (the default) the answer carries the owner's enrolment code once; send it to the bot in a direct message to pair yourself. Slack needs token (xoxb-) and app_token (xapp-); a Slack bot token missing a scope the channel needs is refused 422 channel_credentials_invalid (reason missing_scope). A Telegram bot with a webhook is refused 409 channel_conflict (reason webhook_set), whether the channel is created on or off, unless delete_webhook is true, which removes the webhook (also for a channel created off, which then keeps nothing taken). While the Bot's channels are paused, delete_webhook is refused 409 channel_conflict (reason bot_paused) and nothing is created: resume the channels, then send it again. Discord's intents are not checked at create: once the channel connects, a refused message content intent reads state degraded (state_reason message_content_missing) and refused intents read auth_failed (state_reason missing_intent). With an Idempotency-Key the same create sent again returns the same channel and creates nothing twice. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. 503 service_unavailable means the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now: send the request again, after Retry-After when it is set. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Opaque retry key (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace). The same create sent again with the same key returns its channel; the same key with a different body is 422.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

state.description: The connection: connecting, connected, awaiting_owner (no owner paired yet: send the enrolment code to the bot in a direct message), degraded (reconnecting or rate limited), standby (another channel runs this bot account), conflict, auth_failed (the credentials were refused; replace them), paused (state_reason says why), realm_unserved (the Bot's realm is not served here), stopping, stopped (the Bot is being deleted).

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known. Absent when none. One of: identity_in_use (standby: another channel runs this bot account); other_poller (conflict: another program reads this Telegram bot's updates); webhook_set (conflict: the Telegram bot account has a webhook set, so the channel cannot read its updates; update it with enabled true and delete_webhook true to remove it); stop_stuck (stopping: the channel did not stop in time); payload_too_large (a message to or from the chat app was too large); credentials_missing (the stored credentials cannot be read); unauthorized (auth_failed: the chat app refused the credentials); missing_scope (auth_failed: the Slack token lacks a scope the channel needs); missing_intent (auth_failed: Discord refused the intents); mismatched_app (auth_failed: the two Slack tokens belong to different apps); unreachable (the chat app cannot be reached); app_unverified (auth_failed: the Slack app could not be verified); missing_access (the chat app refused access to a chat: the app was removed from it or may not post there); guild_unavailable (a Discord server is unavailable on Discord's side); message_content_missing (degraded: Discord refused the message content intent); binding_changed (auth_failed: the credentials now name another bot account); rate_limited (degraded: the chat app is rate limiting the bot); storage_failing (degraded: the agent cannot save the channel's state); gateway_refused (degraded: Discord closed the connection with a code a reconnect cannot fix); lock_unavailable (the agent cannot lock the chat app: file locks fail, or a Discord chat app is missing its IDs); lock_lost (the lock was lost while the chat app was running); channel_disabled (paused: the channel is turned off); bot_paused (paused: the Bot's channels are paused); not_running (paused: the channel is on, but no channel runtime is running for the Bot).

A name is repeated only when it is 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter; when no unknown name is, field is empty and the list is empty.

get.summary: How to get the credentials of a chat app.
get.description: The steps to create a bot account in the chat app and the credentials a create needs. For Slack the answer also carries the app manifest to create the app from. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. 503 service_unavailable means the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now: send the request again, after Retry-After when it is set. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

example.name: Ops Bot
steps: Open a chat with @BotFather in Telegram and send /newbot.
Choose a display name and a username ending in "bot".
Copy the token BotFather gives you.

In groups Telegram sends the bot only commands for it and replies to it while its privacy mode is on: send /setprivacy to @BotFather and choose Disable, then remove the bot from the group and add it again; or make the bot an admin of the group.

get.summary: Get one of a Bot's chat channels.
get.description: The channel, its paired people and its chats. Credentials are never returned. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. 503 service_unavailable means the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now: send the request again, after Retry-After when it is set. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: The channel id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The channel.

kind.description: The chat app.

state.description: The connection: connecting, connected, awaiting_owner (no owner paired yet: send the enrolment code to the bot in a direct message), degraded (reconnecting or rate limited), standby (another channel runs this bot account), conflict, auth_failed (the credentials were refused; replace them), paused (state_reason says why), realm_unserved (the Bot's realm is not served here), stopping, stopped (the Bot is being deleted).

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known. Absent when none. One of: identity_in_use (standby: another channel runs this bot account); other_poller (conflict: another program reads this Telegram bot's updates); webhook_set (conflict: the Telegram bot account has a webhook set, so the channel cannot read its updates; update it with enabled true and delete_webhook true to remove it); stop_stuck (stopping: the channel did not stop in time); payload_too_large (a message to or from the chat app was too large); credentials_missing (the stored credentials cannot be read); unauthorized (auth_failed: the chat app refused the credentials); missing_scope (auth_failed: the Slack token lacks a scope the channel needs); missing_intent (auth_failed: Discord refused the intents); mismatched_app (auth_failed: the two Slack tokens belong to different apps); unreachable (the chat app cannot be reached); app_unverified (auth_failed: the Slack app could not be verified); missing_access (the chat app refused access to a chat: the app was removed from it or may not post there); guild_unavailable (a Discord server is unavailable on Discord's side); message_content_missing (degraded: Discord refused the message content intent); binding_changed (auth_failed: the credentials now name another bot account); rate_limited (degraded: the chat app is rate limiting the bot); storage_failing (degraded: the agent cannot save the channel's state); gateway_refused (degraded: Discord closed the connection with a code a reconnect cannot fix); lock_unavailable (the agent cannot lock the chat app: file locks fail, or a Discord chat app is missing its IDs); lock_lost (the lock was lost while the chat app was running); channel_disabled (paused: the channel is turned off); bot_paused (paused: the Bot's channels are paused); not_running (paused: the channel is on, but no channel runtime is running for the Bot).

needs_owner.description: True when dm_policy is owner and the channel has no owner yet: send the enrolment code to the bot in a direct message.

team.description: Slack only: the Slack team the app is installed in.

invite_url.description: Discord only: the link that adds the bot to a server.

identity.description: The bot account in the chat app.

settings.description: The settings set on this channel (the rest inherit).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

allowed_chats.description: When not empty, only these platform chat ids are served; with group_mode allowlist only the listed groups the owner has approved are served (at most 200).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

blocked_chats.description: Platform chat ids whose messages are dropped (at most 200).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

blocked_users.description: Platform user ids whose messages are dropped in every chat, whatever the other access settings say (at most 200).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

channel_lease.description: Keep the agent running while the chat app is enabled. false: the chat app alone does not keep it running; an open Bot session still does.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

chat_commands.description: Chat commands that work: any subset of status, stop, bind, unbind, help. A command not listed is ordinary text.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

command_denied_reply.description: What a sender without the control right hears when they send a command: hint (one line per hour per sender and chat) or silent.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

command_prefix.description: Character that starts a chat command: one of ! . ; ~, or / on Telegram (the default there; ! elsewhere).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

connection_opens_per_hour.description: Slack only: connections the channel may open per hour, failed ones included (1 to 120).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

decide_in_groups.description: Whether approvals may be shown and decided in a group chat. false keeps cards, gate updates and gate decisions out of groups.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

default_rights.description: Rights a person gets when added to the allowlist (and the default for pairing_rights): any subset of chat, control, gates. Open guests can only chat.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

delivery_expiry_hours.description: Hours after which an answer that could not be delivered is given up (1 to 168).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

dm_policy.description: Who may talk to the Bot in a direct message: owner (owners only), allowlist (people the owner added or paired), pairing (a person with a valid pairing code is added; they may talk to the Bot only if the code grants chat), open (anyone, as a guest).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

enabled.description: Run the chat app. false stops it and sends nothing.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

format.description: Send answers with the platform's markup (rich) or as plain text.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

gate_cards.description: How a pending approval is shown: on (a card with buttons), links (a card with the text only), off (no card). Presentation only: who may decide is gate_deciders.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

gate_deciders.description: Who may decide an approval from this channel: none, owner (owners), named (people with the gates right), principals (everyone with the chat right). A guest never decides.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

gate_detail.description: What an approval card shows: summary (the tool, the target and shortened details) or minimal (the tool name only).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

gate_ttl_minutes.description: Minutes after which an approval card is shown as expired and its buttons refuse (0 = never, else 1 to 10080).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

group_mode.description: How group chats are admitted: off (groups are ignored), owner_approves (after the owner approves the group), allowlist (only groups listed in allowed_chats, once the owner has approved them), open (any group where the Bot is addressed; its members are guests).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

hide_secrets.description: Hide the chat app's stored credentials from the agent's tools and, where the sandbox supports masks, from shells it starts afterwards (a shell without that support can still read them). Not a boundary: it does not stop root or sudo.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

home_chat.description: The chat (a direct message or an approved group of this channel) that receives the Bot's own updates; null sends none.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

identify_per_day.description: Discord only: gateway logins the channel may attempt per day (1 to 500).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

identify_per_hour.description: Discord only: gateway logins the channel may attempt per hour (1 to 60).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

lang.description: Language of the channel's fixed lines (en, de, fr, es, pt, it, ja, zh). The Bot's own answers are not translated.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

max_parts.description: Most parts one answer is sent in (1 to 20); a longer answer is cut.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

max_principals.description: Most people a channel keeps (1 to 32); pairing, an allowlist add and owner enrolment beyond it are refused.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

max_text_bytes.description: Longest message accepted, in bytes (256 to 65536; a character outside basic Latin takes 2 to 4).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

mention_only.description: In a group, read only messages that address the Bot (a mention, a reply to the Bot, or the command prefix). false reads every message of an approved group and needs the platform's message-content permission.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

mirror_other_doors.description: Also send the Bot's replies to messages from other places (the app, the API) to the home chat.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

no_reply_notice.description: Send one line to the chat that asked when the Bot's turn ends without an answer.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

outbound_rate.description: Messages per second the channel sends to one chat; at least 0.001 and not above the platform's limit, which is the default.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

overflow_note.description: End a cut answer with a line saying it continues in the session.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

pairing_code_burn_tries.description: Wrong codes in total before the active code stops working (5 to 200).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

pairing_rights.description: Rights a pairing code grants when the request names none: a subset of chat, control, gates. Unset, it follows default_rights.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

pairing_ttl_minutes.description: How long a pairing or owner enrolment code stays valid, in minutes (1 to 1440).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

pairing_user_burn_minutes.description: How long a person who sent too many wrong codes is refused, in minutes (1 to 1440); a correct code is refused too.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

pairing_user_burn_tries.description: Wrong codes from one person before that person is refused for pairing_user_burn_minutes (1 to 20).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

parse_mode.description: Telegram only: the markup used for rich answers, html or plain.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

part_chars.description: Longest message part, in characters (an emoji or other character outside the basic range counts as two): 200 up to the platform's limit (Telegram 4096, Slack 3900, Discord 2000), which is the default.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

push_detail.description: How a pushed update is written: brief (one line) or full (the whole update, split into at most max_parts messages of up to part_chars each).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

push_events.description: Bot updates sent to the home chat on their own, any subset of: report (a delegate finished a turn), gate (the Bot or a delegate asks for an approval or an answer, or that request ended), gone (a delegate was closed), stop (a stop of a delegate went through or failed), waiter (a wait ended: found, ran out or stopped), limit (the Bot stopped at its step limit), budget (the Bot did as much as it may on its own), error (the Bot's turn failed), provider (the model provider refused or filtered a reply), not_sent (a message could not be queued), reset (a reset dropped a message or an answer).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

rate_chat_per_min.description: Messages one chat may send per minute, all senders together (0 = no limit, up to 600).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

rate_user_per_day.description: Messages one person may send per day (0 = no limit, up to 20000).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

rate_user_per_hour.description: Messages one person may send per hour (0 = no limit, up to 3600).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

rate_user_per_min.description: Messages one person may send per minute (0 = no limit, up to 600).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

reply_style.description: How an answer is attached to the message it answers: thread, reply or plain.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

show_sender_name.description: Tell the Bot the sender's display name with each group message (an unverified hint, never authority); direct messages never carry it.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

split_at.description: Where a long answer is split into parts: paragraph, line or word.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

typing.description: Show a typing indicator while the Bot works on an answer (Telegram and Discord; Slack has no bot typing indicator).

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

unpaired_reply.description: What a sender who may not talk to the Bot hears: hint (one line per hour asking them to get a pairing code from the owner) or silent.

source.description: Where the value comes from: the Bot, the channel, or the default.

wake_replies.description: Send the Bot's replies to its own updates (replies nobody in a chat asked for) to the home chat.

code.description: What the note is about.

field.description: The setting it is about.

reason.description: Why, when the code has reasons.

notes.description: Notes about the effective values. hide_secrets_partial: hide_secrets is on, but on this machine only the agent's file tools refuse the secret files; its shell can still read them (reason landlock or unsandboxed). telegram_privacy_on (field group_mode, reason groups_get_only_messages_to_the_bot): the Telegram bot has privacy mode on, so in groups Telegram sends it only commands for it and replies to it, not the other messages; turn privacy mode off with @BotFather (/setprivacy, Disable), then remove the bot from the group and add it again; or make the bot a group admin. slack_history_scopes_missing (field mention_only, reason unmentioned_messages_need_history_scopes): mention_only is false on the channel or one of its chats, but the Slack bot token lacks channels:history or groups:history, so Slack sends the bot no message that does not mention it; add both scopes and the message.channels and message.groups events, reinstall the app and send the new token.

effective.description: The value each setting has here, where it comes from, and notes.

id.description: The person's id on this channel.

platform_user.description: Their user id in the chat app.

rights.description: chat: talk to the Bot. control: stop and steer work. gates: decide approvals.

owner.description: The channel's owner (all rights).

lang.description: Their language, when set.

principals.description: The people paired with the channel.

can_read.description: Whether the bot sees every message of this group, as far as is known: true for a Telegram bot with privacy mode off, or one that is an admin of the group; false for one with privacy mode on that is not an admin there (it sees only commands and replies to it). Absent when not known: other platforms, direct chats, before the account's credential check, or while the channel does not run.

chats.description: The chats the bot is in.

last_error.description: The last connection error. Absent when none.

from.description: Start (RFC 3339).

possible.description: Messages may have been lost, not certainly.

last_gap.description: The last time window in which messages to the bot may have been lost (the channel was down). Absent when none.

patch.summary: Change one of a Bot's chat channels.
patch.description: Renames the channel, turns it on or off, sets its home chat or changes its settings. Turning it on takes the bot account in the chat app again. A refused credential or setting leaves the channel unchanged. After a 503, read the channel before retrying: the settings may already have changed. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. 503 service_unavailable means the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now: send the request again, after Retry-After when it is set. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: The channel id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

state.description: The connection: connecting, connected, awaiting_owner (no owner paired yet: send the enrolment code to the bot in a direct message), degraded (reconnecting or rate limited), standby (another channel runs this bot account), conflict, auth_failed (the credentials were refused; replace them), paused (state_reason says why), realm_unserved (the Bot's realm is not served here), stopping, stopped (the Bot is being deleted).

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known. Absent when none. One of: identity_in_use (standby: another channel runs this bot account); other_poller (conflict: another program reads this Telegram bot's updates); webhook_set (conflict: the Telegram bot account has a webhook set, so the channel cannot read its updates; update it with enabled true and delete_webhook true to remove it); stop_stuck (stopping: the channel did not stop in time); payload_too_large (a message to or from the chat app was too large); credentials_missing (the stored credentials cannot be read); unauthorized (auth_failed: the chat app refused the credentials); missing_scope (auth_failed: the Slack token lacks a scope the channel needs); missing_intent (auth_failed: Discord refused the intents); mismatched_app (auth_failed: the two Slack tokens belong to different apps); unreachable (the chat app cannot be reached); app_unverified (auth_failed: the Slack app could not be verified); missing_access (the chat app refused access to a chat: the app was removed from it or may not post there); guild_unavailable (a Discord server is unavailable on Discord's side); message_content_missing (degraded: Discord refused the message content intent); binding_changed (auth_failed: the credentials now name another bot account); rate_limited (degraded: the chat app is rate limiting the bot); storage_failing (degraded: the agent cannot save the channel's state); gateway_refused (degraded: Discord closed the connection with a code a reconnect cannot fix); lock_unavailable (the agent cannot lock the chat app: file locks fail, or a Discord chat app is missing its IDs); lock_lost (the lock was lost while the chat app was running); channel_disabled (paused: the channel is turned off); bot_paused (paused: the Bot's channels are paused); not_running (paused: the channel is on, but no channel runtime is running for the Bot).

requestBody.description: The fields to change.

enabled.description: Turn the channel on or off. Only here: settings.enabled and unset enabled are refused 400.

home_chat.description: The chat id updates go to; null removes it. Only here: settings.home_chat and unset home_chat are refused 400.

delete_webhook.description: Telegram only, with enabled true: remove the bot's webhook. Refused 409 channel_conflict (reason bot_paused) while the Bot's channels are paused and the channel is not running.

allowed_chats.description: When not empty, only these platform chat ids are served; with group_mode allowlist only the listed groups the owner has approved are served (at most 200).

blocked_chats.description: Platform chat ids whose messages are dropped (at most 200).

blocked_users.description: Platform user ids whose messages are dropped in every chat, whatever the other access settings say (at most 200).

channel_lease.description: Keep the agent running while the chat app is enabled. false: the chat app alone does not keep it running; an open Bot session still does.

chat_commands.description: Chat commands that work: any subset of status, stop, bind, unbind, help. A command not listed is ordinary text.

command_denied_reply.description: What a sender without the control right hears when they send a command: hint (one line per hour per sender and chat) or silent.

command_prefix.description: Character that starts a chat command: one of ! . ; ~, or / on Telegram (the default there; ! elsewhere).

connection_opens_per_hour.description: Slack only: connections the channel may open per hour, failed ones included (1 to 120).

decide_in_groups.description: Whether approvals may be shown and decided in a group chat. false keeps cards, gate updates and gate decisions out of groups.

default_rights.description: Rights a person gets when added to the allowlist (and the default for pairing_rights): any subset of chat, control, gates. Open guests can only chat.

delivery_expiry_hours.description: Hours after which an answer that could not be delivered is given up (1 to 168).

dm_policy.description: Who may talk to the Bot in a direct message: owner (owners only), allowlist (people the owner added or paired), pairing (a person with a valid pairing code is added; they may talk to the Bot only if the code grants chat), open (anyone, as a guest).

format.description: Send answers with the platform's markup (rich) or as plain text.

gate_cards.description: How a pending approval is shown: on (a card with buttons), links (a card with the text only), off (no card). Presentation only: who may decide is gate_deciders.

gate_deciders.description: Who may decide an approval from this channel: none, owner (owners), named (people with the gates right), principals (everyone with the chat right). A guest never decides.

gate_detail.description: What an approval card shows: summary (the tool, the target and shortened details) or minimal (the tool name only).

gate_ttl_minutes.description: Minutes after which an approval card is shown as expired and its buttons refuse (0 = never, else 1 to 10080).

group_mode.description: How group chats are admitted: off (groups are ignored), owner_approves (after the owner approves the group), allowlist (only groups listed in allowed_chats, once the owner has approved them), open (any group where the Bot is addressed; its members are guests).

hide_secrets.description: Hide the chat app's stored credentials from the agent's tools and, where the sandbox supports masks, from shells it starts afterwards (a shell without that support can still read them). Not a boundary: it does not stop root or sudo.

identify_per_day.description: Discord only: gateway logins the channel may attempt per day (1 to 500).

identify_per_hour.description: Discord only: gateway logins the channel may attempt per hour (1 to 60).

lang.description: Language of the channel's fixed lines (en, de, fr, es, pt, it, ja, zh). The Bot's own answers are not translated.

max_parts.description: Most parts one answer is sent in (1 to 20); a longer answer is cut.

max_principals.description: Most people a channel keeps (1 to 32); pairing, an allowlist add and owner enrolment beyond it are refused.

max_text_bytes.description: Longest message accepted, in bytes (256 to 65536; a character outside basic Latin takes 2 to 4).

mention_only.description: In a group, read only messages that address the Bot (a mention, a reply to the Bot, or the command prefix). false reads every message of an approved group and needs the platform's message-content permission.

mirror_other_doors.description: Also send the Bot's replies to messages from other places (the app, the API) to the home chat.

no_reply_notice.description: Send one line to the chat that asked when the Bot's turn ends without an answer.

outbound_rate.description: Messages per second the channel sends to one chat; at least 0.001 and not above the platform's limit, which is the default.

overflow_note.description: End a cut answer with a line saying it continues in the session.

pairing_code_burn_tries.description: Wrong codes in total before the active code stops working (5 to 200).

pairing_rights.description: Rights a pairing code grants when the request names none: a subset of chat, control, gates. Unset, it follows default_rights.

pairing_ttl_minutes.description: How long a pairing or owner enrolment code stays valid, in minutes (1 to 1440).

pairing_user_burn_minutes.description: How long a person who sent too many wrong codes is refused, in minutes (1 to 1440); a correct code is refused too.

pairing_user_burn_tries.description: Wrong codes from one person before that person is refused for pairing_user_burn_minutes (1 to 20).

parse_mode.description: Telegram only: the markup used for rich answers, html or plain.

part_chars.description: Longest message part, in characters (an emoji or other character outside the basic range counts as two): 200 up to the platform's limit (Telegram 4096, Slack 3900, Discord 2000), which is the default.

push_detail.description: How a pushed update is written: brief (one line) or full (the whole update, split into at most max_parts messages of up to part_chars each).

push_events.description: Bot updates sent to the home chat on their own, any subset of: report (a delegate finished a turn), gate (the Bot or a delegate asks for an approval or an answer, or that request ended), gone (a delegate was closed), stop (a stop of a delegate went through or failed), waiter (a wait ended: found, ran out or stopped), limit (the Bot stopped at its step limit), budget (the Bot did as much as it may on its own), error (the Bot's turn failed), provider (the model provider refused or filtered a reply), not_sent (a message could not be queued), reset (a reset dropped a message or an answer).

rate_chat_per_min.description: Messages one chat may send per minute, all senders together (0 = no limit, up to 600).

rate_user_per_day.description: Messages one person may send per day (0 = no limit, up to 20000).

rate_user_per_hour.description: Messages one person may send per hour (0 = no limit, up to 3600).

rate_user_per_min.description: Messages one person may send per minute (0 = no limit, up to 600).

reconnect_backoff_max_seconds.description: Longest wait, in seconds, of the normal backoff between reconnect attempts (5 to 600). A connection-open limit or a retry delay from the chat app can make a wait longer.

reply_style.description: How an answer is attached to the message it answers: thread, reply or plain.

show_sender_name.description: Tell the Bot the sender's display name with each group message (an unverified hint, never authority); direct messages never carry it.

split_at.description: Where a long answer is split into parts: paragraph, line or word.

typing.description: Show a typing indicator while the Bot works on an answer (Telegram and Discord; Slack has no bot typing indicator).

unpaired_reply.description: What a sender who may not talk to the Bot hears: hint (one line per hour asking them to get a pairing code from the owner) or silent.

wake_replies.description: Send the Bot's replies to its own updates (replies nobody in a chat asked for) to the home chat.

settings.description: Settings to set; null removes one so it inherits. enabled and home_chat are not settable here (400, details.field names the key and details.top_level the member to use).

unset.description: Settings to remove so they inherit, like null in settings. enabled and home_chat are refused 400 (use the top-level members). A name both set and unset is 400.

delete.summary: Delete one of a Bot's chat channels.
delete.description: Disconnects the channel and deletes it with its credentials, paired people and chats. When the connection is still stopping, the call waits up to about 10 seconds for it to stop: stopped in time, the channel is deleted and the answer is 200. Still stopping after that (or when the request ends first), the answer is 202 and nothing is deleted yet: the channel is deleted when its connection stops. A delete sent again waits again, and answers 404 once the channel is gone. 503 service_unavailable means one of two things. When the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now, the channel was not deleted: send the delete again, after Retry-After when it is set. When the channel was deleted but its files on disk (its stored credentials included) cannot be removed, the answer is 503 service_unavailable too: the channel is gone, and a delete sent again answers 404. To tell them apart, get the channel: 200 means it is still there (send the delete again), 404 that it was deleted. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

delete.description: Forgets the chat and its settings; if the bot is still in it, it shows up again as a new request. A channel connects the Bot to one bot account in a chat app; people paired with it talk to the Bot there. 503 service_unavailable means the Bot's channels are being handed over or their store is not available right now: send the request again, after Retry-After when it is set. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

summary.description: What it asks, in one line.

generation.description: The gate's generation; echo it with gate_id when answering.

queued_commands.description: Messages from the Bot the delegate has not read yet.

kind.description: interrupt: a message that stopped the current work first.

how.description: Once committed: next_step, read before the delegate's next step; new_turn, read as a new turn; stop, a stop carried out.

from.description: bot: the Bot sent it. user: you did (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/delegates/{sid}/stop).

post.summary: Stop one of a Bot's delegates now.
post.description: Stops the delegate's work at once, whatever the Bot is doing: its running turn, its background tasks, workflow runs and shells end, its loops pause, and messages from the Bot it has not read yet are dropped. With close true its session is then closed. It stops a delegate, never the Bot: to stop the Bot's own running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} shows. Answers 200 once the work is stopped, or 202 when the session is still stopping it after a few seconds (it finishes without you; GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/delegates shows the outcome in last_command). The Bot learns of it from the delegate's report. With an Idempotency-Key, sending the same stop again returns its outcome and stops nothing twice; the same key with a different close is 422. A 503 means the outcome is not confirmed: the stop may be recorded and in flight, and may already have reached the delegate. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key, which never stops anything twice, and check the delegate's last_command on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/delegates. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

title.description: The title the Bot gave it.

state.description: committed: the work is stopped (see stopped). queued: the session is still stopping it; the stop is carried out without you.

post.summary: Make a Bot forget its conversation.
post.description: Moves the log to the archive and clears the Bot session's conversation (posted as /clear when the Bot is free). A reply the Bot was writing when you forget is still written to the new log when its turn ends; its message_ids name the forgotten message it answers. The Bot keeps its settings and its delegates, and receives its guardrails again before the next message. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.summary: Answer the approval or question the Bot itself waits on.
post.description: Decides the gate parked on the Bot's own session: the one GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} shows as pending_gate, with its gate_id, generation and type. An approval (type confirm) takes confirm; a question takes answer. An approval decided here applies to this one call only: it is never remembered for the session, for the files the call touches or for a computer, so confirm takes approved and reason only. 200 means the Bot's session consumed this decision. A gate that already ended answers from the session's record of it: 409 gate_already_resolved with what ended it (details.outcome; details.decision when someone decided it; details.request_id when that decision carried a request_id, so a caller that lost the 200 learns the decision used was its own). A question answered again with the same answer answers 200 with replayed true; another answer is 409 gate_already_answered; 409 gate_cancelled when the question ended without taking the answer. 409 gate_decision_pending while a decision's outcome is not known yet: send the same decision again to learn it. 409 stale_gate when the session holds no record of the gate (its session was replaced), and 409 no_pending_gate when the id is not a gate of the Bot's own session or the Bot's session is not open. Never send a decision again after a 409 gate_already_resolved or gate_already_answered: it was not applied. The gates of the Bot's delegates are decided on their own sessions, and the Bot's own tool calls are never answered here. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

decision_unknown.description: No decision is known: nobody decided, or the record is gone.

gate_id.description: The gate the decision named.

generation.description: That gate's generation.

outcome.description: How the gate ended.

request_id.description: The request_id of the decision consumed, when it carried one.

x-error-codes.title: Gate decision pending
x-error-codes.description: A decision for this gate was sent to the agent and its outcome is not known yet: another caller's decision is in flight, the agent did not answer this one within the wait, or the agent connection was lost (details.reason connection_lost). Nothing is known to be decided; the response carries no decision.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry the same decision naming the gate: once the gate has ended the retry is answered 409 gate_already_resolved with what was decided, and while it is still parked and free the decision is sent.

example.message: a decision for this gate is in flight and its outcome is not known yet; retry naming the gate to learn it

gate_id.description: The gate the decision named.

generation.description: That gate's generation.

reason.description: Present when the agent connection was lost while the decision was in flight.

x-error-codes.title: Gate already answered
x-error-codes.description: The parked gate was already answered by an earlier request (first valid answer wins), or it already resolved with another answer than this one. Only a retry with the same answer gets the original acknowledgement back.
x-error-codes.resolution: With details (gate_id, generation): another answer resolved the gate and yours was not applied; wait for the next gate. Without details: an earlier answer is still being applied; retry the same answer later to get its acknowledgement.

example.message: the parked gate was already answered

x-error-codes.title: Gate cancelled
x-error-codes.description: The gate was resolved without consuming this decision: the turn was cancelled (or the session ended) while the decision was in flight, or approval was granted another way. The decision was NOT applied, and nothing it carried (a directory grant, a session-scope remember) took effect.
x-error-codes.resolution: Do not retry this decision: the gate it answered no longer exists. Re-read GET /sessions/{id}/state and answer the gate parked there, if any.

example.message: the gate was resolved without consuming this decision (cancelled); it was not applied

x-error-codes.title: Stale gate
x-error-codes.description: The supplied gate id/generation does not match the currently parked gate. When a gate of the answered kind is parked, details name it: {gate_id, generation, type}.
x-error-codes.resolution: Answer the gate in details (echo its gate_id and generation), or re-read the pending gate when details are absent.

example.message: the gate id/generation does not match the parked gate

x-error-codes.title: No pending gate
x-error-codes.description: No confirm/question gate is parked for this session, so there is nothing to answer.
x-error-codes.resolution: Dispatch a turn and answer the gate it parks; check the pending gate via GET /sessions/{id}.

example.message: no gate is parked for this session

x-error-codes.title: Bot served by another agent
x-error-codes.description: Another agent process on this machine serves the Bot (details.reason held), or its owner lock cannot be taken on this filesystem (details.reason lock_unavailable). Nothing of the Bot was read or changed. The answer carries Retry-After: 5. details.owner names the serving process (pid, started_at) when known, else null.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after Retry-After seconds, or reach the Bot through the agent that serves it. GET /bots lists such a Bot as a row with owned_elsewhere: true.

example.message: the Bot is served by another gateway on this machine; retry in a moment

owner.description: The process serving the Bot, when known.

reason.description: held: another agent process holds the Bot's lock. lock_unavailable: the lock cannot be taken here.

retry_after_secs.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; the same as Retry-After.
