x-error-codes.title: Login restriction unknown
x-error-codes.description: The agent cannot read yet which realms its login may serve (GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status reports restriction "unknown"), so it refuses realm-scoped requests until it can. Nothing was read or changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the restriction is readable.

example.message: the login's realm restriction could not be read — retry

x-error-codes.title: Decision unconfirmed
x-error-codes.description: The decision was forwarded but the daemon acknowledged neither its consumption nor a refusal within the wait. It may still apply. The gateway's answered mark is rolled back so the gate stays answerable.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry the identical decision with the original gate_id and generation. 200: it applied; with replayed:true it had already applied, and resolved is its original acknowledgement. 409 gate_already_answered with details: the gate took another answer, and yours was not applied; without details: an earlier answer to the gate is still being applied, so retry again later. 409 stale_gate or no_pending_gate: no acknowledgement is retained for that gate (it ended, by an answer, a timeout or a cancel), so whether yours applied is unknown.

example.message: the daemon did not acknowledge the decision within the wait

requestBody.description: The gate, and exactly one of confirm (an approval) or answer (a question).

gate_id.description: The gate: pending_gate.gate_id on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}.

generation.description: pending_gate.generation on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}. Required, at least 1.

request_id.description: Optional, approvals only: your own id for this decision, at most 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'. When this decision is the one the gate used, a later 409 gate_already_resolved for the gate carries it as details.request_id.

approved.description: true to approve this one call, false to refuse it. Required: without it the answer is 400 approved_required.

reason.description: Optional, with approved false only: why the call is refused. The Bot reads it in the refused call's result.

confirm.description: The decision on an approval. Any member other than approved and reason is refused 400.

answer.description: The answer text. Required, not blank.
The answer to a question. Any member other than answer is refused 400.

^(?:computer|computer_id|config_dir|cwd|.description: A scope member (computer, computer_id, config_dir, cwd or realm) is not refused as an unknown field, and its value is ignored: a request's scope comes from its scope headers and parameters, never from the body.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

put.description: Replaces the Bot's guardrails: limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens, not instructions to the Bot. The Bot receives the new text, each line marked [guardrails updated], before its next message (an empty text is announced as "none: every earlier guardrail is removed"). Delegates opened from then on receive it at the top of their first prompt as limits set by the owner of the work; open delegates keep the limits they were given. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: expect_uid
parameters.description: The uid of the Bot you read. When the id now names another Bot (the one you read was deleted and a new one created under the id), the request is refused 412 bot_changed and nothing changes. A Bot that is gone answers 404 not_found, as without it, and a request carrying it never creates chief. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: expect_revision
parameters.description: The revision of the Bot you read. When the Bot's settings or guardrails were written since, the request is refused 412 revision_mismatch and nothing changes. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The Bot after the change.

example.name: Chief
example.role: Keeps the web app's releases moving.

id.description: The Bot's id, unique in its realm and fixed at creation; the {id} of the Bot routes.

uid.description: The Bot's globally unique id, fixed at creation. Use it to tell Bots apart across realms.

realm.description: The realm the Bot lives in, fixed at creation: global, or a realm id.

address.description: How the Bot is named in its own messages and logs: bot:<realm>/<id>.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph; empty when not set. The Bot is told its name and role before its next message.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. Empty when none.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session. Empty until the first message is posted. The Bot runtime posts to it: send your messages with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id this view shows while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. A question on this session whose frame_request kind starts with bot. is one of the Bot's own tool calls: the Bot runtime answers it, so do not answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer.

model.description: The model chosen for the Bot's session; empty means the bot agent's own model. A change takes effect when the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset).

session_model.description: The model the Bot's current session runs, as that session reported it. It differs from model after a change of model until the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Absent while the Bot has no session or its session has not reported a model yet.

guardrails.description: Limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens.

allowed_computers.description: Computers the Bot may open delegates on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents the Bot may open delegates with. Empty means any.

yolo.description: When true, every delegate runs with YOLO mode on: its tool approvals are granted without asking.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: How the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs answer a message whose reply starts delegates. false: the answer waits up to wait_seconds for each delegate the reply started to show its first step (it asks for an approval or an answer, reports, closes, or its first tool call finishes without asking), so an approval asked right away comes in the same answer. true: the answer comes at once, for apps that keep listening on their own; what the delegates ask or report later comes with the answer to the next message (and with the MCP updates tool and the Bot's stream). A reply that starts no delegate never waits, and the Bot's own routes are not affected. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, an answer waits for the delegates its reply started when async is false, a whole number from 1 to 60; 15 until changed. The answer still never waits past its own time limit. Kept but unused while async is true.

mcp_hints.description: Whether the results of the Bot's MCP tools ask, ask_audio, answer and status end with one line saying how many new messages and approvals wait for the caller, and the MCP instructions tell the app to call updates when they do. status reports the counts (pending) either way. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. null when routing is off and names no workers.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed. Empty when not set.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it. Empty when not set.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

stt_model.description: The speech-to-text model of the Bot's spoken messages (a model with the stt capability). Empty: the agent's default.

language.description: The language spoken: a language code such as en, or auto. Speech output always accepts auto. Speech input is checked only when the model lists languages; then it must be one of them (auto only if listed).

speed.description: The speaking speed of tts_model, within the model's range. Omitted: the model's normal speed.

stt_prompt.description: Words the speech-to-text model should expect, such as names. Only for an stt_model that takes a prompt.

speak_wakes.description: Read aloud the Bot's replies to delegate reports, not only its replies to your spoken messages. Default false.

speak_gates.description: Announce approvals and questions waiting on you in a voice conversation. Default true.

tts_chars.description: Characters read aloud per day; 0 turns speech output off.

stt_seconds.description: Seconds of speech transcribed per day; 0 turns spoken messages off.

limits.description: The Bot's own daily speech limits, per UTC day. Each is at most the realm's limit; omitted: the default (200000 characters, 14400 seconds).

speech.description: The Bot's speech settings: the models, voice and language its spoken messages and replies use. null when none are set. An unknown model, one without the needed capability, or one the model catalogue marks unavailable is refused 422 model_unavailable naming the field; a missing key or relay is not checked here (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether the speech settings are ready). A voice, language, speed, prompt or limit the models cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

session_id.description: The delegate session.

state.description: pending: its session has not confirmed the change yet; it is sent again until it does. refused: its approval policy does not allow YOLO mode, so it keeps asking for approvals; it is not sent again until yolo changes.

reason.description: Why the last attempt did not apply, when one failed.

yolo_unapplied.description: Open delegates whose YOLO mode does not match yolo yet. Empty when every open delegate runs as yolo says.

kind.description: api: created through this API. system: created by the agent itself (the default Bot, or a Bot made before creators were recorded).

id.description: Who within the kind, when known.

created_by.description: Who created the Bot. A record only: it grants nothing.

revision.description: The revision of the Bot's settings: it goes up by one on every PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} and PUT /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/guardrails, and never on the Bot's own work. Send it back as expect_revision on those two routes so a change made since you read the Bot is not overwritten; send uid as expect_uid on them and on delete, reset, forget and purge so a Bot created again under the same id is not the one changed.

used.description: Dispatches and delegate messages the Bot made on its own since your last message.

max.description: How many it may make on its own between two of your messages.

per_delegate_max.description: How many of them may go to one delegate.

waiting_for_you.description: true once the Bot reached a limit: it does nothing more on its own until you post a message.

autonomy.description: The Bot's follow-ups without you. Work that reacts to your message is not counted; each message you post starts the count again.

used.description: Realtime user items the Bot has seen; null when they could not be read.

max.description: How many it may see; realtime_max_items, 1048576 until changed.

realtime_items.description: The Realtime user items the Bot has recorded. An item id is recorded once and never forgotten, so a client replaying its history never sends an old item to the Bot again. At max a new item is refused and its connection closed until the owner raises realtime_max_items.

open_delegates.description: Delegate sessions the Bot has open.

queued.description: Messages and delegate events waiting to be posted to the Bot.

turn_running.description: true while the Bot works on a turn: the Bot accepted a post (a message or delegate events) and the turn has not ended. false when the Bot is idle, including while a post waits or was refused.

turn_id.description: The Bot's running turn on its session, present only while turn_running is true. To stop that turn and no later one, send it to POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session.

gate_id.description: The gate's answerable id. Correlate on this string: [gate] log rows name it and the answer routes take it. The number called gate_id inside an answer's `resolved` object and in the session's gate_resolved events is a different id.

type.description: confirm: an approval. question: a question to answer.

summary.description: What it asks, in one line.

generation.description: The gate's generation; echo it with gate_id when answering.

pending_gate.description: A gate parked on the Bot's own session, waiting for you: a rule asked to check in before one of the Bot's dispatches. Answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer for a question) on the Bot's session, echoing gate_id. The Bot never answers it itself. A message sent to the Bot while it waits declines it, telling the Bot a new message was sent, and is posted when the Bot's turn ends; delegate events stay queued until that turn ends. null when none.

kind.description: The platform.

state.description: The connection, as GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels/{cid} reports it.

state_reason.description: Why the channel is in its state, when known (the same values as the channel's own state_reason). Absent when none.

paired_count.description: How many people are paired with it.

requested_chats.description: How many of its chats ask to be approved (state requested).

code.description: What the note is about.

field.description: The setting it is about.

reason.description: Why, when the code has reasons.

notes.description: The notes of the account's last credential check, as the channel's effective.notes carries them (for example telegram_privacy_on); [] when none.

channels.description: The Bot's chat channels, in short; [] when none. GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels has the rest. Credentials are never shown.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

x-error-codes.title: Bad request
x-error-codes.description: The request was malformed or carried invalid parameters.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the request body or query parameters.

x-error-codes.title: Realm scope unsupported
x-error-codes.description: A per-request scope header this route does not take: a realm or computer header on a route without that dimension, or, on an agent pinned to one realm, a different realm.
x-error-codes.resolution: Omit the header. A route without a realm dimension refuses every realm header, the pinned realm included; on a route that takes a realm, an agent pinned to one realm accepts only that realm.

example.message: realm scope not supported on this route

x-error-codes.title: Invalid realm selector
x-error-codes.description: The realm selector is malformed (not ""/"global"/a 24-hex id).
x-error-codes.resolution: Pass a valid realm selector.

x-error-codes.title: Unknown body field
x-error-codes.description: The body carries a top-level member this operation does not declare, and nothing was done. details.unknown_fields lists, sorted, the unknown members whose names may be repeated, and details.field names the first of them. A name is repeated only when it is 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter; when no unknown name is, field is empty and the list is empty. Scope members are not checked here: see the request schema.
x-error-codes.resolution: Remove the member, or send the field under a name the request schema declares.

example.message: unknown field "extra"; this operation takes guardrails

field.description: The first unknown member, "" when no unknown name may be repeated.

unknown_fields.description: The unknown members whose names may be repeated, sorted.

x-error-codes.title: Renamed field
x-error-codes.description: The request uses a retired field name and is refused, never run with the old name ignored. details.renamed lists each {from, to} pair.
x-error-codes.resolution: Send the new name from details.renamed. Update the Hoody CLI and SDK if they still send the old one.

example.message: `container` was renamed to `computer`. Update the Hoody CLI and SDK, then send the new name.

x-error-codes.description: Refused by the Source IP Guard: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only.
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the agent through its URL, for example with `hoody agent …`.

get.description: Returns the Bot's log in order: the messages posted to it, its replies, and the delegate events it was told about. Pages by seq: pass next_since back as since while has_more is true. To open at the newest rows, pass tail=true, then read older pages with before. POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/forget moves the rows to the archive. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return only rows whose seq is greater than this: the next_since of the previous page. Default 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many rows: 100 when omitted or 0, at most 500 (a larger value reads 500). Negative or non-integer = 400. These routes page by since, not by page number: ?page is 400.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Read back from the end: the newest rows whose seq is less than this, oldest first. Pass the answer's before back to read the page older than it. Not with since or tail.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: true: the newest rows of the log, oldest first, as before would give them for the next seq the log writes. The log only (on the archive, 400). Not with since or before.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: A page of rows.

items.text: [report] 9a1be4c07d2f4c11 "Run the tests" (self, default) completed: The tests pass.

seq.description: The row's position in the Bot's log; increases by one per row and survives forget.

role.description: user: a posted message. bot: the Bot's reply to one turn, written when the turn ends; a turn with no reply text writes none. event: a delegate event the Bot is told about ([report], [gate], [gone] or [stop] line), or a [gate] line naming the Bot's own session, which waits for you (pending_gate on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}). system: a note from the runtime.

text.description: The row's text.

session_id.description: The session the row is about: the Bot's own for a reply, the delegate's for an event.

turn_id.description: On a reply: the Bot turn it ends.

message_id.description: On a user row: the id the message was accepted under.

message_ids.description: On a reply, and on a [limit], [provider] or [error] system row about a turn: the message_ids of the messages the turn answered, in the order they were accepted. A turn no message started (a delegate event) has none.

kind.description: user: you. bot: the Bot (id is its uid). delegate: one of its delegates (id is the session). system: the runtime.

id.description: Who within the kind, when there is more than one.

from.description: Who wrote the row. Absent on rows written before it was recorded.

trigger.description: Why the turn the row belongs to ran: human (your message), wake (a delegate's event) or clear (forget). Absent when not known.

via.description: The door the message came through, never set by the client: tui (the terminal app), openai, anthropic or mcp (the compat doors), voice or twilio, or telegram, slack or discord (a message from a chat channel of the Bot). Absent for POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages.

sender.description: On a user row that came through another door than POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages: that door.

schema_version.description: The row's format version. Absent on rows written before versions were recorded.

kind.description: On a runtime row (an event or system row, and a [stop] row written in your name): what it is, from its leading tag ([report] is report, [not sent] is not_sent); note for an event or system row without a tag. Absent on posted messages and replies, and on rows written before it was recorded: read the leading tag of those.

fail_kind.description: On the [provider] or [error] row of a failed Bot turn: the cause. content_filter and refusal are the provider stopping the reply ([provider]); no_credentials, auth and unconfigured mean the Bot could not use its model provider; quota_wait and rate_limit mean the provider asked to wait; model means the provider does not accept the Bot's model; spend_cap means the Bot's session reached a spend cap or its spend settings file is not valid; other is a cause without a name of its own. Absent on rows written before it was recorded.

delegate_title.description: On a row about one of the Bot's delegates: the title the Bot gave it, as it was when the row was written. Absent when it had none, and on rows written before it was recorded.

origin.description: The door the audio came through: rest (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages/audio), mcp, ws (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice), realtime or twilio.

duration_ms.description: The audio's length in milliseconds; 0 when the door does not report it.

lang.description: The language the speech was transcribed as, when known.

conn.description: On a voice-connection message: the connection that sent it, as that connection's session frame names it.

utt.description: On a voice-connection message: the connection's utterance it was assembled from; with conn it names the spoken send.

voice.description: On a user row of a spoken message: how it came. Absent on typed messages (a voice connection's typed text included) and on rows written before it was recorded.

items.description: The page of log rows after since, oldest first.

next_since.description: The seq of the last row returned (since when none): pass it as since to read on.

has_more.description: true when rows after next_since were already written: read on with since=next_since. With before or tail: true when older rows exist; read them with before.

before.description: With before or tail: the seq of the oldest row returned (the before asked for when none). Pass it as before to read the older page. next_since is then the seq right before the one asked for: follow on from there with since or GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream.

post.summary: Post a message to a Bot.
post.description: Queues a message for the Bot and answers 202. When the Bot is free the message is posted within a few seconds and turn_id names the Bot turn it started; while the Bot is busy the answer comes at once with state queued, and the message is posted when the Bot's current turn ends. Each message reaches the Bot with its own id and the time it was accepted. When the Bot's turn ends, every message accepted before the Bot's next post is put together goes out in that post, in order, so a correction sent while the Bot was busy is read with the message it corrects; a message accepted after that waits for the turn after. A delegate reads at its own cutoff: everything the Bot passes on to it before its next step is read together at that step. A correction the Bot passes on after the delegate already took the first message reaches it at its following step, in order; nothing already passed on is taken back. A message sent while a gate on the Bot's own session waits for you (pending_gate on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) declines that gate, telling the Bot you sent a new message, and is posted when the Bot's turn ends. The Bot's reply arrives on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream and in GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/log. Only a turn started from a posted message may approve or answer a delegate's gate; a turn started from a delegate event cannot. The Bot sees which door a message came through (the terminal app, a compat door, voice); this route adds none, and a via or from in the body is refused 400. With an Idempotency-Key, a retry with the same key and text returns the same message_id and the message's current state, and queues nothing again (state dropped when the Bot dropped the message before posting it: send it again under a new key); the same key with a different text, or one already used for another message through another door, is refused 422: a Bot has one set of client keys, shared by this route, the terminal app, the spoken-message route, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio); a voice call takes no client key. A key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A key is remembered while its message is queued and for at least 24 hours after the message was accepted. At most 4096 keys are remembered at once: a new keyed message beyond that is refused 429 and nothing is queued (send it later, or without a key). Follow the message by message_id: its `user` row in the log carries it (written when the message is accepted, so it can come before the reply to an earlier message), and the `bot` row with the reply lists it in message_ids once its turn ends (a turn that fails or stops at its step limit also lists it on its [error], [provider] or [limit] system row, which may be the only row about it). A 503 means the message was not queued: send it again. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

A retry with the same key and text returns the same message_id and the message's current state, and queues nothing again; the same key with a different text, or one used through another door of the Bot, is 422; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is 400. A key is remembered while its message is queued and for at least 24 hours after it was accepted.

post.summary: Post a spoken message to a Bot.
post.description: Transcribes one recording (wav or mp3, at most 16 MiB and 600 seconds) and queues the transcript as a message to the Bot, like POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. Audio with no speech in it is answered 200 {no_speech: true} and nothing is queued or billed. With an Idempotency-Key, a retry with the same key and audio returns the same message_id without transcribing again (and without transcript); the same key with other audio, or one used through another door of the Bot (they share one set of client keys), is 422, and a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is 400. At most 4 recordings per Bot are transcribed at once (503 speech_busy past it); a request that repeats the Idempotency-Key of one still running waits for it (429 speech_busy when too many wait). 409 bot_deleted or bot_reset: the Bot was deleted or reset before the recording was admitted. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Opaque retry key (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace). A retry with the same key and audio returns the same message_id and queues nothing again; the same key with other audio, or one used through another door of the Bot, is 422; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is 400.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. get.summary: Talk to a Bot with an OpenAI Realtime client (WebSocket).
get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket that speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol (GA event names), so a Realtime client such as LiveKit Agents or Pipecat talks to the Bot. The client sends session.update, input_audio_buffer.append, .commit and .clear, conversation.item.create, .delete, .retrieve and .truncate, response.create and response.cancel; the agent answers with the matching server events. Input audio is audio/pcm (24 kHz, 16-bit little-endian, the default) or audio/pcmu or audio/pcma (8 kHz); output audio follows the session's output format. With server_vad the agent hears when the user starts and stops speaking and answers on its own; without turn detection the client commits and asks with response.create. semantic_vad runs the same detection; with no silence_duration_ms it ends a turn after 1200 ms of silence for eagerness low, 800 ms for medium or auto, and 500 ms for high. A conversation.item.create is never undone: a user item reaches the Bot once, by its id. The Bot records every user item id it receives and never forgets one, so a client replaying its history on reconnect does not send an old item again; at the Bot's limit (realtime_items on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) a new item is refused and the connection closed. An event that would change an item already sent (deleting, truncating or editing a user item that waits for a response) closes the connection with 1008; so do a binary or non-JSON frame, a frame over 1 MiB, more than 50 control events a second and input audio faster than 1.5 times real time. One connection controls a Bot's voice at a time, over this door, the voice WebSocket or a phone call: another is refused 409 voice_busy unless it asks takeover=true, which closes the one before. A request that is not a WebSocket upgrade is refused 400 bad_request and takes nothing over. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.summary: Give a Bot a new session.
post.description: Moves the log to the archive and starts a new session for the Bot (with its current model). Its delegates stay its own; messages not yet posted are posted to the new session, and a message the old session already took is not sent again (the log says so). The old session is not closed. A 503 means the reset could not be confirmed: the log or session may already have changed, and retrying performs another reset. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bot id.

parameters.name: expect_uid
parameters.description: The uid of the Bot you read. When the id now names another Bot (the one you read was deleted and a new one created under the id), the request is refused 412 bot_changed and nothing changes. A Bot that is gone answers 404 not_found, as without it, and a request carrying it never creates chief. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.description: Server-Sent Events of the Bot's log: first a `state` frame (the Bot as GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} returns it), then the rows after since, then each new row as it is written, and a new `state` frame whenever the Bot changes. Each `row` frame's id is the row's seq: to resume, reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header (an EventSource sends it by itself) or ?since=<last id>. A resume cursor whose rows were moved to the archive in the meantime (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/forget or /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset), or one ahead of the log (the Bot was deleted and created again), is answered with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) before the rows the log still holds. A forget or reset while the stream is open sends an `archived` frame: the rows shown so far are now in the archive. A client that reads too slowly is caught up from the stored log, not dropped. This stream carries finished rows only: the Bot's reply is one `bot` row written when its turn ends, and a turn that ends without reply text writes no row. For a chat view that shows the reply as it is written, the Bot's thinking, its tool calls and when a turn starts and ends, also follow the Bot's own session: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream, with id the session_id from the `state` frame (it changes after POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Do not answer the questions on that session whose frame_request kind starts with bot.: the Bot runtime answers them. An `end` frame is sent when the Bot is deleted or the server ends the stream. Heartbeat comments every 15 s. The stream counts toward the per-IP stream cap (--http-max-streams-per-ip). A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: SSE resume cursor: the id (a non-negative integer seq) of the last frame received. It overrides ?since, and an SSE client sends it on reconnect. Another value is 400 bad_request.

info.title: hoody-agent GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream stream
info.description: Server-Sent Events frames sent to the client by GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream.

oneOf.name: state
oneOf.title: state
oneOf.description: The Bot, as GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} returns it. Sent first and again when it changes; it has no id.

id.description: The Bot's id, unique in its realm and fixed at creation; the {id} of the Bot routes.

uid.description: The Bot's globally unique id, fixed at creation. Use it to tell Bots apart across realms.

realm.description: The realm the Bot lives in, fixed at creation: global, or a realm id.

address.description: How the Bot is named in its own messages and logs: bot:<realm>/<id>.

role.description: What the Bot is for, in one paragraph; empty when not set. The Bot is told its name and role before its next message.

instructions.description: Optional instructions on how the Bot should work, such as tone or format; they never override its rules or guardrails and are not passed to delegates. Empty when none.

session_id.description: The Bot's own session. Empty until the first message is posted. The Bot runtime posts to it: send your messages with POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages. To stop the Bot's running turn, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel with the turn_id this view shows while turn_running is true: it stops that turn and no later one. A question on this session whose frame_request kind starts with bot. is one of the Bot's own tool calls: the Bot runtime answers it, so do not answer it with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer.

model.description: The model chosen for the Bot's session; empty means the bot agent's own model. A change takes effect when the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset).

session_model.description: The model the Bot's current session runs, as that session reported it. It differs from model after a change of model until the Bot starts its next session (POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset). Absent while the Bot has no session or its session has not reported a model yet.

guardrails.description: Limits on the work that apply to the Bot and to every delegate it opens.

allowed_computers.description: Computers the Bot may open delegates on. Empty means any.

allowed_agents.description: Agents the Bot may open delegates with. Empty means any.

yolo.description: When true, every delegate runs with YOLO mode on: its tool approvals are granted without asking.

guardrail_check.description: How the Bot's dispatches and delegate messages are checked against its guardrails before they go out. strict: work that may break a guardrail is refused, and so is work whose check cannot be completed (the Bot tells you, and tries again later only when that can help). The check needs the guardrail checker (Jev). A key-backed jev.model needs that provider's API key: without one, strict refuses every dispatch and delegate message of a Bot that has guardrails, and the Bot says which key is missing. hoody-ai/hoody-decide needs no key (it is set explicitly in jev.model, it is not the default). With hoody-ai/hoody-decide, while a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up, strict refuses until the reset time the Bot names. lenient: work that may break a guardrail is refused; when the check cannot be completed, the work goes ahead unchecked. off: no check. A Bot with no guardrails is never checked.

async.description: How the Bot's OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP URLs answer a message whose reply starts delegates. false: the answer waits up to wait_seconds for each delegate the reply started to show its first step (it asks for an approval or an answer, reports, closes, or its first tool call finishes without asking), so an approval asked right away comes in the same answer. true: the answer comes at once, for apps that keep listening on their own; what the delegates ask or report later comes with the answer to the next message (and with the MCP updates tool and the Bot's stream). A reply that starts no delegate never waits, and the Bot's own routes are not affected. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, an answer waits for the delegates its reply started when async is false, a whole number from 1 to 60; 15 until changed. The answer still never waits past its own time limit. Kept but unused while async is true.

mcp_hints.description: Whether the results of the Bot's MCP tools ask, ask_audio, answer and status end with one line saying how many new messages and approvals wait for the caller, and the MCP instructions tell the app to call updates when they do. status reports the counts (pending) either way. Default true.

mode.description: off: delegates start as usual. suggest: the pick is shown, nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

light.description: The worker for tasks without a heavy trait. Required unless mode is off.

model.description: The model the delegate's session runs. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable; a fusion composite is refused.

thinking.description: Empty: no thinking setting is sent, so the delegate runs with what its agent sets (the model's own default when the agent sets nothing). off or on: thinking off or on. low, medium, high, xhigh or max: on at that level. A setting the model cannot take is refused 400 bad_request.

heavy.description: The worker for tasks with a heavy trait, and for every task whose check cannot be made in auto mode. Required unless mode is off.

routing.description: Which model and thinking setting each new delegate starts with. light and heavy name two workers (a model and a thinking setting). mode off (the default): delegates start as they always do. suggest: the Bot's routing checker reads each new task and the pick is shown, but nothing changes. auto: each new delegate starts on the picked worker; tasks such as finding an unknown cause, concurrency, security, distributed systems, large rewrites, production migrations, bug-hunting reviews, careful math or new designs go to heavy, the rest to light, and heavy is used when the check cannot be made. A task longer than 6000 characters goes to heavy without a check. When routing is on, the task, including the text of the user's messages it attaches, is sent to the routing checker, a model reached through AI provider, whatever provider the guardrail check uses. Send null to remove routing. null when routing is off and names no workers.

worker_backend.description: What a delegate runs on when the dispatch names no backend: llm (Hoody, the default) or acp (Claude Code). null: llm.

worker_delegated_agent.description: The delegated agent of an acp worker: claude. Required while acp is allowed. Empty when not set.

allowed_worker_backends.description: The backends a dispatch may name. null or never set: worker_backend alone, so setting worker_backend to acp alone allows only acp; send both to allow both.

worker_delegated_model.description: The Claude model an acp delegate starts on, an alias such as sonnet or a Claude model id. Empty or null: the configured Claude Code model when the delegate starts, else Claude Code's own default.

worker_delegated_effort.description: The Claude Code effort an acp delegate starts with: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty or null: Claude Code's own. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_model.description: The model a Hoody (llm) delegate starts on when no routing tier applies; it wins over the agent's own model pin. Empty or null: the agent's model, as before. A model no session could start with is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.field worker_model; a fusion composite is refused 400. Fixed for a delegate when it is opened. Empty when not set.

worker_thinking.description: The thinking of worker_model: off, on, or an effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Empty or null: the model's default. Needs worker_model, and a value the model cannot take is refused 400 naming the field; clearing worker_model clears it. Empty when not set.

tts_model.description: The text-to-speech model of the Bot's spoken replies (a model with the tts capability; list them with GET /api/v1/agent/audio/models).

get.summary: Connect a Twilio Media Stream to a Bot (WebSocket).
get.description: The WebSocket URL for a TwiML <Connect><Stream>: one phone call becomes the Bot's voice controller. Twilio's stream events are taken as documented (connected, start, media, mark, stop, dtmf); audio is μ-law at 8 kHz, mono. What the caller says is cut into utterances by voice activity detection; each one is transcribed in order and posted to the Bot as the user's message. The Bot's reply comes back as 20 ms media frames, one mark per spoken segment. When the caller speaks over the reply, its playback stops (a clear is sent). A stop event, or the call ending, drops the utterance still being spoken: it is never transcribed or posted; utterances already complete are still posted. DTMF digits are ignored. Gates are never announced or answered by voice. The call takes over from another open voice controller only when the stream's start event carries the custom parameter takeover=true (or the URL has ?takeover=true); otherwise a second controller is refused and the stream closes with code 1008. Access to this URL is controlled by the agent's proxy permission rules; configure one before pointing a Twilio number at it. Live Twilio accounts are not supported in this release: the door is tested against a Twilio Media Streams simulator. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.summary: Talk to a Bot by voice (WebSocket).
get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket with subprotocol hoody.voice.v1 that carries the user's speech to the Bot and the Bot's spoken replies back. With require=stt, require=tts or require=stt,tts the agent first checks those speech settings as GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check does: when one is not ready it answers 400 bad_request if every failure is a voice or language the speech model does not offer, otherwise 503 speech_unavailable, with the check's result in details, and takes nothing over. Without require nothing is checked before the upgrade. Binary frames from the client are input audio: one byte 0x00, a big-endian u32 sequence number, then 20 to 200 ms of audio in in_format at in_rate. A pcm16 frame of an odd byte length is not decoded: it counts as lost, and an utterance it falls in ends with transcript.final rejected frame_loss. Audio sent faster than 1.5 times real time over 2 seconds is also lost. Binary frames from the agent are output audio: one byte 0x01, a big-endian u32 out, a big-endian u32 sample offset, then 16-bit little-endian PCM at out_rate. Text frames are JSON objects with a type. The client sends input.commit, ptt.down, ptt.up, output.cancel, playback.mark, own_gate.decide, own_gate.answer, text and ping; the agent sends session, vad.start, vad.end, transcript.partial, transcript.final, reply.provisional, reply.invalidate, reply.final, reply.diverged, output.start, output.end, output.stop, cancel.result, gate.announced, own_gate.pending, own_gate.resolved, busy, error, takeover and pong. mode is fixed for the connection: vad (the default) or ptt. In ptt mode only audio between ptt.down and ptt.up counts; other audio is dropped. One utterance is at most 60 seconds, or the speech-to-text model's limit when that is lower. A spoken message counts once the Bot's log shows it. Only replies to this connection's own messages are spoken (and replies the Bot gives on its own, with speak_wakes); every reply's text still arrives in reply.final. reply.final carries own: true when the turn answers a message sent on this connection, false when it does not, and no own when the connection cannot tell (then match turn_id in GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/log). own is about this connection only: a message sent on an earlier connection is answered with own false. With speak=false no speech is made: replies arrive as text only, every reply.final has spoken false, and nothing is billed for speech synthesis (speech-to-text is still billed); the session frame then shows speak false. A speech failure is described by an error object {code, reason, message, diag_id, retryable, retry_after_secs}: on transcript.final when it failed or was rejected stt_suspect, on reply.final when reason is tts_failed or tts_incomplete, and on an error frame with code service_unavailable when the speech service failed on an announcement (tts_failed or tts_incomplete, once per code and reason per connection). Its message says what happened and what to do next; diag_id names the failure in the agent's log. Voice never answers a delegate's approval or question: answer it on screen or by typing. The Bot's own approvals and questions are answered with own_gate.decide and own_gate.answer; their outcome (applied, resolved, stale, unavailable, not_offered, no_pending_gate, stale_gate, gate_cancelled or decision_unconfirmed) arrives in an own_gate.resolved frame, never as an HTTP status. With refuse=frame, a refusal the agent makes is an accepted upgrade that sends one refused frame and closes with 4000 plus the HTTP status. One connection controls a Bot's voice at a time: a second one is refused 409 voice_busy unless it asks takeover=true, which closes the first. The connection closes with 1000 when the client closes it, after 10 minutes without a frame from the client (the agent's own output does not count; send ping to stay connected), when another connection takes over, or when the Bot is deleted or suspended; 1001 when the Bot is stopped, as when the agent shuts down; 1002 when the client did not offer hoody.voice.v1; 1008 for a malformed frame, more than 50 control frames a second, an input frame outside 20 to 200 ms, or a playback mark past the audio sent; 1009 for a frame over 64 KiB; 1011 when a write fails, the agent runs out of voice memory, or on an internal error; a client that does not read gets no close frame, the connection just ends. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: Output sample rate: 8000, 16000, 24000 (default) or 48000.

parameters.name: in_format
parameters.description: Input encoding: pcm16 (16-bit little-endian, default), pcmu or pcma.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: vad (default): the agent detects when the user starts and stops speaking. ptt (push to talk): the client sends ptt.down and ptt.up.

parameters.name: voice
parameters.description: The voice to speak in; omitted, the Bot's own.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: The language the user speaks; omitted, the Bot's own.

parameters.name: speak_wakes
parameters.description: true: also speak replies the Bot gives on its own; omitted, the Bot's setting.

parameters.name: takeover
parameters.description: true: take over from the connection that controls the Bot's voice now.

parameters.name: speak
parameters.description: false: replies arrive as text only (reply.final); no speech is made and nothing is billed for speech synthesis. Speech-to-text still runs. Default true.

parameters.name: refuse
parameters.description: frame: when the agent refuses the connection, accept the upgrade, send one refused frame with the code, message, details and retry_after_secs of the refusal, then close with 4000 plus its HTTP status (4400, 4404, 4409, 4500 or 4503), so a client that cannot read an HTTP refusal of a WebSocket, such as a browser, learns why. Omitted: refusals are HTTP answers.

parameters.name: play_lead
parameters.description: true: the agent keeps at most 8 seconds of reply audio ahead of what playback.mark says was played, and a reply whose audio waits 5 seconds with no mark moving on stops speaking (output.stop and reply.final reason no_marks, spoken unknown, or partial when whole segments were heard; the turn goes on). Send playback.mark at least every 500 ms while playing. Omitted or false: reply audio is sent as fast as the connection takes it.

parameters.name: require
parameters.description: stt, tts or stt,tts: check those speech settings before the upgrade and refuse it when they are not ready (400 bad_request for a voice or language the model does not offer, else 503 speech_unavailable). tts needs speak=true. Omitted: no check.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

oneOf.name: input.audio
oneOf.title: input.audio
oneOf.description: Binary frame: byte 0x00, a big-endian unsigned 32-bit sequence number (one more than the last), then 20 to 200 ms of audio in in_format at in_rate. A frame outside 20 to 200 ms closes the connection with 1008. A pcm16 frame of an odd byte length is not decoded: it counts as lost, so an utterance it falls in ends with transcript.final rejected frame_loss; the connection stays open.

payload.description: Binary frame: byte 0x00, a big-endian unsigned 32-bit sequence number (one more than the last), then 20 to 200 ms of audio in in_format at in_rate. A frame outside 20 to 200 ms closes the connection with 1008. A pcm16 frame of an odd byte length is not decoded: it counts as lost, so an utterance it falls in ends with transcript.final rejected frame_loss; the connection stays open.

oneOf.name: output.cancel

oneOf.description: Stop speech and cancel turns. With reply_id: that reply's output and its turn. Without: everything playing, and every turn this connection's messages started. With keep_turn true only speech stops: no turn is cancelled, later reply text is not spoken, and reply.final comes when the turn really ends, with spoken judged then against its whole text (true only when playback.mark confirmed all of it). Answered with cancel.result.

Answered with cancel.result.

spoken.description: true: all spoken; false: not spoken; "partial": only part was spoken (reason says why); "unknown": audio went out that no playback.mark confirmed (the client stopped reporting playback, or speech was stopped before its marks came).

reason.description: Why speech stopped or was partial: barge_in (the user spoke), cancelled (output.cancel), busy (the agent had no room), revised (an earlier reply's text was withdrawn), too_long (a segment over the speech limit), tts_cut or tts_incomplete or tts_failed (the speech service), speech_limit (the daily speech budget is spent, or speech output is off: speech.limits.tts_chars 0), diverged (the final text differs from what was spoken), no_marks (with play_lead: reply audio waited 5 seconds for a playback.mark that did not come; spoken is then unknown, or partial when whole segments were heard; the turn was not cancelled).

truncated.description: true when text was cut: to fit the frame, or because the agent had no room to keep all of it (for a spoken reply, reason is usually busy). The whole text is in the Bot's log.

own.description: true when the turn answers a message sent on this connection, false when it does not; absent when the connection cannot tell. It is about this connection only: a message sent on an earlier connection is answered with own false.

failure.description: Present when the turn failed after earlier reply text: the text is what the Bot said before it, and the reply was cut off. content_filter or refusal: the model provider stopped the answer; max_steps: the turn stopped at its step limit. Absent otherwise.

code.description: The most specific cause: a speech code (provider_auth, provider_timeout, speech_unavailable, speech_not_configured, model_unavailable, stt_suspect, …) or the outcome's own code.

oneOf.title: output.start
oneOf.description: An output (a piece of speech) starts. Its audio normally follows in output.audio frames. When speech output is off (speech.limits.tts_chars 0), the speech budget is spent, or the speech service fails before any audio of the reply was sent, no audio follows: output.end with samples 0 comes next, then, for a reply, reply.final with spoken false (reason speech_limit or tts_failed). If a later segment fails or the speech budget runs out after earlier segments of the reply played, the reply ends with spoken partial and a reason from the speech service or budget (tts_failed, tts_cut, tts_incomplete or speech_limit; see reply.final). An announcement (kind announcement) never sends reply.final. When the speech service fails (tts_failed, tts_incomplete) it is reported with an error frame (code service_unavailable), once per code and reason per connection; an announcement stopped for speech_limit or silenced by speech off is not reported.

out.description: The output, numbered up per connection.

kind.description: reply: the Bot's reply; announcement: a spoken notice that a delegate waits on a gate.

ref.description: For an announcement: session_id, gate_id and generation of the gate.

oneOf.description: The answer to a text frame that carried a key.

state.description: posted: the message went out in a Bot turn; queued: it waits for the Bot's current turn to end; dropped: the key's message was dropped before it was posted and never will be (reason says why; send it again under a new key); refused: it was not queued (code says why; send it again only after fixing that); unknown: whether it was queued is not known yet, and it may still arrive: read GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages/by-key/{key} before sending it again (a 404 there proves nothing; read the log).

message_id.description: With posted, queued or dropped: the message's id. With refused idempotency_key_reused: the message the key took.

reason.description: On dropped: access_revoked (the chat-app sender is no longer allowed to send it) or key_conflict (the Bot could not deliver it).

code.description: With refused: bad_request (an empty text, one over 64 KiB, or a bad key), busy (no room now; send it again), idempotency_key_reused (the key was used for other text, or through another door), idempotency_keys_exhausted (the Bot remembers too many recent keys), service_unavailable (the Bot could not take it now; send it again).

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: A request in a frame failed. After protocol or rate_limited the connection closes with 1008; after any other code it stays open.

code.description: What failed: bad_request (a frame had a bad field: a decision other than approve, deny or allow_session, a reason without deny or over 500 characters, a blank answer, an empty text or one over 64 KiB), busy (no room now: an earlier gate decision is still being applied, or too much is waiting; send it again), rate_limited (more than 50 text frames a second; closes 1008), protocol (a malformed frame; closes 1008), service_unavailable (the speech service failed on an announcement: tts_failed or tts_incomplete, once per code and reason per connection; or a typed message was not queued; send it again, unless the message says its delivery is not confirmed: it may still arrive, so check the Bot's log or reply first), stale_utterance (input.commit named an utterance that already ended), no_utterance (nothing to end: input.commit with no utterance open, or ptt.up without ptt.down), wrong_mode (input.commit in ptt mode, or ptt.down or ptt.up in vad mode), server_error (a frame could not be encoded).
The most specific cause: a speech code (provider_auth, provider_timeout, speech_unavailable, speech_not_configured, model_unavailable, stt_suspect, …) or the outcome's own code.

get.summary: Check that a Bot can talk by voice.
get.description: Checks whether a Bot can talk by voice before GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice is opened, the same way speech is resolved when it is used: which speech-to-text model and, unless speak=false, which text-to-speech model the Bot would use (its own setting, else the agent's audio settings), that the model can do that, that the voice and language are ones it offers, and that the agent holds a key for its provider or can use the Hoody AI voice relay. It answers 200 either way. ready says whether the configuration is ready; it is not a promise that a call to the speech provider will succeed. stt and tts (null with speak=false) each carry ok and the model; when ok is false, also code, reason, message (what happened and what to do next), retryable and, when known, retry_after_secs and diag_id. max_utterance_secs is the longest utterance a voice connection takes. When ready is false, diag_id names this check in the agent's log. The check bills nothing and takes at most 6 seconds. GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice with require makes the same check before its upgrade. A Bot lives in one realm: global (not tied to a realm: its delegates see every computer of the account) or a realm id. X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) names the realm; omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve, or a Bot id the realm does not hold, answers 404 not_found. "all" is accepted only as ?realm=all on GET /api/v1/agent/bots and POST /api/v1/agent/bots/resume; anywhere else it is 400 bad_request. An agent pinned to one realm refuses any other realm, and "all", with 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The cwd, config-dir and computer headers are refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.summary: Open a Bot URL: model list or help page.
get.description: A Bot's own URL, to paste into an app: the realm and the Bot are in the path, so no header and no model name is needed. Paste <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/v1 as the base URL of an OpenAI client (chat completions, responses, models), <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot> as the base URL of an Anthropic client (Messages, models), and <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/mcp into an MCP client (an MCP client given the base URL reaches it too: a POST or DELETE of the base URL is MCP). realm is global or a 24-hex realm id; <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<bot>/… uses the agent's current realm instead (a Bot whose id is global or 24 hex is reached by the long form only). GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} lists a Bot's URLs under urls. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base all reach the same Bot. The model a request names is ignored; the model list holds one model, whose id is the Bot's id and whose name is the Bot's name. A GET of the base URL, the MCP URL or a chat URL answers a short text page saying how to use the URL. An unknown Bot, and a realm this login does not serve, answer the same 404. Chat and model errors use the client format's own error body (OpenAI, or Anthropic for …/messages and for a model request carrying anthropic-version). Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Reached through its Bot URL (the Bot's public host), a Bot serves a GET of the host's root (the Bot's chat page, or its text guide for curl, agents, an empty User-Agent or ?view=text) and of …/SKILL.md without a key; called with one of its Bot URL keys, it serves …/v1, …/v1/models, …/v1/models/<model>, …/v1/key (the calling key's name and holder note), …/v1/chat/completions, …/v1/responses, …/v1/messages, …/mcp and …/events. Any other path is 404 path_not_allowed, and a listed path with another method is 405 method_not_allowed.
