GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} lists a Bot's URLs under urls. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base all reach the same Bot. The model a request names is ignored; the model list holds one model, whose id is the Bot's id and whose name is the Bot's name. A GET of the base URL, the MCP URL or a chat URL answers a short text page saying how to use the URL. An unknown Bot, and a realm this login does not serve, answer the same 404. Chat and model errors use the client format's own error body (OpenAI, or Anthropic for …/messages and for a model request carrying anthropic-version). Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Reached through its Bot URL (the Bot's public host), a Bot serves a GET of the host's root (the Bot's chat page, or its text guide for curl, agents, an empty User-Agent or ?view=text) and of …/SKILL.md without a key; called with one of its Bot URL keys, it serves …/v1, …/v1/models, …/v1/models/<model>, …/v1/key (the calling key's name and holder note), …/v1/chat/completions, …/v1/responses, …/v1/messages, …/mcp and …/events. Paste <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/v1 as the base URL of an OpenAI client (chat completions, responses, models), <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot> as the base URL of an Anthropic client (Messages, models), and <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/mcp into an MCP client (an MCP client given the base URL reaches it too: a POST or DELETE of the base URL is MCP). realm is global or a 24-hex realm id; <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<bot>/… uses the agent's current realm instead (a Bot whose id is global or 24 hex is reached by the long form only). GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} lists a Bot's URLs under urls. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base all reach the same Bot. The model a request names is ignored; the model list holds one model, whose id is the Bot's id and whose name is the Bot's name. A GET of the base URL, the MCP URL or a chat URL answers a short text page saying how to use the URL. An unknown Bot, and a realm this login does not serve, answer the same 404. Chat and model errors use the client format's own error body (OpenAI, or Anthropic for …/messages and for a model request carrying anthropic-version). Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Reached through its Bot URL (the Bot's public host), a Bot serves a GET of the host's root (the Bot's chat page, or its text guide for curl, agents, an empty User-Agent or ?view=text) and of …/SKILL.md without a key; called with one of its Bot URL keys, it serves …/v1, …/v1/models, …/v1/models/<model>, …/v1/key (the calling key's name and holder note), …/v1/chat/completions, …/v1/responses, …/v1/messages, …/mcp and …/events. Any other path is 404 path_not_allowed, and a listed path with another method is 405 method_not_allowed. There every error carries its code in X-Hoody-Error-Code (upper case) with a fixed message: bot_disabled, path_not_allowed, method_not_allowed, rate_limited, concurrency_limit, invalid_request, request_not_found, request_conflict, forbidden, upstream_error or internal_error; only a 429 carries Retry-After. Idempotency keys, the keys derived from a conversation and MCP refs belong to the calling key: the same Idempotency-Key under another key names another message, and a ref is unknown to any other key. An answer to the caller's own message also names that message's rows in the Bot's shared log: a top-level hoody object {message_seq, reply_seq} on a chat completion, a Responses response or an Anthropic message (streamed: on the chunk that carries the answer, on response.completed, on message_delta), and the same two fields in the structured content of the MCP ask, answer and ask_audio tools. message_seq is the seq of the row the message wrote, reply_seq that of the last row of its reply (where a spoken reply's audio belongs); each is left out while unknown or when there is none (an answer still working, a reset). They name rows (the seqs of the updates items and of …/events row frames) and are not resume positions; the same Idempotency-Key or ref answers the same two again. Only the caller's own answer carries them: updates and …/events do not. A GET of …/events (through a Bot URL only; it takes no body) is a Server-Sent Events stream of what the MCP status and updates tools return: a status frame first and whenever the status changes (the status tool's structured content), a row frame for each log row with a public form (the updates item; id: its seq), a cursor frame {seq} when rows without one moved the position, and at the end of the catch-up of a stream opened without Last-Event-ID (id: that seq), a gap or archived frame {next_seq} when the log no longer holds the rows after the position or was archived (id: next_seq - 1, possibly 0: the position moves back), a heartbeat comment every 15 s, and end {reason: reconnect} shortly before the stream's 25 s lifetime ends or when the Bot restarts. After the response started, a failure is an error frame {code, message} and the stream closes. The first bytes set retry: 1000. Resume with the Last-Event-ID header (the resume position, which an EventSource keeps by itself): absent or blank, the stream starts at the 20 newest rows; 0, at the oldest row kept; any other value must be decimal digits, at most 16 of them, up to 2^53-1 (else 400 invalid_request). At most 4 streams are open per key, 32 per Bot and 16 per caller address; another is refused 429 concurrency_limit.

post.summary: Chat with a Bot through its URL (OpenAI, Anthropic or MCP).
post.description: A Bot's own URL, to paste into an app: the realm and the Bot are in the path, so no header and no model name is needed. Paste <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/v1 as the base URL of an OpenAI client (chat completions, responses, models), <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot> as the base URL of an Anthropic client (Messages, models), and <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/mcp into an MCP client (an MCP client given the base URL reaches it too: a POST or DELETE of the base URL is MCP). realm is global or a 24-hex realm id; <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<bot>/… uses the agent's current realm instead (a Bot whose id is global or 24 hex is reached by the long form only). GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} lists a Bot's URLs under urls. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base all reach the same Bot. The model a request names is ignored; the model list holds one model, whose id is the Bot's id and whose name is the Bot's name. A GET of the base URL, the MCP URL or a chat URL answers a short text page saying how to use the URL. An unknown Bot, and a realm this login does not serve, answer the same 404. Chat and model errors use the client format's own error body (OpenAI, or Anthropic for …/messages and for a model request carrying anthropic-version). Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Reached through its Bot URL (the Bot's public host), a Bot serves a GET of the host's root (the Bot's chat page, or its text guide for curl, agents, an empty User-Agent or ?view=text) and of …/SKILL.md without a key; called with one of its Bot URL keys, it serves …/v1, …/v1/models, …/v1/models/<model>, …/v1/key (the calling key's name and holder note), …/v1/chat/completions, …/v1/responses, …/v1/messages, …/mcp and …/events. Any other path is 404 path_not_allowed, and a listed path with another method is 405 method_not_allowed. There every error carries its code in X-Hoody-Error-Code (upper case) with a fixed message: bot_disabled, path_not_allowed, method_not_allowed, rate_limited, concurrency_limit, invalid_request, request_not_found, request_conflict, forbidden, upstream_error or internal_error; only a 429 carries Retry-After. Idempotency keys, the keys derived from a conversation and MCP refs belong to the calling key: the same Idempotency-Key under another key names another message, and a ref is unknown to any other key. An answer to the caller's own message also names that message's rows in the Bot's shared log: a top-level hoody object {message_seq, reply_seq} on a chat completion, a Responses response or an Anthropic message (streamed: on the chunk that carries the answer, on response.completed, on message_delta), and the same two fields in the structured content of the MCP ask, answer and ask_audio tools. message_seq is the seq of the row the message wrote, reply_seq that of the last row of its reply (where a spoken reply's audio belongs); each is left out while unknown or when there is none (an answer still working, a reset). They name rows (the seqs of the updates items and of …/events row frames) and are not resume positions; the same Idempotency-Key or ref answers the same two again. Only the caller's own answer carries them: updates and …/events do not. A GET of …/events (through a Bot URL only; it takes no body) is a Server-Sent Events stream of what the MCP status and updates tools return: a status frame first and whenever the status changes (the status tool's structured content), a row frame for each log row with a public form (the updates item; id: its seq), a cursor frame {seq} when rows without one moved the position, and at the end of the catch-up of a stream opened without Last-Event-ID (id: that seq), a gap or archived frame {next_seq} when the log no longer holds the rows after the position or was archived (id: next_seq - 1, possibly 0: the position moves back), a heartbeat comment every 15 s, and end {reason: reconnect} shortly before the stream's 25 s lifetime ends or when the Bot restarts. After the response started, a failure is an error frame {code, message} and the stream closes. The first bytes set retry: 1000. Resume with the Last-Event-ID header (the resume position, which an EventSource keeps by itself): absent or blank, the stream starts at the 20 newest rows; 0, at the oldest row kept; any other value must be decimal digits, at most 16 of them, up to 2^53-1 (else 400 invalid_request). At most 4 streams are open per key, 32 per Bot and 16 per caller address; another is refused 429 concurrency_limit.

delete.summary: End an MCP session on a Bot URL (answers 405: the server is stateless).
delete.description: A Bot's own URL, to paste into an app: the realm and the Bot are in the path, so no header and no model name is needed. Paste <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/v1 as the base URL of an OpenAI client (chat completions, responses, models), <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot> as the base URL of an Anthropic client (Messages, models), and <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<realm>/<bot>/mcp into an MCP client (an MCP client given the base URL reaches it too: a POST or DELETE of the base URL is MCP). realm is global or a 24-hex realm id; <agent>/api/v1/agent/bots/<bot>/… uses the agent's current realm instead (a Bot whose id is global or 24 hex is reached by the long form only). GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} lists a Bot's URLs under urls. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base all reach the same Bot. The model a request names is ignored; the model list holds one model, whose id is the Bot's id and whose name is the Bot's name. A GET of the base URL, the MCP URL or a chat URL answers a short text page saying how to use the URL. An unknown Bot, and a realm this login does not serve, answer the same 404. Chat and model errors use the client format's own error body (OpenAI, or Anthropic for …/messages and for a model request carrying anthropic-version). Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Reached through its Bot URL (the Bot's public host), a Bot serves a GET of the host's root (the Bot's chat page, or its text guide for curl, agents, an empty User-Agent or ?view=text) and of …/SKILL.md without a key; called with one of its Bot URL keys, it serves …/v1, …/v1/models, …/v1/models/<model>, …/v1/key (the calling key's name and holder note), …/v1/chat/completions, …/v1/responses, …/v1/messages, …/mcp and …/events. Any other path is 404 path_not_allowed, and a listed path with another method is 405 method_not_allowed. There every error carries its code in X-Hoody-Error-Code (upper case) with a fixed message: bot_disabled, path_not_allowed, method_not_allowed, rate_limited, concurrency_limit, invalid_request, request_not_found, request_conflict, forbidden, upstream_error or internal_error; only a 429 carries Retry-After. Idempotency keys, the keys derived from a conversation and MCP refs belong to the calling key: the same Idempotency-Key under another key names another message, and a ref is unknown to any other key. An answer to the caller's own message also names that message's rows in the Bot's shared log: a top-level hoody object {message_seq, reply_seq} on a chat completion, a Responses response or an Anthropic message (streamed: on the chunk that carries the answer, on response.completed, on message_delta), and the same two fields in the structured content of the MCP ask, answer and ask_audio tools. message_seq is the seq of the row the message wrote, reply_seq that of the last row of its reply (where a spoken reply's audio belongs); each is left out while unknown or when there is none (an answer still working, a reset). They name rows (the seqs of the updates items and of …/events row frames) and are not resume positions; the same Idempotency-Key or ref answers the same two again. Only the caller's own answer carries them: updates and …/events do not. A GET of …/events (through a Bot URL only; it takes no body) is a Server-Sent Events stream of what the MCP status and updates tools return: a status frame first and whenever the status changes (the status tool's structured content), a row frame for each log row with a public form (the updates item; id: its seq), a cursor frame {seq} when rows without one moved the position, and at the end of the catch-up of a stream opened without Last-Event-ID (id: that seq), a gap or archived frame {next_seq} when the log no longer holds the rows after the position or was archived (id: next_seq - 1, possibly 0: the position moves back), a heartbeat comment every 15 s, and end {reason: reconnect} shortly before the stream's 25 s lifetime ends or when the Bot restarts. After the response started, a failure is an error frame {code, message} and the stream closes. The first bytes set retry: 1000. Resume with the Last-Event-ID header (the resume position, which an EventSource keeps by itself): absent or blank, the stream starts at the 20 newest rows; 0, at the oldest row kept; any other value must be decimal digits, at most 16 of them, up to 2^53-1 (else 400 invalid_request). At most 4 streams are open per key, 32 per Bot and 16 per caller address; another is refused 429 concurrency_limit.

get.summary: Change tokens for the Work lists.
get.description: Returns {scope, tokens}: one opaque token per topic (sessions, todos, workflow_runs, loops, tasks, gates, agents, rules, memory). Read it, then list; later, re-list only the topics whose token moved, and every topic when `scope` changes. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The X-Hoody-Cwd / X-Hoody-Config-Dir headers scope `sessions` and `todos` as they scope GET /api/v1/agent/sessions and GET /api/v1/agent/todos, and with them `tasks`, `gates` and `rules`, which are read over those visible sessions; `rules` also covers the files GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules reads for the same headers. `memory` reads the store GET /api/v1/agent/memory/status reads for the same realm and X-Hoody-Config-Dir. Every token is computed from what the caller can see, so work in another realm or of another account never moves one. One read is shared for 1 s by the requests with the same realm and scope headers, so an answer can be up to 1 s old: after the active realm or account switches, the new `scope` arrives within that second. Tokens are hints; the lists are authoritative.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The change tokens.

scope.description: Names the realm and account the tokens belong to (it never carries the account). When it changes, re-list every topic.

sessions.description: Moves when a visible session is created, closed, renamed or re-persisted (model, agent, cost), when it attaches or detaches, when a turn starts, parks on a gate or ends, when a gate starts or stops waiting for a person, and when a GET /api/v1/agent/sessions row's state changes because this agent holds or releases the session's turn slot or closes it. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions.

todos.description: Moves on any change to a visible todo. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/todos (and GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id} for an open one).

workflow_runs.description: Moves when a visible run starts, steps, finishes, is cancelled or is evicted. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs (GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs/{run_id} for one).

loops.description: Moves when a visible loop is created, deleted, paused, resumed, fires, finishes or spends. Countdowns (next_in_ms, expires_in_ms) do not move it. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/loops.

tasks.description: Moves when a helper task of a visible live session starts, makes progress or ends. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/tasks for the sessions you show.

gates.description: Moves when a gate of a visible live session parks or resolves: the session's own confirm or question, and on a helper_gates session each helper's. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/gates (or GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state for one session: pending_gate, pending_helper_gates).

agents.description: Moves when the realm's agent list changes: a create, delete, rename, model, tools or turns edit, or a source edit. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/agents.

rules.description: Moves when a rules layer of a visible live session changes (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules), or a settings file GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules reads for the same scope headers, with or without a live session. Re-list: GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules / GET /api/v1/agent/hooks / GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies.

memory.description: Moves when the realm's memory changes: a memory saved, edited or deleted, an observation captured, a project erased, a consolidation pass queued, started or ended (GET /api/v1/agent/memory/status `consolidation`), or memory switched on or off. While the store cannot be reached or memory reads are refused, the token holds until that changes. Re-read: GET /api/v1/agent/memory/status / GET /api/v1/agent/memory/projects / GET /api/v1/agent/memory/items.

tokens.description: One opaque token per topic. Compare a token with the one you last saw; when it differs, re-list that topic. Never parse a token.

unavailable.description: Present only when a topic could not be read: topic → reason. That topic has no token in this answer.

get.description: Server-Sent Events over GET /api/v1/agent/changes. The first frame is `snapshot` {scope, tokens}; after it a `changed` {topic, token} frame for each topic whose token moved, and a new `snapshot` when `scope` changes. Tokens are re-read every 2 s (one read per scope per second is shared by every stream). There are no `id:` lines: after a reconnect, start again from the new snapshot and re-list the topics that differ from what you hold. Heartbeat comments every 25 s; `end` {reason} when the tokens cannot be read. The stream counts toward the per-IP stream cap (--http-max-streams-per-ip, default 16): a Frame tab holds this stream, the focused session's /stream and a prompt:stream while sending. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The X-Hoody-Cwd / X-Hoody-Config-Dir headers scope `sessions` and `todos` as they scope GET /api/v1/agent/sessions and GET /api/v1/agent/todos, and with them `tasks`, `gates` and `rules`, which are read over those visible sessions; `rules` also covers the files GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules reads for the same headers. `memory` reads the store GET /api/v1/agent/memory/status reads for the same realm and X-Hoody-Config-Dir. Every token is computed from what the caller can see, so work in another realm or of another account never moves one. One read is shared for 1 s by the requests with the same realm and scope headers, so an answer can be up to 1 s old: after the active realm or account switches, the new `scope` arrives within that second. Tokens are hints; the lists are authoritative.

post.description: Posts the last user message to the Bot the model names and answers with the Bot's reply, in the Anthropic-compatible shape: JSON, or Server-Sent Events when the body sets stream to true. Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. Each Bot is a model whose id is its address, bot:<realm>/<id> (for example bot:global/chief); a bare Bot id names a Bot of the realm X-Hoody-Realm names, else of the agent's current realm. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Errors use this format's own error body, not the agent's. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base reach the same route; a URL no route serves answers 404 naming the base URL to use, and an MCP request names the Bot URLs, which are the MCP servers.

post.summary: Chat with a Bot (OpenAI chat completions).
post.description: Posts the last user message to the Bot the model names and answers with the Bot's reply, in the OpenAI-compatible shape: JSON, or Server-Sent Events when the body sets stream to true. Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. Each Bot is a model whose id is its address, bot:<realm>/<id> (for example bot:global/chief); a bare Bot id names a Bot of the realm X-Hoody-Realm names, else of the agent's current realm. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Errors use this format's own error body, not the agent's. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base reach the same route; a URL no route serves answers 404 naming the base URL to use, and an MCP request names the Bot URLs, which are the MCP servers.

get.description: Lists every Bot of every realm this login serves (an agent pinned to one realm: that realm's Bots), in the OpenAI-compatible model list shape. Each Bot is a model whose id is its address, bot:<realm>/<id> (for example bot:global/chief); a bare Bot id names a Bot of the realm X-Hoody-Realm names, else of the agent's current realm. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Errors use this format's own error body, not the agent's. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base reach the same route; a URL no route serves answers 404 naming the base URL to use, and an MCP request names the Bot URLs, which are the MCP servers.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.description: Opens a voice conversation with the Bot ?model= names (bot:<realm>/<id>, or a Bot id of the request's realm) as an OpenAI Realtime WebSocket. post.description: Posts the last user message of input (a string, or a list of messages) to the Bot the model names and answers with the Bot's reply in the OpenAI Responses shape: JSON, or Server-Sent Events when the body sets stream to true. Nothing is stored: previous_response_id and store are ignored. instructions counts as the system prompt. Only the last message is read, and it must be a user message with text only (an image, audio or file part is refused 400): it is posted to the Bot as a message from you, and the Bot keeps its own history. System messages (and, on …/chat/completions and …/responses, developer messages) count as the system prompt wherever they sit, so a trailing one is passed over when the last message is found. Text blocks of the last message that consist only of a client's <system-reminder> note count as the system prompt too and are not posted; a last message of such notes only is refused 400. A side request an app makes on the model (a conversation title, a summary, follow-up suggestions, tags or an autocompletion: never one that sends tools; recognised when its system prompt or last message starts with a chat app's default prompt for that task (Open WebUI's task prompts, LibreChat's title prompt), Claude Code's session title (no tools, an output_config asking for a JSON object whose one property is title, and a last user message that is its <session> prompt followed by its fixed closing sentence about the title's language), or by an output budget (max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens) of 64 or less; any other wording, including the user's own request for a summary or a title, is a message to the Bot) is not posted: the Bot's model answers it in one completion, outside the Bot's history, with at most 1024 output tokens, or the request's own budget when that is lower; a Bot whose model cannot limit its output this way answers side requests 502 upstream_error and never runs them uncapped. Otherwise system prompts, client tools, sampling settings and output budgets are ignored; an output budget that is not a positive integer is refused 400, and so is a tool_choice that forces a tool. The answer is the Bot's reply to that message, behind the updates the Bot logged since the previous answer (its replies about delegates' reports, limit notices, and its replies to earlier messages of these URLs whose answer was not delivered; never its replies to messages sent another way): an app learns about finished work with its next message. When the reply started delegates, the Bot's async and wait_seconds settings (PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}) say how the answer waits. With async false, the default, it waits up to wait_seconds more (15 until changed) and ends early once every delegate the reply started has asked for an approval or an answer, reported, closed, or finished its first tool call without asking; when one asked, the answer ends with what the Bot said about it; reply in the chat to answer. With async true the answer comes at once. Either way, what a delegate asks or reports later comes with the next answer. The Bot is one conversation shared by every app that talks to it. A request sent again with the same messages (and the same user field, or Anthropic metadata.user_id) within 2 minutes, while its answer was never delivered in full, gets that answer without posting again; once the answer was delivered, or later, the same messages are a new message to the Bot. After an answer that said the Bot is still working, or asked for an approval, the same messages sent again later wait for that message's reply instead. A message the Bot dropped before posting it is answered with a fixed note that it was not delivered; the same messages sent again within 2 minutes of the first, or under the same Idempotency-Key, get that note again and post nothing, and later the same messages are a new message. An Idempotency-Key header names the message instead: the same key gets the same answer while the Bot still holds its record (about 24 hours); after that it can post again, so check status or updates before resending. A Bot has one set of client keys, shared by its HTTP message routes, the terminal app, the OpenAI and Anthropic doors and the MCP door (ask and ask_audio), so a key one of them already used for another message is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused; a key starting with "compat:" or "chan:" is refused 400. A request not streamed waits up to 100 seconds for the reply; a streamed one sends keepalives and waits up to 10 minutes. When the Bot is still working then, the answer says so; the same request sent again waits for the same reply without posting again; otherwise the reply comes with the next answer. A gate on the Bot's own session ends the wait with the gate's summary. A reset of the Bot ends the wait with a note to send the message again, and the same request sent again is posted to the Bot's new session. The answer is sent whole, as one text part or one delta. Requests to one Bot are answered one at a time: a request still waiting for its turn when its wait ends is refused 429 bot_busy and posts nothing. Each Bot is a model whose id is its address, bot:<realm>/<id> (for example bot:global/chief); a bare Bot id names a Bot of the realm X-Hoody-Realm names, else of the agent's current realm. The Authorization and x-api-key headers are ignored: apps may send any value, and access is decided before the request reaches the agent. Errors use this format's own error body, not the agent's. The path is read forgivingly and never redirected: repeated slashes, a trailing slash, a missing or doubled /v1, and a whole …/chat/completions or …/messages URL pasted as the base reach the same route; a URL no route serves answers 404 naming the base URL to use, and an MCP request names the Bot URLs, which are the MCP servers.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm

Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

post.description: Sends `messages` (and an optional `system` prompt) to `model` once, with no tools, no session and no transcript, and answers the whole reply as JSON. `settings` sets per-call thinking, temperature, max_tokens and response_format; a setting the model or its adapter cannot honour is refused with 400 unsupported_setting before any network call, never dropped. `applied` reports what was actually sent. A reply that stops on max_tokens, refusal or content_filter is still a 200 carrying the text so far (read stop_reason); a tool call or an error stop is 502 upstream_error. `json_valid` (present when response_format is set) is a syntax check of the text, not a schema check. OpenAI-style json_object mode needs the word "json" in the prompt. Usage is recorded in the usage log whenever the model was called, success or not. This route takes no stream slot: each client IP may hold up to the gateway's completion cap (default 32) in flight, above which it answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request-rate limit applies as usual. Fan-out clients should use this route rather than POST /api/v1/agent/completions/stream. Every X-Hoody-Realm / ?realm= (including global), X-Hoody-Cwd, X-Hoody-Computer and X-Hoody-Config-Dir is refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported: a completion has no scope. Per-IP limits key on the direct peer unless the gateway's trusted proxies are configured (deploy configuration); without that, every browser behind the proxy shares one per-IP bucket.

schema.description: The finished completion, composed by the gateway from the daemon's llm.complete result.

status.description: "ok".

model.description: The model spec that answered.

text.description: The reply text.

stop_reason.description: Why the reply ended. max_tokens, refusal and content_filter carry the text so far.

json_valid.description: Present only when response_format was set: whether the trimmed text parses as JSON. A syntax check, not a schema check.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens, excluding cache reads and writes.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

reasoning_tokens.description: Present only when the provider reports it (0 is kept): the reasoning share of output_tokens.

cost_usd.description: The call's cost in US dollars; null when it cannot be known. Token-plan models show the catalogue list price (often 0), not plan quota.

cost_source.description: provider (reported by the provider) or estimated (from the model catalogue); null with a null cost_usd.

thinking.description: provider_default: no thinking control was sent.

effort.description: Present when a reasoning level was sent.

temperature.description: Present when a temperature was sent.

max_tokens.description: The output cap sent; null when the backend takes none.

response_format.description: Present when a response format was sent: json_object or json_schema.

duration_ms.description: Wall time of the model call.

requestBody.description: One tool-free model call. Unknown members are refused at every level (400 bad_request, details.field names the JSON path). For every optional member, null is the same as absent.

model.description: A provider/model spec, e.g. hoody-ai/hoody-free. The same policy as a session's model: the provider prefix must be catalogued, the model name after it need not be (an uncatalogued name is sent to the provider, which may reject it as upstream_error). An unknown provider or an empty model name is 422 model_unavailable (reason unknown_model); a fusion/ composite is 422 model_unavailable (reason fusion).

role.description: Who spoke.

messages.description: 1 to 1000 turns, oldest first; the last must be a user turn.

effort.description: Reasoning level; only with type enabled, and only on models that take one.

post.summary: Run one tool-free model completion, streamed over SSE.
post.description: The same call as POST /api/v1/agent/completions, streamed as Server-Sent Events: `start`, then `delta` (text) and `thinking` frames as they arrive, then exactly one `result` (the POST /api/v1/agent/completions body) or `error`, then `end`. Nothing is written before the model call starts: a failure before `start` (validation, unsupported_setting, model_unavailable, timeout, the stream cap) is an ordinary JSON error with its HTTP status. After `start` a failure is an `error` frame {code, message, details?} carrying the same codes (upstream_error, timeout, internal_error). A `: ping` comment is sent every 25 s while the stream is open. There is no `retry:` hint and the stream must not be replayed automatically: every call is billed. Read it with fetch and an AbortController; aborting cancels the model call. Each open stream holds one of the client IP's stream slots (shared with session streams, default 16); over the cap is 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After. Fan-out clients should use POST /api/v1/agent/completions. Every X-Hoody-Realm / ?realm= (including global), X-Hoody-Cwd, X-Hoody-Computer and X-Hoody-Config-Dir is refused with 400 realm_scope_unsupported: a completion has no scope. Per-IP limits key on the direct peer unless the gateway's trusted proxies are configured (deploy configuration); without that, every browser behind the proxy shares one per-IP bucket.

get.summary: List the gates waiting for a human.
get.description: Lists every gate this gateway can answer that is waiting for a human, across the sessions GET /api/v1/agent/sessions shows (the same realm, owner, X-Hoody-Cwd / X-Hoody-Config-Dir and include_system handling): each live session's own confirm or question and, on a helper_gates session, each helper's (a background task's pending gate is its helper's gate, with task_id). Answer one with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer, sending its gate_id. A gate is listed only while this gateway holds its session live: a session held only by another client (the TUI) is not listed until it is attached here. A Bot's tool call, parked on the Bot's own session as a question with frame_request kind bot.dispatch, bot.peek or bot.answer_gate, is not listed and not counted: the Bot runtime answers it. Each item's gate object is the daemon's redacted description of that gate, exactly as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state shows it, and is published only when the daemon still reports the same gate the gateway read first: a gate that resolved or changed during the read is left out and counted in meta.omitted (read again). Order: oldest parked first, then session_id, then generation. Pagination: ?page=N&limit=M (1-based page; an invalid page or limit is 400 bad_request). A page holds at most 100 items: an omitted or zero limit, or one above 100, means 100, and meta.limit echoes the value used. meta.total counts every gate parked when the list was read. The `gates` token of GET /api/v1/agent/changes moves when a gate parks or resolves. Realm: ?realm= (or the X-Hoody-Realm header) lists one realm: "global" (gates not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id; ?realm=all lists every realm this login serves (query only, never the header). Omitted, the agent's current realm. Every row carries its realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm lists only that realm: any other value, all included, is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Cache-Control: no-store.

post.description: Begins a GitHub login. With NO body token this starts a DEVICE flow and returns {status, device_code, user_code, verification_uri, interval, expires_in}; keep device_code private, because whoever holds it can complete the login. The user authorizes that URL out of band, then POST /api/v1/agent/github/auth/login/poll completes the login. With a body `token` (a PAT) this instead validates + persists the token directly (no device flow), returning the linked {status, key, login, host}. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

requestBody.description: Optional login options. Supply `token` to add a PAT directly; omit it to start a device flow. Supply `host` for GitHub Enterprise (GHES).

token.description: Optional PAT. When present the login validates + persists this token (no device flow); never returned.

host.description: GitHub host for GitHub Enterprise (GHES); defaults to github.com. On the device flow it must match the host on the subsequent poll call; a login with a `token` completes in this one call.

activate.description: Whether the linked account becomes the ACTIVE one. Defaults to FALSE: linking stores the credential without changing which account is in use, because activation decides the identity your next push authenticates as. WHICH BRANCH: on the PAT branch (a `token` in this body) the account is linked and activated in this one call, so no follow-up POST /api/v1/agent/github/auth/active is needed. On the DEVICE branch there is no account yet to activate (this call only hands back a verification URL), so the flag is not consumed here; send it on POST /api/v1/agent/github/auth/login/poll instead, which is where the account is created and where activation is applied. The first account ever linked becomes active regardless, since none was. A non-boolean value is rejected.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Poll a GitHub device-flow login to completion.
post.description: Polls an in-flight GitHub device-flow login. Forward the {device_code, interval, expires_in} the start reply returned, plus `activate` if this account should become the active one: the device flow activates HERE, not at start, because the account does not exist until this call completes; the call blocks until the user authorizes (or the flow expires/cancels), then validates + persists the resulting token. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. Required to COMPLETE a device-flow login over HTTP (the start call only returns the verification URL / device code). The token is saved with the realm's GitHub accounts and is never returned; the reply is {status, key, login, host}. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

activate.description: Whether the account this poll links becomes the ACTIVE one. Defaults to FALSE: the credential is stored without changing which account your next push authenticates as. post.description: Forgets a linked GitHub account and deletes the copies of its token that a clone (with persist_credentials) or POST /api/v1/agent/github/repo/reconnect persisted into checkouts the daemon can currently reach. The purge is BEST-EFFORT and partial by construction: a repository in a stopped computer, or one no open session is bound to, keeps its copy, so the reply carries credential_purge:"partial" and a message saying to revoke the token on GitHub for a complete removal. If the removed account was active, the active pointer moves to a remaining account (or clears). Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.description: Reports the GitHub authentication state of a realm: each realm has its own GitHub accounts. Token only in env; never returned. It has no cwd or computer: an X-Hoody-Computer, X-Hoody-Cwd or X-Hoody-Config-Dir header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The device-flow login (POST /api/v1/agent/github/auth/login) and the clone/commit/sync/pr mutators (POST /api/v1/agent/github/clone, POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit, POST /api/v1/agent/github/sync, POST /api/v1/agent/github/pr) are separate write routes. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

post.description: Creates a branch at the current HEAD and switches to it (`git switch -c`) in the requesting cwd's repository. THE NEW BRANCH HAS NO UPSTREAM (`switch -c` sets none), so its first push must ask for one explicitly; the POST /api/v1/agent/github/sync default fetch→pull→push cannot publish it, because the pull step fails on a branch with no upstream before the push is reached. The branch name is validated against the safe-ref rules before it reaches git, so a flag-like or malformed name is refused with a 400 rather than becoming an argument. An ALREADY-EXISTING branch is not an error the daemon anticipates: git exits non-zero and the failure surfaces as 502 git_command_failed carrying "a branch named … already exists". Local changes that the switch would overwrite fail the same way, with the tree left untouched. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

x-error-codes.title: Git command failed
x-error-codes.description: The git/gh command ran in the repository and exited non-zero (a rejected switch, a stash pop conflict, an already-existing branch, a refused checkout). It is NOT a malformed request and NOT a transport failure: the repository itself refused the operation. details.output carries git's own token-redacted output and details.exit_code its exit status. A failure CLASSIFIED as an account problem never arrives here: it answers with its github_* code (github_token_invalid, github_token_forbidden, …). An unclassified failure may carry details.account_observation: the linked token was found dead while checking, without proof it caused this failure.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read details.output: it names the git-level cause. Resolve it in the repository and retry. If details.account_observation is present, also check the linked account.
