requestBody.description: The branch to create (cwd-scoped).

branch.description: The new branch name (required). Validated as a safe ref name before it reaches git: a leading dash, a whitespace/control character, or a name git itself would reject is refused with a 400.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Deletes a LOCAL branch in the requesting cwd's repository with `git branch -D`. FORCED: it deletes the branch even when its commits are merged nowhere, and those commits are then reachable only through the reflog until git garbage-collects them. The remote branch is not touched. A name that is not a safe git ref name (an option such as "-D", a ".." sequence) is refused with 400 before git runs. DESTRUCTIVE, with NO confirmation round: calling this route is the intent (a body `confirmed` is ignored; the gateway confirms server-side). Deleting the currently checked-out branch is refused by git and arrives as 502 git_command_failed. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.description: Lists branches for the requesting cwd's repo. Returns {status, branches} verbatim; not paginated. cwd-scoped by the X-Hoody-* headers; the realm picks the GitHub account. requestBody.description: The clone request. Supply EITHER `repo` (owner/name or an https github URL), from which the service derives the canonical full_name + host-validated clone_url, OR the canonical `full_name` + `clone_url` fields directly. At least one form is required; a request with NEITHER is rejected. If BOTH are supplied the explicit `full_name`/`clone_url` WIN and `repo` only fills a missing one (no mutual-exclusivity error). Token rides only in env, never returned.

repo.description: The repository to clone: "owner/name" or an https github URL (https://<host>/<owner>/<name>[.git]). Translated to full_name + clone_url against the active account host. Supply this OR the canonical full_name+clone_url; if both, the canonical fields win.

dir.description: Optional managed clone root override; the traversal-safe parent/dest are derived under it.

clone_root.description: Canonical form of `dir`; wins when both are sent.

full_name.description: Canonical "owner/name" (alternative to `repo`; used as-is when supplied, taking precedence over a derived value). Requires clone_url.

clone_url.description: Canonical https clone URL (alternative to `repo`; re-validated against the active account host; takes precedence over a derived value). Requires full_name.

flat.description: Optional, default false. true clones to <root>/<name> instead of <root>/<owner>/<name>. An existing checkout at that path is reused only when its origin is the same repository; anything else there is refused. Must be a JSON boolean.

persist_credentials.description: Optional, default false. true writes the account token into a git credential file inside the new checkout's .git (readable only by its owner) and points its credential.helper at it, so plain `git push`/`pull` in that checkout (including by the agent's own shell) authenticate as this account. The token is then ON DISK, readable by anything running as the exec user. false does not write a credential; it does not remove one an earlier clone or POST /api/v1/agent/github/repo/reconnect already wrote into a reused checkout. Writing the credential is best-effort and never fails a clone that succeeded: the reply's credentials_persisted says whether it was written. Must be a JSON boolean.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Stages all changes and commits in the requesting cwd's repo, cwd-scoped. A clean tree answers 409 nothing_to_commit (nothing was committed); a commit git refuses answers 502 git_command_failed with git's output. Destructive; access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

post.description: Stages every change in the requesting cwd's repository, commits it with `message`, and pushes the current branch to its upstream: one call instead of POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit then POST /api/v1/agent/github/sync with direction:push. NOTHING-TO-COMMIT IS NOT AN ERROR here: when the tree is clean it still pushes, so an earlier commit that was committed but never published goes out; the reply then says committed:false. PARTIAL FAILURE IS REPORTED HONESTLY: a push that fails after the commit landed answers 502 push_failed with details.committed:true: the work is committed locally, not published; do not commit it again. A push that TIMES OUT answers 503 service_unavailable with the same details.committed plus details.timed_out:true: the push may or may not have reached the remote, so check the remote before pushing again. A refusal because of the REPOSITORY's state answers 409 with its own code: unsafe_transport_config (an http.* setting that could redirect the credential), unsafe_push_config, detached_head, invalid_branch, invalid_remote, no_remote, ambiguous_remote, unsafe_push_destination, upstream_exists (set_upstream against a branch that already tracks a different remote branch), and when it comes after the commit landed, details.committed:true for the same reason. POST /api/v1/agent/github/sync reports the same codes under its failing push step. A stage or commit step that git itself rejects (a failing commit hook, a path git refuses to add) answers 502 git_command_failed with details.committed:false and git's output in details.output, exactly as POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit does. With force:true the push runs `git push --force-with-lease` and OVERWRITES the remote branch's history with the local one, discarding remote commits the local branch does not have (the lease only refuses when the remote moved since the last fetch); there is no confirmation round. The stage and commit steps run without the token; only the push carries it. Unmerged index entries are refused BEFORE staging with 409 unresolved_conflicts. Body `confirmed`/`flat`/`persist_credentials`/`account_key` and scope keys are stripped; the repository comes from the X-Hoody-* headers. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

x-error-codes.title: Unsafe transport configuration
x-error-codes.description: The repository's own .git/config sets an http.* option that could redirect or intercept the GitHub credential (a forced resolve, TLS verification turned off, a proxy), or its http.* configuration is too large to vet. Nothing that carries the token ran. On POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit/push, details.committed is true when this call's commit DID land before the refusal: the work is committed locally but not published: do not commit it again; fix the cause and push.
x-error-codes.resolution: Remove the named http.* setting from the repository's .git/config, then retry.

x-error-codes.title: Git command failed
x-error-codes.description: A git command of the stage/commit leg ran in the repository and exited non-zero (the commit itself, `git add`, a pre-commit check), or a push-destination check did. Nothing was published; details.committed is false when the commit leg failed. details.output carries git's own token-redacted output and details.exit_code its exit status. requestBody.description: The commit message and push options (the repository comes from the cwd scope).

set_upstream.description: Optional, default false: publish the current branch: push it and make it track the same-named branch on its remote. Refused with 409 upstream_exists (details.committed when a commit landed) when the branch already tracks a DIFFERENT remote branch.

force.description: Optional, default false. Force-pushes with `git push --force-with-lease`, OVERWRITING the remote branch's history: remote commits the local branch lacks are discarded. No confirmation round. Must be a JSON boolean.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Draft a commit message with a model.
post.description: Drafts a commit message for the requesting cwd's pending changes with one tool-free call to `model`. It does NOT commit and does NOT touch the index: the diff is built in a throwaway index seeded from HEAD, covering tracked edits AND new untracked files (what POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit would record), and is capped before it reaches the model. The diff is SENT TO THE MODEL'S PROVIDER: do not call it on a repository whose contents must not leave the box. The call is billed; the reply carries its cost_usd. `model` must be a concrete model spec (provider/model); a fusion/ composite is refused. A clean tree answers 409 nothing_to_commit and makes no model call. Paths on the deny list are refused. Runs without the GitHub token. Scope keys in the body are stripped; the repository comes from the X-Hoody-* headers. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.description: Returns the requesting cwd's repository diff as one unified-diff string. `staged=true` returns the INDEX diff (what a commit would record) instead of the unstaged working-tree diff: the two are disjoint views, so a caller reviewing a commit before making it wants staged=true, and one reviewing uncommitted edits wants the default. Runs tokenless (no credential is involved in a local diff) and with color and external diff drivers disabled, so the output is plain text. BOUNDED: the exec layer caps captured output at 1 MiB and appends a "…(output truncated)" marker when it clamps: check for that marker before treating the diff as complete. A clean tree yields an empty `diff` string, which is a successful read. cwd-scoped from the X-Hoody-* headers. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: staged
parameters.description: When true, return the STAGED (index) diff (what a commit would record) instead of the unstaged working-tree diff. Defaults to false. Accepts true/1/yes/on; every other value, including an empty one, is false.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm

get.description: Resolves which GitHub repository the requesting cwd's checkout belongs to, by asking gh to read the configured remote. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

x-error-codes.title: Git command failed
x-error-codes.description: The git/gh command ran in the repository and exited non-zero (a rejected switch, a stash pop conflict, an already-existing branch, a refused checkout). It is NOT a malformed request and NOT a transport failure: the repository itself refused the operation. details.output carries git's own token-redacted output and details.exit_code its exit status. A failure CLASSIFIED as an account problem never arrives here: it answers with its github_* code (github_token_invalid, github_token_forbidden, …). An unclassified failure may carry details.account_observation: the linked token was found dead while checking, without proof it caused this failure.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read details.output: it names the git-level cause. Resolve it in the repository and retry. If details.account_observation is present, also check the linked account.

get.description: Lists a repository's issues through the GitHub REST API using the ACTIVE account's token. Like GET /api/v1/agent/github/pr it runs NO git command and requires `owner` and `repo` in the query: resolve them with GET /api/v1/agent/github/identity. PULL REQUESTS ARE FILTERED OUT: GitHub's issues endpoint returns PRs as issues, and the daemon drops every entry carrying a pull_request field, so this list and GET /api/v1/agent/github/pr are disjoint. `state` filters open/closed/all (default open). Same recent-slice bound as GET /api/v1/agent/github/pr: sorted by most-recently-updated, 4 pages of 50, so at most 200 issues and no cursor to page past them; and the filtering happens after paging, so a page heavy with PRs yields fewer than 50 issues. Provider-controlled strings (title/state/author/url) are token-redacted. 400 when owner/repo are missing; 429 on the upstream rate limit; an account problem answers with its github_* code; 404 github_not_found when GitHub answers 404 (also what a token without access to a private repository receives). Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Repository owner (user or org login). Required: not derived from the bound checkout; GET /api/v1/agent/github/identity returns it.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name without the owner. Required, same source as `owner`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Which issues to return: open (the default when omitted), closed, or all.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

post.description: Opens an issue on the repository the requesting cwd's checkout belongs to, via gh with the active account's token. THE TARGET COMES FROM THE CHECKOUT, not from the body: unlike GET /api/v1/agent/github/issues (which takes owner/repo explicitly), this creates the issue wherever gh resolves the bound repository's remote to, so bind the intended cwd rather than expecting to choose a repository per request. `title` is required and must be non-empty. A ran-but-failed gh (no linked account with issue permission, issues disabled on the repository, an unresolvable remote) comes back as 502 git_command_failed with gh's output. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

x-error-codes.title: Git command failed
x-error-codes.description: The git/gh command ran in the repository and exited non-zero (a rejected switch, a stash pop conflict, an already-existing branch, a refused checkout). It is NOT a malformed request and NOT a transport failure: the repository itself refused the operation. details.output carries git's own token-redacted output and details.exit_code its exit status. A failure CLASSIFIED as an account problem never arrives here: it answers with its github_* code (github_token_invalid, github_token_forbidden, …). An unclassified failure may carry details.account_observation: the linked token was found dead while checking, without proof it caused this failure.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read details.output: it names the git-level cause. Resolve it in the repository and retry. If details.account_observation is present, also check the linked account.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Lists a repository's pull requests through the GitHub REST API using the ACTIVE account's token: this runs NO git command and does not read the checkout. `owner` and `repo` are REQUIRED and are taken from the query, never inferred from the bound cwd: call GET /api/v1/agent/github/identity first to resolve them for the session's repository. `state` filters open/closed/all (default open). RESULTS ARE A RECENT SLICE, NOT FULL HISTORY: the REST client sorts by most-recently-updated and stops after 4 pages of 50, so at most 200 PRs come back and there is no pagination cursor to continue with: a repository with more has older PRs that this endpoint cannot reach. Every provider-controlled string (title/state/author/head/url) is token-redacted before it reaches the wire, because a hostile GitHub Enterprise host holds the submitted token and could otherwise reflect it back through any of them. 400 when owner/repo are missing; 429 when GitHub rate-limits the account; an account problem answers with its github_* code (409 github_not_linked, 403 github_token_forbidden, …); 404 github_not_found when GitHub answers 404, which for a private repository is also what a token without access receives. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Repository owner (user or org login), e.g. "octocat". Required: it is NOT derived from the bound checkout; GET /api/v1/agent/github/identity returns it.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name without the owner, e.g. "Hello-World". Required, same source as `owner`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Which pull requests to return: open (the default when omitted), closed, or all. An unrecognized value is passed through to GitHub, which rejects it.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The pull-request slice. `pulls` is present and empty when the repository has none matching `state`: an empty list is a successful read, not a failure.

post.description: Opens a pull request for the requesting cwd's repo (the token is passed only in the environment; cwd-scoped). Destructive; access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. A repository whose .git/config sets an http.* option that could redirect the credential is refused before anything runs with 409 unsafe_transport_config. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.description: Checks out a pull request's head commit in the requesting cwd's repository. IT LEAVES THE REPOSITORY IN DETACHED HEAD, deliberately: the daemon fetches the PR head into a transient ref and checks that ref out detached rather than creating or force-updating a local branch, so a pre-existing branch of the same name is never overwritten and its commits are never orphaned. Commit from here and you commit onto no branch: create one with POST /api/v1/agent/github/branch first if you intend to keep the work. NOTE the consequence for pushing: POST /api/v1/agent/github/sync refuses a detached HEAD, because there is no branch to push. The fetch carries the token and the worktree update does NOT: they are separate processes precisely so a hostile in-tree filter cannot run with the credential in its environment. GitHub (and GHES) expose every PR, cross-fork included, under the base repository's refs, so no fork remote is needed. `number` is a positive PR number, as a decimal string ("42") or a JSON integer (what GET /api/v1/agent/github/pr returns); 0, a fraction, a negative or a non-numeric value is refused. A PR that does not exist, or a checkout blocked by local changes, comes back as 502 git_command_failed with git's output. A repository whose .git/config sets an http.* option that could redirect the credential is refused before the fetch with 409 unsafe_transport_config. requestBody.description: The pull request to check out (cwd-scoped).

number.description: The PR number (required): a positive decimal string such as "42", or the JSON integer GET /api/v1/agent/github/pr returns. An empty value, 0, a fraction, a negative or anything non-numeric is refused, so a branch name or URL can never be smuggled in as a target.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Merges a pull request ON GITHUB with the active account's token (`gh pr merge`), in the repository the requesting cwd's checkout belongs to. It changes the BASE BRANCH ON THE REMOTE and cannot be undone by this API. DESTRUCTIVE, with NO confirmation round: calling this route is the intent (a body `confirmed` is ignored; the gateway confirms server-side). `method` picks merge (default), squash or rebase; any other value is refused with 400 rather than falling back to a merge commit. The head branch is not deleted and the local checkout is not updated. To pull the merged result, switch to a checkout of the base branch that tracks its remote, then call POST /api/v1/agent/github/sync with direction pull. A PR that cannot be merged (conflicts, failing required checks, missing permission) comes back as 502 git_command_failed with gh's output, or as the account's github_* code when the token itself is refused. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

requestBody.description: The pull request to merge (the repository comes from the cwd scope).

number.description: The PR number (required): a positive decimal string such as "42", or the JSON integer GET /api/v1/agent/github/pr returns. Anything else (0, a fraction, a branch name or URL) is refused, so the merge can never target a different PR.

method.description: Optional merge method, default merge (a merge commit). squash squashes the PR into one commit; rebase rebases its commits onto the base.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.summary: Read a branch's head on GitHub.
get.description: Reads which commit a branch points at on GitHub, through the GitHub REST API with the ACTIVE account's token. It runs NO git command, never fetches into a checkout and changes nothing, so it is the way to check a push whose outcome is unknown: compare `head_sha` with the local commit. `owner`, `repo` and `branch` are REQUIRED and are taken from the query, never inferred from the bound cwd: GET /api/v1/agent/github/identity resolves owner and repo for the session's repository. `exists` is false only when GitHub shows the repository and no branch of that exact name (an empty repository included); because GitHub answers 404 for a private repository the token cannot see, a branch GitHub does not show while the repository is not visible either is 404 github_not_found, never `exists:false`. 400 when owner, repo or branch is missing or the branch is not a valid branch name; 429 when GitHub rate-limits the account; an account problem answers with its github_* code (409 github_not_linked, 403 github_token_forbidden, …). Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Repository owner (user or org login), e.g. "octocat". Required: it is NOT derived from the bound checkout; GET /api/v1/agent/github/identity returns it.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name without the owner, e.g. "Hello-World". Required, same source as `owner`.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Branch name without refs/heads/, e.g. "feature/login". Required; matched exactly, never as a prefix.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

200.description: The branch's head on GitHub, or that GitHub has no such branch.

schema.description: What GitHub showed at `checked_at`. A branch can move right after this read.

status.description: "ok" on the success body.

exists.description: Whether GitHub has a branch of exactly this name. false only when the repository is visible to the account and the branch is not.

head_sha.description: The full commit id the branch points at (40 or 64 lowercase hex); the empty string when `exists` is false.

post.description: Writes the ACTIVE account's token into a git credential file inside the requesting cwd's checkout (<repo>/.git/hoody-credentials, readable only by its owner) and points the repository's host-scoped credential.helper at it, so plain `git push`/`pull` in that checkout (including the agent's own shell) authenticate as that account. Use it after re-linking or switching accounts, when a checkout still holds a dead or missing credential. The token is ON DISK afterwards, readable by anything that runs as the exec user. A subdirectory resolves to its repository root; a linked worktree or a separated git directory is refused (400), as is a path on the deny list or not inside a git repository. A checkout whose credential belongs to another linked account is re-pointed to the active one: that is the purpose of the call. There is no confirmation round, and a body `persist_credentials` is ignored (the route always persists). A failure to reach the checkout answers 503. Takes NO body fields; the repository comes from the X-Hoody-* scope headers. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

post.description: Saves the requesting cwd's working-tree changes onto the stash and restores the tree to HEAD. IT INCLUDES UNTRACKED FILES (--include-untracked), so files that were never added to git are MOVED OUT of the working directory too: this empties the tree more thoroughly than a bare `git stash` and is the one thing to know before calling it. The operation is reversible through POST /api/v1/agent/github/stash/pop, which is why it is not confirmation-gated, but reversible is not the same as harmless: ignored files stay, untracked ones do not. It takes NO body fields; the repository comes from the X-Hoody-* scope headers. A clean tree produces no stash entry and git says so on the output. Failures (an unreadable path, a repository mid-merge) arrive as 502 git_command_failed. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm

post.summary: Restore the most recent stash entry.
post.description: Applies the MOST RECENT stash entry back onto the requesting cwd's working tree and drops it. There is no entry selector: it is always stash@{0}. TWO OUTCOMES WORTH PLANNING FOR. A clean apply CONSUMES the entry: it is gone from the stash list afterwards. An apply that CONFLICTS leaves the conflict markers in the working tree AND KEEPS the entry (git's own behavior), so the tree is now mid-conflict and the stash still holds the changes; that arrives as 502 git_command_failed with git's output, and POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit will then refuse the repository until the conflicts are resolved. requestBody.description: No fields. The pop always targets the most recent entry (stash@{0}): there is no index selector over HTTP. Send an empty object.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Returns the git working-tree status for the requesting cwd. Scoped two ways: by X-Hoody-Cwd/Computer/Config-Dir (git is repo/cwd-relative), and by realm, which picks the GitHub account the read runs as. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

post.description: Runs fetch → pull → push as one logical sync, stopping at the FIRST non-ok step so a later push never runs against a half-synced tree. The body `direction` lets a caller pull-only (fetch+pull) or push-only; default is the full sync (this is BODY-only; query params are not read, so there is no ?direction alias). Each step is dispatched separately. Destructive; access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. `force:true` makes the push leg a force-push that overwrites the remote branch's history, with no confirmation round (the request is the intent). 502 sync_step_failed carries the steps that ran plus the failing one under details; a step refused because of the repository's state (e.g. unsafe_transport_config, detached_head, upstream_exists, the codes POST /api/v1/agent/github/commit/push answers at 409) carries that code as details.steps[last].result.code. When the failing step was refused because of the ACCOUNT the answer is that github_* code instead (e.g. 403 github_token_forbidden), whose message names the steps that completed and whose details.operation carries the failed step's output, exit code and the steps. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

The push step: unsafe_push_config, detached_head, invalid_branch, invalid_remote, no_remote, ambiguous_remote, unsafe_push_destination, upstream_exists (upstream_exists: set_upstream was asked, but the branch already tracks a different remote branch). requestBody.description: The sync request.

direction.description: Optional: "pull" (fetch+pull) or "push" (push only). Default is the full fetch→pull→push.

set_upstream.description: Optional, default false: PUBLISH the current branch: push it and make it track the same-named branch on its remote. Use it for a branch that tracks nothing yet. Refused (502 sync_step_failed, step code upstream_exists) when the branch already tracks a DIFFERENT remote branch; a no-op when it already tracks exactly that one. Without it a push never changes tracking.

force.description: Optional, default false. FORCE-PUSHES the push leg (git push --force-with-lease): it OVERWRITES THE REMOTE BRANCH'S HISTORY, discarding any remote commits your branch does not contain. The lease only refuses when the remote moved since this repository last fetched it, and the full sync fetches first, so on a full sync it protects almost nothing. There is no confirmation round: sending true is the intent. Ignored by the fetch and pull legs. Must be a JSON boolean.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Lists every worktree attached to the requesting cwd's repository, parsed from git's porcelain form. The MAIN checkout is included in the list, not just the linked ones, and it is the entry whose path matches the repository directory (POST /api/v1/agent/github/worktrees/remove refuses to remove that one). Runs tokenless. cwd-scoped from the X-Hoody-* headers. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

x-error-codes.title: Git command failed
x-error-codes.description: The git/gh command ran in the repository and exited non-zero (a rejected switch, a stash pop conflict, an already-existing branch, a refused checkout). It is NOT a malformed request and NOT a transport failure: the repository itself refused the operation. details.output carries git's own token-redacted output and details.exit_code its exit status. A failure CLASSIFIED as an account problem never arrives here: it answers with its github_* code (github_token_invalid, github_token_forbidden, …). An unclassified failure may carry details.account_observation: the linked token was found dead while checking, without proof it caused this failure.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read details.output: it names the git-level cause. Resolve it in the repository and retry. If details.account_observation is present, also check the linked account.

post.description: Adds a linked worktree of the requesting cwd's repository at `path`: a second checkout of the same repository on a different branch, which is how one session works on a branch without disturbing another's tree. `branch` creates a NEW branch for the worktree (`-b`); omit it to check out an existing ref. `start_ref` is what the new branch starts FROM (a branch, tag or commit) and defaults to the current HEAD. The path is validated lexically AND against the session's deny list before git sees it, so a traversing or deny-listed destination is refused with a 400: the deny-list check is the same one that guards every other path-taking github verb. Branch and start ref are validated as safe ref names. An existing non-empty path, or a branch already checked out in another worktree, is refused by git and arrives as 502 git_command_failed. To remove a worktree use POST /api/v1/agent/github/worktrees/remove. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

requestBody.description: The worktree to add (the repository comes from the cwd scope).

path.description: Where to create the worktree (required). Lexically validated and checked against the session's deny list before git runs; a traversing or deny-listed path is refused with a 400. Must not already exist as a non-empty directory.

branch.description: Optional NEW branch to create for this worktree (git's -b). Validated as a safe ref name. Omit it and send `start_ref` to check that ref out; omit both and git uses a branch named after the last segment of `path`: it checks that branch out when it exists (and is not checked out in another worktree) and creates it from the current HEAD when it does not.

start_ref.description: Optional ref the worktree starts from: a branch, tag or commit. Validated as a safe ref name. With `branch` it is the new branch's start point (default: the current HEAD); without `branch` it is the ref to check out.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Removes a linked worktree of the requesting cwd's repository (`git worktree remove`): its directory is deleted and git forgets it. DESTRUCTIVE, with NO confirmation round: calling this route is the intent (a body `confirmed` is ignored; the gateway confirms server-side). Without `force`, git refuses a worktree with uncommitted or untracked changes, or a locked one, and that refusal arrives as 502 git_command_failed with the tree untouched. With force:true those changes are DISCARDED. The main checkout can never be removed (400), and the path is lexically validated and checked against the session's deny list before git runs (400). Branches are not deleted. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

requestBody.description: The worktree to remove (the repository comes from the cwd scope).

path.description: The worktree's path (required), as GET /api/v1/agent/github/worktrees reports it. Must not be the main checkout.

force.description: Optional, default false. Removes the worktree EVEN WITH uncommitted or untracked changes (git worktree remove --force), DISCARDING them: they are not stashed and cannot be recovered. Must be a JSON boolean.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Drives the FULL agent loop once over an ephemeral gateway-owned session and returns text|json|stream-json. The default (json/text) form is an ASYNC job: it returns 202 {job_id}; poll GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id} / GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}/result for the captured Result. format:stream-json (or stream:true) instead STREAMS the run over SSE (start → result/error → end). Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. RISK: a headless run is ARBITRARY CODE EXECUTION on the bind: confirm and plan cards are approved automatically, except human_only cards, a helper's cards and a card a tool-call rule raised (it carries rules: a check-in, or rules that could not be checked), which are denied; a question takes its first option (an empty answer when it has none); and bash/exec are NOT write-gated, so the computer's proxy permission policy is the only control (write permission gates the designated file-write tools and dir-scope home gates file-tool paths; bash can write within the OS sandbox's allowed paths and runs unsandboxed with a warning when no sandbox is available). DAEMON-FAILURE DELIVERY: the initial HTTP exchange returns only the pre-dispatch statuses (400/403/413/429/503/500; 403 forbidden means the request was refused by the Source IP Guard: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only) plus the 200 SSE / 202 job ack: it CANNOT return 404/504, because the daemon run starts AFTER the response. A daemon failure is delivered LATER: in the ASYNC form it completes the job (the failure shows in GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}/result as {status:"failed", error}); in the STREAM form it is the `error` SSE frame. A run whose turn was CANCELLED is not a success: the async job settles canceled with the captured Result kept (status:"cancelled", outcome:"cancelled", the partial output in `result`), and the stream form sends that Result as its `result` frame. A run that FAILED (its turn ended failed, e.g. a model the provider refused, or the run was refused before any turn, e.g. a missing required workflow input) is not a success either: the async job settles failed with the captured Result kept (status:"failed", is_error true, the reason in `error`), and the stream form sends an `error` frame whose `result` is that Result. A timed-out or cancelled run ends its ephemeral session, as a finished one does. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported, and a realm this login does not serve fails the run with error_code realm_not_allowed.

model.description: Optional model spec for the run.

format.description: Output rendering: text | json | stream-json. stream-json (or stream:true) streams the run over SSE; otherwise the run is an async job.

oneOf.name: result
oneOf.title: result
oneOf.description: The captured headless run. The output TEXT is the `result` field; there is no `text` field. `status` is ok, or cancelled when the run's turn was cancelled (a cancelled run is not a success: its partial output is kept). A failed run is sent as the `error` frame, not this one. `outcome` is the turn's terminal outcome. Also carries session_id (the only handle on the run afterwards), model, agent, is_error, error, error_code (the typed code when the run's own input or workflow was refused before any turn, e.g. realm_not_allowed or restriction_unknown, or the code the run's turn ended with; a failed run is sent as the error frame), num_turns, duration_ms, a `steps` list, and `usage` with input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_tokens and cache_read_tokens. usage is NOT keyed tokens.input/tokens.output.

status.description: ok for a run that ended, cancelled when its turn was cancelled. A cancelled run keeps every other field, its partial `result` included.

outcome.description: The turn's terminal outcome (agent_done): completed, failed or cancelled; empty when the run ended without one.

oneOf.name: error
oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: The run failed/timed out; carries {code,message}. A failure after the stream opened arrives here, for example code:"timeout" when the run exceeds its bound, or code:"admin_unauthorized" when the agent was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. These are NOT HTTP statuses on this operation: the run starts after the 200 SSE response. A run that ran and failed also ends here: code is its error_code when it has one (e.g. spend_cap or realm_not_allowed), else run_failed, and `result` carries the captured Result (status:"failed", is_error, error, outcome, session_id, usage).

post.description: Installs the Hoody platform credential from a raw token: the programmatic equivalent of an interactive login. The token must belong to this box's owner: it is checked against this box's own computer on one of the token's realms (or on the account, for an all-realms token) and refused 403 login_not_for_this_box otherwise. It must also carry the full login grant: created from a signed-in session (not from another token), with vault access, the computer, project and resource permissions the agent uses, and permission to create tokens. Otherwise it is refused 403 login_grant_insufficient with the list of what it lacks; a session login (the account's JWT) is not an API token and is refused 403 login_grant_insufficient too; a token that expires within 15 minutes is refused 403 login_expiring, and a platform administrator's token is refused 403 admin_login_refused. A token whose account or permissions change while it is being installed is refused 409 login_changed. On a box with no credential the token is installed (201 installed) and any local sessions or todos without an owner are adopted by the account. On a box already logged in to the SAME account the token replaces the stored one (200 renewed): this is how a realm-limited login's realm set is changed; a token for a different account is refused 409 agent_login_conflict, and a credential from the HOODY_TOKEN environment variable is never replaced (409 credential_present). Enabled by default; a deployment can disable it, in which case the route returns 404. The Content-Type media type must be application/json; parameters such as charset=utf-8 are accepted. Where the deployment also set an operator capability, a matching capability must be supplied in the body (mismatch → 404). The token is write-only and is never returned; the reply carries the outcome, the resulting connection state, the account id, whether the login is limited to specific realms and, if so, those realm ids.

200.description: Replaced the stored credential with a same-account token; secret-free identity returned.

schema.description: {status and outcome, both "renewed" (status mirrors outcome), connected, account_id, restricted, realm_ids (when restricted), and the secret-free identity (username/email/alias)}.

201.description: Installed a new credential on a box that had none; secret-free identity returned.

schema.description: {status and outcome, both "installed" (status mirrors outcome), connected, account_id, restricted, realm_ids (when restricted), and the secret-free identity}.

get.summary: Hoody platform identity and realm scope.
get.description: Reports which Hoody account the agent is logged in as and which realm it is scoped to, without opening a session. connected/source describe the platform credential; account_id, username and alias identify the account when the login recorded them. auth_active and owner_fingerprint are the session-ownership view: every session this agent creates reports owner_fingerprint as its started.owner_fingerprint, and sessions are readable only while the same account is active. auth_active=false means no platform credential is active (every local session is visible); auth_active=true with no owner_fingerprint means the identity is not resolved yet, and session reads by id are refused until it is. restricted/realm_ids/restriction describe a realm-limited login: restriction is realms, none or unknown (with restriction_reason while the login's metadata cannot be read); realm_ids lists the realms it serves. realm_isolation_by_realm maps each realm the agent has resolved tokens for to {state: active|unavailable, reason?, retry_at?}; unconfirmed_revokes counts realm tokens whose revoke the platform has not confirmed yet. realm is the scope session listing and by-id reads use: the agent's pinned realm when it has one, otherwise its active realm selection (an empty id means no realm is selected). A pinned agent also refuses to attach to another realm's session; an unpinned agent attaches by id to a session in its own frozen realm, whatever the current selection, and under a realm-limited login it also reads and drives by id a session of any realm the login serves. PUT /api/v1/agent/hoody/realm switches the active realm. Secret-free: no token, no email, no expiry. The platform credential has no per-request scope, so any realm, computer, cwd or config-dir header is refused 400.

schema.description: {connected, source, account_id?, username?, alias?, auth_active, owner_fingerprint?, identity_unavailable?, realm_isolation, realm_isolation_reason?, realm_isolation_realm?, realm_isolation_retry_at?, restricted?, realm_ids?, restriction?, restriction_reason?, realm_isolation_by_realm?, unconfirmed_revokes?, last_error?: {code, at, missing?, credential_rejected?}, realm: {id, pinned, blocked?, boot_hint?: {realm_id, outcome, at}}}. Fields marked ? are present only when known; blocked is reported for an unpinned agent. boot_hint (unpinned agents only) says what happened at startup to the realm the account last used (its hoody.last_realm hint, consulted when no realm was selected): outcome applied (the agent started in realm_id), skipped_not_member (this computer is not tagged into realm_id, so the agent stayed on all realms) or skipped_membership_unknown (the computer's realms could not be read, so the agent stayed on all realms); at is RFC3339. Absent when no hint was consulted. last_error is the latest refused login attempt (a launch or pasted token, or a bootstrap: its code, such as login_grant_insufficient, and what the token lacks) or, with credential_rejected, the platform refusing the account login on a call made with it (code hoody_auth_expired: it was revoked or expired, and a new login is needed; a realm token failing is not counted). connected reports the stored credential, so it stays true until then. last_error is dropped when the credential changes, and a rejection also when a later call with the same login succeeds.

put.description: Switches the realm the agent is working in, exactly like the realm selector of its terminal interface: the selection is saved and applies to every client, and it is the realm new sessions bind to by default and the realm session listing uses on an agent without a pinned realm. realm_id is a 24-hex realm id, or an empty string for all realms. Sessions already open keep their own realm. The selection is process-wide, so any realm, computer, cwd or config-dir header is refused 400.

put.description: Creates or updates a hook. Requires the begin-write nonce and a live session_id (hooks are session-scoped). Defining a hook persists an arbitrary command that fires on lifecycle events. A hook's IDENTITY is the triple `event` + `matcher` + `command`: the daemon requires a valid `event` and a non-empty `command` on every call, an absent `matcher` means the wildcard group, and a call whose triple already exists updates that entry in place (preserving keys it does not carry). Editing a hook's command text therefore CREATES a second hook: delete the old triple to replace it. Creating a NEW hook requires non-empty `name` and `description` (the daemon rejects an undocumented create); updating an existing hook may omit them to preserve the current values. This route asks for no human confirmation: the model-facing hook-write tool refuses an autonomous caller, but this route writes the hook for any caller the proxy admits. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. A Stop or SubagentStop hook may carry a `when` condition over the calls the agent made in its current turn (see `when`); omitting `when` keeps the stored condition and `[]` removes it. The condition is part of the hook trust hash: on a fleet box an edited condition is held until acknowledged. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

requestBody.description: Hook definition + the begin-write nonce (op:upsert).

session_id.description: Live session id (hooks are session-scoped). Required, either here or as the `session_id` query parameter; a non-empty value here wins over the query.

nonce.description: The single-use write nonce from POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/begin-write minted for op:upsert + this scope; the RPC fails closed without it.

scope.description: Scope of the settings file to write: user, project or local. It must match the nonce's scope.

event.description: Lifecycle event the hook fires on; part of the hook's identity triple. Required: the daemon rejects any value outside the enum.

matcher.description: Matcher selecting when the hook fires (a tool name, a Claude Code alias such as Bash/Edit, or a regex); part of the identity triple. Omit it (or pass "*") for the wildcard group.

command.description: Command to run when the hook fires; part of the identity triple. Required and non-empty: a different command text addresses a DIFFERENT hook.

timeout.description: Per-fire timeout in whole seconds (optional; non-negative whole numbers only: a fractional or negative value is refused, and anything above 86400 (24h) is clamped to it). Omit to keep an existing entry's timeout; 0 or absent means the per-event default, which is 60s for UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd and 600s for every other event. Two ceilings override this value at fire time: SessionEnd is always capped at 60s so a hook cannot wedge daemon shutdown, and every fire through POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/test is capped at 60s.

name.description: Short human label shown in the Hooks tab. CONDITIONALLY required: a NEW hook (an identity triple event+matcher+command not yet in the settings) is refused 400 without it; on an UPDATE of an existing hook omit it to preserve the stored value. Not in the schema's required list only because of the update case. A character displays hide (a control, bidi or zero-width character, or a soft hyphen) is refused 400, as in command.

description.description: Short description of what the hook does. CONDITIONALLY required exactly like name: a NEW hook is refused 400 without it; omit on update to preserve. It may hold tabs and newlines; any other character displays hide is refused 400, as in command.

when.description: Optional condition; Stop and SubagentStop hooks only (a condition on any other event is refused 400 bad_request and nothing is written). Up to 8 atoms, checked left to right over the calls the acting agent made in its current turn: `+names` means such a call happened (after the previous `+` atom's match), `-names` means none happened since. names is a tool name, `a|b` (at most 8), or `*`; Claude Code aliases such as Bash are accepted and cover their whole set of tools. An optional `(key=regex)` or `(regex)` matches the call's arguments, and an optional `:success` or `:error` its outcome. Example: `["+edit_file|write_file", "-bash(command=go test):success"]` holds when a file was edited and no passing go test ran since. A condition matches the acting agent's own tool calls as written, not their effects, and that agent controls them, so `when` is not a security boundary; calls made by helpers the agent started are not counted. A hook whose condition is false does not run. When the daemon cannot see enough of the turn to decide (after `run_workflow` or `tool_orchestrator`, after a restart, after a tool error it cannot classify, in a fusion turn, after more than 256 calls, while a Claude Code call is unsettled or held, after a call from a Claude Code subagent, or in a Claude Code session whose tools do not run through Hoody), the hook runs and its stdin carries `when_indeterminate: true`; it carries `when_indeterminate: false` when the condition held, and no such key for a hook without `when`. A hook that should act only when sure can exit 0 when it is true. Omit to keep the stored condition; `[]` or null removes it. An invalid condition is refused 400 bad_request and nothing is written. The condition is part of the hook trust hash: on a fleet box an edited condition is held until acknowledged.

delete.description: Deletes a hook. Requires the begin-write nonce (minted by POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/begin-write for op:delete) and a live session_id (hooks are session-scoped). Name the hook by the same identity triple PUT /api/v1/agent/hooks wrote: `event` (required and validated) + `matcher` + `command`. Omitting `command` is not a wildcard-safe shortcut: it deletes EVERY command in the matched event+matcher group. A triple that matches nothing is an error ("no hook found"), not a silent success, so read GET /api/v1/agent/hooks first and copy the values back verbatim. A hook listed with `disabled_reason: "hidden_characters"` is shown marked, so its triple cannot be sent back: delete it by its place instead, sending its `matcher_index` and `index` with `event`, `matcher` and `command` exactly as listed. That form removes only such a hook, and only while the file still holds it there; otherwise it answers "no hook found". Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.
