requestBody.description: Hook identity + the begin-write nonce (op:delete).

session_id.description: Live session id (hooks are session-scoped). Required, either here or as the `session_id` query parameter; a non-empty value here wins over the query.

nonce.description: The single-use write nonce from POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/begin-write minted for op:delete + this scope; the RPC fails closed without it.

scope.description: Scope of the settings file to write: user, project or local. It must match the nonce's scope.

event.description: Lifecycle event of the hook to remove; required: the daemon rejects any value outside the enum.

matcher.description: Matcher of the hook to remove, exactly as GET /api/v1/agent/hooks reports it. Omit it (or pass "*") to address the wildcard group.

command.description: Command text of the entry to remove (exact match). Omitting it removes EVERY command in the matched event+matcher group. With `index`, required: the command exactly as GET /api/v1/agent/hooks lists it, marks included.

matcher_index.description: With `index`: the place of the hook's matcher group in its settings file's list for `event`, as GET /api/v1/agent/hooks reports it on a hook disabled for hidden characters. Send both or neither.

index.description: With `matcher_index`: the place of the hook in its matcher group, as GET /api/v1/agent/hooks reports it on a hook disabled for hidden characters. Only such a hook is removed this way.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Issues the two-step write nonce required before EVERY guarded hook mutation, not just upsert/delete but also toggle, disable-all and the rules write. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.description: Returns the tool-call rules of a realm's settings with no session: the same `rules` block GET /api/v1/agent/hooks returns, without its session half (`live`, `timeout_ms` and `scopes`; no `session`, `stale`, `active` or `note`, which compare against a running session). Use it where no session is live, such as a rules panel whose home session was reaped; to see what one live session checks and tells an agent, use GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies. The `user` scope (the realm's profile) is always read. X-Hoody-Cwd adds the `project` and `local` scopes of that directory; without it those scopes are not read or listed. X-Hoody-Config-Dir reads the override's `project` and `local` scopes, and there is no `user` scope. Both must be absolute paths: a relative one is 400 bad_request, whichever header carries it. A settings file whose real location (symlinks resolved) is another realm's profile, or the Global realm's for a scoped realm, is never read, and no symlink is followed when it is opened. When it is the `user` file or under X-Hoody-Config-Dir, the whole read is 404 not_found. When it is the `project` or `local` file of X-Hoody-Cwd (a scoped realm's cwd at or above the home directory, or a project `.hoody` linked into a profile), that layer is left out with a message in `warnings` and no revision, and a session started with that cwd leaves it out too. A box whose account identity is never resolved (an environment token only) is answered. 200.description: The rules of the realm's settings scopes.

schema.description: The tool-call rules of the realm's settings scopes, read with no session.

text.description: The rule in plain words.

kind.description: limit: a call that breaks the rule is denied. check_in: a call the rule covers asks the user first. guidance: standing advice the covered agents follow. playbook: a procedure the covered agents follow when the situation its text describes comes up. limit and check_in are checked by Jev before covered tool calls; guidance and playbook are never checked, they are added to the system prompt of every session and helper they cover.

applies_as.description: Output only, derived from kind: POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules ignores it and never lets it change kind. How the rule reaches the agent: checked = Jev checks covered tool calls against it (limit, check_in); prompt = its text is in the covered agents' system prompt, in the team-rules block (guidance, playbook).

tools.description: The tools the rule is limited to; empty = every tool that is not read-only, except ask_question_to_user, report_outcome and request_view, which only a rule naming them covers. The Bot's control tools (stop, peek, delegates, answer_gate, wait) are never checked. Always empty for guidance and playbook rules.

agents.description: The agents whose calls the rule covers; empty = every agent.

when.description: The rule's condition as written (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules `when`); absent when it has none. A rule with `when` is listed as applying. Whether it applies to a call depends on the calls made earlier in that turn; it applies whenever the daemon cannot see the turn's calls: after `run_workflow` or `tool_orchestrator`, after a restart, after a tool error it cannot classify, in a fusion turn, after more than 256 calls, while a Claude Code call is unsettled or held, after a call from a Claude Code subagent, or in a Claude Code session whose tools do not run through Hoody.

source.description: The settings file that declared the rule.

scope.description: Output only: the settings scope whose file declared the rule, the scope POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules writes that file through (user: the realm's profile settings; project: the folder's shared settings file, or the X-Hoody-Config-Dir settings.json; local: the folder's personal settings file, settings.local.json, or the X-Hoody-Config-Dir settings.local.json). Always set for a rule read from a scope's file; when two scopes name one file, the first in load order (user, project, local). POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules ignores it.

folder.description: Output only, on project and local rules: the folder those scopes belong to, as the daemon's settings resolution names it. With a config dir it is that directory: X-Hoody-Config-Dir (GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules) or the session's config dir. Otherwise it is the folder whose settings hold the file: the X-Hoody-Cwd directory (GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules), or the session's settings folder (GET /api/v1/agent/hooks, POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies), the cwd its settings were resolved for, which can differ from the directory a remote or delegated session runs in. Absent on user rules. POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules ignores it.

live.description: The rules as they load from the scopes' files now, merged in load order (user, project, local), checked and prompt kinds together.

timeout_ms.description: The effective Jev budget for one rules check in ms (the scopes' rules_timeout_ms, else the default 3000).

scope.description: The settings scope.

revision.description: The scope file's rules revision: pass it as the POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules expected_revision.

scopes.description: One entry per scope read whose file could be read, in load order. `project` and `local` are listed only with X-Hoody-Cwd or X-Hoody-Config-Dir; `user` is not listed under X-Hoody-Config-Dir.

computer_id.description: The computer id (24 hex) the grant is keyed by; a computer name is never used.

realm.description: The realm the grant applies in: _global or a realm id (24 hex).

name.description: The computer name when the grant was made, for display (at most 128 bytes).

source.description: card: an exec card answered with trust_computer. rules_panel: POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules (the default for a row sent without one).

exec_trust.description: The per-computer exec trust grants of the user scope (the realm's profile, or the X-Hoody-Config-Dir override): on each computer, in its realm, hoody_exec_* calls ask no card, human-only actions included, until the row is removed with POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules. Empty when there are none or the user scope was not read. A row that fails validation is left out.

warnings.description: Every problem the scopes' files raised: a file that could not be read or parsed, a file skipped for a missing or wrong `version`, a rule that failed validation or is past its kind's cap, and problems that leave every rule in place (an unknown hook event, a matcher that did not compile, an out-of-range rules_timeout_ms, a checked rule that names only tools no rule checks, so it covers no call). The GET /api/v1/agent/hooks `live.warnings` carries the same messages for a session. Empty when there were none.

rule_warnings.description: The warnings that can leave a rule out: a scope file this read cannot show or that could not be read or parsed, a file whose rules were skipped for a missing or wrong `version`, a rule that failed validation or is past its kind's cap. A hook-only warning is never listed here. Empty when every rule was read.

rules_complete.description: true when rule_warnings is empty: `live` holds every rule the scopes' files declare. A client that must not act on a partial rule set checks this field, not `warnings`.

rules.description: The GET /api/v1/agent/hooks rules block without its session half.

post.description: Replaces the tool-call rules in one settings scope. Rules are sentences checked by Jev before every tool call that is not read-only: a `limit` rule the call breaks denies it, and a `check_in` rule the call falls under asks the user first. ask_question_to_user, report_outcome and request_view are checked only by a rule whose `tools` list names them. The Bot's control tools (stop, peek, delegates, answer_gate, wait) are never checked, not even by a rule that names them: a checked rule whose `tools` lists only them covers no call, so it is saved with a warning and left out of every count (the hooks summary, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies, the trust hash). If Jev cannot answer in time, the call is not let through: the main session asks, and a helper agent is denied. This is a guarded WRITE: it requires the begin-write nonce minted by POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/begin-write for op:rules_set plus a live session_id. `rules` is the COMPLETE list for the scope and is validated all-or-nothing; send an empty array to remove every rule. The same write also carries the per-computer exec trust grants (`exec_trust`, user scope only): the Rules panel adds and revokes them here, and with `exec_trust` sent `rules` may be omitted. Rules are part of the hook trust hash, so on a fleet box the new set holds every covered call until it is acknowledged: read the GET /api/v1/agent/hooks `trust.hash`, then call POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/trust/ack. The reply carries the session's rules and effective timeout after the reload, the scope's new `revision`, and `warnings` (always present, usually empty): one names each checked rule that covers no call; and when the saved set has checked rules and Jev cannot check any call right now (Jev disabled, or no usable key for its model's provider), the rules are still saved, but every call they cover asks first, or is denied where no one can be asked. The GET /api/v1/agent/hooks `rules` block carries the same `warnings`. Coverage: rules check the session's own tool calls, helper agents, workflow steps (including inline $(bash:…) and execute_if shells), tool_orchestrator inner calls, a trusted skill's !`cmd` shell commands, loop stop_when probes (only rules whose `tools` list names the probed tool, since every probe tool is read-only), a fusion member's read-only exploration calls (only rules whose `tools` list names the tool; a check-in there is denied, since no one can be asked) and POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{name}/run. Only these routes are checked: a tool run through any other entry point is not. A rule is matched by tool NAME, so a rule scoped to bash does not cover tools that run code by other means (run_codex, hoody_exec_run and similar): leave `tools` empty, or list those tools too. An oversized input fails closed, except a file-writing tool's (write_file, edit_file and their minified forms), which Jev sees as the path, the size and the first and last 8 KiB of each long text field. Auto-reply never approves a rules check-in: it is denied. Known limits: a workflow's own `env` values are not shown to Jev (only its input and step values are), so a command such as `eval "$FOO"` hides what it runs; and a confirmed run (confirm:true, which POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{name}/run accepts only with the parked run's confirm_token) passes a check-in, never a limit. Guidance and playbook rules share the list and the revision, but Jev never checks them: each covered session and helper gets them in a delimited team-rules block of its system prompt (guidance first, then playbooks, each in settings order), at most 8192 bytes of rule lines per agent; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies names what did not fit. A project-scope guidance or playbook rule comes from the repository's own project settings file, so a repository can add text to the prompt. A scope holds at most 32 checked rules and 32 guidance and playbook rules, capped separately; across the loaded settings files each kind keeps its first 32 and the rest is dropped with a warning, so guidance and playbook rules never displace a checked rule. A guidance or playbook rule's text must not spell a <system-reminder> tag (matched case-insensitively on a compatibility-folded form, with spaces, underscores or dashes (a minus sign included) between the words, and an HTML-entity bracket with or without its semicolon or a \u003c / \x3c escape) or contain an invisible format character (refused 400 bad_request; dropped with a warning at load). A session sees an edit from its next model request (its next turn at the latest); a helper keeps the rules it was spawned with. prompt_blocks `team_rules: false` drops the block. They are not in the trust hash: adding one never holds checked calls pending an ack, and their text reaches the model on a fleet box without an ack (like the user's agent instructions). Each rule in the reply and in GET /api/v1/agent/hooks carries applies_as (checked | prompt), derived from kind, and scope (user | project | local) with, on project and local rules, folder; an applies_as, scope or folder sent here is ignored. A limit or check_in rule may carry a `when` condition over the calls the acting agent made earlier in its turn (see rules[].when). A row whose id names a stored rule that has a condition must carry the `when` key, or the write is refused 400 bad_request and nothing is written: an editor that does not know `when` cannot drop a condition silently. Send `when: []` to remove it. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

requestBody.description: The begin-write nonce (op:rules_set) + the session/scope it binds to, plus the operation's own fields.

session_id.description: Live session id (hooks are session-scoped). Required, either here or as the `session_id` query parameter; a non-empty value here wins over the query.

nonce.description: The single-use write nonce from POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/begin-write minted for op:rules_set + this scope; the RPC fails closed without it.

scope.description: Scope of the settings file to write: user, project or local. It must match the nonce's scope. A shipped-hook toggle (shipped_id) does not need it: it always writes the first settings layer.

id.description: Stable rule id: 1-64 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ or -, starting with a letter or digit.

text.description: The rule in plain words, at most 500 characters, no control characters.

kind.description: limit: a call that breaks the rule is denied. check_in: a call the rule covers asks the user first. guidance: standing advice the covered agents follow. playbook: a procedure the covered agents follow when the situation its text describes comes up. limit and check_in are checked by Jev before covered tool calls; guidance and playbook are never checked, they are added to the system prompt of every session and helper they cover. A playbook's text states the situation and the steps.

tools.description: Optional: only check calls to these tools (hoody tool names or Claude Code aliases such as Bash; at most 32). Omit to check every tool that is not read-only (ask_question_to_user, report_outcome and request_view are checked only by a rule that names them). limit and check_in only: a guidance or playbook rule with tools is refused with 400 rule_tools_not_allowed.

agents.description: Optional: only check calls made by these agents (agent names such as general or a custom agent's name; at most 16, no duplicates). The acting agent is the session's own agent for its calls (orchestrator in orchestrator mode), the helper's agent for a spawned helper, and the step's agent for a workflow agent step; a fusion member acts for the agent whose turn it serves. A native workflow step (bash, tool, inline shell) has no agent, so only a rule without `agents` covers it. Omit to check calls by every agent.

when.description: Optional, limit and check_in only (a guidance or playbook rule with a condition is refused 400 bad_request): the rule applies to a call only when this condition holds over the calls the acting agent made earlier in its current turn. Up to 8 atoms, checked left to right over the calls the acting agent made in its current turn: `+names` means such a call happened (after the previous `+` atom's match), `-names` means none happened since. names is a tool name, `a|b` (at most 8), or `*`; Claude Code aliases such as Bash are accepted and cover their whole set of tools. An optional `(key=regex)` or `(regex)` matches the call's arguments, and an optional `:success` or `:error` its outcome. Example: `["+edit_file|write_file", "-bash(command=go test):success"]` holds when a file was edited and no passing go test ran since. A condition matches the acting agent's own tool calls as written, not their effects, and that agent controls them, so `when` is not a security boundary; calls made by helpers the agent started are not counted. The rule applies whenever the daemon cannot see that turn's calls (after `run_workflow` or `tool_orchestrator`, after a restart, after a tool error it cannot classify, in a fusion turn, after more than 256 calls, while a Claude Code call is unsettled or held, after a call from a Claude Code subagent, or in a Claude Code session whose tools do not run through Hoody). A row whose id names a stored rule that has a condition must carry the `when` key, or the write is refused 400 bad_request and nothing is written; send `when: []` to remove the condition.

rules.description: The complete rule list for the scope (at most 32 checked and 32 guidance/playbook rules; ids unique). An empty array removes the scope's rules.

timeout_ms.description: Optional: the scope's Jev budget for one rules check, 100 to 120000 ms; 0 removes it (back to the default 3000). Omit to leave it unchanged. This is the only way to write rules_timeout_ms.

computer_id.description: The computer id (24 hex) the grant is keyed by; a computer name is never used.

realm.description: The realm the grant applies in: _global or a realm id (24 hex).

name.description: The computer name when the grant was made, for display (at most 128 bytes).

source.description: card: an exec card answered with trust_computer. rules_panel: POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules (the default for a row sent without one).

exec_trust.description: Optional: the COMPLETE list of per-computer exec trust grants, replacing the scope's (at most 64 rows, each (computer_id, realm) once, validated all-or-nothing); [] revokes every grant. Accepted only for the user scope (the realm's profile, or the X-Hoody-Config-Dir override); any other scope is 400. When it is sent, `rules` may be omitted and the rules stay as they are. The grants share the scope's revision with the rules.

expected_revision.description: Optional: the scope's rules revision this edit is based on, from GET /api/v1/agent/hooks `rules.scopes[].revision`. When it no longer matches the scope file (another tab, a hand edit, a timeout change), the write is refused with 409 revision_conflict, nothing is written, and details.current_revision carries the current value: re-read, re-apply the change, begin a new write (the refused call used up its nonce) and retry. The check and the write are one settings transaction. Omit it (or send null) to replace the rules unconditionally. The reply carries the new `revision`. The revision is bound to the realm of the session it is read and written through, so a revision read through another realm's session is refused 409 revision_conflict, on a gateway with or without a realm pin.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Run a hook command now, or dry-run a shipped hook.
post.description: Test-fires a hook command: this EXECUTES an arbitrary command now. This route adds no human confirmation of its own (the model-facing hook tool refuses an autonomous caller). A session whose approval policy is "always" refuses a command test with 409 approval_policy_unsatisfiable and nothing runs; the shipped-hook dry run described below is not refused. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. Requires a live session_id (hooks are session-scoped). Which fields you must send depends on the variant, so only session_id is unconditionally required. Passing `shipped_id` selects the shipped-hook DRY RUN: it evaluates that catalogue hook's trigger against a sample command (`command` + `exit_code`, both optional) and reports whether it would dispatch: it executes nothing. Every other call requires a valid `event` and does execute: pass `command` to run an unsaved command inline (test-before-save, with an optional `timeout`), or omit `command` to fire the SAVED hooks matching `event` + `match_value`. A saved hook's `when` is not evaluated, and no `when_indeterminate` key is added; pass it in `payload` to try that branch. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

event.description: Lifecycle event to fire. Required on every branch except the shipped dry-run; the daemon rejects any value outside the enum.

match_value.description: Value the saved hooks' matchers are evaluated against (e.g. the tool name for PreToolUse). Ignored when `command` supplies an inline hook.

command.description: On the ordinary branch: an unsaved command to run INLINE now (this executes it) instead of the saved matching hooks. On the shipped branch: the sample command the trigger predicate is evaluated against (defaults to a representative failing invocation).

timeout.description: Timeout in whole seconds for an inline `command` (positive integers only; a fractional or non-positive value is ignored rather than truncated). Hard-capped at 60s per command: a larger value, an ignored one, and a saved hook's own longer timeout are all clamped to the 60s test ceiling. A call that fires several saved hooks runs them one after another and ends after at most 120 seconds.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the sample command on the shipped dry-run branch (default 2).

payload.description: Extra fields merged into the hook's stdin JSON. The daemon stamps session_id, cwd, hook_event_name and hook_test itself: values supplied here for those keys are overwritten.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Toggles a single hook's enabled state. This is a guarded WRITE: it requires the begin-write nonce minted by POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/begin-write for op:toggle (the daemon RPC fails closed without it) plus a live session_id (hooks are session-scoped). There are two mutually exclusive ways to name the hook, which is why nothing past session_id/nonce is required unconditionally. A SHIPPED hook is addressed by `shipped_id` + `enabled`: enabling records it in the first settings layer, disabling REMOVES the key so it falls back to the catalogue default (disabled). A shipped toggle never carries event/matcher/command. Every other hook is addressed by its full identity triple `event` + `matcher` + `command` (all three, exactly as GET /api/v1/agent/hooks reports them) plus `disabled` for the new state. A toggle never authors a hook: an unmatched triple fails with "no hook found", and the entry's timeout/name/description are preserved rather than rewritten. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.description: Evaluates `state` against named questions and returns calibrated answers. The body is the provider request, passed through without narrowing: `state` is a string, a JSON object or a JSON array (never null, a number or a boolean); `questions` maps a name to a question: {type:"noul", instructions, criteria?:{true, false}} (yes/no; answer {noul: P(yes)}), {type:"choice", instructions, criteria:{label: description|null, …}} with 1 to 255 labels (answer {choice, confidence, probabilities}), or {type:"score", instructions, criteria:[level, …]} with 1 to 10 levels (Hoody Decide: 2 to 10), low to high (answer {score, confidence, probabilities, legend}). Every instructions/description slot may be a string, a JSON object or a JSON array. Unknown fields ride along. Optional: `model` (a provider/model spec; default the effective model; hoody/hoody-decide and hoody-decide, any case, mean hoody-ai/hoody-decide), `timeout_ms` (100 to 120000), and the routing extras `provider`, `session_id`, `trace`, `user` and `x_session_id` (sent as the x-session-id header), sent only to a provider that forwards them; on other providers those are not sent and are listed in `ignored_fields`. Checks run before any network call (label and level limits, per-provider nullability); the 32k-token context is judged by the provider, and the reply carries an advisory context_estimate_tokens. Every answer is validated. A transport failure, 5xx or 429 is retried once (a 429 or 503 only when its Retry-After is at most 5 s and fits the budget); no other 4xx is retried, and neither is a jev_limit. hoody-ai/hoody-decide calls cost 0 (usage.cost_usd 0) and are bounded by per-AI-server plan decision limits (jev_limit). The reply carries answers, model (the version that answered), requested_model, provider, id / request_id / generation_id, ignored_fields and usage {cost_usd (null when any attempt's spend is unknown), known_cost_usd (the proven subtotal), cost_unknown_attempts, attempts, latency_ms, model, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens}.

get.description: Returns the Jev settings of this install and the usage since the agent started. `model` is the explicit jev.model ("" when unset); `effective_model` is the model calls use, with `source` "explicit" or "derived" (derived = the default of the first provider with a key, preferring typesafe, then AI provider, then vercel; hoody-ai/hoody-decide is used only when chosen). `provider` and `key_set` describe the effective model's provider. `usage` totals every Jev call this agent made: calls, errors, attempts, cost_usd (null once any call's spend is unknown), known_cost_usd (the proven subtotal), unknown_cost_calls, tokens, and the last call's latency, model and error code. `effective` {enabled, model, source, key_ready, usable} says whether a decision would run now: usable is true only when Jev is enabled, the effective model is valid and its provider has a usable key (key_ready). X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the install; a computer header is rejected. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Omitted, an agent pinned to one realm uses that realm's settings and any other agent the Global realm's. With X-Hoody-Config-Dir, the settings of that root are read or changed instead (the realm is still checked). A session decides with the settings of the root it was opened in, and `effective` answers for the settings this request selects. Credentials and `usage` belong to the whole agent.

kind.description: What minted the job: session.input a prompt turn, session.workflow a workflow run, session.question_assist an answer:assist request, headless.run a headless run, tool.run_gated a tool run, and todos.message / todos.run / todos.triage the todo message, run and triage dispatches.

delete.summary: Cancel a pending/running job, or delete a finished record.
delete.description: Cancels a PENDING/RUNNING async job, or deletes a finished job's record (succeeded, failed, canceled or unknown): the kit /jobs convention. An `unknown` job whose start was never confirmed can still change state when a late answer arrives. A pending/running job transitions to `canceled` and its work is stopped at the source: a sessionless run (headless / long tool call) has its bounded context cancelled (the daemon honors the cancelled context); a session dispatch / workflow turn is stopped by cancelling the session's active turn (the session and its background tasks are spared). A terminal job's record is removed. Returns 200 {status:ok, canceled:true} on a cancel and {status:ok, deleted:true} on a terminal-record delete; 404 when the job id is unknown. The cancel is authoritative: a late terminator never flips a canceled job back to succeeded/failed. EXCEPTION: an in-flight answer:assist job is NOT independently cancellable (the daemon helper is bound to the question lifecycle with no per-assist cancel on the wire): DELETE returns 409 job_not_cancellable rather than falsely reporting a cancel; it completes on its own or is cancelled by answering the question / cancelling the session turn.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The job id.

schema.description: The gateway-local cancel/delete outcome. Only the applicable field is present: a cancel carries canceled and NO deleted, a delete carries deleted and NO canceled. Read them for truthiness; do not test either against false.

status.description: Always "ok" on success.

canceled.description: Present and true when a pending/running job was transitioned to canceled. Absent on a record delete.

deleted.description: Present and true when a terminal job's historical record was removed. Absent on a cancel.

cancel_delivered.description: Present and false when the job was marked canceled but the stop signal could not reach the session because its connection is gone; the turn ends with the disconnect. Absent otherwise.

message.description: Present with cancel_delivered: why the stop signal was not delivered.

get.description: Queries the active log stream. Filters ride query params; only the parameters declared below reach the daemon: any other query key is DISCARDED before the call, so an undeclared filter silently matches everything. For local sources, paginate by SEQ CURSOR, not by page: ?since_seq=<seq> returns only rows newer than that seq and ?before_seq=<seq> only rows older. Take each cursor from the ENTRIES you received: the newest returned seq to go forward, the oldest returned seq to go back. The reply also carries `latest_seq` (the head, a valid forward cursor) and `oldest_seq` (the oldest sequence still retained, for spotting history evicted from the ring, NOT a backward cursor: paging from it skips everything between it and your page). A platform source (activity, events, proxy) returns one page with `meta` and no seq fields; the seq cursors do not page it. ?since and ?until are TIME bounds (RFC3339, or a relative "1h"/"30m"/"7d"), NOT cursors: a bare non-zero number is rejected 400 (0, +0 and -0 mean now). ?limit=N caps the page: for local sources, omitted it is 200, and any explicit value is clamped to the ring maximum of 500 (limit=0 also means 500). activity takes at most 100 (default 50) and events at most 500 (default 100). Active-only: logs have NO realm parameter at any layer: a realm header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The SSE log tail is GET /api/v1/agent/logs/stream. Each filter names the sources it applies to; a filter the selected source cannot apply (with no source, a filter for a platform source) is rejected 400 bad_request instead of being ignored.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter to a log source/facet (see GET /api/v1/agent/logs/sources). One local source, or exactly ONE platform source (activity|events|proxy); mixing them is rejected.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Filter to a minimum log level (debug|info|warn|error); the same filter as min_level.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Only entries correlated with this session id (exact match on the entry's session_id).

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Only entries correlated with this workflow/task run id (exact match on the entry's run_id).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Lower TIME bound: RFC3339, or a relative duration like "1h"/"30m"/"7d". This is NOT a cursor: a bare non-zero number is rejected 400 (use since_seq); 0, +0 and -0 mean now. Unparseable values are rejected the same way.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Upper TIME bound, same forms as since. Paging BACKWARDS by repeatedly lowering until works, but it is coarse (rows sharing a timestamp repeat); before_seq is the exact backwards cursor.

parameters.name: since_seq
parameters.description: Forward cursor: return only entries NEWER than this gateway seq. A page holds the NEWEST matches up to limit: when more than limit rows matched since the cursor, the older ones are not returned and latest_seq moves past them. To follow the log use GET /api/v1/agent/logs/stream (it resumes from since_seq, oldest first, and sends a `lagged` event with `replay_gap` when entries were evicted before it could read them: reconcile from the `min_seq` it carries); to read history, page backwards with before_seq. A non-numeric value is rejected 400.

parameters.name: before_seq
parameters.description: Backward cursor: return only entries OLDER than this seq. Take it from the SEQ OF THE OLDEST ENTRY THIS PAGE RETURNED, not from oldest_seq, which is the oldest sequence still retained in the ring and is usually far older than the page you just read. Paging back from oldest_seq jumps past every entry in between and returns an empty page, which reads as "history exhausted" when it is not. A non-numeric value is rejected 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Caps this page. Local sources: omitted it is 200; ANY explicit value is clamped to the ring maximum of 500, and limit=0 means 500 rather than 200: a caller that needs more than 500 rows pages backwards with before_seq. activity takes at most 100 (default 50) and events at most 500 (default 100). A non-numeric value is rejected 400.

get.summary: Export logs as a downloadable file.
get.description: Streams the filtered, ALWAYS-redacted log set as a download (Content-Disposition: attachment). MEDIA TYPE FOLLOWS ?format: jsonl (the default, one wire row per line) is served as application/x-ndjson, and txt (human-readable) as text/plain; charset=utf-8. Both media types are declared on the 200 below; branch on the response Content-Type (or on the ?format you sent). Local sources export a point-in-time-consistent snapshot of the in-daemon ring (bounded at the seq observed when the export starts); source=activity|events|proxy exports ONE platform query page, at most the source's own page maximum (see limit), and marks the export partial when more remained. Every export ends with an in-band terminator (jsonl: a final {"_hoody_export":{...}} line; txt: a trailing '# export: ...' comment). It carries rows/gap/partial, and the jsonl form adds complete:true, which is the terminator SENTINEL, not an outcome: it is written as true unconditionally and the txt form omits it, so read the terminator's PRESENCE as "the download finished" and gap/partial for whether the content is whole. Its absence means the download was truncated. Filters mirror the Logs tab (source, min_level, comp, session_id, text, since, until, event, tool, model, status, method, min_status, max_status, errors_only, event_type, resource_type, computer, kind, host). Note the computer filter is `computer`, NOT `computer_id`: computer_id is a reserved scope-identity key the gateway strips from every query, and the handler lifts `computer` back onto the daemon's computer_id filter. ?since_seq exports incrementally; ?limit caps total rows; ?filename overrides the download name (reduced to a safe basename). A filter this route does not take (run_id, or the level alias: send min_level) is rejected 400 bad_request instead of being ignored. Active-only: a realm header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.description: Tails the active log stream over Server-Sent Events. Paginates with a cursor it advances each round (since_seq = the previous reply's next_seq), so no row is skipped under load. The tail rides the SAME seq/replay convention the session stream uses: an `entry` frame per redacted row CARRYING `id: <seq>` (so a reconnecting client resumes via the Last-Event-ID header, which overrides ?since_seq), a `lagged` frame such as {"code":"replay_gap","min_seq":981,"max_seq":1042} when the caller's cursor fell behind the ring (reconcile a replay gap from min_seq), periodic `:` heartbeat comments, and an `end` frame with a `reason` when the tail fails. A client disconnect ends the stream without a frame. Filters ride query params (source, level, min_level, comp, text, event, tool, model, status, session_id, run_id, since_seq); ?limit caps each poll batch. Local sources only: a platform source is rejected 400. Each filter names the sources it applies to; a filter the selected source cannot apply (with no source, a filter for a platform source) is rejected 400 bad_request instead of being ignored. Active-only: a realm header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Entries are ALWAYS redacted.

get.description: Lists the recurring agent loops of every live session the caller may see, oldest first, as the kit list envelope {items, meta:{total}} with optional page/limit pagination (applied gateway-side). A loop is listed only when its session passes the same realm and owner check as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/loops, so loops in another realm's or another account's session are absent, never marked. Loops live only as long as their session, so a closed session's loops are gone. Each item carries its session_id and its session's realm; manage a loop through the /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/loops routes (with X-Hoody-Realm set to the item's realm). Realm: ?realm= (or the X-Hoody-Realm header) lists one realm: "global" (loops not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id; ?realm=all lists every realm this login serves (query only, never the header). Omitted, the agent's current realm. Every row carries its realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm lists only that realm: any other value, all included, is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.summary: Import MCP servers from another tool's config.
post.description: Imports a batch of servers from a pasted config document or an explicit array. Understands the hoody (mcp_servers list), Claude/Cursor (mcpServers map) and VS Code (servers map) dialects; a document carrying more than one of them is REFUSED rather than guessed at. Validation is WHOLE-BATCH: one bad entry aborts everything, because a partial import leaves a config the operator did not author. Imported servers land DISABLED for review; enable them with POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers/enable. A name another settings layer already defines is refused, since that layer's fields would merge into the import; so is an entry carrying env_keys or header_keys, which are fields of the server list, not settings. Requires the begin-write nonce for op:import. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

schema.description: The operation's JSON reply, passed through verbatim.

status.description: "ok" on success.

sessions.description: How many live sessions this write reconciled the CONNECT half for (the caller's own synchronously, the rest in the background). Revocation was applied to every live session (these and the partial ones) before this response returned. Sessions already tearing down are not counted.

partial_sessions.description: How many live sessions had a settings layer that failed to read or parse. They were revoked against the layers that DID load (fail-closed: a server defined only in the broken layer is cut off until the layer is fixed and reinstated in place on the next clean reconcile) and their connect half was skipped. Non-zero means: fix the layer, then reconnect. When the caller's own session is among them, `servers` below describes the file, not what that session has connected.

revoked.description: How many builds were cut off across every live session. A COUNT, not a list of names.

deferred_sessions.description: How many sessions OTHER than the one you named had their reconnect left to the background pass. Their revocation already happened; only reconnecting is deferred.

deferred_started.description: False when that background pass was skipped entirely because every fanout slot was busy: those sessions MAY hold a stale tool list until the next write or an explicit reconnect (a no-op change leaves them already current). True when it was started, or when there was nothing to defer. It cannot report how many SUCCEEDED: the pass outlives this response by design.

scope.description: The settings layer the entry comes from: user, project or local; empty when it is none of those. Always present.

enabled.description: Effective enabled state (an entry with no `enabled` key is enabled). Always present.

require_confirmation.description: Whether every call from this server goes through the confirm flow. Always present.

command.description: The stdio command. Present only when the entry has one.

args.description: The command's arguments; an empty list, never null. Present only when `command` is.

url.description: The http/sse endpoint. Present only when the entry has one.

env_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's env variables. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

header_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's HTTP headers. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

allowed_tools.description: The tool allow-list; an empty list exposes no tools. Present only when the entry restricts its tools.

connected.description: Whether the session's build of this server is connected. Always present; false for a disabled or never-connected entry.

protocol_version.description: The protocol revision negotiated. Present when the session's current generation holds a build of this server (one that connected at some point, whether still connected or since died or been revoked).

server_name.description: The name the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

server_version.description: The version the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

tool_count.description: How many tools the server advertises. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

pid.description: The server process id; 0 for an http or sse server, which runs no local process. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

revoked.description: true when the build was cut off. Present only then.

revoked_reason.description: Why the build was cut off. Present only with `revoked`.

stderr_tail.description: The last lines (up to 20) of the server's stderr, secrets redacted. Present only when there is any.

servers.description: The effective server list for the session you named, after the write: the same entries GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers returns.

requestBody.description: The document or server array, plus the begin-write nonce (op:import).

session_id.description: Live session id. Required, either here or as the `session_id` query parameter; a non-empty value here wins over the query.

nonce.description: Single-use nonce from POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/write-intents minted for op:import and this scope.

scope.description: Settings layer to write. Must match the scope the nonce was minted for.

document.description: A pasted config document in any supported dialect. Mutually exclusive with the servers field. The hoody dialect is accepted here, so anything expressible via servers can be passed as a document.

name.description: Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, max 64 chars, no `__` (it separates the tool name). May not be `hoody` or `mcp`: both are reserved namespaces, and that check alone is case-insensitive, so `Hoody` is refused too.

type.description: `stdio` (default), `http` (aliases `url`, `streamable`, `streamable-http`) for Streamable HTTP, or `sse` for the deprecated 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport, matched case-insensitively.

command.description: The stdio server's executable.

url.description: The endpoint for the http and sse transports.

env.description: Environment variables for the stdio child. A CREDENTIAL field: values are strings and support full ${VAR} expansion, so a token lives in your environment rather than in settings.json. On upsert, null deletes that key; on import, null-valued keys are omitted. A probe refuses null.

headers.description: Headers sent with every HTTP request. A CREDENTIAL field: values are strings and support full ${VAR} expansion. On upsert, null deletes that key; on import, null-valued keys are omitted. A probe refuses null.

allowed_tools.description: Restricts which of the server's tools are advertised AND dispatchable. Absent means no restriction; an empty list exposes nothing.

require_confirmation.description: Park every call from this server for human approval.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A disabled server keeps its config but is neither connected nor advertised.

servers.description: Explicit server entries, in hoody's own shape (the PUT /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers server entry). Mutually exclusive with document. The CLI takes them from a file: --servers @servers.json.

replace.description: Overwrite entries whose name already exists. Without it, a collision aborts the whole import.

expect_hash.description: The mcp_servers hash you last read.

schema.description: The operation's JSON reply, passed through verbatim.

status.description: "ok" on success.

sessions.description: How many live sessions this write reconciled the CONNECT half for (the caller's own synchronously, the rest in the background). Revocation was applied to every live session (these and the partial ones) before this response returned. Sessions already tearing down are not counted.

partial_sessions.description: How many live sessions had a settings layer that failed to read or parse. They were revoked against the layers that DID load (fail-closed: a server defined only in the broken layer is cut off until the layer is fixed and reinstated in place on the next clean reconcile) and their connect half was skipped. Non-zero means: fix the layer, then reconnect. When the caller's own session is among them, `servers` below describes the file, not what that session has connected.

revoked.description: How many builds were cut off across every live session. A COUNT, not a list of names.

deferred_sessions.description: How many sessions OTHER than the one you named had their reconnect left to the background pass. Their revocation already happened; only reconnecting is deferred.

deferred_started.description: False when that background pass was skipped entirely because every fanout slot was busy: those sessions MAY hold a stale tool list until the next write or an explicit reconnect (a no-op change leaves them already current). True when it was started, or when there was nothing to defer. It cannot report how many SUCCEEDED: the pass outlives this response by design.

scope.description: The settings layer the entry comes from: user, project or local; empty when it is none of those. Always present.

enabled.description: Effective enabled state (an entry with no `enabled` key is enabled). Always present.

require_confirmation.description: Whether every call from this server goes through the confirm flow. Always present.

command.description: The stdio command. Present only when the entry has one.

args.description: The command's arguments; an empty list, never null. Present only when `command` is.

url.description: The http/sse endpoint. Present only when the entry has one.

env_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's env variables. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

header_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's HTTP headers. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

allowed_tools.description: The tool allow-list; an empty list exposes no tools. Present only when the entry restricts its tools.

connected.description: Whether the session's build of this server is connected. Always present; false for a disabled or never-connected entry.

protocol_version.description: The protocol revision negotiated. Present when the session's current generation holds a build of this server (one that connected at some point, whether still connected or since died or been revoked).

server_version.description: The version the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

tool_count.description: How many tools the server advertises. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

pid.description: The server process id; 0 for an http or sse server, which runs no local process. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

revoked.description: true when the build was cut off. Present only then.

revoked_reason.description: Why the build was cut off. Present only with `revoked`.

stderr_tail.description: The last lines (up to 20) of the server's stderr, secrets redacted. Present only when there is any.

warnings.description: The loader's warnings for that session's layers after the write: the same lines GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers returns (an entry it had to drop and why, a reserved env key, a skipped layer), followed, on POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/import, by the parser's advisories for the document: a `${...}` placeholder in a field other than env/headers left literal, an unresolvable or VS Code-predefined variable (`${workspaceFolder}`, `${file}`) flagged, a dropped `envFile`. put.summary: Create or update an MCP server.
put.description: Writes one mcp_servers entry, merging FIELD BY FIELD over any existing entry of the same name so fields you omit keep their stored value, including fields this build does not model. env and headers merge PER KEY: a key you send sets that one credential, a key you omit is kept, a key set to JSON null is DELETED, and an empty map ({}) clears the whole map. A JSON null for a top-level field is refused (omit the key to keep the stored value); so is a field name that differs from a server field only in case (`Args`), a null inside args, and two header names that differ only in case. Restating the identity you read back is not a re-point (`type` may be spelled by any accepted alias and an absent `args` equals `[]`; `command` and `url` are compared byte for byte); a genuine change to `type`, `command`, `args` or `url` is a re-point, and it clears env/headers unless the same request re-supplies them. A stored entry the loader refuses to load (two header names differing only in case, a field name in another case (`Args`), a null inside args) is repaired by a write that supplies the exact field (`args`, or `headers: {}` then the one spelling) and refused otherwise, naming the repair. Requires the begin-write nonce for op:upsert. A body carrying the redaction placeholder for a credential is REFUSED rather than stored. On success a re-pointed server is REVOKED in every live session before the response, and the new config is APPLIED to the session you named before the response: its reconnect is AWAITED rather than merely started, so nothing is still pending when this returns. Awaited is NOT succeeded: a server that fails to start or handshake still returns 200, so read `servers[].connected` in this reply before calling its tools. A session that is MID-TURN keeps the tool set it was shown and picks the new one up at the next turn boundary. Other live sessions reconnect in the BACKGROUND, so this never waits out an unrelated session's slow server (it may pause briefly for a free background slot under sustained write pressure); that background pass is best-effort and is skipped under sustained pressure, in which case those sessions pick the change up on the next write or an explicit reconnect. Revocation is never best-effort. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.description: Live session id, as an alternative to the body's `session_id`. When the body carries a non-empty `session_id`, that value is used and this parameter is ignored; otherwise this value, trimmed of surrounding spaces, is used.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm

On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

200.description: Written; revoked everywhere, your session's reconnect awaited. Check servers[].connected for the outcome.

schema.description: The operation's JSON reply, passed through verbatim.

status.description: "ok" on success.

sessions.description: How many live sessions this write reconciled the CONNECT half for (the caller's own synchronously, the rest in the background). Revocation was applied to every live session (these and the partial ones) before this response returned. Sessions already tearing down are not counted.

partial_sessions.description: How many live sessions had a settings layer that failed to read or parse. They were revoked against the layers that DID load (fail-closed: a server defined only in the broken layer is cut off until the layer is fixed and reinstated in place on the next clean reconcile) and their connect half was skipped. Non-zero means: fix the layer, then reconnect. When the caller's own session is among them, `servers` below describes the file, not what that session has connected.

revoked.description: How many builds were cut off across every live session. A COUNT, not a list of names.

deferred_sessions.description: How many sessions OTHER than the one you named had their reconnect left to the background pass. Their revocation already happened; only reconnecting is deferred.

deferred_started.description: False when that background pass was skipped entirely because every fanout slot was busy: those sessions MAY hold a stale tool list until the next write or an explicit reconnect (a no-op change leaves them already current). True when it was started, or when there was nothing to defer. It cannot report how many SUCCEEDED: the pass outlives this response by design.

scope.description: The settings layer the entry comes from: user, project or local; empty when it is none of those. Always present.

enabled.description: Effective enabled state (an entry with no `enabled` key is enabled). Always present.

require_confirmation.description: Whether every call from this server goes through the confirm flow. Always present.

command.description: The stdio command. Present only when the entry has one.

args.description: The command's arguments; an empty list, never null. Present only when `command` is.

url.description: The http/sse endpoint. Present only when the entry has one.

env_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's env variables. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

header_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's HTTP headers. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

allowed_tools.description: The tool allow-list; an empty list exposes no tools. Present only when the entry restricts its tools.

connected.description: Whether the session's build of this server is connected. Always present; false for a disabled or never-connected entry.

protocol_version.description: The protocol revision negotiated. Present when the session's current generation holds a build of this server (one that connected at some point, whether still connected or since died or been revoked).

server_name.description: The name the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

server_version.description: The version the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

tool_count.description: How many tools the server advertises. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

pid.description: The server process id; 0 for an http or sse server, which runs no local process. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

revoked.description: true when the build was cut off. Present only then.

revoked_reason.description: Why the build was cut off. Present only with `revoked`.

stderr_tail.description: The last lines (up to 20) of the server's stderr, secrets redacted. Present only when there is any.

servers.description: The effective server list for the session you named, after the write: the same entries GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers returns.

warnings.description: The loader's warnings for that session's layers after the write: the same lines GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers returns (an entry it had to drop and why, a reserved env key, a skipped layer), followed, on POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/import, by the parser's advisories for the document: a `${...}` placeholder in a field other than env/headers left literal, an unresolvable or VS Code-predefined variable (`${workspaceFolder}`, `${file}`) flagged, a dropped `envFile`. requestBody.description: The server entry, the begin-write nonce (op:upsert) and the expected content hash.

session_id.description: Live session id. Required, either here or as the `session_id` query parameter; a non-empty value here wins over the query.

nonce.description: Single-use nonce from POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/write-intents minted for op:upsert and this scope; the RPC fails closed without it.

scope.description: Settings layer to write. Must match the scope the nonce was minted for.

expect_hash.description: The mcp_servers hash you last read, as returned by POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/write-intents or GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers. REQUIRED: a mismatch returns a conflict instead of overwriting a concurrent edit, and a first write into a file that does not exist yet states its expectation with the empty-array hash rather than omitting this.

name.description: Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, max 64 chars, no `__` (it separates the tool name). May not be `hoody` or `mcp`: both are reserved namespaces, and that check alone is case-insensitive, so `Hoody` is refused too.

type.description: `stdio` (default), `http` (aliases `url`, `streamable`, `streamable-http`) for Streamable HTTP, or `sse` for the deprecated 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport, matched case-insensitively.

command.description: The stdio server's executable.

url.description: The endpoint for the http and sse transports.

env.description: Environment variables for the stdio child. A CREDENTIAL field: values are strings and support full ${VAR} expansion, so a token lives in your environment rather than in settings.json. On upsert, null deletes that key; on import, null-valued keys are omitted. A probe refuses null.

headers.description: Headers sent with every HTTP request. A CREDENTIAL field: values are strings and support full ${VAR} expansion. On upsert, null deletes that key; on import, null-valued keys are omitted. A probe refuses null.

allowed_tools.description: Restricts which of the server's tools are advertised AND dispatchable. Absent means no restriction; an empty list exposes nothing.

require_confirmation.description: Park every call from this server for human approval.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A disabled server keeps its config but is neither connected nor advertised.

server.description: The server entry. A key set to JSON null inside env or headers deletes that one key.

delete.description: Removes one mcp_servers entry from the named settings layer. Requires the begin-write nonce for op:delete. 200.description: Updated; a disable is revoked in every live session before this returned.

schema.description: The operation's JSON reply, passed through verbatim.

status.description: "ok" on success.

sessions.description: How many live sessions this write reconciled the CONNECT half for (the caller's own synchronously, the rest in the background). Revocation was applied to every live session (these and the partial ones) before this response returned. Sessions already tearing down are not counted.

partial_sessions.description: How many live sessions had a settings layer that failed to read or parse. They were revoked against the layers that DID load (fail-closed: a server defined only in the broken layer is cut off until the layer is fixed and reinstated in place on the next clean reconcile) and their connect half was skipped. Non-zero means: fix the layer, then reconnect. When the caller's own session is among them, `servers` below describes the file, not what that session has connected.

revoked.description: How many builds were cut off across every live session. A COUNT, not a list of names.

deferred_sessions.description: How many sessions OTHER than the one you named had their reconnect left to the background pass. Their revocation already happened; only reconnecting is deferred.

deferred_started.description: False when that background pass was skipped entirely because every fanout slot was busy: those sessions MAY hold a stale tool list until the next write or an explicit reconnect (a no-op change leaves them already current). True when it was started, or when there was nothing to defer. It cannot report how many SUCCEEDED: the pass outlives this response by design.

scope.description: The settings layer the entry comes from: user, project or local; empty when it is none of those. Always present.

enabled.description: Effective enabled state (an entry with no `enabled` key is enabled). Always present.

require_confirmation.description: Whether every call from this server goes through the confirm flow. Always present.

command.description: The stdio command. Present only when the entry has one.

args.description: The command's arguments; an empty list, never null. Present only when `command` is.

url.description: The http/sse endpoint. Present only when the entry has one.

env_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's env variables. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

header_keys.description: Sorted NAMES of the entry's HTTP headers. Values are never returned. Always present, possibly empty.

allowed_tools.description: The tool allow-list; an empty list exposes no tools. Present only when the entry restricts its tools.

connected.description: Whether the session's build of this server is connected. Always present; false for a disabled or never-connected entry.

protocol_version.description: The protocol revision negotiated. Present when the session's current generation holds a build of this server (one that connected at some point, whether still connected or since died or been revoked).

server_name.description: The name the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

server_version.description: The version the server reported. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

tool_count.description: How many tools the server advertises. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

pid.description: The server process id; 0 for an http or sse server, which runs no local process. Present under the same condition as protocol_version.

revoked.description: true when the build was cut off. Present only then.

revoked_reason.description: Why the build was cut off. Present only with `revoked`.

stderr_tail.description: The last lines (up to 20) of the server's stderr, secrets redacted. Present only when there is any.

servers.description: The effective server list for the session you named, after the write: the same entries GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers returns.

warnings.description: The loader's warnings for that session's layers after the write: the same lines GET /api/v1/agent/mcp/servers returns (an entry it had to drop and why, a reserved env key, a skipped layer), followed, on POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/import, by the parser's advisories for the document: a `${...}` placeholder in a field other than env/headers left literal, an unresolvable or VS Code-predefined variable (`${workspaceFolder}`, `${file}`) flagged, a dropped `envFile`. Always present, usually empty; read it when a server you just wrote is missing from `servers`.

path.description: The settings file that was written.

hash.description: The mcp_servers hash AFTER this write. Pass it as expect_hash on your next write instead of round-tripping POST /api/v1/agent/mcp/write-intents: an empty expect_hash is refused.

requestBody.description: Which write is intended, and in which settings layer.

session_id.description: Live session id (MCP config is resolved against the session's settings layers). Required, either here or as the `session_id` query parameter; a non-empty value here wins over the query.

op.description: Which write the nonce authorizes. The minted nonce is valid for this op alone.

scope.description: Settings layer to write. Defaults to user, or project when there is no user layer (which is the case under --config-dir).

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Enqueues a consolidation pass for a project. Consolidation spends multi-LLM passes and evolves memory state irreversibly, so it is a guarded write: it requires the single-use intent from POST /api/v1/agent/memory/write-intents (op "consolidate", same project) in the body as `nonce`. The intent binds the store, the realm it was minted in, the op and the project, so a wipe_project intent, an intent for another project, or one minted before a realm switch is refused. A missing, expired, spent or mismatched intent is refused 409 write_intent_invalid and nothing is enqueued. Every request that enters the authorized consolidate handler spends the intent, whether the pass is then enqueued or refused (a realm that no longer matches, a missing project, an unavailable store, a full queue), so a retry needs a fresh one. A request refused before it reaches the consolidate handler does not spend the intent (for example a malformed or unsupported realm, a computer header, an X-Hoody-Cwd or X-Hoody-Config-Dir header that is not valid UTF-8, a body that cannot be read, a failed admin authorization, a rate limit (429), or a 403 because Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only); the intent stays valid until it expires. The pass runs in the background: a 200 means it was enqueued, not finished. 503 consolidate_unavailable when the maintenance queue is full or memory is disabled; retry shortly with a fresh intent. The agent's own memory_consolidate tool is unaffected: it still needs an interactive human. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the install. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

put.summary: Assign this computer as the memory data host.
put.description: Elects THIS computer as the realm's memory data host: the recovery action when a realm's memory has no reachable host. Only self-assignment is implemented; naming a peer is refused 400 unsupported. The realm the assignment is for is named by `expect_realm` in the body, or by the request's realm (below); one of them is MANDATORY ("global" or a 24-hex id): the daemon reads an absent realm as the global realm rather than as "unspecified", so naming none is refused 400 at the edge rather than silently assigning global. When both are given and name different realms the request is refused 400 bad_request. Only the agent's active realm can be assigned: a realm switch between the data-host read and this call, or another realm, is refused 409 refused_realm_changed. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. The assignment acts on this agent's own memory coordinator: X-Hoody-Config-Dir does not change what is assigned. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

put.description: Flips the memory privacy switch: persists features.memory and applies it immediately. Not restricted to admins (the daemon applies no admin check to this call). Body: {enabled: bool}. A named realm writes that realm's settings. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Omitted, an agent pinned to one realm writes that realm's settings; any other agent writes the Global realm's, and also its active realm's when that is a realm other than Global it may use. With X-Hoody-Config-Dir, only that root's settings are written. When settings.local.json keeps another value in effect, the switch is still written and the answer is 409 memory_setting_overridden (details.enabled is the state in effect). When only some of the settings files could be written the answer is 500 store_failed with details.partial true and details.enabled the state in effect where it was written.
