servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Lists memory records for a project. Filter via ?project=&kind=&type=&query=. The ?type= and ?query= filters apply ONLY to kind=memory (the default store); the lesson/slot/observation stores do not support these filters, so passing type/query with one of those kinds is REJECTED 400 rather than silently returning an unfiltered page. DAEMON-PAGINATED (unlike the client-paginated collections): the daemon caps the page size at 200 and never returns an unbounded set, so the response ALWAYS carries meta.page + meta.limit reflecting the EFFECTIVE page size: an omitted ?limit (or one over 200) pages at 200, NOT "no pagination". Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy; the daemon's own admin check may still refuse with 403 admin_unauthorized when the daemon was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project key to scope the listing to.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The store to list: memory (the default), lesson, slot or observation. Each answers its own row shape (see items).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Memory type to filter by (e.g. workflow, fact). kind=memory ONLY: rejected 400 with a lesson/slot/observation kind.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free-text filter over the records. kind=memory ONLY: rejected 400 with a lesson/slot/observation kind.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page (1..200). 0 or omitted pages at the 200 ceiling; a value over 200 is clamped to 200. The effective page size is echoed in meta.limit. NOT "no pagination": the daemon never returns an unbounded set.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of rows. With kind=memory (the default) each element is a memory row with the properties below, and always carries id, type, title, strength, version and updated_at (files only when the memory names any). The other kinds answer their own rows: observation {id, ts, title?, tool_name?}; lesson {ID, Project, Content, Context, Confidence, Deleted, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt}; slot {Project, Name, Content, UpdatedAt}. Lesson and slot members are sent with those capitalized names.

id.description: Memory id: the {id} of GET /api/v1/agent/memory/items/{id}, PATCH /api/v1/agent/memory/items/{id} and DELETE /api/v1/agent/memory/items.

strength.description: Ranking strength, a whole number from 1 (weakest) to 10 (strongest). It is set when the memory is saved and replaced by PATCH /api/v1/agent/memory/items/{id}; the agent's consolidation may change it.

version.description: Version number, from 1. An edit of the content, type, concepts or files makes a new version, which the list then shows in place of this one; a strength or expiry edit does not.

updated_at.description: When the memory last changed (RFC 3339).

files.description: File paths the memory is about. Absent when it names none.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages (the full count, not the page size).

limit.description: Items per page (present only when limit>0).

requestBody.description: The memory record.

project.description: Project key the memory belongs to.

type.description: Memory type: pattern, preference, architecture, bug, workflow or fact. Omitted or empty saves a fact; any other value is REFUSED, as on edit.

concepts.description: Concept tags to index the memory under.

files.description: File paths the memory is about.

ttl_days.description: Days until the memory expires, counted from the save. Omitted, 0 or a negative value means no expiry. Must be a whole number between -2147483648 and 106751 (about 292 years: the longest expiry the store can represent); a value outside that range is REFUSED, never clamped and never treated as no expiry. A fractional value like 30.5 and a numeric string like "30" are both REFUSED too, never truncated or coerced: a silent coercion to 0 would store the memory with no expiry at all while reporting success.

strength.description: Initial ranking strength, a whole number from 1 (weakest) to 10 (strongest). Omitted or 0 takes the store's default of 7. Any other value (a negative number, anything above 10, a fractional value or a numeric string) is REFUSED, never coerced and never silently replaced with the default.

delete.description: Deletes a memory record. The delete is cross-project. requestBody.description: Patch fields for the memory record (the {id} comes from the path). An absent field preserves the stored value; a present one overwrites it.

project.description: Project key the record belongs to.

kind.description: Which store the record lives in. Omitted means memory. It selects which of the fields below apply; observation is not editable.

content.description: Replacement content. Applies to every kind, and is REQUIRED for kind=slot (a slot edit with no content is refused; an empty or whitespace-only content deletes the slot, as the delete route does).

type.description: kind=memory: replacement memory type (e.g. workflow, fact).

concepts.description: kind=memory: replacement concept tags. The whole list is replaced, and a malformed array is rejected rather than silently truncated.

files.description: kind=memory: replacement file paths. The whole list is replaced, and a malformed array is rejected rather than silently truncated.

strength.description: kind=memory: replacement ranking strength, a whole number from 1 (weakest) to 10 (strongest). Any other value (0, a negative number, anything above 10, a fractional value or a numeric string) is REFUSED, never coerced, and the stored strength is left unchanged.

ttl_days.description: kind=memory: days until the memory expires, counted from now. 0 or a negative value CLEARS the expiry and makes the memory permanent, so omit the field entirely on an edit that is not about retention. Must be a whole number between -2147483648 and 106751 (about 292 years: the longest expiry the store can represent); a value outside that range is REFUSED, never clamped, and the stored expiry is left unchanged. A fractional value like 30.5 and a numeric string like "30" are both REFUSED too, never truncated or coerced.

context.description: kind=lesson: replacement context. Send it verbatim to preserve it: an absent value preserves the stored one, but the field is how the TUI resends it unchanged.

expect_realm.description: Optional realm assertion: "global" or a 24-hex realm id. The edit is refused when it does not name the realm the request acts in (the named realm, else the agent's active realm).

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Lists the memory projects. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy; the daemon's own admin check may still refuse with 403 admin_unauthorized when the daemon was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. delete.description: Erases everything a project owns: its observations, memories, summaries, sessions, lessons, slots, documents, search index and relation graph, and everything derived from them. IRREVERSIBLE, and NOT the same as deleting every item the listing returns: summaries and the relation graph cannot be deleted item by item, so an item-by-item delete leaves a project that still shapes future recall. Requires the single-use intent from POST /api/v1/agent/memory/write-intents (op "wipe_project", same project) in the body as `nonce`; every request that enters the authorized wipe handler spends the intent, whether the wipe then succeeds or is refused (a realm that no longer matches, a missing project), so a retry needs a fresh one. A request refused before it reaches the wipe handler does not spend the intent (for example a malformed or unsupported realm, a computer header, an X-Hoody-Cwd or X-Hoody-Config-Dir header that is not valid UTF-8, a body that cannot be read, a failed admin authorization, a rate limit (429), or a 403 because Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only); the intent stays valid until it expires. Memory captured before the erasure is erased with it, and no session re-injects erased content, whether the wipe succeeds or fails. An audit entry survives by design: it records counts, never content. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the install; the project comes from the path. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy; the daemon's own admin check may still refuse with 403 admin_unauthorized when the daemon was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. 503 store_unavailable when the memory store is not warm. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. get.description: Reports whether memory is on, whether its store resolved, and what it holds. This is the discriminator the other memory reads cannot be: GET /api/v1/agent/memory/projects and GET /api/v1/agent/memory/items return a SUCCESSFUL empty result for a realm whose memory is off, which is byte-identical to a healthy store with nothing in it. `enabled` is the persisted capture switch, `available` says whether a store resolved, `degraded` distinguishes a real fault from an off realm, and `reason`/`remedy`/`recoverable` describe it. An off or degraded store is a 200 describing that state, not an error: only the server's admin gate and a realm-pin mismatch fail the request. `totals` covers the whole store; pass ?project= to also get that project's `counts`, `embedding_coverage` and `last_consolidated_at`. `last_consolidated` discriminates recorded/never/unreadable, because a store that could not be read must not report the same "never" as one that has genuinely never consolidated. `degraded_reads` names any block whose read failed. `consolidation` says what a consolidation pass is doing on this agent now (queued, running, or idle with how and when the last one ended), so a client shows a POST /api/v1/agent/memory/consolidate request as done only once it is idle with a `last_done_ms` after the request and a `last_result` of ok; `unknown` means the agent could not confirm a write of that pass, so its work may or may not be saved. Counts are the durable rows and may lag an in-flight capture batch; call POST /api/v1/agent/memory/flush first for a barrier. No database path and no pre-formatted privacy text are returned: `remote` and `available` are the facts a client renders its own egress disclosure from. Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. ?project= filters ROWS and never selects a store; X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the install. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

schema.description: The verbatim reply {enabled, available, degraded, reason, remedy, recoverable, remote, project, memory_model, embeddings_model, totals, counts?, embedding_coverage?, last_consolidated, last_consolidated_at, counters, capture_latency, breakers, consolidation?, degraded_reads}.

state.description: idle: no pass waits or runs; queued: a pass waits for the agent's memory worker; running: a pass is executing.

project.description: The project the state is about. Absent without ?project= until a pass has been seen.

queued_at_ms.description: Only while queued: when the oldest pass still waiting was queued (Unix ms).

last_done_ms.description: When the last pass ended, whatever its last_result (Unix ms). Absent until a pass has ended since the agent started.

last_result.description: How the last pass ended, sent with last_done_ms. The first rule that applies wins. failed: a step of it failed or was skipped because the memory model kept failing, its output was discarded because its sources changed under it (rerun_needed says when no reattempt is coming), or it was taken off the queue without running. unknown: otherwise, the agent never got a definite answer to one of its writes (the answer was lost, or the call timed out or was cancelled after it was sent), so that write, and the pass's work, may or may not be saved, even if the pass was then cut short. failed: otherwise, it was cut short (memory turned off, even if turned on again before it ended, the project erased, the agent stopping). ok: it ran to its end.

rerun_needed.description: Only true, sent with last_result failed: the last pass discarded its output because its sources changed under it and no reattempt is queued (its reattempts ran out, or the agent's memory work queue was full), so that work is consolidated only by a new pass.

consolidation.description: Present when a store resolved (available true): what a consolidation pass is doing on this agent now. With ?project= it is that project's; without, the running pass, else the longest-waiting one, else the one that ended last. It is this agent's own record, so it starts idle after the agent restarts (last_consolidated_at is the stored time of the last pass). A pass the agent consolidates on its own shows here too.

totals.description: Whole-store counts; omitted if its read fails.

counts.description: The ?project= project's counts. Present only when a project is named and its read succeeds.

counters.description: When the memory store is available, counters contains capture and maintenance counters (captured, dropped, dropped_bytes, deduped, session_capped, flush_timeouts, flush_tx_capped, compress_failed, compress_dropped, breaker_dropped, summary_failed, maint_dropped, embedded, embed_failed, embed_dropped, graph_extract_failed, graph_discarded, consolidated, consolidate_failed, consolidate_discard, evicted, auto_forgotten, contradictions).

post.description: Mints the single-use intent a guarded memory write requires. The intent binds {store, op, project} and is rejected for any other operation or project. Every guarded write that enters its authorized handler spends it, whether the write then succeeds or is refused (a realm that no longer matches, a missing project), so every retry needs a fresh one. A request refused before it reaches that handler does not spend the intent (for example a malformed or unsupported realm, a computer header, an X-Hoody-Cwd or X-Hoody-Config-Dir header that is not valid UTF-8, a body that cannot be read, a failed admin authorization, a rate limit (429), or a 403 because Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only); the intent stays valid until it expires. `op` is "wipe_project" (the intent for DELETE /api/v1/agent/memory/projects/{project}) or "consolidate" (the intent for POST /api/v1/agent/memory/consolidate); an intent minted for one never authorizes the other. It also binds the realm it was minted in (the named realm, else the active one), so a realm switch between the mint and the write invalidates it rather than acting on another realm's project. It expires, so mint it when you submit rather than when a form opens. When the agent already holds the most unexpired intents it keeps, the answer is 429 memory_write_intents_full with a Retry-After header; that is not the request rate limit (rate_limited). Naming a realm whose memory is not connected on the agent right now answers 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After; the request never connects it. X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the install. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.description: Lists the MERGED model catalogue: every catalogued provider model (spec, display name, context window, output limit, reasoning flag, prices) AND every selectable fusion composite (spec fusion/<slug>, with its method + member specs). Each entry carries source:"provider" or source:"fusion" so a caller can tell them apart; a composite's context_window is the minimum across its catalogued members and it carries no per-token price. A single read returns the full set of bindable specs: no separate GET /api/v1/agent/settings/fusion round-trip is required. Only SELECTABLE composites appear (a broken composite is excluded; fetch GET /api/v1/agent/settings/fusion?include_invalid=true to manage those). Prices are the rates the agent prices usage at (the rates its cost figures and spend caps use), in US dollars per million tokens: cost_in (input), cost_out (output), cost_cache_read (input read from the prompt cache) and cost_cache_write (input written to the prompt cache). A price is omitted when it is unknown; 0 means free. cost_reported_by_provider true marks a model whose provider reports the cost of each reply itself: its prices are list prices, and its usage is charged at what the provider reports. A provider model also carries efforts, the thinking levels a session on it can be sent (low, medium, high, xhigh, max; an empty list means it takes no level), input_modalities (for example text, image) when the catalogue knows them, and tool_call (true when the model calls tools, false when it does not; omitted when the catalogue does not say, which means unknown, not false). Fusion composites are cwd/config_dir scoped, so X-Hoody-Cwd / X-Hoody-Config-Dir are honored to resolve them; a per-request realm header (and X-Hoody-Computer, which has no model dimension) returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

Any value other than true or false returns 400 bad_request.

get.description: Reports whether the agent is paused (see PUT /api/v1/agent/pause), since when, and the pause generation. The pause is daemon-wide: it covers every session of the agent in every realm, so a realm, computer, cwd or config-dir header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. It counts within one run of the agent: after a restart it starts again at 0, so a gen lower than the last one seen, or a session stream that restarted, means the state was reset.

put.description: {"paused":true} pauses the agent: each session holds at the next step the agent controls, which is its next model request or tool batch (helpers and workflow agent steps included), and a due loop does not fire until resumed. A Claude Code session holds before each prompt the agent sends it, and its calls to the agent's tools wait while paused; the model requests Claude Code makes between them are held only when the installed Claude Code supports that, and work Claude Code does by itself, such as compacting its own conversation, is not held. Work already running is not cancelled: a model reply being written or a tool already running finishes first. A held turn is still running, so cancelling it (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/cancel) still ends it. {"paused":false} resumes: each held session continues where it stopped. The pause is daemon-wide: it covers every session of the agent in every realm, so a realm, computer, cwd or config-dir header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Asking for the state already in force changes nothing and answers that state with the same gen. A request whose answer was lost is not sent again automatically: another caller may have changed the state since, so read GET /api/v1/agent/pause and decide. Every change is sent to every attached session's stream as event.pause_state {paused, since_ms, gen}. The pause lasts while the agent runs: it is not saved, so after the agent restarts it is running again (paused false, gen 0) and held work, such as a turn the restart cut that the agent continues, goes ahead; pause again after a restart if work must stay held. To stop work rather than hold it, use POST /api/v1/agent/stop. paused is required and is the only field: any other field is 400 bad_request.

200.description: The pause state after the request.

get.description: Lists every catalogued LLM provider from the merged providers.json catalogue. post.description: Adds a custom AI provider: an endpoint that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages API, with its models. Its models are selectable as <model_prefix>/<model> wherever a model is (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions, PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/model, agents, Jev) once its key is stored. Keys never go in this body: store the provider's key with PUT /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/api-key once the provider exists. The change applies at once, with no restart: new sessions, model switches and Jev see it, and every open session using one of the provider's models picks it up before its next turn. base_url must be an https URL with no user name, password, query or fragment, at a public address. Create, and update when it changes base_url, refuse with 422 provider_invalid a host written as an internal address, a name that does not resolve, a name with no IPv4 address, and a name that resolves to an internal IPv4 address. The address is checked again whenever a new connection to the provider is opened, so a name whose DNS later points inside is refused then. To retry a create safely, send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and body answers 201 with the provider the first try created; the same key with another body is refused 422 idempotency_key_reused. Without a key, a retry whose first try succeeded answers 409 provider_exists. Then use the models: store the key (PUT /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/api-key), and start a session on one (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions with model "<model_prefix>/<model>"), switch an open session to one (PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/model) or pin one on an agent (PATCH /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/model). Process-wide: a per-request realm, cwd, config-dir or computer header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

id.description: The provider id: 1-40 lowercase letters, digits or inner hyphens. It cannot be changed later.

model_prefix.description: The prefix of the provider's model specs (acme for acme/<model>). It must equal the id; omitted, it is the id. No provider's id or prefix may already use it, and fusion is reserved.

display_name.description: Display name. Omitted on create, it is the id.

wire_format.description: The API the endpoint speaks: chat_completions (OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, the default on create), responses (OpenAI Responses) or messages (Anthropic Messages).

base_url.description: The endpoint's base URL, the part before /chat/completions, /responses or /v1/messages (e.g. https://api.acme.example/v1). base_url must be an https URL with no user name, password, query or fragment, at a public address. Create, and update when it changes base_url, refuse with 422 provider_invalid a host written as an internal address, a name that does not resolve, a name with no IPv4 address, and a name that resolves to an internal IPv4 address. The address is checked again whenever a new connection to the provider is opened, so a name whose DNS later points inside is refused then.

auth_scheme.description: How the stored key is sent. It follows wire_format: bearer (Authorization: Bearer <key>) with chat_completions and responses, x-api-key with messages. Omitted, it is that value; any other pairing is refused 422 provider_invalid.

headers.description: Static request headers sent on every request, chat_completions only, at most 16. Credential and transport headers (Authorization, x-api-key, api-key, Cookie, Host, Content-Type, Content-Length, Connection and the other hop-by-hop headers) are refused. Values must not contain ${...}. On PATCH the object replaces the current headers; {} or null clears them.

model.description: The model id the endpoint expects, as sent upstream (e.g. llama-3.3-70b). The model's spec is <model_prefix>/<model>.

context_window.description: Input context window in tokens. 0 or omitted means unknown, which also turns automatic compaction off for the model.

output_limit.description: Maximum output tokens. 0 or omitted means unknown.

reasoning.description: Marks a reasoning-capable model in the catalogue. Default false.

models.description: The provider's models, 1 to 500, each selectable as <model_prefix>/<model>. On PATCH the list replaces the current one.

get.description: Returns {status: "ok", provider: {...}}. provider carries the provider's metadata as on GET /api/v1/agent/providers (id, display_name, prefix, wire_format, model_count, custom), its readiness (status, as on GET /api/v1/agent/providers), its definition_rev (a short revision of its definition, to bind a key save with if_definition_rev) and its full catalogued model list. A provider added by the owner also carries custom_definition {base_url, wire_format, auth_scheme, header_names, managed}: header names only, never header values; base_url and auth_scheme appear only there. Each model in models carries spec, display_name, context_window, output_limit, reasoning, efforts, input_modalities and tool_call (each when known) and its prices, as in GET /api/v1/agent/models. Prices are the rates the agent prices usage at (the rates its cost figures and spend caps use), in US dollars per million tokens: cost_in (input), cost_out (output), cost_cache_read (input read from the prompt cache) and cost_cache_write (input written to the prompt cache). A price is omitted when it is unknown; 0 means free. cost_reported_by_provider true marks a model whose provider reports the cost of each reply itself: its prices are list prices, and its usage is charged at what the provider reports.

delete.description: Removes a custom provider and the API key stored for it. The key is removed first, then the definition. The reply says what happened to each: api_key is removed (its own stored key was removed), none (it had none) or kept_shared (a stored key another provider may read was kept); definition is removed. When a step fails the answer is 500 store_failed with details.api_key (failed: nothing was changed; removed: the key was removed but the definition is still listed) and details.definition kept; deleting again finishes the job, and a delete after full removal answers 404 not_found. Built-in providers cannot be removed (409 provider_builtin), nor can a custom provider defined in a project's providers file (409 provider_not_managed). An open session using one of its models becomes unconfigured: its next prompt fails with session_unconfigured naming the removed provider, and switching the session to another model (PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/model) recovers it. A session in a turn finishes that turn first. Agents and Jev settings that name one of its models keep the name and fail the same way until changed. Process-wide: a per-request realm, cwd, config-dir or computer header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

put.description: Stores a provider's API key in the agent's owner-only credential file inside the computer. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. SECURITY: the key is NEVER returned: the reply carries only the secret-free auth status, with api_key_prefix and the short fingerprint api_key_fingerprint. api_key_prefix is the first 10 bytes of a key longer than 12 bytes and `(short:N)` for a shorter key (N is its length in bytes). Sessions already running on this provider resolve their credential again before their next turn. With check:true the key is first tried against the provider: a refused key answers 422 api_key_refused and nothing is saved; an inconclusive try still saves and the reply says check:"inconclusive". With if_definition_rev (from GET /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}) the save is bound to that provider definition: a definition changed before or during the check answers 409 definition_changed and nothing is saved. 422 auth_method_unsupported for a provider that takes no API key (a passwordless one included).

schema.description: The verbatim reply {status, auth, check?:"valid"|"inconclusive", check_detail?}; check_detail is omitted for a valid check. auth is {provider, api_key_stored, api_key_prefix, api_key_fingerprint, oauth_stored, oauth_supported, default, no_auth_ready, ready, accounts}: api_key_fingerprint is 16 hexadecimal characters when a key is stored and "" otherwise; default is api_key, oauth, or "" for a passwordless provider; accounts is the secret-free OAuth account pool (see GET /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/accounts).

post.description: Begins an interactive OAuth login for a provider and returns {success, job_id, verification_uri, user_code?}. Drive the flow with GET /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/oauth/{job} (poll) and, for a manual/PKCE code, POST /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/oauth/{job}/code (submit): the same poll shape as POST /api/v1/agent/github/auth/login/poll, NOT a generic /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}/result fetch. Stop it with DELETE /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/oauth/{job}. One sign-in per provider may be pending at a time: another start (here or on POST /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/accounts) answers 409 oauth_in_progress with details.job_id naming the pending job, to continue or cancel. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried start answers the same job. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy; the daemon's own admin check may still refuse with 403 admin_unauthorized when the daemon was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. SECURITY: the job carries only the non-secret verification URL / user code: never a token. 422 oauth_unsupported when the provider has no OAuth flow.

get.description: Polls an in-flight OAuth login job: the provider analogue of POST /api/v1/agent/github/auth/login/poll. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. 404 job_not_found when the job is unknown/expired; 422 oauth_unsupported when the provider has no OAuth flow.

get.description: Lists the ledger rows over the scripts of the computer computer_id, from every realm that can own its scripts (its realms, Global and the request's realm; realms this login may not use are skipped). A row of the request's realm carries path, template ("" when the row predates template names), has_token, alias_id when an alias serves it, and state (active, provisioning, deleting or moving). A row of another realm is only {path, state: managed_elsewhere}. Every listed path is managed: change it only through these routes. The agent first connects to any of those realms it is not connected to yet, waiting up to 30 seconds; a realm that could not connect is not tried again for 30 seconds. A realm among them that has no data host yet gets one: when this agent's computer is in that realm (or the realm is Global) and it is not the agent's selected realm, the agent runs one election for it, waiting up to 20 seconds; a realm that got no host is not tried again for 30 seconds. When any of those ledgers cannot be read, a realm that did not connect or has no data host included, it is 503 ownership_unknown, never a shorter list. When they cannot be read because the agent has no Hoody login it is 409 not_logged_in, and 409 hoody_auth_expired when its login was refused; nothing is read then. The answer comes within 45 seconds. Cache-Control: no-store. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.description: Deletes the script at path on the computer computer_id only if its revision is still if_revision, under the computer's operation id op_id, then revokes its token and frees its ledger row. It always uses the computer's guarded delete and never an unguarded one: a computer that cannot guard the delete is 409 guard_unavailable with nothing deleted. A refusal by the computer (a changed revision, say) is kit_refused with the computer's status; nothing is revoked. A path owned by another realm is 409 managed_elsewhere and nothing is sent. When ownership cannot be read it is 503 ownership_unknown and nothing is sent; when the cause is the agent's own Hoody login it is 409 not_logged_in or hoody_auth_expired and nothing is sent. A result that is unknown is 503 outcome_unknown: send the same request (the same op_id included) with the same Idempotency-Key to settle it, or settle op_id on the computer. Offered only when GET /api/v1/agent/version reports script_instances_guarded available. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Retry key, required. 1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace. The same key with the same body returns the first answer with replayed true and does nothing again; the same key with another body is 422 idempotency_key_reused; while the first request still runs it is 409 in_progress. A key whose request was answered, or whose outcome is unknown, is remembered for 24 hours after its last answer or replay; a key whose request is still running is remembered until it ends. When many keys are held, the oldest answered keys are forgotten first; a key whose outcome is unknown is not. Every key is forgotten when the agent restarts. A retry of a remembered unknown outcome, and a request whose key is no longer remembered, are settled from the computer: the first answer comes back, with replayed true, only when the computer shows the request took effect. Otherwise the answer is 503 outcome_unknown, or a definite refusal such as 409 script_exists or path_reserved, because the computer now shows the path held by a script it cannot prove came from this request; that script may still be this request's own earlier effect. While too many keyed requests are unsettled, a new key is 429 idempotency_keys_exhausted and nothing is done.

post.summary: Make a script from a template.
post.description: Renders a kit template with vars and writes it to script_path on the computer computer_id, create-only: an occupied path is 409 script_exists and is never overwritten. A template that needs a minted token is 422 template_needs_token. caller_key (exactly 43 base64url characters), when given, becomes the script's one `// @token` line in its leading comment block (after the file's leading `//` lines, or as line 1 when it starts with anything else, within the first 30 lines; a `@token` line already there takes the key as its value); a script that starts with a `#!` line has no such place. When the line cannot be placed so that it parses it is 422 caller_key_unplaceable and nothing is written. The key is written into the script on the computer and is never returned in a response or logged. managed true means the script has a ledger row (GET /api/v1/agent/script-instances lists it); false means the realm's ledger predates managed scripts. A write whose result is unknown is 503 outcome_unknown: send the same request with the same Idempotency-Key to settle it. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Retry key, required. 1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace. The same key with the same body returns the first answer with replayed true and does nothing again; the same key with another body is 422 idempotency_key_reused; while the first request still runs it is 409 in_progress. A key whose request was answered, or whose outcome is unknown, is remembered for 24 hours after its last answer or replay; a key whose request is still running is remembered until it ends. When many keys are held, the oldest answered keys are forgotten first; a key whose outcome is unknown is not. Every key is forgotten when the agent restarts. A retry of a remembered unknown outcome, and a request whose key is no longer remembered, are settled from the computer: the first answer comes back, with replayed true, only when the computer shows the request took effect. Otherwise the answer is 503 outcome_unknown, or a definite refusal such as 409 script_exists or path_reserved, because the computer now shows the path held by a script it cannot prove came from this request; that script may still be this request's own earlier effect. While too many keyed requests are unsettled, a new key is 429 idempotency_keys_exhausted and nothing is done.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

get.summary: Read what a keyed session create became.
get.description: Reads what became of a session create (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions with an Idempotency-Key) whose answer was lost, by its key, without reserving, creating or waiting. {key} is the Idempotency-Key the request was sent with (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace; URL-encode it). A create is answered only in the realm it was made in. A create made with a config dir (body config_dir or X-Hoody-Config-Dir) keeps its key in that install: send the same X-Hoody-Config-Dir to read or retire it; without the header the default install is read. X-Hoody-Cwd and X-Hoody-Computer are 400 realm_scope_unsupported. 404 create_not_found proves nothing: the create may still be on its way, or its session may be gone; POST /api/v1/agent/session-create-keys/{key}/retire settles it. Cache-Control: no-store. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.summary: Retire a session create key no read found.
post.description: Settles a keyed session create whose answer was lost and that GET /api/v1/agent/session-create-keys/{key} did not find. {key} is the Idempotency-Key the request was sent with (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace; URL-encode it). A key no create reserved is retired durably: the answer is retired true, admitted "false", and a create sent with the key earlier and delivered later is refused 409 create_key_retired, also after the agent restarts; nothing is ever created with it. Retiring it again answers the same. A key a create already holds is never retired; the answer says what it holds: started (admitted "true", session_id when the session can be seen; none when it is gone), allocated with in_flight true (a create is running: ask again shortly; admitted "unknown"), or allocated with in_flight false (session_id and admitted "true" when the session was built, else admitted "unknown"). A key reserved in another realm answers admitted "unknown". A 503 is unknown: nothing is proven, retire again after Retry-After. The original create is never run. The request has no body. A create made with a config dir (body config_dir or X-Hoody-Config-Dir) keeps its key in that install: send the same X-Hoody-Config-Dir to read or retire it; without the header the default install is read. X-Hoody-Cwd and X-Hoody-Computer are 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.description: Lists persisted sessions for the requesting cwd (open + closed), with an Attached flag for live sessions. Realm: ?realm= (or the X-Hoody-Realm header) lists one realm: "global" (sessions not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id; ?realm=all lists every realm this login serves (query only, never the header). Omitted, the agent's current realm. Every row carries its realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm lists only that realm: any other value, all included, is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. Pagination: the x-pagination params ARE honored: pass ?page=N&limit=M to receive the page-th window of size M (page is 1-based; an invalid page/limit is 400 bad_request); omit limit (default_limit:0) to receive the full set. Order (order): started = newest started first (started_at, then id), which a turn does not change, so paging returns every session that exists for the whole walk once (one created or deleted during the walk can still shift a row); last_active = most recently active first (last_request_at, then id), where a session that becomes active during a walk moves to the front, so a later page can miss it or repeat a row. Omitted: started with limit, last_active without. meta.total is always the full pre-slice count; meta.page/meta.limit echo the window when limit is supplied.

items.description: The page of session summaries, in the order the order parameter names; each element is the daemon's session summary with the properties below.

id.description: Session id. The daemon mints a lowercase UUID; a stored record is listed with the id it holds.

model.description: The session's model (provider/model spec). Empty on a record that names none.

agent.description: The chat agent. Omitted on a record from before the field.

first_message.description: The first user message, the default label. Omitted when there is none.

name.description: The session's title: set by a person (PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}) or, when name_auto is true, generated by the agent after the first finished exchange (feature session_titles). Omitted when there is none.

name_auto.description: True when name was generated by the agent, not set by a person. Omitted when false.

started_at.description: When the session started (RFC3339). Omitted when unknown.

last_request_at.description: Last activity (RFC3339): stamped when each turn opens and closes, falling back to started_at. The list is sorted by it. Omitted when neither is known.

attached.description: True while the session is live in the daemon. Omitted when false.

attached_clients.description: Connections subscribed to a live session (this gateway counts as one). Omitted when zero.

tool_mode.description: The session's tool mode. Omitted when unset (standard).

tool_mode_locked.description: True once the session has started, which fixes tool_mode. Omitted when false.

dir_scope.description: The session's directory scope. Omitted when unset.

dir_scope_locked.description: True once the session has started, which fixes dir_scope. Omitted when false.

total_cost_usd.description: Lifetime spend in US dollars. Omitted when zero.

realm.description: The session's realm: "global" for a session not tied to a realm, else its 24-hex realm id. Pass it as X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) to reach the session by id.

kind.description: A daemon-owned resident session: todo_worker, todo_thread or todo_triage. Omitted for a user chat; residents are listed only with include_system=true.

todo_ref.description: The todo a todo_worker or todo_thread resident works on. Omitted otherwise.

backend_kind.description: acp on a session delegated to an external agent. Omitted for a normal session.

delegated_agent.description: The external agent a delegated session runs. Omitted otherwise.

auto_approving.description: A delegated session whose agent does not route every write and exec through the confirm gate. Omitted when false.

routes_writes.description: A delegated agent that routes its file writes through the confirm gate. Omitted when false.

routes_exec.description: A delegated agent that routes its command execution through the confirm gate. Omitted when false.

brutal.description: A delegated session whose agent's own tools are off, so Hoody runs every tool. Omitted when false.

delegated_model.description: The model a delegated session was configured with. Omitted when it uses the agent's default.

delegated_effort.description: The reasoning effort a delegated session was configured with. Omitted when it uses the agent's default.

effort.description: Reasoning level; only with type enabled, and only on models that take one.

thinking.description: Reasoning: {type: enabled|disabled, effort?: low|medium|high|xhigh|max}. effort is allowed only with enabled. Absent keeps the model's default reasoning.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, 0 to 2 (the model's own range applies; many models accept it only with thinking disabled).

max_tokens.description: Output cap, 1 to 1000000, clamped to the model's output limit.

strict.description: json_schema only: ask for strict schema adherence.

model_settings.description: The session's stored model settings. Omitted when it has none.

state.description: The session's run state, as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state reports it: running while a turn runs or holds this gateway's single-writer slot, parked while the session's own turn waits on a gate, closed once this gateway committed to closing it, else idle (always idle for a session that is not live).

bot_id.description: The Bot's id within its realm.

realm.description: The Bot's realm: global or a realm id.

origin.description: Present on a session a Bot opened, its own or a delegate: which Bot, and for a delegate the Bot's reference for the work it handed over. A fork does not carry it. Omitted on every other session.

post.summary: Create, fork, or attach a session.
post.description: Opens a new agent session (or forks/attaches an existing one), freezing realm/computer/cwd/backend at start (session-frozen scope). tool_mode and dir_scope are initial values for a new session: its first turn may carry its own, which replace them, and that first turn locks both. A fork takes its parent's values instead (locked once it copies history). An attach keeps the session's own values and ignores the body's, except when it reloads a saved session that never started. BYOA: backend:"acp" + delegated_agent delegate the session to an external CLI agent; the daemon enforces the per-agent enable gate (the local sandbox is mandatory; there is no trust gate). Per-agent environment values are used only when Claude Code runs on this agent's own computer. A session bound to another computer uses Claude Code's credentials there, not that computer's agent secret store. Any effective per-agent environment values on the driving agent (secret or non-secret) cause a remote launch to be refused, even if the target is already authenticated. Clear all such values on the driving agent before using remote sessions; clearing a credential can prevent local sessions from authenticating. POST /sessions may return 201 before this launch check; the refusal is reported on the first turn with delegated_launch_failed. Send a standard Idempotency-Key header to make the create RETRY-SAFE: a retry with the same key re-joins the SAME session (replayed:true) instead of creating a second one. A session that has never been prompted is a draft and is not saved: once no client has been attached to it for 5 minutes it is closed and discarded, and later calls by its id answer 404. Send the first prompt, or keep a stream or an attachment lease open, to keep it. A session with at least one turn is saved and can be re-attached by id after it is closed. For a keyed create, every start refusal except admission_write_failed, session_terminating and restriction_unknown consumes the key: create again with a new Idempotency-Key. After restriction_unknown, resend the same key first; if it answers 409 creation_interrupted, list sessions to find the session an earlier send may have created before using a new key.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Opaque retry key (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace). A retry with the same key after the first try started a session re-joins that session (replayed true); a first try that never started one answers 409 creation_interrupted and the key cannot create again, so use a new key. The same key with a different request body is 422.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm

On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. schema.description: The opened session.

session_id.description: The session id.

started.description: The daemon's session_started acknowledgement: the frozen binding (realm_selector, computer_id, cwd, tool_mode, dir_scope, backend), the effective approval policy, and model_settings: the session's stored model settings (the create request, merged over the parent's on a fork), absent when it has none. tool_ceiling is "script-writer" or "github-installer" on a session whose tools are fixed to that agent's ceiling, absent otherwise.

The capability (lease) is returned once, here; it never rides a stream frame, and a later attach is never handed it.

503.description: Service unavailable: this request created nothing, and it is safe to retry. After admission_write_failed or session_terminating, retry with the same Idempotency-Key. After policy_commit_failed the key was already reserved: a keyed create must use a NEW Idempotency-Key (the old one answers 409 creation_interrupted). After restriction_unknown, retry once the restriction is readable, resending the SAME Idempotency-Key first: if an earlier send with this key created the session, the same key re-joins it; if it answers 409 creation_interrupted, the earlier send may still have created the session: list sessions to find it before creating with a NEW Idempotency-Key. On a gateway with no pinned realm, the realm a create or fork names is checked before anything is reserved: a service_unavailable from that check leaves the key unused, so the same key may be retried.

x-error-codes.resolution: Retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key: once the key's first create finishes, the retry re-joins its session if it started, or answers 409 creation_interrupted if it was never acknowledged: that create may still have made the session, so list sessions to find it before creating with a NEW Idempotency-Key. requestBody.description: Session start binding (all optional; header scope augments the body, body wins). backend:"acp" requires delegated_agent.

realm.description: Realm selector to scope the session (frozen at start): global or a realm id. A realm the agent's login does not serve is 404 not_found.

computer.description: Computer id/selector to run tools on (frozen at start).

cwd.description: Working directory for the session (frozen at start).

model.description: Model for this session. On a fresh create/fork it OVERRIDES the chat agent's pinned model for this session only (it is NOT written to the agent; use PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/model to change it and rewrite the model line of the agent file that sources it, which then applies to later sessions that use that file). Omit it to use the agent's pinned model (or your default). A model with no known provider prefix, or a fusion composite that does not exist, is refused 422 unknown_model and no session is created (GET /api/v1/agent/models lists the choices); a speech model is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.reason speech_model. Rejected (400) together with attach (a resumed session keeps its model). With backend:"acp", and on a fork of a Claude Code session (a fork keeps Claude Code: backend takes only "acp" or nothing, and "llm" is 400 bad_request), it is the Claude Code model, as PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/model takes it (a Claude alias such as opus, sonnet or haiku, or a Claude model id, with or without the anthropic/ prefix), and needs no provider credential; on such a fork it replaces the model the fork would inherit, and omitting it keeps the parent's. Another model is refused 422 model_unavailable with details.reason not_claude on a create, and 422 unknown_model on such a fork.

agent.description: Initial chat-agent name. An agent that does not exist in the session's realm (or whose definition cannot be parsed) is refused 422 unknown_chat_agent and no session is created; a keyed create must then retry with a new Idempotency-Key. Rejected (400) together with fork (a fork inherits its parent's chat agent) or attach (a resumed session keeps its agent). The bot agent is refused 400 bad_request: it runs only inside a Bot (POST /api/v1/agent/bots). A fork of a Bot's session continues on the default chat agent. The script-writer agent freezes the script-writer tool ceiling on the session (started.tool_ceiling): it can run only hoody_exec_validate, hoody_exec_routes and hoody_exec_monitor, and its agent cannot be changed later; it is refused 400 bad_request together with backend acp, frame_tools or outcome_claims. A fork of a script-writer session keeps the agent and the ceiling. The github-installer agent (capability github_installer) works the same way with its own ceiling (started.tool_ceiling "github-installer"): it can run only bash, bash_job_wait, read_file, glob_files, grep, write_file, edit_file, ask_question_to_user, hoody_daemon_programs and hoody_daemon_control; it is refused 400 bad_request on the same options; and a Bot cannot dispatch a delegate onto it.

tool_mode.description: Initial tool mode for a new session: standard (the default) or orchestrator. A tool_mode its first turn carries replaces it; that first turn then fixes the mode for the session's lifetime (tool_mode_locked). A fork takes its parent's mode instead, and an attach keeps the session's own (see the operation description). Any other value is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode.

dir_scope.description: Initial directory-access scope for a new session: home or full. A dir_scope its first turn carries replaces it; that first turn then fixes the scope for the session's lifetime (dir_scope_locked). A fork takes its parent's scope instead, and an attach keeps the session's own (see the operation description). Any other value is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope.

attach.description: Attach to an existing session instead of creating one; the value is that session's id.

fork.description: Fork from an existing session; the value is that session's id. The source must be LIVE in the daemon: fork copies its in-memory state and does not load a saved record the way attach does. An unknown id, a session in another realm, or one that has ended (closed, reaped or lost to a restart) is refused 404 not_found and no session is created; attach the ended session first to reload it, then fork it.

fork_turn_idx.description: With fork: the 0-based turn the fork copies the parent's conversation through (0 = the first turn only). Omitted: through the parent's last turn, the whole conversation. A negative index, or one the parent does not have, is refused 400 bad_request and no session is created.

backend.description: Session backend: "" (Hoody LLM) or "acp" (BYOA delegated agent). Any other value, "llm" included, is 400 bad_request.

follow_realm_backend.description: true runs this new session on the realm's default delegated agent (GET /api/v1/agent/acp/default): Claude Code when it is claude, Hoody models when it is empty. The default is read once, when the create is admitted, and the session keeps that backend; a retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same session even if the default changed in between. When the default names an agent that cannot start here the create is refused 409 delegated_agent_unavailable (details.reason) and does not fall back to Hoody models. Refused 400 bad_request (details.field names the field) together with backend, model, agent, model_settings, prompt_blocks, helper_gates:true, outcome_claims:true, frame_tools:true, fork or attach. Defaults to false: without it, omitting backend is a Hoody models session, as always.

headless.description: Start the session in headless posture.

mode.description: The approval mode to assert: default (the session's ordinary policy) or always (each gated side-effecting call waits for an explicit decision from the approver; read-only calls are not gated). An empty string means default, exactly like omitting the property; the value is compared after surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

locked.description: Lock the policy so later changes (PUT /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approval, turning YOLO on with PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/yolo) are refused. Turning YOLO off stays allowed.

approval.description: Approval policy assertion. On a create/fork it SETS the session's policy; on an attach it is CHECKED against the live session (a session that cannot honour it is 409 approval_policy_unsatisfiable, and it is closed for this caller). Asserting "always" also hands this caller the approver lease when none is live (approver_lease in the response, returned once).

realm.description: The realm selector the session must have resolved to.

computer.description: The computer id the session must have resolved to.

cwd.description: The working directory the session must have resolved to.

backend.description: The backend the session must be running on: llm (Hoody LLM) or acp (BYOA delegated agent). An empty string leaves this dimension unasserted, exactly like omitting the property.

expected_binding.description: Fail-closed binding assertion: only the dimensions given are compared with the binding the session actually resolved to; a contradiction is 409 binding_mismatch (details name each mismatch) and the session is closed.

contract.description: The task-completion contract (finish the task, verify results, say what remains). Callers that read a session's outcome rely on it; turn it off only when you handle outcome reporting yourself.

transcripts.description: Where this realm's other session transcripts are stored.

frequent_files.description: The list of files the agent opens most often in this project.

memory.description: Project memory recalled for this session.

agent_instructions.description: The user's global instructions for every agent.

team_rules.description: The team rules (guidance and playbook rules from POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules) that cover the agent.

workflows.description: The catalogue of available workflows and the workflow hint.

fleet_notice.description: The notice that fleet tools are unavailable in this session.

environment.description: The line with today's date (and, for a local session whose agent has tools, the OS and the git branch) on a native turn's message, sent again only when it changes.

prompt_blocks.description: Switches for the optional system-prompt blocks, for a lean session: false turns a block off for this session. Switches only turn blocks off: true undoes a false in the agent's own prompt_blocks frontmatter, but never turns on a block the box settings turned off. An omitted key keeps the block. Frozen at create and kept on resume; a fork inherits its parent's switches and applies its own on top. An unknown key is 400; rejected (400) together with attach.

effort.description: Reasoning level; only with type enabled, and only on models that take one.

thinking.description: Reasoning: {type: enabled|disabled, effort?: low|medium|high|xhigh|max}. effort is allowed only with enabled. Absent keeps the model's default reasoning.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, 0 to 2 (the model's own range applies; many models accept it only with thinking disabled).

max_tokens.description: Output cap, 1 to 1000000, clamped to the model's output limit.

schema.description: json_schema only: the JSON Schema the reply must follow.

strict.description: json_schema only: ask for strict schema adherence.

response_format.description: {type: json_object}, or {type: json_schema, schema: {...}, name?, strict?}. name matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ and defaults to "response".

model_settings.description: Per-turn model settings for this session, the same object as the completion route's settings: thinking, temperature, max_tokens, response_format. Per field they win over the chat agent's own frontmatter thinking, temperature and response_format; an omitted field keeps the agent's value. Every turn applies them leniently: a setting the model or its adapter cannot take is left out of that request and logged, never an error, and they are kept across a model or agent switch. Frozen at create and kept on resume; a fork inherits its parent's settings and applies its own on top. Unknown or invalid members are 400 (details.field names the path); rejected (400) together with attach. A delegated (acp, Claude Code) session takes thinking (with its effort) and max_tokens as Claude Code launch options for its whole life; temperature and response_format are refused 400 unsupported_setting, with backend acp and on a fork of a delegated session that names no backend. Subagents and workflow steps do not inherit them.

helper_gates.description: true parks a spawn_agent helper's approvals (a hook asking to confirm) and questions as gates on this session instead of failing them. Each is listed under pending_helper_gates and answered by its gate_id on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer, beside the lead's own gate. Fixed when the session starts: set it on the create, or on an attach that reopens a closed session (it is not saved, so that attach must send it again). On an attach to a live session, true for a session started without it is refused 400 helper_gates_unavailable; false or omitted changes nothing. Defaults to false.

outcome_claims.description: true gives the model the report_outcome tool and one prompt line asking it to call the tool last, alone, to say what it did and cite the tool calls that show it. A response whose every tool call is an accepted report_outcome ends the turn through the same end-of-turn checks as a normal finish (pending task notices, todo prompts, Stop hooks), and any of them can continue it; a later report replaces the earlier one. The turn then sends event.outcome_claims just before event.agent_done: the model's claims and, for each cited call, whether it is one of this turn's own calls and what it returned. The claims are the model's words; nothing says they are true. /replay keeps the report after the tool_result of its call. Once a report_outcome call has run, its input in the conversation history keeps only a report_ref (a refused call keeps an empty input), so the claims are not sent to the model again, carried into a fork or captured into memory; the report itself is kept beside the history. On backend acp the tool is on the agent's Hoody tool plane, and only the calls Hoody ran can be cited as the turn's own. There a report-only response does not end the turn at once: the agent makes one more model request, and Hoody runs no further tool call unless an end-of-turn check (a Stop hook, a todo prompt) continues the turn, whose new request then runs its tool calls as usual. The agent also keeps the claims in its own conversation, so they can reach its model again; Hoody's history still keeps only the report_ref. Fixed when the session starts, like helper_gates; on an attach to a live session, true for a session started without it is refused 400 outcome_claims_unavailable. Defaults to false.

frame_tools.description: true gives the model the request_view tool and one prompt line asking it to use the tool when the user asks for a View: a live page of their data, such as a table of their computers. Set it only from a Frame that answers it. A call parks as a question gate (event.user_question with category frame_request and frame_request {kind: view, request, id}, listed as pending_gate); the Frame makes the View and answers on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer with its status JSON {v: 1, status: published, awaiting_approval, dismissed, stopped, gap, failed or busy, view?, issues, notes} as answer, which the tool returns to the model. Without an answer within 15 minutes the tool returns {status: no_frame}. Never shown to a headless, orchestrator or resident session (a delegated Claude Code session is shown it and its agent calls it like any other tool); an automated turn (a loop, TODO or background-task fire) is refused it. Fixed when the session starts, like helper_gates; on an attach to a live session, true for a session started without it is refused 400 frame_tools_unavailable. Defaults to false.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Returns the distinct working directories across all persisted sessions, most-recent first, and `home`, the folder a new session starts in when it names no cwd. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm whose sessions are read ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: The distinct working directories, under a single key the gateway adds. Not a daemon reply.

cwds.description: Distinct working directories, empty when there are none.

home.description: The folder a new session starts in when POST /api/v1/agent/sessions names no cwd and no computer: the agent's own working folder, the same one the start resolves, for every realm. Read-only. A session bound to another computer starts in that computer's default folder instead, which this route does not report. Absent when the agent cannot read its working folder.

x-error-codes.resolution: Omit the header. A route without a realm dimension refuses every realm header, the pinned realm included; on a route that takes a realm, an agent pinned to one realm accepts only that realm.
