schema.description: The session read, assembled by the gateway: the daemon reply is re-keyed, so these are not the daemon action's own fields.

id.description: Session id. The daemon mints a lowercase UUID; a stored record is listed with the id it holds.

model.description: The session's model (provider/model spec). Empty on a record that names none.

agent.description: The chat agent. Omitted on a record from before the field.

first_message.description: The first user message, the default label. Omitted when there is none.

name.description: The session's title: set by a person (PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}) or, when name_auto is true, generated by the agent after the first finished exchange (feature session_titles). Omitted when there is none.

name_auto.description: True when name was generated by the agent, not set by a person. Omitted when false.

started_at.description: When the session started (RFC3339). Omitted when unknown.

last_request_at.description: Last activity (RFC3339): stamped when each turn opens and closes, falling back to started_at. The list is sorted by it. Omitted when neither is known.

attached.description: True while the session is live in the daemon. Omitted when false.

attached_clients.description: Connections subscribed to a live session (this gateway counts as one). Omitted when zero.

tool_mode.description: The session's tool mode. Omitted when unset (standard).

tool_mode_locked.description: True once the session has started, which fixes tool_mode. Omitted when false.

dir_scope.description: The session's directory scope. Omitted when unset.

dir_scope_locked.description: True once the session has started, which fixes dir_scope. Omitted when false.

total_cost_usd.description: Lifetime spend in US dollars. Omitted when zero.

realm_selector.description: The session's frozen realm: "global" (also for a record from before the field, or with an unreadable value) or a 24-hex realm id.

realm.description: The session's realm: "global" for a session not tied to a realm, else its 24-hex realm id. Pass it as X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) to reach the session by id.

computer_id.description: The computer the session is bound to. Omitted for a local session.

kind.description: A daemon-owned resident session: todo_worker, todo_thread or todo_triage. Omitted for a user chat; residents are listed only with include_system=true.

todo_ref.description: The todo a todo_worker or todo_thread resident works on. Omitted otherwise.

backend_kind.description: acp on a session delegated to an external agent. Omitted for a normal session.

delegated_agent.description: The external agent a delegated session runs. Omitted otherwise.

auto_approving.description: A delegated session whose agent does not route every write and exec through the confirm gate. Omitted when false.

routes_writes.description: A delegated agent that routes its file writes through the confirm gate. Omitted when false.

routes_exec.description: A delegated agent that routes its command execution through the confirm gate. Omitted when false.

brutal.description: A delegated session whose agent's own tools are off, so Hoody runs every tool. Omitted when false.

delegated_model.description: The model a delegated session was configured with. Omitted when it uses the agent's default.

delegated_effort.description: The reasoning effort a delegated session was configured with. Omitted when it uses the agent's default.

effort.description: Reasoning level; only with type enabled, and only on models that take one.

thinking.description: Reasoning: {type: enabled|disabled, effort?: low|medium|high|xhigh|max}. effort is allowed only with enabled. Absent keeps the model's default reasoning.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, 0 to 2 (the model's own range applies; many models accept it only with thinking disabled).

max_tokens.description: Output cap, 1 to 1000000, clamped to the model's output limit.

schema.description: json_schema only: the JSON Schema the reply must follow.

strict.description: json_schema only: ask for strict schema adherence.

response_format.description: {type: json_object}, or {type: json_schema, schema: {...}, name?, strict?}. name matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ and defaults to "response".

model_settings.description: The session's stored model settings. Omitted when it has none.

state.description: The session's run state, as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state reports it: running while a turn runs or holds this gateway's single-writer slot, parked while the session's own turn waits on a gate, closed once this gateway committed to closing it, else idle (always idle for a session that is not live).

pending_gate.description: True while an approval or question waits for a person on the session: the session's own (state parked) or one of its helpers' (state unchanged). A Bot tool's request, which the Bot runtime answers itself, parks the session without setting it. GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state returns the gate. Omitted when false.

kind.description: What opened the session.

bot_id.description: The Bot's id within its realm.

realm.description: The Bot's realm: global or a realm id.

ref.description: The Bot's reference for the work it handed to this session. Omitted on the Bot's own session.

origin.description: Present on a session a Bot opened, its own or a delegate: which Bot, and for a delegate the Bot's reference for the work it handed over. A fork does not carry it. Omitted on every other session.

live.description: Only on a live session that has not been persisted yet: true.

started.description: Only on a live session that has not been persisted yet: false, no turn has been dispatched. Not the top-level started object.

effort.description: Only on a live session: the reasoning-effort override set with PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/effort. Absent while the model's default applies. Not kept across a daemon restart, and cleared by a model switch. On a Claude Code (delegated) session it is the effort Claude Code runs with: the PATCH value, else the configured default, with an explicit model_settings thinking effort winning; it is kept with the session across a restart and a model switch, and absent while Claude Code's own default applies.

verbosity.description: Only on a live session: the response-verbosity level (PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/verbosity). A restart starts from the ui.verbosity default.

command_capability.description: How soon the session reads a new message sent while it works. next_step: before its next model request. turn_end: when its current turn ends (a Claude Code session, a fusion model, while a workflow run holds the session, or while it runs a turn started by a loop or a finished background task). unsupported: a headless session, which takes no messages after it starts.

kind.description: model: the model is answering or about to be asked. tool: a tool call or a workflow run is running. gate: waiting for an approval or an answer. idle: no work is running.

tool.description: When kind is tool: the running tool call that started last, or run_workflow while a workflow run holds the session and no other call is running. Omitted otherwise.

since.description: When the session entered this step (RFC 3339). For a session that is not live, its last activity.

current_step.description: What the session is doing now, coarsely, and since when.

tokens.description: The size of the session's last prompt in tokens. 0 when unknown (no turn yet, or after a clear).

window.description: The context window the tokens are measured against, in tokens: the model's window, or for a Claude Code session the window Claude Code reports. 0 when unknown.

estimated.description: True when tokens is an estimate made by a compaction rather than a size the model provider reported; the next model request replaces it with a reported size.

context.description: How full the session's context is: the same reading the agent's own context meter shows.

after_compaction.description: The session's after-compaction message (PUT /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/after-compaction). Omitted when none is set.

session.description: The session summary: the GET /api/v1/agent/sessions row, including model_settings (the session's stored model settings; absent when it has none). A live session that has not dispatched a turn is not listed yet, so its summary is built from its start binding: it carries live and started, and no model. A live session also carries its current effort and verbosity. Every session carries command_capability, current_step and context, after_compaction when one is set, and origin when a Bot opened it.

attached.description: Whether the session is attached to this gateway right now.

started.description: The session's start parameters, for an attached session, including model_settings when the session has any and tool_ceiling when its tools are fixed to a ceiling.

incarnation.description: The namespace of every sequence number and gate id this attachment mints. Absent when the session is not attached.

id.description: The answerable gate id. Echo it verbatim as gate_id on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer. Scoped to the session incarnation, so an id from before a re-attach never matches.

generation.description: The hub gate generation. It restarts on re-attach, so it is not an identity on its own: send id.

tool_name.description: The tool awaiting a decision (confirm gates). Omitted when empty.

gate_cause.description: Why the gate parked, for example static_stakes, dir_access, hook_ask or approval_policy (confirm gates). Omitted when the agent did not say.

risk.description: The agent's coarse risk label for the call (confirm gates), as event.confirm_request's risk. Omitted when the agent did not say.

human_only.description: true when only a person may answer. Always present.

provenance.description: What produced the gate, when the agent says. Omitted otherwise.

helper_id.description: A helper's gate: the helper that parked it. Omitted for the session's own gate.

parent_tool_call_id.description: A helper's gate: the tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started the helper. Omitted for the session's own gate.

task_id.description: A background helper's gate: its task (equal to helper_id). Omitted otherwise.

params.description: Confirm gates: the parameters of the call awaiting the decision. Omitted on other gates or when the call has none.

lease_required.description: Confirm gates: true when the decision must carry the approver lease (X-Hoody-Approver-Lease). Omitted on other gates.

lease_generation.description: Confirm gates: the approver-lease generation to send as lease_generation on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm. Omitted when the session has no lease. Not the gate generation: send generation for that.

pending_gate.description: Present only while a gate is parked: the id, generation and type to echo on the confirm or answer, what is being asked and, on a confirm gate, the call's params and the lease the decision needs.

id.description: The answerable gate id. Echo it verbatim as gate_id on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer. Scoped to the session incarnation, so an id from before a re-attach never matches.

generation.description: The hub gate generation. It restarts on re-attach, so it is not an identity on its own: send id.

tool_name.description: The tool awaiting a decision (confirm gates). Omitted when empty.

gate_cause.description: Why the gate parked, for example static_stakes, dir_access, hook_ask or approval_policy (confirm gates). Omitted when the agent did not say.

risk.description: The agent's coarse risk label for the call (confirm gates), as event.confirm_request's risk. Omitted when the agent did not say.

human_only.description: true when only a person may answer. Always present.

provenance.description: What produced the gate, when the agent says. Omitted otherwise.

helper_id.description: A helper's gate: the helper that parked it. Omitted for the session's own gate.

parent_tool_call_id.description: A helper's gate: the tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started the helper. Omitted for the session's own gate.

pending_helper_gates.description: Present only on a helper_gates session while a helper has a gate parked: one entry per gate, oldest first, each with the id, generation and type to echo plus helper_id, parent_tool_call_id and, for a background helper, task_id. patch.description: Sets the session's title, or clears it back to the automatic title with name:"". A title set here is never replaced by a generated one. Works on a live session (renamed in place; attached clients receive event.session_renamed) and on a closed one (its persisted record is rewritten where it lies; a closed session stays closed). Clearing asks for a new automatic title: when the session_titles feature is on, a live session that has a finished exchange gets one generated in the background (event.session_renamed with name_auto true; nothing changes if it cannot be made), a closed one after its next finished turn. The daemon sanitizes the title (control characters removed, surrounding whitespace trimmed, secret-shaped tokens redacted, capped at 120 characters) and returns the value it stored. A live session that has not run a turn yet keeps the title in memory and persists it with its first turn. `name` is required: an absent field is a 400, never a silent clear. A session in another realm, owned by another account, managed by the agent itself, or simply unknown is the same plain 404. CONFIG-DIR: a closed session's record is resolved under X-Hoody-Config-Dir, the same asymmetry as DELETE /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404. A computer header is rejected.

delete.description: Closes the live session connection (the daemon cancels the session). ?hard=true also removes the persisted record; a live session that was never prompted has no record, so closing it removes it and the hard delete answers 200 (when the request resolves the store the session was opened in: the same X-Hoody-Config-Dir as its create config_dir). A session CREATED with a body config_dir override (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions config_dir) is persisted under THAT override's sessions dir, so to hard-delete it you MUST send the SAME directory as X-Hoody-Config-Dir; otherwise the delete resolves the home sessions dir, finds nothing, and returns 404 (the record is undeletable via the bare call).

put.description: Sets the session's after-compaction message: text the agent adds back to the conversation as a user message right after the summary of every compaction (automatic, manual, and the one that recovers from a context overflow), so it is in place before the next model request. Use it for standing instructions such as an identity or ground rules that a summary could lose. The text is stored and re-added byte for byte, never in the system prompt. An empty or whitespace-only text removes the message. At most 16 KiB. The message is saved with the session, kept across restarts and inherited by a fork; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state show it as after_compaction. On a Claude Code session, where Claude Code does the compacting, the message is sent to Claude Code with the first message after each compaction. A live session only: a closed one answers 404 not_found.

requestBody.description: Question-gate answer. Send answer (or text) for a free-form reply, or answers (a map) for a structured multi-field question. A body with no answer, no text and no answers is 400 bad_request: nothing is sent and the question stays parked. gate_id/generation are echoes of the parked gate (a mismatch is 409).

gate_id.description: Echo of the parked gate id, as published on the frame that parked it (gate.id), by GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} (pending_gate.id) and in 409 details. Valid only for the session in the path. Optional for compatibility, but an answer without it applies to whatever gate is parked when it arrives: a client binding an answer to a gate the user saw must send it. Ids are unique per session incarnation, so an id from before a re-attach never matches (stale/mismatch → 409).

generation.description: Optional echo of the parked gate generation. It restarts when the session is re-attached, so it is not an identity on its own: send gate_id.

answer.description: Free-form answer text. When it is absent or blank, text is used in its place. It may be empty when text or answers carries the answer. For a frame_request of kind view, send a JSON-encoded object with v: 1 and status: published, awaiting_approval, dismissed, stopped, gap, failed or busy. issues and notes are arrays of objects with string code and message fields, never arrays of strings; use [] when empty. The optional view object uses id (a non-empty string), title (string) and placed (boolean). The tool keeps at most five entries per array and truncates each string to 400 Unicode code points. An unreadable answer becomes status failed with issue code answer_unrecognized in event.tool_result. HTTP 200 with resolved.outcome answered acknowledges consumption of the answer, not successful parsing or View creation.

text.description: Answer text used when answer is absent or blank. For a workflow question with options, answer names the option and text is that option's input (has_user_input); otherwise text is ignored when answer is set.

answers.description: Structured per-field answers for a multi-field question.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Propose answers for a parked question (helper model).
post.description: Runs a one-shot helper-model call that proposes answers for the parked question (event.question_suggestion). The real answer still travels via /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer: the daemon never answers itself. 409 no_pending_gate when no question is parked. When the session's realm is not usable under the login the assist is refused (403 realm_not_allowed, 503 restriction_unknown); a refusal that arrives after the 202 fails the job with that error_code.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm

On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. get.description: Returns the session's effective approval policy (mode default|always, the monotonic lock, the revision), the waiver posture (yolo, auto_write, auto_dir_access, backend_auto_approving), the session permission rules, and the approver lease state. put.summary: Set a session's approval mode and lock.
put.description: Changes the session's approval mode ("default" | "always") and/or its lock under an optional If-Match (the ETag from GET; * or absent is unconditional). "always" makes every side-effecting Hoody-visible invocation require one explicit decision naming its gate (Under always every side-effecting invocation waits for a decision (bash, writes/deletes, non-GET web_fetch, fleet actions, non-read-only MCP tools, image generation and notifications), while memory_save, the todo mutators (create/update/claim/finish_todo, append_todo_note, triage_todos) and propose_cron_entry stay ungated as agent-internal state and drafts; reads, grep/glob and the task tools are never gated. Nested executors that cannot park are refused). Switching into "always" also arms the approver lease requirement, and this call mints no lease (the answer shows lease.held false): every later decision must present a lease acquired with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approver-lease and name the exact gate_id and its generation, or it is refused (409 approver_lease_required; 400 bad_request) and the gate stays parked. A create or attach that asserts "always" is handed a lease. "locked" freezes the mode and every waiver alias (YOLO, allow rules, session-scoped remembered approvals, auto-reply arming) for the session's lifetime: it is monotonic and never unlocked. Under "always", beyond the per-invocation decision: executors that cannot park a decision are refused, namely subagents, workflow runs and resumes (approval_policy_unsatisfiable, also as the turn's event.error and agent_done error_code when reached through the session), the orchestrator, foreign CLIs, run_todo and test_hook; the user's configured hook commands are SKIPPED, each disclosed as event.hook_run {decision:"skipped"} and as an agent_done notice (code hook_skipped_by_policy); configured MCP servers are NOT started (event.error approval_policy_unsatisfiable at session start); stdin to a background bash process is refused. OUTSIDE any session's policy, by design: sessionless headless runs, sessionless tool runs and management operations. Every MACHINE-confirmed execution path (a composite (fusion) model's winner-commit run in writes mode, subagents, workflow tool steps, auto-reply) has its side-effecting invocations REFUSED under "always" (error_code approval_policy_unsatisfiable, disclosed as the turn notice machine_execution_refused_by_policy naming the tool): a fusion model cannot commit writes under "always"; reads still pass. ADMISSION LEDGER: for a turn sent through this API, its admission and its dispatch are each recorded durably before the turn runs; when either cannot be recorded the turn does not run (admission_write_failed). A turn's terminal outcome is recorded before event.agent_done is sent, with two exceptions: when that record cannot be written, agent_done still arrives and carries error_code ledger_write_failed, and a receipt read later will not show the outcome; and a turn cut off by the agent shutting down is left unfinished, so after a restart its receipt reports it interrupted (effects_may_have_occurred:true even without recorded tool calls). Records of turns sent with an Idempotency-Key or a client turn id are kept for the session's whole lifetime (they deduplicate retries), while unkeyed records are pruned past the newest 200, so recording a transition takes longer as a session's keyed turns accumulate; the ledger is deleted with the session. An omitted field keeps its current value. A stale If-Match is 412 (the response ETag carries the current revision); a locked policy, including an unlock attempt or weakening an inherited lock, is 409 approval_policy_locked; an unknown mode, or "always" on a delegated session whose agent runs its own tools, is 409 approval_policy_unsatisfiable; a busy session (a turn in flight, a parked confirm OR question, queued turns, background children or running interactive shells) is 409 session_busy (the policy only changes at quiescence); a failed durable commit is 503 policy_commit_failed (nothing acknowledged). Emits event.approval_policy_changed to every attached client.

post.summary: Acquire the right to answer this session's gates.
post.description: Acquires the session's approver lease: a random capability bound to the session, the daemon execution epoch, this holder and a generation, with a visible expiry. holder is REQUIRED: an opaque per-caller id (it is what the event.gate_resolved stream event reports as the answerer). It is never a credential. On an "always" session (from its switch to "always", or from the first lease minted) EVERY decision (/api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm, a WS confirm frame, a gated tool-run confirmation) must present the CURRENT capability (X-Hoody-Approver-Lease over HTTP, approver_token in a WS confirm frame); the daemon verifies it at decision consumption, so a peer, a fenced holder or a capability minted for another session cannot resolve the gate (409 approver_lease_invalid; none presented is 409 approver_lease_required). A verified capability is accepted whatever lease generation the gate was parked under, but the decision itself still names the gate's gate_id and generation (400 bad_request without them); while a gate is parked a lease change is broadcast as event.decision_requirements {gate_id, generation, lease_required}. EXPIRY FAILS CLOSED: an expired lease keeps the requirement (410 approver_lease_expired) until a holder acquires again. Expiry never lets anyone answer. TAKEOVER NEEDS PROOF: while a lease is live, acquire is 409 approver_lease_held unless the request presents the current capability (X-Hoody-Approver-Lease or body.lease); a capability that is not the current one is 409 approver_lease_invalid. On its own, replace:true never authorises, and holder strings are never compared. A create or attach that asserts "always" is handed a lease only when none is live (approver_lease_error: approver_lease_held otherwise; an assertion never evicts). Leases are in-memory: after a daemon restart GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approval reports held:false and the client acquires again. The capability is returned once, here.

post.summary: Hold a live session (and its parked gate) alive.
post.description: Acquires a renewable attachment lease that keeps the live session (a parked approval gate especially) from being reaped by the 5-minute idle sweep while no stream is attached, so a client that dispatched a turn and disconnected can reconnect and still answer the gate. Returns {lease_id, expires_at}; renew with PATCH before it expires, release with DELETE. The acquire is decided atomically against the reaper: a session whose close is already committed answers 404. An attachment lease only keeps the session alive; the APPROVER lease is a separate resource with its own expiry (renew it with PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approver-lease; an expired approver lease fails closed). Leases are in-memory: a daemon/gateway restart ends them (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state then shows the session's real state) and the client re-acquires.

post.summary: Stop one of a session's background shells.
post.description: Stops one background shell the path session started. outcome stopped: the job is no longer running (already_ended true when it had ended before this stop). failed: the job is still running (reason still_running), or its record cannot be acted on safely so nothing was signalled (reason unsafe_record). unknown: the stop's result could not be confirmed (reason unconfirmed: no readable answer, or the job's main process on its computer is gone without having recorded an exit, so other processes it started may still run; or end_not_seen when the job did not exit within a few seconds of the signal); the job may or may not still be running, so list the jobs to read it back. An Idempotency-Key header is required: a retry with the same key answers the first call's outcome (duplicate true) and never stops anything again; the same key for another job is 422. Keys are remembered for 24 hours (and while their stop runs), until the agent restarts; a retry after a restart stops again, which for an ended job answers stopped with already_ended. A key whose job does not exist is not remembered. When too many recent stops are remembered, a new key is refused 503 service_unavailable with Retry-After and nothing is stopped. The session must be open.

post.summary: Cancel the active turn (Esc), or one named turn.
post.description: With turn_id (JSON body or ?turn_id=): cancels ONLY that turn: the turn_id returned when it was dispatched (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/messages, prompt:sync, prompt:stream's X-Hoody-Turn-Id header, a workflow run). It is cancelled if it is running, the moment it starts if it is still queued, and not at all if it already ended, so a late Stop can never stop a newer turn, including one started by another client on the same session. Only that turn's job is marked cancel_requested; it settles with the turn's outcome (canceled, or succeeded when the turn completed before the cancel reached it). A direct tool run is not touched. The reply's matched is true when the id named the turn this gateway is running; false for an id that already ended or is not this gateway's (a benign race: no job was marked). Without turn_id: stops whatever turn is running on the shared session (the historical behaviour, which can stop a turn another client started), marks the session's in-flight dispatch jobs cancel_requested (each settles with its turn's outcome), and aborts an in-flight in-session direct tool run (POST /sessions/{id}/tools/{name}:run), which holds the same serial turn slot. Either form spares the session and background tasks (distinct from close).

post.summary: Send a message, an interrupt or a stop to a session.
post.description: Sends a command to a live session, whether it is working or idle, and returns 202 with its receipt once the agent has recorded it. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a retry with the same key and the same command returns the stored receipt (duplicate true) and admits nothing; the same key with a different command is 422 idempotency_key_reused. A key is remembered while its command waits and for 24 hours after the command settled (committed, superseded, refused or failed); after that its receipt is gone (GET is 404) and the same key admits a new command. A session remembers at most 4096 keys: a command with a new key beyond that is 429 idempotency_keys_exhausted. A stop is never refused because of the remembered-key limit, and its key is remembered like any other. kind message: the text reaches the session at its next step: before its next model request, before its next tool call (a tool call the model asked for in the same response and that has not started is not run, and its result says so), or when the turn would end. An idle session starts a turn for it; a session whose model cannot run (no API key or login for its provider) keeps it queued, says why on the session stream (event.error no_credentials or session_unconfigured), and delivers it once a key is stored or the session switches to a model that can run. Commands that are waiting when the session reaches a step are delivered together, in the order they were sent, as one user message. on_gate deny (the default) declines a confirmation or question the session is waiting on ("declined: the user sent a new message") so the message is read at once; on_gate wait leaves it waiting, and the message waits behind it. A Claude Code session reads the message only when its turn ends (command_capability turn_end); on_gate deny still declines its confirmations, and every confirmation it asks for while the message waits, so the turn ends and the message is read. A fusion model, or a turn started by a loop or a finished background task, also reads the message when the turn ends, and on_gate deny does not decline what that turn is waiting on. kind interrupt: stops the work the session was running when the interrupt was sent, then delivers the text as a new turn; background tasks, background workflow runs and background shells keep running (a stop ends them). Its receipt says whether work was running (interrupted). kind stop: stops all of the session's work, pauses its loops, and supersedes every message and interrupt sent before it that has not been delivered; its receipt lists what it stopped (stopped). With close true the session is then closed, and later commands are 409 session_closed. A stop carries no text. order (optional) orders one caller's commands: a message or interrupt with a lower order than a stop already received is superseded at once. Each text is at most 32 KiB (more is 400 bad_request); the text waiting on one session is at most 128 KiB (more is 429 command_queue_full with Retry-After). A configured UserPromptSubmit hook sees each message before delivery and can refuse it (state refused, reason hook). event.command_committed announces delivered commands on the session stream and event.command_settled the ones that ended otherwise; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id} reads a receipt. Commands reach live sessions only: a closed session is 409 session_closed and an unknown one 404; a headless or internal session is 409 command_unsupported.

The key is remembered while the command waits and for 24 hours after it settled. Past 4096 remembered keys a new key is 429 idempotency_keys_exhausted; a stop is never refused because of the remembered-key limit.

202.description: The command was recorded (or this is the stored receipt of the same key).

schema.description: A command receipt: what the command became. It never contains the command's text.

command_id.description: The command's id (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id} reads it; event.command_committed and event.command_settled name it).

kind.description: The command kind.

state.description: queued: recorded, not yet in the conversation. committed: it is in the conversation, with turn_id and how (a stop: carried out). superseded: a stop ended it before it was committed. refused: it will not be committed; reason says why (hook, closed or unsupported). failed: the session could not record it (reason write_failed); it will not be committed.

admitted_at.description: RFC3339 time the command was recorded.

duplicate.description: true when this is the stored receipt of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key: nothing was admitted again.

turn_id.description: The turn the command reached: the running turn (how next_step) or the turn it started (how new_turn). Absent until committed, and for a stop.

how.description: How it was committed: next_step (inside the running turn, before its next model request or tool call), new_turn (the session was idle and it started a turn), stop (a stop carried out). Absent until committed.

committed_at.description: RFC3339 commit time. Absent until committed.

interrupted.description: An interrupt only: whether running work was stopped for it (false when nothing was running). Absent while that is not decided yet, and when the session ended before it was recorded: then it is unknown, and running work may have been stopped.

reason.description: Why it was superseded, refused or failed. superseded: stop (a stop sent after it), order (a stop with a higher order) or withdrawn (its sender took it back with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id}/withdraw before the session took it). refused: hook (a UserPromptSubmit hook blocked it), closed (the session closed before it was committed) or unsupported (the session cannot take it, for example its realm cannot be used under the current login; detail says why). failed: write_failed, in two cases: the conversation could not be saved with the message (the running turn stops, event.error admission_write_failed), or an idle session could not record the turn the message would start; that is tried 5 times, again after 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds, each failure an event.error ledger_write_failed, and the 5th failure in a row ends it failed.

detail.description: More about reason, for example the hook's message.

superseded_by.description: The command_id of the stop that superseded it.

kind.description: What was stopped: session (the running turn or parked gate), task (a background task), workflow_run, bash_job (a background shell the session started, on this machine or its computer), loop (paused, not deleted).

id.description: The item's id: the session id, <session id>/<task id> for a task, a run id, a bash job id or a loop id.

outcome.description: stopped: the stop reached running work and it ended (a loop: paused). already_done: it had finished before the stop reached it. failed: it was still running when the checks ended; detail says why.

detail.description: Present on failed: why.

cleanup.description: Present on stopped when the stop could not guarantee it reached every process the work started: detached_may_survive means a process a shell command of the work started in the background (detached) may still be running. Absent when the stop reached them all.

stopped.description: A committed stop: the work it acted on and how each ended. Absent when nothing was running.

cleanup.description: A committed stop, whether or not it found work running: detached_may_survive means a shell command the session ran may have left a process (started in the background, detached) that no stop can be shown to have reached, so it may still be running. Absent when there is no such process.

close.description: A stop sent with close: the session is closed once its work is stopped.

order.description: The order the command was sent with.

kind.description: user: a person; bot: the user's Bot; delegate: another agent session; system: the agent itself.

id.description: The sender's id (at most 256 bytes). Attribution only, never authorization.

from.description: Who sent it, as the request named it.

trigger.description: What caused it, as the request named it.

kind.description: message, interrupt or stop.

text.description: The message (message and interrupt: required, non-empty, at most 32 KiB). Delivered verbatim. A stop takes none.

close.description: A stop only: close the session once its work is stopped.

on_gate.description: A message only: deny (default) declines a confirmation or question the session is waiting on so the message is read now; wait leaves it waiting. A Claude Code session reads the message when its turn ends; deny still declines its confirmations, so the turn ends. A fusion model, or a turn started by a loop or a finished background task, keeps waiting either way.

order.description: Optional, at least 0: a sequence number for your commands. A message or interrupt with a positive order lower than the highest stop order the session has recorded is superseded, whoever sent the stop. 0, or omitting it, skips this check.

kind.description: user: a person; bot: the user's Bot; delegate: another agent session; system: the agent itself.

id.description: The sender's id (at most 256 bytes). Attribution only, never authorization.

from.description: Optional: who sends it. It changes how the message is introduced to the model (from the user, from the user via their Bot, from another session, from the system). The agent does not verify it: it is a claim made by the caller and grants nothing. Set it only when your client relays a message on someone's behalf (a Bot runtime, a session forwarding to another); a client sending a person's own message leaves it out, which reads as from the user.

trigger.description: Optional: what caused it, recorded on the receipt. With from kind bot, human introduces the message as the user's via their Bot and wake or clear as the Bot's own. Like from, it is the caller's claim, not verified, and grants nothing; leave it out unless your client relays messages.

schema.description: A command receipt: what the command became. It never contains the command's text.

command_id.description: The command's id (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id} reads it; event.command_committed and event.command_settled name it).

kind.description: The command kind.

state.description: queued: recorded, not yet in the conversation. committed: it is in the conversation, with turn_id and how (a stop: carried out). superseded: a stop ended it before it was committed. refused: it will not be committed; reason says why (hook, closed or unsupported). failed: the session could not record it (reason write_failed); it will not be committed.

admitted_at.description: RFC3339 time the command was recorded.

duplicate.description: true when this is the stored receipt of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key: nothing was admitted again.

turn_id.description: The turn the command reached: the running turn (how next_step) or the turn it started (how new_turn). Absent until committed, and for a stop.

how.description: How it was committed: next_step (inside the running turn, before its next model request or tool call), new_turn (the session was idle and it started a turn), stop (a stop carried out). Absent until committed.

committed_at.description: RFC3339 commit time. Absent until committed.

interrupted.description: An interrupt only: whether running work was stopped for it (false when nothing was running). Absent while that is not decided yet, and when the session ended before it was recorded: then it is unknown, and running work may have been stopped.

reason.description: Why it was superseded, refused or failed. superseded: stop (a stop sent after it), order (a stop with a higher order) or withdrawn (its sender took it back with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id}/withdraw before the session took it). refused: hook (a UserPromptSubmit hook blocked it), closed (the session closed before it was committed) or unsupported (the session cannot take it, for example its realm cannot be used under the current login; detail says why). failed: write_failed, in two cases: the conversation could not be saved with the message (the running turn stops, event.error admission_write_failed), or an idle session could not record the turn the message would start; that is tried 5 times, again after 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds, each failure an event.error ledger_write_failed, and the 5th failure in a row ends it failed.

detail.description: More about reason, for example the hook's message.

superseded_by.description: The command_id of the stop that superseded it.

kind.description: What was stopped: session (the running turn or parked gate), task (a background task), workflow_run, bash_job (a background shell the session started, on this machine or its computer), loop (paused, not deleted).

id.description: The item's id: the session id, <session id>/<task id> for a task, a run id, a bash job id or a loop id.

outcome.description: stopped: the stop reached running work and it ended (a loop: paused). already_done: it had finished before the stop reached it. failed: it was still running when the checks ended; detail says why.

detail.description: Present on failed: why.

cleanup.description: Present on stopped when the stop could not guarantee it reached every process the work started: detached_may_survive means a process a shell command of the work started in the background (detached) may still be running. Absent when the stop reached them all.

stopped.description: A committed stop: the work it acted on and how each ended. Absent when nothing was running.

cleanup.description: A committed stop, whether or not it found work running: detached_may_survive means a shell command the session ran may have left a process (started in the background, detached) that no stop can be shown to have reached, so it may still be running. Absent when there is no such process.

close.description: A stop sent with close: the session is closed once its work is stopped.

order.description: The order the command was sent with.

post.summary: Retire a command key no read found.
post.description: Settles a keyed command whose answer was lost. {key} is the Idempotency-Key the request was sent with (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace; URL-encode it). A key whose command is kept answers retired false, admitted "true" and the receipt. Otherwise the key is retired durably on this session: retired true, and a command sent with it earlier and delivered later is refused 409 command_key_retired; retiring it again answers the same. admitted is "false" only while no receipt of this session has expired; otherwise "unknown" (the key may have admitted a command whose receipt is gone: treat it as possibly run). The session must be live: a closed session is 409 session_closed. A 503 is unknown: nothing is proven, retire again after Retry-After. 409 command_fences_exhausted: the key was NOT retired, so a delayed command sent with it can still be admitted; never send a replacement. A retire request never runs the original command, but a command already admitted with the key may have run or may still run. The request has no body.

schema.description: A command receipt: what the command became. It never contains the command's text.

command_id.description: The command's id (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id} reads it; event.command_committed and event.command_settled name it).

kind.description: The command kind.

state.description: queued: recorded, not yet in the conversation. committed: it is in the conversation, with turn_id and how (a stop: carried out). superseded: a stop ended it before it was committed. refused: it will not be committed; reason says why (hook, closed or unsupported). failed: the session could not record it (reason write_failed); it will not be committed.

admitted_at.description: RFC3339 time the command was recorded.

duplicate.description: true when this is the stored receipt of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key: nothing was admitted again.

turn_id.description: The turn the command reached: the running turn (how next_step) or the turn it started (how new_turn). Absent until committed, and for a stop.

how.description: How it was committed: next_step (inside the running turn, before its next model request or tool call), new_turn (the session was idle and it started a turn), stop (a stop carried out). Absent until committed.

committed_at.description: RFC3339 commit time. Absent until committed.

interrupted.description: An interrupt only: whether running work was stopped for it (false when nothing was running). Absent while that is not decided yet, and when the session ended before it was recorded: then it is unknown, and running work may have been stopped.

reason.description: Why it was superseded, refused or failed. superseded: stop (a stop sent after it), order (a stop with a higher order) or withdrawn (its sender took it back with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands/{command_id}/withdraw before the session took it). refused: hook (a UserPromptSubmit hook blocked it), closed (the session closed before it was committed) or unsupported (the session cannot take it, for example its realm cannot be used under the current login; detail says why). failed: write_failed, in two cases: the conversation could not be saved with the message (the running turn stops, event.error admission_write_failed), or an idle session could not record the turn the message would start; that is tried 5 times, again after 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds, each failure an event.error ledger_write_failed, and the 5th failure in a row ends it failed.

detail.description: More about reason, for example the hook's message.

superseded_by.description: The command_id of the stop that superseded it.

kind.description: What was stopped: session (the running turn or parked gate), task (a background task), workflow_run, bash_job (a background shell the session started, on this machine or its computer), loop (paused, not deleted).

id.description: The item's id: the session id, <session id>/<task id> for a task, a run id, a bash job id or a loop id.

outcome.description: stopped: the stop reached running work and it ended (a loop: paused). already_done: it had finished before the stop reached it. failed: it was still running when the checks ended; detail says why.

detail.description: Present on failed: why.

cleanup.description: Present on stopped when the stop could not guarantee it reached every process the work started: detached_may_survive means a process a shell command of the work started in the background (detached) may still be running. Absent when the stop reached them all.

stopped.description: A committed stop: the work it acted on and how each ended. Absent when nothing was running.

cleanup.description: A committed stop, whether or not it found work running: detached_may_survive means a shell command the session ran may have left a process (started in the background, detached) that no stop can be shown to have reached, so it may still be running. Absent when there is no such process.

close.description: A stop sent with close: the session is closed once its work is stopped.

order.description: The order the command was sent with.

post.description: Withdraws a message sent with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands that the session has not taken yet, and returns 200 with outcome and the command's receipt. The decision is made together with the session's queue, so a message is either withdrawn or delivered, never both. outcome withdrawn: the message was still waiting; it is recorded as state superseded with reason withdrawn before this answer, its text is dropped, it will never reach the session (not at its next step, not as a new turn, not after a restart), and event.command_settled announces it. Repeating the request answers withdrawn again and changes nothing. outcome taken: the session has already taken the message (it is being delivered, or it is in the conversation: the receipt's state says which). It was NOT withdrawn and nothing was changed. outcome ended: the message had already ended without reaching the session for another reason (a stop superseded it, a hook refused it, the session could not record it); the receipt says which, and nothing was changed. Only a message can be withdrawn: an interrupt or a stop is 409 command_not_withdrawable. A command id this session never admitted, or one whose receipt is no longer kept, is 404. The session must be live: a closed session is 409 session_closed. The Idempotency-Key the message was sent with keeps answering its receipt, so a resend under that key never admits it again; a changed message is a new POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands under a new key, sent only after outcome withdrawn or ended. 503 withdraw_unconfirmed means the outcome is unknown: repeat the request. 503 withdraw_write_failed and session_terminating mean nothing was withdrawn. The request has no body. Cache-Control: no-store.

requestBody.description: Confirm-gate answer. On a session that requires approval on every action, gate_id and generation are required as well as approved, and once the session's approver lease was minted every decision also carries it in X-Hoody-Approver-Lease. gate_id/generation are echoes of the parked gate (a mismatch is 409). request_id is optional. approved is always required: a confirm without a boolean approved is rejected 400 (approved_required) and the gate stays parked. On a default-policy session gate_id and generation are optional. On a session that requires approval on every action they are required too: a confirm missing any of them is rejected 400 and the gate stays parked.

gate_id.description: Echo of the parked gate id, as published on the frame that parked it (gate.id), by GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} (pending_gate.id) and in 409 details. Valid only for the session in the path. Optional for compatibility, but an answer without it applies to whatever gate is parked when it arrives: a client binding an answer to a gate the user saw must send it. Ids are unique per session incarnation, so an id from before a re-attach never matches (stale/mismatch → 409). Required on a session that requires approval on every action: a confirm without it is rejected 400.

generation.description: Echo of the parked gate generation. It restarts when the session is re-attached, so it is not an identity on its own: send gate_id. Optional on a default-policy session; required, and non-zero, on a session that requires approval on every action.

approved.description: Required: true to approve, false to deny. There is no default; a missing, null or non-boolean value is rejected 400.

reason.description: Optional, with approved false only: why the action is refused. The agent reads it in the refused call's result, flattened to one line, together with the instruction not to reach the same effect another way. At most 500 characters; sent with approved true, or longer, it is rejected 400 bad_request.

persist_dirs.description: Persist an approved directory grant to settings.json (WS↔REST parity).

remember.description: With approved true: false approves this call only. Omitted or true, approving a file change also lets later changes to that file run without asking for the rest of the session, and persist_dirs is honoured; false asks again for the next change and saves nothing to settings.json (persist_dirs is ignored).

superseded.description: With approved false only, and no reason or session_scope: the call is declined because the user sent a new message instead of answering. The agent reads that the call was not run and that the new message decides what to do; it does not read a refusal, so it may still do the same thing if the new message asks for it, and the tool is not denied for the session. Sent with approved true, a reason or session_scope, it is rejected 400 bad_request.

session_scope.description: Remember this decision for the rest of the session (the Allow/Deny for session answer): with approved true the tool stops asking, with approved false it is refused without asking. Offer allow-for-session only when the gate's event.confirm_request carried offer_session_allow. Under a locked approval policy the wider grant is refused, but the one-shot decision still applies and the reply says so (session_scope_applied false, note).

trust_computer.description: With approved true, accept the gate's exec_trust offer (event.confirm_request): the call runs and exec cards on that computer in this realm stop until the grant is revoked (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules exec_trust). Ignored when the gate carried no offer or the approval policy is locked.

request_id.description: Optional: the caller's own id for this decision, at most 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-' (anything else is 400 bad_request). When this decision is the one the gate consumed, a later 409 gate_already_resolved for the gate echoes it as details.request_id, so a caller that lost the 200 knows the recorded decision is its own.

lease_generation.description: The approver-lease generation the decision was made under: the generation of the gate's event.confirm_request, of a later event.decision_requirements, pending_gate.lease_generation on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}, /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/replay and prompt:sync, or pending_gate.generation on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state (the daemon's gate). Forwarded as is; omitted or 0 sends none. A decision carrying the lease capability (X-Hoody-Approver-Lease) is checked against the current lease whatever it sends; without one, a stale generation is refused. Not the gate generation above.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

patch.description: Live reasoning-effort change (low|medium|high|xhigh, or "" for the model default). With model_settings (or agent frontmatter) thinking: the effort is ignored while thinking is disabled or names its own effort, and supplies the level when thinking is enabled without one, on models that take a level. On a Claude Code (delegated) session it is Claude Code's --effort and applies from the next turn (a change sent during a turn applies when it ends), under the same precedence: an explicit model_settings thinking effort wins and thinking disabled ignores it; "" is Claude Code's own default, kept over a configured default; the state's effort reads back the effort Claude Code runs with; an installed Claude Code bridge too old to change it mid-session is refused 409 delegated_session and the effort does not change; while the session is still connecting the change is accepted and then refused with an error event (code delegated_session), the effort stays unchanged, so read the session state back.

get.summary: Read an image attached to a session message.
get.description: Returns the bytes of one image a person attached to a message of the session. image_id is the image_id of an image block in GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/transcript (or event.replay); the transcript carries only the block's media_type and size, never the bytes. Like the transcript it reads the session record, for a live or closed session, and never attaches. The Content-Type is what the bytes are (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif), with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Disposition: inline and Cache-Control: private, no-store. The image lasts as long as its message: once the message leaves the transcript (trim, clear, compaction) or the session is deleted, the id is unknown. An image block without image_id cannot be read here. The agent answers these reads one at a time, each from the whole session record: ask for a few at once, not for all of a long conversation in parallel. One plain 404 answers a session that is not visible to this caller, an id this session does not hold and a malformed id alike. CONFIG-DIR: X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the record store, as on the transcript. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404.

x-error-codes.title: Decision limit reached
x-error-codes.description: hoody-ai/hoody-decide only: a decision limit of this AI server's plan is used up (requests per minute or per day, questions per day, input tokens per day, or concurrent requests). details.limit names it (per_minute_requests, per_day_requests, per_day_questions, per_day_tokens or concurrent), details.retry_after_ms says when it frees up and details.reset_at (RFC 3339, when sent) the time; Retry-After carries the wait in seconds. details.request_id is the x-hoody-request-id. Never retried by the agent; the limit is shared by all computers on that server.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait until reset_at (or Retry-After), or use a plan with higher limits. A model of another provider with its own key is not limited by the plan.

get.description: Lists the recurring agent loops scheduled for a session, returned as the kit list envelope {items, meta:{total}} with optional page/limit pagination (loops are a session-scoped snapshot; the page/limit window is applied gateway-side).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session id.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number for pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum items per page (0 = no pagination).

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of items; each element is the forwarded daemon row's own shape.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages (the full count, not the page size).

limit.description: Items per page (present only when limit>0).

post.description: Creates a recurring agent loop on a session: interval, max_runs, stop_when predicate, cost/wall budgets, expiry, and an optional immediate first fire. Loop fires run separately from the session's command queue. Two limits apply and both refuse the create rather than adjusting it: the interval floor of 60 seconds, and a ceiling of 8 active loops per daemon: the 9th create is rejected. Loops live in daemon memory: they end when their session closes and are lost on a daemon restart. A running loop keeps its session from the idle sweep while no client is attached; a paused one does not.

requestBody.description: Loop definition (the session_id comes from the path).

prompt.description: The prompt fired each loop run.

interval.description: Run interval as a duration token, for example "30m". Required, with no default: a create without it is rejected. The minimum accepted interval is 60 seconds: a shorter one is refused rather than rounded up.

max_runs.description: Stop after this many runs. Omitted, 0 or negative applies the default ceiling of 50 runs; there are no unbounded loops.

kind.description: Which kind of predicate this is. Required inside stop_when.

expr.description: For kind expression: the expression to evaluate.

tool.description: For kind toolCall: the tool to call.

check.description: For kind toolCall: the check applied to the tool result.

judge.description: For kind judgeRef: the judge to consult.

args.description: Arguments passed to the tool or judge.

threshold.description: For kind convergence: the convergence threshold.

min_iters.description: For kind convergence: the minimum iterations before the predicate can stop the loop.

allow_network.description: Whether the predicate may reach the network.

stop_when.description: Optional stop predicate, evaluated after each run. Omit the field entirely when there is no predicate: a string value is rejected, and that includes the empty string.

max_cost_usd.description: Cost ceiling in USD, a number >= 0. 0 or absent means unlimited. It counts priced usage only: a Claude Code session's fires are unpriced (their usage carries no cost), so there the ceiling never stops the loop; bound such a loop with max_runs or max_wall_ms. A value that is not a JSON number (a string such as "5", true or null) or is negative is refused with 400 bad_request.

max_wall_ms.description: Wall-clock ceiling, as a whole number of milliseconds from 0 up to (not including) 2^63. 0 or absent means unlimited. Any other value (a string such as "2h", a fraction, a negative number, true or null) is refused with 400 bad_request.

expires_in.description: Optional expiration as a duration from now, in the same grammar as interval (for example "2h" or "3 days"); omitted, "", "never", "none" or "off" (case-insensitive) means no expiration. An expired loop stops firing. Without fire_now an expiry shorter than one interval is rejected, because the loop would never fire; with fire_now it must be at least 2 seconds, so the immediate first run can happen.

fire_now.description: Run the first fire on the next scheduler tick instead of one interval out; later fires keep the normal cadence. Default false.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

patch.description: Updates a loop by body shape: set EXACTLY ONE intent per request: its run state pause/resume/stop via a `paused` field; its expiry via an `expires_in` field; or a budget revive (sets/revives the cost/wall budgets only via max_cost_usd/max_wall_ms; it does NOT change interval or prompt in v1). A budget revive replaces both ceilings: the one the body leaves out becomes 0 (unlimited), so send both to keep a ceiling. A request that mixes more than one intent is rejected 400 rather than silently applying one and dropping the others, and so is a request that names none (an empty body, or only if_state / if_max_cost_usd / if_max_wall_ms preconditions): it is 400 bad_request and nothing changes. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404.

requestBody.description: Exactly one update intent: run state, expiry, or budget.

expires_in.description: Expiry intent: a duration-from-now token, e.g. "2h"; "" or "never" clears it.

max_cost_usd.description: Budget intent: the cost ceiling in USD, a number >= 0; 0 = unlimited. A budget update sets both ceilings: sent without max_wall_ms, it also sets the wall-clock ceiling to 0 (unlimited). A value that is not a JSON number (a string such as "5", true or null) or is negative is refused with 400 bad_request, and nothing changes.

max_wall_ms.description: Budget intent: the wall-clock ceiling, as a whole number of milliseconds from 0 up to (not including) 2^63; 0 = unlimited. Any other value (a string such as "2h", a fraction, a negative number, true or null) is refused with 400 bad_request, and nothing changes. A budget update sets both ceilings: sent without max_cost_usd, it also sets the cost ceiling to 0 (unlimited).

if_state.description: Precondition (any intent): the loop's state as listed (running, firing, paused, error, expired, stopped, ended). When the loop is not in it now, nothing changes and the answer is 409 loop_changed. if_state stopped with the budget fields starts a stopped loop again only if it is still stopped.

if_max_cost_usd.description: Precondition (any intent): the loop's cost ceiling as listed (0 = none). When it differs now, nothing changes and the answer is 409 loop_changed.

if_max_wall_ms.description: Precondition (any intent): the loop's wall-clock ceiling in ms as listed (0 = none). When it differs now, nothing changes and the answer is 409 loop_changed.

post.description: Dispatches a user turn and returns {job_id, session_id, turn_id}; observe agent_done on the session's stream (its turn_id matches). turn_id names this turn for a scoped cancel (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/cancel with turn_id), which can never stop a later turn. Refuses a new turn when the session already has a parked gate (409 gate_parked, the parked gate under details.pending_gate) or a turn is already running (409 turn_in_flight): single-writer, no duplicate parked turns. ADMISSION LEDGER: an input that carries neither an Idempotency-Key nor a turn_id (an interactive TUI turn) is forwarded and logged when the admission ledger cannot be read or written: no receipt and no ledger row, exactly as before this release; keyed and gateway-dispatched (turn-identified) inputs are refused 503 admission_write_failed instead, because a lost row could let a retry run twice. Keyed rows are never pruned, so a replay always answers with its stored receipt; after a daemon restart every non-terminal turn reports state interrupted with effects_may_have_occurred:true and is never re-run.

requestBody.description: Turn input: the user text, optional inline image attachments, plus the optional tool_mode / dir_scope the session's first turn fixes.

text.description: Required (may be empty only with attachments). The user message text for this turn: empty or whitespace-only text with no attachments is refused (400 empty_prompt) and no turn runs.

tool_mode.description: Optional tool mode: standard or orchestrator. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (tool_mode_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode; any other value is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode too.

dir_scope.description: Optional directory-access scope: home or full. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (dir_scope_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope; any other value is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope too.

media_type.description: The image media type, e.g. "image/png". Must match the actual bytes (image/jpg is read as image/jpeg); a mismatch is refused 400.

data.description: The image itself, base64-encoded (standard encoding): a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP. Other bytes are refused 400. Required: HTTP attachments are inline bytes.

name.description: Optional display name (the original filename), shown in the transcript instead of a staging path.

attachments.description: Optional images for this turn, as INLINE base64 bytes. At most 4 per turn, each at most 4 MiB DECODED (~5.33 MiB of base64); the request body limit applies on top and is authoritative, so several individually-legal images can still exceed it. A violation is refused with 400 BEFORE the turn is accepted: nothing is silently dropped. `path` is not supported here: it would name a file on the CALLER's machine, so an attachment with a non-empty path refuses the whole request with 400 bad_request before a turn is accepted. If the active model cannot accept images the daemon reports that on the session stream.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

patch.description: SYNCHRONOUS live model switch: applies the model inline and answers what actually happened: {status:ok, model, persisted} on success (persisted=false when the frontmatter write failed: the live switch stands but reverts next session), 409 gate_parked/turn_in_flight while the session is busy, 404 for an unknown/closed session, 400 for a blank model, 422 model_unavailable for a model the catalogue does not list (details.reason unknown_model; GET /api/v1/agent/models lists the choices), a speech model (details.reason speech_model) or a spec that cannot be constructed; nothing changes on a refusal. On a Claude Code (delegated) session the model is a Claude Code launch option: a Claude alias (opus, sonnet, haiku) or Claude model id, with or without the anthropic/ prefix, applies from the session's next turn on the same conversation, is kept with the session and rewrites no agent file; a model from another provider is 422 model_unavailable (details.reason not_claude), and 409 delegated_session means the installed Claude Code bridge is too old to change the model mid-session. scope picks what a native switch changes: "agent" (the default) also rewrites the model line of the chat agent's file in the profile layer that sources it (project before home; in a scoped realm that has only the shipped default, a new copy in that realm's profile layer), so it applies to later sessions that use that file (it is not global); "session" changes only this session, kept with it (persisted says whether its record holds it), and leaves the agent's file alone. Any other scope is 400 bad_request (details.field scope). A Claude Code session's switch is always the session's own (scope reads session). The reply's scope says which applied. Peers converge via the emitted init_state event.

post.summary: Dispatch a turn and stream the response.
post.description: Dispatches a turn and opens an SSE stream at the seq captured just before the dispatch, so the first frames are this turn's rather than the retained ring's backlog. WHERE IT ENDS: this is an ordinary session stream positioned at a cursor, NOT a per-turn stream: it does NOT close when the turn finishes. After the turn's agent_done it keeps delivering whatever else happens on the session, including turns another client dispatches, until the caller disconnects or the session ends. Stop reading at the agent_done whose turn_id matches the X-Hoody-Turn-Id response header and close the connection yourself; a client that waits for EOF waits forever. The X-Hoody-Turn-Id response header carries the turn's id (it is also the id for a scoped cancel); the stream's replay_boundary frame carries the same id as turn_id, for a client that cannot read response headers. The explicit X-Hoody-Gate-Policy: auto_approve header (or ?policy=auto_approve) auto-answers confirm gates with approved=true for the life of the stream, except a gate a tool-call rule raised (the confirm_request carries rules) and a destructive-shape gate (gate_cause static_stakes), which it answers approved=false, and a human_only gate, which it never answers and leaves for a person (/api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm), off by default; the gateway asks for no separate credentials to use it; access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Bad request
x-error-codes.description: The request was malformed or carried invalid parameters.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the request body or query parameters.

x-error-codes.title: Realm scope unsupported
x-error-codes.description: A per-request scope header this route does not take: a realm or computer header on a route without that dimension, or, on an agent pinned to one realm, a different realm.
x-error-codes.resolution: Omit the header. A route without a realm dimension refuses every realm header, the pinned realm included; on a route that takes a realm, an agent pinned to one realm accepts only that realm.

example.message: realm scope not supported on this route

x-error-codes.title: Empty prompt
x-error-codes.description: The turn has no text (empty or only whitespace) and no attachments, so there is nothing to send to the model. No turn was started. details.field is "text".
x-error-codes.resolution: Send the message text, or at least one image attachment.

example.message: text is empty and there are no attachments; send the message text, or at least one image

x-error-codes.title: Invalid tool mode
x-error-codes.description: tool_mode is not standard or orchestrator (details.field is "tool_mode"), or a turn names a tool mode other than the one the session's first turn fixed (or, before that turn runs, the one an earlier queued turn carries). Nothing was started.
x-error-codes.resolution: Send standard or orchestrator, or omit tool_mode. A later turn sends the session's own tool mode or omits it.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid directory scope
x-error-codes.description: dir_scope is not home or full (details.field is "dir_scope"), or a turn names a directory scope other than the one the session's first turn fixed (or, before that turn runs, the one an earlier queued turn carries). Nothing was started.
x-error-codes.resolution: Send home or full, or omit dir_scope. A later turn sends the session's own scope or omits it.

x-error-codes.title: Invalid realm selector
x-error-codes.description: The realm selector is malformed (not ""/"global"/a 24-hex id).
x-error-codes.resolution: Pass a valid realm selector.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Realm not allowed for this login
x-error-codes.description: The agent is logged in with a token limited to some realms (GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status lists them in realm_ids), and this session's realm is not one of them, or is the global scope (a session restored from before the login, or a realm the login was narrowed away from). The session can still be read; nothing was run.
x-error-codes.resolution: Continue in a session of a realm the login serves, or log the agent in with a token that covers this session's realm.

example.message: realm 0123456789abcdef01234567 is not allowed for this realm-limited login

x-error-codes.title: Forbidden (Source IP Guard)
x-error-codes.description: Refused by the Source IP Guard: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only.
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the agent through its URL, for example with `hoody agent …`.

example.message: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only
