x-error-codes.title: Not found
x-error-codes.description: The requested resource does not exist.
x-error-codes.resolution: Verify the path and identifier.

409.description: A gate is parked, a turn is already running, or auto_approve was requested on an always-approval session.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Gate parked
x-error-codes.description: A confirm/question gate is parked on this session, so a new turn/workflow run is refused until it is answered. The parked gate is surfaced under details.pending_gate.
x-error-codes.resolution: Answer the parked gate (/confirm or /answer, echoing its gate_id) and retry; read it from details.pending_gate, from pending_gate on GET /sessions/{id}, or from the gate field of the stream frame that parked it.

example.message: a gate is parked on this session

x-error-codes.title: Turn in flight
x-error-codes.description: A turn is already running on this session; the single serial turn slot is occupied, so a new turn/workflow run is refused.
x-error-codes.resolution: Wait for the running turn to finish (observe agent_done on the session stream), then retry.

example.message: a turn is already running on this session

x-error-codes.title: Approval policy active
x-error-codes.description: This session requires an explicit decision on every action, so an automatic-answer alias (the auto_approve gate posture, arming YOLO, an allow rule) is refused.
x-error-codes.resolution: Answer each gate through POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm, or change the policy first (PUT /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approval) if it is not locked.

example.message: this session requires approval on every action; auto_approve is refused

x-error-codes.title: Replay unavailable
x-error-codes.description: The Idempotency-Key names a turn that already ran (details.turn is its receipt); prompt:stream cannot re-stream the original events, and it never re-runs the turn.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read details.turn / GET details.turn.result_url for the outcome, or attach GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream with a cursor you hold.

example.message: this idempotency key names a turn that already ran; its events cannot be re-streamed

x-error-codes.title: Idempotency key retired
x-error-codes.description: The Idempotency-Key was retired on this session, and from now on it admits no turn. details.admitted repeats what was recorded when the key was retired: "false" means no turn was admitted with the key; "unknown" means a turn sent with it earlier may have been admitted and run. Nothing beyond details.admitted is guaranteed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read details.admitted. If it is "false", the turn may be sent under a new Idempotency-Key. If it is "unknown", check whether the earlier turn took effect before sending it again.

example.message: the idempotency key was retired; no turn was admitted with it, so you may send it under a new key

admitted.description: What was recorded when the key was retired: "false" means nothing was admitted with the key; "unknown" means a request sent with it earlier may have been admitted and run.

x-error-codes.title: Payload too large
x-error-codes.description: The request body exceeds the configured size limit (default 8 MiB). Reduce the request body.
x-error-codes.resolution: Reduce the request body below the configured limit (default 8 MiB); split a large payload into smaller requests.

example.message: request body exceeds the configured size limit

422.description: The Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Idempotency key reused
x-error-codes.description: The Idempotency-Key was already used for a DIFFERENT request on this session. A key binds to one request; reusing it for another is a client bug. details.turn_id names the turn the key admitted (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id} reads it).
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a fresh Idempotency-Key for a different request, or resend the identical request to get the original receipt.

example.message: this idempotency key was used for a different request

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Too many requests
x-error-codes.description: The per-client request rate limit was exceeded; the gateway throttled the request before dispatch.
x-error-codes.resolution: Honor the Retry-After header and retry; reduce the request rate.

500.description: Pre-stream dispatch failure (transport error before SSE opens).

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Internal error
x-error-codes.description: An unexpected error occurred while handling the request.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if persistent, inspect the daemon logs.

503.description: Service unavailable / admission not confirmed / ledger write failed.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying when the session's turn record could not be read or the session is shutting down.

x-error-codes.title: Service unavailable / Turn record unreadable
x-error-codes.description: The daemon could not service the request (too busy, or a per-client stream concurrency cap was hit). The session's turn record could not be read or made durable, so whether this Idempotency-Key admitted a turn is unknown: it may have been.
x-error-codes.resolution: Honor Retry-After and retry with the same Idempotency-Key; never change the key, since the turn may already run.

example.message: the session's turn record could not be read; retry with the same idempotency key

x-error-codes.title: Admission unconfirmed
x-error-codes.description: The turn was sent but the daemon's admission receipt did not arrive within the wait. It may still have been accepted: details.turn_id / details.result_url name the turn to poll. The gateway keeps the turn slot and job rather than inventing or discarding acceptance.
x-error-codes.resolution: GET details.result_url; retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key only after it reports the turn was not recorded (404).

example.message: the daemon did not acknowledge the turn's admission within the wait

x-error-codes.title: Admission write failed
x-error-codes.description: The daemon could not durably record the turn's admission, so the turn was NOT run (fail-closed: nothing runs unrecorded).
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if it persists, check the daemon's session store (disk / permissions).

example.message: the admission ledger could not be written; the turn was not accepted

x-error-codes.title: Login restriction unknown
x-error-codes.description: The agent cannot read yet which realms its login may serve (GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status reports restriction "unknown"), so it runs no work in any session until it can. Nothing was run.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the restriction is readable.

example.message: the login's realm restriction could not be read (introspection failed) — retry, or log in again

x-error-codes.title: Session terminating
x-error-codes.description: The session is shutting down, so this request was refused before anything was recorded for it. The refusal does not cover an earlier attempt with the same Idempotency-Key: that attempt may have been admitted and run.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the Retry-After delay with the same Idempotency-Key. If an earlier attempt with that key ended uncertain (a timeout or a lost connection), read GET /sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id} for it first. If the session has closed meanwhile, attach it again first (POST /sessions with attach).

requestBody.description: Turn input: the user text, optional inline image attachments, plus the optional tool_mode / dir_scope the session's first turn fixes.

text.description: Required (may be empty only with attachments). The user message text for this turn: empty or whitespace-only text with no attachments is refused (400 empty_prompt) and no turn runs.

tool_mode.description: Optional tool mode: standard or orchestrator. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (tool_mode_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode; any other value is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode too.

dir_scope.description: Optional directory-access scope: home or full. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (dir_scope_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope; any other value is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope too.

media_type.description: The image media type, e.g. "image/png". Must match the actual bytes (image/jpg is read as image/jpeg); a mismatch is refused 400.

data.description: The image itself, base64-encoded (standard encoding): a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP. Other bytes are refused 400. Required: HTTP attachments are inline bytes.

name.description: Optional display name (the original filename), shown in the transcript instead of a staging path.

attachments.description: Optional images for this turn, as INLINE base64 bytes. At most 4 per turn, each at most 4 MiB DECODED (~5.33 MiB of base64); the request body limit applies on top and is authoritative, so several individually-legal images can still exceed it. A violation is refused with 400 BEFORE the turn is accepted: nothing is silently dropped. `path` is not supported here: it would name a file on the CALLER's machine, so an attachment with a non-empty path refuses the whole request with 400 bad_request before a turn is accepted. If the active model cannot accept images the daemon reports that on the session stream.

info.title: hoody-agent session events
info.description: Session events sent to the client by POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/prompt:stream. A session event (a message titled event.<name>) is sent inside an envelope {seq, incarnation, turn_id?, gate?, event: {type, data}}: the message title is event.type and the message payload describes event.data. Every other message is sent as described, outside the envelope.

oneOf.name: EventAccountRotated
oneOf.title: event.account_rotated
oneOf.description: Provider account rotated mid-turn.

payload.description: Free-form payload. Provider account rotated mid-turn.

oneOf.name: EventAgentDone
oneOf.title: event.agent_done
oneOf.description: Turn complete: it ends a prompt turn. Carries the turn's typed outcome / error_code and notices [{code, message?, detail?}]. Notices are advisory, never an error: hook_skipped_by_policy when a configured user hook was skipped under the always policy, agent_compacts_itself when a Claude Code session's agent decides on its own when to compact its conversation, history_unsaved when a Claude Code session answered from a conversation Hoody could not save, spend_cap_warning when the session's spend file sets action warn and the turn ran over a spend cap (detail session_cap or turn_cap; one notice per cap) (open set). A turn a spend cap stopped fails with error_code spend_cap.

turns.description: The session's current count of recorded turns, the numbering POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/trim uses. Do not count agent_done frames instead: some commands end without recording a turn, and compaction renumbers. Omitted when 0.

outcome.description: How the turn stopped running. It says nothing about whether the task was done well. Omitted when the agent cannot classify it.

turn_id.description: The turn this closes: the id the dispatching request returned (X-Hoody-Turn-Id, the 202 turn_id). Omitted for a turn not dispatched with one: TUI input, a loop fire, a background-task fire, an auto-reply round.

error_code.description: A stable machine code when outcome is failed. Omitted otherwise. Key hints on it, never on message text.

code.description: A stable code, for example hook_skipped_by_policy.

message.description: A short description. Omitted when none.

detail.description: Optional context; for hook_skipped_by_policy, the hook event and matcher. Omitted when none.

notices.description: Coded facts about how this turn ran that are not errors, for example hook_skipped_by_policy, or spend_cap_warning (detail session_cap or turn_cap) when the turn ran over a spend cap set to warn. Open set. Omitted when there are none.

run_id.description: The workflow run, as in workflows.get_run and GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs/{run_id}. The note names it too.

note.description: The app-generated outcome note, recorded on the user side: the workflow name, the run id, completed, FAILED (with a short error) or cancelled, and how long it ran.

ack.description: The fixed acknowledgement recorded on the assistant side after the note.

workflow_note.description: Set when this closes a workflow run started in the session: the outcome note the agent recorded in the conversation, so the model knows how the run ended. It is its own recorded turn (turns counts it). A reload of the transcript shows the same two messages. Omitted on every other turn.

payload.description: Turn complete: it ends a prompt turn. Carries the turn's typed outcome / error_code and notices [{code, message?, detail?}]. Notices are advisory, never an error: hook_skipped_by_policy when a configured user hook was skipped under the always policy, agent_compacts_itself when a Claude Code session's agent decides on its own when to compact its conversation, history_unsaved when a Claude Code session answered from a conversation Hoody could not save, spend_cap_warning when the session's spend file sets action warn and the turn ran over a spend cap (detail session_cap or turn_cap; one notice per cap) (open set). A turn a spend cap stopped fails with error_code spend_cap.

oneOf.name: EventApprovalPolicyChanged
oneOf.title: event.approval_policy_changed
oneOf.description: The session's approval policy (mode / lock / rules) changed; carries the new revision.

payload.description: Free-form payload. The session's approval policy (mode / lock / rules) changed; carries the new revision.

oneOf.name: EventAuthChanged
oneOf.title: event.auth_changed
oneOf.description: Hoody platform auth state changed: login, token adopt, or logout (global broadcast; mirrors GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status).

payload.description: Free-form payload. Hoody platform auth state changed: login, token adopt, or logout (global broadcast; mirrors GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status).

oneOf.name: EventAutoReply
oneOf.title: event.auto_reply
oneOf.description: Auto-user composed the next user turn.

payload.description: Free-form payload. Auto-user composed the next user turn.

oneOf.name: EventAutoReplyProgress
oneOf.title: event.auto_reply_progress
oneOf.description: Auto-user composition progress.

payload.description: Free-form payload. Auto-user composition progress.

oneOf.name: EventBashJobList
oneOf.title: event.bash_job_list
oneOf.description: Background bash job list snapshot.

id.description: The job's id (the job_id of GET /sessions/{id}/bash-jobs).

command.description: The command the job runs. Omitted when empty.

running.description: Whether the job is still running.

interactive.description: Whether the job runs on a terminal that can be attached; always true in this list.

exit.description: The exit status text once the job finished. Omitted while it runs.

jobs.description: The background shells that can be attached as a terminal, running or recently finished; null or empty when there are none. GET /sessions/{id}/bash-jobs lists every background shell the session started.

payload.description: Background bash job list snapshot.

oneOf.name: EventBashJobOutput
oneOf.title: event.bash_job_output
oneOf.description: Background bash job output tail chunk.

job_id.description: The job.

data.description: A chunk of the job's terminal output, base64 (it carries raw control bytes). Omitted when empty.

next_offset.description: The output offset after this chunk; attach again from it to continue. Omitted when 0.

gap.description: true when output before this chunk was dropped because the viewer fell behind. Omitted when false.

eof.description: true on the final event: the job ended, or there is no such attachable job. Omitted when false.

exit.description: The job's exit status text, on the final event once it is known. Omitted otherwise.

err.description: Why the attach ended without output (for example, no such job). Omitted otherwise.

payload.description: Background bash job output tail chunk.

oneOf.name: EventClear
oneOf.title: event.clear
oneOf.description: Conversation cleared.

payload.description: Free-form payload. Conversation cleared.

oneOf.name: EventCommandCommitted
oneOf.title: event.command_committed
oneOf.description: Commands sent with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands reached the session: messages added to the conversation (how next_step inside the running turn, new_turn in a turn of their own, with turn_id), or a stop carried out (how stop, with what it stopped). Carries command_ids.

command_ids.description: The commands, in the order they were sent.

turn_id.description: The turn they reached (how next_step: the running turn; new_turn: the turn they started). Omitted for a stop, and for a turn not dispatched with an id.

how.description: next_step: added inside the running turn; new_turn: started a turn; stop: a stop carried out.

kind.description: What was stopped: session (the running turn or parked gate), task (a background task), workflow_run, bash_job (a background shell the session started, on this machine or its computer), loop (paused, not deleted).

id.description: The item's id: the session id, <session id>/<task id> for a task, a run id, a bash job id or a loop id.

outcome.description: stopped: the stop reached running work and it ended (a loop: paused). already_done: it had finished before the stop reached it. failed: it was still running when the checks ended; detail says why.

detail.description: Present on failed: why.

cleanup.description: Present on stopped when the stop could not guarantee it reached every process the work started: detached_may_survive means a process a shell command of the work started in the background (detached) may still be running. Absent when the stop reached them all.

stopped.description: A stop: the work it acted on and how each ended. Omitted otherwise.

cleanup.description: A committed stop, whether or not it found work running: detached_may_survive means a shell command the session ran may have left a process (started in the background, detached) that no stop can be shown to have reached, so it may still be running. Absent when there is no such process.

payload.description: Commands sent with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands reached the session: messages added to the conversation (how next_step inside the running turn, new_turn in a turn of their own, with turn_id), or a stop carried out (how stop, with what it stopped). Carries command_ids.

oneOf.name: EventCommandSettled
oneOf.title: event.command_settled
oneOf.description: Commands sent with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands ended without reaching the session: superseded by a stop, refused (a hook blocked them, the session closed, or the session cannot take them) or failed (the session could not record them). Carries command_ids, state and reason.

state.description: What they became.

reason.description: Why (as the receipt's reason).

detail.description: More about reason. Omitted when none.

superseded_by.description: The stop that superseded them. Omitted otherwise.

payload.description: Commands sent with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/commands ended without reaching the session: superseded by a stop, refused (a hook blocked them, the session closed, or the session cannot take them) or failed (the session could not record them). Carries command_ids, state and reason.

oneOf.name: EventWaiterDone
oneOf.title: event.waiter_done
oneOf.description: A waiter this session owns (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters) ended: an outcome was found, or it timed out, was cancelled, or its target closed. Carries the waiter.

label.description: The label it was created with.

owner.description: The session that waits (the path session).

name.description: The outcome's name: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. timeout, cancelled, target_closed, interrupted, access_lost and judge_unavailable are reserved.

when.description: A sentence describing one event to look for, for example "the unit tests pass" or "a file named report.md is written" (at most 300 characters). It is judged by a model against the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; what the worker writes in its replies is not evidence. Name one event: counting, times and and/or conditions are not judged reliably; use match, or several outcomes. Give exactly one of when and match.

kind.description: The kind of event.

tool.description: The tool's name, for example bash or write_file.

exit_code.description: tool_result only: the exit status the command must have ended with. A result with no observed exit status never matches.

is_error.description: tool_result only: whether the tool reported an error.

text_contains.description: Text the event must contain (case-sensitive, at most 200 characters).

outcome.description: turn_end only: how the turn ended.

match.description: An exact event: every given field must hold. Checked on every event, without a model. Give exactly one of when and match.

from.description: The target turn it reads from, when one was given.

state.description: waiting or done.

outcome.description: When done: the name of the outcome found, or timeout (nothing found before the deadline), cancelled (by request, or the owner session closed), target_closed (the watched session ended first), interrupted (the agent restarted while waiting; events in between were not watched), access_lost (the current login can no longer reach a session or its realm) or judge_unavailable (judged outcomes could not be checked and no exact outcome was left).

reason.description: A sentence saying why it ended.

also_found.description: Other outcomes found in the same check, in the order they were given.

seq.description: The event's number in the target's event list.

turn_id.description: The target turn the event belongs to, when it has one.

kind.description: The event's kind.

tool.description: The tool's name.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, when observed.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported an error.

excerpt.description: The start of the event's text, with secrets removed.

by.description: match: an exact outcome matched. judge: a model judged that the events show the outcome; it points at this event, it does not prove it.

p.description: judge only: the model's probability that the events show the outcome.

evidence.description: The event the outcome was found in.

on_timeout.description: What the creator said to do on timeout, kept for the creator's use; the agent does not act on it.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from creation to the end.

max_checks.description: The most model requests it may make (a retried request counts again).

gap.description: true when some target events may not have been read (the start turn was too old, or many events arrived at once).

cost_usd.description: What its model checks cost, in US dollars.

cost_known.description: false when the price of some check was not reported.

model.description: The model judged outcomes are checked with.

waiter.description: The waiter, ended (as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters/{waiter_id} returns it).

payload.description: A waiter this session owns (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters) ended: an outcome was found, or it timed out, was cancelled, or its target closed. Carries the waiter.

oneOf.name: EventConfirmRequest
oneOf.title: event.confirm_request
oneOf.description: Tool/plan confirmation requested (parks a gate). On a helper_gates session a helper's request carries helper_id, parent_tool_call_id and, for a background helper, task_id; it parks beside the session's own gate and is answered by its own id.

tool_name.description: The tool waiting for a decision.

params.description: The tool input the decision is about, redacted, without the agent's own dispatch markers. Always present; null when the call had no input.

requested_dirs.description: Directories outside the session's scope the call needs. Omitted when none.

detail.description: A preview for the person deciding: a fenced command or a diff. A call that touches a known credential store starts with a line ⚠ credential store: <label> (not on an edit's diff or a dangerous card). A gate parked because the tool-call rules could not be checked starts with a line ⚠ rules not checked: <why>. Omitted when none.

offer_session_allow.description: true when an allow-for-the-session answer may be offered (session_scope on /confirm). Omitted when false.

gate_id.description: The agent's own number for this gate, for diagnostics. It is NOT what /confirm takes: echo the frame envelope's gate.id.

gate_cause.description: Why the gate exists, for example static_stakes, dir_access, hook_ask or approval_policy. Open set. Omitted by an older agent.

risk.description: The agent's coarse risk label for the call: read, write or destructive for a fleet action, write for a file write or edit, destructive for a file delete, high for a human-only gate, credential_access when a read, write or unknown call touches a known credential store (a label only: it parks and denies nothing by itself), unknown when the call has no class. Omitted by an older agent.

human_only.description: true when no automatic policy may answer this gate; a person must. Always present.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation a decision must carry (lease_generation on /confirm). Omitted when there is no lease.

lease_required.description: true when the decision must come from the approver-lease holder. Always present.

task_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the background task of the helper that parked the gate. Omitted otherwise.

computer_id.description: The resolved computer id the grant is keyed by.

computer_name.description: The computer name the call used. Omitted when the call named the id.

realm.description: The realm the grant applies in: _global or a realm id.

label.description: Button text, for example Always allow exec on my-box.

exec_trust.description: On a hoody_exec_* card: the per-computer trust option. Answer /confirm with approved true and trust_computer true to run the call and stop exec cards on that computer in this realm until the grant is revoked (exec_trust on POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules). Omitted when no grant can be offered: another tool, a computer that did not resolve, a hook or rules ask, the always approval policy, a headless session.

rule_ids.description: The ids of the rules behind it, in settings order (the same ids GET /api/v1/agent/hooks and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies report).

outcome.description: ask: check-in rules cover the call. deny: the call breaks these limit rules. unchecked: the rules check could not complete (Jev failed or timed out, the input was too large, or the rules await a trust ack); rule_ids is every rule the check covered.

reason.description: Why the rules check could not complete, in plain words (for example Jev has no usable key for its model's provider). Only with outcome unchecked; omitted otherwise.

rules.description: When tool-call rules asked: the rules behind the gate. outcome ask = these check_in rules cover the call; unchecked = the rules check could not complete, so it asks instead (rule_ids = every rule it covered). gate_cause is rules when only rules asked; when a shell hook asked too it stays hook_ask and rules is still present. Omitted when no rule asked.

helper_id.description: The helper that produced this event (a background helper's task id, or a per-spawn helper id). Omitted on the session's own events.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted on the session's own events.

payload.description: Tool/plan confirmation requested (parks a gate). On a helper_gates session a helper's request carries helper_id, parent_tool_call_id and, for a background helper, task_id; it parks beside the session's own gate and is answered by its own id.

oneOf.name: EventDecisionRequirements
oneOf.title: event.decision_requirements
oneOf.description: The decision requirements of the PARKED gate changed (the approver lease was acquired, taken over, renewed past expiry or released while a gate is parked): {gate_id, generation, lease_required, helper_id?}. A client that captured the gate at park time refreshes what its decision must carry. On a helper_gates session each parked helper confirm is re-announced too, with its helper_id.

gate_id.description: The agent's own number for the parked confirm (the payload gate_id of its event.confirm_request). It is NOT what /confirm takes.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation a decision must now carry (lease_generation on /confirm); 0 when there is no lease.

lease_required.description: true when the decision must now come from the approver-lease holder.

helper_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the helper whose parked confirm this is. Omitted for the session's own gate.

payload.description: The decision requirements of the PARKED gate changed (the approver lease was acquired, taken over, renewed past expiry or released while a gate is parked): {gate_id, generation, lease_required, helper_id?}. A client that captured the gate at park time refreshes what its decision must carry. On a helper_gates session each parked helper confirm is re-announced too, with its helper_id.

oneOf.description: A delegated turn went quiet past the stall window but is still running (not fatal, not an error).

agent.description: The delegated agent that went quiet.

idle_ms.description: The stall window it went quiet for, in milliseconds.

message.description: A sentence to show the person: the turn is still running and can be stopped.

oneOf.name: EventError
oneOf.title: event.error
oneOf.description: Session error (e.g. join_not_ready).

code.description: A machine code when there is one, for example session_not_found or session_busy, or quota_wait_too_long / rate_limit when a model rate limit ended the turn, or model_unavailable when the provider refused the model itself, or spend_cap when a spend cap refused or stopped the turn or the spend settings file is not valid (agent_done carries the same error_code). Omitted otherwise.

provider.description: The provider id. Omitted when unknown.

model.description: The model name without its provider prefix. Omitted when unknown.

base_url.description: The endpoint called, without credentials or query. Omitted when unknown.

key_source.description: Where the key came from: env, dotenv, oauth-token, network or none. Omitted when unknown.

key_prefix.description: A redacted fragment of the key, never the key. Omitted when none.

http_status.description: The provider's HTTP status. Omitted when the failure was not an HTTP error.

retryable.description: Whether the failure was classed retryable. Omitted when false.

attempts.description: Attempts made before giving up. Omitted when unknown.

req_id.description: The turn's id in the agent's log (per-attempt rows are <id>.N), to find the full cause in GET /api/v1/agent/logs. Omitted when none.

err_code.description: The failure class, shared with the usage statistics: max_tokens is a tool call cut off at the model's output limit, bad_tool_args tool calls whose arguments were not valid JSON too many times in one turn. Omitted when unclassified.

stop_reason.description: Why the model stopped writing the response that failed, when it said: max_tokens means the answer was cut off at the model's output limit. Omitted when unknown.

last_error.description: The last attempt's cause: one line, credentials scrubbed, at most 600 characters. Omitted when none.

diag.description: Provider diagnostics for a failed model call (provider, model, endpoint, key source and a redacted prefix, HTTP status, attempts). With code no_credentials it names the provider and model that have no stored key. Omitted for every other error.

max_steps.description: With code max_steps: the step limit in force for the turn that stopped (the agent's max_steps_per_turn). Omitted on every other error.

reason.description: With code delegated_agent_unavailable: why the realm's default delegated agent cannot start here (unknown_agent, disabled, not_installed, missing_launcher, probe_failure or settings_unreadable). With code spend_cap: session_cap (the session's spend reached max_session_usd), turn_cap (the turn's own model requests reached max_turn_usd) or invalid_setting (the spend settings file is not valid, so no work runs until it is fixed or deleted; the message names the file's path and the problem). Omitted on every other error.

retry_after_secs.description: The seconds the model provider asked to wait before the next request: always with code quota_wait_too_long (the turn ended instead of waiting), and on a failed model request whose last answer (a rate limit or a busy provider) named a wait. Send the message again after that. Omitted otherwise.

retry_at.description: With retry_after_secs: when that wait ends, RFC 3339 in UTC (for example 2026-10-10T14:47:00Z), the same time the message names. Send the message again after it. Omitted otherwise.

spend_cap_usd.description: With code spend_cap and reason session_cap or turn_cap: the cap that was reached, in US dollars. Omitted otherwise.

spent_usd.description: With spend_cap_usd: the spend that reached it, in US dollars (the session's whole spend for session_cap, the turn's own model requests for turn_cap). Omitted otherwise.

resume_run_id.description: With code resume_superseded (a workflow run's resume was refused after it was accepted, because a newer run of the same original run started a step): the run to resume instead. Omitted otherwise.

payload.description: Session error (e.g. join_not_ready).

oneOf.name: EventGateResolved
oneOf.title: event.gate_resolved
oneOf.description: A parked confirm/question gate was resolved (possibly by another attached client).

kind.description: Which kind of gate was resolved.

gate_id.description: The agent's own number for a resolved confirm gate. Omitted on a question gate.

question_id.description: The agent's own number for a resolved question gate. Omitted on a confirm gate.

outcome.description: How the gate ended: answered by a decision, cancelled without one, auto-approved by switching YOLO mode on while it was parked, or (a helper's gate only) denied because nobody answered within the helper agent's ask_timeout.

provenance.description: What resolved the gate. Only decision is a real answer; every other value means nobody decided, and the outcome is then never answered. timeout is a helper's gate that ran out of time. Omitted by an older agent.

holder.description: The approver-lease holder whose decision resolved a confirm gate (the holder sent when the lease was acquired). Omitted when there is none.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation the decision was made under. Omitted when there is none.

request_id.description: The request id of the decision that resolved the gate, when that decision carried one. On the copy sent only to the sender of a retried or late decision (one naming a gate that already resolved, including a helper gate that timed out or was cancelled while the decision was in flight), it is that decision's own request id.

helper_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the helper that parked this gate (its event.confirm_request or event.user_question carried the same helper_id). Omitted for the session's own gates.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted for the session's own gates.

task_id.description: The background task of that helper (equal to helper_id). Omitted for a foreground helper and for the session's own gates.

approved.description: The tool was approved (true) or denied.

persist_dirs.description: An approved directory grant was persisted to settings.json.

session_scope.description: The decision was asked to apply for the rest of the session.

trust_computer.description: The gate's exec_trust offer was accepted.

remember.description: false when the approval applied to this call only (sent with remember false). Omitted otherwise.

superseded.description: true when the call was declined because the user sent a new message instead (sent with superseded true). Omitted otherwise.

decision.description: On a confirm gate whose outcome is answered: the decision it consumed. Omitted otherwise.

session_scope_applied.description: false when an approving session_scope decision applied once only (a locked approval policy keeps the session-wide rule from being added); see note. Omitted otherwise.

note.description: Present beside session_scope_applied: why the wider grant did not apply.

payload.description: A parked confirm/question gate was resolved (possibly by another attached client).

oneOf.name: EventSessionStarted
oneOf.title: event.session_started
oneOf.description: Session attached. Its data is the same `started` object POST /api/v1/agent/sessions returns. It is the first frame (seq 1) of a fresh attach while the stream still retains seq 1. A resume with `since` does not repeat it, except when the cursor cannot be resumed: an invalid `since` (or Last-Event-ID), an `incarnation` that does not match the session's current one, or a cursor ahead of the stream is each answered with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) and the whole retained stream, which includes it if seq 1 is still retained. A late attach after the oldest frames were evicted starts with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) instead and does not carry it. In either case read the same object as `started` from GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}, which carries it while the session is attached.

It is the first frame (seq 1) of a fresh attach while the stream still retains seq 1. A resume with `since` does not repeat it, except when the cursor cannot be resumed: an invalid `since` (or Last-Event-ID), an `incarnation` that does not match the session's current one, or a cursor ahead of the stream is each answered with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) and the whole retained stream, which includes it if seq 1 is still retained. A late attach after the oldest frames were evicted starts with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) instead and does not carry it. In either case read the same object as `started` from GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}, which carries it while the session is attached.

A client holding every frame after it can reconnect with ?since=turn_since to replay the whole turn. post.summary: Dispatch a turn and block until it ends (no reply text: read it from the transcript)
post.description: Dispatches a turn and blocks until agent_done. The response carries the outcome (status, turn_id), not the assistant's reply: read the reply with GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/transcript (hoody agent sessions transcript get --id <id>) or from the stream. By default (interactive posture) it returns {pending_gate} the moment a turn parks: it NEVER auto-approves implicitly. Repeated prompt:sync against a parked session returns the SAME pending_gate (no duplicate parked turns). The explicit X-Hoody-Gate-Policy: auto_approve header (or ?policy=auto_approve) adopts the headless posture and auto-answers confirm gates with approved=true, except a gate a tool-call rule raised (the confirm_request carries rules: a check-in, or rules that could not be checked) and a destructive-shape gate (gate_cause static_stakes: a recursive force delete, curl piped to a shell, sudo, a force push...), which it answers approved=false; a human_only gate is never answered automatically: it returns as {pending_gate} for a person, as under the interactive posture, off by default; the gateway asks for no separate credentials to use it; access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy. The request waits at most 290 seconds (the gateway's prompt-sync timeout, under the 300-second response-header limit of Node's fetch): a turn still running then answers 503 service_unavailable with details.turn_id and details.turn_running:true, or {pending_gate} when a gate needs a person. The turn is not cancelled: follow it on the stream or with GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}. Under auto_approve the posture is bound to the TURN, not the request: once the request has ended (timeout, or the client went away) the gateway keeps auto-answering that turn's confirm gates until it ends (details.auto_approve:"until_turn_end"); question and plan gates still wait for /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer or /plan.

requestBody.description: Turn input: the user text, optional inline image attachments, plus the optional tool_mode / dir_scope the session's first turn fixes.

text.description: Required (may be empty only with attachments). The user message text for this turn: empty or whitespace-only text with no attachments is refused (400 empty_prompt) and no turn runs.

On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode; any other value is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode too.

dir_scope.description: Optional directory-access scope: home or full. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (dir_scope_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope; any other value is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope too.

get.description: Returns the tool-call rules a live session checks for one agent's calls, from the same selection the rules check itself runs: a rule without `tools` skips read-only tools, a rule with `tools` covers only those, and a rule with `agents` covers only those agents' calls. `agent` defaults to the session's own agent; name a helper's or a workflow step's agent to see what its calls are checked against. With `tool`, the reply's checked rules (applies_as: checked) are exactly the rules sent to Jev for that call; without it, every checked rule that covers the agent's calls to some tool. Either way the reply also lists the prompt rules below, and count covers both (a thread header's count). `fail_closed_reason` says when every covered call fails closed right now. Guidance and playbook rules are listed too, with `applies_as: prompt`: the ones the agent's team-rules system block carries, from the same selection the injection uses; `prompt_over_budget` names covered ones that did not fit the byte budget. A dormant session answers 404 not_found. Cache-Control: no-store.

schema.description: The rules the session checks for the agent's calls.

agent.description: The acting agent asked about: the `agent` query value, else the session's own agent (its chat agent, or orchestrator in orchestrator mode).

tool.description: The tool asked about. Omitted when no tool was named.

read_only.description: Whether the named tool is read-only (a rule without a `tools` list skips read-only tools). Omitted when no tool was named.

active.description: Whether the session has rules that are checked at all (limit or check_in, covering at least one call). Guidance and playbook rules never make it true, nor does a checked rule that names only tools no rule checks.

count.description: len(rules): the rules that apply to the agent, checked and prompt together.

text.description: The rule in plain words.

kind.description: limit: a call that breaks the rule is denied. check_in: a call the rule covers asks the user first. guidance: standing advice the covered agents follow. playbook: a procedure the covered agents follow when the situation its text describes comes up. limit and check_in are checked by Jev before covered tool calls; guidance and playbook are never checked, they are added to the system prompt of every session and helper they cover.

applies_as.description: Output only, derived from kind: POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules ignores it and never lets it change kind. How the rule reaches the agent: checked = Jev checks covered tool calls against it (limit, check_in); prompt = its text is in the covered agents' system prompt, in the team-rules block (guidance, playbook).

tools.description: The tools the rule is limited to; empty = every tool that is not read-only, except ask_question_to_user, report_outcome and request_view, which only a rule naming them covers. The Bot's control tools (stop, peek, delegates, answer_gate, wait) are never checked. Always empty for guidance and playbook rules.

agents.description: The agents whose calls the rule covers; empty = every agent.

when.description: The rule's condition as written (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules `when`); absent when it has none. A rule with `when` is listed as applying. Whether it applies to a call depends on the calls made earlier in that turn; it applies whenever the daemon cannot see the turn's calls: after `run_workflow` or `tool_orchestrator`, after a restart, after a tool error it cannot classify, in a fusion turn, after more than 256 calls, while a Claude Code call is unsettled or held, after a call from a Claude Code subagent, or in a Claude Code session whose tools do not run through Hoody.

source.description: The settings file that declared the rule.

scope.description: Output only: the settings scope whose file declared the rule, the scope POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules writes that file through (user: the realm's profile settings; project: the folder's shared settings file, or the X-Hoody-Config-Dir settings.json; local: the folder's personal settings file, settings.local.json, or the X-Hoody-Config-Dir settings.local.json). Always set for a rule read from a scope's file; when two scopes name one file, the first in load order (user, project, local). POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules ignores it.

folder.description: Output only, on project and local rules: the folder those scopes belong to, as the daemon's settings resolution names it. With a config dir it is that directory: X-Hoody-Config-Dir (GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules) or the session's config dir. Otherwise it is the folder whose settings hold the file: the X-Hoody-Cwd directory (GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules), or the session's settings folder (GET /api/v1/agent/hooks, POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies), the cwd its settings were resolved for, which can differ from the directory a remote or delegated session runs in. Absent on user rules. POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules ignores it.

rules.description: The rules that apply to the agent, in settings order. applies_as checked: with a tool, exactly the rules the check sends to Jev for that agent's call to that tool; without one, every checked rule that covers the agent's calls to at least one tool. applies_as prompt: the guidance and playbook rules the agent's team-rules block carries (with or without a tool; they are never sent to Jev); none when prompt_off is true.

prompt_off.description: Whether prompt_blocks drops the team-rules block for this agent (team_rules: false), so no guidance or playbook rule reaches it. For the session's own agent this is the session's prompt_blocks over the agent's frontmatter, which is what the session itself uses; a helper of the same agent follows its frontmatter alone. For any other agent it is that agent's frontmatter, as a helper uses it.

prompt_bytes.description: The size in bytes of the rule lines the agent's team-rules block carries (each line is `- [id] text` and a newline). 0 when prompt_off is true.

prompt_budget_bytes.description: The most rule-line bytes one agent's team-rules block carries (8192). Rules are taken in settings order; one that does not fit is left out and listed in prompt_over_budget, and a later one that fits still goes in.

get.summary: List the slash commands a session's chat offers.
get.description: Returns the commands a user can type after a slash in a LIVE session's chat, in display order: the built-in commands, then the session's enabled skills (only those the session's skill settings and its agent allow; names and descriptions, never a skill's body). Each entry says whether it takes an argument and whether only the terminal app runs it (tui_only). A skill entry also says where the skill comes from (source: bundled, project, user or config) and, when the agent does not trust it, untrusted; built-in entries carry neither. To run one that is not tui_only, send it as the text of a turn (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns or /messages), for example `/compact` or `/<skill> <text>`. Two forms only a person at the terminal app may run are refused in a turn sent through this API: `/memory consolidate` and `/memory wipe CONFIRM`. A skill named like a built-in command, or exit, is not listed: what its text does then depends on its arguments and on the client. The skills are the ones the session last announced to its clients, so a skill enabled a moment ago shows once the session has re-read its skills. Pagination: pass ?page=N&limit=M for a window; omit limit for the full list. 404 when the session is not live.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of slash commands, in display order.

name.description: The command name, typed after a leading slash (`compact` is sent as `/compact`).

description.description: One line saying what the command does. A skill's description is written by the skill's author.

kind.description: `builtin` for a command the agent ships, `skill` for one of the session's enabled skills.

category.description: The group the command is listed under. Elements of one category are contiguous, in display order.

args.description: Whether the command takes text after its name: `none` (the bare command), `optional` (the bare form works; text changes what it does) or `required` (the bare form is a usage error).

tui_only.description: True for a command only the terminal app runs. Sent in a message to this API it is not a command: it reaches the model as ordinary text. A false entry works as the text of a turn sent with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns or /messages.

source.description: Skills only; absent on built-in commands. Where the copy of the skill the session uses comes from: `bundled` for a skill that ships with Hoody and that Hoody keeps up to date, `project` for one in the session's project, `user` for the person's own, `config` for one in the configuration the agent was started with. A person's own skill named like a bundled one reads by where it is, never `bundled`.

untrusted.description: Skills only; absent on built-in commands and on trusted skills. True when the agent will not run the skill's commands or show its description to the model until a person trusts it, for example an installed skill nobody has trusted yet, or one whose files changed after it was trusted.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages (the full count, not the page size).

limit.description: Items per page (present only when limit>0).

items.description: Summarize all but the last turn to free context (/compact N keeps turns after N)
items.name: compact

items.description: Fork a new session from a turn (/fork [N]; omit N for the last turn)
items.name: fork

get.description: Returns one consistent snapshot a client can rebuild from: the daemon's state object: session_id, epoch, state (idle | running | parked; closed when this gateway's reaper committed the close), current_turn_id, queued_turn_ids, the approval policy + waiver posture, the redacted pending_gate (with its decision requirements: generation, lease_required) and last_detach {reason: last_client_cancelled | process_restart, at}, paired with this gateway's stream watermark: incarnation and seq (resume the stream with ?since=seq&incarnation=…; the watermark is read BEFORE the daemon snapshot, so any event that lands during the read is replayed, never lost) and, while a gate is parked, pending_gate_ref (the addressable id/generation + gate_cause/risk/human_only). TWO ids describe that one gate and only ONE is answerable: pending_gate_ref.id is the string POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm and /answer take, while the daemon's pending_gate.gate_id is a per-kind NUMBER for diagnostics. Echoing the number is refused (400, naming the field). Works for a live or dormant session (a dormant one carries no incarnation/seq). Cache-Control: no-store.

live.description: Whether the daemon session is live (false for a dormant record).

epoch.description: The daemon execution epoch (an opaque id) (changes on restart; leases and parked gates do not survive it).

state.description: Coarse state. running while a turn holds the session's single-writer slot, one this gateway dispatched or a peer client's, including the moment after the agent finished it and before its event.agent_done reached the stream: a new turn is refused turn_in_flight until the state is idle. current_turn_id may be null while running in that window.

current_turn_id.description: The turn the agent is running, if any. It may be null while state is running (see state).

approval.description: The effective approval policy + waiver posture (the same object GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approval returns).

gate_id.description: Confirm gates: the DAEMON's gate nonce. Diagnostic only: never echo it to /confirm; use pending_gate_ref.id.

question_id.description: Question gates: the DAEMON's question nonce. Diagnostic only: never echo it to /answer; use pending_gate_ref.id.

generation.description: The daemon's approver-lease generation for this gate: send it as lease_generation on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm. Never echo it as generation; that is pending_gate_ref.generation.

tool_name.description: The tool awaiting a decision (confirm gates).

requested_dirs.description: Directories the run asked to reach outside the session's scope.

gate_cause.description: Why the gate parked (e.g. approval_policy, static_stakes, dir_scope).

risk.description: The daemon's risk assessment of the parked action (as event.confirm_request's risk).

human_only.description: True when only a human may answer (a machine-stamped decision is refused).

lease_required.description: True when the answer must carry the approver lease (X-Hoody-Approver-Lease).

status.description: The gate's status as the daemon sees it.

params.description: The tool input the decision is about, redacted, without the agent's own dispatch markers. Always present; null when the call had no input.

detail.description: A preview for the person deciding: a fenced command or a diff. A call that touches a known credential store starts with a line ⚠ credential store: <label> (not on an edit's diff or a dangerous card). A gate parked because the tool-call rules could not be checked starts with a line ⚠ rules not checked: <why>. Omitted when none.

offer_session_allow.description: true when an allow-for-the-session answer may be offered (session_scope on /confirm). Omitted when false.

computer_id.description: The resolved computer id the grant is keyed by.

computer_name.description: The computer name the call used. Omitted when the call named the id.

realm.description: The realm the grant applies in: _global or a realm id.

label.description: Button text, for example Always allow exec on my-box.

exec_trust.description: On a hoody_exec_* card: the per-computer trust option. Answer /confirm with approved true and trust_computer true to run the call and stop exec cards on that computer in this realm until the grant is revoked (exec_trust on POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules). Omitted when no grant can be offered: another tool, a computer that did not resolve, a hook or rules ask, the always approval policy, a headless session.

rule_ids.description: The ids of the rules behind it, in settings order (the same ids GET /api/v1/agent/hooks and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies report).

outcome.description: ask: check-in rules cover the call. deny: the call breaks these limit rules. unchecked: the rules check could not complete (Jev failed or timed out, the input was too large, or the rules await a trust ack); rule_ids is every rule the check covered.

reason.description: Why the rules check could not complete, in plain words (for example Jev has no usable key for its model's provider). Only with outcome unchecked; omitted otherwise.

rules.description: When tool-call rules asked: the rules behind the gate. outcome ask = these check_in rules cover the call; unchecked = the rules check could not complete, so it asks instead (rule_ids = every rule it covered). gate_cause is rules when only rules asked; when a shell hook asked too it stays hook_ask and rules is still present. Omitted when no rule asked.

question.description: The question, for a single question. Always present; empty on a batch, which uses questions instead.

options.description: Suggested answers for a single question (answer). Always present: null on a batch, and it may be empty, in which case any text is accepted.

has_user_input.description: true when choosing it also takes free text. Omitted when false.

rich_options.description: Structured options (workflow tool steps). Omitted when none.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text for a free-form answer. Omitted when none.

category.description: A short label for the question. Omitted when none. frame_request on a question a request_view or a Bot tool parked (frame_request is then set).

kind.description: view: a View the Frame is asked to make. bot.dispatch, bot.message, bot.stop, bot.delegates, bot.answer_gate, bot.peek, bot.wait: a Bot tool call, answered by the Bot runtime.

request.description: view: the request, in the user's words. A Bot tool: the call's input, as a JSON object.

id.description: This park's own id, minted per call: with the session and gate ids it names the job answering it.

tool_use_id.description: A Bot tool: the tool_use id of the model's call that parked it, which matches the request with the Bot's transcript. Model providers can repeat tool ids, so the job answering it is named by id. Omitted for a view.

frame_request.description: On a frame_tools session, a question the model's request_view parked: what it asks the Frame to make. The Frame answers it on /answer with its status JSON as answer. On a Bot's own session, a call to one of the Bot's tools (kind bot.dispatch, bot.message, bot.stop, bot.delegates, bot.answer_gate or bot.peek), answered by the Bot runtime. Omitted on every other question.

id.description: The key to answer this question under, in answers.

category.description: A short label for the question.

options.description: Suggested answers. Omitted when any text is accepted.

questions.description: A batch of questions; when present it replaces the single-question fields. Answer each by its id in answers.

pending_gate.description: The DAEMON's gate (its own numbers): never echo it to /confirm or /answer; echo pending_gate_ref.id and pending_gate_ref.generation. It describes the parked gate (what is being asked) or is null. Its gate_id is the daemon's own per-kind counter (confirm ids and question ids are separate spaces) and is NOT what POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm takes: that route takes the addressable string published as pending_gate_ref.id below (and as pending_gate.id on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} and /replay, and as the stream frame ENVELOPE's gate.id (a sibling of `event`, NOT a field inside the event payload; the payload's own gate_id is the daemon's number)). Besides status, type, generation and lease_required, it carries the fields of the parked gate's event (event.confirm_request or event.user_question) at this level.

last_detach.description: How the last detach ended {reason: last_client_cancelled | process_restart, at}, or null.

effort.description: Live sessions only: the reasoning-effort override set with PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/effort. Absent while the model's default applies. Not kept across a daemon restart, and cleared by a model switch. On a Claude Code (delegated) session it is the effort Claude Code runs with: the PATCH value, else the configured default, with an explicit model_settings thinking effort winning; it is kept with the session across a restart and a model switch, and absent while Claude Code's own default applies.

verbosity.description: Live sessions only: the response-verbosity level (PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/verbosity). A restart starts from the ui.verbosity default.

command_capability.description: How soon the session reads a new message sent while it works. next_step: before its next model request. turn_end: when its current turn ends (a Claude Code session, a fusion model, while a workflow run holds the session, or while it runs a turn started by a loop or a finished background task). unsupported: a headless session, which takes no messages after it starts.

kind.description: model: the model is answering or about to be asked. tool: a tool call or a workflow run is running. gate: waiting for an approval or an answer. idle: no work is running.

tool.description: When kind is tool: the running tool call that started last, or run_workflow while a workflow run holds the session and no other call is running. Omitted otherwise.

since.description: When the session entered this step (RFC 3339). For a session that is not live, its last activity.

current_step.description: What the session is doing now, coarsely, and since when.

tokens.description: The size of the session's last prompt in tokens. 0 when unknown (no turn yet, or after a clear).

window.description: The context window the tokens are measured against, in tokens: the model's window, or for a Claude Code session the window Claude Code reports. 0 when unknown.

estimated.description: True when tokens is an estimate made by a compaction rather than a size the model provider reported; the next model request replaces it with a reported size.

context.description: How full the session's context is: the same reading the agent's own context meter shows.

after_compaction.description: The session's after-compaction message (PUT /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/after-compaction). Omitted when none is set.

kind.description: What opened the session.

bot_id.description: The Bot's id within its realm.

realm.description: The Bot's realm: global or a realm id.

ref.description: The Bot's reference for the work it handed to this session. Omitted on the Bot's own session.

origin.description: Present on a session a Bot opened, its own or a delegate: which Bot, and for a delegate the Bot's reference for the work it handed over. A fork does not carry it. Omitted on every other session.

incarnation.description: This gateway's stream namespace (live sessions only).

seq.description: The stream watermark read before the snapshot; resume with ?since=seq (live sessions only).

pending_lead_gates.description: Present only while the session's own turn has two or more gates parked (parallel workflow lanes): the daemon's description of each, oldest first, in pending_gate's shape; pending_gate is the oldest. Their gate_id numbers are diagnostic: answer each by its pending_lead_gate_refs id.

pending_lead_gate_refs.description: The ADDRESSABLE refs of pending_lead_gates, in the same order, each {id, generation, type, tool_name?, gate_cause?, risk?, human_only}. Answer one with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm by its id. A ref is published only for a gate the daemon still reports with the same type and nonce; one parked during the read appears on the next read. Omitted when none.

pending_helper_gate_refs.description: The ADDRESSABLE refs of the gates spawn_agent helpers have parked (a helper_gates session), oldest first, each {id, generation, type, tool_name?, gate_cause?, risk?, human_only, helper_id, parent_tool_call_id?, task_id?}. Answer one with POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /answer by its id. A ref is published only for a helper gate the daemon still reports with the same type, nonce and helper; one parked during the read appears on the next read. Omitted when none.

turn_since.description: While a turn runs (live sessions only): the stream cursor just before that turn's first frame. It says where the running turn starts among GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/replay events (its start was evicted only when turn_since is below min_seq - 1). After a reload that kept no cursor, attach from /replay max_seq and drop repeated seqs, not from turn_since: a turn can end between the two reads. It is read after the daemon snapshot, so it describes the turn still running then; match frames to a turn by their envelope turn_id. Omitted while idle.

id.description: The answerable gate id. Echo it verbatim as gate_id on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /answer. Scoped to the session incarnation, so an id from before a re-attach never matches.

generation.description: The hub gate generation. It restarts on re-attach, so it is not an identity on its own: send id.

tool_name.description: The tool awaiting a decision (confirm gates).

risk.description: The daemon's risk assessment (as event.confirm_request's risk).

human_only.description: True when only a human may answer.

pending_gate_ref.description: The identity to echo on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm or /answer: the ADDRESSABLE identity of the parked gate (live sessions), published only when it names the same gate as pending_gate (type and daemon nonce): when the gate changed during the read it is omitted and pending_gate stands alone; read again for the ref. Its id is the value POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm and /answer take: echo it verbatim; never build it yourself and never send pending_gate.gate_id instead.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.summary: Attach to a session's event stream (WebSocket / SSE).
get.description: WebSocket (primary) or SSE attach to a live session's full event.* taxonomy. Each frame is {seq, incarnation, turn_id?, gate?, event}: a gateway-stamped monotonic int64 seq and the incarnation that stamped it; turn_id, at the envelope level, is the id of the turn dispatched through this gateway that held the slot when the frame arrived (its agent_done included), omitted while idle, during a direct tool run and on a turn another client started, except on that turn's own user_echo, workflow_start and agent_done, which carry its id; ?since=<seq> / Last-Event-ID resume from the 1024-event replay ring (a gap past eviction emits event: lagged {code:replay_gap} then streams from min_seq). A session that is re-attached by the same id starts a new incarnation whose seq restarts at 1, so pass ?incarnation=<the one you last saw> with a resume cursor: a mismatch is answered with replay_gap and the full retained ring instead of a silent resume into a different history. A frame that parks a confirm/question gate also carries gate {id, generation, type} at the ENVELOPE level, beside seq/incarnation/event: the identity to echo on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm, /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer or a WS confirm/answer frame. Read it from the frame, not from the event payload: the payload of event.confirm_request carries the DAEMON's numeric gate_id, which is a different id space and is never what you echo. A WS client needs nothing but this frame to answer the gate. SSE NAMES DROP THE PREFIX: an SSE frame's `event:` line carries the taxonomy name with the leading "event." removed, while the JSON on the `data:` line keeps the full name, so `event.agent_done` arrives as `event: agent_done` wrapping `{"event":{"type":"event.agent_done", ...}}`. Match on the data payload's type, or add the prefix back, rather than comparing the SSE name to the taxonomy. The WS transport does no such rewriting: it delivers the frame verbatim. The gateway's own control frames (lagged, end, replay_boundary) are NOT taxonomy events and carry no prefix in either place. RE-JOINING AFTER A RELOAD: a page that kept the last seq it applied resumes with ?since=<that seq>&incarnation=<its incarnation>. A page that kept nothing reads GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/replay and applies its events, then attaches with ?since=<replay max_seq>&incarnation=<replay incarnation> and drops any frame whose seq it already applied: the cursor is never past the last frame the page holds, so a turn that ends between two reads is still delivered once. GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state turn_since only locates the running turn's first frame among the replayed ones (below min_seq: its start was evicted, so show that earlier output is unavailable). Turns older than the ring come from the transcript. The replay_boundary frame carries turn_id and turn_since too. Match a turn by its turn_id, never by taking the first agent_done as yours: a turn can end between two reads. A slow client is dropped lagged and never backpressures the daemon. WS clients may post inline answer frames (confirm/answer/cancel/workflow_message); a confirm frame is settled as POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm is, so a gate that already ended or a decision still in flight gets a refused frame (gate_already_resolved, gate_decision_pending); a workflow_message frame the daemon refuses (no_active_workflow when no workflow is running, or a realm code) or does not answer in time (admission_unconfirmed) gets a refused frame on that connection.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session id.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Resume from this gateway int64 seq (also accepted as the Last-Event-ID header).

parameters.name: incarnation
parameters.description: The incarnation the since cursor belongs to (from a frame, replay_boundary, or GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}). When it differs from the live session's, the cursor is treated as invalid: a replay_gap frame, then the full retained ring.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: SSE resume cursor: the gateway int64 seq to resume from (the in:header alias of ?since); sent automatically by an SSE client on reconnect.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

info.title: hoody-agent session events
info.description: Session events sent to the client by GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream. A session event (a message titled event.<name>) is sent inside an envelope {seq, incarnation, turn_id?, gate?, event: {type, data}}: the message title is event.type and the message payload describes event.data. Every other message is sent as described, outside the envelope.

oneOf.name: confirm
oneOf.title: confirm
oneOf.description: Inbound WS frame: answer a parked confirm gate. Carries {type:"confirm", gate_id?, generation?, approved, persist_dirs?, trust_computer?, reason?, remember?, superseded?}. trust_computer (with approved) accepts the event.confirm_request exec_trust offer, as on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm. reason, remember and superseded are as on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm: reason (with approved false, at most 500 characters) reaches the agent in the refused call's result; remember false approves this call only; superseded (with approved false, no reason, no session_scope) declines because the user sent a new message instead, and the agent does not read it as a refusal. gate_id is the stream frame ENVELOPE's gate.id (a sibling of `event`, NOT a field inside the event payload; the payload's own gate_id is the agent's own number, a different id), and is published as pending_gate.id on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} and /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/replay and as pending_gate_ref.id on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state. It is a STRING: sending the payload's number is refused bad_frame, naming the field; without it the answer applies to whatever gate is parked when it arrives. request_id? is the client's own id for the decision (at most 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_', '-'). Every outcome is ANSWERED, never silently dropped: a consumed decision by the broadcast event.gate_resolved, anything else by a `refused` frame naming the code. That covers a stale or absent gate, a gate that already ended (gate_already_resolved, with what was decided; never a second forward) and a decision in flight (gate_decision_pending). approved is required in every mode: a frame without a boolean approved is refused approved_required and never resolves a gate. On an always session the frame must also carry the exact gate_id and its generation, or it is refused decision_incomplete.

payload.description: Free-form payload. Inbound WS frame: answer a parked confirm gate. Carries {type:"confirm", gate_id?, generation?, approved, persist_dirs?, trust_computer?, reason?, remember?, superseded?}. trust_computer (with approved) accepts the event.confirm_request exec_trust offer, as on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm. reason, remember and superseded are as on /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm: reason (with approved false, at most 500 characters) reaches the agent in the refused call's result; remember false approves this call only; superseded (with approved false, no reason, no session_scope) declines because the user sent a new message instead, and the agent does not read it as a refusal. gate_id is the stream frame ENVELOPE's gate.id (a sibling of `event`, NOT a field inside the event payload; the payload's own gate_id is the agent's own number, a different id), and is published as pending_gate.id on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} and /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/replay and as pending_gate_ref.id on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state. It is a STRING: sending the payload's number is refused bad_frame, naming the field; without it the answer applies to whatever gate is parked when it arrives. request_id? is the client's own id for the decision (at most 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_', '-'). Every outcome is ANSWERED, never silently dropped: a consumed decision by the broadcast event.gate_resolved, anything else by a `refused` frame naming the code. That covers a stale or absent gate, a gate that already ended (gate_already_resolved, with what was decided; never a second forward) and a decision in flight (gate_decision_pending). approved is required in every mode: a frame without a boolean approved is refused approved_required and never resolves a gate. On an always session the frame must also carry the exact gate_id and its generation, or it is refused decision_incomplete.

oneOf.title: answer
oneOf.description: Inbound WS frame: answer a parked question gate. Carries {type:"answer", gate_id?, generation?, answer?, text?, answers?}; gate_id is as for confirm. A stale, duplicate or absent gate is a `refused` frame, and a retry that names the question this client already resolved replays the original `gate_resolved_ack` when it carries the same answer (another answer is a `refused` frame, gate_already_answered).

payload.description: Free-form payload. Inbound WS frame: answer a parked question gate. Carries {type:"answer", gate_id?, generation?, answer?, text?, answers?}; gate_id is as for confirm. payload.description: Turn complete: it ends a prompt turn. Carries the turn's typed outcome / error_code and notices [{code, message?, detail?}].
