kind.description: What was stopped: session (the running turn or parked gate), task (a background task), workflow_run, bash_job (a background shell the session started, on this machine or its computer), loop (paused, not deleted).

id.description: The item's id: the session id, <session id>/<task id> for a task, a run id, a bash job id or a loop id.

outcome.description: stopped: the stop reached running work and it ended (a loop: paused). already_done: it had finished before the stop reached it. failed: it was still running when the checks ended; detail says why.

stopped.description: A stop: the work it acted on and how each ended. Omitted otherwise.

cleanup.description: A committed stop, whether or not it found work running: detached_may_survive means a shell command the session ran may have left a process (started in the background, detached) that no stop can be shown to have reached, so it may still be running. oneOf.name: EventWaiterDone
oneOf.title: event.waiter_done
oneOf.description: A waiter this session owns (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters) ended: an outcome was found, or it timed out, was cancelled, or its target closed. Carries the waiter.

label.description: The label it was created with.

owner.description: The session that waits (the path session).

name.description: The outcome's name: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. timeout, cancelled, target_closed, interrupted, access_lost and judge_unavailable are reserved.

when.description: A sentence describing one event to look for, for example "the unit tests pass" or "a file named report.md is written" (at most 300 characters). It is judged by a model against the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; what the worker writes in its replies is not evidence. Name one event: counting, times and and/or conditions are not judged reliably; use match, or several outcomes. Give exactly one of when and match.

kind.description: The kind of event.

tool.description: The tool's name, for example bash or write_file.

exit_code.description: tool_result only: the exit status the command must have ended with. A result with no observed exit status never matches.

is_error.description: tool_result only: whether the tool reported an error.

text_contains.description: Text the event must contain (case-sensitive, at most 200 characters).

outcome.description: turn_end only: how the turn ended.

match.description: An exact event: every given field must hold. Checked on every event, without a model. Give exactly one of when and match.

from.description: The target turn it reads from, when one was given.

state.description: waiting or done.

outcome.description: When done: the name of the outcome found, or timeout (nothing found before the deadline), cancelled (by request, or the owner session closed), target_closed (the watched session ended first), interrupted (the agent restarted while waiting; events in between were not watched), access_lost (the current login can no longer reach a session or its realm) or judge_unavailable (judged outcomes could not be checked and no exact outcome was left).

reason.description: A sentence saying why it ended.

also_found.description: Other outcomes found in the same check, in the order they were given.

seq.description: The event's number in the target's event list.

turn_id.description: The target turn the event belongs to, when it has one.

kind.description: The event's kind.

tool.description: The tool's name.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, when observed.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported an error.

excerpt.description: The start of the event's text, with secrets removed.

by.description: match: an exact outcome matched. judge: a model judged that the events show the outcome; it points at this event, it does not prove it.

p.description: judge only: the model's probability that the events show the outcome.

evidence.description: The event the outcome was found in.

on_timeout.description: What the creator said to do on timeout, kept for the creator's use; the agent does not act on it.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from creation to the end.

max_checks.description: The most model requests it may make (a retried request counts again).

gap.description: true when some target events may not have been read (the start turn was too old, or many events arrived at once).

cost_usd.description: What its model checks cost, in US dollars.

cost_known.description: false when the price of some check was not reported.

model.description: The model judged outcomes are checked with.

waiter.description: The waiter, ended (as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters/{waiter_id} returns it).

payload.description: A waiter this session owns (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters) ended: an outcome was found, or it timed out, was cancelled, or its target closed. Carries the waiter.

requested_dirs.description: Directories outside the session's scope the call needs. Omitted when none.

A call that touches a known credential store starts with a line ⚠ credential store: <label> (not on an edit's diff or a dangerous card). A gate parked because the tool-call rules could not be checked starts with a line ⚠ rules not checked: <why>. Omitted when none.

offer_session_allow.description: true when an allow-for-the-session answer may be offered (session_scope on /confirm). Omitted when false.

gate_id.description: The agent's own number for this gate, for diagnostics. It is NOT what /confirm takes: echo the frame envelope's gate.id.

gate_cause.description: Why the gate exists, for example static_stakes, dir_access, hook_ask or approval_policy. Open set. Omitted by an older agent.

human_only.description: true when no automatic policy may answer this gate; a person must. Always present.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation a decision must carry (lease_generation on /confirm). Omitted when there is no lease.

lease_required.description: true when the decision must come from the approver-lease holder. Always present.

task_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the background task of the helper that parked the gate. Omitted otherwise.

computer_id.description: The resolved computer id the grant is keyed by.

computer_name.description: The computer name the call used. Omitted when the call named the id.

realm.description: The realm the grant applies in: _global or a realm id.

label.description: Button text, for example Always allow exec on my-box.

exec_trust.description: On a hoody_exec_* card: the per-computer trust option. Omitted when no grant can be offered: another tool, a computer that did not resolve, a hook or rules ask, the always approval policy, a headless session.

rules.description: When tool-call rules asked: the rules behind the gate. outcome ask = these check_in rules cover the call; unchecked = the rules check could not complete, so it asks instead (rule_ids = every rule it covered). gate_cause is rules when only rules asked; when a shell hook asked too it stays hook_ask and rules is still present. Omitted when no rule asked.

helper_id.description: The helper that produced this event (a background helper's task id, or a per-spawn helper id). Omitted on the session's own events.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted on the session's own events.

request_id.description: The request id of the decision that resolved the gate, when that decision carried one. helper_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the helper that parked this gate (its event.confirm_request or event.user_question carried the same helper_id). Omitted for the session's own gates.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted for the session's own gates.

task_id.description: The background task of that helper (equal to helper_id). Omitted for a foreground helper and for the session's own gates.

approved.description: The tool was approved (true) or denied.

persist_dirs.description: An approved directory grant was persisted to settings.json.

oneOf.name: lagged
oneOf.title: lagged
oneOf.description: Control frame: the subscriber was dropped for slowness, or a ?since= resume cursor fell past the replay ring or belongs to another incarnation. Carries {code: lagged|replay_gap[, min_seq, max_seq, incarnation, resume]}; reconcile by reconnecting with ?since= and ?incarnation=.

code.description: lagged: this subscriber was dropped for reading too slowly and the stream ends. replay_gap: the resume cursor was behind or ahead of the retained ring, invalid, or from another incarnation; the frames that follow are the whole retained ring.

min_seq.description: On replay_gap, the lowest seq still retained.

max_seq.description: On replay_gap, the highest seq retained.

incarnation.description: On replay_gap, the live session's incarnation.

resume.description: On an SSE lagged frame, how to recover: reconnect with ?since= set to the last seq read. The WS frame omits it; the recovery is the same.

payload.description: Control frame: the subscriber was dropped for slowness, or a ?since= resume cursor fell past the replay ring or belongs to another incarnation. Carries {code: lagged|replay_gap[, min_seq, max_seq, incarnation, resume]}; reconcile by reconnecting with ?since= and ?incarnation=.

oneOf.name: replay_boundary
oneOf.title: replay_boundary
oneOf.description: Control frame: the ring→live boundary. Everything before it is buffered replay; everything after is live. Carries {max_seq, incarnation, turn_id?, turn_since?}; turn_id names the turn being watched and turn_since the cursor before its first frame (see the payload).

max_seq.description: The highest seq the ring held when the stream attached: frames up to it are replay, later frames are live. Pass the last seq you read as ?since= to resume.

incarnation.description: The incarnation max_seq belongs to. Pass it as ?incarnation= with the cursor.

turn_id.description: The turn this stream is watching: on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/prompt:stream, the turn the request dispatched (equal to X-Hoody-Turn-Id); on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream, the turn dispatched through this API that was running when the stream attached. Omitted when no such turn is running, including a turn another client (the TUI) started on the same session; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state current_turn_id covers that case. It names the turn for POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/cancel turn_id and matches its agent_done turn_id. Later frames carry their own envelope turn_id.

turn_since.description: While a turn runs: the cursor just before its first frame (the same value as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state turn_since). A client holding every frame after it can reconnect with ?since=turn_since to replay the whole turn. Omitted when idle, and on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/prompt:stream when the dispatched turn already ended and another holds the slot.

payload.description: Control frame: the ring→live boundary. Everything before it is buffered replay; everything after is live. Carries {max_seq, incarnation, turn_id?, turn_since?}; turn_id names the turn being watched and turn_since the cursor before its first frame (see the payload).

oneOf.name: end
oneOf.title: end

reason.description: Why the stream ended: "session closed" or "session not authorized" (the session's owner is no longer the active account).

payload.description: Control frame: the stream is terminating because the session closed. Carries {reason}.

oneOf.name: refused
oneOf.title: refused
oneOf.description: Control frame, connection-local: the WS command this client just sent was REJECTED and was not applied. It is the WS twin of a REST error envelope. Carries {frame: the client frame type that was refused, code, reason}. Codes match the REST ones for the same condition: bad_frame (the frame did not decode; the reason names the field and the JSON type it must carry, e.g. a gate_id sent as the event payload's number instead of the envelope's string), no_pending_gate / stale_gate / gate_already_answered / gate_type_mismatch (the frame did not match the parked gate), approved_required (a confirm frame without a boolean approved; it never resolves a gate), decision_incomplete (an always session needs an explicit approved, the exact gate_id and its generation; or a confirm without gate_id while several gates are parked). For a confirm: gate_already_resolved (the gate already ended and this decision was not applied; the frame also carries gate_id, generation, outcome, decision {approved, persist_dirs, session_scope, trust_computer, remember?, superseded?} or decision_unknown:true, and request_id when the decision consumed carried that request_id) and gate_decision_pending (a decision for the gate is in flight and its outcome is not known yet: another client's, or this one past the wait; carries gate_id, generation and reason:connection_lost when the agent connection was lost; retry naming the gate to learn the outcome). For an answer: bad_request (the frame carries no answer, text or answers, an empty answer never resolves a question; or a workflow question with options gets an answer that names none of them, and stays parked), gate_cancelled (the question was resolved without consuming this answer) and decision_unconfirmed (the answer was not acknowledged within the wait; it may still apply). It is sent ONLY to the client that sent the frame, never broadcast.

payload.description: Free-form payload. Control frame, connection-local: the WS command this client just sent was REJECTED and was not applied. It is the WS twin of a REST error envelope. Carries {frame: the client frame type that was refused, code, reason}. Codes match the REST ones for the same condition: bad_frame (the frame did not decode; the reason names the field and the JSON type it must carry, e.g. a gate_id sent as the event payload's number instead of the envelope's string), no_pending_gate / stale_gate / gate_already_answered / gate_type_mismatch (the frame did not match the parked gate), approved_required (a confirm frame without a boolean approved; it never resolves a gate), decision_incomplete (an always session needs an explicit approved, the exact gate_id and its generation; or a confirm without gate_id while several gates are parked). For a confirm: gate_already_resolved (the gate already ended and this decision was not applied; the frame also carries gate_id, generation, outcome, decision {approved, persist_dirs, session_scope, trust_computer, remember?, superseded?} or decision_unknown:true, and request_id when the decision consumed carried that request_id) and gate_decision_pending (a decision for the gate is in flight and its outcome is not known yet: another client's, or this one past the wait; carries gate_id, generation and reason:connection_lost when the agent connection was lost; retry naming the gate to learn the outcome). For an answer: bad_request (the frame carries no answer, text or answers, an empty answer never resolves a question; or a workflow question with options gets an answer that names none of them, and stays parked), gate_cancelled (the question was resolved without consuming this answer) and decision_unconfirmed (the answer was not acknowledged within the wait; it may still apply). It is sent ONLY to the client that sent the frame, never broadcast.

oneOf.name: gate_resolved_ack
oneOf.title: gate_resolved_ack
oneOf.description: Control frame, connection-local: the replayed acknowledgement of a question answer. When an answer frame is a RETRY naming the question gate this client already resolved, with the same answer, it carries replayed:true and {resolved: the ORIGINAL event.gate_resolved payload}. A retry never forwards a second answer. A confirm retry is refused gate_already_resolved instead. Sent only to the client that sent the frame.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Returns the session's background-subagent task catalog INLINE: no attach, no live session required, and no stream to observe. The catalog is the union of the LIVE registry and the PERSISTED per-session task store, keyed by task id with the live entry winning: the live registry evicts completed tasks at spawn time, so a finished task can leave memory while its transcript is still durable, and a live-only list would hide it. `session_live` reports whether a live session backed this read. A session that is not visible to this caller is a plain 404 (uniform envelope). CONFIG-DIR: X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the record store. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

items.description: One row per background task, oldest first by started_at: two stamps that parse as RFC3339 and name different instants are ordered by instant; otherwise (the same instant, or a stamp that does not parse) by the started_at strings, and by id only when those strings are equal; each element is the daemon's task info with the properties below.

get.description: Returns a background subagent task's transcript INLINE: entries, the task's summary row (the same fields a GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/tasks item carries), and the cursor state. No attach, no live session required: a task that reached a terminal state is persisted per session, so its transcript is readable for a dormant session and after a daemon restart. A task still RUNNING when the daemon died is NOT recoverable (persistence happens at terminal status) and reads 404. `source` is "live" when served from the live registry and "store" when served from the persisted task store. `complete` reports whether this response reflects a terminal projection DURABLY COMMITTED to that store: it is false for a task that has just finished but whose write has not landed, and false for a placeholder written by session teardown whose real terminal projection may still arrive. after_seq is an int64 UPSERT-POLL cursor, exclusive, EXCEPT that a still-open entry is re-sent even when its seq is at or below the cursor (viewers upsert by seq). OMITTING after_seq returns the whole transcript from the beginning, which is DISTINCT from after_seq=0; that value is exclusive and skips a closed seq-0 entry. It is not the GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/transcript after_turn cursor, not the gateway's stream seq, and not a monotonic replay cursor. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404.

schema.description: The task's transcript slice plus its summary row and the cursor/durability state.

session_id.description: The session the task belongs to.

task_id.description: The task id, as supplied in the path.

task.description: The task's summary row, the same shape as a GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/tasks item: {id, name, status, kind?, prompt, started_at, updated_at?, tool_calls?, elapsed_ms?, output_preview?, computer?, cwd?, parent_tool_call_id?, rev?}.

seq.description: The entry's sequence number; a viewer upserts by it. -1 is the presentation-only "…earlier output trimmed…" note, present only on a from-the-beginning read.

kind.description: The entry kind.

text.description: The entry's text: the reply or reasoning text, a tool_result's preview, a usage line or a note. Omitted when empty.

tool.description: tool_call and tool_result entries: the tool. Omitted otherwise.

is_error.description: A tool_result entry: the tool failed. Omitted when false.

open.description: The last text or thinking entry of a running task while it is still growing; it is re-sent on every read until it closes. Omitted when false.

tool_call_id.description: tool_call and tool_result entries: the tool_use id pairing a result with its call. Omitted otherwise.

command.description: A bash entry: the command line, secret-scrubbed and capped at 2 KiB. Omitted otherwise.

exit_code.description: A bash tool_result entry: the exit status, 0 included. Omitted when no process exit was observed.

complete.description: A tool_result entry whose text holds the whole output (nothing was elided by the preview). Omitted otherwise. Unrelated to the response-level complete.

entries.description: Transcript entries {seq, kind, text?, tool?, is_error?, open?, tool_call_id?, command?, exit_code?, complete?}. kind is one of text|thinking|tool_call|tool_result|usage|note. A seq of -1 is the presentation-only "…earlier output trimmed…" marker, present only on a from-the-beginning read. tool_call_id pairs a tool_call entry with its tool_result. command is the bash command line (secret-scrubbed, capped at 2 KiB) on a bash entry. exit_code is bash's exit status on a tool_result entry, 0 included; absent when no process exit was observed. A tool_result's text is a preview: the first 8 and last 12 lines around an "… N more lines …" marker; complete:true means nothing was elided (this entry-level flag is unrelated to the response-level complete, which is about durability).

trimmed.description: Whether entries were dropped: by the live ring before the snapshot, or by the store's per-task cap.

after_seq.description: The applied cursor, echoed. -1 means the request omitted it (from the beginning).

complete.description: Whether this response reflects a terminal projection durably committed to the task store. False for a task that just finished but whose write has not landed, and for a teardown-written placeholder whose real terminal result may still arrive.

source.description: "live" when served from the live task registry, "store" when served from the persisted task store.

session_live.description: Whether a live session backed this read.

post.summary: Run a tool inside a live session (gated).
post.description: Runs a tool on a LIVE session, through the same permission checks as the agent's own tool calls: caller-supplied control keys are ignored, and the tool runs in the session's own scope (its realm, computer, cwd, tool mode and dir scope) with every check applied. It claims the session's single serial turn slot so a direct tool run never races the turn loop (409 turn_in_flight if a turn is running; 409 gate_parked if a gate is parked). Because it occupies the turn slot it is also CANCELLABLE the same way a turn is: a concurrent POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/cancel (or a WS cancel frame, or session close) aborts the in-flight run. A parked confirmation returns 409 tool_needs_confirmation with the echoed params; re-issue with confirm:true, the returned confirm_token and the params originally sent (the echo may be redacted). A tool-call rule (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules) is checked here too: a `limit` the call breaks answers 200 is_error; a `check_in` it falls under, or a rules check that could not complete, answers 409 tool_needs_confirmation with details.gate_cause "rules" and details.reason naming the rule. 404 tool_not_found when the tool is not in the session's effective tool list. The session-level tools todo_read, todo_write, task_output, list_tasks and bash_job_wait run here like any other tool, after the same checks; bash_job_wait only observes the job: it arranges no completion notice and leaves any notice the agent is owed in place. spawn_agent, run_workflow, review_with_panel and ask_question_to_user need the session's model loop or a human, so they are refused with 422 tool_not_directly_runnable and nothing runs; ask the agent for them in a turn instead. On a session whose approval policy is "always" a tool that is itself a nested executor (spawn_agent, run_workflow, review_with_panel, tool_orchestrator, run_codex, …) is 409 approval_policy_unsatisfiable instead; every other side-effecting tool parks for confirmation as usual, and the confirmation must carry the approver lease (X-Hoody-Approver-Lease) when one was minted: a confirmation without it is refused with the same typed codes POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm answers: 409 approver_lease_required (none presented), 409 approver_lease_invalid (it does not verify) and 410 approver_lease_expired, never a generic 400. Which tools those are is not left to example: Under always every side-effecting invocation waits for a decision (bash, writes/deletes, non-GET web_fetch, fleet actions, non-read-only MCP tools, image generation and notifications), while memory_save, the todo mutators (create/update/claim/finish_todo, append_todo_note, triage_todos) and propose_cron_entry stay ungated as agent-internal state and drafts; reads, grep/glob and the task tools are never gated. A tool in the ungated set runs here without parking a decision even under "always": that is the policy, not a gap in this endpoint. NOTE (headless-live exception): a session CREATED with headless:true HARD-DENIES the high-risk bash shapes (rm -rf /, curl|sh, git push --force) and outside-cwd file writes (200 is_error, no 409 confirm round): those confirm-gated shapes are parkable only on a non-headless session or the sessionless ephemeral path; a headless live session has no interactive confirmer for them. MCP tools (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`) that a server config marks require_confirmation (or that a server annotates destructiveHint) are likewise NOT parkable over HTTP: every forwarded run is machine-stamped and an MCP confirmation must come from a human at the daemon, so the run answers 200 is_error ("requires confirmation from a human") rather than 409: a deliberate posture, not a gap.

requestBody.description: Tool parameters and an optional confirmation posture. Caller-supplied `confirmed`/`_`-prefixed control keys are ignored: they are never trusted from the wire.

params.description: The tool's input parameters (its JSON-Schema body).

confirm.description: Re-issue a previously-parked confirmation. MUST be paired with the confirm_token of the parked run; a confirm:true with no valid token does NOT bypass the gate: the run is sent unconfirmed, so it parks again, except that a sessionless run of a non-read-only tool without allow_mutations is refused 400 tool_mutation_refused. A wire confirmed key in params is always scrubbed.

confirm_token.description: The single-use token of the parked run: in the 409 tool_needs_confirmation details of POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{name}/run and POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/tools/{name}/run, in the polled job result of POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{name}/runAsync (whose own answer is a 202), and in the needs_confirmation frame of POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{name}/stream (whose own answer is a 200 stream). Bound to the tool/session/params it was minted for; present it with confirm:true and the params originally sent to approve the parked run (the echoed params may be redacted, and a redacted copy parks the run again).

allow_mutations.description: Sessionless only: opt a non-read-only tool into running with every permission check applied (else a sessionless mutating run is refused 400 tool_mutation_refused). Set it on the first call; a confirm:true without a valid confirm_token does not stand in for it.

params.reason: check the working tree before committing

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.summary: Read a session's transcript without attaching.
get.description: Returns the persisted conversation: the event.replay message projection (text/thinking/tool_use/tool_result blocks, an image block for each image a person attached, read with GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/images/{image_id}, and on an outcome_claims session an outcome_claims block, its report as in event.outcome_claims, right after the tool_result of each report_outcome call) plus turn boundaries, for a live or closed session, read from the session record. It never attaches, never resumes, and never consumes the exclusive attach slot. For a LIVE session the content is fresh to the last persist point (turn ends + state changes); the mid-turn streaming tail is served by GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/replay (live ring) and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream (event.replay) instead. A session that has never persisted, or is not visible to this caller, is a plain 404 (uniform envelope). after_turn=N skips completed turns 1..N (exclusive cursor; 0 = full transcript; past-end values clamp; the response echoes the applied value; this is NOT the tasks-transcript after_seq upsert-poll cursor). turn_boundaries are RESPONSE-LOCAL after a slice: for local boundary index i, the 0-based turn index POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/trim turn_idx consumes is after_turn + i (the 1-based turn ordinal is after_turn + i + 1). Messages past the last boundary (a persisted mid-turn tail) are always included and never counted in turns_total/turns_returned. CONFIG-DIR: X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the record store (same asymmetry as DELETE /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}); X-Hoody-Cwd is NOT a match filter here (unlike GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}). Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404.

schema.description: The transcript itself. The gateway unwraps it out of the daemon reply, so the body is the transcript object, not the reply that carried it: there is no status field and no transcript key to read through.

session_id.description: The session the transcript belongs to.

live.description: Whether the session is running right now.

realm.description: The session's realm.

name.description: The session's title, when it has one.

name_auto.description: True when the title was generated by the agent, false when a person set it or there is none.

model.description: The model the session runs.

turns_returned.description: Turns in this response, after the skip cursor.

after_turn.description: The skip cursor actually applied, clamped to turns_total.

turn_boundaries.description: Index into messages where each returned turn ends; -1 for a turn that emitted nothing.

role.description: Who wrote the message.

kind.description: The block kind. An image block marks an image a person attached to the message; its bytes are read with GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/images/{image_id}.

text.description: text and thinking blocks: the text. Omitted when empty.

tool_id.description: tool_use and tool_result blocks: the tool_use id pairing a result with its call; an outcome_claims block: the report_outcome call it follows. Omitted otherwise.

tool_name.description: tool_use blocks: the tool. Omitted otherwise; a tool_result block names its call by tool_id.

input.description: A tool_use block: the tool input, with secrets redacted. Omitted when empty.

output.description: A tool_result block: the tool's output, with secrets redacted. Omitted when empty.

is_error.description: A tool_result block: the tool failed, or the call was denied or cancelled. Omitted when false.

error_code.description: A tool_result block: outcome_unknown when the call may have taken effect although it reported a failure (check before retrying), as on the live event.tool_result. Omitted otherwise.

turn_id.description: The turn it closes, as on event.agent_done. Omitted for a turn not dispatched with one.

tool_id.description: The tool_use id of the report_outcome call these claims are from.

text.description: The claim, in the model's words.

tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id the model cited.

status.description: linked: a call the session itself made in this turn (the report_outcome call itself never is). foreign: a helper's call, or one of an earlier turn. ambiguous: more than one call of this turn used the id, or a call of this turn and a helper's or an earlier turn's call did. unknown: no such call.

is_error.description: The call failed, or was denied or cancelled.

exit_code.description: The process exit status when one was observed (bash), 0 included. Omitted when unknown.

truncated.description: true when the call's output was cut (event.tool_result truncated). Omitted when unknown.

after_last_write.description: true when the call ran and every other call of this turn that can change something (anything but a read-only tool or the session's todo, task and question bookkeeping) finished before it started. Writes by helpers and background tasks are not counted.

receipt.description: What the agent recorded about the call. Present only when status is linked.

evidence.description: The tool calls the model cited for the claim, in its order. Empty when it cited none.

evidence_status.description: linked when at least one cited call is linked; none when the claim cites nothing, or nothing of this turn. A none claim is still reported: show it as the agent's word, not checked.

claims.description: The claims of the turn's last accepted report, in the model's order.

replaced.description: true when this report replaced an earlier report_outcome of the same turn. Omitted otherwise.

outcome.description: An outcome_claims block: the turn's report, as in event.outcome_claims. Omitted otherwise.

image_id.description: An image block: the id GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/images/{image_id} takes, valid for this session only. Omitted, with media_type and bytes, when the stored image cannot be read there (a type other than PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, bytes that do not start as such an image, or an image over 16 MiB). Only the start of the image is checked, as when it was sent: an image whose later bytes are damaged keeps its id and is returned as stored.

media_type.description: An image block with image_id: what the image is. Omitted otherwise.

bytes.description: An image block with image_id: the image's size in bytes. Omitted otherwise.

blocks.description: The message's content blocks, in order. Never empty.

messages.description: The conversation messages, with secrets redacted at this boundary.

started_at.description: When the session started. Absent when unknown.

last_request_at.description: When the session was last active. Absent when unknown.

schema.description: The session's durable turn receipts.

session_id.description: The session.

turn_id.description: The turn's id (names it for a scoped cancel and matches the agent_done frame).

job_id.description: The gateway job id for this turn (poll GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}); null when this gateway holds no job for the turn: the session is not live here (dormant), the gateway restarted since, or the finished job's record has been pruned; the ledger receipt is the record.

state.description: Ledger state.

duplicate.description: true when the Idempotency-Key was seen before and this is the stored receipt (nothing ran again).

outcome.description: Terminal outcome (completed | failed | cancelled | interrupted); absent until terminal.

error_code.description: Typed failure code when the turn failed; absent otherwise. Known codes: no_credentials (the model's provider has no credential), session_unconfigured (no usable model/provider), approval_policy_unsatisfiable (the turn reached an executor the "always" policy refuses), admission_write_failed (the dispatch mark could not be recorded: the turn did not run), ledger_write_failed (the terminal outcome could not be persisted), max_steps (the chat agent's max_steps_per_turn limit ended the turn after that many model requests; post.description: Dispatches a user turn and returns 202 {turn_id, job_id, state, result_url, stream_url} once the daemon has durably admitted it. Send a standard Idempotency-Key header to make the create RETRY-SAFE: a retry with the SAME key returns the SAME receipt (duplicate:true) and never runs the turn twice, including while the original is still running (the receipt is looked up before any busy refusal); the same key with a DIFFERENT request is 422 idempotency_key_reused. That verdict is only returned once the recorded turn has actually been COMPARED against this request: if the recorded turn's session can no longer be resolved the retry is neither acknowledged as a duplicate nor dispatched: the busy refusal stands (409) and nothing runs, because an unverified match is not a match. Retry once the session is readable, or read the receipt directly with GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}. Refuses a new turn when the session has a parked gate (409 gate_parked) or a turn already running (409 turn_in_flight): single-writer; a busy refusal records nothing. If the daemon does not acknowledge within the wait the answer is 503 admission_unconfirmed carrying turn_id/result_url: the turn may still have been accepted, so poll result_url before retrying (acceptance is never invented and never rolled back). A ledger write failure is 503 admission_write_failed (fail-closed: the turn does not run unrecorded). A turn interrupted by a daemon restart replays as state interrupted with effects_may_have_occurred and is never re-run. The optional X-Hoody-Gate-Policy: auto_approve header (or ?policy=auto_approve) auto-answers the admitted turn's confirm gates until it ends, as prompt:sync does once its request has ended; question and plan gates still wait for /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer or /plan. The policy is part of the request: the same Idempotency-Key with a different policy is 422 idempotency_key_reused, a duplicate's replay changes no posture, and a session whose approval policy is "always" refuses it 409 approval_policy_active before anything runs.

parameters.description: The session id.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.description: auto_approve auto-answers the admitted turn's confirm gates until it ends (alias of the X-Hoody-Gate-Policy header); off by default; the gateway asks for no separate credentials to use it; access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Gate-Policy
parameters.description: Confirm-gate posture: "auto_approve" adopts the headless auto-answer posture: it approves approval cards for their one call, and denies a card a tool-call rule raised and a destructive-shape card (static_stakes: a recursive force delete, curl piped to a shell, sudo, a force push...), as a headless run refuses those (off by default; the in:query alias is ?policy=). parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

x-error-codes.resolution: Honor the Retry-After header and retry; reduce the request rate.

x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if persistent, inspect the daemon logs.

503.description: Admission not confirmed / ledger write failed.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying when the session's turn record could not be read or the session is shutting down.

x-error-codes.title: Service unavailable / Turn record unreadable
x-error-codes.description: The daemon could not service the request (too busy, or a per-client stream concurrency cap was hit). The session's turn record could not be read or made durable, so whether this Idempotency-Key admitted a turn is unknown: it may have been.
x-error-codes.resolution: Honor Retry-After and retry with the same Idempotency-Key; never change the key, since the turn may already run.

example.message: the session's turn record could not be read; retry with the same idempotency key

x-error-codes.title: Admission unconfirmed
x-error-codes.description: The turn was sent but the daemon's admission receipt did not arrive within the wait. It may still have been accepted: details.turn_id / details.result_url name the turn to poll. The gateway keeps the turn slot and job rather than inventing or discarding acceptance.
x-error-codes.resolution: GET details.result_url; retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key only after it reports the turn was not recorded (404).

example.message: the daemon did not acknowledge the turn's admission within the wait

x-error-codes.title: Admission write failed
x-error-codes.description: The daemon could not durably record the turn's admission, so the turn was NOT run (fail-closed: nothing runs unrecorded).
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if it persists, check the daemon's session store (disk / permissions).

example.message: the admission ledger could not be written; the turn was not accepted

x-error-codes.title: Login restriction unknown
x-error-codes.description: The agent cannot read yet which realms its login may serve (GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status reports restriction "unknown"), so it runs no work in any session until it can. Nothing was run.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the restriction is readable.

example.message: the login's realm restriction could not be read (introspection failed) — retry, or log in again

x-error-codes.title: Session terminating
x-error-codes.description: The session is shutting down, so this request was refused before anything was recorded for it. The refusal does not cover an earlier attempt with the same Idempotency-Key: that attempt may have been admitted and run.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the Retry-After delay with the same Idempotency-Key. If an earlier attempt with that key ended uncertain (a timeout or a lost connection), read GET /sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id} for it first. If the session has closed meanwhile, attach it again first (POST /sessions with attach).

requestBody.description: Turn input: the user text, optional inline image attachments, plus the optional tool_mode / dir_scope the session's first turn fixes.

text.description: Required (may be empty only with attachments). The user message text for this turn: empty or whitespace-only text with no attachments is refused (400 empty_prompt) and no turn runs.

tool_mode.description: Optional tool mode: standard or orchestrator. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (tool_mode_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode; any other value is refused 400 invalid_tool_mode too.

dir_scope.description: Optional directory-access scope: home or full. It is not a per-turn override: the session's first turn applies it and fixes it for the session's lifetime (dir_scope_locked). On a later turn, one queued before the first turn ran included, the same value is accepted and a different one is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope; any other value is refused 400 invalid_dir_scope too.

media_type.description: The image media type, e.g. "image/png". Must match the actual bytes (image/jpg is read as image/jpeg); a mismatch is refused 400.

data.description: The image itself, base64-encoded (standard encoding): a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP. Other bytes are refused 400. Required: HTTP attachments are inline bytes.

name.description: Optional display name (the original filename), shown in the transcript instead of a staging path.

attachments.description: Optional images for this turn, as INLINE base64 bytes. At most 4 per turn, each at most 4 MiB DECODED (~5.33 MiB of base64); the request body limit applies on top and is authoritative, so several individually-legal images can still exceed it. A violation is refused with 400 BEFORE the turn is accepted: nothing is silently dropped. `path` is not supported here: it would name a file on the CALLER's machine, so an attachment with a non-empty path refuses the whole request with 400 bad_request before a turn is accepted. If the active model cannot accept images the daemon reports that on the session stream.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.summary: Read a turn by its idempotency key.
get.description: Returns the durable receipt of the turn a keyed POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns or POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/messages admitted, by its key: the same record GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id} returns. {key} is the Idempotency-Key the request was sent with (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace; URL-encode it). Works for a live or dormant session; reads never admit anything. 404 turn_not_found with details.retired false proves nothing (the turn may still be on its way); POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/by-key/{key}/retire settles it. Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.description: The session id.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: A turn receipt: the durable admission record plus the URLs to observe it.

turn_id.description: The turn's id (names it for a scoped cancel and matches the agent_done frame).

job_id.description: The gateway job id for this turn (poll GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}); null when this gateway holds no job for the turn: the session is not live here (dormant), the gateway restarted since, or the finished job's record has been pruned; the ledger receipt is the record.

state.description: Ledger state.

duplicate.description: true when the Idempotency-Key was seen before and this is the stored receipt (nothing ran again).

outcome.description: Terminal outcome (completed | failed | cancelled | interrupted); absent until terminal.

error_code.description: Typed failure code when the turn failed; absent otherwise. Known codes: no_credentials (the model's provider has no credential), session_unconfigured (no usable model/provider), approval_policy_unsatisfiable (the turn reached an executor the "always" policy refuses), admission_write_failed (the dispatch mark could not be recorded: the turn did not run), ledger_write_failed (the terminal outcome could not be persisted), max_steps (the chat agent's max_steps_per_turn limit ended the turn after that many model requests; send a message to continue), step_limit_unavailable (a Claude Code session cannot stop at the agent's max_steps_per_turn, so the turn was refused before it started), step_report_failed (mid-turn, a Claude Code session could not report to the step limit, so it was stopped; earlier tool calls of the turn may have run), context_overflow (a Claude Code session's conversation no longer fits its model, and the turn's automatic compaction and resend did not cure it; run /compact or /clear), max_tokens (the model's answer was cut off at its output limit), bad_tool_args (the model sent tool calls whose arguments were not valid JSON too many times in the turn), quota_wait_too_long (the provider's usage limit or busy window asked for a wait longer than the agent waits; retry_at says when to send again), rate_limit (the provider refused the request for its rate limit), conversation_reset (Claude Code could not open the session's conversation; the next message starts a new one with the session's history passed in as text), auth on a Claude Code session (Claude Code is not logged in where it runs), delegated_sandbox_unavailable (the sandbox that must confine Claude Code is not available where it runs, so it was not started), delegated_connect_timeout (Claude Code did not answer when started; it may not be logged in there), delegated_launch_failed (Claude Code could not be started; the event.error text says why), spend_cap (a spend cap refused or stopped the turn, or the spend settings file is not valid; the turn's event.error reason says which). The same code rides the turn's event.error and event.agent_done frames on the stream. An open set: treat an unknown code as a generic failure.

retry_at.description: With error_code: when the wait the provider named ends, RFC 3339 UTC (the turn's event.error retry_at). Send the message again after it. Absent when the provider named no wait.

retry_after_secs.description: With retry_at: the seconds the model provider asked to wait, the same number event.error carried as retry_after_secs. retry_at is when that wait ends. A turn recorded before this field reads the whole seconds left until retry_at, at least 1 while it is still ahead (0 once passed).

effects_may_have_occurred.description: True conservatively for every unfinished turn recovered as interrupted, even if it was only accepted, has no recorded tool calls, or was waiting for approval. This does not prove that a tool ran or an external effect occurred. The original turn is never re-run.

dispatched_at.description: RFC3339 time the turn was dispatched to run. Absent until then, and absent on a 202 built from the admission receipt (every fresh turn, and a duplicate the agent answers at admission); present once dispatched on a receipt read from the turn record (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}, and a duplicate answered while the session is busy).

source.description: What admitted the turn: input (a prompt) or workflow (a workflow run). Absent on a 202 built from the admission receipt (every fresh turn, and a duplicate the agent answers at admission); present on a receipt read from the turn record (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}, and a duplicate answered while the session is busy).

terminal_at.description: RFC3339 terminal time when known; absent until terminal and when a restart prevented recording the time.

continuation.description: On a turn interrupted by a restart, read while its session is live: what became of the turn's restart continuation. A turn a session message command started is continued once the agent is back (its message is not sent again). owed: a continuation is owed, or not yet decided, so the turn's end is not final yet; spent: a continuation turn ran for it (continued_by names that turn, whose own end is this one's); retired: no continuation will run (a stop, new work, the retry allowance used up, or a trimmed or cleared history); none: a turn a restart never continues (a prompt or a workflow). Absent on any other turn, for a dormant session, and from an agent that does not report it.

continued_by.description: With continuation spent: the turn id of the continuation that ran for this turn.

result_url.description: GET this for the durable receipt.

stream_url.description: Attach here (WS/SSE) to observe the turn from just before it was dispatched: the session stream path with since and incarnation query parameters, for example /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream?since=41&incarnation=<incarnation>.

code.description: Notice code (open set; hook_skipped_by_policy, machine_execution_refused_by_policy, agent_compacts_itself, history_unsaved and spend_cap_warning today).

detail.description: What it applied to (e.g. the hook event and matcher).

notices.description: Advisory notices stamped on the turn: never an error (outcome and error_code are unaffected). Codes in use: hook_skipped_by_policy (a configured user hook was skipped because the approval policy is always) and machine_execution_refused_by_policy (a machine-confirmed executor, such as a composite/fusion commit run, a subagent, a workflow tool step or auto-reply, asked to run a side-effecting tool under always and was refused; detail names the tool) and agent_compacts_itself (a Claude Code session's agent decides on its own when to compact its conversation, so the agent's compaction settings do not apply to it; detail names the agent) and history_unsaved (a Claude Code session answered from a conversation Hoody could not save, so the turn stopped and the next message passes the session's history in as text) and spend_cap_warning (the session's spend file sets action warn and the turn ran over a spend cap; detail is session_cap or turn_cap, one notice per cap); an open set.

x-error-codes.title: No turn with this key
x-error-codes.description: No turn was admitted with this idempotency key on this session. details.retired says whether the key was retired; while it is not, the miss proves nothing (the turn may still be on its way).
x-error-codes.resolution: Retire the key (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/by-key/{key}/retire) to settle it.

example.message: no turn with this idempotency key in this session; a miss proves nothing until the key is retired

admitted.description: With retired true: what was recorded when the key was retired. "false": nothing was admitted with the key. "unknown": a request sent with it earlier may have been admitted and run.

retired.description: true when the key was retired: nothing is admitted with it from now on. false: the miss proves nothing yet (the request may still be on its way); retire the key to settle it.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again when the turn record could not be read, the retired key could not be made durable, or the session is shutting down.

x-error-codes.title: Outcome unknown
x-error-codes.description: The turn record could not be read, or the retired key could not be made durable, so whether a turn was admitted with this key is unknown: it may have been. Nothing is reported as missing, and a retire is unconfirmed: it may have been recorded.
x-error-codes.resolution: Honor Retry-After and ask again with the same key. Never send the turn again under a new key on this answer.

example.message: the turn record could not be read; whether a turn was admitted with this key is unknown

admitted.description: Always "unknown": the request sent with the key may have been admitted and run.

x-error-codes.title: Login restriction unknown
x-error-codes.description: The agent cannot read yet which realms its login may serve (GET /api/v1/agent/hoody/auth/status reports restriction "unknown"), so it refuses realm-scoped requests until it can. Nothing was read or changed.
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry after the restriction is readable.

example.message: the login's realm restriction could not be read — retry

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Retire a turn key no read found.
post.description: Settles a keyed turn whose answer was lost. {key} is the Idempotency-Key the request was sent with (1–255 printable ASCII, no whitespace; URL-encode it). A key that admitted a turn answers retired false, admitted "true" and the turn's receipt. Otherwise the key is retired durably on this session: retired true, admitted "false", and a turn sent with it earlier and delivered later is refused 409 turn_key_retired; retiring it again answers the same. The session must be live: a dormant one answers 503 (unknown) until it is attached. A 503 is unknown: nothing is proven, retire again after Retry-After. 409 turn_fences_exhausted: the key was NOT retired, so a delayed turn sent with it can still be admitted; never send a replacement. A retire request never runs the original turn, but a turn already admitted with the key may have run or may still run. The request has no body.

schema.description: A turn receipt: the durable admission record plus the URLs to observe it.

turn_id.description: The turn's id (names it for a scoped cancel and matches the agent_done frame).

job_id.description: The gateway job id for this turn (poll GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}); null when this gateway holds no job for the turn: the session is not live here (dormant), the gateway restarted since, or the finished job's record has been pruned; the ledger receipt is the record.

state.description: Ledger state.

duplicate.description: true when the Idempotency-Key was seen before and this is the stored receipt (nothing ran again).

outcome.description: Terminal outcome (completed | failed | cancelled | interrupted); absent until terminal.

error_code.description: Typed failure code when the turn failed; absent otherwise. Known codes: no_credentials (the model's provider has no credential), session_unconfigured (no usable model/provider), approval_policy_unsatisfiable (the turn reached an executor the "always" policy refuses), admission_write_failed (the dispatch mark could not be recorded: the turn did not run), ledger_write_failed (the terminal outcome could not be persisted), max_steps (the chat agent's max_steps_per_turn limit ended the turn after that many model requests; send a message to continue), step_limit_unavailable (a Claude Code session cannot stop at the agent's max_steps_per_turn, so the turn was refused before it started), step_report_failed (mid-turn, a Claude Code session could not report to the step limit, so it was stopped; earlier tool calls of the turn may have run), context_overflow (a Claude Code session's conversation no longer fits its model, and the turn's automatic compaction and resend did not cure it; run /compact or /clear), max_tokens (the model's answer was cut off at its output limit), bad_tool_args (the model sent tool calls whose arguments were not valid JSON too many times in the turn), quota_wait_too_long (the provider's usage limit or busy window asked for a wait longer than the agent waits; retry_at says when to send again), rate_limit (the provider refused the request for its rate limit), conversation_reset (Claude Code could not open the session's conversation; the next message starts a new one with the session's history passed in as text), auth on a Claude Code session (Claude Code is not logged in where it runs), delegated_sandbox_unavailable (the sandbox that must confine Claude Code is not available where it runs, so it was not started), delegated_connect_timeout (Claude Code did not answer when started; it may not be logged in there), delegated_launch_failed (Claude Code could not be started; the event.error text says why), spend_cap (a spend cap refused or stopped the turn, or the spend settings file is not valid; the turn's event.error reason says which). The same code rides the turn's event.error and event.agent_done frames on the stream. An open set: treat an unknown code as a generic failure.

retry_at.description: With error_code: when the wait the provider named ends, RFC 3339 UTC (the turn's event.error retry_at). Send the message again after it. Absent when the provider named no wait.

retry_after_secs.description: With retry_at: the seconds the model provider asked to wait, the same number event.error carried as retry_after_secs. retry_at is when that wait ends. A turn recorded before this field reads the whole seconds left until retry_at, at least 1 while it is still ahead (0 once passed).

effects_may_have_occurred.description: True conservatively for every unfinished turn recovered as interrupted, even if it was only accepted, has no recorded tool calls, or was waiting for approval. This does not prove that a tool ran or an external effect occurred. The original turn is never re-run.

dispatched_at.description: RFC3339 time the turn was dispatched to run. Absent until then, and absent on a 202 built from the admission receipt (every fresh turn, and a duplicate the agent answers at admission); present once dispatched on a receipt read from the turn record (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}, and a duplicate answered while the session is busy).

source.description: What admitted the turn: input (a prompt) or workflow (a workflow run). Absent on a 202 built from the admission receipt (every fresh turn, and a duplicate the agent answers at admission); present on a receipt read from the turn record (GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns, GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}, and a duplicate answered while the session is busy).

terminal_at.description: RFC3339 terminal time when known; absent until terminal and when a restart prevented recording the time.

continuation.description: On a turn interrupted by a restart, read while its session is live: what became of the turn's restart continuation. A turn a session message command started is continued once the agent is back (its message is not sent again). owed: a continuation is owed, or not yet decided, so the turn's end is not final yet; spent: a continuation turn ran for it (continued_by names that turn, whose own end is this one's); retired: no continuation will run (a stop, new work, the retry allowance used up, or a trimmed or cleared history); none: a turn a restart never continues (a prompt or a workflow). Absent on any other turn, for a dormant session, and from an agent that does not report it.

get.summary: Read a session's per-call LLM usage.
get.description: Returns one row per recorded LLM call of the session (its turns, and the helpers and workflow steps it ran) with the token counts the provider reported (cache reads and cache writes apart from uncached input), the cost and the latency, oldest first, plus totals over the whole session. Use it to see how much of each prompt the provider served from its cache. A failed attempt is its own row. Works for a live or closed session without attaching. after_id is an exclusive cursor: rows with a larger id. To read every row, send next_after_id back as after_id while has_more is true; polling with next_after_id later returns only rows written since. limit caps the page (1 to 5000, default 500). totals always cover the whole session, whatever page was asked for. A session that is not visible to this caller is a plain 404 (uniform envelope). CONFIG-DIR: X-Hoody-Config-Dir selects the record store. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm the session is looked up in ("global", not tied to a realm, or a 24-hex realm id); omitted, the agent's current realm. A session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is the plain 404.

schema.description: A page of the session's usage rows plus its totals.

id.description: The row's id in the usage log; ids grow in write order, so pass the last one back as after_id.

ts.description: When the row was written, in Unix seconds.

turn_id.description: Groups the rows of one model request: its failed attempts and the row that records its outcome share this id. Every model request gets its own id, and a turn that runs tools makes several, so this is not the turn id that agent_done, the X-Hoody-Turn-Id header and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id} use. The member calls of a model fusion request carry that request's id. A row that sums a whole run of calls (a background helper, an auto-reply, a verifier vote, an external coding-agent CLI call) has an id of its own. A recorded context compaction call has an id starting with "compact:".

attempt.description: -1 for the row that records a call's outcome; 0 and up for one failed attempt that came before it; -2 for the spend of a failed model fusion turn, which is not a call of its own.

model.description: The model that served the call.

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens read without the cache (cache reads and cache writes are not included).

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the provider's prompt cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Prompt tokens written to the provider's prompt cache.

cost_usd.description: The call's cost in US dollars: the provider's figure when it reports one, otherwise an estimate; 0 when no price is known.

latency_ms.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds; 0 for a failed attempt.

success.description: Whether the call returned a complete response.

error_code.description: Why the call failed (timeout, rate_limit, auth, network, provider, canceled, context_overflow, provider_incomplete_response, max_tokens, bad_tool_args, unknown): max_tokens is a tool call cut off at the model's output limit, bad_tool_args tool calls whose arguments were not valid JSON too many times in one turn; empty on success.

kind.description: What made the call: chat (a model request of the session), compaction (a context compaction), side (a tool-free completion) or speech (one text-to-speech or speech-to-text call).

op.description: For a speech row: tts or stt. Empty otherwise.

units.description: For a speech row: what the call consumed (text_in_tokens, audio_in_tokens, text_out_tokens, audio_out_tokens, chars_in, audio_in_seconds, audio_out_seconds). Absent otherwise.

cost_state.description: For a speech row: reported (the provider's figure), estimated (from the listed price) or unknown (no price; cost_usd is 0). Empty otherwise.

cost_uncertain.description: true when the call ended early (timeout, broken stream, cancel), so its cost may be off.

provider_cost_usd.description: The cost the provider reported, in US dollars, or null.

pricing_source.description: Where the price came from; empty when none.

pricing_version.description: The version of that price; empty when none.

generation_id.description: The provider's id for the call, when it gave one.

origin.description: Which surface made a speech call; empty otherwise.

quota_op.description: For a speech row: the id of the daily-limit charge the call made. Empty otherwise.

cache_saved_usd.description: What the call's cache reads and writes saved, in US dollars, against sending those tokens as uncached input, at current list prices; negative when writing the cache cost more than reading it saved. 0 when the call used no cache. null for a speech row, a call of a delegated Claude Code session (its price is not known), a model fusion call's own row and the spend of a failed fusion turn (its member calls have their own rows), and a call whose cache price is not known.

items.description: The rows after after_id, oldest first.

calls.description: Chat and compaction rows counted as calls: every such row except attempt -2. Speech rows are counted in by_kind.speech.

input_tokens.description: Sum of input_tokens over the chat and compaction rows.

cache_read_tokens.description: Sum of cache_read_tokens over the chat and compaction rows.

cache_write_tokens.description: Sum of cache_write_tokens over the chat and compaction rows.

output_tokens.description: Sum of output_tokens over the chat and compaction rows.

It is judged by a model against the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; what the worker writes in its replies is not evidence. Name one event: counting, times and and/or conditions are not judged reliably; use match, or several outcomes. Give exactly one of when and match.

state.description: waiting or done.

reason.description: A sentence saying why it ended.

also_found.description: Other outcomes found in the same check, in the order they were given.

seq.description: The event's number in the target's event list.

turn_id.description: The target turn the event belongs to, when it has one.

kind.description: The event's kind.

tool.description: The tool's name.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, when observed.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported an error.

excerpt.description: The start of the event's text, with secrets removed.

by.description: match: an exact outcome matched. judge: a model judged that the events show the outcome; it points at this event, it does not prove it.

p.description: judge only: the model's probability that the events show the outcome.

evidence.description: The event the outcome was found in.

on_timeout.description: What the creator said to do on timeout, kept for the creator's use; the agent does not act on it.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from creation to the end.

max_checks.description: The most model requests it may make (a retried request counts again).

gap.description: true when some target events may not have been read (the start turn was too old, or many events arrived at once).

post.summary: Wait for an outcome in another session's work.
post.description: Creates a waiter owned by the path session: it watches another live session of the same realm (target) until one of the named outcomes shows in the target's work, or until the deadline. An outcome is exact (match: an event's kind, tool, exit status, error flag, text or turn outcome, checked on every event) or judged (when: a sentence a model checks against a short window of the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; the target's replies are not evidence, so a worker saying it is done is not taken as done). A judged outcome is found only when the model is confident and points at one event; it is a finding, not a proof. Judged checks run a few seconds after new tool results, at most every 5 seconds, and at once when a target turn ends; each model request, a retried one included, costs a fraction of a cent and counts toward max_checks. When the deadline passes, events already seen get one last check. The end is announced on the path session's stream as event.waiter_done, carrying the waiter; GET reads it while it is retained: at most 64 ended waiters are retained, and those older than 24 hours may be removed. A waiter does not survive a restart of the agent: it then reads outcome interrupted. Idempotency-Key (optional): the same key and body on this session answers the same waiter (200); the same key with another body is 422. X-Hoody-Cwd and X-Hoody-Config-Dir are not read: the path session supplies both.

name.description: The outcome's name: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. timeout, cancelled, target_closed, interrupted, access_lost and judge_unavailable are reserved.

when.description: A sentence describing one event to look for, for example "the unit tests pass" or "a file named report.md is written" (at most 300 characters). It is judged by a model against the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; what the worker writes in its replies is not evidence. Name one event: counting, times and and/or conditions are not judged reliably; use match, or several outcomes. Give exactly one of when and match.

kind.description: The kind of event.

tool.description: The tool's name, for example bash or write_file.

exit_code.description: tool_result only: the exit status the command must have ended with. A result with no observed exit status never matches.

is_error.description: tool_result only: whether the tool reported an error.

text_contains.description: Text the event must contain (case-sensitive, at most 200 characters).

outcome.description: turn_end only: how the turn ended.

match.description: An exact event: every given field must hold. Checked on every event, without a model. Give exactly one of when and match.

from.description: The target turn it reads from, when one was given.

state.description: waiting or done.

outcome.description: When done: the name of the outcome found, or timeout (nothing found before the deadline), cancelled (by request, or the owner session closed), target_closed (the watched session ended first), interrupted (the agent restarted while waiting; events in between were not watched), access_lost (the current login can no longer reach a session or its realm) or judge_unavailable (judged outcomes could not be checked and no exact outcome was left).

turn_id.description: The target turn the event belongs to, when it has one.

kind.description: The event's kind.

tool.description: The tool's name.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, when observed.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported an error.

excerpt.description: The start of the event's text, with secrets removed.

by.description: match: an exact outcome matched. judge: a model judged that the events show the outcome; it points at this event, it does not prove it.

cost_known.description: false when the price of some check was not reported.

x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the request body or query parameters.

requestBody.description: The waiter.

target.description: The session to watch: live, in the same realm, not the path session.

name.description: The outcome's name: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. timeout, cancelled, target_closed, interrupted, access_lost and judge_unavailable are reserved.

when.description: A sentence describing one event to look for, for example "the unit tests pass" or "a file named report.md is written" (at most 300 characters). It is judged by a model against the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; what the worker writes in its replies is not evidence. Name one event: counting, times and and/or conditions are not judged reliably; use match, or several outcomes. Give exactly one of when and match.

kind.description: The kind of event.

tool.description: The tool's name, for example bash or write_file.

exit_code.description: tool_result only: the exit status the command must have ended with. A result with no observed exit status never matches.

is_error.description: tool_result only: whether the tool reported an error.

text_contains.description: Text the event must contain (case-sensitive, at most 200 characters).

outcome.description: turn_end only: how the turn ended.

match.description: An exact event: every given field must hold. Checked on every event, without a model. Give exactly one of when and match.

outcomes.description: 1 to 4 outcomes. The first found ends the waiter; outcomes found in the same check are listed in also_found.

max_s.description: Seconds until the deadline, 10 to 86400. Default 600.

from.description: A target turn id: read the target's events from that turn's start (also a turn sent but not started yet). Without it, only events after creation are read.
