on_timeout.description: Optional note for the creator on what to do at the deadline; kept on the waiter, not acted on.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Returns one waiter of the path session. A waiter belonging to another session, or one no longer retained, returns 404. X-Hoody-Cwd and X-Hoody-Config-Dir are not read: the path session supplies both.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session id.

parameters.name: waiter_id
parameters.description: The waiter id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

reason.description: A sentence saying why it ended.

also_found.description: Other outcomes found in the same check, in the order they were given.

seq.description: The event's number in the target's event list.

turn_id.description: The target turn the event belongs to, when it has one.

kind.description: The event's kind.

tool.description: The tool's name.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, when observed.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported an error.

excerpt.description: The start of the event's text, with secrets removed.

by.description: match: an exact outcome matched. judge: a model judged that the events show the outcome; it points at this event, it does not prove it.

p.description: judge only: the model's probability that the events show the outcome.

evidence.description: The event the outcome was found in.

on_timeout.description: What the creator said to do on timeout, kept for the creator's use; the agent does not act on it.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from creation to the end.

max_checks.description: The most model requests it may make (a retried request counts again).

gap.description: true when some target events may not have been read (the start turn was too old, or many events arrived at once).

cost_usd.description: What its model checks cost, in US dollars.

cost_known.description: false when the price of some check was not reported.

model.description: The model judged outcomes are checked with.

post.summary: Send a message to a running workflow.
post.description: Injects user feedback/input into the workflow running in this session (foreground or background). The message is delivered to the workflow itself, not queued as a new session turn, and only to the run that was active when it was accepted: a run that starts later never receives it. 200 means the daemon accepted it for that run. 409 no_active_workflow when no workflow is running: nothing is delivered or kept. 503 admission_unconfirmed when the daemon's answer did not arrive within the wait: it may still be delivered.

patch.description: Flips the session's YOLO auto-approve on or off: the same power as the TUI's YOLO toggle, including clearing actions the agent otherwise reserves for a person (a caller that can reach this API is treated as having that permission). Answered from the daemon's own acknowledgement. Arming is refused with 409 approval_policy_locked on a locked policy and 409 approval_policy_active on an "always" policy. get.summary: Watch up to 32 live sessions' events on one stream (SSE).
get.description: One SSE stream for up to 32 live sessions, so a page watching many sessions spends one stream slot instead of one each. Each session keeps exactly what GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream gives it over SSE: its own seq and incarnation, the replay ring from its own cursor, its own replay_gap, replay_boundary ({session_id, max_seq, incarnation}) and lagged drop, and the same event names (the `event:` line drops the "event." prefix; the data keeps the full type). Every session frame's data is {session_id, seq, incarnation, turn_id?, gate?, event}. The per-session control frames carry session_id: replay_boundary; session_lagged {session_id, code: replay_gap|lagged, …} (the lagged frame of the single-session stream); session_end {session_id, reason} (its end frame). They are named session_lagged and session_end because only the last frame, end {reason: "no sessions left"}, ends the stream. A gap or a drop in one session never resets another: a session dropped for slowness gets session_lagged {session_id, code: lagged} and leaves the stream while the others go on; reconnect it with its own cursor. Frames carry no SSE id line (one id cannot hold every session's cursor): keep the last seq applied per session and resume with ?since=<id>:<seq>,…&incarnation=<id>:<incarnation>,…, the per-session cursor and incarnation of GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream, with the same rules (a cursor past the ring, an invalid cursor or another incarnation is answered with that session's replay_gap and its full retained ring). Sessions start in the order of ids. An id that is not live, or that the caller may not see, gets session_end {session_id, reason: "session not found"}; a session that closes gets session_end {session_id, reason: "session closed"}, and one whose owner is no longer the active account session_end {session_id, reason: "session not authorized"}. It reads only: answer gates on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/confirm and /answer, with the gate id from the frame's envelope.

parameters.description: Comma list of <session id>:<seq>, the last gateway seq applied per session; ids not listed start from their whole retained ring.

parameters.name: incarnation
parameters.description: Comma list of <session id>:<incarnation>, the incarnation each since cursor belongs to; a session whose incarnation differs gets replay_gap and its full retained ring.

oneOf.name: agent_done
oneOf.title: agent_done
oneOf.description: Turn complete: it ends a prompt turn. Carries the turn's typed outcome / error_code and notices [{code, message?, detail?}]. Notices are advisory, never an error: hook_skipped_by_policy when a configured user hook was skipped under the always policy, agent_compacts_itself when a Claude Code session's agent decides on its own when to compact its conversation, history_unsaved when a Claude Code session answered from a conversation Hoody could not save, spend_cap_warning when the session's spend file sets action warn and the turn ran over a spend cap (detail session_cap or turn_cap; one notice per cap) (open set). A turn a spend cap stopped fails with error_code spend_cap.

outcome.description: How the turn stopped running. It says nothing about whether the task was done well. Omitted when the agent cannot classify it.

turn_id.description: The turn this closes: the id the dispatching request returned (X-Hoody-Turn-Id, the 202 turn_id). Omitted for a turn not dispatched with one: TUI input, a loop fire, a background-task fire, an auto-reply round.

error_code.description: A stable machine code when outcome is failed. Omitted otherwise. Key hints on it, never on message text.

code.description: A stable code, for example hook_skipped_by_policy.

message.description: A short description. Omitted when none.

detail.description: Optional context; for hook_skipped_by_policy, the hook event and matcher. Omitted when none.

notices.description: Coded facts about how this turn ran that are not errors, for example hook_skipped_by_policy, or spend_cap_warning (detail session_cap or turn_cap) when the turn ran over a spend cap set to warn. Open set. Omitted when there are none.

run_id.description: The workflow run, as in workflows.get_run and GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs/{run_id}. The note names it too.

note.description: The app-generated outcome note, recorded on the user side: the workflow name, the run id, completed, FAILED (with a short error) or cancelled, and how long it ran.

ack.description: The fixed acknowledgement recorded on the assistant side after the note.

workflow_note.description: Set when this closes a workflow run started in the session: the outcome note the agent recorded in the conversation, so the model knows how the run ended. It is its own recorded turn (turns counts it). A reload of the transcript shows the same two messages. Omitted on every other turn.

data.description: Turn complete: it ends a prompt turn. Carries the turn's typed outcome / error_code and notices [{code, message?, detail?}]. Notices are advisory, never an error: hook_skipped_by_policy when a configured user hook was skipped under the always policy, agent_compacts_itself when a Claude Code session's agent decides on its own when to compact its conversation, history_unsaved when a Claude Code session answered from a conversation Hoody could not save, spend_cap_warning when the session's spend file sets action warn and the turn ran over a spend cap (detail session_cap or turn_cap; one notice per cap) (open set). cleanup.description: Present on stopped when the stop could not guarantee it reached every process the work started: detached_may_survive means a process a shell command of the work started in the background (detached) may still be running. Absent when the stop reached them all.

stopped.description: A stop: the work it acted on and how each ended. Omitted otherwise.

cleanup.description: A committed stop, whether or not it found work running: detached_may_survive means a shell command the session ran may have left a process (started in the background, detached) that no stop can be shown to have reached, so it may still be running. Absent when there is no such process.

oneOf.name: waiter_done
oneOf.title: waiter_done
oneOf.description: A waiter this session owns (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters) ended: an outcome was found, or it timed out, was cancelled, or its target closed. Carries the waiter.

session_id.description: The session this frame belongs to: one of ?ids=.

turn_id.description: The turn this frame belongs to, when it belongs to one.

gate.description: The parked gate this frame concerns (id, generation, type, …), as on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream.

label.description: The label it was created with.

owner.description: The session that waits (the path session).

name.description: The outcome's name: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. timeout, cancelled, target_closed, interrupted, access_lost and judge_unavailable are reserved.

when.description: A sentence describing one event to look for, for example "the unit tests pass" or "a file named report.md is written" (at most 300 characters). It is judged by a model against the target's tool calls, tool results and questions; what the worker writes in its replies is not evidence. Name one event: counting, times and and/or conditions are not judged reliably; use match, or several outcomes. Give exactly one of when and match.

kind.description: The kind of event.

tool.description: The tool's name, for example bash or write_file.

exit_code.description: tool_result only: the exit status the command must have ended with. A result with no observed exit status never matches.

is_error.description: tool_result only: whether the tool reported an error.

text_contains.description: Text the event must contain (case-sensitive, at most 200 characters).

outcome.description: turn_end only: how the turn ended.

match.description: An exact event: every given field must hold. Checked on every event, without a model. Give exactly one of when and match.

from.description: The target turn it reads from, when one was given.

state.description: waiting or done.

outcome.description: When done: the name of the outcome found, or timeout (nothing found before the deadline), cancelled (by request, or the owner session closed), target_closed (the watched session ended first), interrupted (the agent restarted while waiting; events in between were not watched), access_lost (the current login can no longer reach a session or its realm) or judge_unavailable (judged outcomes could not be checked and no exact outcome was left).

reason.description: A sentence saying why it ended.

also_found.description: Other outcomes found in the same check, in the order they were given.

seq.description: The event's number in the target's event list.

turn_id.description: The target turn the event belongs to, when it has one.

kind.description: The event's kind.

tool.description: The tool's name.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, when observed.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported an error.

excerpt.description: The start of the event's text, with secrets removed.

by.description: match: an exact outcome matched. judge: a model judged that the events show the outcome; it points at this event, it does not prove it.

p.description: judge only: the model's probability that the events show the outcome.

evidence.description: The event the outcome was found in.

on_timeout.description: What the creator said to do on timeout, kept for the creator's use; the agent does not act on it.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from creation to the end.

max_checks.description: The most model requests it may make (a retried request counts again).

gap.description: true when some target events may not have been read (the start turn was too old, or many events arrived at once).

cost_usd.description: What its model checks cost, in US dollars.

cost_known.description: false when the price of some check was not reported.

model.description: The model judged outcomes are checked with.

waiter.description: The waiter, ended (as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters/{waiter_id} returns it).

data.description: A waiter this session owns (POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/waiters) ended: an outcome was found, or it timed out, was cancelled, or its target closed. Carries the waiter.

oneOf.name: confirm_request
oneOf.title: confirm_request
oneOf.description: Tool/plan confirmation requested (parks a gate). On a helper_gates session a helper's request carries helper_id, parent_tool_call_id and, for a background helper, task_id; it parks beside the session's own gate and is answered by its own id.

session_id.description: The session this frame belongs to: one of ?ids=.

turn_id.description: The turn this frame belongs to, when it belongs to one.

gate.description: The parked gate this frame concerns (id, generation, type, …), as on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream.

tool_name.description: The tool waiting for a decision.

params.description: The tool input the decision is about, redacted, without the agent's own dispatch markers. Always present; null when the call had no input.

requested_dirs.description: Directories outside the session's scope the call needs. Omitted when none.

detail.description: A preview for the person deciding: a fenced command or a diff. A call that touches a known credential store starts with a line ⚠ credential store: <label> (not on an edit's diff or a dangerous card). A gate parked because the tool-call rules could not be checked starts with a line ⚠ rules not checked: <why>. Omitted when none.

offer_session_allow.description: true when an allow-for-the-session answer may be offered (session_scope on /confirm). Omitted when false.

gate_id.description: The agent's own number for this gate, for diagnostics. It is NOT what /confirm takes: echo the frame envelope's gate.id.

gate_cause.description: Why the gate exists, for example static_stakes, dir_access, hook_ask or approval_policy. Open set. Omitted by an older agent.

risk.description: The agent's coarse risk label for the call: read, write or destructive for a fleet action, write for a file write or edit, destructive for a file delete, high for a human-only gate, credential_access when a read, write or unknown call touches a known credential store (a label only: it parks and denies nothing by itself), unknown when the call has no class. Omitted by an older agent.

human_only.description: true when no automatic policy may answer this gate; a person must. Always present.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation a decision must carry (lease_generation on /confirm). Omitted when there is no lease.

lease_required.description: true when the decision must come from the approver-lease holder. Always present.

task_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the background task of the helper that parked the gate. Omitted otherwise.

computer_id.description: The resolved computer id the grant is keyed by.

computer_name.description: The computer name the call used. Omitted when the call named the id.

realm.description: The realm the grant applies in: _global or a realm id.

label.description: Button text, for example Always allow exec on my-box.

exec_trust.description: On a hoody_exec_* card: the per-computer trust option. Answer /confirm with approved true and trust_computer true to run the call and stop exec cards on that computer in this realm until the grant is revoked (exec_trust on POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules). Omitted when no grant can be offered: another tool, a computer that did not resolve, a hook or rules ask, the always approval policy, a headless session.

rule_ids.description: The ids of the rules behind it, in settings order (the same ids GET /api/v1/agent/hooks and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies report).

outcome.description: ask: check-in rules cover the call. deny: the call breaks these limit rules. unchecked: the rules check could not complete (Jev failed or timed out, the input was too large, or the rules await a trust ack); rule_ids is every rule the check covered.

reason.description: Why the rules check could not complete, in plain words (for example Jev has no usable key for its model's provider). Only with outcome unchecked; omitted otherwise.

rules.description: When tool-call rules asked: the rules behind the gate. outcome ask = these check_in rules cover the call; unchecked = the rules check could not complete, so it asks instead (rule_ids = every rule it covered). gate_cause is rules when only rules asked; when a shell hook asked too it stays hook_ask and rules is still present. Omitted when no rule asked.

helper_id.description: The helper that produced this event (a background helper's task id, or a per-spawn helper id). Omitted on the session's own events.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted on the session's own events.

data.description: Tool/plan confirmation requested (parks a gate). On a helper_gates session a helper's request carries helper_id, parent_tool_call_id and, for a background helper, task_id; it parks beside the session's own gate and is answered by its own id.

A client that captured the gate at park time refreshes what its decision must carry. On a helper_gates session each parked helper confirm is re-announced too, with its helper_id.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation a decision must now carry (lease_generation on /confirm); 0 when there is no lease.

lease_required.description: true when the decision must now come from the approver-lease holder.

helper_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the helper whose parked confirm this is. Omitted for the session's own gate.

oneOf.name: error
oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Session error (e.g. join_not_ready).

session_id.description: The session this frame belongs to: one of ?ids=.

turn_id.description: The turn this frame belongs to, when it belongs to one.

gate.description: The parked gate this frame concerns (id, generation, type, …), as on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream.

code.description: A machine code when there is one, for example session_not_found or session_busy, or quota_wait_too_long / rate_limit when a model rate limit ended the turn, or model_unavailable when the provider refused the model itself, or spend_cap when a spend cap refused or stopped the turn or the spend settings file is not valid (agent_done carries the same error_code). Omitted otherwise.

provider.description: The provider id. Omitted when unknown.

model.description: The model name without its provider prefix. Omitted when unknown.

base_url.description: The endpoint called, without credentials or query. Omitted when unknown.

key_source.description: Where the key came from: env, dotenv, oauth-token, network or none. Omitted when unknown.

key_prefix.description: A redacted fragment of the key, never the key. Omitted when none.

http_status.description: The provider's HTTP status. Omitted when the failure was not an HTTP error.

retryable.description: Whether the failure was classed retryable. Omitted when false.

attempts.description: Attempts made before giving up. Omitted when unknown.

req_id.description: The turn's id in the agent's log (per-attempt rows are <id>.N), to find the full cause in GET /api/v1/agent/logs. Omitted when none.

err_code.description: The failure class, shared with the usage statistics: max_tokens is a tool call cut off at the model's output limit, bad_tool_args tool calls whose arguments were not valid JSON too many times in one turn. Omitted when unclassified.

stop_reason.description: Why the model stopped writing the response that failed, when it said: max_tokens means the answer was cut off at the model's output limit. Omitted when unknown.

last_error.description: The last attempt's cause: one line, credentials scrubbed, at most 600 characters. Omitted when none.

diag.description: Provider diagnostics for a failed model call (provider, model, endpoint, key source and a redacted prefix, HTTP status, attempts). With code no_credentials it names the provider and model that have no stored key. Omitted for every other error.

max_steps.description: With code max_steps: the step limit in force for the turn that stopped (the agent's max_steps_per_turn). Omitted on every other error.

reason.description: With code delegated_agent_unavailable: why the realm's default delegated agent cannot start here (unknown_agent, disabled, not_installed, missing_launcher, probe_failure or settings_unreadable). With code spend_cap: session_cap (the session's spend reached max_session_usd), turn_cap (the turn's own model requests reached max_turn_usd) or invalid_setting (the spend settings file is not valid, so no work runs until it is fixed or deleted; the message names the file's path and the problem). Omitted on every other error.

retry_after_secs.description: The seconds the model provider asked to wait before the next request: always with code quota_wait_too_long (the turn ended instead of waiting), and on a failed model request whose last answer (a rate limit or a busy provider) named a wait. Send the message again after that. Omitted otherwise.

retry_at.description: With retry_after_secs: when that wait ends, RFC 3339 in UTC (for example 2026-10-10T14:47:00Z), the same time the message names. Send the message again after it. Omitted otherwise.

spend_cap_usd.description: With code spend_cap and reason session_cap or turn_cap: the cap that was reached, in US dollars. Omitted otherwise.

spent_usd.description: With spend_cap_usd: the spend that reached it, in US dollars (the session's whole spend for session_cap, the turn's own model requests for turn_cap). Omitted otherwise.

resume_run_id.description: With code resume_superseded (a workflow run's resume was refused after it was accepted, because a newer run of the same original run started a step): the run to resume instead. Omitted otherwise.

data.description: Session error (e.g. join_not_ready).

oneOf.name: gate_resolved
oneOf.title: gate_resolved
oneOf.description: A parked confirm/question gate was resolved (possibly by another attached client).

session_id.description: The session this frame belongs to: one of ?ids=.

turn_id.description: The turn this frame belongs to, when it belongs to one.

gate.description: The parked gate this frame concerns (id, generation, type, …), as on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream.

kind.description: Which kind of gate was resolved.

gate_id.description: The agent's own number for a resolved confirm gate. Omitted on a question gate.

question_id.description: The agent's own number for a resolved question gate. Omitted on a confirm gate.

outcome.description: How the gate ended: answered by a decision, cancelled without one, auto-approved by switching YOLO mode on while it was parked, or (a helper's gate only) denied because nobody answered within the helper agent's ask_timeout.

provenance.description: What resolved the gate. Only decision is a real answer; every other value means nobody decided, and the outcome is then never answered. timeout is a helper's gate that ran out of time. Omitted by an older agent.

holder.description: The approver-lease holder whose decision resolved a confirm gate (the holder sent when the lease was acquired). Omitted when there is none.

generation.description: The approver-lease generation the decision was made under. Omitted when there is none.

request_id.description: The request id of the decision that resolved the gate, when that decision carried one. On the copy sent only to the sender of a retried or late decision (one naming a gate that already resolved, including a helper gate that timed out or was cancelled while the decision was in flight), it is that decision's own request id.

helper_id.description: On a helper_gates session, the helper that parked this gate (its event.confirm_request or event.user_question carried the same helper_id). Omitted for the session's own gates.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted for the session's own gates.

task_id.description: The background task of that helper (equal to helper_id). Omitted for a foreground helper and for the session's own gates.

approved.description: The tool was approved (true) or denied.

persist_dirs.description: An approved directory grant was persisted to settings.json.

session_scope.description: The decision was asked to apply for the rest of the session.

trust_computer.description: The gate's exec_trust offer was accepted.

remember.description: false when the approval applied to this call only (sent with remember false). Omitted otherwise.

superseded.description: true when the call was declined because the user sent a new message instead (sent with superseded true). Omitted otherwise.

decision.description: On a confirm gate whose outcome is answered: the decision it consumed. Omitted otherwise.

session_scope_applied.description: false when an approving session_scope decision applied once only (a locked approval policy keeps the session-wide rule from being added); see note. Omitted otherwise.

note.description: Present beside session_scope_applied: why the wider grant did not apply.

data.description: A parked confirm/question gate was resolved (possibly by another attached client).

oneOf.name: session_started
oneOf.title: session_started
oneOf.description: Session attached. Its data is the same `started` object POST /api/v1/agent/sessions returns. It is the first frame (seq 1) of a fresh attach while the stream still retains seq 1. A resume with `since` does not repeat it, except when the cursor cannot be resumed: an invalid `since` (or Last-Event-ID), an `incarnation` that does not match the session's current one, or a cursor ahead of the stream is each answered with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) and the whole retained stream, which includes it if seq 1 is still retained. A late attach after the oldest frames were evicted starts with a `lagged` frame (code replay_gap) instead and does not carry it. In either case read the same object as `started` from GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}, which carries it while the session is attached.

session_id.description: The session this frame belongs to: one of ?ids=.

turn_id.description: The turn this frame belongs to, when it belongs to one.

gate.description: The parked gate this frame concerns (id, generation, type, …), as on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream.

tool_id.description: The tool_use id of the call this result answers (the tool_id of its event.tool_call).

output.description: The tool's output text, with secret-shaped text redacted. It may be shorter than what the tool produced: see truncated. Always empty for tool_orchestrator.

is_error.description: The tool failed, or the call was denied or cancelled.

detail.description: Rich preview for the chat (an edit diff, the first lines of a written file). Omitted when there is none.

error_code.description: A stable machine code for a failed result, for example hook_held when a hook that covers the tool waits for a person to trust it, or its trust cannot be checked: the call did not run, and retrying cannot help until a person acts; or outcome_unknown when the call may have taken effect although it reported a failure, so check before retrying. Omitted on success and on failures that carry only text.

hint.description: A remediation sentence for a coding-CLI tool's sign-in failure. Omitted otherwise.

hint_cmd.description: The command that fixes the failure hint describes. Omitted otherwise.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the tool ran, in milliseconds (0 is a real value). Omitted when the tool never ran or its run was not timed.

exit_code.description: The bash exit status, 0 included. Omitted when no process exit was observed; evidence of success needs exit_code 0, not just is_error false.

truncated.description: true is positive evidence that output is not the tool's whole output. It is set by bash (including computer and long-running commands), bash_job_wait, read_file, read_minified_file, grep, glob_files, web_fetch, load_hoody_skill, MCP tools and tool_orchestrator, when the agent cut the output to a size cap, a file search stopped past max_results or the computer's search limits, or the event leaves the output out (tool_orchestrator). A range the model asked for (read_file offset and limit) is not a cut, and neither is secret redaction or deny-list filtering. A missing truncated is inconclusive, even from an agent with the tool_output_completeness capability: other tools never set it, and some tools say in their own output when they shortened it.

original_bytes.description: When truncated is true, the size in bytes of the text the cut was applied to: the whole output, or for a log tail or a fetched page that log or page alone. Omitted when the size is unknown, for example when the agent stopped reading a stream or a computer cut it first.

helper_id.description: The helper that ran the tool (see helper_ids). Omitted for the session's own tools.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started that helper. Omitted for the session's own tools.

rule_ids.description: The ids of the rules behind it, in settings order (the same ids GET /api/v1/agent/hooks and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies report).

outcome.description: ask: check-in rules cover the call. deny: the call breaks these limit rules. unchecked: the rules check could not complete (Jev failed or timed out, the input was too large, or the rules await a trust ack); rule_ids is every rule the check covered.

reason.description: Why the rules check could not complete, in plain words (for example Jev has no usable key for its model's provider). Only with outcome unchecked; omitted otherwise.

rules.description: On a call a tool-call rule denied: the rules behind it. outcome deny = the call breaks these limit rules; unchecked = the rules check could not complete where no one can be asked (a helper), so the call was denied. Omitted on every other result.

data.description: Tool result.

oneOf.description: Control frame, per session: that session's ring→live boundary, as on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream.

session_id.description: The session this frame belongs to: one of ?ids=.

max_seq.description: The highest seq the ring held when the stream attached: frames up to it are replay, later frames are live. Pass the last seq you read as ?since= to resume.

incarnation.description: The incarnation max_seq belongs to. Pass it as ?incarnation= with the cursor.

turn_id.description: The turn this stream is watching: on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/prompt:stream, the turn the request dispatched (equal to X-Hoody-Turn-Id); on GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/stream, the turn dispatched through this API that was running when the stream attached. Omitted when no such turn is running, including a turn another client (the TUI) started on the same session; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state current_turn_id covers that case. It names the turn for POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/cancel turn_id and matches its agent_done turn_id. Later frames carry their own envelope turn_id.

turn_since.description: While a turn runs: the cursor just before its first frame (the same value as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state turn_since). A client holding every frame after it can reconnect with ?since=turn_since to replay the whole turn. Omitted when idle, and on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/prompt:stream when the dispatched turn already ended and another holds the slot.

patch.description: Applies a SHALLOW top-level merge into the home settings.json (a nil value deletes a key): a top-level key you send replaces that whole key. Process-wide config (global/no-realm): settings have no realm dimension, so a per-request realm header returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported. SECURITY: security-load-bearing keys (deny_list, deny_urls, features, allowed_directories, hooks, disableAllHooks, mcp_servers, tools, rules, rules_timeout_ms, shipped_hooks, exec_trust, audio) cannot be modified over HTTP and return 403 settings_key_protected: change features with PATCH /api/v1/agent/settings/features and MCP servers with the /api/v1/agent/mcp routes, and edit settings.json at the host to change a guardrail. A non-null top-level "model" is rejected 400: nothing consumes it (pin a model on the chat agent via PATCH /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/model, or switch a live session via PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/model); {"model":null} still deletes a previously-persisted value. "session_title_model" (a provider/model string) picks the model that names chats; absent or "" uses each chat's own model (turn naming off with the session_titles feature, PATCH /api/v1/agent/settings/features). Returns {status, settings}: settings is the resulting home object.

get.description: Reads the instructions every agent in the realm gets, whether they are on, and their revision. When they are on and not blank, the realm's chats, helpers and workflow steps receive them, unless a chat's or agent's prompt settings leave them out; a separate setting can also leave them out for helpers and workflow steps. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

get.description: Lists the persisted model-fusion composites. Pass ?include_invalid=true to also receive the entries that failed validation as a TOP-LEVEL `invalid` array beside `items` (each with the failure reason and its stable raw-file index; never mixed into or paginated with the selectable items) so a broken composite is DIAGNOSABLE. put.description: Replaces the spend caps, all three values together, when the caps still have expected_revision (from GET /settings/spend-caps; an empty string when no file existed); otherwise 409 revision_conflict with details.current_revision and nothing is written. A cap is a number from 0 (off) to 1000000 US dollars; action is stop or warn; anything else is 400 bad_request (details.field). Writing over a file that is not valid fixes it. Chats apply the new caps from their next check; work already running is never stopped. Writers of the agent take one lock across the check and the write; an edit made by hand in the same instant can still be lost. 500 store_failed when the file cannot be written, is a symbolic link, or cannot be read because it is not a regular file; with details.outcome_unknown true the new caps are in place but may not survive a crash, so read them again. Answers the caps after the write. Process-wide: every scope header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.description: SCAFFOLDS a new local skill. `name` is the only input: the daemon creates the skill directory in the writable skills root and writes a fixed SKILL.md template: frontmatter carrying that name and a literal `description: TODO` placeholder, plus a stub body. It does NOT accept the skill's description or content, and a new skill is unusable until you replace them, because the description is what the model reads to decide whether to load the skill. So this is step one of two: create the skill here, then take the returned root_dir + rel_dir, GET the scaffold with GET /api/v1/agent/skills/source, and write the real frontmatter and body with PUT /api/v1/agent/skills/source. The create fails when a skill of that name (or that target directory) already exists in ANY root, and when the scope has no writable skills root. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

requestBody.description: The discovered skills to import: the import source and the selected entries returned by the import scan, plus an optional overwrite flag. A client-supplied filesystem path is not an input: every source location is re-derived from the source and the selected entry.

source.description: The import source the entries were scanned from.
The entry's import source. Optional; when set it must equal the request `source`, or that entry is refused.

rel_dir.description: The entry's directory, as the import scan reported it. Required: an entry without it is refused in results.

items.description: The selected scan entries to import. At least one is required.

overwrite.description: Replace an already-installed skill at the same destination instead of refusing that entry. Defaults to false.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.summary: Stop the work running in the realm that the caller may see (at most 256 items per call; next_cursor continues).
post.description: Stops, in one call, all running work in one realm that the caller may see (the same realm and account gates as the list routes). Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A cwd, config-dir or computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. It covers: running or parked session turns (every live session, including system, resident and headless ones; each is stopped like POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/cancel with the turn_id of the turn that was running when the call listed it, so a turn that starts later is never stopped, only reported under started_during_call), background tasks, workflow runs, todo runs (the lease is released as cancelled, as POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/cancel-run does), detached local background bash jobs, detached background bash jobs on bound computers, loops (PAUSED, never deleted: resume one with PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/loops/{loopId} {"paused":false}), and this gateway's detached headless and gated tool jobs. Work it does not reach is named in not_covered. Each stop runs under a 2 s timeout (10 s for a computer bash job, whose kill is a computer exec that allows 3 s for SIGTERM before SIGKILL; at most 8 of those run at once and at most 32 per call), so a stuck item fails instead of holding the call; each stopped item is then re-read until it has stopped, for at most 5 s, and reported stopped only when a re-read saw it stopped. Finally the work is listed again: anything running that was not in the first list started during the call and is reported under started_during_call, not stopped. At most 256 items are acted on per call, in the fixed kind order of the items' kind enum, then by id. When the cap is hit, complete is false and next_cursor names where the call stopped: send it back as after to continue with the items behind it. The cursor is opaque: send it back unchanged. A call with after does not act on items at or before the cursor; those still running are listed under behind_cursor and make complete false (call again without after to reach them). complete is true only when the call reached every item and nothing started meanwhile; otherwise call again. With nothing running the call answers 200 with empty lists and complete true, so it is safe to repeat.

schema.description: The per-item outcomes of this call. Composed by the gateway.

not_covered.reason: synchronous and streaming tool and headless requests end when their HTTP request is closed

kind.description: What the item is. session: a session turn or parked gate; task: a background task; workflow_run; todo_run; bash_job: a detached local background shell; remote_bash_job: a detached background shell on a bound computer (already_done when it had finished, its recorded leader process had exited, or no process was left to signal); loop: a recurring loop (paused); gateway_job: a detached headless or gated tool job of this gateway.

id.description: The item's id: a session id, <session id>/<task id> for a task, a run id, a todo id, a bash job id (local or computer), a loop id or a job id.

outcome.description: stopped: the stop reached running work and a re-read after it saw it stopped (a loop: paused). already_done: it had finished before the stop reached it. failed: the stop was refused, did not return in time, or the item was still running when the re-reads ended; detail says which.

detail.description: Present on failed: why.

items.description: One result per item acted on, in item order.

kind.description: What the item is (as items[].kind).

started_during_call.description: Work that was running at the end of the call but not at its start (a session: a turn or tool run it began during the call). Not stopped: call again.

kind.description: What the item is (as items[].kind).

behind_cursor.description: With after: the items at or before the cursor that were still running (at most 256 are listed). Not acted on by this call: call again without after to reach them. Empty without after.

complete.description: True when the call reached every item in scope and no work started during it: no next_cursor, and behind_cursor and started_during_call are empty.

next_cursor.description: Present when the item cap was hit: pass it, unchanged, as after to continue. Opaque.

kind.description: The kind of work.

reason.description: Why it is not stopped here, and how to stop it.

count.description: For remote_bash_job_unowned: how many such records the realm has that are not known to have ended. For gateway_job_unscoped: how many such jobs are in flight.

not_covered.description: Kinds of work this route does not stop, with why. Always sync_request. Under an active login, also remote_bash_job_unowned with a count when the realm has computer bash job records written before jobs recorded their owner: no caller can see them, so they are never stopped here. Also gateway_job_unscoped with a count while detached headless runs started with no concrete realm are in flight: the gateway cannot place them in a realm, so it does not stop the jobs (the daemon still stops their sessions when they are in this realm).

requestBody.description: Optional. Omit (or send {}) to start from the first item.

after.description: A next_cursor from an earlier call, unchanged (the cursor is opaque): act only on the items after it. Any other value is 400 bad_request.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

get.description: Lists master todos for the requesting cwd/config_dir, with `revision`, a change-detection cursor for the todos visible in the selected realm and account (null with ?realm=all; compare it for inequality only). It is NOT the per-todo CAS token: the update, archive, snooze and claim calls take each todo's own `revision` from GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}). Filter with the query parameters states, tags (repeat the parameter for several values), query, open_only and all; an invalid boolean or unknown state is a 400. Realm: ?realm= (or the X-Hoody-Realm header) lists one realm: "global" (todos not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id; ?realm=all lists every realm this login serves (query only, never the header). Omitted, the agent's current realm. Every row carries its realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm lists only that realm: any other value, all included, is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A realm's list holds its own todos and the global ones; ?realm=all holds the global ones only when this login serves global. With ?realm=all, revision is null: there is no revision on an all-realm list. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

parameters.name: states
parameters.description: Only todos in one of these states. Repeat the parameter for several (?states=ready&states=blocked).

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Only todos carrying these tags. Repeat the parameter for several (?tags=a&tags=b).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free-text filter over title/body.

parameters.name: open_only
parameters.description: When true, only open (non-terminal) todos.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: When true, include archived todos. Closed todos are listed without it.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: List order. `default` (or omitted): open todos first, then priority, rank, number. `closed_at`: closed todos by `closed_at`, newest first; todos without a `closed_at` follow in the default order. Any other value is 400.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: The realm to list: "global" (todos not tied to a realm), a 24-hex realm id, or "all" for every realm this login serves. Also accepted as the X-Hoody-Realm header, except "all". Omitted, the agent's current realm.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number for pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum items per page (0 = no pagination).

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of todos: open before closed, then by priority, rank and number (sort=closed_at orders closed todos newest close first). Each element is the todo record GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id} returns without its timeline and proposals.

id.description: Stable todo id. The daemon mints todo_ followed by 24 lowercase hex characters; a stored record is listed with the id it holds.

revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency token, bumped on every persisted change (including timeline entries, leases and proposals) except the triage stamp (triaged_at). Send it back as `revision` on a write to this todo; a stale value is rejected.

content_rev.description: Bumped only on substantive changes: an edit to title, body, priority, tags, cwd, acceptance, automation, suggested_agent, needs_human, question_for_human or blocked_reason, an added link, and every state change, including the ones the agent makes itself (a fresh claim starting a run, a run finishing with a new state or a question, an expired lease returning the todo to ready, a snooze waking a blocked todo). Not bumped by comments (including the clearing of needs_human and question_for_human that a human reply causes), rank or wake_at changes, lease renewals, proposals, the triage stamp or archiving. Omitted when zero.

title_auto.description: True while the title is provisional (taken from the body's first line) and the next triage pass may rewrite it. Omitted when false.

body.description: Todo body. Omitted when empty.

state.description: Lifecycle state: inbox, ready, blocked, in_progress, review, done, dropped as the daemon writes it. A stored todo carries the state its file holds, which the todo store does not check on load, so this is not an enum.

rank.description: Manual order within a priority band.

tags.description: Labels. Omitted when empty.

tags_auto.description: True while the next triage pass should fill the labels. Omitted when false.

cwd.description: Working directory the todo belongs to.

computer_id.description: Hoody computer the todo was filed from. Omitted for a local todo.

computer_name.description: That computer's name as captured when the todo was filed. Omitted when unknown.

container_id.description: Deprecated, read-only. Set only on a todo filed before the computer rename from a remote computer: it names that computer and the todo is shown read-only. New todos carry computer_id.

container_name.description: Deprecated, read-only. The computer name captured on a todo filed before the computer rename. New todos carry computer_name.

read_only.description: True on a todo that cannot be changed: it was filed from a remote computer before the computer rename (container_id and no computer_id), or it carries two different computer identities. A write to it is refused. Omitted otherwise.

realm_id.description: Realm the todo was filed from, fixed at creation. Omitted for the global realm.

owner_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the account that filed the todo; reads hide a todo owned by another account. Omitted when unstamped.

source.description: Where the todo came from: {kind, session_id?, agent?, turn?, loop_id?, run_id?}, kind one of manual, agent, workflow, loop, cli, github.

links.description: Typed references to other artifacts: {kind, target, label?}, kind one of session, workflow_run, workflow_def, file, url, todo, github. Omitted when empty.

automation.description: Automation level. Current writers set one of inherit (project/global setting), manual (never auto-act), triage (auto-triage only) or full (auto-triage and auto-execute); an older record may carry another value, which is returned as stored. Omitted when unset.

parent_id.description: Parent todo id. Omitted when none.

fingerprint.description: Dedupe key derived from the todo's content, computer and realm; re-filing the same todo lands on this record. Omitted when unset.

filed_body_digest.description: Digest of the body as first filed, so a redelivery of that filing still lands on this record after the body was edited. Omitted on older todos.

needs_human.description: True when triage wants a human decision. Omitted when false.

question_for_human.description: The question triage wants answered. Omitted when empty.

suggested_agent.description: Agent triage suggests for the work. Omitted when empty.

blocked_reason.description: Why the todo is blocked. Omitted when empty.

session_id.description: Worker session. Omitted when none.

run_id.description: The run holding the lease: an opaque id the agent mints for each fresh lease, kept when the owner renews it. Compare it for equality only. POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/cancel-run takes it as `expected_run`. Omitted on a lease taken before run ids existed.

expires_at.description: When the lease lapses unless renewed (RFC3339).

lease.description: Present while a worker is executing the todo.

attempts.description: Worker runs attempted. Omitted when zero.

wake_at.description: Snooze end (RFC3339); a blocked todo also moves back to ready then. Omitted when not snoozed.

tombstone.description: True on an archived todo. Omitted when false.

archived_at.description: When the todo was archived (RFC3339). Omitted when not archived.

pending_proposals.description: How many of the todo's proposals wait for a person: status pending and not past expires_at (approve and deny take them on GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}). Omitted when zero. A proposal that passes expires_at leaves the count at the next list without moving the revision.

comment_count.description: Number of conversation entries in the timeline: comments posted by a human plus the orchestrator's replies (agent_msg). Omitted when zero.

last_activity.description: Most recent activity (RFC3339). Omitted when unset.

triaged_at.description: Last triage pass (RFC3339). Omitted when never triaged.

closed_at.description: When the todo reached done or dropped (RFC3339). Omitted while open.

realm.description: The todo's realm: "global" for one not tied to a realm, else its 24-hex realm id. Pass it as X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) to reach it by id.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages (the full count, not the page size).

limit.description: Items per page (present only when limit>0).

revision.description: The store-wide poll cursor for this realm and account, a JSON integer: the value GET /api/v1/agent/todos/revision returns. It moves when a todo this caller can see changes; it is not a todo's own revision (PATCH /api/v1/agent/todos/{id} takes that one, from the row). null with ?realm=all: there is no revision on an all-realm list.

post.description: Files a new master todo. Deterministic triage (normalize, fingerprint-dedupe, defaults) runs server-side. A filing is deduped (deduped true, the open todo returned) only when an open todo of the same owner has the same normalized title, cwd, computer and realm AND the same body (whitespace runs compared as one space; the body it was first filed with matches too, after an edit); a different body files a new todo. requestBody.description: New todo (deterministic triage runs server-side). The todo's working directory is taken from the body `cwd` OR, if omitted, the X-Hoody-Cwd request-scope header; one of the two is required (an empty cwd is rejected).

title.description: Todo title. Longer input is not rejected: the title is cut to its first 200 Unicode code points before it is stored.

body.description: Todo body / description. Longer input is not rejected: the body is cut to its first 1,024 Unicode code points before it is stored.

priority.description: Optional priority band 0..4 (0 = P0 urgent … 4 = P4 someday); defaults to 2 when omitted. Must be a JSON integer in range: a string or out-of-range value is rejected.

post.description: Permanently and irreversibly removes the selected realm's todos that were archived more than 90 days ago, or that have no readable archive time; more recently archived ones are kept. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A purge removes only the selected realm's own archived todos: a realm id's purge never removes the global todos, which only a purge in realm global removes.

post.description: Kicks an LLM triage pass over the inbox and returns {job_id}. Each call triages at most the first 10 inbox todos in list order. It spends model budget on an autonomous LLM run and asks for no human confirmation: the same property that makes POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/run a privileged operation. Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy; the daemon's own admin check may still refuse with 403 admin_unauthorized when the daemon was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A realm's view holds its own todos and the global ones; a todo it cannot see is 404 not_found.

schema.description: The operation's JSON reply, passed through verbatim.

status.description: "ok" on a 200.

id.description: Stable todo id. The daemon mints todo_ followed by 24 lowercase hex characters; a stored record is listed with the id it holds.

revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency token, bumped on every persisted change (including timeline entries, leases and proposals) except the triage stamp (triaged_at). Send it back as `revision` on a write to this todo; a stale value is rejected.

content_rev.description: Bumped only on substantive changes: an edit to title, body, priority, tags, cwd, acceptance, automation, suggested_agent, needs_human, question_for_human or blocked_reason, an added link, and every state change, including the ones the agent makes itself (a fresh claim starting a run, a run finishing with a new state or a question, an expired lease returning the todo to ready, a snooze waking a blocked todo). Not bumped by comments (including the clearing of needs_human and question_for_human that a human reply causes), rank or wake_at changes, lease renewals, proposals, the triage stamp or archiving. Omitted when zero.

title_auto.description: True while the title is provisional (taken from the body's first line) and the next triage pass may rewrite it. Omitted when false.

body.description: Todo body. Omitted when empty.

state.description: Lifecycle state: inbox, ready, blocked, in_progress, review, done, dropped as the daemon writes it. A stored todo carries the state its file holds, which the todo store does not check on load, so this is not an enum.

rank.description: Manual order within a priority band.

tags.description: Labels. Omitted when empty.

tags_auto.description: True while the next triage pass should fill the labels. Omitted when false.

cwd.description: Working directory the todo belongs to.

computer_id.description: Hoody computer the todo was filed from. Omitted for a local todo.

computer_name.description: That computer's name as captured when the todo was filed. Omitted when unknown.

container_id.description: Deprecated, read-only. Set only on a todo filed before the computer rename from a remote computer: it names that computer and the todo is shown read-only. New todos carry computer_id.

container_name.description: Deprecated, read-only. The computer name captured on a todo filed before the computer rename. New todos carry computer_name.

read_only.description: True on a todo that cannot be changed: it was filed from a remote computer before the computer rename (container_id and no computer_id), or it carries two different computer identities. A write to it is refused. Omitted otherwise.

realm_id.description: Realm the todo was filed from, fixed at creation. Omitted for the global realm.

owner_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the account that filed the todo; reads hide a todo owned by another account. Omitted when unstamped.

source.description: Where the todo came from: {kind, session_id?, agent?, turn?, loop_id?, run_id?}, kind one of manual, agent, workflow, loop, cli, github.

links.description: Typed references to other artifacts: {kind, target, label?}, kind one of session, workflow_run, workflow_def, file, url, todo, github. Omitted when empty.

automation.description: Automation level. Current writers set one of inherit (project/global setting), manual (never auto-act), triage (auto-triage only) or full (auto-triage and auto-execute); an older record may carry another value, which is returned as stored. Omitted when unset.

parent_id.description: Parent todo id. Omitted when none.

fingerprint.description: Dedupe key derived from the todo's content, computer and realm; re-filing the same todo lands on this record. Omitted when unset.

filed_body_digest.description: Digest of the body as first filed, so a redelivery of that filing still lands on this record after the body was edited. Omitted on older todos.

needs_human.description: True when triage wants a human decision. Omitted when false.

question_for_human.description: The question triage wants answered. Omitted when empty.

suggested_agent.description: Agent triage suggests for the work. Omitted when empty.

blocked_reason.description: Why the todo is blocked. Omitted when empty.

session_id.description: Worker session. Omitted when none.

run_id.description: The run holding the lease: an opaque id the agent mints for each fresh lease, kept when the owner renews it. Compare it for equality only. POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/cancel-run takes it as `expected_run`. Omitted on a lease taken before run ids existed.

expires_at.description: When the lease lapses unless renewed (RFC3339).

lease.description: Present while a worker is executing the todo.

attempts.description: Worker runs attempted. Omitted when zero.

wake_at.description: Snooze end (RFC3339); a blocked todo also moves back to ready then. Omitted when not snoozed.

ts.description: When the entry was written (RFC3339). Informative only: entries are ordered by insertion.

kind.description: What the entry records. Current writers produce the values below; an older entry may carry another value, which is returned as stored. filed: the todo was created. comment: a posted comment. note: a daemon note. triage: a triage pass's output. state: a state transition. run_start / run_end: a worker run began / ended with its outcome. proposal: a run proposal was made, resolved or expired. agent_msg: an orchestrator reply, or a note that the orchestrator thread could not run. lease: the execution lease was claimed. snooze: the todo woke from a snooze.

actor.description: Who wrote the entry: {kind, session_id?, agent?}, kind one of human, agent, triage, orchestrator, worker, daemon.

body.description: The entry text. Omitted when empty.

meta.description: String-valued detail keyed by name (e.g. `proposal` on a proposal entry). Omitted when empty.

timeline.description: The todo's activity thread, oldest first. Append-only; the first `filed` entry is always kept when older entries are trimmed. Absent when empty.

id.description: Proposal id, the value approve and deny take.

action.description: What approval starts.

agent.description: Agent the worker would run as. Omitted when unset.

prompt.description: Prompt the worker would receive. Omitted when empty.

todo_revision.description: The todo's content_rev when the proposal was made; a substantive edit since then invalidates it.

expires_at.description: RFC3339; after this the proposal expires.

status.description: Proposal state.

proposals.description: Human-approvable run proposals. Omitted when none.

tombstone.description: True on an archived todo. Omitted when false.

archived_at.description: When the todo was archived (RFC3339). Omitted when not archived.

comment_count.description: Number of conversation entries in the timeline: comments posted by a human plus the orchestrator's replies (agent_msg). Omitted when zero.

last_activity.description: Most recent activity (RFC3339). Omitted when unset.

triaged_at.description: Last triage pass (RFC3339). Omitted when never triaged.

closed_at.description: When the todo reached done or dropped (RFC3339). Omitted while open.

requestBody.description: CAS-guarded field patch / state transition (the {id} comes from the path). Only the keys present are patched.

revision.description: The TODO's own current `revision` (from GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}, NOT the store-wide revision); a stale value is rejected.

title.description: New title. Longer input is not rejected: the title is cut to its first 200 Unicode code points before it is stored.

body.description: New body. Longer input is not rejected: the body is cut to its first 1,024 Unicode code points before it is stored.

state.description: Move the todo to this state (the board move). Allowed moves, from the current state: inbox → ready | blocked | dropped; ready → blocked | dropped | inbox; blocked → ready | inbox | dropped; in_progress → review | ready | blocked | dropped; review → done | ready | dropped; done → inbox | ready; dropped → inbox | ready. Sending the current state leaves the state as it is (the other fields still apply). in_progress is not settable here: POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/claim or POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/run enters it by taking the lease, and while a worker holds the lease the state cannot be changed (POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/cancel-run or POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/release ends it). Any other move is 400 bad_request ("invalid transition <from> → <to>"), and so is any update to an archived todo, whatever its revision. Otherwise the revision is checked first: a stale one is 409 todo_conflict whatever the state. Compatibility: in_progress is no longer in this enum, so a client that validates against the schema can no longer echo state in_progress on an in_progress todo (the daemon still accepts that same-state write); omit state to leave it unchanged.

tags.description: New tag set. Each is trimmed of whitespace and a leading #, cut to 40 code points; empty and duplicate tags are dropped, and at most 12 are kept.

automation.description: New automation level: inherit (follow the project or global setting), manual (never act on its own), triage (triage only, never run) or full (triage and run). An empty string leaves the level unchanged; any other string is 400 bad_request.

suggested_agent.description: The agent suggested to work on the todo. An empty string clears it.

needs_human.description: Whether the todo waits for a person. A move to done or dropped, or out of blocked, clears it unless the same request sets it.

question_for_human.description: The question the todo puts to a person. An empty string clears it. A move to done or dropped, or out of blocked, clears it unless the same request sets it.

blocked_reason.description: Why the todo is blocked. An empty string clears it.

wake_at.description: Snooze the todo until this RFC 3339 time, or send an empty string to clear the snooze. Any other text, or a value that is not a string (null included), is 400 bad_request. A done or dropped todo never keeps a wake time: the request that closes it clears it, and a wake_at sent to a closed todo is not stored.

reason.description: Optional free text for the audit trail. When the request moves the todo to another state, it is recorded on that state change in the todo's timeline; otherwise it is not stored.

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Archives a todo. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. outcome.description: How the run ended. done → review; blocked → blocked; failed → ready and increments the attempt counter; cancelled → ready without incrementing it. Required: any other value is rejected.

summary.description: Short account of what the run did, written to the timeline as the run_end entry (capped at 1024 characters).

question_for_human.description: A question to surface to the operator alongside the outcome: the field a blocked run uses to say what it needs (capped at 1024 characters).

servers.description: The computer's agent kit: projectId and computerId name the computer, server the server that hosts it, and serviceIndex the kit instance (1-500).

post.description: Dispatches a background worker to autonomously work a todo and returns {job_id, session_id}. The request itself counts as the human approval and no further confirmation is asked (the model-facing run_todo tool, by contrast, refuses an autonomous caller). Access is decided by the computer's proxy permission policy; the daemon's own admin check may still refuse with 403 admin_unauthorized when the daemon was started with a separate administrator token, which an HTTP request cannot supply. The minted job completes at DISPATCH (it carries the worker session_id for correlation, but the resident worker runs asynchronously and is NOT tracked by the job lifecycle): a `succeeded` job means the run was STARTED, not that the TODO is finished. Poll the TODO itself (GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}): it lands in `review` when the worker is done. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A realm's view holds its own todos and the global ones; a todo it cannot see is 404 not_found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The todo id.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
parameters.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
parameters.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Computer
parameters.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

parameters.name: X-Hoody-Realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

202.description: Dispatched; poll the minted job.

schema.description: The gateway-minted job ack for the dispatch: a `job_id` plus the daemon reply's passthrough fields (the daemon `status` field is stripped).

job_id.description: Gateway-minted job id; poll GET /api/v1/agent/jobs/{id}. The dispatch is accepted immediately and completes to succeeded (the orchestrator/worker progress is observed on the todo worker's own stream, not this job).

session_id.description: The daemon worker session the run was dispatched onto (the job is bound to it for correlation).

run_id.description: The run's id, as the todo's `lease.run_id` shows it; POST /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}/cancel-run takes it as `expected_run`.

x-error-codes.title: Rejected by the daemon's own admin gate
x-error-codes.description: The daemon's own administrator check refused the request. post.description: Runs a tool with NO open session, through the same permission checks as the agent's own tool calls: caller-supplied control keys are ignored, an ephemeral local session is created from the scope headers (X-Hoody-Cwd / X-Hoody-Config-Dir), and the tool runs with every check applied (deny list / high-risk command shapes / read-before-edit / dir-scope / write-permission / tool-membership). Sessionless runs are read-only by default: the first call of a non-read-only tool needs allow_mutations:true (else 400 tool_mutation_refused; a confirm:true without a valid confirm_token is refused the same way). A parked confirmation returns 409 tool_needs_confirmation with details.confirm_token and the echoed tool+params; re-issue the same request with confirm:true, that confirm_token and the params originally sent (the echo may be redacted). A tool-call rule (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules) is checked here too: a `limit` the call breaks answers 200 is_error; a `check_in` it falls under, or a rules check that could not complete, answers 409 tool_needs_confirmation with details.gate_cause "rules" and details.reason naming the rule. FILESYSTEM REACH: a sessionless run resolves paths under the caller-supplied X-Hoody-Cwd subtree (dir-scope defaults to home/restricted-to-cwd). Runs locally only: X-Hoody-Computer is refused 400 realm_scope_unsupported; open a session to run on a computer. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. With no realm named, an agent pinned to one realm runs in that realm, and any other agent uses its base settings (the files realm global uses).

post.summary: Run a tool with a streamed result (sessionless, gated).
post.description: Streaming form of POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{name}/run over Server-Sent Events: a `start` frame, then a `result` / `needs_confirmation` / `error` frame, then `end`. The work is a one-shot gated RPC, so there is no per-token stream: the SSE shape mirrors the kit streaming convention for symmetry with the session stream. A non-read-only sessionless run still needs allow_mutations:true. Runs locally only: X-Hoody-Computer is refused 400 realm_scope_unsupported; open a session to run on a computer. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins). A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. With no realm named, an agent pinned to one realm runs in that realm, and any other agent uses its base settings (the files realm global uses).
