get.description: Returns the HTTP API contract version (api_version), the build version, the session protocol version, the gateway's realm pin (pinned_realm), and the capability list: one row per feature a client may depend on, each with supported (this build knows it) and available (its route/event is mounted here). Answered by the gateway alone (no daemon call); Cache-Control: no-store so a proxy never serves a stale capability list across a deploy. The answer describes the running gateway, so it takes no scope: any scope header (realm, working directory, config directory or computer) returns 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

schema.description: Contract version and capability list.

capabilities.description: GET and PUT /api/v1/agent/acp/default read and set a realm's default delegated agent (claude or empty), and POST /api/v1/agent/sessions takes follow_realm_backend:true to run a new session on it: resolved once when the create is admitted, kept by a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, and refused 409 delegated_agent_unavailable (details.reason) when the agent cannot start. GET /api/v1/agent/acp/agents rows carry setup_user. An agent without this capability ignores follow_realm_backend and starts a Hoody models session, so send it only when this capability is listed.
capabilities.name: acp_default

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/agents rows carry shipped_default true when Hoody ships an agent of that name, whatever file defines it now: it can be reset to the shipped definition, and it cannot be renamed, nor deleted except as a scoped realm's own copy (a shared project-layer copy is not the realm's own) that is not the configured default (is_configured_default).
capabilities.name: agent_shipped_default

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source returns the source's revision; PUT /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source takes expected_revision and refuses a stale one with 409 revision_conflict, writing nothing.
capabilities.name: agent_source_revision

capabilities.description: PATCH /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/tools with `none: true` and an empty tools list writes `tools: none`: the agent publishes no tool and every call is refused. GET /api/v1/agent/agents reports such an agent's tools as an empty array (an absent list is every tool unless strict_tools). The shipped `chat` agent (Just chat) has no tools.
capabilities.name: agent_tools_none

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/version with api_version and this capability list.
capabilities.name: agent_version

capabilities.description: GET/PUT /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/approval (ETag/If-Match), PUT/DELETE .../approval/rules/{tool}, PATCH .../yolo; event.approval_policy_changed carries the revision.
capabilities.name: approval_policy

capabilities.description: An always-policy session hands its approver a lease (acquire/renew/release); decisions must carry it.
capabilities.name: approver_lease

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/attachments + PATCH/DELETE .../attachments/{lease_id}: an HTTP client holds the session open by renewing a lease.
capabilities.name: attachment_lease

capabilities.description: The channel summaries of the Bot view (channels[] on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} and GET /api/v1/agent/bots rows) carry requested_chats, how many chats ask to be approved, and notes, the account's credential-check notes such as telegram_privacy_on; a channel's chats[] (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/channels/{cid}) carry can_read on a Telegram group when it is known whether the bot sees every message there.
capabilities.name: bot_channel_waiting

capabilities.description: DELETE /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}, POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/reset, /forget and /purge, PUT /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/guardrails and PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} take ?expect_uid=<uid>: when the id now names another Bot (the one read was deleted and a new one created under the id) they answer 412 bot_changed and change nothing; a Bot that is gone answers 404, and a request carrying expect_uid never creates chief. PUT /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/guardrails and PATCH /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} also take ?expect_revision=<revision>: the Bot view's revision goes up by one on each of their writes, and a stale one answers 412 revision_mismatch. Without the parameters the routes behave as before.
capabilities.name: bot_expect

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/gate decides the approval or question the Bot itself waits on (pending_gate on GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}): an approval applies to that one call only, and a gate that already ended is answered from the session's record (409 gate_already_resolved with details.request_id when the decision used carried one; a question answered again with the same answer is 200 replayed).
capabilities.name: bot_gate_http

capabilities.description: User rows of spoken messages in the Bot log (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/log, /archive, the row frames of /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream) carry voice: origin, duration_ms, lang and, from a voice connection, conn and utt, the utterance the message was assembled from.
capabilities.name: bot_log_voice

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages takes an Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key and text returns the first message_id and the message's current state, and queues nothing again; the same key with a different text is 422 idempotency_key_reused. A key is remembered while its message is queued and for at least 24 hours after it was accepted; at most 4096 keys are remembered at once, and a new keyed message beyond that is 429 idempotency_keys_exhausted. Without this capability, send messages without a key.
capabilities.name: bot_message_idempotency

capabilities.description: The Bot doors answer a Bot's Bot URL (its public host): only the Bot URL paths are served, the Bot is never created, a Bot recreated under the same id is not the published one, every error carries its code in X-Hoody-Error-Code, and idempotency keys and MCP refs belong to the calling key. Available once this build's public answers are wired; until then every Bot URL request is refused internal_error.
capabilities.name: bot_public_door

capabilities.description: Bot log rows (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/log, /archive, the row frames of /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream) carry kind, a runtime row's typed kind (report, gate, gone, stop, limit, provider, error, …; note for an untagged one), fail_kind, the cause of a failed turn's [provider] or [error] row, and delegate_title, the title of the delegate a row is about. Rows written before them have none: read their leading tag.
capabilities.name: bot_row_kind

capabilities.description: The Bot view (GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}, GET /api/v1/agent/bots rows, the state frames of /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream) carries session_model, the model the Bot's current session runs as that session reported it (absent until it did, and after a reset), and turn_id, the Bot's running turn (present only while turn_running is true).
capabilities.name: bot_session_view

capabilities.description: One agent process on a machine serves each Bot: it holds the Bot's owner lock, taken before any of the Bot's files is read or written. Another agent process sharing the same storage answers every route naming that Bot with 409 bot_owned_elsewhere and Retry-After: 5, lists it in GET /api/v1/agent/bots as a row {id, realm, address, owned_elsewhere: true}, leaves it out of the compat model lists, and takes the Bot over once the lock is free.
capabilities.name: bot_single_writer

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id} carries speech_usage: what the Bot and its realm have used of today's speech limits, with the limits that apply and when they reset. Absent when the usage cannot be read.
capabilities.name: bot_speech_usage

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/cancel {turn_id} stops the Bot's running turn named by the view's turn_id, and only that turn: a turn that already ended, and any later turn, is not touched. The answer's matched says whether the named turn was the Bot's running turn.
capabilities.name: bot_turn_cancel

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check reports whether a Bot's speech settings are ready; GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice takes speak=false (text-only replies) and require=stt,tts (check before the upgrade).
capabilities.name: bot_voice_check

capabilities.description: The text-to-speech stage of GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice/check carries max_input_chars when it is ok: the most characters one speech call takes with the resolved model, for any of its languages and voices.
capabilities.name: bot_voice_check_limits

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice takes play_lead=true: reply audio is then sent at most 8 seconds ahead of what playback.mark says was played, over every output still playing, and a reply whose audio waits 5 seconds with no mark moving on stops speaking with output.stop and reply.final reason no_marks (spoken unknown, or partial when whole segments were heard); its turn goes on. The session frame then carries play_lead true.
capabilities.name: bot_voice_play_lead

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice takes refuse=frame: a refusal the agent makes (a bad option, require not ready, no such Bot, voice busy, the realm or the Bot not served here, voice not available, too many streams) is then an accepted upgrade that sends one refused frame {code, message, details, retry_after_secs} and closes with 4000 plus the HTTP status, so a browser can read why. Nothing is taken over.
capabilities.name: bot_voice_refuse_frame

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice takes output.cancel {reply_id, keep_turn: true}: speech stops and no turn is cancelled (cancel.result turn_continues); reply.final comes at the turn's real end with spoken judged against its whole text: true only when playback.mark confirmed all of it, partial for a confirmed part, unknown when audio went out unconfirmed, false when none did.
capabilities.name: bot_voice_stop_speech

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/voice takes text {text, key}: the typed message is queued under key in the same set of keys as POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages and is answered by one text.result {key, state, message_id, code}: posted or queued, refused (not queued), or unknown (it may still arrive; GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages/by-key/{key} answers 503 while it is being accepted).
capabilities.name: bot_voice_text_key

capabilities.description: A Bot's settings carry worker_backend (llm or acp: what a delegate runs on when the dispatch names none), allowed_worker_backends (what a dispatch may name), worker_delegated_agent (claude) and worker_delegated_model (the Claude model of an acp delegate); the Bot's dispatch takes backend, inside the owner's list; delegate rows carry backend and delegated_agent, fixed when the delegate was opened.
capabilities.name: bot_worker_backend

capabilities.description: A Bot's settings carry the helper options: worker_model and worker_thinking (the model and thinking a Hoody delegate starts on when no routing tier applies, over the agent's own model) and worker_delegated_effort (the Claude Code effort of an acp delegate). Each is fixed for a delegate when it is opened; empty keeps the earlier behaviour.
capabilities.name: bot_worker_options

capabilities.description: The /api/v1/agent/bots routes: a Bot is a long-lived assistant that talks with you and delegates every real task to sessions of its own, then tells you what they did. POST /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/messages talks to it and GET /api/v1/agent/bots/{id}/stream follows its log. Its tool calls park on its own session as event.user_question with category frame_request and kind bot.dispatch, bot.message, bot.stop, bot.delegates, bot.answer_gate or bot.peek; the Bot runtime answers them, never a client.
capabilities.name: bots

capabilities.description: Stop and SubagentStop hooks (PUT /api/v1/agent/hooks `when`) and limit and check_in rules (POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules rules[].when) take a `when` condition over the calls the acting agent made in its current turn; GET /api/v1/agent/hooks, GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies rows carry it. A rules write that names a stored rule with a condition and does not carry `when` is refused 400 bad_request. An agent without this capability ignores `when` on hooks and rules, so send it only when this capability is listed.
capabilities.name: call_when

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/changes and GET /api/v1/agent/changes/stream: one opaque token per topic (sessions, todos, workflow_runs, loops, tasks, gates, agents, rules, memory) for the gateway's realm and owner; a moved token means re-read that topic.
capabilities.name: changes

capabilities.description: Agent frontmatter `compaction_max_tokens: N` (a whole number of at least 8192) starts the agent's automatic compaction, as the chat agent, at N prompt tokens when that is lower than the box's threshold. GET /api/v1/agent/agents reports it per agent and POST /api/v1/agent/agents takes it. The shipped bot agent sets 131072.
capabilities.name: compaction_max_tokens

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/completions and POST /api/v1/agent/completions/stream: one tool-free model call with no session. `settings` (thinking, temperature, max_tokens, response_format) is refused with 400 unsupported_setting when the model cannot honour it; the typed codes are model_unavailable, unsupported_setting, upstream_error and timeout.
capabilities.name: completions

capabilities.description: This gateway reads computer names: `computer` on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions and POST /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name}/runs, `computer_id` where an operation declares it, `allowed_computers` on a Bot and its guardrails, `trust_computer` on a gate decision, the X-Hoody-Computer header and the /computers alias. It refuses the retired container spellings with 400 upgrade_required. A client that names a computer reads this capability and session_protocol_version first: a gateway without it ignores the member and runs the request on its own computer.
capabilities.name: computer_binding

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/session-create-keys/{key} carries started {realm_selector, computer_id, owner_fingerprint} whenever it names a session: the session's frozen binding, to compare with the binding the create asked for before attaching.
capabilities.name: create_key_binding

capabilities.description: Helper transcripts (GET .../tasks/{tid}/transcript) pair each tool_call and tool_result entry by tool_call_id and record the bash command. A tool_result entry carries exit_code (0 included) and complete, and its text is a head/tail preview. event.tool_result carries exit_code too.
capabilities.name: evidence_fields

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions with `frame_tools: true` gives the model the request_view tool: it asks the Frame that started the session to make a View from a request in plain words. The call parks as event.user_question with category frame_request and a frame_request object {kind: view, request, id}; the Frame answers it on POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/answer with its status JSON as the answer, and the tool returns that status to the model (no_frame after 15 minutes without an answer). A live attach asking for it on a session started without it is 400 frame_tools_unavailable.
capabilities.name: frame_tools

capabilities.description: event.confirm_request carries gate_cause, risk, human_only, generation and lease_required; event.gate_resolved carries provenance.
capabilities.name: gate_envelope

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions accepts agent "github-installer": the session installs and starts one program from the GitHub repository its turn names (one line REPO {clone, folder, ref?, path?}) and ends its reply with one RESULT line. It may call only bash, bash_job_wait, read_file, glob_files, grep, write_file, edit_file, ask_question_to_user, hoody_daemon_programs and hoody_daemon_control (any other tool call is answered error_code tool_ceiling and never runs), and its started block carries tool_ceiling "github-installer". Starting, enabling, restarting, stopping or disabling a program the session itself added, after a person approved the add, asks no confirmation while the program's definition is unchanged; every other program change asks as usual.
capabilities.name: github_installer

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions with `helper_gates: true` parks a spawn_agent helper's approvals and questions as gates on the session (event.confirm_request / event.user_question carrying helper_id), each bounded by the agent's `ask_timeout`; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state lists pending_helper_gates.
capabilities.name: helper_gates

capabilities.description: Every event a spawn_agent helper forwards carries helper_id and parent_tool_call_id (the tool_use id of the spawn_agent call that started it). task_started/task_activity/task_done and TaskInfo carry them too, and TaskInfo and tasks_snapshot carry rev so that stale snapshots can be ordered and dropped.
capabilities.name: helper_ids

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules sets the tool-call rules: sentences Jev checks before a covered tool call, a limit denying and a check_in asking. A check that cannot complete never lets the call through.
capabilities.name: hook_rules

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules reads the tool-call rules of the realm's settings scopes with no session, with the same scopes revisions POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules checks; the `rules` token of GET /api/v1/agent/changes moves on those files with or without a live session.
capabilities.name: hook_rules_read

capabilities.description: Jev decisions: GET/PUT /api/v1/agent/jev/settings, GET /api/v1/agent/jev/models, POST /api/v1/agent/jev/test, POST /api/v1/agent/jev/decide and the session-bound POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/jev/decide (typed jev_* errors, usage with cost_usd null when unknown and known_cost_usd); usage is reported in each reply and totalled by GET /api/v1/agent/jev/settings, and a session-bound call also emits event.jev_usage on the session stream.
capabilities.name: jev

capabilities.description: GET and PUT /api/v1/agent/jev/settings take a realm (X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm=) and act on that realm's settings, which the realm's sessions decide with; the reply carries effective {enabled, model, source, key_ready, usable}, true only when a decision would run now. Without this capability the settings are the Global realm's and the reply has no effective.
capabilities.name: jev_realm_settings

capabilities.description: PATCH /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/loops/{loopId} takes if_state, if_max_cost_usd and if_max_wall_ms with any intent: each one sent must equal the loop's state or limit at the moment of the change, checked together with it, or nothing changes and the answer is 409 loop_changed with the loop's state and limits now in details. if_state stopped with max_cost_usd and max_wall_ms starts a stopped loop again only while it is still stopped. An agent without this capability ignores the fields, so send them only when it is listed.
capabilities.name: loop_preconditions

capabilities.description: Agent frontmatter `mcp_tools` lists the MCP tools the agent gets (`server/tool`, `server/*` or `mcp__server__tool`): present means exactly those, an empty list means none.
capabilities.name: mcp_tools

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/models, GET /api/v1/agent/models/{spec} and GET /api/v1/agent/providers/{id} give each provider model efforts (the thinking levels a session on it can be sent; an empty list means none) input_modalities when known, and tool_call (whether it calls tools; omitted when unknown); its prices are the rates the agent prices usage at, and cost_reported_by_provider marks a provider that reports each reply's cost itself. Without this capability prices are catalogue list prices and none of these fields is sent.
capabilities.name: model_picker_fields

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions takes `model_settings` (the completion route's settings object) for every turn of the session, and agent frontmatter takes thinking, temperature and response_format; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} reports the stored model_settings.
capabilities.name: model_settings

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions with `outcome_claims: true` gives the model the report_outcome tool: it calls it last to say what it did and cite the tool calls that show it, and the turn closes with event.outcome_claims (each cited call linked, foreign, ambiguous or unknown, and for a linked call what the agent recorded about it). GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/transcript carries each report as an outcome_claims block after its call's tool_result. The agent does not judge a claim. A live attach asking for it on a session started without it is 400 outcome_claims_unavailable.
capabilities.name: outcome_claims

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/gates lists every gate waiting for a human across the visible sessions this gateway holds live (each session's own confirm or question and each helper's), oldest first, each with the gate_id /confirm and /answer take and the gate as GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state shows it.
capabilities.name: pending_gates

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions and agent frontmatter take `prompt_blocks`, an object of block name to boolean: false drops that optional system-prompt block. Switches only turn blocks off.
capabilities.name: prompt_blocks

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules takes the rule kinds guidance and playbook: never checked by Jev, they are added to the system prompt of every session and helper they cover, within a byte budget. Every rule reports applies_as (checked | prompt); GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies lists both and names the prompt rules over the budget. prompt_blocks team_rules drops the block.
capabilities.name: prompt_rules

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/oauth and POST /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/accounts take method:"device_code" (a code entered on the provider's page) and an Idempotency-Key; one sign-in per provider may be pending (409 oauth_in_progress with details.job_id), and DELETE /api/v1/agent/providers/{id}/auth/oauth/{job} cancels it, answering cancelled when nothing was saved or complete when the sign-in had already been saved.
capabilities.name: provider_oauth_device

capabilities.description: Conditional writes work on a gateway without a realm pin: the workflow revisions of GET and PUT /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name} and PUT /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name}/summary are bound to the realm the request resolves to, and the rules and agent source revisions name their realm, so a revision read in another realm is refused with revision_conflict and never written there (409 on PUT /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name}/summary, POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules and PUT /api/v1/agent/agents/{name}/source; 200 with is_error and code on PUT /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name}). pinned_realm says whether this gateway is pinned.
capabilities.name: realm_bound_revision

capabilities.description: Every route declares the daemon actions it may dispatch; an undeclared dispatch is refused (500 internal_error, details.reason undeclared_action).
capabilities.name: route_actions

capabilities.description: A tool-call rule takes `agents`: it then covers only calls made by those agents (the session's own agent, a helper's, a workflow agent step's). GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/rules/applies answers which rules the check sends to Jev for an agent's call, from the same selection.
capabilities.name: rule_agents

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/hooks reports each scope file's rules revision (rules.scopes); POST /api/v1/agent/hooks/rules takes expected_revision and refuses a stale one with 409 revision_conflict, writing nothing.
capabilities.name: rules_revision

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/script-instances lists a computer's managed scripts; a row of another realm is only {path, state: managed_elsewhere}.
capabilities.name: script_instances

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/script-instances/delete deletes a managed script through the computer's guarded delete (if_revision, op_id). Available only once the agent has confirmed that the program it reaches computers through has the guarded delete; until then, or when it does not, available is false.
capabilities.name: script_instances_guarded

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/script-templates and GET /api/v1/agent/script-templates/{name} read the realm's script templates; POST /api/v1/agent/script-templates/{name}/instantiate makes a script from a kit template, create-only, with an optional caller key and a required Idempotency-Key.
capabilities.name: script_templates

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions accepts agent "script-writer": the session may call only the script check, route and monitor tools (any other tool call is answered error_code tool_ceiling and never runs), and its started block carries tool_ceiling "script-writer". A session without started.tool_ceiling has no ceiling.
capabilities.name: script_writer

capabilities.description: The daemon refuses unregistered session commands with event.command_refused (session protocol version 3) instead of dropping them.
capabilities.name: session_command_registry

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions:events?ids=… streams up to 32 live sessions over one SSE stream; every frame carries session_id, and each session keeps its own seq, incarnation, replay, gap and drop (session_lagged, session_end), resumed with since=<id>:<seq>,…; end comes once, when no session is left
capabilities.name: session_events_mux

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/transcript and event.replay carry an image block {kind: image, image_id, media_type, bytes} for each image a person attached to a message, and GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/images/{image_id} returns its bytes.
capabilities.name: session_images

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions rows (and the GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id} summary) carry state (idle, running, parked, closed), pending_gate (an approval or question waits for a person, the session's own or a helper's) and origin; GET /api/v1/agent/sessions takes order=started|last_active.
capabilities.name: session_row_state

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/state: ONE snapshot to rebuild from: the daemon's state object (turn, parked gate, policy) as of its read, the gateway's stream watermark read BEFORE it (so nothing between the two is lost), and the gateway gate ref validated against the daemon's parked gate.
capabilities.name: session_state

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/settings/spend-caps reads the spend caps chats are held to (per chat, per turn, stop or warn), with a revision and whether the caps file is valid; PUT /api/v1/agent/settings/spend-caps replaces them when the revision still matches.
capabilities.name: spend_caps

capabilities.description: Agent frontmatter `strict_tools: true` makes `tools:` the exact tool set (a missing or empty list means only the benign specials, never all tools). GET /api/v1/agent/agents reports strict_tools per agent, and POST /api/v1/agent/agents takes it as a JSON boolean.
capabilities.name: strict_tools

capabilities.description: GET /api/v1/agent/todos rows carry pending_proposals, how many of the todo's proposals wait for a person (pending and not past expires_at); omitted when zero. The proposals themselves stay on GET /api/v1/agent/todos/{id}.
capabilities.name: todo_pending_proposals

capabilities.description: event.tool_result carries truncated (and original_bytes when the size is known) when bash, bash_job_wait, read_file, read_minified_file, grep, glob_files, web_fetch, load_hoody_skill, an MCP tool or tool_orchestrator cut its output. truncated is positive evidence only: a missing flag is inconclusive, because other tools never set it. A helper transcript's tool_result entry is not complete when the tool cut its output.
capabilities.name: tool_output_completeness

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns with Idempotency-Key admits a turn exactly once: the durable receipt is the 202 body, and GET .../turns/{turn_id} (or the list at GET .../turns) re-reads it. The daemon's event.turn_receipt answers the dispatching request only: it is never on the stream.
capabilities.name: turn_idempotency

capabilities.description: event.tool_result.error_code and event.agent_done.outcome/error_code are stable machine codes.
capabilities.name: typed_outcomes

api_version.description: HTTP API contract version (semver); moves when the wire contract changes.

build_version.description: Build version of the running agent.

session_protocol_version.description: Session-connection command contract version (2 = unregistered commands are refused with event.command_refused).

pinned_realm.description: The realm this gateway is pinned to (--http-realm / HOODY_HTTP_REALM): every request resolves to it. null when the gateway is not pinned and resolves the agent's active realm per request; conditional writes then use realm-bound revisions (capability realm_bound_revision).

available.description: Its route/event is mounted on this deployment.

capabilities.description: One row per capability.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Bad request
x-error-codes.description: The request was malformed or carried invalid parameters.
x-error-codes.resolution: Correct the request body or query parameters.

x-error-codes.title: Realm scope unsupported
x-error-codes.description: A per-request scope header this route does not take: a realm or computer header on a route without that dimension, or, on an agent pinned to one realm, a different realm.
x-error-codes.resolution: Omit the header. A route without a realm dimension refuses every realm header, the pinned realm included; on a route that takes a realm, an agent pinned to one realm accepts only that realm.

example.message: realm scope not supported on this route

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Forbidden (Source IP Guard)
x-error-codes.description: Refused by the Source IP Guard: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only.
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the agent through its URL, for example with `hoody agent …`.

example.message: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Not found
x-error-codes.description: The requested resource does not exist.
x-error-codes.resolution: Verify the path and identifier.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

details.description: Optional structured detail payload (present only for codes that carry it, e.g. gate_parked → details.pending_gate).

x-error-codes.title: Too many requests
x-error-codes.description: The per-client request rate limit was exceeded; the gateway throttled the request before dispatch.
x-error-codes.resolution: Honor the Retry-After header and retry; reduce the request rate.

schema.description: Structured error envelope {code, message, details?} returned by every JSON error response (see x-error-codes for the per-code code/message/details examples).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (the x-error-codes key).

get.summary: Snapshot in-flight and recent workflow runs.
get.description: Returns a snapshot of in-flight + recently-finished workflow runs. Running runs are always kept; finished runs are kept up to the newest 50 for the whole computer, all realms together, and an older finished run is dropped: GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs/{run_id} answers 404 not_found for it and it can no longer be resumed. Poll this to track a run's progress; live events also flow on the owning session's stream. Realm: ?realm= (or the X-Hoody-Realm header) lists one realm: "global" (runs not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id; ?realm=all lists every realm this login serves (query only, never the header). Omitted, the agent's current realm. Every row carries its realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm lists only that realm: any other value, all included, is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

schema.description: Kit list envelope: a page of items plus pagination metadata.

items.description: The page of runs in the registry's insertion order (runs read from the run history first, then runs started since, oldest first); each element is the daemon's run info with the properties below, keyed by run_id.

run_id.description: Run id; GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs/{run_id} and POST /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs/{run_id}/cancel take it. The daemon mints a lowercase UUID; a run from the history file is listed with the id it holds.

session_id.description: The session that started the run.

cwd.description: The run's working directory. Omitted when empty.

started_at.description: When the run started (RFC3339, nanosecond resolution).

finished_at.description: When the run finished (RFC3339). Omitted while running.

current_step.description: The step the run is on, or was last on. Omitted when none has started.

status.description: Run status. A run from the history file with any other status is listed as failed.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens used. Omitted when zero.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens used. Omitted when zero.

cost.description: Spend in US dollars. Omitted when zero.

error.description: A failed run's sanitized error preview. Omitted otherwise.

last_step.description: The last step recorded before the run ended; with parallel steps it is not necessarily the one that failed. Omitted when none.

realm_id.description: The realm the run started in: "global" or a 24-hex id. Omitted on an older run that recorded no realm; such a run belongs to the global realm.

owner_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the owning account; the list hides runs another account owns. Omitted when unstamped.

resumed_from.description: The run this one resumed. Omitted for an ordinary run.

computer_binding.description: The computer the owning session was bound to when the run started. Omitted for a local run.

container_binding.description: Deprecated, read-only. Set only on a run started before the computer rename with a remote computer bound: such a run cannot be resumed or replayed. New runs carry computer_binding.

realm.description: The run's realm: "global" for one not tied to a realm, else its 24-hex realm id. Pass it as X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) to reach it by id.

post.summary: Resume a failed or cancelled workflow run.
post.description: Resumes a terminal (failed/cancelled) run in a live session: committed steps replay from the run's recorded journal and execution continues live from the first incomplete step. Body: {"session_id"}. The resuming session must match the run's realm, owner, working directory, and computer binding, and must be idle (no turn running and no confirmation or question waiting: 409 session_busy). A run is resumable once: a run whose resume is running or has completed is refused. After a failed or cancelled resume, only the newest run of the lineage that started a step can be resumed: a resume of an older one, or of a resume that ran no step while the run it resumed did, is 409 resume_superseded naming that run in details.resume_run_id; a resume that ended before its first step leaves the run it resumed resumable. When that cannot be read, 503 resume_lineage_unknown (retry). A finished run beyond the newest 50 kept (GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs) is no longer retained and cannot be resumed: 404 not_found. Refusals return an actionable message. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm (or ?realm=) selects the realm: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. Omitted, the agent's current realm. A realm this login does not serve is 404 not_found. An agent pinned to one realm acts only in that realm: any other value is 400 realm_scope_unsupported. The run and the session must both be in that realm; a run or session in another realm is 404 not_found. A computer header is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

post.description: Opens a new session and dispatches the named workflow onto it in one call, returning 202 {job_id, session_id, run_id, turn_id}. Equivalent to POST /api/v1/agent/sessions followed by POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/workflows/{name}/runs: the run's events flow on that session's stream, a gate it parks is answered through that session, and job.run_id is null until the workflow loop registers the run. The name is checked against the new session's own realm and project: an unknown name is a 404 and the session is closed without being recorded. The check is best-effort: if the workflow list cannot be read the run is dispatched anyway and an unknown name fails on the session stream. An Idempotency-Key header is refused (400): workflow runs are not deduplicated, so before retrying a run whose response was lost, check GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/runs for it. The session is an ordinary session: it stays listed, and the gateway releases it once it is idle with no attached client, and a parked gate counts as idle, so a run that parks a gate while nobody is attached is cancelled after the idle timeout (5 minutes). Attach to the session's stream to answer its gates, or start it with headless:true to have them decided without a human. If the request ends after the run was sent but before the daemon confirmed it, the session is closed (cancelling the run) since its ids were never returned. The POST /api/v1/agent/sessions fields attach, fork, fork_turn_idx, backend, delegated_agent, approval and expected_binding are refused (400), never ignored: create the session first and use POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/workflows/{name}/runs.

Only that field is written, atomically, so a concurrent edit to the steps is never overwritten. Setting the summary of a shipped system workflow the realm has no copy of yet saves a copy of it first. A workflow supplied by the project (listed with project:true) is refused (400): its steps run without confirmation, so it cannot be copied into your own workflows by an edit: copy it explicitly first. An unknown name is a 404 not_found. A failure to read or write the workflow file is a 500 store_failed. Pass expected_revision (the revision from GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name}?include_revision=true) to refuse the write if the workflow changed since that read: the refusal is 409 revision_conflict with details.current_revision. The revision is bound to the realm this request resolves to: on a gateway without a realm pin, a revision read while another realm was active is refused 409 revision_conflict (details.current_revision is this realm's), never written into the other realm. A 409 revision_conflict can also come back WITHOUT expected_revision when the realm's profile was swapped underneath the write: re-read and retry. A workflow that does not exist is 404 not_found "workflow not found", and so is a realm this login does not serve. Realm: X-Hoody-Realm or ?realm= names the realm ("global" or a 24-hex realm id; the header wins); omitted, the agent's own realm. A malformed realm is 400 invalid_realm, a realm this login does not serve 404 not_found, and on an agent pinned to one realm any other realm is 400 realm_scope_unsupported.

expected_revision.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard: the 'revision:' value from GET /api/v1/agent/workflows/{name} (?include_revision=true). If the workflow changed or was deleted since that read, the write is refused 409 revision_conflict and nothing is written. Omit to write unconditionally. get.description: Get progress of currently running downloads into the directory requested. Lists only the jobs whose every path (directory and file, or archive and destination) the caller may read. A rule that lets the caller only list a folder does not count: an account limited to `/alice:rw` may list the root but not read it, so it sees only the jobs whose paths all lie under `/alice`. Unless the caller has read-write on `/`, each URL (`url`, and any URL in a past download's `error_message`) has its user, password, query and fragment removed: a presigned or `user:pass@` URL is a credential of whoever started the download.

message.description: What failed. A schema failure reads "Validation failed: " followed by the path and the reason of each failing check. A JSON body that cannot be parsed reads "Invalid JSON in request body".

data.description: The failing checks, when there are any. A schema failure sends an array with one entry per failing check, each with `instancePath` (the JSON pointer of the field, for example `/name`), `schemaPath`, `keyword`, `params` and `message`. A check made by the operation itself may send other details. A JSON body that cannot be parsed sends none.

instanceGeneration.description: Identity of the browser PROCESS behind this address, regenerated on every start/restart. Pass it back as `instanceGeneration` on /browse, /snapshot, /action and /wait to get `409 INSTANCE_CHANGED` instead of silently acting on a replacement instance. The server has always returned it; it was missing from this schema, so typed SDK callers could not read the value those operations tell them to send.

engine.description: Automation engine the instance actually loaded: `playwright` when stealth was requested but Patchright could not be loaded

stealth.description: Whether the instance was launched in stealth mode using Patchright (Chromium only)

headless.description: Whether the browser was launched headless

chromiumBuildId.description:
Puppeteer-style Chrome build identifier that was downloaded/used for this instance.
Usually a full Chrome version string (e.g. `136.0.7103.113`).

chromiumExecutablePath.description: Absolute path to the Chromium executable used for this instance.

browserExecutablePath.description: Absolute path to the browser executable used for this instance.

fingerprintId.description: Base fingerprint profile id used to seed launch/context defaults

display.description: Display identifier

iframe_url.description: URL for the display iframe, if configured

timezoneId.description: The IANA timezone the browser runs in: the applied `timezoneId` (request option, `userProfile`, or fingerprint profile, in that order of precedence) or, when none was applied, the timezone the browser itself reports (the host's). `null` only when neither is known.

locale.description: The locale the browser runs in: the applied `locale` (request option, `userProfile`, or fingerprint profile, in that order of precedence) or, when none was applied, the browser's own `navigator.language`. `null` only when neither is known.

viewportSource.description: Where the current viewport policy came from: "creation" until the first successful POST /viewport, then "runtime".

operatingSystemName.description: Operating system name of the host the browser runs on (for example `Linux`), whatever the user agent says

webSocketDebuggerUrl.description:
Chrome DevTools WebSocket debugger URL for remote debugging.

**How to use this URL**:
- **Chrome DevTools**: Open `chrome://inspect`, click "Configure", add this URL as a network target
- **Puppeteer**: `await puppeteer.connect({ browserWSEndpoint: url })`
- **Playwright**: `await playwright.chromium.connectOverCDP(url)`

**Availability**: Only populated when browser is launched with `useRemoteDebuggingPort: true`.
In Hoody computer deployments this URL is rewritten onto the `cdp-{N}` proxy hostname
(paired 1:1 with the `browser-{N}` instance it debugs). The raw WebSocket URL is not
promised stable across browser restarts: prefer connecting with
`chromium.connectOverCDP("https://{projectId}-{computerId}-cdp-{N}.{server}.computers.hoody.com/")`, which resolves the live WebSocket URL via
`/json/version` and cold-starts instance `N` on demand if it isn't already running.

**Security Warning**: This URL provides full control over the browser instance.
Only expose to trusted clients in secure environments.

devtoolsHttpUrl.description:
Chrome DevTools HTTP discovery URL (`/json/version`) for this instance.
Tools can resolve the WebSocket URL from this endpoint.
In Hoody computer deployments this URL is rewritten onto the `cdp-{N}` proxy hostname
pattern (paired 1:1 with the `browser-{N}` instance), the same on-demand relay used by
`connectOverCDP("https://{projectId}-{computerId}-cdp-{N}.{server}.computers.hoody.com/")`.

devtoolsFrontendUrl.description:
Public URL to access Chrome DevTools frontend in a browser.
Uses the `cdp-{N}` subdomain pattern routed by the Hoody reverse proxy, paired 1:1 with the
`browser-{N}` instance; on-demand: hitting this URL cold-starts instance `N` if it is not
already running.
Open this URL to get a live DevTools inspector for the running browser.

extensions.description: List of loaded Chrome extension directory paths (if any)

useRemoteDebuggingPort.description: Whether the instance was launched with a DevTools remote debugging port

remoteDebuggingAddress.description: Interface address the DevTools port is bound to, or null when the instance was started with `useRemoteDebuggingPort` false. Connect through the URLs `/devtools-url` returns.

quicDisabled.description: Whether QUIC transport is disabled for this instance. Defaults to `true` to enforce TCP-only transport.

http3Disabled.description: Whether HTTP/3 is disabled for this instance. This follows QUIC policy and defaults to `true`.

dnsOverHttpsEnabled.description: Whether DNS-over-HTTPS is enabled for this instance. Defaults to `true`.

dnsOverHttpsUrl.description: DoH resolver endpoint used by the browser when DoH is enabled. Defaults to Cloudflare.

tabs.description: List of currently open tabs in the browser instance

url.description: Current URL loaded in the tab

isActive.description: Whether the tab is the active one

browser_InstanceViewport.description: The viewport the instance reports: the size the page is emulated at (`width`, `height`), or `null` when the page follows the real browser window (`viewport=null` / `noViewport=true`). `deviceScaleFactor`, `screenWidth` and `screenHeight` are accepted when you pass `viewport` but are not reported back.

browser_ViewportStatus.description: Live viewport policy of a browser instance.

viewport.description: The runtime policy: {width,height} or null (responsive: the page follows the real window).

source.description: "creation" until the first successful POST /viewport, then "runtime".

tabs.description: Number of live tabs at the time of the read (crashed tabs are not counted).

converged.description: Whether every live page currently reflects the policy (crashed tabs are skipped).

url.description: Current tab URL

isActive.description: Whether the tab is currently active

crashed.description: Present, and `true`, only when the tab's renderer crashed. Such a tab answers `502 PAGE_CRASHED` on every tab route and is skipped by `POST /viewport`; close it with `/tab/close`.

url.description: The page's URL when it was read, with secrets in it redacted

title.description: The document's `<title>` on one line, URLs in it redacted, at most 1024 characters (may be empty)

httpStatus.description: HTTP status of the main document when this call navigated (`url`); null otherwise. A website 404 is data, not an API error.

fetchedAt.description: When the HTML was read (ISO 8601, UTC)

markdown.description: The Markdown, with the frontmatter block on top when `frontmatter=true`; empty when the page has no content

truncated.description: Whether the Markdown body was cut at `maxChars`

metadata.description: Page metadata as Defuddle extracts it (meta tags, schema.org data). Strings have URLs in them redacted, are at most 1024 characters, and are null when the page states nothing.

links.description: Only with `includeLinks=true`: the page's `http`/`https` links, published like the Markdown's links, sorted, deduplicated, at most 10 000

linksTruncated.description: Only with `includeLinks=true`: whether more than 10 000 links were found

tabId.description: The ID of the tab used

url.description: The final URL after navigation

created.description: Whether a new tab was created

reused.description: Whether an existing tab was reused

requestedUrl.description: The URL that was requested (before redirects)

title.description: Document title after navigation (may be empty, e.g. with waitUntil=commit)

httpStatus.description: HTTP status of the main document response; null for about:blank or same-document navigations. A website 404 is data, not an API error.

instanceGeneration.description: Generation of the instance that served the navigation (see /metadata).

browser_HealthCheck.title: HealthCheck
browser_HealthCheck.description: Standardized health response (9-field contract shared across all kit services).

status.description: Literal 'ok' when the service is healthy.

built.description: When this build was made (ISO 8601); null when unknown.

started.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the process started.

fds.description: Number of open file descriptors (null on non-Linux).

pid.description: Process id.

total.description: Running instances; `total` and `active` are the same count.

active.description: Running instances; `total` and `active` are the same count.

byAge.description: Running instances by age. The `lessThan*` buckets are cumulative: each counts every running instance younger than its threshold, so `lessThan5Min` includes `lessThan1Min`. `moreThan15Min` counts the rest.

oldestInstance.description: Age of oldest instance in milliseconds

newestInstance.description: Age of newest instance in milliseconds

tabs.description: Open tabs across all instances, as each instance last reported them (at most about 5 seconds old)

maxTabsPerInstance.description: The most tabs any one instance has open, reported the same way

code.description: Error code

details.description: Additional error details

browser_Target.description: Element target for /action and /wait. Exactly ONE of ref, selector, role, label, text, placeholder, testId must be set (400 otherwise). `name` only with role; `snapshotId` required with ref; `exact` only with role/label/text/placeholder (default true). Every target is strict: more than one match → 409 AMBIGUOUS_TARGET. Semantic and CSS targets address the top document only; use a ref to act inside an iframe. Refs are opaque tokens: a prefix like `f2` is Playwright's frame-sequence namespace and says nothing about iframes. Pass refs back verbatim.

ref.description: Element reference from the latest /snapshot of this tab (e.g. "e12"). Requires snapshotId.

snapshotId.description: The snapshotId the ref came from. Must be the tab's latest and no main-frame navigation may have happened since (409 STALE_SNAPSHOT otherwise).

selector.description: A single CSS selector (forced through Playwright's css engine; ">>" chaining and other engines are rejected with 400).

role.description: ARIA role (Playwright's closed role list; unknown → 400). Combine with name.

label.description: Form control by its label text.

text.description: Element by its text content.

exact.description: Exact (true) or substring, case-insensitive (false) matching for role/label/text/placeholder.

browser_DialogPolicy.description: Authorizes handling of ONE dialog raised during this action; it never requires one (no dialog → `dialog: null`). A dialog that does not match, or a second dialog, is dismissed and the action fails with 409 UNEXPECTED_DIALOG (details.outcome says whether the mutation had completed).

promptText.description: Text to enter when accepting a prompt. Never echoed back.

message.description: If set, the dialog's message must equal this exactly to be handled.

browser_WaitCondition.description: Discriminated by `kind`. target: {target, state}; text: {target, text, match?}; url: exactly one of {url} (absolute, compared as normalized href) or {urlPrefix} (verbatim startsWith on href); loadState: {state}. A miss is 504 TIMEOUT (phase wait), never matched:false.

state.description: target: attached|detached|visible|hidden|enabled|disabled (detached/hidden are satisfied by absence). loadState: domcontentloaded|load.

text.description: text kind: text to find in the target's innerText (whitespace-normalized, case-sensitive). innerText does not read an input's value.

url.description: url kind: absolute URL; matched exactly against the normalized current href (no wildcards).

urlPrefix.description: url kind: verbatim prefix of the current href.

browser_AutomationError.description: Error envelope of the automation routes. Messages are server-authored (never raw engine text). Codes: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR | INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT; 404 TAB_NOT_FOUND | ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND | NOT_FOUND; 409 INSTANCE_CHANGED | STALE_SNAPSHOT | TAB_BUSY | AMBIGUOUS_TARGET | UNEXPECTED_DIALOG; 422 INVALID_ACTION_TARGET | ELEMENT_NOT_VISIBLE (/screenshot); 502 BROWSER_DISCONNECTED | PAGE_CRASHED | NAVIGATION_ERROR (from the instance) | UPSTREAM_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE | PROXY_ERROR (from the server); 504 TIMEOUT; 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.

instanceGeneration.description: Present on errors answered by the instance; absent on those answered by the server (phase "proxy", or 409 with details.expected null).

details.description: Code-specific. TIMEOUT: {phase, outcome}. STALE_SNAPSHOT: {reason: superseded|navigated|frame-gone|unknown, current: the tab's current snapshot id (`<generation>:<counter>`, for example `gen_4a1c9f2b7d3e5081:4`), or null when the tab has none; on /action also outcome when a navigation landed during the action: `not-started` means nothing reached the page and a retry is safe, `unknown` means the input was dispatched and the action may have taken effect, so read the page (/snapshot) before retrying}. TAB_BUSY: {tabId, op, sinceMs}. AMBIGUOUS_TARGET: {count, candidates}: `candidates` describes up to 5 of the matching elements as {tag, role, id, name}, with `role` and `id` null when the element has none; these are not snapshot refs. Both are best effort: `count` can be missing and fewer candidates can be listed (a candidate's name never includes text typed into editable elements inside it). UNEXPECTED_DIALOG: {dialog:{type,message}, outcome}. INSTANCE_CHANGED: {expected}: the current instanceGeneration of the instance at this address, or null when none runs there.

outcome.description: Whether the final mutating call was invoked: not-started = it was not (safe to retry); unknown = invoked, did not resolve; completed = resolved.

url.description: Final URL after navigation (cut to 8192 characters)

requestedUrl.description: Original URL passed to /browse (cut to 8192 characters)

httpStatus.description: HTTP status code, null for manual navigations

source.description: Navigation source: api = /browse endpoint, page = a navigation the page or browser made (link click, redirect, SPA route, the first page of a tab the page or a CDP client opened)

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp

created.description: Whether a new tab was created

reused.description: Whether an existing tab was reused

state.description:
Always `stopped`. The process has exited, or was killed after a
grace period, and the instance's port is free again.

code_InstanceError.description:
The error shape of `DELETE /api/v1/code`. Branch on `error`; the
message is written for a person and may be reworded.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code. The set is closed and every value is
listed here.

code_ExtensionError.description:
The error shape used by the extensions operations. It differs from
`Error` by carrying a stable `error` code, which is the field to branch
on: the message is written for a person and may be reworded.

Some codes add fields of their own. A `downgrade-refused` names
`logicalKey`, `stagedVersion`, `offeredVersion` and `retryWith`; a
rejected archive names `reason`. Nothing in an error names an address
or a path.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code. This is the field to branch on; the
message is written for a person and may be reworded.

The set is closed and every value is listed here. A code not in
this list did not come from these operations.

code_ExtensionIdentity.description:
Who an extension is, read from the archive's own manifest rather than
from its filename.

logicalKey.description:
Publisher and name, lowercased. The target platform is reported
separately and is not part of it: the editor installs every staged
file it finds, so one extension id is one staged file and a
platform-specific build replaces a universal one.

targetPlatform.description: Platform-specific builds only; null for a universal VSIX.

sha256.description:
Content hash of the archive. Two stages of the same bytes are one
artifact, and are what `unchanged` means.

instanceId.description:
The instance named by the request. It echoes the selector and does
not scope the stage: with `stageScope` reporting
`shared-across-instances`, what was written serves every instance,
including instances that do not exist yet. Read `stageScope`, not
this field, to know who is affected.

outcome.description:
`staged` is new, `replaced` superseded an existing version, and
`unchanged` means these exact bytes were already staged. The same
version with different bytes is a replacement, not a repeat.

requiresRestartToApply.description:
Always true. The editor installs staged extensions only while
starting, so this is reported as data rather than left to prose.

replaced.description: The version this stage superseded, or null if it superseded nothing.

comparison.description:
How the staged version compares with the one it replaced.
`incomparable` means the two versions could not be ordered.

removedDuplicates.description:
Other staged builds of this same extension that this install
removed, and what each of them would have offered.

One version of an extension is staged at a time, identified by
publisher and name. The target platform is NOT part of that
identity, because the editor installs every file it finds in the
stage directory and two files carrying one extension id is an
ambiguity it has no way to resolve. So staging a platform-specific
build over a universal one, or the reverse, removes the loser and
names it here.

Normally empty. It is always present, so a client never has to tell
"nothing was removed" from "an older server that did not say".

targetPlatform.description: What that build declared, which is what made it a separate file.

version.description: The version an instance would have been offered and now will not be.

stageScope.description:
Whether the stage directory serves every instance or only this one.
This deployment stages shared, so an extension staged through one
instance is installed by all of them.

message.description: Restates that this was a stage and not an install.

code_StagedExtensionEntry.description:
One file in the stage directory. The fields describing identity are
nullable because a file that could not be read still has to be
reportable: leaving it out would make an unreadable file look like an
absent one.

fileName.description:
Name of the file in the staging directory. A package staged
through this service is named after its logical key followed by
`.vsix`, without the version; `canonicalName` says whether this
file has that name.

reason.description: Why, for anything other than `ok`.

scannable.description:
Whether the editor's startup scan will pick this file up. A file
dropped into the directory by hand can be scannable without having
been staged through this API.

canonicalName.description: Whether the filename is the canonical name for the identity inside it.

status.description:
What the instance appears to have, relative to what is staged.

`running` is the staged version, installed and live. `stale` is
anything else on a running instance that is not yet a failure: no
version installed, an older one, a newer one, or an instance that
started too recently to have finished installing. It is the normal
state between a stage and the next start. `failed` is a running
instance that started AFTER the stage, had time to install it, and
does not have it. `stopped` is reported whatever is installed,
because nothing is live to be stale against. `unavailable` means
the instance's state could not be determined, so no judgement is
offered.

installedOnly.description:
Installed with nothing staging it. Usually the consequence of
removal being out of scope: unstaging never uninstalls.

desired.description:
What has been staged for installation. When `status` is
`unavailable` the `extensions` key is ABSENT rather than empty, so
a client that walks the array gets nothing instead of rendering
"no extensions" for a directory nobody could read.

reason.description: Present only when `status` is `unavailable`.

observed.description:
What this instance appears to have installed. Follows the same
absent-rather-than-empty rule as `desired`. Unlike `desired`, an
`unavailable` here is often not a fault: an instance with no
extensions directory has nothing to observe, and the answer to
"what is staged" is still complete.

scope.description: Always `instance`. What is observed belongs to one instance.

reason.description: Present only when `status` is `unavailable`.

partial.description:
True when either section is `unavailable`, so the answer is not a
complete picture. One field to branch on without inspecting both.

message.description: Restates what the two sections are and why they disagree.

version.description: Version of the running orchestrator build, or null if undeterminable.

path.description: Absolute path of the packaged editor tree these figures came from.

version.description: Wrapper version from the packaged tree. `0.0.0` in normal builds.

commit.description: Build commit stamped into the packaged wrapper, the meaningful identifier.

status.description:
Why the figures above are null, when they are. `missing` (no such
tree) and `unreadable` (a tree that could not be read) are
different operational problems and are not collapsed together.

start_url.description: Absolute path on this origin. Never relative.

sizes.description: Present only when the icon is an SVG image, as `any`.

type.description:
The image MIME type `/favicon.ico` serves, lowercased and without
parameters: `image/png` for the built-in icon, and `image/png`
when the icon answers with `image/png; charset=binary`. Omitted
when the type is not a valid `image/` type.

curl_AsyncJobAccepted.description: Body of the 202 answer to a `mode=async` request.

job_id.description: ID of the created job; read it with `GET /api/v1/curl/jobs/{id}`.

curl_CreateScheduleRequest.description: Request to create a scheduled job

cron.description:
Cron expression with six fields, `second minute hour day month weekday`,
and an optional seventh `year` field.

enabled.description:
`false` creates the schedule disabled: it never fires until it is
enabled, and its expression need not have a future occurrence yet.
Defaults to `true`.

schedule_id.description: Id of the new or already existing schedule; pass it to `GET /api/v1/curl/schedule/{id}`.

code.description: Machine-readable code; the operation's x-error-codes lists the ones it can return

curl_CurlHealthMemory.description: Memory use reported by the health check.

curl_CurlHealthResponse.description: Body of `GET /api/v1/curl/health`. All nine fields are always present.

built.description: Modification time of the running binary (RFC 3339, UTC), or `null` when it cannot be read.

fds.description: Number of open file descriptors, or `null` when they cannot be counted.

ip.description: The caller's IP address as the service saw it, or `unknown`.

oneOf.description: Memory use, or `null` when it cannot be read.

pid.description: Process id of the service.

status.description: Always `ok`.

userAgent.description: The request's `User-Agent` header, or `null` when it was not sent.

purged.description:
`true` when the job's record and saved downloads were deleted
(`?purge=true`); `false` for a cancellation.

removed_files.description: Saved download files removed by a purge (0 for a cancellation).

curl_CurlRequest.description:
cURL request parameters

A JSON body carrying any field not listed here is rejected with `400`. This
protects against silently sending a removed or not-yet-released field that
would otherwise slip past validation unnoticed.

bearer_token.description:
Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. An `Authorization` entry in
`headers` wins: the token is then not sent, so the request carries
one `Authorization` header.

data.description:
Raw request body, sent as given (curl's `-d`). With no `method`, a
request that has a body is sent as `POST`.

form.description:
Form fields, sent URL-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).
With no `method`, a request that has a body is sent as `POST`.

json.description:
JSON request body, sent with `Content-Type: application/json`. An
explicit `"json": null` sends the document `null`, like `?json=null`
on the GET route; leave the field out for no JSON body. With no
`method`, a request that has a body is sent as `POST`.

max_filesize.description: Maximum response size, in bytes (1 to 16 GiB).

max_redirects.description: Maximum number of redirects to follow (at most 50).

method.description:
HTTP method. When absent, `POST` if `data`, `json` or `form` is set,
otherwise `GET` (curl's `-d`/`--json` rule). An explicit value is
sent as given, including `GET` with a body.

retry_count.description: Number of retries after a failed attempt (at most 5).

retry_delay.description:
Retry delay, in seconds (at most 60; default 1). The nth retry waits n
times this value. Requires `retry_count` greater than 0. The total
backoff must not exceed the server's cap, 300 seconds by default.

save_path.description:
Relative path under this job's download directory (downloads/by-job/{job_id}).
Must not be absolute or contain `..`.

timeout.description: Request timeout, in seconds (1 to 7200).

primary_ip.description:
The IP libcurl actually connected to on the terminal hop
(`CURLINFO_PRIMARY_IP`), serialized as a string. `None` if the
transfer never connected (cancelled before connect) OR if the IP
couldn't be parsed. Skipped in serialization to keep the wire
shape stable for existing clients.

removed_files.description:
Number of entries removed: `1` for a file; for a `by-job/{job_id}`
directory, the files it held. For any other directory, every entry
under it, links included: a `by-domain` or `by-date` directory holds
links only, so the files they point to stay under `by-job`.

request.description:
The request as submitted. Serialized redacted: a job
record is only serialized to be shown or kept as history, never to be
executed again, so credentials read as `[REDACTED]` in `GET
/jobs/{id}` and in the job file. The in-memory copy the executor runs
keeps the clear values.

oneOf.description:
Serialized with `effective_url` redacted like `request.url`: a record
written before finalization redacted it still holds the clear URL.

retry_attempts.description:
Number of attempts the executor has actually made so far: 1 for a
job that ran once, plus one per retry after a transfer error (see
`request.retry_count`). Following a redirect is not a new attempt;
0 while the job is pending or when it was cancelled before it ran.

retry_count.description:
Reserved for persisted retry-policy metadata on the job record.

The current runtime keeps retry configuration on `request.retry_count`.

body.description:
UTF-8 text for text responses, or base64 for binary responses.

Check `is_binary` before decoding.

headers.description:
One entry per header name, lowercased. A list header the server sent
more than once (`vary`, `cache-control`, `link`, `via`,
`www-authenticate`, ...) has its values joined with `, ` in the order
received (RFC 9110 section 5.3). Any other header the server sent more
than once keeps only its first value here: `set-cookie` (RFC 6265
section 3), single-value headers such as `content-type` or `location`,
and headers the kit does not know as lists. Read every value, and every
cookie, from `raw_headers`.

is_binary.description: Indicates whether `body` contains base64 (`true`) or plain UTF-8 text (`false`).

job_id.description:
Always null on a synchronous response. A `mode=async` request is
answered 202 with `{success, job_id, message}` instead.

raw_headers.description:
Every header line of the response the kit returns, in order, with each
name as the server sent it. Repeated headers such as `Set-Cookie`
appear once per line. When the kit decoded a compressed body,
`Content-Encoding` is removed and `Content-Length` gives the decoded
size. A response served from the kit's response cache carries the
stored headers, without hop-by-hop headers and with `Content-Length`
set to the stored body size (for `HEAD`, the upstream's value).

curl_ResponseHeader.description: A single response header as received from the upstream server.

cron.description:
Cron expression with six fields, `second minute hour day month weekday`,
and an optional seventh `year` field.

last_used.description: Updated when response cookies are persisted, not on every read/apply.

job_id.description:
UUID parsed from the storage path when present.

For synchronous saves this may be a storage-only UUID rather than an async job ID.

path.description: Path relative to the downloads root (for example `by-job/...` or `by-date/...`).

url.description: Always `null` in storage listings in this version.

curl_StoredCookie.description: Persisted cookie metadata used to prevent cross-domain replay.

expires_at.description:
Absolute expiry as Unix seconds, derived from `Max-Age` (preferred) or
`Expires` when the cookie arrived. Omitted for a session cookie, which
lives as long as the session.

curl_ToggleScheduleRequest.description: Request to enable or disable a schedule

enabled.description: `true` enables the schedule, `false` disables it.

curl_UpdateScheduleRequest.description:
Partial update of a schedule. Every field is optional, at least one is
required; absent fields keep their current value.

cron.description:
New cron expression with six fields, `second minute hour day month weekday`,
and an optional seventh `year` field.

enabled.description: `true` enables the schedule, `false` disables it.

oneOf.description:
Replacement request, validated like the one given to `POST /api/v1/curl/schedule`.
Replaces the whole request (not merged); `job_name` becomes the
schedule's `name`.

rss.description: Resident set size in bytes, or null when it cannot be read

heap.description: Language runtime heap in bytes (null for Rust)

started.description: Process start time as RFC3339 string

ingressReplyRoute.description: State of the computer's ingress reply routing. `degraded` means published services for this computer are unreachable because a VPN's routing rules outrank the daemon's; it is not self-repairable. Reported as a field rather than by flipping `status`, because the daemon itself is serving.

ip.description: IP address the request's connection came from, or null when it is not known

sandbox.description: Availability of the parts the program sandbox needs, checked once and cached. Which parts a program needs depends on its policy: every effective sandbox needs `bwrap` and `systemd_run`; an ingress policy additionally needs `nft`; `network.mode: restricted` additionally needs `landlock_abi` of 4 or more; `process.tmp_size` additionally needs `bwrap_tmpfs_size`. A program whose policy needs a missing part fails closed: it never starts. Sandbox problems do not change this endpoint's HTTP status or its top-level `status`.

bwrap.description: Whether the sandbox runtime is present and executable.

nft.description: Whether the firewall tool used for ingress rules is present and executable. Without it no ingress policy can be applied.

systemd_run.description: Whether the component that applies the sandbox's process limits is present and executable.

landlock_abi.description: Kernel support level for per-program TCP port restriction; `network.mode: restricted` needs 4 or higher. 0 when the kernel has no such support.

bwrap_version.description: Version the sandbox runtime reports, or null when it is absent or answers something unreadable.

bwrap_tmpfs_size.description: Whether the sandbox runtime can size temporary directories (version 0.10.0 or newer), which `process.tmp_size` needs. A program that sets `tmp_size` on a host where this is false is refused at launch with a `sandbox:` reason; it never starts with unsized temporary directories.

firewall.description: Computer-wide state of the ingress table: `ok` when the live table matches the fingerprint recorded at the last successful apply, `degraded` when it does not, or when the saved firewall state cannot be read (or the table cannot be read while a fingerprint is recorded), `none` when the committed state holds no active and no draining record, or when no sandbox runtime is installed or no firewall state, snapshot or marker exists at all (an unreadable state file is `degraded`); it describes committed records, not whether a desired program would owe rules. Per-program drains are visible only on `GET /programs/{id}/sandbox`; this value never says `draining`. Evaluated on each health request, from the committed records and the live table; nothing recomputes it in the background.

id.description: Unique program identifier, 0 to 2147483646 (auto-assigned if not provided).

name.description: Program name - must be unique, cannot contain quotes

description.description: Human-readable description of the program purpose

enabled.description: Whether the program is currently enabled and should be managed by the daemon

command.description: Full command to execute including all arguments. Use for your custom programs only, such as `node app.js`, `python main.py`, `ruby server.rb`. Do not use for system services like `apache2`, `nginx`, `postgresql`; use `systemctl` for those. Must not contain a line feed, carriage return or NUL.

boot.description: Start automatically on system boot. A program with a `display` is started as soon as that display is ready.

delay_seconds.description: The startup window: seconds the program must STAY RUNNING for the start to count as successful. Nothing is postponed: the program is launched immediately. NOTE that 0 does NOT disable the window: at 0 the window is 1 second. Under `autorestart` `"unexpected"` or `"true"`, a non-zero exit or a signal inside the window is a FAILED start, retried a limited number of times and then marked `fatal`. An end that is not a crash under `autorestart` (any end under `"false"`, an exit 0 otherwise) is not a failed start, however quick: the daemon holds it back until the window has passed, so a one-shot runs once. Under `"false"` and `"unexpected"` it is reported as `exited` as soon as it ends, with its exit code or its signal in `last_run`; under `"true"` it is not reported as `exited` and is started again once the window has passed. A stop, edit or removal sent in that window can take up to this long to return. Hoody Kit programs keep the plain rule: the window is also 1 second at 0, and any exit inside the window is a failed start, whatever `autorestart` says.

autorestart.description: Restart policy: `"unexpected"` (default) restarts after an exit code other than 0, including a deliberate nonzero exit; `"true"` always; `"false"` never. Booleans `true`/`false` are accepted too and are stored and returned as sent. A program that exits on its own has finished, however quickly it exits: any end under `"false"`, and an exit 0 under `"unexpected"`, is reported as `exited` as soon as it ends, with its exit code or its signal in `last_run`, and is held back until the startup window (`delay_seconds`; 1 second when 0) has passed, so a one-shot runs once; under `"true"` an exit 0 is held the same way and then started again. Under `"unexpected"` and `"true"` a non-zero exit or a signal inside that window is still a failed start, retried a limited number of times and then marked `fatal`. Hoody Kit programs keep the plain time-based rule: any exit before `delay_seconds` is a failed start, retried whatever this is.

user.description: System user account to run the program as (must exist on the system). A Linux account name matched case-insensitively: starts with a letter or `_`, continues with letters, digits, `_` and `-`, may end in `$`, at most 32 bytes. A sandboxed program cannot run as an account resolving to uid 0.

environment.description: Environment variables as key-value pairs. Names match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` (up to 128 characters); values must not contain a line feed or carriage return, nor whitespace followed by `;` or `#` (the rest of the value would be read as a comment and the program could not load; refused with 400 unless the program has a `terminal_id` and no `port_range`; judged after line feeds, carriage returns and NULs are stripped). Nor may a value hold both a double and a single quote, or begin or end with either: values are written quoted with no escape character, so the first has no delimiter and the second arrives with the quote stripped (refused with 400 naming the variable, unless the program has a `terminal_id`, no `port_range` and a `user` other than root, for which such values are passed another way). A value with a double quote and no single quote is written in single quotes, any other in double quotes. The stored map is not the whole process environment: with `inject_computer_env` the program also receives PID 1's environment (Kit programs only its `HOODY_*` variables in the default mode), depending on the daemon's injection mode and on that environment being readable; without it, only the variables its `command` names. Explicit values override injected ones.
