A value with a double quote and no single quote is written in single quotes, any other in double quotes. The stored map is not the whole process environment: with `inject_computer_env` the program also receives PID 1's environment (Kit programs only its `HOODY_*` variables in the default mode), depending on the daemon's injection mode and on that environment being readable; without it, only the variables its `command` names. Explicit values override injected ones. On edit the map REPLACES the stored one: resend every variable you want kept; `{}` clears it.

hoody_kit.description: Read-only. Server-derived: true when the program's directory is under `/hoody/plugins`, or when its name is a known Hoody Kit name AND its command is that kit program's. Any value supplied in a create or update request body is ignored.

inject_computer_env.description: Whether the daemon adds the computer's environment (PID 1's) to the program's. When absent: true for a Hoody Kit program (see `hoody_kit`), false for every other program. When true, the daemon's injection mode applies: by default a Kit program gets only the `HOODY_*` variables and any other program all of them; `--inject-all-env` and `--inject-hoody-env-only` override that for every program. When false, nothing from PID 1 is added, `HOODY_*` included, except the variables the program's `command` names as `$X`, `${X}` or `%(ENV_X)s`: each of those is resolved from the program's `environment`, then PID 1, then (for `$X` and `${X}` in a program without `port_range`) the daemon's own environment, and only that variable is added. A named variable is filtered like any other source: for a sandboxed program a value that is not literal, or a loader name, is dropped; a named variable with no value anywhere is left alone. This controls the daemon's own injection only: the program still inherits the environment of the process manager that runs it. On edit: absent or null leaves the stored value unchanged (null is not a separate state); to return to the derived default, send the value it derives (true for a Hoody Kit program, false otherwise).

boot_if_exists.description: Absolute path of a marker file. Every time the daemon starts, it starts this program once if the path is a regular file (a symlink, a directory or a missing path does not count) and the process manager has not started the program since it came up. A program that is running stays as it is, and one that was stopped by hand stays stopped on a daemon restart or an update, but a reset stops and removes every program and replays the defaults, so after a reset a program whose file exists is started even if it had been stopped by hand; when the file is absent the program stays lazy. Meant for a lazy program (`lazy_load`) that must be running after a reboot only while it has work: the program keeps the file present while it does. The path must be absolute, contain no `..` segment and no control character, and be at most 4096 bytes. Allowed only for a standard program or a `port_range` of a single port (`start` equal to `end`); a wider range is refused with 400, on create and on an edit that widens the range of a program that has it. The daemon looks at the file only while it starts, never afterwards, so setting this field on an existing program starts nothing by itself. It does not change `boot` or `lazy_load`. Absent or `null` leaves the stored value unchanged on edit; an empty string clears it.

port_range.description: Port range for multi-instance programs. Each port in the range creates a separate INSTANCE (running process). Example: {start:8000, end:8099} creates 100 instances. Independent from lazy_load - can use with boot:true (all instances auto-start) OR lazy_load:true (instances start on-demand). A range must not overlap any other stored program's range. When either side has an effective sandbox, its ports are also compared with enabled programs' declared listening sets, and ports held by active or draining sandbox firewall records are refused until those records are gone. On edit the object replaces the stored range and needs both `start` and `end`. On edit, omitted keeps the stored range and `null` removes it, together with `port_param` unless the request sends one: the program becomes a single process.

end.description: Inclusive ending port, at least `start`. Both endpoints are 1 to 65535, and `end - start + 1` must not exceed 4096.

port_param.description: Parameter name for passing port (e.g. --port, -p). Valid ONLY together with port_range; sending it on its own is rejected with "port_param requires port_range to be set". Has no schema default on purpose. Omit it and the server applies --port itself, so a default here would make every port-less create fail.

lazy_load.description: Enable lazy loading. When true, program/instances NOT started automatically. Started on-demand by edge proxy via ensure-started endpoint. Cannot be combined with boot:true.

ready_port.description: TCP readiness port. When set, a start with `wait=true` is reported successful only once this port accepts a TCP connection, closing the gap where `running` only means "the startup window passed without an exit" while the listener is not up yet. The program must also be up: it is reported running, or it is still starting and only its own processes listen on this port, so a program that listens early is ready at once. For a program whose port lives inside its own command line rather than in a `port_range`. For a sandboxed program it joins `port_range` in the listening set that `sandbox.network.bind_ports` defaults to and must cover. The port counts as ready once the program accepts the TCP connection the daemon opens to it from inside the computer; a program that does not accept that connection never becomes ready (each attempt waits up to 300 ms). An accepted connection shows that something listens on that port, not that it is this program's listener or that it serves anything. `0` is refused. It is checked against active or draining sandbox firewall reservations, and against enabled programs' declared listening sets when either side has an effective sandbox; two unsandboxed programs' readiness ports are not compared. With `if_not_running`, an already-running or shared result can come back without this polling, and an already-running port-range instance is not probed.

stop_wait_seconds.description: Seconds a stop waits for the program to exit after the stop signal before it is killed, from 1 to 600. Omit it to leave the value unchanged; send 0 to go back to the default of 10 seconds.

display.description: Hoody Display number for GUI programs, 1 to 40000 (display 0 is not accepted; only screen 0, so ":1" or ":1.0"). Accepts "1", ":1" or the number 1. Before the program starts, the display is brought up (always in terminal N, where N is the display number, never in the program's own `terminal_id`) and the program's `user` is given access to it; if either fails, the request fails and the program is not started. For a persistent `boot` program the add, edit or enable is still saved in that case, but not applied. A display number equal to the program's own `terminal_id` is refused, and so are a display number equal to another program's `terminal_id` and a `terminal_id` equal to another program's display number, when the request creates that pairing. An edit that does not change `display` does not re-check a stored value.

terminal_id.description: Hoody Terminal integration: Session ID (1-65535). Designed for use with hoody-terminal web interface. When specified, program runs in that terminal: terminal N of the computer, opened at the `terminal-N` host in a browser, with `hoody daemon programs terminal connect`, or with the SDK's `client.daemon.programs.connectTerminal`. The program's input and output are connected to that terminal session. Must be unique among persistent programs. Cannot be combined with an effective `sandbox`, or with `port_range` (a port-range program has no terminal; a program stored with both is not refused an edit that leaves them). The program runs as its `user`, root or not, and gets `TERM=xterm-256color` unless its environment sets `TERM`. When the command ends, the program ends with the command's exit code, so its status and `autorestart` follow the command, and clients attached to its terminal are disconnected with WebSocket close code 4404 (`daemon program ended`); a restarted program is reached by attaching again. In interactive mode that is when the shell left after the command ends, and with `tmux` when the tmux client does. Output the program writes while hoody-terminal has no connection to it waits in the terminal, up to about 19 KB, and a program that writes more blocks until something attaches; once anything has attached or used the terminal's REST automation, hoody-terminal stays connected until the program ends or the terminal session is deleted. Output that reaches hoody-terminal, the program's stderr included, is also written to the program's stdout log as raw terminal output (control sequences and `\r\n` line ends kept), with the same size limit and rotation as any program's log, so its last output can still be read with the program's logs after it ends, when its terminal no longer answers. Two kinds of output are not in that log: output still waiting in the terminal when the program ends because nothing had attached, and output written faster than the log takes it in. The stderr log holds errors from setting up the terminal and from its connections; warnings are left out. A stop ends everything the program runs in its terminal: TERM first, KILL after 7 s for whatever ignores it. On edit, omitted keeps the stored terminal and `null` removes it, together with `terminal_shell` and `terminal_interactive` unless the request sends them; a running program leaves its terminal at its next start.

terminal_shell.description: Hoody Terminal integration: the shell that loads the environment, or `tmux`. A non-blank value requires `terminal_id`, and the daemon accepts only an installed `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `sh` or `tmux`. A blank string means direct execution, like an omitted one. With a shell, the command is one shell command line (pipes, `&&` and variables work); without one, its words are passed as they are, with quotes grouping words and nothing expanded, and, as for a program without a terminal, a `#` or `;` after a space starts a comment, even inside quotes. Omitted or null on edit, the stored shell is kept.

terminal_interactive.description: Hoody Terminal integration: Override auto-detection of interactive vs service mode. true = interactive (-ic, shell persists), false = service (-c, exec replaces shell), undefined = auto-detect (recommended). Works with hoody-terminal web interface. In service mode the shell loads its rc file and is replaced by the command when it is a single command; a list, pipe or leading assignment runs as written. In interactive mode the command runs and the shell stays. On edit, omitted or null keeps the stored value, including an earlier override; send true or false to change it.

webhooks.description: Webhook notification configuration for program lifecycle events `enabled` and `urls` are REQUIRED whenever this object is present: the daemon's `WebhookConfig` has no default for either, so a webhooks object without them is a 400 from the add or edit handler (`invalid program body: missing field ...`). On an edit the two are replaced rather than merged, and only `events`, `headers`, `timeout` and `retry` keep their stored value when omitted, so a partial webhook edit has to resend `enabled` and `urls`. `webhooks: null` does not clear stored webhooks. Delivery needs more than this object: the daemon's `notifications.enabled` and `notifications.event_listener_enabled` must be true and the daemon's event listener must be running. Known limitation: event-driven delivery is not verified end to end; poll status for monitoring that has to be reliable. There is no HTTP endpoint for event streams or webhook management: configure webhooks through add and edit, and poll status for monitoring.

enabled.description: Enable webhooks for this program

urls.description: Webhook URLs. When `enabled` is true: 1 to 5 URLs, HTTPS, no credentials, and public destinations only. A disabled configuration skips these checks. A name that resolves to a non-public address can save and then fail at delivery.

events.description: A single event name or an array, trimmed and case-insensitive: `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `BACKOFF`, `STOPPING`, `STOPPED`, `EXITED`, `FATAL`, `UNKNOWN` (without `PROCESS_STATE_`). `[]`, `"all"` or `"*"` select all, and a new configuration without `events` selects all. On edit, omitted `events` keep the stored filter.

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers, at most 10 when `enabled` is true. On edit, supplied headers replace the stored map and omitted headers keep it.

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds. When `enabled` is true it must be 1 to 60; when no value is stored the dispatcher uses 10.

retry.description: Retry attempts on failure. When `enabled` is true it must be 0 to 5; when no value is stored the dispatcher uses 3.

sandbox.description: Per-program confinement. Three-state on `programs/edit/{id}`: absent leaves the current block unchanged, `null` clears it, and an object REPLACES it as a unit. There is no field-level merge into a sandbox block, so an edit must resend every field it wants kept. On `programs/add` absent and `null` are the same thing. A policy rejection by the daemon's validation is a 400 carrying the usual `{success: false, error: ...}` envelope; a body that is not valid JSON, an unknown key inside `sandbox`, or a field of the wrong type is a 400 carrying the same envelope (`invalid program body: ...`). An accepted edit that changes the resolved policy replaces the loaded definition, which stops the instance running under the old one (whether a new one starts follows `boot` and `lazy_load`); an apply that fails after persistence is a 400 that says so, with the program persisted.

error.example: Failed to read log file: No such file or directory

log_file.description: Present on a file error: the path that was read.

daemon_LogStreamEvent.description: The JSON `data` of one event on `GET /api/v1/daemon/programs/{id}/logs/stream`. Which fields are present depends on the SSE `event` name: `open` carries `log_file`, `type`, `offset`, `exists`; `line` carries `line`, `offset`; `reset` carries `reason`, `offset`; `error` carries `error`.

line.description: One log line, without its terminator (`line`).

offset.description: Byte offset: just past the line (`line`, and equal to the event id), where following starts (`open`), or 0 (`reset`).

reason.description: Why reading restarted (`reset`).

exists.description: Whether the file existed when the stream opened (`open`).

daemon_LastRun.description: The result of a program's last ended run: the run's own report (`source: launcher`), or the process manager's record when there is no report (`source: supervisor`). Absent before the first run ends.

exit_code.description: The program's exit code, or `null` when it was ended by a signal or never ran. A sandboxed or terminal program reports a signal death as `128+n` here, with `signal` null.

signal.description: Name of the signal that ended the program, such as `SIGKILL`, or `null`.

error.description: Why the program never ran (a command that cannot be executed, a sandbox that cannot be set up), or the daemon's own reason: `ttl expired`, `daemon restarted before the program finished`. Otherwise `null`.

ended_at.description: When the run ended, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

final.description: `true` when no automatic restart or retry follows, whether the run succeeded or not; `false` while the program will be started again automatically.

source.description: Where the result came from: `launcher`, the run's own report; `supervisor`, the process manager's record alone.

daemon_RunResult.description: A finished run's result, without the error text a `LastRun` can carry (that text can quote the program's command). Every field is always present.

exit_code.description: The exit code, or `null` when the run was ended by a signal or never ran.

signal.description: The name of the signal that ended the run, such as `SIGKILL`, or `null`.

ended_at.description: When the run ended, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

final.description: `true` when no automatic restart or retry follows.

source.description: `launcher`: the run's own report. `supervisor`: the process manager's record alone.

failure.description: Why the run ended without an exit status: `launch_failed`, the command could not be started; `ttl_expired`, a quick-start reached its time limit; `daemon_restarted`, the daemon restarted before a quick-start finished. `null` otherwise. Treat a value not listed here as a failure.

daemon_OverviewInstance.description: One process of a program. Every field is always present.

port.description: The instance's port for a port-range program; `null` for a standard program's one process.

status.description: The process state. `failed` is a quick-start whose creation failed; `unknown` is a state the daemon could not read or does not recognise.

pid.description: The process id while it is starting or running.

started_at.description: When the process was last started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, when known.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since that start, while it is starting or running.

supervisor_state.description: The process manager's own state, when it differs from `status` (a one-shot command that finished shows `exited` while the process manager still reports it running, for example).

last_result.description: The last finished run, when one is known.

daemon_OverviewProgram.description: One program in the overview. Holds only fields that are safe to show: never the command, environment, user, directory, webhooks, log file paths or sandbox. Every field is always present.

lazy_load.description: Started when it is first used, not at boot.

hoody_kit.description: One of the Hoody Kit's own programs.

autorestart.description: When the program is started again after it exits: `always`, `unexpected` (after an exit code it does not expect), `never`.

port_range.description: The ports of a port-range program, inclusive; `null` for a standard program.

states_known.description: `false` when the process states could not be read: `status` is then `unknown` and `instances` is empty. Never read that as stopped.

status.description: The process state. `failed` is a quick-start whose creation failed; `unknown` is a state the daemon could not read or does not recognise. For a port-range program, `running` when any instance is starting or running; `partial` says whether all of them are.

partial.description: `true` for a port-range program some of whose instances are starting or running while another is in a state other than stopped (a failed one, say); `status` is then `running`. `false` otherwise, and always for a standard program. A stopped instance never makes a range partial.

last_result.description: A standard program's last finished run; `null` for a port-range program, whose instances carry their own.

instances.description: Every loaded process: one, with `port: null`, for a standard program; one per loaded port for a port-range program. Empty when the program is not loaded or the states are unknown.

daemon_OverviewTemporary.description: One quick-start program. Never carries its command, environment, user or directory. Every field is always present.

name.description: The name given when the quick-start was created; `null` when the daemon chose it.

status.description: The process state. `failed` is a quick-start whose creation failed; `unknown` is a state the daemon could not read or does not recognise.

expires_at.description: When it is stopped by its time limit, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; `null` without one.

last_result.description: The last finished run, when one is known.

features.description: The actions this daemon offers: `restart` (`POST /programs/{id}/restart`) and `boot_switch` (`POST /programs/{id}/boot`). Ignore names you do not know.

pid_before.description: The process id before the restart; `null` when it was not running.

pid_after.description: The process id after it; `null` until it is seen running again.

started_at.description: When it was started again, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

daemon_RestartAnswer.description: A restart's receipt. Every field is always present. `error` is a fixed sentence per `code`; it never carries the program's own output.

state.description: `reserved`: the key is held and nothing was sent yet. `accepted`: the restart is under way. `completed`: done, see `outcome`. `unknown`: it is not known whether the program restarted: a reply was lost, a stop or start was not confirmed, or the daemon does not hold the key (it was never used, or the daemon restarted since). Never read `unknown` as not restarted. `null` on a refusal.

outcome.description: With `completed`: `restarted` when every target runs under a new process id; `failed` when a target was stopped and did not start again.

row.description: The program's overview row after the restart, once it is done.

daemon_BootAnswer.description: Every field is always present. `error` is a fixed sentence per `code`.

row.description: The program's overview row after the change.

code.description:
Machine-readable error code. Every error body on this API has this
shape: `error`, `code`, and `details` with `message` and `help`.

reason.description:
Set on some 503 DISPLAY_NOT_AVAILABLE answers to say why there is
no display. `dependency_missing` means the computer is missing
software the display needs; retrying does not help until the
computer runs an image that has it.

state.description:
Set on a 503 DISPLAY_NOT_AVAILABLE answer when the display runs
without what the request needs. `x-live` means X runs on the
display but its viewer server does not, for example because
another program holds the display's port: programs and input
still work, the viewer and screenshots do not.

reason.description:
Set on some 503 DISPLAY_NOT_AVAILABLE answers to say why there is
no display; see `Error.details.reason`.

state.description:
Set on a 503 DISPLAY_NOT_AVAILABLE answer when the display runs
without what the request needs; see `Error.details.state`.

display_ActionScreenshotError.description:
The 500 of `/input/act` and `/input/wait`. With `SCREENSHOT_FAILED` the action (or the
wait) completed and `action` carries its answer, as the 200 would.

action.description: What completed before the screenshot failed (`SCREENSHOT_FAILED` only).

display_InputActionResponse.description:
The answer of an input action. `action` names what was done and `details` holds, per
route, the values the action used (defaults filled in) and what it reports back:

| Route | `action` | `details` |
|---|---|---|
| `mouse/click` | `click` | `button`, `repeat` |
| `mouse/double-click` | `double-click` | `button` |
| `mouse/move` | `move` | `x`, `y` |
| `mouse/move-relative` | `move-relative` | `x`, `y` |
| `mouse/down` | `mousedown` | `button`, `holdMs` |
| `mouse/up` | `mouseup` | `button` |
| `mouse/scroll` | `scroll` | `direction`, `clicks`, and `x`, `y` when given |
| `keyboard/type` | `type` | `length` (UTF-16 code units), `warning` when set |
| `keyboard/key` | `key` | `keys`, `warning` when set |
| `keyboard/key-down` | `keydown` | `key`, `holdMs` |
| `keyboard/key-up` | `keyup` | `key` |
| `window/move` | `window-move` | `windowId`, `x`, `y` |
| `window/resize` | `window-resize` | `windowId`, `width`, `height` |
| `window/minimize` | `window-minimize` | `windowId` |
| `window/close` | `window-close` | `windowId` |
| `window/raise` | `window-raise` | `windowId` |
| `input/click-at` | `click-at` | `x`, `y`, `button`, `repeat`, `pointer` |
| `input/type-at` | `type-at` | `x`, `y`, `length` |
| `input/drag` | `drag` | `startX`, `startY`, `endX`, `endY`, `button` |
| `input/select` | `select` | `x`, `y`, `endX`, `endY` |
| `input/reset` | `reset` | `message` |
| `clipboard` (POST) | `clipboard-write` | `length`, `selection` |

windowId.description: The window ID as it was sent (decimal or hex 0x...)

inputFocus.description:
`true` when the window has keyboard focus, so untargeted
`keyboard/*` input reaches it. `false` when the window was
activated but could not be focused because it is not viewable
(hidden, for example minimized in a viewer).

warning.description:
Present when `inputFocus` is `false`, saying why keyboard
input cannot reach the window, and when the display has no
window manager: the window then has keyboard focus but was
not activated or raised, and `/window/active` cannot report
it.

button.description: Mouse button (1=left, 2=middle, 3=right; 4-7 are the scroll wheel: 4=up, 5=down, 6=left, 7=right)

repeat.description:
Number of clicks. `repeat` x `delay` must not exceed 4000 ms, or the
request is rejected with 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming both fields.
The count is never silently capped, so `repeat: 100` stays valid at
`delay: 40` or less.

delay.description:
Milliseconds to wait after every click, the last one included
(that is intended, not a rounding error). Defaults to
100 ms when omitted, which is what the 4000 ms `repeat` x
`delay` budget is counted against.

sync.description: Accepted and ignored. The pointer is at its new position when the call answers, whether or not it is set, and a move to where the pointer already is answers at once.

clicks.description:
Wheel clicks. `clicks` x `delay` must not exceed 4000 ms, or the
request is rejected with 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `clicks: 100`
therefore needs `delay: 40` or less.

delay.description:
Milliseconds between wheel clicks. Defaults to 100 ms.
Lower it to scroll far in one call without exceeding the budget.

x.description:
Scroll at this point instead of wherever the pointer happens to be.
Must be given together with `y`. The move and the wheel events are
sent as one chained command, so no other request can move the
pointer in between.

text.description:
Text to type, without NUL characters. A line break presses Return, a tab presses Tab.
Each line is typed as one command and must fit its 4000 ms: its characters times
`delay` (12 ms when not given; 0 counts as 1 ms), so 333 characters per line at the
default delay, more with a lower one. The whole text must fit 25000 ms: all its
characters times `delay`, plus 100 ms per line break (200 lines of a few characters fit
at the default delay). Text over either bound is a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`: the message
names the largest `delay` that fits when one does, and otherwise asks you to send at
most 4000 characters per line or to split the text into several requests.

items.description: A key name or combination of letters, digits, `_`, `+`, `-` and `.` (for example `Return`, `ctrl+c`, `KP_1`). Names of reserved commands are refused, in any letter case.

keys.description:
Key combinations (e.g. ['ctrl+c', 'Return']), with X11 key names, which are
case-sensitive: `Return`, `BackSpace`, `Escape`, `minus`, not `Enter`, `Backspace`,
`Esc`, `-` inside a combination. Unknown names are a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming
every one (with a very long list the message says "perhaps more" and that some other
keys may not have been sent); otherwise the request's other keys, if it had any, were
pressed. Every key, and every part of a
combination, takes `delay` (12 ms when not given): their number times `delay` may
not exceed 4000 ms.

key.description: Key name (X11 keysym, e.g. Shift_L, ctrl). Letters, digits, `_`, `+`, `-` and `.` only. Names of reserved commands are refused, in any letter case.

sync.description:
Wait for the change to be applied before answering. On
`window/focus` this is what makes a following `keyboard/*` action
land in the window that was just focused. When the display is
running but the change is not seen within 5 s (the window manager
refused it, or the window was already that way), the call answers
409 `SYNC_TIMEOUT`; the request was still sent.

windowId.description: X window ID (decimal, or hex like 0x60000c; 32-bit)

sync.description: Wait (up to 2 s) until the window manager reports the window as no longer minimized. Defaults to true, unlike the other window actions: the restore request is a message the window manager may ignore, so without waiting the response cannot say whether it worked. A window still minimized after 2 s answers 409 `SYNC_TIMEOUT`.

previousState.description: `normal` means the window was not minimized; the call was a no-op.

state.description:
`normal` once observed; `null` when `sync` was false, since the
request was sent but not observed. The exception is a window
that was already normal: nothing has to be waited for, so that
no-op answers `normal` with `synced: true` even for
`sync: false`.

windowId.description: Window ID: a decimal number up to 4294967295, or 0x followed by 1-8 hex digits

x.description: Screen x of the window's top-left corner, or the distance to move with `relative`.

y.description: Screen y of the window's top-left corner, or the distance to move with `relative`.

sync.description: Wait until the window is at the new position before answering. A move to where the window already is answers at once. When the display is running but the window has not moved within 2 s (the window manager refused it), the call answers 409 `SYNC_TIMEOUT`; the request was still sent.

relative.description: Move by `x`,`y` from the current position instead of to it.

windowId.description: Window ID: a decimal number up to 4294967295, or 0x followed by 1-8 hex digits

width.description: New width. In pixels, or in the window's own size units with `useHints`.

height.description: New height. In pixels, or in the window's own size units with `useHints`.

sync.description: Wait until the change is seen before answering. When the display is running but the change is not seen within 5 s (the window manager refused or adjusted it, or the window was already that way), the call answers 409 `SYNC_TIMEOUT`; the request was still sent.

useHints.description: Read `width` and `height` in the window's own size units instead of pixels, for programs that state a size step (a terminal emulator counts character cells, for example). Without it, or for a window with no such step, they are pixels.

pattern.description:
Extended POSIX regular expression, matched case-insensitively. A pattern that does not
compile, or that contains a NUL character, is a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

name.description: Search by window name/title. This is also what is searched when none of `name`, `class` and `classname` is set.

onlyVisible.description:
Restrict the search to windows that are currently viewable.
This is not a way to skip minimized windows: a window stays viewable
after `window/minimize`, even once the display's window manager
reports it iconic. What it does filter is unmapped
windows.

Note that `GET /windows` has a parameter of the same name with a
different test: there it drops windows carrying
`_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN`, which a minimized window does carry, so
that one does exclude minimized windows.

button.description: Mouse button (1=left, 2=middle, 3=right; 4-7 are the scroll wheel: 4=up, 5=down, 6=left, 7=right)

repeat.description:
Clicks at that point, in one chained invocation, so no other
request can move the pointer between them. Same 4000 ms `repeat` x `delay`
budget as `/mouse/click`.

delay.description:
Milliseconds after every click, the last one included. Defaults to
100 ms. A double-click needs `repeat: 2` with a `delay`
under the desktop's double-click time.

x.description: Screen x of the point to click before typing.

y.description: Screen y of the point to click before typing.

text.description:
Text to type, without NUL characters. A line break presses Return, a tab presses Tab.
Each line is typed as one command and must fit its 4000 ms: its characters times
`delay` (12 ms when not given; 0 counts as 1 ms), so 333 characters per line at the
default delay, more with a lower one. The whole text must fit 25000 ms: all its
characters times `delay`, plus 100 ms per line break (200 lines of a few characters fit
at the default delay). Text over either bound is a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`: the message
names the largest `delay` that fits when one does, and otherwise asks you to send at
most 4000 characters per line or to split the text into several requests.

startX.description: Screen x where the drag starts.

startY.description: Screen y where the drag starts.

endX.description: Screen x where the drag ends.

endY.description: Screen y where the drag ends.

button.description: Mouse button held during the drag: `1` left, `2` middle, `3` right, `4` to `7` wheel directions. Default `1`.

steps.description: Number of intermediate mouse positions for smooth drag

x.description: Screen x where the selection starts (a click).

y.description: Screen y where the selection starts (a click).

endX.description: Screen x where the selection ends (a shift-click).

endY.description: Screen y where the selection ends (a shift-click).

action.description:
Action path. One of:

`mouse/click`, `mouse/double-click`, `mouse/move`, `mouse/move-relative`,
`mouse/down`, `mouse/up`, `mouse/scroll`, `keyboard/type`, `keyboard/key`,
`keyboard/key-down`, `keyboard/key-up`, `input/click-at`, `input/type-at`,
`input/drag`, `input/select`, `input/wait`, `clipboard/read`,
`clipboard/write`, `window/focus`, `window/raise`, `window/minimize`,
`window/restore`, `window/move`, `window/resize`, `window/close`,
`window/search`.

`params` are validated against the same schema the standalone route uses,
except that a nested `input/wait` accepts only `ms` and an optional
`screenshot: false`; use the outer `screenshot` field of /input/act to
capture an image.

`actions` holds 1 to 50 entries; each needs a non-empty `action` of at
most 50 characters and an optional `params` object. A malformed entry
rejects the whole request with 400. An unknown action name that passes
these checks, or a bad field inside `params`, is reported as `failed`
in the 200 body.

display_ActBody.description:
One action, then a screenshot. The action runs first and the screenshot is taken after
`screenshotDelay`. A failure of the screenshot or of its crop is answered after the
input was already delivered, so a retry of the same request repeats the input.

action.description:
Action path. One of:

`mouse/click`, `mouse/double-click`, `mouse/move`, `mouse/move-relative`,
`mouse/down`, `mouse/up`, `mouse/scroll`, `keyboard/type`, `keyboard/key`,
`keyboard/key-down`, `keyboard/key-up`, `input/click-at`, `input/type-at`,
`input/drag`, `input/select`, `input/wait`, `clipboard/read`,
`clipboard/write`, `window/focus`, `window/raise`, `window/minimize`,
`window/restore`, `window/move`, `window/resize`, `window/close`,
`window/search`.

`params` are validated against the same schema the standalone route uses,
except that a nested `input/wait` accepts only `ms` and an optional
`screenshot: false`; use the outer `screenshot` field of /input/act to
capture an image.
`act` runs one action, so a rejection here IS a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`
(inside `/input/batch` the same rejection is reported in the 200 body
as `failed.error` instead).

screenshot.description: Capture a screenshot after the action. When false, the answer has no `screenshot`.

screenshotDelay.description: Milliseconds to wait after the action before the screenshot is taken (0-5000)

screenshotRegion.description:
Crop the screenshot to `x1,y1,x2,y2`, in screen coordinates: minimum 10x10 px, maximum
65535 on each axis, `x2 > x1` and `y2 > y1`; anything else is a 400
`VALIDATION_ERROR`, answered before the action runs. A cropped image carries no
`dataUrl`.

condition.description:
`window-present` waits for at least one window to match `pattern`.
`window-absent` waits for the last match to go away, or for a
specific `windowId` to stop existing.

pattern.description:
Extended POSIX regex. Required for
`window-present`; for `window-absent` give either this or
`windowId`, not both. A pattern that does not compile is a 400,
not an empty result, and so is one containing a NUL (it could never
reach the subprocess).

match.description:
Which window property `pattern` is matched against. `name` is the
title, which changes while an application runs; `class` is stable
across a window's life and is the better choice for "has the app
started yet".

onlyVisible.description:
Restrict the search to windows that are currently viewable.
This is not a way to skip minimized windows: a window stays viewable
after `window/minimize`, even once the display's window manager
reports it iconic. What it does filter is unmapped
windows.

Sending it alongside `windowId` is rejected: that is an identity
check, not a search, so the flag would be silently ignored. The
same goes for `match`.

windowId.description:
Wait for this exact window to stop existing. `window-absent` only,
and not together with `pattern`, `match` or `onlyVisible`.

pollMs.description:
Gap between observations. An explicit value above `timeoutMs` is
rejected; the default is not, so a `timeoutMs` under 250 is a legal
request for a single look rather than an error.

success.description: Whether the condition held before the timeout.

polls.description:
Observations that completed. An observation that was aborted, or
killed before it could answer, is not counted, so `polls: 0` with
`timedOut: true` means the condition was never actually observed.

timedOut.description: Present and true when the timeout expired with the condition unmet.

windows.description:
Window ids that matched, for a satisfied `window-present`. Empty
for a `windowId` check and for `window-absent`.

text.description:
Clipboard text content, up to 1,048,576 characters. Its UTF-8 encoding may not exceed
4 MiB, and the whole request body is limited to 2 MiB. An empty string empties the
selection.

result.description:
What the action read back. Present only for actions that
return something: `clipboard/read` (the text, as a bare
string), `window/focus` (`{ inputFocus, warning? }`),
`window/restore` (`{ windowId, previousState, state,
synced }`), `window/search` (an array of window ids) and
`input/click-at` (`{ pointer: { x, y, window } }`).
`keyboard/type` and `keyboard/key` carry `{ warning }` when
the keys went to a named `window` as simulated input (see
those endpoints). Absent for actions whose only outcome is
that they happened.

skipped.description: Indexes of the actions that were not run. Omitted when there are none.

windowId.description: The window the window manager marks active; null when it marks none (nothing focused yet, or the active window was minimized or closed), as `focusedWindowId` of `GET /api/v1/display/windows` reports it.
The window ID exactly as written in the request path (decimal or hex 0x...).
The window ID exactly as written in the request path (decimal or hex 0x...).

pid.description:
Process id of the program that owns the window, as the program reports it.
Null when the window does not report one. A null or missing `pid` says nothing
about which program owns the window; older display versions omit the field.

focusedWindowId.description: The window the window manager marks active; null when no window is active (or the display has no window manager).

wmName.description: The window title, the UTF-8 one when the window sets both.

pid.description: Process id the window names as its own; null when it names none.

transientFor.description: The window this one is a dialog or transient of; null when none.

action.description: The action's own answer. `action` is the full route path such as `input/click-at`; `details` holds the validated parameters, defaults included and unknown fields left out.

result.description:
What the action read back, for the actions that read something:
`clipboard/read` (the text, as a bare string), `window/focus`
(`{ inputFocus, warning? }`), `window/restore` (`{ windowId,
previousState, state, synced }`), `window/search` (an array
of window ids) and `input/click-at` (`{ pointer: { x, y,
window } }`); `keyboard/type` and `keyboard/key` carry
`{ warning }` when the keys went to a named `window` as
simulated input. Absent otherwise.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the screenshot, as in `ScreenshotInfo`.

path.description:
Absolute file path, `<display>/<unix seconds>.<pid>.<random>.png` under the screenshot
storage directory (a thumbnail ends in `.thumbnail.png`).

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in seconds, used for `/screenshot/{timestamp}` and `/thumbnail/{timestamp}` queries

thumbnail.description: Thumbnail file, or null. A new capture returns null.

data.description: Base64 encoded image data (without data URL prefix)

dataUrl.description: Complete data URL ready for use. Absent from a cropped image (`region` on a screenshot, `screenshotRegion` on `input/act`).

info.description: Describes the stored capture. For a cropped screenshot it still describes the full image.

cursor.description:
Pointer position in screen coordinates. Only present on `GET /screenshot` with
`?cursor` and `?base64`.

display_DisplayLatency.description:
Round-trip time between the display and its connected viewer, in milliseconds. `null`
while no viewer is connected. Each value is `null` when the display does not report it.

display_DisplayInfoWindow.description:
A window as the display's viewer server knows it. `id` is a viewer window id, not an X
window id: it cannot be passed to the window and input routes. Use `GET /windows`, or
`POST /window/search`, to get the ids those routes take.

pid.description: Process id of the program that owns the window; null when it does not report one.

state.description: Window states, for example `_NET_WM_STATE_MAXIMIZED_VERT`.

group_leader_xid.description: X window id of the window's group leader, in hex (`0x...`). Empty when unknown.

command.description: Command line of the program that owns the window. Empty when unknown.

display_DisplayInfo.description:
The display's session, its windows and its stored screenshots. A display that no program
has used yet is started first, so the answer describes a running display.

display.description: Display ID

pid.description: Process id of the display's viewer server.

user.description: User the display runs as.

project_id.description: Hoody project ID of the computer. Empty when unknown.

computer_id.description: Hoody computer ID. Empty when unknown.

start_time.description: When the display's session started (ISO 8601). Null when unknown.

connected_clients.description: Number of viewers connected to the display.

last_activity_timestamp.description:
Last keyboard or mouse activity on the display, as an ISO 8601 string. When it cannot be
read the value is the string `"null"` (text, not JSON null), so check for it before
parsing the value as a time.

windows.description: Windows on the display. Viewer window ids, see `DisplayInfoWindow`.

state.description:
Only set when the display was still waiting for its first use at the moment of the
read, which the request itself normally prevents by starting it. Then the entry has
no session, windows or latency, and `connected_clients` is 0.

ip.description: Address of the caller, as the service sees it.

exec_AnyValue.description: Flexible value type used for defaults metadata

parse_window_lines.description: How many lines at the top of a script are read for magic comments.

unknown_keys_behavior.description: Keys that are not directives are ignored when magic comments are written.

code.description: Machine-readable error code (e.g. ERROR_400, ERROR_404, ERROR_500, ERROR_503).

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp emitted by the server.

details.description: Optional additional error details (shape varies per endpoint).

label.description: Human-readable label for this mount. Absent when it has none.

mount_path.description: Absolute filesystem path where the mount is accessible. Use this path to read and write files on the mounted backend.

status.description: mounting: not serving yet. active: serving. error: not serving; see error. unmounting and unmounted: being removed.

status_message.description: What the mount is waiting for, or how many of its files are kept on the server and not uploaded, and why. Absent when there is nothing to say.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp of the last change to this mount

files_MountDeleteUploads.description: With `uploads=wait` or `uploads=discard`, and with `uploads=keep` on a mount served by its backend's shared connection that held files not uploaded yet or open: what became of what was written on the removed mount, or the removed backend's mounts, and not uploaded yet. Absent with `uploads=keep` otherwise.

delivered.description: true: nothing is held open and nothing is left to upload. false: with `wait`, the deadline passed first, or the uploads had already stopped with something left (that is then kept on the server and is not uploaded); with `keep`, files were left: kept on the server as the pending upload `pending_upload_id`, or still uploading through the shared connection, which another mount of the backend or a request to it uses; with `discard`, always.

dirty.description: With `wait` or `keep`, when delivered is false: files written and not uploaded yet. null when that could not be seen in full: a stored record that cannot be read leaves every wait unsure until it is deleted (GET /api/v1/pending-uploads/unreadable).

discarded.description: With `discard`: files deleted without being uploaded. null when that could not be counted, or a stop could not be confirmed; the uploads of that part then go on as with `keep`. A backend DELETE that answers null keeps the backend: repeat it to delete what is left. When repeats stay null, a stored record that cannot be read may be the cause: GET /api/v1/pending-uploads/unreadable lists it.

open_handles.description: With `wait` or `keep`, when delivered is false: files and folders still held open on the mount. null when that could not be seen in full.

pending_upload_id.description: With `keep` on a mount served by its backend's shared connection: the pending upload that keeps what was not uploaded, listed by GET /api/v1/pending-uploads before the answer. Absent when nothing was left, or the files still upload through the connection because another mount or a request to the backend uses it.

files_MountDeleteUploads.title: Mount Delete Uploads

files_MountLimitError.description: An error response. With DEDICATED_VFS_LIMIT, retiring also says how many connections of changed or removed mounts count against the limit.

code.description: The error code, one of those listed for the response. Only some responses carry it; where it is absent, rely on the status and the message.

retiring.description: With DEDICATED_VFS_LIMIT: connections of mounts whose settings were changed or that were removed, kept for files still open on them, that count against the limit

files_MountLimitError.title: Mount Limit Error

files_MountUploads.description: What the mount's running connection holds right now: files written through the mount and not uploaded yet, and files open on it. Present in the answers of GET /api/v1/mounts and GET /api/v1/mounts/{id}. Mounts that use the default settings share one connection per backend, so they report the same values.

dirty.description: Files written and not uploaded yet, the ones uploading included. null when state is unknown.

open_handles.description: Open files, working directories and memory mappings that programs hold on the mount. null when state is unknown.

state.description: idle: nothing waits to upload and nothing is open on the mount. busy: files wait to upload or are uploading, or programs hold files or folders open on the mount. unknown: it could not be seen in full within 3 seconds, or no connection is running for the mount (it is not active, or could not be restored); check again.

files_MountUploads.title: Mount Uploads

files_MoveRequest.description: Request to move a file or directory to a new path

move_to.description: Full destination path, from the serve root. A path without a leading '/' is also taken from the serve root, not from the source's folder.

files_MoveRequest.title: Move Request

files_PathItem.description: Represents a file or directory entry

revisions.description: Number of journal revisions of this file. Absent when the journal holds none for it (a file never changed through Hoody Files, or the journal is off) and for a file on a remote backend

size.description: File size in bytes or number of items in directory

files_PathItem.title: Path Item

files_PendingUpload.description: Unsent upload data of one mount session: files still uploading on their own (state uploading), or held back because they may be incomplete or out of date. The files are listed by GET /api/v1/pending-uploads/{id}/files.

backend_id.description: The backend the files belong to. Absent when that backend no longer exists; the files can still be delivered to another backend with backend_id, downloaded or discarded.

deliverable.description: Whether a delivery with the item's saved connection settings can start now. false when those settings are no longer accepted, or may be any of several backends' (unsettled_backend_ids), so deliver with backend_id instead; when no held file is complete, or while the item is uploading or delivering. An item whose backend was removed still delivers with its saved settings.

incomplete_count.description: Number of files with complete: false, which can only be downloaded or discarded

last_error.description: Why the last delivery ended early, for example not enough disk space to prepare the upload, or uploads that kept failing. Absent when there is none.

mount_id.description: The mount the files were written through. Absent when they do not belong to one mount, or the mount no longer exists.

needs_reconcile.description: Present when the item's last state change could not be saved yet. It is retried every minute and before any action on the item; discard still works. Absent otherwise.

reasons.description: How many files have each reason; see PendingUploadFile.reason

since.description: Unix timestamp since which the item has been in its current state

state.description: uploading: the files are still being uploaded on their own, by uploads that kept running through a service restart or that belong to a mount that was removed or changed, or files are still open on such a mount; stop turns them into a pending item. pending: held, waiting for the caller. delivering: a delivery is running; files leave the item as each one lands, and stop ends it.

unknown_holders.description: Programs that may be using the item's mount and could not be inspected, so its earlier settings cannot be retired: end those programs, or stop the item. Absent when there are none.

pid.description: Program ID

unsettled_backend_ids.description: Present when a switch of the item's saved connection settings to another backend was cut short by a restart or an error: the backends whose settings they may now be. That is why a delivery without backend_id is refused (409, deliverable is false) until a delivery with backend_id installs that backend's settings. A running delivery is stopped by deleting the backend it uploads to with uploads=discard. Absent otherwise.

files_PendingUpload.title: Pending Upload

complete.description: Whether the held copy is known to be whole. Only complete files can be delivered. An incomplete file can be downloaded, with any missing ranges read as zeros, or discarded.

modified_at.description: Unix timestamp of the held copy's last change

path.description: The path relative to the backend root, present only when its bytes are valid UTF-8; exactly those bytes.

path_b64.description: The file's identifier: its path relative to the backend root, as raw bytes in base64url without padding. Every file has one; it is the only way to name a file whose name is not valid UTF-8.

path_display.description: Present when path is absent: the path with each byte that is not valid UTF-8 shown as U+FFFD. For display only; no request accepts it, and it can look the same as another file's path.

reason.description: open_when_stopped: the file was open when its mount stopped and may be incomplete. unconfirmed_at_stop: its mount stopped unexpectedly, so whether the file was complete is not known. metadata_unreadable: its cache record is damaged; download or discard it, it cannot be delivered. upload_failing: its upload kept failing. stopped_by_request: its upload was stopped on request before the file was sent. changed_on_storage: the file changed on the storage since it was cached; deliver or download it to choose. check_failed: the storage could not be checked, so whether the file changed there is not known. cannot_verify: the storage cannot show whether this file changed since it was cached; deliver or download it to choose.

files_PendingUploadsSummary.description: Files written through this mount, or to this backend, that are not uploaded yet: every file of its pending uploads, in any state.
files_PendingUploadsSummary.title: Pending Uploads Summary

files_RenameRequest.description: Request to rename a file or directory
files_RenameRequest.title: Rename Request

files_RenameResponse.description: Result of a rename in the same directory (a JSON body with name)

name.description: The new name, as the request gave it

files_RenameResponse.title: Rename Response

files_UnreadablePendingUpload.description: A stored record of unsent files that cannot be read, so what it holds is unknown. While one exists, a mount or backend DELETE with `uploads=wait` or `uploads=discard` cannot confirm that nothing was left unsent.

reason.description: unreadable: it could not be read. damaged: it was read, and is cut short, damaged, or not one this server wrote.

size.description: The record's size in bytes. Absent when it cannot be seen.

files_UnreadablePendingUpload.title: Unreadable Pending Upload

files_VfsConfig.description: The VFS settings a mount runs with: its own settings where it has them, the defaults elsewhere. Sizes are in bytes, durations in seconds.

allow_non_empty.description: Whether the mount may cover a non-empty directory

allow_other.description: Whether users other than the server's own can use the mount

cache_max_age.description: How long an unused file stays in the local cache, in seconds

cache_max_size.description: Maximum size of the local cache, in bytes. 0 means no limit.

cache_mode.description: How file contents are cached locally

contimeout.description: How long connecting to the backend may take, in seconds. Absent when not set (1 minute).

dir_cache_time.description: How long directory listings are cached, in seconds

low_level_retries.description: How many times one failed request to the backend is retried. Absent when not set (10).

poll_interval.description: How often the backend is checked for changes, in seconds (0: never)

read_chunk_size.description: Size of each read from the backend, in bytes

read_only.description: Whether the mount path refuses writes

timeout.description: How long a transfer with the backend may stay idle before it fails, in seconds. Absent when not set (5 minutes).

write_back.description: Upload delay after a file is closed, in seconds

files_VfsConfig.title: VFS Config

files_VfsConfigPatch.description: VFS settings to change. Each field you send replaces the mount's current value, and fields you omit keep it. Send at least one field.

allow_non_empty.description: Accepted only as false, so a GET response can be sent back unchanged. It cannot be set.

allow_other.description: Accepted only as false, so a GET response can be sent back unchanged. It cannot be set.

cache_max_age.description: How long an unused file stays in the local cache. Seconds as a whole number, or a string such as "30s", "5m" or "1h30m" (units h, m and s; a number without a unit is seconds). Between 0 and 2592000 seconds (30 days). Default for new mounts: 1h.

cache_max_size.description: Maximum size of the local cache. Bytes as a whole number, or a string such as "10G" or "128M" (K, M, G and T are powers of 1024, with an optional trailing B; a string without a unit is bytes). 0 means no limit; otherwise between 1M (1048576) and 9007199254740991 bytes. Default for new mounts: 10G.

cache_mode.description: How file contents are cached locally: off (no cache; a file cannot be opened for reading and writing at once), minimal, writes (files opened for writing), or full. Default for new mounts: writes.

contimeout.description: How long connecting to the backend may take before the attempt fails (1 minute when not set). Seconds as a whole number, or a string such as "30s", "5m" or "1h30m" (units h, m and s; a number without a unit is seconds). Between 1 and 120 seconds (2m).

dir_cache_time.description: How long directory listings are cached. Seconds as a whole number, or a string such as "30s", "5m" or "1h30m" (units h, m and s; a number without a unit is seconds). Between 0 and 2592000 seconds (30 days). Default for new mounts: 5m.

low_level_retries.description: How many times one failed request to the backend is retried before the operation fails: a whole number between 0 and 10. Not set for new mounts: 10 retries.

poll_interval.description: How often the backend is checked for changes, on backends that support it; 0 turns checking off. Seconds as a whole number, or a string such as "30s", "5m" or "1h30m" (units h, m and s; a number without a unit is seconds). Between 0 and 2592000 seconds (30 days). Default for new mounts: 1m.

read_chunk_size.description: Size of each read from the backend. Bytes as a whole number, or a string such as "10G" or "128M" (K, M, G and T are powers of 1024, with an optional trailing B; a string without a unit is bytes). Between 1M (1048576) and 1G (1073741824) bytes. Default for new mounts: 128M.

read_only.description: Refuse writes through the mount path. The backend file API can still write. Default for new mounts: false.

timeout.description: How long a transfer with the backend may stay idle before it fails. A lower value makes reads and uploads fail sooner when the backend stops answering (5 minutes when not set). Seconds as a whole number, or a string such as "30s", "5m" or "1h30m" (units h, m and s; a number without a unit is seconds). Between 1 and 600 seconds (10m).

write_back.description: Upload delay: how long a file written and closed waits before it is uploaded. Seconds as a whole number, or a string such as "30s", "5m" or "1h30m" (units h, m and s; a number without a unit is seconds). Between 0 and 3600 seconds (1h). Default for new mounts: 5s.

files_VfsConfigPatch.title: VFS Config Patch

heap.description: Language runtime heap in bytes (null for Rust)

started.description: Process start time as RFC3339 string

ip.description: IP address of the connecting client, or `unknown`.

details.description: Detailed error message (especially in development mode)

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, when the error has one (see the response's `x-error-codes`)

message.description: Human-readable explanation, when the error has one

id.description: Notification ID. IDs are assigned per display, so the same ID can appear on two displays; identify a notification by `display_id` plus `id`.

display_id.description: Display the notification was shown on. Written by the desktop notification daemon, so it can be a number (`1`) or a string (`"1"` or `":1"`). Omitted when the source record has none.

appname.description: Name of the application that triggered the notification

summary.description: Notification summary/title

body.description: Notification body text

message.example: Focus or Open a Window: Click to focus the window

icon_url.description: Relative URL to the notification icon

has_icon.description: Whether the notification has an icon

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the notification was created

timeout.description: Expiry timeout the notification was sent with, in milliseconds. `-1` means the notification server's default, `0` means it never expires. `0` when the source record has none.

progress.description: Progress value (0-100) for progress notifications, `0` when not set

urgency.description: Urgency level, upper-cased as stored by the notification daemon. `NORMAL` when the source record has none.

stack_tag.description: Stacking tag the sender set to replace an earlier notification in place, when set

default_action_key.description: Key of the default action, when the notification has one

actions.description: Action buttons attached to the notification

notifications_Notification.description: A desktop notification read from the notification history. Unrecognised fields in the source record are passed through unchanged.

body.description: Notification body, up to 1000 characters by default; longer is rejected with 400, never truncated. No NUL byte. Tabs, newlines and carriage returns are kept; other ASCII control characters are removed, and a non-empty body that becomes empty that way is rejected.
body.example: This is a test message from the API.

category.description: Notification category, at most 50 characters. Rejected when it contains a NUL byte or is empty once control characters are removed.

display.description: Target display, `"1"` or `":1"`, from 1 to 40000. Display 0 in any spelling (`0`, `:0`, `00`) and numbers above 40000 are rejected with 400. At most 5 digits; leading zeros are allowed (`"0001"` is display 1).

expire_time.description: Expiry timeout in milliseconds, 0-300000 (0 = never expires). Sent as notify-send `-t`.

icon.description: Icon name or path, at most 1024 characters. No NUL byte. ASCII control characters other than tab, newline and carriage return are removed; a non-empty value that becomes empty that way is rejected with 400.

summary.description: Notification title, 1 to 200 characters by default; longer is rejected, never truncated. Must contain something other than control characters and no NUL byte.

urgency.description: Notification urgency level (lower-case on input; history reports it upper-cased)

notifications_NotificationAction.description: An action button attached to the desktop notification.

key.description: Action identifier sent back when the action is invoked

text.description: User-facing button label

notifications_PushSubscriptionSummary.description: A stored push subscription, redacted: the browser keys and the full endpoint URL are never returned.

endpointHost.description: Host of the browser's push service

origin.description: Origin of the page that subscribed; alert links open there

displays.description: `"all"`, or the display numbers this device receives

userAgent.description: Browser label given at subscribe time (at most 200 characters)

lastSuccessAt.description: Last time the push service accepted a message (Unix ms)

lastFailureStatus.description: HTTP status of the last failed delivery; null for a network error or timeout

consecutiveFailures.description: Failed deliveries since the last success. While non-zero the device is in a cooldown (1 minute after the last failure, doubling per further failure, at most 1 hour): alerts that reach it during the cooldown are skipped and never replayed (history keeps them). A success ends the cooldown; a test push ignores it.

replaced.description: The record of `replacesEndpoint` now holds this endpoint

code.description: Machine-readable error code. The codes each status can carry are listed in that response's x-error-codes.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

exists.description: True when an entry already exists at the path. 409 only; absent when the file could not be created safely.

path.description: The path parameter as sent.

kv_table.description: The kv_table parameter (default kv_store). Present even when init_kv is false, in which case no KV table was created.

path.description: The path parameter as sent (the server-resolved path is not disclosed).

size.description: Size of the new database file in bytes.

tables.description: Tables created: always _query_history, plus the KV table and its _history table when init_kv is true.

is_valid.description: Whether the file starts with a SQLite header.

mod_unix.description: Last modification time as Unix seconds.

path.description: Full path of the file.

size_str.description: File size in human-readable form (for example "4.0 KB").

databases.description: The matching files, newest first, or null when nothing matches.

code.description: INTERNAL_ERROR or DELETE_INCOMPLETE.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

files_removed.description: DELETE_INCOMPLETE only: files removed before the failure (sidecars; the database file itself is always still in place).
Number of files removed: the database itself plus any -wal, -shm or -journal file beside it.

path.description: The db parameter as sent (the server-resolved path is not disclosed).

code.description: Machine-readable error code. The codes each status can carry are listed in that response's x-error-codes.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

directory_mode.description: The separate cache of open directory-mode KV stores.

max_size.description: Capacity of the connection cache. Size can exceed it while every entry is in use.

size.description: Number of open databases held in the connection cache.

held.description: Stores in use by a request right now; these cannot be evicted.

max_size.description: Capacity of the directory-mode cache. Size can exceed it while every entry is in use.

size.description: Number of directory-mode stores held open.

heap.description: Always null: heap size is not measured.

built.description: Modification time of the server binary (RFC 3339), or null when it cannot be read. Verbose only.

cache.description: Cache snapshot, the same object GET /health/cache returns. Verbose only.

counters.description: Operational counters and gauges keyed by name. New names may be added. Verbose only.

fds.description: Number of open file descriptors, or null when it cannot be read. Verbose only.

features.description: API features this server supports, for clients that talk to servers of different versions. New names may be added. Verbose only. kv_etag: ETags on KV reads and writes; kv_conditional_writes: If-Match / If-None-Match on KV writes and batch item conditions; kv_conditional_reads: If-None-Match (304) on KV reads; kv_entry: GET /kv/{key}/entry; kv_ttl_controls: POST /kv/{key}/expire and /persist; kv_idempotency: Idempotency-Key on KV writes; kv_changes: the change feed (/changes, /changes/stream); kv_list_cursor: after / next_after paging of GET /kv; retry_after: Retry-After on retryable failures.

ip.description: The caller's IP address as the server sees it. Verbose only.

memory.description: Process memory, or null when it cannot be read. Verbose only.

pid.description: Server process ID. Verbose only.

started.description: When the server started (RFC 3339). Verbose only.

status.description: Always "ok" when the server answers.

userAgent.description: The caller's User-Agent header, or null when none was sent. Verbose only.

avg_exec_time_ms.description: Mean execution time of the stored entries in milliseconds, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when there are none.

failure_count.description: Stored entries that failed or were rolled back.

last_hour.description: Entries recorded in the last hour.

last_minute.description: Entries recorded in the last 60 seconds.

total_queries.description: Number of history entries stored for the database (the server keeps the most recent 1000).

current_etag.description: Its current ETag; null when the key does not exist or has expired. An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

deleted.description: Number of keys that existed and were deleted.

results.description: One entry per requested key, keyed by the key: null when the key does not exist or has expired.

content_type.description: The content type stored with the value. Absent when error is set.

error.description: Why this key could not be read; the other fields are absent. The other keys are still answered.

etag.description: The key's ETag, as GET /kv/{key} sends it. Absent when error is set, and when the server could not verify the table's versions (database busy). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

value.description: The value, parsed, when its content type is JSON and it parses; null for a stored JSON null. Absent otherwise.

value_base64.description: The value as base64, when its content type is not JSON or it does not parse as JSON. Absent otherwise.

code.description: PRECONDITION_FAILED.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the batch. An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

items.description: One entry per item, in request order, with the key's ETag after the batch. A key may repeat only in a batch without conditions (both entries then carry the final ETag); when any item has if_match or if_none_match, a repeated key is refused with 400 INVALID_PARAMETERS.

code.description: CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED or CHANGE_CURSOR_INVALID.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

reason.description: Why the cursor is no longer valid.

content_type.description: include_values only: the content type of value / value_base64.

cursor.description: Cursor of this event: resume after it with since (or Last-Event-ID).

etag.description: ETag of the row after this change (set/ttl only): matches the ETag a read returns while the row is unchanged. An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

expire_at.description: Expiry the row has after the change (set/ttl), Unix seconds; null when it does not expire and for delete/expire. Clients must treat the row as gone from this time.

op.description: set: the row was written (created or replaced); ttl: only its expiry changed; delete: the row was removed; expire: an expired row was removed.

seq.description: Position of the event in the database's change log.

ts.description: When the change was made, Unix seconds.

value.description: include_values only: the value, parsed, for JSON content that parses: any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean or null).

value_base64.description: include_values only: the value as base64 when it is not JSON content.

value_omitted.description: include_values only: why no value is attached. superseded: the row changed again (or is gone) since this event; expired: the row has expired; too_large: the value is over 256 KiB. Read GET /kv/{key}/entry for the current value.

cursor.description: The newest position of the change log when the page was read. Without since, start from here.

events.description: Matching events after since, in log order. Empty without since (bootstrap).

has_more.description: true when more changes are already available after next_cursor.

next_cursor.description: Where to continue: pass as since. The position scanned, which can be past the last event when later changes did not match prefix.

oldest_cursor.description: The oldest cursor still accepted; older ones get 410 CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the write (also sent as the ETag header). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

path.description: The path that was changed. Present only when path was sent.

value.description: The value after the change; with path, the nested value.

deleted.description: Always true on a 200 (a missing key is a 404).

directory_mode.description: Always true when present. Directory mode only.

change_type.description: What happened to the key between the two timestamps.

from_content_type.description: The content type at from. deleted and modified only.

from_value.description: The value at from, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses; null for a stored JSON null. deleted and modified only.

from_value_base64.description: The value at from as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON; an empty string for an empty value. deleted and modified only.

new_expire_at.description: When the key is set to expire at to, Unix seconds. created and modified only, and absent when the key has no TTL at to.

old_expire_at.description: When the key was set to expire at from, Unix seconds. deleted and modified only, and absent when the key had no TTL at from.

operations_between.description: The recorded writes after the one that set the from value, up to and including the one that set the to value, oldest first. modified only, and absent when there are none.

to_content_type.description: The content type at to. created and modified only.

to_value.description: The value at to, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses; null for a stored JSON null. created and modified only.

to_value_base64.description: The value at to as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON; an empty string for an empty value. created and modified only.

checkpoint.description: True on a SET that a rollback recorded rather than a client wrote: it keeps the value the rollback restored readable by time travel, and its old and new value are that same value. Absent otherwise.

delta.description: The signed change the INCR or DECR applied: positive for INCR, negative for DECR (a DECR of 5 is recorded as -5). History written by earlier versions, which accepted a zero or negative delta, may hold zero or the opposite sign. null for every other operation.

operation.description: The recorded operation: SET, DELETE, INCR, DECR, PUSH, POP or REMOVE, or UNRECORDED for the record that a write made with history=false touched the key, which carries no value.

path.description: The JSON path the operation targeted; empty for the whole value.

timestamp.description: When the operation was recorded, Unix seconds.

candidate_truncated.description: True when the candidate-key scan stopped at its internal cap, so changed keys may be missing without appearing in gap_keys; name the keys with keys to get a complete answer for them. Always false when keys is given.

changes.description: One entry per key that was created, modified or deleted between the two timestamps. Unchanged keys are only counted in stats. null when nothing changed.

from_timestamp.description: The requested from timestamp, Unix seconds.

gap_keys.description: Keys left out of changes because a write made with history=false leaves their value at either timestamp unknown. null when has_gaps is false, a non-empty array when it is true.

to_timestamp.description: The requested to timestamp, Unix seconds.

created.description: Keys absent at from and present at to.

deleted.description: Keys present at from and absent at to.

modified.description: Keys present at both timestamps whose value or content type differs.

unchanged.description: Keys present at both timestamps with the same value and content type. Keys absent at both are not counted.

content_type.description: The content type stored with the value.

created_at.description: When the key was created, Unix seconds.

etag.description: The key's ETag (also sent as the ETag header). Null when the server could not verify the key's version (database busy); retry for a tag. An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

expire_at.description: When the key expires, Unix seconds; null when it has no TTL.

updated_at.description: When the key was last written, Unix seconds.

value.description: The value, parsed, when its content type is JSON and it parses; null for a stored JSON null. Absent otherwise.

value_base64.description: The value as base64, when its content type is not JSON or it does not parse as JSON; an empty string for an empty value. Absent otherwise.

operation.description: The recorded operation.

checkpoint.description: True on a SET that a rollback recorded rather than a client wrote: it keeps the value the rollback restored readable by time travel, and its old and new value are that same value. Absent otherwise.

created_key.description: True when an INCR, DECR or PUSH created the key, which did not exist just before. Absent otherwise.

delta.description: The signed change the INCR or DECR applied: positive for INCR, negative for DECR (a DECR of 5 is recorded as -5). History written by earlier versions, which accepted a zero or negative delta, may hold zero or the opposite sign. null for every other operation.

has_new_value.description: True when new_value holds the value after the operation, a JSON null included. Only on history written by earlier versions; absent otherwise.

has_old_value.description: True when old_value holds the value before the operation, a JSON null included. Only on history written by earlier versions; absent otherwise.

has_raw_new_value.description: True when the entry records the value after the operation in raw_new_value. Absent otherwise.

has_raw_old_value.description: True when the entry records the value before the operation in raw_old_value. Absent otherwise.

new_content_type.description: Content type of the value after the operation. Absent when the entry records none; a recorded value without one is JSON.

new_expire_at.description: When the key is set to expire after the operation, Unix seconds. Absent when it has no TTL.

new_value.description: The value after the operation, parsed. null on what this server records, which keeps that value in raw_new_value; set only on history written by earlier versions.

old_content_type.description: Content type of the value before the operation. Absent when the entry records none; a recorded value without one is JSON.

old_expire_at.description: When the key was set to expire before the operation, Unix seconds. Absent when it had no TTL.

old_value.description: The value before the operation, parsed. null on what this server records, which keeps that value in raw_old_value; set only on history written by earlier versions.

op.description: The recorded operation: SET, DELETE, INCR, DECR, PUSH, POP or REMOVE, or UNRECORDED for the record that a write made with history=false touched the key, which carries no value.

path.description: The JSON path the operation targeted; empty for the whole value.

popped_value.description: The element a POP removed; null for every other operation.

raw_new_value.description: The value after the operation, base64, byte for byte as it was stored. Absent when the operation left no value (DELETE, UNRECORDED), and when that value is empty (has_raw_new_value is then true).

raw_old_value.description: The value before the operation, base64, byte for byte as it was stored. Absent when the key did not exist before the operation, and when that value was empty (has_raw_old_value is then true).

removed_index.description: The array index of the element a REMOVE removed; null for every other operation.

removed_value.description: The element a REMOVE removed; null for every other operation.

timestamp.description: When the operation was recorded, Unix seconds. On an UNRECORDED entry, the first untracked write it covers.
