unrecorded_until.description: On an UNRECORDED entry, when the last untracked write it covers happened, Unix seconds: the key's value is unknown from timestamp to unrecorded_until. Absent otherwise.

operations.description: The key's recorded operations, newest first (highest op_number first), at most limit of them.

content_type.description: The content type the value had after that operation.

value.description: The value, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses; null for a stored JSON null. Absent otherwise.

value_base64.description: The value as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON. Absent otherwise.

content_type.description: The content type. In regular mode, the one stored with the value; in directory mode, derived from the file extension; in at_timestamp mode, the one the value had at the timestamp, application/json when none was recorded.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix seconds. Regular and directory mode only; in directory mode it is the file modification time.

etag.description: The entry's current ETag, the same value GET /kv/{key} sends; usable in If-Match. Regular mode only; absent when the page was read without versions (change_cursor is null then). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

existed_at_timestamp.description: Always true: only keys that existed at the timestamp are listed. at_timestamp mode only.

expire_at.description: Expiry time, Unix seconds. Regular mode only, and present only when the key has a TTL.

op_number.description: History operation number of the write that set the value seen at the timestamp; 0 when the key has no recorded history and its current value is reported. at_timestamp mode only.

size.description: Size of the stored value; in directory mode, the file size in bytes. Regular and directory mode only.

size_estimate.description: Approximate size: the size of the recorded history entry for that write, or of the current value when the current value is reported. Not the exact size of the value. at_timestamp mode only.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix seconds. Regular and directory mode only; in directory mode it is the file modification time.

candidate_truncated.description: True when the candidate-key scan stopped at its internal cap, so keys may be missing from items without appearing in gap_keys; narrow the request with prefix to get a complete listing. at_timestamp mode only, where it is always present.

change_cursor.description: Change-feed cursor read in the same snapshot as items: pass it as since to GET /changes or /changes/stream to receive every write made after this page was read. Regular mode only, where it is always present; null when the page was read without versions (the database was busy).

directory_mode.description: Always true when present. Directory mode only.

gap_keys.description: Keys left out of items because a write made with history=false leaves their state at the timestamp unknown. at_timestamp mode only, where it is always present: null when has_gaps is false, a non-empty array when it is true.

has_gaps.description: True when gap_keys is non-empty. at_timestamp mode only, where it is always present.

has_more.description: True when at least one more key follows this page. Regular and directory mode only, where it is always present.

items.description: The page of keys, or null. In regular mode an empty page is always null. In directory and at_timestamp mode it is null only when no key matches at all; an offset past the end of a non-empty listing gives an empty array.

limit.description: The page size applied, after the 1000 cap. Regular and directory mode only; absent in at_timestamp mode.

next_after.description: Cursor for the next page: pass it as after. The last key this page covered (a key left out of items because it could not be read, or whose file vanished in directory mode, still counts), or null when no key follows. With limit=0 it echoes after, null when after was not given. Regular and directory mode only, where it is always present.

scan_errors.description: Rows that could not be read and were left out of items. Regular mode only, and present only when at least one row was left out.

timestamp.description: The requested at_timestamp. at_timestamp mode only.

total.description: Number of keys matching prefix before pagination. Directory mode only.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the write (also sent as the ETag header). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

length.description: Number of elements left in the array.

path.description: The path of the array. Present only when path was sent.

value.description: The element removed from the end of the array; any JSON value, null included.

code.description: PRECONDITION_FAILED. Absent on a failed PUT compare-and-swap (the if_match parameter).

current_etag.description: The key's current ETag; null when the key does not exist or has expired. Absent on a failed PUT compare-and-swap. An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the write (also sent as the ETag header). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

length.description: Number of elements in the array after the append.

path.description: The path of the array. Present only when path was sent.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the write (also sent as the ETag header). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

length.description: Number of elements left in the array.

path.description: The path of the array. Present only when path was sent.

removed.description: The element that was removed; any JSON value, null included.

directory_mode.description: Always true when present. Directory mode only.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the write (also sent as the ETag header). SQLite mode only. An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file that holds the value. Directory mode only.

path.description: The path that was set. Present only when path was sent.

size.description: Size of the stored value in bytes. With path, the size of the whole updated value.

content_type.description: The content type the value had at the timestamp.

op_number.description: History operation number of the write that set this value; 0 when no recorded write establishes it and the current value is reported.

value.description: The value at the timestamp, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses; null for a stored JSON null. Absent otherwise.

value_base64.description: The value at the timestamp as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON; an empty string for an empty value. Absent otherwise.

candidate_truncated.description: True when the candidate-key scan stopped at its internal cap, so keys may be missing from keys without appearing in gap_keys; narrow the request with prefix to get a complete view.

gap_keys.description: Keys left out of keys because a write made with history=false leaves their value at the timestamp unknown. null when has_gaps is false, a non-empty array when it is true.

keys.description: The keys that existed at the timestamp with their values, ordered by key and cut to limit. null when none did.

snapshot_time.description: The requested timestamp as an RFC 3339 UTC string.

timestamp.description: The requested timestamp, Unix seconds.

total_keys_at_snapshot.description: Number of keys that existed at the timestamp before limit was applied.

etag.description: The key's ETag after the change (also sent as the ETag header). An opaque strong entity tag, double quotes included.

expire_at.description: When the key now expires, Unix seconds; null when it has no TTL.

action.description: rollback: the value is set back; delete: the key is removed; restore: the key is recreated.

current_content_type.description: Content type of the current value (rollback and delete).

current_value.description: The current value, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses (rollback and delete).

current_value_base64.description: The current value as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON (rollback and delete).

operations_to_undo.description: Operations that would be undone on this key; 0 for delete and restore.

reason.description: Why the key changes; set on delete.

rollback_content_type.description: Content type of the value at to_timestamp (rollback and restore).

rollback_value.description: The value at to_timestamp, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses (rollback and restore).

rollback_value_base64.description: The value at to_timestamp as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON (rollback and restore).

changes.description: One entry per key that would change, or null when none would.

discovery_truncated.description: True when key discovery stopped at its scan limit, so keys may be missing from this preview; a real run would be refused with 413.

keys_to_delete.description: Keys that would be deleted because they did not exist at to_timestamp.

keys_to_restore.description: Keys that would be recreated because they existed at to_timestamp and are gone now.

keys_to_rollback.description: Keys whose value would be set back.

operations_to_reverse.description: Operations that would be undone across the keys set back.

untouched_keys.description: Keys with nothing to roll back (their history holds only writes made with history=false, and they no longer exist).

deleted.description: Real run only: keys deleted because they did not exist at to_timestamp.

duration_ms.description: Real run only: time the rollback took, in milliseconds.

preview.description: Dry run only: what a real run would change.

restored.description: Real run only: keys recreated because they existed at to_timestamp and are gone now.

rolled_back.description: Real run only: keys whose value was set back.

total_operations_reversed.description: Real run only: operations undone across the rolled-back keys.

untouched_keys.description: Real run only: keys with nothing to roll back (their history holds only writes made with history=false, and they no longer exist).

content_type.description: The content type the value had at the timestamp.

op_number.description: History operation number of the write that set the value; 0 when no recorded write establishes it and the current value is reported. Absent when the key has no recorded history at all.

op_timestamp.description: Time of that write, Unix seconds; 0 when op_number is 0. Absent when op_number is absent.

timestamp.description: The requested at_timestamp, Unix seconds.

value.description: The value, parsed, when it is JSON content that parses; null for a stored JSON null. Absent otherwise.

value_base64.description: The value as base64, when it is not JSON content or does not parse as JSON; an empty string for an empty value. Absent otherwise.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. The codes each status can carry are listed in that response's x-error-codes.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

reqIdx.description: -1 when present: the error concerns the whole request. Some errors, such as an expired request deadline, leave it out.

op.description: The operation that ran, as requested.

result.description: "ok" when the operation completed; for quick_check, the first result row ("ok" on a healthy database, otherwise the first problem found).

error.description: The error message of a failed entry; absent on success.

id.description: Entry ID. Pass it as {index} to DELETE /api/v1/sqlite/history/{index}.

is_statement.description: True for a statement (a write), false for a query (a read).

source.description: "kv" or "sql"

sql.description: The SQL that ran; for source kv, the statement the KV operation ran.

timestamp.description: When the query ran (RFC 3339).

count.description: Number of entries in this page.

entries.description: The same page as history (kept for older clients).

history.description: The page of entries, newest first, or null when the page is empty.

limit.description: The page size applied, after the default and the 1000 cap.

total.description: Number of entries stored for the database (at most about 1000), independent of limit and offset.

columns.description: Column keys, in result order. A repeated column name (any `SELECT *` over a join) is renamed `name:N` (N = its occurrence number) so every key in a row is distinct; these are the keys each resultSet row uses.

query.description: The SQL that ran: the sql parameter, decoded when it was base64url.

resultSet.description: One object per row, keyed by the names in columns, or null when the query returned no rows. Values are JSON scalars: TEXT and UTF-8-valid BLOBs are strings, a BLOB that is not valid UTF-8 is an object {"value_base64": "<standard base64>"}, INTEGER and REAL are numbers (an INTEGER beyond 2^53 loses precision in JavaScript), NULL is null.

truncated.description: True when the result was cut off at 10000 rows; narrow the query (WHERE / LIMIT / OFFSET) to read the rest.

if_match.description: Delete this key only if its current ETag is one of these (a comma-separated list of strong entity-tags, as in the If-Match header), or "*" for "the key exists". Checked for every item before any key is deleted; one failure fails the whole batch with 412.

key.description: Key to delete. Must not be empty or whitespace-only.

items.description: Keys to delete, each with an optional if_match condition. 1-100 entries. Send keys or items, not both.

keys.description: Keys to delete. 1-100 entries; no entry may be empty or whitespace-only. Send keys or items, not both.
Keys to retrieve. 1-100 entries; no entry may be empty or whitespace-only.

content_type.description: Content type recorded alongside the value. Defaults to application/octet-stream.

if_match.description: Write this item only if the key exists and its current ETag is one of these (a comma-separated list of strong entity-tags, as in the If-Match header), or "*" for "the key exists". Checked for every item before any is written; one failure fails the whole batch with 412.

if_none_match.description: "*" to write this item only if the key does not exist (or has expired). Any other value is rejected with 400. Checked for every item before any is written; one failure fails the whole batch with 412.

key.description: Key to write. Must not be empty or whitespace-only.

ttl.description: Lifetime in seconds from now. 0 or omitted stores without expiry; negative is rejected.

value.description: Value to store.

items.description: Items to write in a single transaction. 1-100 entries.

value.description: Remove the first element equal to this value. Any JSON value; an explicit null removes the first null element, which is not the same as leaving value out. Ignored when the index parameter is set. Without index, value is required.

exclude_keys.description:
Keys to leave untouched. Applied after keys.
At most 10000 entries; more is rejected with 413.

keys.description:
Keys to roll back. Omit or leave empty to roll back the whole table.
At most 10000 entries; more is rejected with 413.

dest_path.description:
Destination file for vacuum_into. Required for that operation and
ignored by the others. Jailed like the db parameter, and it must not
already exist.

src_path.description:
Source file for restore: an existing SQLite database, such as a
vacuum_into copy. Required for that operation and ignored by the
others. Jailed like the db parameter, and it must not be the database
itself. It is only read.

resultFormat.description: Row format for query results: "list" (any case) returns each row as an array in column order (resultSetList); any other value, or none, returns one object per row keyed by column name (resultSet).

transaction.description: The statements to run, in order; at least one.

query.description: SQL that returns rows (SELECT, WITH, PRAGMA, ... RETURNING). The item answers resultHeaders and resultSet (or resultSetList).

statement.description: SQL statement to execute (preferred field). What the item answers depends on what the SQL produces, not on its text: SQL that produces result columns (SELECT, WITH, PRAGMA, VALUES, EXPLAIN, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ... RETURNING) answers its rows exactly like `query` (resultHeaders, resultSet or resultSetList, truncated, the same row cap and response size limit); SQL that produces none answers rowsUpdated. With valuesBatch the statement never returns rows, only rowsUpdatedBatch. An item holding several `;`-separated statements runs them in order, each to the end, and answers for the last one: its rows, or its rowsUpdated.

values.description: Bind parameters for the statement: a JSON array for positional (?) parameters, or a JSON object for named (:name) parameters. Elements must be JSON scalars (string, number, boolean, null); numbers must fit int64/float64 (else 400). A nested array or object cannot be bound: the request fails with 400 SQL_BIND_ERROR, or, for an item with noFail, that item reports the error and the rest of the request goes on. The values must fit the statement: an array holds one entry per positional slot (each ? takes the next slot, ?NNN and $NNN name slot NNN), an object one key per distinct name. A missing or surplus entry or key fails the same way, before the item runs.

valuesBatch.description: Batch bind parameters: one entry per execution of the statement; each entry follows the same rules as `values`. With noFail, an entry that does not fit the statement is skipped and named in rowErrors, and the other entries run.

params.description: Alias for `values`. Sending both is accepted when they hold the same value; different contents are refused with 400 VALUES_CONFLICT, and an explicit null counts as a value.

sqlite_main.requestItem.description: One transaction item: SQL in `query` or `statement` (alias `sql`), exactly one of them; bind values in `values` (alias `params`) or `valuesBatch`; and `noFail`. Any other key is refused with 400 UNKNOWN_FIELD.

code.description: Machine-readable code for error; present only on items that failed under noFail=true.

resultHeaders.description: Column names of resultSet / resultSetList, for a query, or a statement whose SQL produces result columns. Absent for a statement whose SQL produces no result columns.

resultSet.description: Query items, and statement items whose SQL produces result columns (SELECT, WITH, PRAGMA, RETURNING; with several statements, the last one), default result format: one object per row, keyed by column name (a repeated column name is renamed name:N, as in resultHeaders). Values are JSON scalars; a BLOB is a base64 string. Empty when the query returned no rows. Absent for a statement whose SQL produces no result columns.

resultSetList.description: The same items with resultFormat "list": one array per row, values in column order.

rowErrors.description: valuesBatch statements under noFail=true: one message per row that failed to parse and was skipped. With success=true, the other rows ran. Absent when every row parsed.

rowsUpdated.description: Rows changed, for a statement whose SQL produces no result columns (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE without RETURNING, DDL). With several statements in one item, the last one's count.

rowsUpdatedBatch.description: Rows changed by each valuesBatch row, in order. A batched statement never returns result rows.

truncated.description: True when the result was cut off at 10000 rows; narrow the query (WHERE / LIMIT / OFFSET) to read the rest.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. The codes each status can carry are listed in that response's x-error-codes.

error.description: Human-readable description of the failure. Not a contract: match on code.

reqIdx.description: Index of the transaction item that failed, or -1 for a request-level error.

type.description: Mouse event kind. `click` expands to down/up; `scroll` uses wheel buttons.

button.description: Mouse button. Non-scroll events accept 1-3; scroll accepts 4-5.

amount.description: Scroll repeat count for scroll events.

direction.description: Optional scroll direction; overrides the scroll button.

modifiers.description: Keyboard modifiers applied to the mouse event.

watch_CreateWatcherRequest.description:
Create a watcher. Only `paths` is required. A field the service does not
know (a misspelt option such as `recursiv`) is refused with 400
`INVALID_REQUEST` naming it, as on update, rather than ignored.

coalesce_ms.description: Coalescing window in milliseconds. A smaller value is raised to 10.

exclude.description: Optional exclude glob patterns. Excludes take precedence over includes.

history_size.description: Replay history capacity for this watcher. A smaller value is raised to 32.

ignore_dirs.description:
Directory names or subdirectory paths to skip entirely (no inotify watches, no scanning).
Supports simple names ("node_modules") and compound paths ("ibus/bus").
Omitted, the server's default list applies, which unless the server sets another is:
`node_modules`, `.git`, `target`, `__pycache__`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.cache`, `dist`,
`.next`, `.nuxt`, `vendor`, `bower_components`. Build-output folders such as `dist`
are skipped by default: pass `[]` to turn the list off, or a list of your own. Hidden
directories are also skipped while `skip_hidden` is true.

include.description:
Optional include glob patterns. If non-empty, a path must match one include;
omitted or `[]` means no include filter.

paths.description: Absolute or relative filesystem paths to watch.

recursive.description: Recursive mode. Defaults to server config value.

skip_hidden.description:
When true, hidden directories (dot-prefixed basenames, e.g. `.git`,
`.cache`, `.venv`) are never watched or scanned into: no inotify watches
are placed inside them. Hidden *files* in visible directories still emit
events. Defaults to the server's `--default-skip-hidden` (false unless
configured). Note: this governs whether we watch/scan *into* hidden
directories; a single create/rename/remove event *about* a hidden
directory itself may still flow. A directory renamed from a visible name
to a hidden name while watched retains its existing watch (same limitation
as `ignore_dirs`).

next_after_id.description:
When `has_more`: pass as `after_id` to fetch the next page. A decimal
event id.

total.description: Events matching the request's cursor now (all pages, not this page).

details.description: Details, mainly for overflow and error events. Omitted when there are none.

is_dir.description: Whether the path is a directory. Omitted when not known.

new_size_bytes.description: Current file size in bytes. Omitted when not known.

old_path.description: Old path for rename events. Omitted on other events and when not known.

old_size_bytes.description: Previous file size in bytes. Omitted when not known.

path.description: New/current path for the event.

watch_UpdateWatcherRequest.description:
Reconfigure a live watcher. Every field is optional; an omitted field keeps
the watcher's current value, but at least one field must be given. The
watcher keeps its id, its replay history and its connected SSE/WebSocket
clients. Reconfiguration preserves replay history, except that lowering
`history_size` evicts retained events beyond the new capacity (minimum 32).
Later replay returns 409 `HISTORY_GAP` if an event strictly after the
requested cursor was evicted or could not be retained; `since_id=0` always
returns retained history without a gap.

coalesce_ms.description: Coalescing window in milliseconds. A smaller value is raised to 10.

exclude.description: Replacement exclude globs. `[]` removes every exclude filter.

history_size.description:
Replay history capacity. A smaller value is raised to 32. Growing keeps
every retained event; shrinking drops only the oldest events beyond the
new cap.

ignore_dirs.description: Replacement ignore list. `[]` disables it; omit to keep the current list.

include.description: Replacement include globs. `[]` removes every include filter.

kinds.description: Replacement event kind filter. `[]` accepts every kind.

paths.description: Replacement path list (non-empty). Omit to keep the current paths.

watch_WatchEventKind.description:
What changed. Writes, including writes through a shared memory mapping,
are `modified`; opening a file for writing and closing it unchanged may
also report `modified`. Opening, reading or listing a file or directory
(and a read-only close) is not reported. `modified` and `metadata` are
reported only for a path that exists when the event is processed, so a
write or close through a descriptor that outlives the file's name is not
reported. A change may be reported as only the `removed` or `renamed`
that follows it, when the file, or a directory above it, is removed or
renamed away before the change is processed. `overflow` means events were
lost (backend queue overflow or stream saturation); the service then rescans
the watched paths, but does not replay the lost changes. `other` is
reserved for a backend event that fits no other kind; the Linux backend
produces none.

oneOf.description: A managed entry.

allOf.description:
A job line written by hand: it runs, but has no id and is not managed
here.

oneOf.description:
A job line written by hand: it runs, but has no id and is not managed
here.

cron_AllEntriesResponse.description:
The managed entries and hand-written job lines of every user
(`GET /entries`). Comment and environment lines, and job lines whose
schedule or command cannot be read, are only counted.

entries.description:
The page of managed entries and hand-written job lines, by user name,
then in crontab order.

job_lines.description:
Job lines written by hand that are not listed because their schedule
or command could not be read. They may still run.

other_lines.description:
Environment assignment and comment lines in the crontabs read, which
are never returned.

unreadable_users.description:
Users whose crontab could not be read or used: their entries are
missing from the list (read the user's entries for the reason).

cron_CronDaemonState.description: Whether the system cron daemon, which runs the crontabs, is running.

cron_CronImpl.description: Which cron daemon runs the crontabs.

cron_CronInfoResponse.description: The service's time zone, cron daemon, run reports and run history.

booted_at.description: When the computer started (`@reboot` entries run then); null when unknown.

features.description:
What this service offers: `entries_all` (`GET /entries`), `next_runs`
(the timing fields of entries), `runs` (`GET /api/v1/cron/runs`),
`history_persisted` (runs kept on disk now), `describe`
(`POST /schedule/describe`), `run_now` (`POST .../run`, receipts at
`GET /api/v1/cron/runs?key=`), `entry_revision` (`revision` and
`expected_revision`), `raw_parse` (hand-written job lines listed by
`GET /entries`).

history_persisted.description: Whether runs are kept on disk, so `GET /api/v1/cron/runs` keeps them across restarts.

history_since.description: Since when the run history on disk was kept; null when it is not.

reports_since.description: Since when run reports are received; null when `report_listener` is off.

timezone.description:
IANA name of the system time zone, which crontab times are read in;
null when the system does not name it.

utc_offset_seconds.description: The system zone's offset from UTC now, in seconds.

cron_CronRun.description: One run of a managed job, from the reports its crontab line sends.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status; null while running and for a lost run.

key.description:
The Idempotency-Key of the request that started a manual run; null for
a timer run.

pid.description: Process id of the job's shell.

oneOf.description:
Only with `key`: the Run now receipt of that key (`state: unknown` for
a key the service does not hold).

cron_CronRunStatus.description:
Where a run is: `running` until its line reports the end (`finished`), or
until its shell exits without that report (`lost`).

cron_CronRunTrigger.description:
What started a run: the cron daemon at a scheduled time (`timer`), or a
request to run the entry now (`manual`).

oneOf.description: The latest reported run of the entry, or null.

next_runs.description:
The next times the entry runs (at most 3, soonest first), in the
system time zone with its offset. null when it has no next time: it is
paused, it runs at reboot only, its schedule never fires, it expires
first, or it runs under its own time zone (`tz_override`). Around a
daylight saving change these follow Vixie cron's rule (`GET /api/v1/cron/info`
`cron_impl: vixie`; another cron may differ there): a skipped fixed
time runs right after the change and a repeated one runs once, while
a schedule with `*` in its minute or hour follows the clock.

recent_due.description:
The latest times the entry was due (at most 5, newest first, none
later than now and none at or after `expires_at`), computed like
`next_runs` and null in the same cases except expiry. Compare them
with the runs reported (`GET /api/v1/cron/runs`) to see whether a run was
reported for a time. They follow from the schedule alone, so a new
entry already lists due times from before it was created.

revision.description:
SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of what the entry runs as (see
`ManagedEntryResponse.revision`).

revision_seen_at.description:
When the service first saw the entry as it is now: its stored lines
and the environment assignments above it. A change made outside the
service moves it too. For an entry already there when the service
started, the service's start time.

run_reports.description:
Whether the entry's runs are reported (`GET /api/v1/cron/runs`, `job_*` events):
its line carries the run report, which an enabled entry under a POSIX
`SHELL` gets.

tz_override.description:
A `CRON_TZ` or `TZ` assignment above the entry may give it another
time zone than the system's, so `next_runs` and `recent_due` are null
and `warnings` says why.

warnings.description:
Present when the schedule is valid but can never fire, or when
the entry runs under its own time zone (see `tz_override`).

command.description: For a job line: its command as written. null for any other line.

schedule.description:
For a job line written by hand: its schedule (the five time fields,
or the `@` macro). null for any other line.

schedule_human.description:
The schedule in words; null when the line is not a job, or its
schedule is one a managed entry may not have.

cron_DescribeScheduleResponse.description: What a schedule means, without saving anything.

details.description: Why it is not valid (`minute 61 out of range 0-59`); null when valid.

next_runs.description:
The next times it would run (at most 3, soonest first) in the system
time zone, as `next_runs` of an entry; null when it is not valid, runs
at reboot only or never fires. An entry under its own time zone
(`tz_override`) does not follow them.

schedule_human.description:
The schedule in words (`At 03:00 on Monday through Friday`); null
when it is not valid.

valid.description: Whether a managed entry may have this schedule.

warnings.description: Problems with a valid schedule, such as a date that never comes.

etag.description:
Strong ETag of the user's whole crontab as stored, whatever the page (quoted). Send
it as `If-Match` on `PUT /users/{user}/crontab` to replace the crontab only if it
has not changed since.

cron_HandWrittenJob.description: A job line written by hand in a crontab.

command.description: The command as written (cron reads an unescaped `%` as a line break).

line.description: Its line number in the user's crontab (1-based).

schedule.description: The five time fields, or the `@` macro, as written.

schedule_human.description:
The schedule in words; null when it is one a managed entry may not
have (cron may still run it).

ip.description:
Address of the client connection that made this request, as the
service sees it.

user_agent.description: User-Agent header of this request; null when none was sent.

oneOf.description: The latest reported run of the entry, or null.

next_runs.description:
The next times the entry runs (at most 3, soonest first), in the
system time zone with its offset. null when it has no next time: it is
paused, it runs at reboot only, its schedule never fires, it expires
first, or it runs under its own time zone (`tz_override`). Around a
daylight saving change these follow Vixie cron's rule (`GET /api/v1/cron/info`
`cron_impl: vixie`; another cron may differ there): a skipped fixed
time runs right after the change and a repeated one runs once, while
a schedule with `*` in its minute or hour follows the clock.

recent_due.description:
The latest times the entry was due (at most 5, newest first, none
later than now and none at or after `expires_at`), computed like
`next_runs` and null in the same cases except expiry. Compare them
with the runs reported (`GET /api/v1/cron/runs`) to see whether a run was
reported for a time. They follow from the schedule alone, so a new
entry already lists due times from before it was created.

revision.description:
SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of what the entry runs as: its stored lines and
the crontab's environment assignments in effect above it, `SHELL`
among them. Any change of these, made here or elsewhere, changes it.
Send it as `expected_revision` to change, delete or run the entry only
if it is still what was read.

revision_seen_at.description:
When the service first saw the entry as it is now: its stored lines
and the environment assignments above it. A change made outside the
service moves it too. For an entry already there when the service
started, the service's start time.

run_reports.description:
Whether the entry's runs are reported (`GET /api/v1/cron/runs`, `job_*` events):
its line carries the run report, which an enabled entry under a POSIX
`SHELL` gets.

tz_override.description:
A `CRON_TZ` or `TZ` assignment above the entry may give it another
time zone than the system's, so `next_runs` and `recent_due` are null
and `warnings` says why.

warnings.description:
Present when the schedule is valid but can never fire (e.g. `0 0 31 2 *`),
or when the entry runs under its own time zone (see `tz_override`).

etag.description:
Strong ETag of the user's crontab as stored (quoted). Send it as `If-Match` on
`PUT /users/{user}/crontab` to replace the crontab only if it has not changed since.

Strong ETag of the user's crontab as written (quoted). Send it as `If-Match` on
`PUT /users/{user}/crontab` to replace the crontab only if it has not changed since.

cron_ReceiptState.description:
Where a Run now request is. `accepted`, `running` and `completed` prove
the command was started; `reserved` and `unknown` mean it may have run.

cron_ReportDrops.description: Run reports the service did not record since it started.

rate_limited.description: Refused because one user sent too many in a short time.

untracked.description: Starts not tracked because too many runs were running.

cron_ReportListenerState.description: Whether runs are reported to the service.

expected_revision.description:
The entry's `revision` as last read: the run is refused with 412
`PRECONDITION_FAILED` if the entry changed since.

cron_RunEntryResponse.description:
A Run now answer: the run started (202), or the receipt of the same key
and body (200).

run_id.description:
The run it started (`GET /api/v1/cron/runs?run_id=`); null while `reserved`, and
for `unknown`.

cron_RunReceipt.description: The receipt of a Run now request with an `Idempotency-Key`, kept 24 hours.

entry_id.description:
The entry; null when the service holds no receipt for this key. A
receipt whose start could not be confirmed after a restart can be
`unknown` and still carry it.

reserved_at.description:
When the key was reserved; null when the service holds no receipt for
this key. A receipt whose start could not be confirmed after a restart
can be `unknown` and still carry it.

run_id.description: The run it started; null until it started.

started_at.description: When the command started; null until it started.

user.description:
The entry's user; null when the service holds no receipt for this
key. A receipt whose start could not be confirmed after a restart can
be `unknown` and still carry it.

expected_revision.description:
The entry's `revision` as last read: the update is refused with 412
`PRECONDITION_FAILED` if the entry changed since.

built.description: When this build was made (ISO 8601); null when unknown

started.description: Process start time as ISO 8601 string

ip.description: Address of the caller as the service sees it, or `unknown`.

pipe_PipeStatus.description: One snapshot of a pipe name, from `GET /{path}?status`. Every key is always present; `null` where it does not apply.

kind.description: `null` when idle, `pipe` for an HTTP transfer, `ws` for a WebSocket pair (`?ws`), `live` for a live stream

peers.description: `ws`: peers connected now (0-2; 0 once the pair ended). `null` for pipes

transferId.description: A generated UUID set once the transfer starts streaming, or the sender's own `transfer` id from its arrival; equals the receivers' `X-Hoody-Pipe-Transfer-Id`

activeReceivers.description: Receivers connected now (`live`: viewers). `null` for a `ws` pair

totalReceivers.description: The receiver count `n` the transfer waits for. `null` for a `ws` pair and for `live`

speed.description: Bytes per second, averaged since streaming started (frozen at the end)

eta.description: Seconds left while streaming with a known size

elapsed.description: Seconds since streaming started (frozen at the end)

reason.description: Why a failed transfer failed

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the forwarded bytes, on a complete `?sha256` transfer

bindAddr.description:
PULL only: the loopback address the listener bound. Port alone does not
identify a PULL listener (two sessions can hold the same port on
different addresses in `127.0.0.0/8`), so without this two distinct rows
would be indistinguishable. Omitted for EXPOSE, which binds `0.0.0.0`.

kind.description: `http` for an EXPOSE binding, `tcp` for a PULL binding.

mode.description: `expose` or `pull`.

bindAddr.description:
PULL only: the loopback address this listener bound. Two PULL bindings
on different 127/8 addresses can legitimately hold the same port, so
without this the rows are indistinguishable by anything but bind id and
give no way to reach either socket. Omitted for EXPOSE, which binds
`0.0.0.0`.

kind.description: `http` for an EXPOSE binding, `tcp` for a PULL binding.

mode.description: `expose` or `pull`.

heap.description: Always null: this service reports no separate heap figure.

userAgent.description: The caller's User-Agent header, or an empty string when it is absent.

code.description: Machine-readable error code: `INVALID_GRACE_MS` or `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.

status.description: Always `closing`: the close has started and may not be complete yet.

bindAddr.description:
PULL only: the loopback address this listener bound. Two PULL bindings
on different 127/8 addresses can legitimately hold the same port, so a
port alone no longer identifies the socket. Omitted for EXPOSE, which
binds `0.0.0.0`.

protocol.description: Protocol version of the session: `v2` or `v1`.

egress_UpstreamLease.description: The time limit on an upstream set with `lease`. Absent when the upstream has none.

id.description: Names the lease for `POST /api/v1/egress/upstream/renew`. Not a credential.

ttl.description: Seconds each renewal extends the lease by, as set with `lease`

expires_at.description: Unix time (seconds) at which the upstream is disabled unless renewed

expires_in.description: Seconds left until `expires_at`, by the service's clock

egress_UpstreamStatus.description: Current upstream configuration. Credentials are never returned; `auth` reports only whether they are set.

enabled.description: Whether an upstream proxy is configured. Also true when an unreadable startup setting leaves the service unable to determine whether one is, in which case it refuses traffic rather than assuming there is none.

state.description: Which upstream configuration is in force. `active`: an address for the configured upstream has been checked and approved, and requests are sent through it. This reports the configuration, NOT that the upstream is reachable, so a permitted address with nothing listening on it stays `active` while requests fail. `unavailable`: an upstream has no approved address (refused, not resolvable, the configured text does not parse, or the persisted setting could not be read), so proxied requests are answered `502 configured upstream proxy is unavailable` and are never sent directly instead; the retry continues in the background. `direct`: no upstream is configured and requests are sent directly.

scheme.description: Upstream scheme. Absent when there is no parsed upstream configuration to report

host.description: Upstream host. Absent when there is no parsed upstream configuration to report

port.description: Upstream port. Absent when there is no parsed upstream configuration to report

auth.description: Whether upstream credentials are set. Absent when there is no parsed upstream configuration to report, as when `state` is `direct`.

config_path.description: Path of the file the setting is persisted to

heap.description: Always null: this service reports no separate heap figure.

started.description: Process start time as RFC3339 string

run_Os.description: Target app runtime OS (not the host OS). Determines which candidates are eligible.

run_Arch.description: Target CPU architecture for filtering candidates.

run_AppKind.description: Application kind filter - gui for graphical apps, cli for terminal apps, any for both.

run_SourceKind.description: Package source provider kind. Used for filtering candidates by source and as the provider field on candidates.

run_PickMode.description:
Candidate selection mode:
- ask: return candidate list without selecting (default)
- first: automatically select the highest-ranked candidate
- index: select by 0-based index (requires pick_index)
- id: select by candidate_id (requires candidate_id)

run_OutputFormat.description: Output format override. When set, takes precedence over Accept header content negotiation.

run_PrintCurlMode.description:
Curl command generation mode:
- hoody-run: generate curl for the hoody-run /api/v1/run/resolve endpoint

run_RecommendedMode.description: Recommended execution mode returned by preflight.

run_SourceType.description: Specific source implementation type. Determines how the source resolves and syncs candidates.

run_SourceHealthStatus.description:
Runtime health status for a source.
- warming: a nix source whose first (cold) evaluation runs in the background; searches skip it until it finishes (see provider_details.warm_up)

run_ProfileSourceMode.description:
How a profile interacts with the global source list:
- inherit: start from global sources, apply overrides
- allowlist: disable all sources first, then enable only those listed in the profile's sources array

run_RunStatus.description:
Status of a run request:
- resolved: candidates found but no single candidate selected (no pick or pick=ask)
- dry-run: candidate selected and its exact shell command returned (hoody-run never executes)
- printed-curl: equivalent curl command generated (print_curl set)
- error: an error occurred during resolution

run_JobStatus.description: Current status of an async background job. done, error and cancelled are final; cancelled is set by POST /api/v1/run/jobs/{job_id}/cancel.

run_JobResultType.description: Type of inline job result payload.

run_Selector.description:
Full selector (search/run request) combining query filters, pick mode,
execution context, and output control fields. Can be expressed via query
parameters, path segments, or JSON body.

app.description: Primary name query. A JSON body must use app; the q and name aliases apply only to query strings.

source.description: Source kind filter (repeatable). Empty means the selected profile's default source filter applies when it has one, otherwise no filter. ["any"] matches every source kind.

source_id.description: Search only the configured sources with these ids (repeatable in a query, source_ids is accepted as an alias in a JSON body; GET /api/v1/run/sources shows the ids). Intersects with source, the profile and the policy, and is part of the query-cache key. It never enables a source or changes the config: a named source that is disabled or filtered out adds a SOURCE_NOT_SEARCHED warning. An id that names no configured source gives 400 INVALID_SELECTOR. Empty means no filter.

tags.description: Free-form selector tags. Accepted and passed through to sources and recipe templates; they do not filter or rank candidates

channel.description: Release channel hint (e.g. stable, beta, nightly). Accepted but not applied yet: no source filters or ranks on it, and setting it adds a SELECTOR_HINT_IGNORED warning

version.description: Exact version or constraint, interpreted by the source. pkgx, npm-registry-search, pypi-exact, oci-ghcr and oci-docker-hub-search sources apply it; other sources (nix, AppImage, registry, system and local OCI images) do not pin a version from it.

variant.description: Provider-defined variant (e.g. portable, headless). Accepted but not applied yet: no source filters or ranks on it, and setting it adds a SELECTOR_HINT_IGNORED warning

publisher.description: Keep only candidates by this publisher, compared case-insensitively (a leading @ and a github.com/, ghcr.io/ or hub.docker.com/u/ prefix are ignored). Docker Hub: the namespace or publisher name (library or docker for official images); GHCR: the owner; npm: the scope (@anthropic-ai or anthropic-ai), the package name or the publisher; PyPI: the author; AppImage: the GitHub owner (owner or owner/name); trusted list: repo:owner/name and publisher:name tags. A candidate whose source reports no publisher (nix, pkgx, system) is kept, with a provider note saying the filter was not applied to it. Part of the query-cache key

repo.description: Repository hint (e.g. owner/name for GitHub sources)

release.description: Release hint (e.g. tag for release-based sources)

set_id.description: Bind pick to a specific candidate set to avoid races

display.description: X11 DISPLAY number (defaults to terminal_id)

dry_run.description: Force command-only output. hoody-run never executes, so this is always in effect.

limit.description: Maximum candidates to return (default: 25). Any non-negative value is accepted; the service clamps it to 1-100.

enrich.description: Fill candidate details more completely with extra requests per candidate, inside the same per-source timeout: the Docker Hub repository and tag pages, the npm packument, PyPI download stats (pypistats.org) and the project JSON of a pinned version, and GitHub repository metadata for a candidate whose repository_url is a github.com repository. At most 10 candidates per source and 4 requests in flight per source, each bounded to 4 seconds. A lookup that fails or runs late leaves the field out and adds a provider note `enrichment incomplete: <what>`; it never drops a candidate or fails a source. Enriched candidates carry details.enriched = true. False (the default) makes none of these requests. An enriched and a plain search are separate query-cache entries; enrich never changes candidate_id or set_id.

args.description: Launch arguments for the selected app, at most 64, each at most 4096 bytes, no NUL. Appended as separate words to the selected command: after `--` for a nix result, after the fixed arguments of a starter app, after the image for OCI. A candidate whose command is a source-authored shell plan (manifest and trusted-list entries) answers 400 ARGS_UNSUPPORTED. Like every launch option, it applies to the selected candidate after the pick and never changes candidate_id or set_id.

pass_env.description: Env names an OCI command passes into the container, as `--env NAME` without a value (docker reads the value from the env of the shell that runs the command, so it is never on argv). At most 32. No effect on other candidates, which inherit the shell env anyway.

launch_tag.description: Client-chosen tag of one launch (64 random bits as 16 lowercase hex characters). On an OCI command it adds `-it --name hoody-run-<tag> --label hoody.run.tag=<tag>`, so the launching client can find and remove exactly that container. A tagged command is meant to run in a terminal. No effect on other candidates.

run_LaunchEnvMode.description:
Where the env of the selected command goes:
- inline (default): `shell_command` exports each value (`export KEY='value'`), as before
- separate: no value is written into any command text; the values are returned in the top-level `launch_env`, and `run_plan.env` / `execution_plan.env` show each name with "(set at launch)", for a caller that passes env out of band

secret.description: True for credentials (the injected AI defaults); show the value as secret and never print it.

run_OpensIn.description: Where an app opens once it runs - window (the computer's screen), terminal, or web (a browser tab at its address).

run_StarterWeb.description: Address of a starter web app. It listens on IPv4 0.0.0.0 at this port.

run_StarterInfo.description: Launch metadata of a starter catalog candidate (source_id starter).

secret_env.description: Env values the launching client generates (generate - 32 random bytes, base64url) and passes only through the launch env, never on argv or in a URL.

catalog_id.description: Stable id; resolve it with pick=first to open the entry

available.description: False while resolve cannot offer the entry - its prerequisite tool is missing, or the starter source is disabled or not allowed

enrich.description: The enrich search flag (fuller candidate details with extra requests).

run_SelectorTemplate.description: Partial selector template used by saved recipes and recipe override requests.

limit.description: Maximum candidates to return. Any non-negative value is accepted; the service clamps it to 1-100.

run_Candidate.description: A standardized runnable application candidate produced by a source provider. Contains all information needed to identify, rank, and return exact shell commands for execution.

candidate_id.description: Stable hash of canonical candidate payload, unique within a candidate set

description.example: Mozilla Firefox web browser via nixpkgs

kind.description: Whether the candidate is a GUI or CLI application. `any` means the source does not classify it; only sources with an explicit kind (e.g. manifest registries) emit gui/cli.

version.description: Provider-reported version string

tags.description: Tags the source attaches to the candidate, for categorization. They do not rank candidates. The publisher filter reads a trusted-list candidate's repo:owner/name and publisher:name tags.

source_id.description: ID of the source that produced this candidate

score.description: Ranking score (higher is better). Candidates are ordered by their source's priority first, then by score.

reasons.description: Human-readable reasons why this candidate matched or ranked highly

verified.description: Whether the candidate was verified by a trusted source or integrity check

shell_command.description: Exact shell command after applying run_plan.env and run_plan.cwd wrapping

href_path.description: Path-only reference URL (no domain) for HTML links

run_CandidateDetails.description: What a person or an agent needs to curate a candidate list: popularity, freshness, publisher, trust, license, links and platforms. Filled from data the source already returned (no extra request per candidate); with enrich=true, extra lookups fill it more completely and enriched is true. Informational only - never part of candidate_id, set_id or any hash. Every field is optional and left out when empty; the whole object is left out when the source has nothing to say.

publisher.description: Publisher or account that published it (Docker Hub publisher, npm publisher or, for a CI trusted publisher, the first maintainer, PyPI author or maintainer, GHCR owner).

trust.description:
How far the source vouches for the publisher.
- official: Docker Official Image
- verified_publisher: Docker Hub verified publisher
- open_source: Docker-Sponsored Open Source
- curated: a hoody-run curated table or list (starter catalog, trusted list, curated images)
- community: a public registry package without a trust mark (npm, PyPI, GHCR): unreviewed, matched by name only
- unknown: the source cannot tell

downloads.description: Raw download or pull count over downloads_period.

downloads_label.description: The count as the source shows it - Docker Hub's rounded bucket (such as 1M+), at or below downloads.

stars.description: Star count on the source (Docker Hub); with enrich=true, GitHub stars when the source has none.

created_at.description: When it was created, RFC 3339 as the source gives it - the Docker Hub repository, the PyPI project's first release file, the GHCR image (created annotation).

updated_at.description: Last update, RFC 3339 as the source gives it - the Docker Hub repository's last push, the npm latest version's publish date, the newest file of the PyPI latest release, the AppImage release's publish time.

license.description: License as the source gives it (an SPDX id or expression on npm, PyPI license_expression and OCI annotations; PyPI's free-text license is cut to its first line, at most 80 characters).

repository_url.description: Source repository as a browsable https URL.

homepage_url.description: Another home page link, only when it differs from the candidate's homepage.

latest_version.description: Newest version the source knew at search time (the command may still run a pinned or floating version).

versions.description: Available versions or tags, at most 10. GHCR - version-like tags (main, latest, stable, 1.2.3[-suffix]; no git-*, sha-* or digest tags) from the first tag-list page, in the registry's order (not sorted by date), plain tags before suffixed ones. Docker Hub with enrich=true - the 10 most recently pushed tags, most recent first.

operating_systems.description: Operating systems the image is built for.

categories.description: Source categories (Docker Hub categories, PyPI classifiers - at most 10).

archived.description: The source marks the repository archived (with enrich=true, also GitHub's archived flag).

deprecated.description: Deprecation message, when the source marks the package deprecated.

requires_runtime.description: What must be installed to run the command (docker, npx, uvx, nix, pkgx, fuse, ...).

runner.description: The tool the returned command runs (docker, npx, uvx, nix, pkgx, appimage, system).

runner_fallback.description: True when the command fell back to nix because the store's own tool (npx, uvx) is not installed.

requires_python.description: Python versions the package supports (PyPI requires_python).

opens.description: Where a curated app opens once it runs.

extra.description: Source-specific raw values without a typed field (Docker Hub has_security_attestations; npm search_score, maintainers, downloads_monthly, engines_node; PyPI yanked, yanked_reason; AppImage asset_size; local OCI image_created_at, image_size). With enrich=true also - Docker Hub storage_size, status_description, tag_count, tag, full_size, arch_sizes (architecture to bytes), tag_last_pushed; npm version_count, dist_tags; PyPI downloads_last_day, downloads_last_month; GitHub github_topics, github_pushed_at, open_issues.

enriched.description: True when the search asked for enrich=true and this candidate went through it (at most the first 10 of each source), so a field still missing is unknown rather than not asked. Left out otherwise.

run_RunPlan.description: Execution plan for a candidate. Contains the base shell command with optional environment variables and working directory metadata.

command.description: Complete shell command (no placeholders)

env.description: Environment variables to set before command execution

run_Integrity.description: Optional integrity and provenance information for a candidate, including download URL, hash, and optional Ed25519 signature.

url.description: Download or source URL

author_pubkey_ed25519.description: Ed25519 public key of the manifest author (base64)

sig_ed25519.description: Ed25519 signature of the manifest content (base64)

run_SearchResponse.description: Response from the search endpoint containing a set ID for race-free selection and the ranked list of candidates.

set_id.description: Stable identifier for this candidate set (hash of ordered candidate IDs). Can be used with pick=id to ensure race-free selection.

candidates.description: Ranked list of candidates, ordered by source priority (highest first), then by score (highest first).

warnings.description: Sources that failed, timed out or were skipped during this search (SOURCE_* codes); the candidates are partial when it is not empty

items.description: At most 100 items; a longer list is refused as a whole with 400 BATCH_TOO_LARGE.

run_WarningEntry.description:
Non-fatal advisory. Source-level codes carry source_id:
- SOURCE_WARMING: a nix source skipped while its first evaluation runs in the background
- SOURCE_BACKOFF: a nix source skipped until its next warm-up attempt after a failed one, or an appimage source that skipped release lookups for the GitHub hourly budget or a rate limit (its found candidates are kept)
- SOURCE_TIMEOUT: the source did not answer within the per-source timeout (an appimage-catalog search whose release lookups ran out of time keeps its finished candidates)
- SOURCE_FAILED: the source search failed (nixpkgs may still return its unchecked fallback candidate)
SELECTOR_HINT_IGNORED (no source_id): the request set channel or variant,
which no source filters or ranks on yet; the message names the fields that were set.
SOURCE_NOT_SEARCHED (no source_id): the request's source_id named sources the search
did not run (disabled in the config or by the profile, denied by the policy, or excluded
by the source filter); the message gives the reason for each. source_id never enables a source.
SOURCE_HINT (no source_id): the query names a curated image that only the oci-ghcr
source serves, Docker Hub was searched and oci-ghcr was not; the message says to enable it.
Preflight adds NO_PICK and ASK_MODE.

source_id.description: Source the warning is about (source-level codes only)

launch_env.description: The env of the selected command, with launch_env=separate only

run_HandoffState.description:
Liveness of the handoff. hoody-run never executes, so the only state is:
- preview: nothing executed; preview_* URLs show where the app WILL appear

run_RunHandoff.description: Where the selected app will appear once the returned command runs.

preview_display_url.description: Preview display page URL, where the app will appear. Omitted when no URL can be determined (for example outside a Hoody computer).

preview_terminal_url.description: Preview terminal viewer URL, where the app will appear. Omitted when no URL can be determined (for example outside a Hoody computer).

run_HandoffSuggestion.description: For a client that opens the selected app itself. Present when a candidate is selected.

band.description: First and last terminal id of the band to allocate the app's terminal from

opens_in.description: A starter's own opens_in; otherwise terminal for OCI images, window for candidates of kind gui, terminal for anything else

page_size.description: Candidates per page (default: 25). Any non-negative value is accepted; the service clamps it to 1-100.

warnings.description: Source warnings of the search that built the set (empty on cursor pages, which read the cached set)

run_RunResponse.description:
Response from run endpoints. The shape varies by status:
- resolved: set_id + candidates (no single candidate selected)
- dry-run: set_id + selected + shell_command (hoody-run never executes)
- printed-curl: set_id + selected + curl command
- error: set_id + error message

shell_command.description: Exact shell command for the selected candidate (present when a candidate is selected)

curl.description: Generated curl command (present when print_curl is set)

launch_env.description: The env of the selected command, present with launch_env=separate and a selected candidate. Holds every value the inline command would have exported

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories, including sources that failed, timed out or were skipped (SOURCE_* codes, see WarningEntry)

run_SourceConfig.description: Configuration for a package source including its type, provider, priority, and provider-specific settings.

enabled.description: Whether this source is active for searches

priority.description: Source priority (higher values are searched first and ranked higher)

provider.description: The provider of source_type, and it must match it: nix for nix-pkgs and nix-flake, pkgx for pkgx, appimage for the app-image-* types, oci for the oci-* types, registry for manifest-registry, manifest-remote-index, trusted-list-file and starter-catalog, system for system-path, npm for npm-registry-search, pypi for pypi-exact. any is not a provider; a mismatch is refused with 400 SOURCE_PROVIDER_MISMATCH.

config.description: Provider-specific configuration (varies by source_type), always an object; `{}` when omitted, and null or any other type is refused with 400 INVALID_SOURCE. Keys and values depend on the provider. nix-pkgs takes `flake`, nix-flake takes `flake_ref`, manifest takes `path`, oci-local-images, oci-docker-hub-search and oci-ghcr take `args` (extra `docker run` arguments), oci-docker-hub-search takes `base_url` (default https://hub.docker.com), oci-ghcr takes `base_url` (default https://ghcr.io), npm-registry-search takes `base_url` (default https://registry.npmjs.org), pypi-exact takes `base_url` (default https://pypi.org).

run_SourceUpdate.description: Partial source update. Only the fields present in the body are applied; everything else keeps its stored value. The merged source is re-validated before it is committed, so a patch that would downgrade a signed remote index is refused.

enabled.description: Whether this source is active for searches

priority.description: Source priority (higher values are searched first and ranked higher)

pin.description: Pin to apply. Send null to clear the pin; omit the field to keep the stored one.

config.description: Provider-specific configuration. Replaces the stored object as a unit; null or any other type than an object is refused with 400 INVALID_SOURCE.

run_SourcePin.description: Pin configuration for a source, including URL and optional integrity verification fields.

url.description: Pinned URL for the source

author_pubkey_ed25519.description: Ed25519 public key of the source author (base64)

run_ProfileConfig.description: User profile containing default preferences and source overrides.

run_ProfileUpdate.description: Partial profile update, applied as a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) onto the stored profile. Only the fields present in the body are applied; everything else keeps its stored value. Nested objects (defaults, policy) merge field by field; null resets a field to its default; arrays replace the stored list as a unit. The merged profile is validated before it is stored, and an invalid value or an unknown top-level field is a 400 with nothing stored (unknown keys inside a nested object are ignored, as on create). The profile's name is taken from the path and cannot be changed here.

description.description: Human-readable profile description. Send null to clear it.

sources_mode.description: Source mode. Send null to reset it to inherit.

sources.description: Per-source overrides (enable/disable/reprioritize). Replaces the stored list as a unit; null clears it.

run_ProfileDefaults.description: Default selector values applied when a profile is active and the request does not explicitly set these fields.

source.description: Default source filter

display.description: Default X11 DISPLAY number

limit.description: Default maximum candidates to return. Any non-negative value is accepted; the service clamps it to 1-100.

source_id.description: ID of the source to override

enabled.description: Override enabled state

run_SelectedProfileResponse.description: Confirms which profile is currently selected as the active default profile.

run_RecipeUpdate.description: Partial recipe update, applied as a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) onto the stored recipe. Only the fields present in the body are applied; everything else keeps its stored value. selector_template merges field by field; null resets a field to its default; arrays replace the stored list as a unit. The merged recipe is validated before it is stored, and an invalid value or an unknown top-level field is a 400 with nothing stored (unknown keys inside a nested object are ignored, as on create). The recipe's name is taken from the path and cannot be changed here.

description.description: Human-readable recipe description. Send null to clear it.

allowed_overrides.description: Selector fields a caller may override when running this recipe. Replaces the stored list as a unit; null clears it.

run_ConfigFile.description: Full runtime configuration snapshot including sources, profiles, and active profile selection.

version.description: Configuration file schema version

selected_profile.description: Name of the active profile applied to requests that do not specify a profile explicitly

run_ApiError.description: Standard JSON error payload for request validation, lookup failures, and upstream/service issues.

code.description:
Symbolic error code to branch on. Operation-specific codes are listed under each response's x-error-codes
(POST /api/v1/run/batch lists its per-item codes at operation level). The generic codes, which come from the layers around
the handlers (routing, the access check, request parsing, serialization), are listed here in x-error-codes:
INVALID_REQUEST (400), INVALID_JSON (400, malformed body), INVALID_BODY (400, the body does not fit the schema,
e.g. an unknown enum value; 413, a JSON body larger than 2 MiB), INVALID_QUERY (400), INVALID_PATH (400), UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE (415),
NOT_FOUND (404), METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED (405), FORBIDDEN (403), INTERNAL_ERROR (500).

x-error-codes.title: Invalid request
x-error-codes.description: The request was refused (400) and no more specific code applies
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the error message and fix the request

x-error-codes.title: Malformed JSON
x-error-codes.description: The request body is not valid JSON (400)
x-error-codes.resolution: Send a well-formed JSON body

x-error-codes.title: Invalid request body
x-error-codes.description: The body is valid JSON but does not fit the request schema, for example an unknown enum value or a wrongly typed field (400), or a JSON body is larger than 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes; 413)
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the field named in the error against the request schema; keep a JSON body under 2 MiB

x-error-codes.title: Invalid query string
x-error-codes.description: A query parameter has a value its type refuses (400)
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the parameter named in the error

x-error-codes.title: Invalid path parameter
x-error-codes.description: A path parameter could not be read
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the path against the operation's parameters

x-error-codes.title: Unsupported media type
x-error-codes.description: A JSON body was sent without Content-Type application/json (415)
x-error-codes.resolution: Set Content-Type to application/json

x-error-codes.title: Forbidden
x-error-codes.description: The service's access check refused the caller's address (403)
x-error-codes.resolution: Call the service through its edge proxy URL

x-error-codes.title: Route not found
x-error-codes.description: No route matches the request path (404)
x-error-codes.resolution: Check the path against this document

x-error-codes.title: Method not allowed
x-error-codes.description: The path exists but not with this HTTP method (405)
x-error-codes.resolution: Use a method this document lists for the path

x-error-codes.title: Internal error
x-error-codes.description: The service failed while handling the request (500)
x-error-codes.resolution: Retry; if it persists, check the service logs

status.description: HTTP status code of the response

run_Job.description: Represents an async background job (e.g. source sync).

job_id.description: Unique job identifier

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the job was created

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last status change

result.description: Inline result when available. For a finished search job (result_type search-response) it is a SearchResponse object with set_id, candidates and warnings.

progress.description: Optional progress metadata for long-running jobs

cache_hint.description: Which cache or scan backs this source, for example PATH scan or local OCI image list. Absent when none applies, as for nix sources.

provider_details.description: Provider-specific runtime details. Nix sources report a warm_up object with flake (the flake ref) and state (cold, warming, ready or backoff). It may also contain running_ms, cap_ms, last_error, failed_at, retry_in_ms, consecutive_failures and last_duration_ms, depending on the state and available measurements.

heap.description: Language runtime heap in bytes (null for Rust)

started.description: Process start time as RFC3339 string

run_ProfileDefaultsUpdate.description: Merged field by field into the stored profile defaults. A null field resets it; null for the whole object resets every default.

os.description: Target app runtime OS (not the host OS). Determines which candidates are eligible.

kind.description: Application kind filter - gui for graphical apps, cli for terminal apps, any for both.

source.description: Default source filter

pick.description:
Candidate selection mode:
- ask: return candidate list without selecting (default)
- first: automatically select the highest-ranked candidate
- index: select by 0-based index (requires pick_index)
- id: select by candidate_id (requires candidate_id)

display.description: Default X11 DISPLAY number

limit.description: Default maximum candidates to return. Any non-negative value is accepted; the service clamps it to 1-100.

run_PolicyConfigUpdate.description: Merged field by field into the stored policy, so setting one flag keeps the deny lists. A null field resets it; the deny lists replace as a unit.

run_SelectorTemplateUpdate.description: Merged field by field into the stored selector template, so setting pick keeps app, source and the rest. A null field resets it; arrays replace as a unit.

os.description: Target app runtime OS (not the host OS). Determines which candidates are eligible.

kind.description: Application kind filter - gui for graphical apps, cli for terminal apps, any for both.

arch.description: Target CPU architecture for filtering candidates.

pick.description:
Candidate selection mode:
- ask: return candidate list without selecting (default)
- first: automatically select the highest-ranked candidate
- index: select by 0-based index (requires pick_index)
- id: select by candidate_id (requires candidate_id)

format.description: Output format override. When set, takes precedence over Accept header content negotiation.

print_curl.description:
Curl command generation mode:
- hoody-run: generate curl for the hoody-run /api/v1/run/resolve endpoint

limit.description: Maximum candidates to return. Any non-negative value is accepted; the service clamps it to 1-100.

requestBody.description: The stored request body, redacted. Present only when the read asked for it with `includeRequestBody` and a body was stored.

responseBody.description: The stored response body, redacted. Present only when the read asked for it with `includeResponseBody` and a body was stored.

bodyTruncated.description: True when a stored body was cut short and is not complete.

entries.description: Newest first (descending `id`), except with `afterId` or `last`, which return oldest first.

total.description: Entries matching the request across all pages (with `afterId`, all entries after the cursor; with `last`, the entries returned).

bodiesOmitted.description: Present (true) when the read asked for bodies and they came to more than 4 MiB: past that budget the remaining entries are returned without their bodies. The first entry with a body always gets it, so a smaller page (or `limit=1` with `afterId`) reaches any entry's body.

newestId.description: Per-computer logs URL: the largest row id in this computer's logs when the read ran (at least every `id` in `entries`), or null when there are none. An export can stop at it so it does not chase new entries.

retained.description: Per-computer logs URL: the oldest entry still stored, or null when there are none. Entries are removed oldest first when the row or size limit is reached, so a reader walking forward from a cursor below `oldestId` has missed entries. Entries past the age limit are removed by time, which this does not show: compare with `retention.hours`.

retention.description: Per-computer logs URL. How the logs are kept: entries older than `hours` are not served and are removed; past `maxRows` entries or `maxBytes` bytes the oldest entries are removed first.

byStatusClass.description: Present when a filter was given. Entries per HTTP status class. `none` counts entries without a status (or with one outside 100-599). All six keys are always present.

buckets.description: Present with `bucketMs`: one item per bucket, oldest first, empty buckets included.

byStatusClass.description: Entries per HTTP status class. `none` counts entries without a status (or with one outside 100-599). All six keys are always present.

retention.description: Per-computer logs URL. How the logs are kept: entries older than `hours` are not served and are removed; past `maxRows` entries or `maxBytes` bytes the oldest entries are removed first.

features.description: Per-computer logs URL: the read capabilities this server has (`filters2`: the list, status, address and Bot URL filters; `beforeId`; `buckets`; `retention`: the reply facts). A reader that needs one this list lacks is talking to an older server.

code.description: The error code, from a fixed set. Branch on this, not on `message`: the message is human-readable text and may change.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the identical request could succeed without anything else changing.

display.description: The VM's X display number, as in `spec.display`.

url.description: The browser address of that display. Omitted when this request did not arrive through the computer's `vm` URL, or for display 0, which has no browser address.

share.description: Disk usage of this VM's `share/` folder. Absent until a measurement has completed; absence does not mean the folder is small or empty.

bytes.description: Allocated size in bytes (allocated blocks, not apparent size). Data shared by reflink between `share/` and the VM's disk is counted in both, so this can exceed what deleting the share would free. A hard-linked file is counted once.

partial.description: `true` when the measurement stopped early (too many entries, too deep, too slow, or an unreadable subdirectory), so `bytes` is a lower bound, not a total. A lower bound above `quota_bytes` still refuses a start; one below it proves nothing.

sampled_unix.description: When the measurement was taken, in Unix seconds. A measurement taken while the guest runs describes a folder that may be changing. The measurement taken when a start is checked against the quota is made while the VM is stopped, so nothing in the guest is writing; it can still be partial, and then `bytes` is a lower bound.

quota_bytes.description: This VM's `share_quota_bytes`; absent when the share has no size limit.

over_quota.description: Whether the share is over its quota (`quota_bytes`). `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota.

run.description: The run ID: 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits, never all zeros.

sidecars.description: Health of the VM's helper processes (network, shared folder, TPM). Reported separately from `state`: a VM whose network helper has permanently failed is still `Running`. Omitted when empty.

spec.description: The VM's committed configuration. Absent while the VM is being created, when the configuration cannot be read, and when it changed during each of four consecutive reads because the VM is being reconfigured; read again in that case.

display_url.description: The address of this VM's screen in the browser: the computer's `display-N` URL for the number in `spec.display`. Only in the answer to `GET /vms/{name}`, and only when the VM has a display numbered above 0 and the request came through the computer's `vm` URL; omitted otherwise. `GET /vms/{name}/display` redirects to the same address.

monitor_stalled.description: The QMP monitor is connected and has stopped answering: QEMU accepts commands and replies to none. Omitted when false, so absence means healthy. `state` still reads `Running` and the guest itself is unaffected, but the VM can no longer be managed normally: `pause` and `resume` are refused with `BadState`, and `stop` skips the graceful shutdown steps and terminates QEMU directly. The field clears if the monitor answers again, but do not wait for that: a common cause, a stopped shared-folder helper (virtiofsd), does not recover by itself. Confirm with `GET /vms/{name}`, then stop the VM; stop completes without the monitor.

seq.description: The VM's event counter as of this response. To combine a stream with a read of this resource, open the stream first, then read. A `state` event whose non-zero `seq` is not above this value describes a change this response already reflects and can be skipped. Process every other event whatever its `seq`: events with `seq: 0` are not counted here, and a `resync` always reports a gap. The per-VM stream already applies this rule to its own opening snapshot. Absent when no events have been published for this VM.

error.description:
The typed reason the current run failed to start, as a nested error envelope: the code is at `error.error.code`, one level deeper than it looks. `POST /vms/{name}/start` answers 200 before the launch is decided, so a start failure is reported here rather than as that call's status.
