A refusal found while planning the launch can already be in the start call's 200 body, where `state` may still read `Starting`; treat a populated `error` as the refusal. A failure found later in the launch (QEMU handshake, QEMU exiting early, KVM reported disabled, a helper process or internal storage failure) appears here beside `state` `Failed`, in the start body or on a later `GET`. Poll `GET /vms/{name}` until `Running` or `Failed`.

Cleared when a new start begins. A `Failed` VM with no `error` has only the prose `reason`: this happens for a refusal with no typed code (for example `NotFound`) and for `RunAbnormalExit`, a guest that reached `Running` and later died. Same `{code, message, retryable, ...}` envelope as a synchronous refusal.

share.description: Disk usage of this VM's `share/` folder. Absent until a measurement has completed; absence does not mean the folder is small or empty.

bytes.description: Allocated size in bytes (allocated blocks, not apparent size). Data shared by reflink between `share/` and the VM's disk is counted in both, so this can exceed what deleting the share would free. A hard-linked file is counted once.

partial.description: `true` when the measurement stopped early (too many entries, too deep, too slow, or an unreadable subdirectory), so `bytes` is a lower bound, not a total. A lower bound above `quota_bytes` still refuses a start; one below it proves nothing.

sampled_unix.description: When the measurement was taken, in Unix seconds. A measurement taken while the guest runs describes a folder that may be changing. The measurement taken when a start is checked against the quota is made while the VM is stopped, so nothing in the guest is writing; it can still be partial, and then `bytes` is a lower bound.

quota_bytes.description: This VM's `share_quota_bytes`; absent when the share has no size limit.

over_quota.description: Whether the share is over its quota (`quota_bytes`). `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota.

vm_VmSpecView.description: The VM's committed configuration. Fields marked mutable can be changed with `PATCH /vms/{name}` while the VM is stopped; the rest are fixed for the life of the VM. The guest's UUID, MAC address and disk serial are not exposed.

memory_mib.description: Guest RAM in MiB. Mutable while stopped.

vcpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs. Mutable while stopped.

disk_bytes.description: Size of the system disk in bytes. Mutable while stopped, grow only. Absent when the size could not be read; absence does not mean zero.

firmware.description: System firmware; `uefi-secure-boot` is UEFI with Secure Boot active. Fixed at create.

bus.description: System disk controller. Fixed at create: a guest installed on one bus does not boot from the other.

display_adapter.description: The guest's display adapter. Fixed at create; new VMs get `virtio-vga`. With it the guest is offered the size of its window, so a guest with a virtio-gpu driver (Linux has one built in; Windows needs the virtio-win display driver) changes its resolution to fill the display. `vga` appears only on VMs created before this field existed: their picture is scaled to the display at the resolution the guest chose.

cpu.description: CPU model. Fixed at create. `westmere` is what `cpu: portable` gives at create. `qemu-default` appears only on VMs created before the `cpu` field existed; it lacks POPCNT and SSE4.2 and cannot boot Windows 11 24H2.

tpm.description: Whether the VM has a TPM 2.0. Fixed at create.

file_sharing.description: Whether the VM's `share/` folder is shared into the guest. Fixed at create.

agent.description: Whether this VM has the guest-agent channel (the device, not whether an agent is running in the guest). Fixed at create.

console.description: Whether this VM has a serial console (`isa-serial`, guest `ttyS0`). Fixed at create. When `false`, `GET /vms/{name}/console` is refused permanently; retrying will not help.

console_input.description: Whether `POST /vms/{name}/console` may write to the console. Fixed at create; always `false` when `console` is `false`.

audio.description: Whether this VM has a sound device. Fixed at create. `output` is speaker output only and requires a display, because sound reaches the browser through the display session.

machine_type.description: The QEMU machine type this VM is pinned to. It can differ from the one new VMs get.

display.description: X display number; absent when the VM is headless. Mutable while stopped.

cdroms.description: Attached read-only media by slot, in boot order: slot 0 boots first. `null` is an empty slot, which keeps its position. Replaced whole while stopped (`PATCH /vms/{name}`); one slot at a time while running or paused (`PUT /vms/{name}/cdroms/{slot}`, `DELETE /vms/{name}/cdroms/{slot}`). Omitted when the VM has no CD-ROM slots.

autostart.description: Whether the VM starts automatically when the service starts. Mutable while stopped.

disk_bps.description: Disk throughput limit in bytes per second; absent when unlimited. Mutable while stopped.

disk_iops.description: Disk operations per second limit; absent when unlimited. Mutable while stopped.

share_quota_bytes.description: Size limit in bytes for this VM's `share/` folder (the quota); absent when unlimited. Mutable while stopped. Checked only at start: a VM measured over the limit is refused with `InsufficientSpace`, but a running guest can grow the folder past it. If the folder cannot be measured in time, or at all, the quota check is skipped; the start can still be refused by its other checks. `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota.

ports.description: Inbound port forwards; absent when the VM accepts no inbound connections, which is the default. Without a rule, nothing can connect to the VM. Mutable while stopped.

stop_grace_seconds.description: How long a graceful stop of this VM waits for the guest to power itself down before stopping it forcibly, in seconds; absent when the default of 30 applies. Mutable while stopped.

vm_PortForward.description: One inbound port forward from `host` on the computer's addresses to `guest` inside the VM. Port forwards are the only way to reach a VM: without one, nothing can open a connection to it (not the internet, not this computer, not hoody-display), and traffic is outbound-only.

proto.description: Transport protocol. TCP and UDP are forwarded separately, so a service that uses both (for example DNS or QUIC) needs one rule for each.

host.description: Port opened on every address of the computer, so anything that can reach the computer can reach this guest service; the platform firewall is the boundary. Host ports are shared by every VM in the computer: a port already declared by another VM, even a stopped one, is refused with 409 `PortForwardConflict`. Must be at or above `capabilities.unprivileged_port_start` (1024 when that is `null`): a lower port is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid` by create and `PATCH`, and each start re-checks it against the current value, refusing the start with `SpecInvalid` in the VM's `error`.

guest.description: Port the guest listens on. Not shared between VMs, so every VM can forward to its own port 22.

vm_UpdateVmRequest.description: Every field is optional and an omitted field is left unchanged. At least one field is required: an empty object is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`. `disk_gib` cannot be combined with any other field; send it in a separate request.

memory_mib.description: Guest RAM in MiB from the next start, from 1 to 1048576. Checked against the computer's free memory at that start, not now, so a VM can be given more RAM than currently fits and is then refused when it starts.

vcpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs from the next start. The ceiling is the most QEMU's q35 machine type accepts; a larger value is refused by this call. `POST /vms` uses the same ceiling.

disk_gib.description: Grow the system disk to this size in GiB (absolute, not an increment). The current size is a no-op; a smaller size is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`. The guest must still extend its own partition and filesystem afterwards. Cannot be combined with any other field: send other changes in a separate request.

display.description: `null` makes the VM headless; a number from 1 to 9999 (also written `":N"`) moves it to that X display. Each VM gets a display of its own, started for it at its first start: a VM never runs on a display something else is already using, such as the desktop, a terminal's or a browser's display, or another VM's. An explicit number already in use is refused with 409 `DisplayInUse`, here and again when the VM starts; `"auto"` is the easy way to get a free one. A display can be started for numbers 1 to 9999 only, so any other number is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`. `"auto"` picks the lowest free number from 7001 to 8000 (the service can be started with a different first number; the range is always 1000 numbers and ends at or below 9999), which keeps VMs off the numbers the desktop, terminals and browsers use. A number is free when no other VM has it, no terminal session uses it, and nothing is already drawing on it. If none is free, the request is refused with 409 `DisplayRangeExhausted`, and if the service cannot check, with 503 `DisplayUnavailable`. Nothing is drawing on the picked number yet: starting the VM starts a display there, and if that fails the start is refused with `DisplayUnavailable` in the VM's `error`. Deleting the VM stops the display that was started for it, identified by the terminal session started for it rather than by the X server on the number. The stop checks that session again immediately before it signals, so a session replaced while the stop waited keeps its display. If that session is gone or is another one, the display cannot be stopped, or the service cannot check, the display may be left running. A number is held by what occupies it: it stays taken while a display runs on it or a terminal session holds it, never by the deleted VM's record alone. A cleanup that fails partway is not undone: a display can be stopped while its terminal session was not deleted, and a stop whose answer was lost can still finish. A VM that already has a number in that range keeps it while the VM can still use it (no other VM has it, any display running there is the one started for this VM, and no terminal session holds it while no display runs), so sending `"auto"` again changes nothing; otherwise the VM moves to the lowest free number. The number the VM ends up with is in `spec.display` in the response. Changing the display number is invisible to the guest. Going from headless to a display adds a VGA adapter, a USB controller and a tablet, and the response carries a warning. `null` is refused on a VM whose `spec.audio` is `output`, because its sound needs a display. `display_id` is another name for this field.

display_id.description: Another name for `display`, with the same values and the same meaning, including `null`, `"auto"` and the rule that a VM runs only on a display of its own. Send either one. If you send both, they must have the same value; otherwise the request is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`.

cdroms.description: Replaces the attached media slots, in boot order: slot 0 boots first, so put an installer there. `[]` removes every slot. `null` keeps a slot empty in its position; a running VM can receive a disc in a slot (`PUT /vms/{name}/cdroms/{slot}`) only if the slot held one when the VM started. Each path must be absolute and must exist. At most six slots, or five when the system disk uses `sata`; an empty slot counts.

disk_bps.description: Disk throughput limit in bytes per second, reads and writes together, shared by every attached disk and CD-ROM. `null` removes the limit; omitted leaves it unchanged. `0` is refused by this call (QEMU would read it as unlimited), and so is any value below the minimum, which is the same one `POST /vms` uses. Does not limit shared-folder (virtiofs) traffic.

disk_iops.description: Disk operations per second limit, reads and writes together. Same rules as `disk_bps`: one budget shared by every attached medium, `null` removes it, `0` and values below the minimum are refused (same minimum as `POST /vms`), and shared-folder traffic is not limited.

share_quota_bytes.description: Size limit in bytes for this VM's `share/` folder (the quota). `null` removes the limit; omitted leaves it unchanged; `0` is refused. Enforced at start only: it does not stop a running guest writing. Since it can be changed while the VM is stopped, a VM refused for exceeding it can always be fixed. `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota. Removing the quota from a VM that is over it therefore always publishes `over: false` and clears `over_quota`. Unrelated to `disk_bps` and `disk_iops`, which limit the block device and not the shared folder.

ports.description: Replaces this VM's inbound port forwards with this list (it is not merged, so send every rule you want to keep). Omitted leaves them unchanged; `[]` removes every rule and makes the VM outbound-only; `null` is refused. Refused with 409 `PortForwardConflict` if another VM already declares one of these host ports, running or not.

stop_grace_seconds.description: How long a graceful stop of this VM waits for the guest to power itself down before stopping it forcibly, in seconds (5 to 900). `null` returns it to the default of 30; omitted leaves it unchanged. A stop request's `grace_seconds` overrides it for that stop. Not applied when the service itself shuts down, which gives every VM the default.

warnings.description: Things you should know about a change that succeeded, for example that adding a display added devices the guest will see. Omitted when there are no warnings.

kind.description: Which helper: `passt` provides the guest's network, `virtiofsd` its shared folder, `swtpm` its TPM.

state.description: `degraded` means the helper has failed and will not recover during this run; the VM keeps running with reduced function. For `swtpm` and `virtiofsd`, stopping and starting the VM recovers it; `passt` is restarted automatically a limited number of times per run.

fell_back.description: Set when the disk could not be cloned by reflink and was fully copied instead, which takes longer and uses more space.

warnings.description: Things you should know about a create that succeeded. For example, a clone of a VM with a TPM gets a new TPM rather than a copy, so anything the source sealed to its TPM (BitLocker in particular) cannot be unlocked in the clone without its recovery key. Omitted when there are no warnings.

error.description: Present only when `phase` is `failed`: why the create failed, in the same error envelope a synchronous refusal uses, so one decoder handles both. A create is accepted with 202 before it can fail, so this is where its failure is reported.

display.description: The X display number this VM will use, including the one picked for `display: "auto"`. The same number appears as `spec.display` once the create has finished. Absent when the VM is headless.

memory_mib.description: Guest RAM in MiB, from 1 to 1048576. Required on every create, including from a `snapshot-artifact` source, because an artifact does not record sizing.

vcpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs. Required on every create, including from a `snapshot-artifact` source. Not the same as `cpu`, which picks the CPU model. The ceiling is the most QEMU's q35 machine type accepts; a larger value is refused by this call with 400 `SpecInvalid` rather than failing at start. `PATCH /vms/{name}` uses the same ceiling.

firmware.description: System firmware. Defaults to `uefi`, which every `os` preset, Windows 11 and `secure_boot` need. Fixed at create. With a `snapshot-artifact` source the artifact's firmware is used: `uefi` is treated as omitted, and `bios` against a UEFI artifact is refused.

bus.description: System disk controller. `virtio` is fastest and what every template uses, but Windows has no built-in driver for it. `sata` works in every OS without a driver, at lower throughput. Fixed at create: a guest installed on one bus does not boot from the other. The default is `virtio`, except that a `windows-*` `os` preset uses `sata` on a host with no virtio-win driver ISO. Setting `bus` explicitly always wins.

display.description: X display to render the VM on, from 1 to 9999, as a number or a `:`-prefixed string: `7`, `"7"` and `":7"` are the same display. hoody-display serves that display, so the VM is visible in the browser with no further setup. Each VM gets a display of its own, started for it at its first start: a VM never runs on a display something else is already using, such as the desktop, a terminal's or a browser's display, or another VM's. An explicit number already in use is refused with 409 `DisplayInUse`, here and again when the VM starts; `"auto"` is the easy way to get a free one. A display can be started for numbers 1 to 9999 only, so any other number is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`. `"auto"` picks the lowest free number from 7001 to 8000 (the service can be started with a different first number; the range is always 1000 numbers and ends at or below 9999), which keeps VMs off the numbers the desktop, terminals and browsers use. A number is free when no other VM has it, no terminal session uses it, and nothing is already drawing on it. If none is free, the request is refused with 409 `DisplayRangeExhausted`, and if the service cannot check, with 503 `DisplayUnavailable`. Nothing is drawing on the picked number yet: starting the VM starts a display there, and if that fails the start is refused with `DisplayUnavailable` in the VM's `error`. Deleting the VM stops the display that was started for it, identified by the terminal session started for it rather than by the X server on the number. The stop checks that session again immediately before it signals, so a session replaced while the stop waited keeps its display. If that session is gone or is another one, the display cannot be stopped, or the service cannot check, the display may be left running. A number is held by what occupies it: it stays taken while a display runs on it or a terminal session holds it, never by the deleted VM's record alone. A cleanup that fails partway is not undone: a display can be stopped while its terminal session was not deleted, and a stop whose answer was lost can still finish. The number is in this call's response as `display`, and in `spec.display` once the create has finished. Omitted means headless: nothing can see the guest's screen, and no number is ever picked unless you ask. `display_id` is another name for this field.

display_id.description: Another name for `display`, with the same values and the same meaning, including `"auto"` and the rule that a VM runs only on a display of its own. Send either one. If you send both, they must have the same value; otherwise the request is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid`.

cpu.description: The guest's CPU model. `portable` (the default) is a fixed model (Westmere) with the same CPUID on every host, so the guest sees the same CPU if the computer moves between machines; it meets Windows 11 24H2's requirements (POPCNT and SSE4.2) and includes AES-NI for BitLocker. `host` passes the physical CPU through: fastest, but the guest's CPU changes with the machine it runs on, so use it only for a VM that will not move between hosts with different CPUs. Fixed at create. Refused with a `snapshot-artifact` source, which carries its own model; an artifact whose model is `host` imports with a warning.

agent.description: Give the VM a guest-agent channel: a virtio-serial port named `org.qemu.guest_agent.0` that the guest's qemu-ga can open. On by default: it costs one PCI slot and needs nothing running, and because it is fixed at create, a VM made without it can never report its own IP addresses. Having the channel does not mean an agent is running in the guest; `GET /vms/{name}/agent` tells you that.

console.description: Give the VM a serial console (an `isa-serial` device, guest `ttyS0`) that `GET /vms/{name}/console` reads. On by default, since the console is often the only place a failed boot or install is visible. Fixed at create: a VM created with `console: false` can never gain one. Published as `spec.console`. With a `snapshot-artifact` source, setting this field at all is refused; the artifact decides.

console_input.description: Allow `POST /vms/{name}/console` to write to the console. Defaults to whether the VM has a console. `true` is refused unless `console` is also on. Fixed at create and published as `spec.console_input`. This is not a security boundary (the same caller can already rewrite or delete the VM); it records whether the console accepts input. Both console routes are disabled as agent tools, and console output is sanitised line by line.

audio.description: Give the guest a sound card whose output plays in the browser. Off by default, because a VM with audio fails to start if the display session's sound server cannot be reached. Requires `capabilities.provisioning.audio`; asking for it on a host without it is refused with a message saying which requirement is missing. Also requires a `display`: `"audio": "output"` without a display is refused, and so is a later `PATCH` of `"display": null`. Speaker output only, no microphone. Fixed at create. With a `snapshot-artifact` source the artifact's sound card is used: `none` is treated as omitted, and `output` against an artifact with no sound card is refused. An imported VM with a sound card still needs a `display` in this request.

share.description: Share this VM's `share/` folder into the guest over virtiofs. Off by default, because a VM with a share cannot start if the virtiofsd helper cannot run. Requires `capabilities.provisioning.file_sharing`; asking for it on a host without it is refused. Fixed at create. In the guest, Linux mounts the tag `hoody` with its built-in driver; Windows also needs WinFsp and virtio-win's VirtioFsSvc.

os.description:
The guest operating system. Sets the hardware that OS needs: `windows-11` turns on UEFI, Secure Boot and a TPM; `windows-server` turns on UEFI and a TPM but not Secure Boot; `linux` turns on neither (Secure Boot would refuse an unsigned custom kernel).

It also sets `bus`, depending on the host: a `windows-*` preset uses `virtio`, but on a host where `capabilities.provisioning.virtio_win_iso` is `false` it uses `sata`, because Windows Setup would otherwise find no disk. The same request can therefore build a `virtio` VM on one host and a slower `sata` VM on another, and `bus` cannot be changed later. The substitution is reported in the create's warnings.

These are defaults only: any field set explicitly in this request wins, and omitting `os` changes nothing.

secure_boot.description: Boot with Secure Boot active (enforcing, Microsoft keys enrolled). Off by default, because it can stop an unsigned guest from booting. Requires `"firmware": "uefi"` (`bios` with `secure_boot` is refused) and a host with `capabilities.provisioning.secure_boot`; on a host without it the request is refused rather than creating a VM with Secure Boot silently disabled. Windows 11 needs this and `tpm`. Fixed at create.

disk_bps.description: Limit the VM's disk throughput in bytes per second, reads and writes together. Omitted means unlimited. One budget is shared by every attached disk and CD-ROM. `0` is refused by this call (QEMU would read it as unlimited), and so is any value below the minimum, under which a guest appears to hang. `PATCH /vms/{name}` uses the same minimum. This limits the block device only: shared-folder traffic (`"share": true`, virtiofs) is not limited. There is no network bandwidth limit.

disk_iops.description: Limit the VM's disk operations per second, reads and writes together. Omitted means unlimited. Same rules as `disk_bps`: one shared budget, `0` and values below the minimum refused, the same minimum as `PATCH`, and shared-folder traffic not limited.

share_quota_bytes.description: Size limit in bytes for this VM's `share/` folder (the quota). Omitted means unlimited. A size limit, unrelated to `disk_bps` and `disk_iops`. A VM whose share is measured over the limit is refused at start with 507 `InsufficientSpace`, carrying `need` (the measured size) and `have` (the limit); if the folder cannot be measured in time, or at all, the quota check is skipped and the start is subject only to its other checks. It does not stop a running guest writing past the limit; a hard limit has to come from the computer's filesystem quota. `0` is refused, and so is a limit on a VM without `share`. Mutable while stopped. `over_quota` is the state left by the last crossing, not a comparison with the latest measurement. It turns `true` when a measurement exceeds the quota; a partial measurement counts, because its size is a lower bound. It turns `false` only when a complete measurement is at or below the return level, `quota - quota / 16` (integer division, rounded down), or when the quota is removed; a partial measurement never clears it, so it can stay `true` while the measured size is below the quota but above the return level. Changing the quota re-checks the last measurement against the new value, when one is available, and changes the state only if that check does; with no measurement available, only removing the quota changes it. Each change of `over_quota` publishes one `share-quota` event, and nothing else publishes one. `over_quota` is always `false` when there is no quota.

ports.description: Inbound port forwards. Omitted or empty means the VM is outbound-only: without a rule, nothing can connect to it (not the internet, not this computer, not hoody-display). `host` is opened on every computer address and is shared by all VMs in the computer: a host port already declared by another VM, even a stopped one, is refused with 409 `PortForwardConflict`. Mutable while stopped.

autostart.description: Start this VM automatically when hoody-vm starts. Off by default. This is the only thing that brings a VM back after the computer restarts; VMs that survive a restart of the service alone are reconnected regardless. A VM with `autostart` set comes back at the next computer start even if it was stopped on purpose. A VM refused at startup (typically for lack of capacity) is reported, and the service and other VMs are unaffected.

tpm.description: Give the guest a TPM 2.0 (backed by swtpm). Omitted means yes if the host supports it (`capabilities.provisioning.tpm`). Windows 11 setup stops before disk selection without a TPM. Asking for `true` on a host without TPM support is refused; omitting it there is not. Separate from `secure_boot`, which Windows 11 also needs. Fixed at create. The TPM is created once, at create: if its state later goes missing, the VM refuses to start rather than presenting the guest a different TPM.

stop_grace_seconds.description: How long a graceful stop of this VM waits for the guest to power itself down before stopping it forcibly, in seconds (5 to 900). Omitted means 30. A stop request's `grace_seconds` overrides it for that stop. Not applied when the service itself shuts down, which gives every VM the default. Mutable while stopped.

vm_DiskSource.description: The disk to create the VM from. A tagged union on `type`: each variant has its own required fields and rejects the others.

id.description: Template catalog id. Templates already include their guest drivers.

gib.description: Size of the empty disk in GiB. Allocated sparsely, so it uses only what the guest writes, but it is the size the guest sees. Can be grown later with `PATCH /vms/{name}` `disk_gib`, never shrunk.

oneOf.title: iso
oneOf.description: Install from an ISO onto a new blank disk. Name the ISO with either `sha256` (preferred) or `path`, not both.

gib.description: Size in GiB of the blank disk created for the installation. Required.

sha256.description: An image in the ISO store, uploaded with `POST /isos/{sha256}` or fetched with `POST /isos/downloads`. Preferred, because the store verifies that the contents hash to this name. An upload still in progress is refused like a missing image.

path.description: Absolute path to an installer ISO already on the host. Used in place, so it must still exist at every start, not only at create. Its contents are not verified.

url.description: Not accepted: any `url` is refused. To install from a URL, fetch the image with `POST /isos/downloads`, wait until it is ready, then create from its `sha256`.

path.description: Absolute path to a disk image already on this host. The image is copied into the new VM (by reflink where the filesystem allows, which usually costs no extra space), so the source can be removed afterwards. Its contents are not verified.

name.description: Name of an existing VM whose disk is cloned. The source must not be running. The clone gets a new identity and a new TPM.

oneOf.title: snapshot-artifact
oneOf.description:
Rebuild a VM from a snapshot artifact uploaded to the import store. The disk, UEFI variables, TPM state and machine profile (machine type, firmware, TPM, CPU model, guest-agent channel, console, sound card, shared folder) come from the artifact. Request fields fall into three groups.

Refused if present: `os`, `tpm`, `secure_boot`, `share`, `agent`, `cpu`, `console`. Each names hardware the artifact already defines, and the error names the refused fields. `firmware` and `audio` are refused like the seven above only when they contradict the artifact (`"firmware": "bios"` for a UEFI artifact, `"audio": "output"` for one with no sound card): their default values are treated as omitted, and a value that matches the artifact is accepted. `console_input` is not refused: it defaults to the artifact's console and is checked against it.

Taken from this request, because the artifact does not record them: `memory_mib` and `vcpus` (both required), plus `display`, `autostart`, `disk_bps`, `disk_iops`, `share_quota_bytes` and `stop_grace_seconds`.

`bus` is required with this source and omitting it is refused with 400. An artifact does not record the bus, and the wrong one leaves a guest that cannot boot (Windows stops with INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE) with a bus that cannot be changed later. The create reports in a warning that the bus was chosen by the caller.

There is no `gib`: the disk keeps the artifact's size. Grow it afterwards with `PATCH /vms/{name}` `disk_gib`.

sha256.description: Names an artifact published in the import store (uploaded with `POST /imports/{sha256}`). A lookup key only: the store verified the bytes when the upload was finalized and verifies them again during the rebuild, so this value does not check anything you hold. An artifact that was never finalized is refused like one that does not exist. There is no `path` form.

duplicate_tpm_identity.description: Acknowledgement required for every artifact that carries TPM state, which includes every Windows 11 guest. Read this before setting it. A TPM holds an identity meant to exist once: its endorsement key and every key the guest sealed to it (BitLocker's volume key, Windows Hello credentials, keys in the platform store). With this set, two live machines hold the same secrets and each can unseal what the other sealed. Nothing retires the source machine or consumes the artifact, so the same artifact can be imported any number of times, and attestation cannot tell the copies apart. A `vm-disk` clone avoids this by creating a fresh TPM; an import cannot, because dropping the TPM would boot a BitLocker guest to a recovery prompt. Set it only if you intend the copy and control both machines; if you only want the error to go away, use a fresh install or a clone instead. Setting it for an artifact without TPM state has no effect. Regardless of this field, the guest's OS identity (machine-id, SSH host keys, Windows SID) always comes along in the disk, and the create reports that as a warning.

vm_StopVmRequest.description: Optional body of the stop request (`POST /vms/{name}/stop`). Omit the body, or send `{}`, to use the VM's own grace period.

grace_seconds.description: How long this stop waits for the guest to power itself down before stopping it forcibly, in seconds. Overrides the VM's `stop_grace_seconds` for this stop only.

keys.description: The keys to press together, in order, using QEMU's key names: letters `a`-`z`, digits `0`-`9`, `f1`-`f12`, modifiers (`shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `meta_l` and their right-hand `_r` forms), `ret` (Enter), `spc` (Space), `esc`, `tab`, `backspace`, `delete`, arrows (`up`, `down`, `left`, `right`), the keypad (`kp_*`) and punctuation. Power, sleep and wake keys are not accepted: use the lifecycle routes.

hold_ms.description: How long the keys are held down, in milliseconds. Omitted means QEMU's default (100 ms).

vm_ChangeCdromRequest.description: Body of the CD-ROM change request (`PUT /vms/{name}/cdroms/{slot}`).

source.description: Absolute path of the disc image to put in the slot, as one entry of `cdroms` in `PATCH /vms/{name}`: it must exist, be a regular file, and not be part of another VM's storage. A file in this VM's shared folder (`share/`) is allowed. Opened as a raw image, never probed for a format.

label.description: Snapshot label: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter or digit. The same rule as a VM name. Unique per VM.

disk_bytes.description: Size of the captured disk, in bytes.

nvram_bytes.description: Size of the captured UEFI varstore, in bytes. Absent when this VM has no UEFI varstore (an empty varstore is reported as a size, not omitted).

tpm_bytes.description: Size of the captured vTPM state, in bytes. Absent when this VM has no vTPM.

reflinked.description: True when the disk shares storage with the live disk instead of being copied, so the snapshot initially takes no extra space. False means it occupies the full size of the disk now.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems noticed while taking the snapshot, as sentences. Absent when there are none.

created_unix.description: When the snapshot was taken, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

disk_bytes.description: Size of the captured disk, in bytes.

nvram_bytes.description: Size of the captured UEFI varstore, in bytes. Absent when the VM had no varstore when the snapshot was taken (an empty varstore is reported as a size). A snapshot without a varstore cannot be restored onto a VM with UEFI firmware, because the guest would be left with no boot configuration; `restorable` is false in that case. Any change to the VM's machine profile since the snapshot was taken also blocks the restore.

tpm_bytes.description: Size of the captured vTPM state, in bytes. Absent when the VM had no vTPM when the snapshot was taken. A snapshot without TPM state cannot be restored onto a VM that has a vTPM, because keys the guest sealed to its TPM (such as a BitLocker key) would become unusable; `restorable` is false in that case.

restorable.description: Whether restoring this snapshot onto the VM as it is now would be accepted, using the same rule the restore enforces. It can change: for example, a later change to the VM's machine profile can make it false.

blocked_reason.description: Why the snapshot cannot be restored. Present exactly when `restorable` is false.

bytes.description: Total size of the artifact in bytes, including its framing and header. Empty disk regions are not included, so this is usually well below the sum of the components' sizes. Pass it as `bytes` to `POST /imports/{sha256}`.

part_size.description: Size of every part except the last, in bytes. Fixed for the lifetime of this export.

parts.description: Number of parts: ceil(bytes / part_size). Part n covers `[n*part_size, min((n+1)*part_size, bytes))`; the last part may be shorter.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the whole artifact (framing, header and contents). The disk, varstore and vTPM state are not addressable separately; the artifact is imported as one unit.

created_unix.description: When the export was prepared, in seconds since the Unix epoch. Calling export again returns the same value.

generation.description: The VM's state generation after this restore. Only increases; 0 is the state the VM was created with. Lets a caller tell its own restore from someone else's.

disk_bytes.description: Size of the restored disk, in bytes.

nvram_bytes.description: Size of the UEFI varstore this restore put back, in bytes. Absent when the snapshot had none, which on a successful restore means the VM has no varstore either. The guest's boot configuration is now the one captured with this snapshot.

tpm_bytes.description: Size of the vTPM state this restore put back, in bytes. Absent when the snapshot had none, which on a successful restore means the VM has no vTPM. When present, the guest's sealed keys are now the ones captured with this snapshot, and anything sealed since is gone.

bytes.description: The image's total size in bytes. It reserves no space; it lets the call fail at once with 507 if the image can never fit. On a resume, a different total replaces the declared one if it is at least the bytes already stored, and the resume point is recomputed from it, so a mis-declared upload is corrected by sending this request again with the right total. A total below the bytes already stored is SpecInvalid.

vm_IsoStatus.description: One entry of a content-addressed store, published or still uploading. Returned by the snapshot artifact (`/imports`) operations, and extended by `IsoEntry` for installer images. "Entry" means an installer image or a snapshot artifact.

sha256.description: The entry's SHA-256 digest, which is its identity. Lowercase hex only.

phase.description: `uploading`: parts are still being sent. `ready`: the bytes were verified to hash to `sha256`. Only a `ready` entry can be used by a VM, as installer media or as the artifact a `snapshot-artifact` create is rebuilt from.

bytes.description: Bytes durably stored: the final size when `ready`, the resume point when `uploading`. Read from the stored data, so it is accurate after a crash on either side. If an upload was interrupted mid-part, this reports the last complete part boundary; the incomplete tail is overwritten when that part is sent again.

part_size.description: The exact size every part but the last must have, in bytes. Returned on every response so clients need not hardcode it.

next_part.description: The part index to send next. Absent on a `ready` entry. On an `uploading` entry it is absent when the stored `bytes` equal the declared total (the upload is complete; call finalize), and also when no total was declared or more bytes are stored than declared (call finalize; a mismatch there is refused without discarding anything). When present on an entry shorter than the declared total, it points at the part to send next, including a part that was interrupted mid-transfer. If the total is an exact multiple of `part_size`, this stays present after the last part. Drive the upload loop from `bytes` reaching the declared size, not from this field disappearing.

modified_unix.description: Last modification time, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

vm_IsoEntry.description: One installer image: every `IsoStatus` field, plus what the image identifies itself as. Returned by every `/isos` operation.

vm_IsoMedia.description: What an image declares about itself, and which operating system the host's OS database matches it to. Absent while the entry is `uploading` (unverified content is not read), when the file is not ISO-9660, or when it declares no identifiers. The four identifier fields come from a file the caller uploaded; they are length-bounded and stripped of control and formatting characters, but are not escaped, so treat them as untrusted text and escape them for your own context.

volume_id.description: The ISO-9660 volume identifier. Linux media is usually self-describing (`Debian 12.5.0 amd64 n`, `Ubuntu-Server 24.04.1 LTS amd64`); Windows media is opaque (`CCCOMA_X64FRE_EN-US_DV9`), so use `os` to identify it.

os.description: Every OS the database matches these identifiers to. Usually one; more than one when several entries match equally. Empty when the host has no `osinfo-db` (`GET /osinfo` reports `available: false`) or the database does not know this image, most often because the image is newer than the installed database.

vm_IdentifiedOs.description: One operating system the database matched, and the matching medium.

id.description: The database's identifier, a URI, for example `http://debian.org/debian/13`.

arch.description: The matched medium's architecture. Check it before creating a VM from the image: this service boots only `x86_64`; media for other architectures can be stored but never booted.

live.description: True when the medium boots into a live system without installing.

installer.description: True when the database states this medium is an installer. False means the database does not say, not that it is not an installer.

url.description: The image to fetch. `http` or `https` only, at submission and on every redirect; a redirect to another scheme fails the job.

sha256.description: The vendor's SHA-256 checksum, lowercase hex, if you have one. When present, the fetched bytes must hash to it or nothing is published. When absent, the bytes are published under whatever they hash to and the job reports `verification: "tofu"`.

vm_DownloadJob.description: An image download job. Progress is read from the bytes already written to disk, so it stays correct after a restart of the service.

state.description: `running`: fetching. `verifying`: the bytes have arrived and are being hashed. `ready`: published under `sha256`. `failed`: see `error`. `cancelled`: stopped by a delete. `interrupted`: a service restart cut the transfer off; it is never resumed or deleted automatically.

url.description: The URL this job is fetching. Normally the one you supplied, but if your request joined a running download for the same `sha256`, it is the URL that download was started with. Caller-supplied text, length-bounded and stripped of control characters.

effective_url.description: When a redirect was followed, the URL of the last redirect target that answered. Absent when no redirect was followed or no redirect target answered; never a target that was refused, could not be resolved or was unreachable. May equal `url` for a self-redirect. On a failed job, the last target that answered before the failure. Remote-controlled text, sanitised the same way as `url`.

fetched_bytes.description: Bytes fetched so far, read from the partial file on disk, so the value stays correct across a restart.

expected_bytes.description: The size the origin declared for the image (its `Content-Length`): what the origin declared, not verified; absent when the origin sent none or used chunked encoding. Never used to verify or publish the image.

sha256.description: The digest the image was published under. Present once `state` is `ready`; pass it as the `sha256` of an `iso` source when you create a VM (`POST /vms`).

verification.description: `asserted`: you supplied a sha256 and the bytes matched it. `tofu`: no checksum was supplied, so nothing checked that these are the vendor's bytes. Only the job records this; `GET /isos` does not.

error.description: Why the download failed, as a sentence written by this service (never raw output from the remote server or fetch program).

vm_Catalogue.description: Install media the host's OS database advertises.

arch.description: The architecture the rows were filtered to; null when `arch=all` was asked for.

available.description: True when a database was loaded and has entries. When false, `status` says why.

status.description: Database health. `absent`: no database files; install `osinfo-db`. `damaged`: files exist but some could not be read (see `unreadable`) or they describe nothing; the package is installed, so reinstall or repair it. `healthy`: files present, entries loaded, nothing failed to parse.

unreadable.description: Number of database files that could not be read or parsed. `0` on a healthy host; non-zero means `status` is `damaged`.

vm_CatalogueEntry.description: One operating system and the media advertised for it.

id.description: The database's identifier, a URI, for example `http://debian.org/debian/13`.

eol.description: End-of-life date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when the database records one.

url.description: Where the image can be fetched. Pass it to `POST /isos/downloads` to have this service fetch it and publish it under the sha256 of the downloaded bytes, or fetch it yourself and upload it under its sha256. `osinfo-db` ships no checksums, so a URL fetched without an expected digest is trust on first use.

arch.description: Image architecture. `x86_64` is the only architecture this service can boot.

live.description: True when the image boots into a live system without installing.

installer.description: True when the database states this image is an installer. False means the database does not say, not that the image is not an installer; most entries leave it unset.

identifiable.description: Whether this image can be recognised from its own labels once uploaded. False means `GET /isos` will not resolve a name for it.

bytes.description: The artifact's total size in bytes, as `POST /vms/{name}/snapshots/{label}/export` reported it. It reserves no space; it lets the call fail at once with 507 if the artifact can never fit. On a resume, a different total replaces the declared one if it is at least the bytes already stored, and the resume point is recomputed from it, so a mis-declared upload is corrected by sending this request again with the right total. A total below the bytes already stored is SpecInvalid.

reachable.description: Always true. An agent that does not answer produces a 409 instead.

version.description: The agent's version string, as reported by the guest, length-limited and with control characters removed. Absent if the agent reported none.

supported_commands.description: Every command the agent lists in its `guest-info` answer, including commands this service never uses and commands the agent marks `enabled: false`. At most 256 entries; entries that are not a plain command name (`[a-zA-Z0-9-]`, 1 to 64 characters) are dropped. Either cut is reported in `warnings` with the agent's own entry count. Absent when nothing usable came back. Useful to explain why an inventory section is missing. This is what the guest claims, not a test of what its agent will do.

warnings.description: One line for each change made to the agent's answer: the agent's own entry count when it listed more than 256 commands, and how many entries were dropped as unusable command names. Always present; empty means `supported_commands` is the agent's complete list.

vm_GuestInventory.description:
What the guest agent reports about the guest. Every section is optional. A section is absent when the agent does not support it, refused it, ran out of time before it was asked, or answered with the wrong JSON type; `warnings` says which. All values are reported by the guest, not measured by this service.

Every string, including nested values, array elements and object keys, is cut to 512 characters, with a `…` added as character 513 to mark the cut. Characters that affect presentation rather than content are replaced by U+FFFD: C0 and C1 control characters, Unicode format characters (category `Cf`, including bidirectional overrides, zero-width joiners and the invisible tag characters U+E0000 to U+E007F), line and paragraph separators, non-space separators and variation selectors. Objects have at most 64 keys, nested arrays at most 256 elements, and anything nested deeper than 8 levels is replaced by null. Each list section states its limit as `maxItems`. An `os` that is not an object, and list entries that are not objects, are dropped and reported in `warnings`.

This is not escaping: characters such as `<`, `'`, `;` and `../` are passed through. Treat every value as untrusted text and escape it for wherever you display or use it.

hostname.description: The hostname the guest reports. Longer names are cut to 255 characters plus a `…` marking the cut, so a shortened name is never mistaken for a complete one.

os.description: The agent's OS information, passed through as reported: typically `id`, `name`, `version`, `kernel-release` and `machine`. Keys differ between guest operating systems and are chosen by the guest. Keys and values are sanitised like every other string: at most 64 keys, nested arrays at most 256 elements, nothing deeper than 8 levels.

time_ns.description: The guest's clock, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. Compare it with the host's clock: a large difference commonly makes TLS connections fail inside the guest.

interfaces.description: Network interfaces with their MAC and IP addresses, as the agent reports them. The guest's DHCP-assigned address is available only here. At most 64 entries; if the guest reported more, `warnings` gives its count.

filesystems.description: Mounted filesystems with used and total bytes as the guest sees them, at most 128. These sizes are the guest's view and can differ from the disk's size on the host. The shared folder (virtiofs) never appears here, whether mounted or not, so its absence does not mean the guest has not mounted it.

users.description: Logged-in users, as the agent reports them. At most 256 entries.

warnings.description: One line for each section that is missing, shortened or dropped: the agent's own reason for a section it refused; `not asked` for each section after the agent stopped responding (that section's own line gives the reason, and earlier answers are kept); the guest's original entry count when a list was cut to its limit; and the JSON type received when it was not the expected one. Always present; empty when every section answered in full.

run.description: The run ID: 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits, never all zeros. Pass it when marking this run as dead (`POST /unidentified-runs/{run}/force-mark-dead`), which releases the memory it holds

reason.description: Why this run has no VM name

liveness.description: Always `unknown`: no process is recorded for the run, so the service cannot tell whether it is alive. Clearing it therefore needs a human's confirmation

admitted_bytes.description: Bytes of memory held against this run. This is the whole memory ceiling, because the run's real size is unknown; null when the computer has no memory limit. The key is always present

estimated.description: Always true: `admitted_bytes` is an estimate, not a measurement

clear_route.description: The route that releases this run's memory

confirm_run.description: Must equal `{run}` in the path. Naming the run twice guards against clearing the wrong one

content.description: The returned lines, joined with newlines. For `source=console` each line is sanitised: escape sequences, C0/C1 control characters, bidirectional overrides and invisible characters are removed, while the text, line breaks and non-ASCII scripts are kept. The text is still chosen by the guest, so treat it as untrusted. For the unaltered console bytes (for example to watch a text-mode installer as a terminal would draw it), use `GET /vms/{name}/console`.

disk_bytes.description: Size of the template's disk in bytes. This is also the smallest disk a VM created from it can have.

unprivileged_port_start.description: The lowest port number this host lets unprivileged processes bind (`net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start`). A port forward's host port must be at or above it: a lower one is refused with 400 `SpecInvalid` by create and `PATCH`, and because the value can change, each start checks it again and a VM whose rule is now below it is refused with `SpecInvalid` in its `error`. It may be 0, which makes every port usable. `null` when the value could not be read; the key is always present, so clients must accept `null`. When it is `null`, port forwards are checked against the kernel default of 1024.

ceiling_bytes.description: The computer's memory limit in bytes; null when it has none. The key is always present

items.description: Memory held by one run. Each entry has exactly one of `name` (an ordinary VM) or `unidentified_run` (a run that holds memory but could not be matched to a VM)

name.description: The VM holding this memory. Absent when the run belongs to no known VM; see `unidentified_run`

unidentified_run.description: Present only when `name` is absent: the id of a run that holds memory but could not be matched to a VM. `GET /unidentified-runs` lists these runs; marking one as dead (`POST /unidentified-runs/{run}/force-mark-dead`) releases its memory

admitted_bytes.description: Bytes of memory held by this run; null when it holds the whole limit of a computer that has none (an unidentified run). The key is always present

estimated.description: True when `admitted_bytes` is a reservation, not a measurement

free_bytes.description: Bytes free for VM storage at the time of this request. Informational only: nothing is reserved, and a write that does not fit is refused with `InsufficientSpace` (carrying `need` and `have`) when it happens. These operations check the size up front against free space: a create with a new blank disk (a `blank` source, and the blank disk created beside an `iso` source), a `snapshot-artifact` create (checked against the artifact's full declared size), a disk grow, and an upload to `/isos` or `/imports` (checked at the start against the declared size, and again for each part). Creates cloned from an existing disk (`template`, `offline-file`, `vm-disk`), snapshots and restores are not checked up front. On storage that supports copy-on-write clones they use almost no new space, so a disk larger than this number can still be created or restored. Otherwise they make a full copy, which fails with `InsufficientSpace` if space runs out.

uefi.description: This host can create UEFI VMs. UEFI is the default firmware, so when this is false, create VMs with `"firmware": "bios"` or the create fails.

virtio_win_iso.description: A virtio-win driver ISO is attached automatically as a second CD-ROM beside any installer ISO. Windows has no built-in virtio drivers, so without it Windows setup finds no disk to install to.

templates.description: This host has a template catalog, so `template` disk sources can be used. See `GET /templates`.

machine_type.description: The machine type (`pc-q35-<version>`) given to newly created VMs. Existing VMs keep the machine type they were created with, which may differ.

tpm.description: This host can create VMs with a TPM 2.0 (requires both the `swtpm` and `swtpm-tools` packages). Windows 11 will not install without a TPM.

secure_boot.description: This host can create VMs with Secure Boot enabled and enforcing, with Microsoft keys enrolled. False when the host could only provide Secure Boot-capable firmware with Secure Boot turned off. Windows 11 needs both this and `tpm`.

audio.description: This host can create VMs with a sound device. True only when all three hold: hoody-vm was started with `--pulse-socket-path` naming the desktop session's PulseAudio socket, QEMU can load its `pa` audio driver, and QEMU has the `ich9-intel-hda`/`hda-output` device models. True does not mean the desktop session's audio is running: that is checked at each start, and a start whose audio socket has nothing listening fails with `AudioBackendUnavailable`, naming the socket path. On Debian, QEMU's `pa` driver is in the `qemu-system-gui` package, which an image built without recommended packages lacks.

file_sharing.description: This host can share a folder into guests (`virtiofsd` is present). Every VM has a `share/` folder; this says whether it can be served to the guest. Linux guests mount it with a built-in driver. Windows guests also need WinFsp and the virtio-win `VirtioFsSvc` service, which an unattended Windows install does not set up by itself. This API cannot tell whether the guest has actually mounted the share: the guest agent does not report virtiofs mounts.

display_DisplayNotAvailable.description:
Target display is not running, or did not answer in time. A computer has
no display until a terminal session starts one, so this is the usual
answer on a fresh computer. A display a session made but no program has
used yet starts on the first request that needs it running; this answer
then means it did not start. Every
display route answers this state with this status and code. Only the
screenshot and display-information routes and `POST /api/v1/display/ensure`
set `details.reason` or `details.state`; other routes leave them out.
There, `details.reason` is `dependency_missing` when the computer is
missing software the display needs, and `details.state` is `x-live` when
X runs on the display but its viewer server does not (input still works;
the viewer and screenshots do not).

display_NoWindowManager.description:
The display runs no window manager: a desktop started without a
desktop environment, or one whose window manager has exited. Only a
window manager keeps the window list and the active window, so this
is a state of the display rather than a failure, and retrying does
not change it. `window/search`, window geometry and name, the mouse
and keyboard actions, and `window/focus` on a viewable window (it
gives the window keyboard focus) work without a window manager.
Code `NO_WINDOW_MANAGER`.

display_SyncTimeout.description:
With `sync`, the display is running and the request was sent, but the
change was not seen within 5 s (2 s for `/window/move` and
`/window/restore`): the window manager refused or adjusted it, or the
window was already that way. Code `SYNC_TIMEOUT`.

x-error-codes.resolution: Read the window's current geometry or state before retrying, or send the request without `sync`.

display_KeyboardTargetNotViewable.description:
No viewable window has keyboard focus, so the keys could reach
nothing and none were sent. Nothing has keyboard focus, or the
focused window is hidden, and keyboard input sent to
it is lost. This is a state of the display: restore the window with
`window/restore` if it is hidden, focus it with `window/focus`
(its `inputFocus` must be `true`) and retry. Code
`WINDOW_NOT_VIEWABLE`.
