Restore a hidden window with /window/restore and retry: for keyboard input, focus the window with /window/focus first (inputFocus must be true); for click-at and type-at, pick a point on a window in a fresh screenshot (screenshot pixels are screen coordinates).

x-error-codes.title: Change not seen in time
x-error-codes.description: With `sync`, the display is running and the request was sent, but the change was not seen while the call waited: the window manager refused or adjusted it, or the window was already that way.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the window's current geometry or state before retrying, or send the request without `sync`.

example.error: Window 0x600003 did not change size after the resize request within 5 s

details.message: Window 0x600003 did not change size after the resize request within 5 s
details.help: The display is running and the request was sent, but the change was not seen while the call waited: the window manager may have refused or adjusted it, or the window was already that way. Read the window's current geometry or state before retrying, or send the request without sync.

example.error: The display has no window manager, so it has no active window to read or set

details.message: The display has no window manager, so it has no active window to read or set
details.help: The display has no window manager. Start one (for example a desktop session with a desktop environment); window/search, window geometry and name, the mouse and keyboard actions, and window/focus on a viewable window work without one.

example.details: Displays query parameter must be "all", "*", or a comma-separated list of numeric display IDs (max 5 digits each), optionally colon-prefixed.

notifications_BadRequest.description: Bad Request - an SSE request without `displays`, or with a `displays` value that is not `all`, `*` or a comma-separated list of display IDs (numeric, at most 5 digits each, optionally colon-prefixed). `error` is `Validation Error` and `details` gives the accepted values. The body has no `code` field.

example.message: You have exceeded the 60 requests in 1 minutes limit on this endpoint.

notifications_TooManyRequests.description: Too Many Requests: rate limit exceeded. Limits are fixed windows per client IP, 60 seconds by default. By default 60 requests count across all routes together, POST /notify and POST /push/test each have a separate extra limit of 10, and icons an extra limit of 100. CORS preflights (OPTIONS) are never counted. The body has no `code` field. `error` is `Rate Limit Exceeded` and `message` explains the limit: the example is the message of the limit across all routes; POST /notify sends `Too many notification requests. Please try again later.`, POST /push/test sends `Too many test push requests. Please try again later.` and GET /icons/{iconId} sends `Too many icon requests. Please try again later.` Wait the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then retry.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the current window ends (rounded up, at least 1)

notifications_StreamOriginForbidden.description: Forbidden - WebSocket upgrade from an Origin not listed in `WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Sent before the upgrade; SSE requests are not origin-checked. The body has no `code` field. `error` is `Forbidden` and `message` is `Origin not allowed`. Connect from an origin listed in `WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

notifications_ServiceUnavailableShutting.description: Service Unavailable - the server is shutting down and accepts no new streams. The body has no `code` field. `error` is `Service Unavailable` and `message` is `Server is shutting down`. Reconnect with backoff; the restarted server accepts the connection.

proxyLogs_ServiceUnavailable.description: Unavailable. Variants by `errorCode`: `COMPUTER_PROVISIONING` (the computer is being provisioned), `migration_pending` (the computer's permission settings are being updated), `permission_backend_unavailable` (permission checks are temporarily unavailable; every request is refused until they recover), `COMPUTER_STOPPED` (the computer is stopped; start it, then try again. It is sent without `Retry-After`, since waiting does not help), `COMPUTER_PAUSED` (the computer is paused; resume it, then try again. Also sent without `Retry-After`). The first three are temporary: retry after `Retry-After`.

retryAfter.description: Present on the provisioning variant only

browser_BrowserId.name: browser_id
browser_BrowserId.description: Selects the instance: SDK and CLI clients send the request to the `browser-<N>` service host. A value that conflicts with the host's instance is refused with 400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT. On `/history` it also filters. Against a bare server it selects nothing; address instances there with `browser_host` + `browser_port`.

browser_LaunchArguments.name: launchArguments
browser_LaunchArguments.description: Additional Chromium/Firefox command-line arguments. Pass the query key repeatedly (`launchArguments=--a&launchArguments=--b`) or a single JSON array string (`launchArguments=["--a","--b"]`); every value is kept. Entries must be strings (400 otherwise). On Chromium, every entry must be a switch (`--name` or `--name=value`) that does not open a page: a positional URL or path and `--app` are refused, because a startup page loads before the browser's local-file block is in place. A kit started with local-file access enabled accepts them.

browser_BrowserEngine.name: browser
browser_BrowserEngine.description: Browser engine to use (`chromium` or `firefox`). The raw HTTP query also accepts `chrome` as an alias of `chromium`; the SDK and the CLI accept only `chromium` and `firefox`. Fixed for the life of the instance.

browser_FirefoxVersion.name: firefoxVersion
browser_FirefoxVersion.description:
Firefox version label (informational only). Playwright-managed Firefox builds are used by default.
If omitted, a Playwright Firefox build is downloaded on demand. A value that is not a label (letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`, at most 64 characters) is ignored.

browser_FirefoxExecutablePath.name: firefoxExecutablePath
browser_FirefoxExecutablePath.description: Absolute path to a custom Firefox executable (overrides download)

browser_ShowDevtools.name: showDevtools
browser_ShowDevtools.description: Whether to open DevTools on launch (Chromium only)

browser_UserProfile.name: userProfile
browser_UserProfile.description: Optional user profile object (JSON string): `locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgentString`, `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport`. Precedence for each field: the top-level request option (`locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgent`, `geolocation`, `viewport`) > `userProfile` > the fingerprint profile (`fingerprintId`, `default` when omitted) > the engine default. A value set here always replaces the fingerprint profile's value. `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport` must be objects and get the same checks as the top-level `geolocation` and `viewport`; a bad value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the field. An empty value (`null`, `false`, `0`, `""`) is treated as not set.

browser_StartInstance.name: start
browser_StartInstance.description:
Controls instance creation behavior.
- Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation.
- When auto-start is disabled globally: set to `true` to create an instance.

Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

browser_TabId.name: tabId
browser_TabId.description: The ID of an open tab, from `/tabs`; tab ids start at 1. Omitted: all tabs for `/console` and `/network`; a new tab for `/browse`, unless `onlyIfNotExists=true` finds a tab already showing the URL; the active tab for other tab operations. Supplied: exactly that tab. An unknown id returns `404 TAB_NOT_FOUND` (with `details.openTabs`) and a malformed id `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; the request never falls back to another tab. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`tabId must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.

browser_Url.name: url
browser_Url.description: The URL to navigate to. Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`), on GET and on POST alike: a request naming two destinations is answered rather than silently resolved to one of them. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `url` is governed by the body schema. Only an absolute `http`, `https` or `data` URL, `about:blank`, or (on Chromium engines only) a `chrome:` URL is accepted. Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an http, https or data URL, about:blank, or a chrome URL on Chromium; file and other local schemes are refused`), and a value that is not an absolute URL (such as `/etc/hostname`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an absolute URL, like https://example.com/`). Every other `about:` page is refused (Firefox's `about:reader?url=file:…` loads a local file), and `chrome:` is refused on Firefox, where it is the browser's own privileged UI. A value that is not a string is `url must be a string`. The `url` is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On `/screenshot` and `/pdf` a supplied but empty `url=` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too (omit `url` to capture the current tab). The browser itself blocks local files as well (see "Local files" in the API overview).

code_FolderParam.name: folder
code_FolderParam.description:
Absolute path to workspace folder. Sent with a non-empty value
together with `id` to open an editor. See the `folder` parameter of
`/api/v1/code` for the normalisation rules and for how an empty value
is treated.

code_IdParam.name: id
code_IdParam.description:
Instance selector, an unsigned decimal integer. Sent with a non-empty
value together with `folder` to open an editor. The upper bound is
`65535 - basePort` for the deployment, not a fixed number. See the
`id` parameter of `/api/v1/code` for the full parsing rules and for
how an empty value is treated.

daemon_ProgramId.name: id
daemon_ProgramId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the program. An id that is not a valid `i32` (a word, an empty segment, a number too large) is refused with a plain-text 404, on every route that takes an id, which is NOT the documented JSON 404 of the routes that have one. An id that parses but names no program is the handler's own answer, a 400 carrying the `{success: false, error: ...}` envelope, except on the routes that document a 404. The Hoody Kit programs take the lowest ids on a new computer (the terminal kit is usually 1), so the examples use 100: add your program with `id: 100` (the `complete` add example does), or use the `program.id` the add call returns. Never point a write at a Hoody Kit program's id.

display_displayIdQuery.name: displayId
display_displayIdQuery.description:
Display ID to use (overrides the `*-display-N.*` hostname pattern).
Valid range: 1-999999

display_base64.name: base64
display_base64.description:
Return base64-encoded JSON response instead of binary image.
Useful for AI agents and systems that can't handle binary data.

Accepted values:
- `true`, `1`, `` (empty) - Return base64 JSON
- `false`, `0` - Return binary (default)

display_regionQuery.name: region
display_regionQuery.description:
Crop the returned image to `x1,y1,x2,y2`. Minimum 10x10 px, maximum
65535 on each axis, `x2 > x1` and `y2 > y1`; anything else, an empty
`region` or one given twice included, is a 400.

A capture spans the whole screen, so these are screen coordinates: the
same ones `POST /input/click-at` takes and
`GET /input/display-geometry` describes. The cropped image starts at
`x1,y1`: its pixel (x, y) is screen point (x1 + x, y1 + y).

The region must lie inside the captured screen (`x2` at most its width,
`y2` at most its height): one that does not is a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`
naming the screen size. That check needs the capture, so it comes after
the display was started.

display_cursorQuery.name: cursor
display_cursorQuery.description:
Include the pointer position in the response. Only has an effect on the
base64 JSON form, which gains a `cursor` object; a binary PNG response
has nowhere to put it.

Accepted values: `true`, `1`, `` (empty). Anything else is off.

display_timestamp.name: timestamp
display_timestamp.description:
The screenshot to return. Any of these names it:

- Unix time in seconds (`1749541160`), with or without a fraction (`1749541160.5`).
- Unix time in milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds (`1749541160123`); the unit is
  read from the number of whole digits after any leading zeros (12 or more is milliseconds, 15
  or more microseconds, 18 or more nanoseconds). A number that equals a stored `timestamp`
  exactly, as written, matches that screenshot first.
- A date and time, such as the `timestamp_human` field (`2025-06-10T07:39:20+00:00`): an ISO 8601
  calendar date written with dashes (`2025-06-10T07:39:20Z`, with an offset or none, or
  `2025-06-10` alone), an RFC 2822 date (`Tue, 10 Jun 2025 07:39:20 GMT`), or a date such as
  `06/10/2025 07:39:20`. A date with no zone is read as UTC. ISO 8601 week and ordinal dates and
  the form without dashes are not accepted. A date first matches the screenshot whose
  `timestamp_human` is that second, then one whose `timestamp` is: `timestamp_human` is when the
  file was written, which can be a few seconds after `timestamp`, so one second can name two
  different screenshots. Unix time matches `timestamp` only.
- The screenshot's file name from `full.path` or `thumbnail.path`
  (`1749541160.4242.17.png`), or the whole path, URL-encoded. This names exactly that
  screenshot, even when another was taken in the same second. The `.png` can be left off a
  name in three parts (`1749541160.4242.17`); an older single-number name (`1749541160.png`)
  needs it, as without it the value is Unix time.
- `latest` (or `newest`): the newest stored screenshot.

Times are matched to the second. Two screenshots taken in the same second share a
timestamp: Unix time returns the newer one (after any exact match as written), a date the
first one whose `timestamp_human` is that second (which can be the older). Use the file name
to pick a screenshot exactly.
Anything else is a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

display_decorations.name: decorations
display_decorations.description:
Show window decorations (title bar with close/minimize/maximize buttons).
Set to false for headless/kiosk mode.

display_toolbar.name: toolbar
display_toolbar.description:
Show the toolbar: the menu trigger and the menu.
Set to false to hide all menu UI elements. Has the same effect as
`menu=false`; either one hides both.

display_menu.name: menu
display_menu.description:
Show the Hoody menu trigger icon.
Set to false to hide the menu completely. Has the same effect as
`toolbar=false`; either one hides both.

display_maximize_new_windows.name: maximize_new_windows
display_maximize_new_windows.description:
Open new top-level application windows maximized. On by default; off by
default with `decorations=false` or `decorations=0`, where windows have
no title bar to un-maximize from. `false` keeps the centred placement:
a window smaller than 1024x1024 is enlarged to 1024x1024 (never beyond
the screen or the size the application allows) and centred. Dialogs
and windows of a fixed size keep their size and are centred.

Only applies to windows that do not request their own position, and
skips override-redirect windows, dialogs, other non-NORMAL window
types, and windows the app itself marks undecorated via metadata
(which would have no title bar to un-maximize from). Windows can
still be un-maximized from their title bar.
Setting it to `true` together with `decorations=false` is honoured as
explicit kiosk intent: windows open maximized without a title bar.

display_encoding.name: encoding
display_encoding.description:
Encoding the viewer asks the server to use for window updates. Defaults to
`webp`, which keeps text sharp. `auto` lets the server choose, and it may switch
busy windows to a video encoding that looks blurry. The server only uses an
encoding that both ends support.

display_offscreen.name: offscreen
display_offscreen.description:
Decode and paint in a Web Worker (offscreen canvas). The default depends on the
browser: on in Chrome and Chromium over https and in Firefox 108 or newer, off in
Safari and other WebKit browsers (and in Chrome over plain http). It is the only
path that decodes video encodings. `false` turns it off; `true` forces it on where
the browser supports it.

display_bandwidth_limit.name: bandwidth_limit
display_bandwidth_limit.description: Bandwidth limit in bits per second (0 = unlimited)

display_override_width.name: override_width
display_override_width.description: Override virtual desktop width (auto or numeric value)

display_keyboard.name: keyboard
display_keyboard.description: Show the on-screen virtual keyboard. On by default in mobile browsers, off elsewhere.

display_keyboard_layout.name: keyboard_layout
display_keyboard_layout.description: Keyboard layout (us, gb, fr, de, etc.). When unset, the viewer uses the browser's own layout.

display_swap_keys.name: swap_keys
display_swap_keys.description: Swap the Cmd and Ctrl keys. On by default on macOS, off elsewhere.

display_notification_server_url.name: notification_server_url
display_notification_server_url.description:
External notification server URL for real-time notification integration.

**URL Format:**
`https://{project}-{computer}-n-{display}.{node}.computers.hoody.com/notification-client.js`

**Auto-detection:**
If not provided, the client will attempt to auto-detect from the current hostname pattern.
The client transforms the display URL pattern by replacing 'display' with 'n'.

**Examples:**
- Manual: `?notification_server_url=https://my-project-computer-n-6.node.computers.hoody.com/notification-client.js`
- Auto-detected from: `https://my-project-computer-display-6.node.computers.hoody.com`

**Integration:**
The notification server (port 3999) provides:
- Historical notification retrieval
- Real-time WebSocket notification updates
- Notification icons serving
- Desktop notification triggering

See external notification server OpenAPI spec for complete API documentation.

display_scroll_reverse_y.name: scroll_reverse_y
display_scroll_reverse_y.description: Reverse vertical scrolling direction (auto, true, false)

display_scroll_speed.name: scroll_speed
display_scroll_speed.description:
Global scroll speed multiplier for wheel input.
Applies to non-touchpad-like wheel events.
Runtime clamp range: 0.2 to 3.0.

display_touchpad_scroll_scale.name: touchpad_scroll_scale
display_touchpad_scroll_scale.description:
Scroll speed multiplier for touchpad-like pixel wheel deltas.
Lower values reduce perceived scroll sensitivity.
Runtime clamp range: 0.2 to 2.0.

display_legacy_wheel_tiny_delta_boost.name: legacy_wheel_tiny_delta_boost
display_legacy_wheel_tiny_delta_boost.description:
Minimum synthetic delta boost for tiny touchpad wheel deltas in legacy wheel mode.
Set to 0 to disable boost.
Runtime clamp range: 0 to 120.

display_suspend_inactive_tab.name: suspend_inactive_tab
display_suspend_inactive_tab.description:
Suspend client updates when browser tab is inactive.
Enables power saving by calling client.suspend() on tab hide and client.resume() on tab show.
Recommended to keep enabled for better performance.

display_readonly.name: readonly
display_readonly.description:
Enable read-only/view-only mode.
Blocks all keyboard and mouse input from the client.
Perfect for dashboards, monitoring, or demo scenarios.
Works independently or combines with server readonly setting.

display_title_show_display_id.name: title_show_display_id
display_title_show_display_id.description: Show display ID in browser title

display_parent_keys.name: parent_keys
display_parent_keys.description:
Hand keyboard chords to the embedding page. With `true` or `1`, Ctrl+Alt+B and
Ctrl+Alt+Arrow keys are not sent to the display: the page that frames the viewer
receives a message naming the chord
(`{"type": "hoody-parent-key", "v": 1, "chord": "escape"}`; chords `escape`, `left`,
`right`, `up`, `down`), posted only to the origin of that page (from the referrer,
else `parent_origin`). Not framed, or that origin unknown: the keys reach the display
as usual.

display_parent_origin.name: parent_origin
display_parent_origin.description:
Origin of the page that frames the viewer, for `parent_keys` (for example
`https://app.example.com`). Used when the browser sends no referrer naming that page.
The viewer also writes the origin it uses into its own address, so its own reloads and
reconnects keep reaching the framing page. A value that is not an http(s) origin is ignored.

display_path.name: path
display_path.description: Connection path for the display server

display_action.name: action
display_action.description:
Connection action type.
- `connect` - Connect to existing session
- `start` - Start new session
- `shadow` - Shadow existing display

display_vrefresh.name: vrefresh
display_vrefresh.description:
Vertical refresh rate in Hz. Use -1 for auto-detect.
Minimum 30 when explicitly set.

display_clipboard_poll.name: clipboard_poll
display_clipboard_poll.description:
Poll the browser clipboard to keep it in sync with the display. On by default, except in
Firefox (off); in Safari it is on only when the page is not served over https.

display_app.name: app
display_app.description:
Window to bring forward once the session has started. The viewer finds a window,
maximizes and focuses it, and minimizes every other window. It does not launch
anything. The value is read as:
- a number: a viewer window id, or else a 1-based position in the window list;
- `REGEX:pattern` (or `REGEX:/pattern/flags`): a regular expression tested against
  window titles;
- any other text: a case-insensitive part of a window title.

When no window matches, a notice is shown and all windows are minimized.

name.summary: Focus the window whose title contains "firefox"

regex.summary: Focus a window whose title matches a regex

display_remote_logging.name: remote_logging
display_remote_logging.description: Enable remote logging to the display server

display_insecure.name: insecure
display_insecure.description: Allow insecure authentication (not recommended for production)

display_quality.name: quality
display_quality.description:
Fixed image quality, 0 to 100. A value outside that range, or one that is not a whole
number, is ignored. With it set, the viewer always asks for that quality, the "Image
Quality" menu entry is hidden and `quality_mode` has no effect. Lower values use less
bandwidth and look rougher. Encodings that a lower quality does not shrink (png, rgb
and avif) ignore it. Unset by default: quality follows `quality_mode`.

display_quality_mode.name: quality_mode
display_quality_mode.description:
Image quality mode, the same choice as the "Image Quality" menu.
- `auto` (default) - full quality, switching to a lower quality (shown as "Low bandwidth
  mode") while the connection is detected as slow, and back when it recovers. Each
  switch reconnects the viewer; at most 5 automatic switches happen in 10 minutes.
  Automatic switching needs `reconnect` to be on: with `reconnect=false` the viewer stays
  at full quality.
- `best` - always full quality.
- `reduced` - a lower quality, which uses less bandwidth, for picture formats that have a
  lower quality to use. Formats that do not shrink with quality (`png`, `png/P`, `png/L`,
  `rgb`, `rgb24`, `rgb32`, `avif`) stay as they are.

Any other value counts as `auto`. Ignored when `quality` is set.

display_scroll.name: scroll
display_scroll.description:
Use the `scroll` encoding, where the server sends region copies instead of pixels when a
window scrolls. On by default except in Safari and other WebKit browsers, where it is off
(a few glyphs can stay stale after wheel scrolling there). Without this parameter the
viewer offers `scroll` only to a server that has reported itself safe for it in an earlier
connection from the same host, and only while `reconnect` is on. `true` or `false` here
overrides all of that.

display_colorScheme.name: colorScheme
display_colorScheme.description:
Color scheme of the viewer: `light`, `dark` or `system` (follows the operating system).
Defaults to `system`. `dark_mode=true` is the same as `colorScheme=dark`.

display_theme.name: theme
display_theme.description:
Color theme of the viewer. One of `oc-1` (the default), `aura`, `ayu`, `carbonfox`,
`catppuccin`, `dracula`, `gruvbox`, `monokai`, `nightowl`, `nord`, `onedarkpro`,
`shadesofpurple`, `solarized`, `tokyonight` or `vesper`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`
only.

display_font.name: font
display_font.description:
Font family for the viewer's interface, for example `Ubuntu` or `IBM Plex Mono`, with the
default font as the fallback. Letters, digits, spaces, `_` and `-` only. Unset by default
(the default interface font).

display_reconnect_count.name: reconnect_count
display_reconnect_count.description:
The automatic retry limit after a viewer that was connected loses its connection: it waits
one second after each failed attempt, then tries again, and stops after this many
failures. The offline message can show while retries continue. The count starts again
after every successful connection. Does nothing when `reconnect` is false, and does not
apply to a viewer that has not connected yet (see `soft_giveup_attempts`). Clamped to
1-1000.

display_soft_giveup_attempts.name: soft_giveup_attempts
display_soft_giveup_attempts.description:
Failed first connection attempts after which the viewer stops showing a plain "connecting"
state and offers the connection settings. It keeps retrying slowly in the background (see
`slow_retry_delay`). Applies only to a viewer that has not connected yet. Clamped to 1-1000.

display_soft_giveup_ms.name: soft_giveup_ms
display_soft_giveup_ms.description:
Milliseconds of failed first connection attempts after which the viewer offers the
connection settings, as `soft_giveup_attempts` does; whichever limit is reached first
counts. Clamped to 1000-3600000.

display_slow_retry_delay.name: slow_retry_delay
display_slow_retry_delay.description:
Milliseconds between background connection attempts once the viewer has offered the
connection settings. Clamped to 2000-300000.

display_slow_retry_max_ms.name: slow_retry_max_ms
display_slow_retry_max_ms.description:
Milliseconds after which the viewer stops its background connection attempts and closes.
`0` retries forever. Clamped to 0-7200000.

display_record.name: record
display_record.description:
Start recording the display about two seconds after the recorder is ready, which happens
after the viewer has painted the display for the first time, or 4 seconds after it began
to wait for that paint if nothing paints. The recording is
saved as a file in the browser. See `record_format`, `record_codec` and `record_fps`.

display_record_codec.name: record_codec
display_record_codec.description:
Video codec used with `record`. `h264` or `h265` for `mp4`, `vp8` or `vp9` for `webm`.
Defaults to `h264` for `mp4` and to `vp9` (else `vp8`) for `webm`. A codec the format or
the browser does not support is replaced by another codec of the same format when the
browser has one; when it has none (no MP4 codec, or no WebM support), recording does not
start and the viewer does not switch to another format. Not used for `gif`.

display_record_fps.name: record_fps
display_record_fps.description: Frames per second used with `record`, 1 to 60. Defaults to 30, and to 10 for `gif`.

egress_UpstreamLeaseSeconds.name: lease
egress_UpstreamLeaseSeconds.description: Lease the upstream for this many seconds. The service disables the upstream (as `DELETE` does) unless the lease is renewed before then with `POST /api/v1/egress/upstream/renew`. For an upstream that only works while its client is alive, such as the loopback exit `hoody egress local start` installs.

vm_VmName.name: name
vm_VmName.description: The VM name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

agent_XHoodyCwd.name: X-Hoody-Cwd
agent_XHoodyCwd.description: Per-request working-directory scope: the .hoody project layer / record cwd / tool+workflow cwd. Required by routes that resolve a cwd (e.g. POST /api/v1/agent/todos, which also accepts a body cwd). The value must be UTF-8: other bytes (a non-ASCII path sent as Latin-1) are refused 400 bad_request.

agent_XHoodyConfigDir.name: X-Hoody-Config-Dir
agent_XHoodyConfigDir.description: Per-request --config-dir override selecting which on-disk .hoody install a stateless read/write resolves against. The value must be UTF-8: other bytes are refused 400 bad_request.

agent_XHoodyComputer.name: X-Hoody-Computer
agent_XHoodyComputer.description: Per-request bound remote computer (omitted = local). Rejected (400) on routes with no computer dimension.

agent_XHoodyRealm.name: X-Hoody-Realm
agent_XHoodyRealm.description: Per-request realm selector: "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id (also accepted as ?realm=). On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

agent_RealmQuery.name: realm
agent_RealmQuery.description: Per-request realm selector: the in:query alias of the X-Hoody-Realm header (read when the header is absent or empty): "global" (not tied to a realm) or a 24-hex realm id. "all" is taken only by a list route's own realm parameter, never by this one. On a session route it names the realm the session is looked up in: a session in another realm, or in a realm this login does not serve, is 404 not_found. Rejected (400 realm_scope_unsupported) on active-only / no-realm routes, and for any other realm on an agent pinned to one realm.

notesIdentityBearer.description: Act as a specific notes user. The token is the base64url encoding of the JSON object {"userId", "notebookId", "username", "role"} (role: owner, admin, collaborator, guest or none); it is trusted as-is, because edge proxy is the authentication boundary in front of the kit. A valid Notes bearer identity takes precedence over the query identity. Other authorization schemes, and Bearer values that are not one base64url string or whose decoded text does not start with `{` after leading whitespace, are ignored: the request is handled as if it had no Authorization header. A Bearer value whose decoded text starts with `{` after leading whitespace but is malformed or is not a valid Notes identity returns 401. From the SDK, pass it as kit auth (`kitAuth: { type: 'token', value }`), which sends it as this bearer. A token that decodes (and a successful identity lookup) does not grant notebook membership and provisions nothing. Routes scoped to a notebook return 403 unless the username is a member of that notebook with a role other than none, and requests use that member's stored role, not the role in the token. Membership is granted by creating a notebook (the creator) or adding a user to it, or by the query identity below for the default notebook (unless first seen with role none).

notesIdentityUsername.name: username
notesIdentityUsername.description: Used when no Authorization header is sent. Username (1–32 characters: letters, digits, _ and -; stored lowercase) of a user in the default notebook. The first call with a new username makes it a user of the default notebook with the `role` of that call (a read-only default notebook adds no one: the caller acts with role `none`), and later calls never change the stored role. That user is a member of the default notebook unless its role is `none`: a user first seen with `role=none` gets 403 from routes scoped to the default notebook, until that user's role there is changed. Defaults to `user`. Other notebooks still need membership (add the user to the notebook).

notesIdentityRole.name: role
notesIdentityRole.description: Used with `username`: the role given to that user when it is first provisioned and reported for the request (owner, admin, collaborator, guest or none). Defaults to `owner`. Notebook routes act with the stored role, not this one; `none` provisions a user that is not a member.

notesExportTicket.name: ticket
notesExportTicket.description: Ticket from the export-ticket endpoint of a node, valid for 3 uses within 2 minutes. Accepted only when reading a document with `output=html`, which requires it (the HTML export is meant to be opened by a browser that holds no bearer).
